### Chapter I. The First Book of Moses.

6. **And GOD said: Let there be a firmament <note>The original German uses "Veste," meaning a solid expanse or fortification, often translated as firmament or expanse.</note> between the waters / and let it make a division between both kinds of waters!**

7. **Then GOD made the firmament / and made a division between the water that was under the firmament / and between the water that was above the firmament. And it happened so.**

8. **And GOD called the firmament Heaven. Then there was evening / and there was morning / the second day.**

The firmament is the expansion and stretching out / which GOD made between the waters / and thereby allowed upper and lower waters to come into being / between which this fortification is made / so that the upper waters may not fall down / which are contained in the uppermost thin and lowermost thick clouds / and are supported there by the air / which is, as it were, a thinned-out water / where rain / thunder and lightning / are generated / and in which the winds also arise. Of which David speaks in Ps. 104:2, 3. and Job Chapter 26:7-10. See also Job 36:27-30. Jer. 10:12, 13. Ps. 18:10-16. Isa. 40:22. Ps. 147:8. Prov. 8:27, 28.

Since GOD had already previously made the heaven / which is His throne-seat; He here makes the firmament / as the visible or bodily heaven. For everything that has a body is, without doubt, firm. And because all things / which GOD willed to make / were to consist of spirit and body; therefore it is said / that He first and in the beginning made the heaven / that is / all spiritual being / upon which He rests as if upon His throne.

The water, however / whose chief quality consists in fluidity / was divided into the subtler and thicker parts for future use / and the subtle was drawn out from the coarse. And the purer one part became / the more spiritual and less visible it also became: on the other hand, the other part became so much more visible and manifest / the thicker it became. Therefore the elementary water / wherein the fish weave and swim with their fins / is thicker than our air / in which the birds swim, as it were, with their wings: as it is also written of both in v. 20 / that they were created out of the water. Then the ethereal air is further refined / as a still-subtler and less visible water. The most subtle of all is the water above the firmament / which is the crystalline sea / from which water, because of its subtlety, there is no fear at all of falling down.

<column-break/>

9. **And GOD spoke: Let the water under the heaven gather itself into one place / so that the dry land may be seen! And it happened so.**

10. **And**

Through the gathering of the waters into one place / and the separation and strengthening and founding of the dry land / which was specifically called the Earth / just as that gathering was called the Sea / GOD has now brought the Earth, distinct from the uppermost throne-heaven, out of the wasteland into its wise and wonderful order and distinction from the atmospheric heaven, the dry earth, and the sea along with its rivers / and thus made it fit to be filled with special creatures. And because this work herewith reaches its end / the blessing of goodness from GOD followed on this day: whereby the completion of this work of forming the visible creation of the earth was made known. See regarding this Ps. 24:1, 2; 104:5-10; 136:6; Job 38:4-11; Isa. 45:18; Eccl. 1:7.

And just as GOD now bestows upon the firmament or the expanse the name of Heaven / which He had created before: so He calls the dry land Earth / because He has placed within it the power to bring forth fruit. So also

When the natural and sensory passions are gathered together / and made subject to divine understanding; then the soul <note>German: "Gemüthe," referring to the internal disposition or mind.</note> / free from sensory lusts and other disturbances / just like the earth dried from the waters / must bring forth plants of God’s planting. And

In the soul, the gathered waters of bitterness and sadness are assembled into a single place / when they enter into the boundaries assigned to them. These boundaries, however, surround the heart. Then the dry land emerges / and the soul begins to enter into a new landscape / which it had never seen before / since its conversion. In this, both the dry and the parched land are revealed. This, however, comes to the soul as much harder to bear / than the waters of bitterness. For these waters covering the whole earth were still mixed with some sweetness. But as soon as they are set into their boundaries / they become sea / (namely, full of bitterness /) and that which they previously covered becomes sheer parchedness.

***

According to the hidden understanding, GOD places the firmament between divine and human wisdom: so that a greater influence might not occur / than this lower world would be capable of receiving. The ancient theologians consider this day's work to be unlucky: and the Jews from of old read it in a mournful manner with the <term>Sarka accent<note>A specific musical notation or "trope" in Hebrew cantillation that has a distinct, winding sound, here interpreted as a sign of sorrow or restriction.</note></term>, as if grieving over this obstacle / over this bolt / which hinders the influence of divine wisdom and goodness in and over us. The fountainhead of divine grace and goodness is very rich / very overflowing: but divine justice weighs out to each his measure / of which he is capable and receptive.

Who is now wise and prudent among us / who will apply himself in good time / to also become a good artist of separation <note>German: "Scheide-Künstler," a term often used for alchemists or chemists, here applied to spiritual discernment.</note> / and to separate the waters of earthly wisdom from below out of the depth of the abyss / in which Leviathan / the sea-dragon / swims / yes, to separate himself therefrom through the bitter waters of repentance with tears / and through the spirit of faith / which is a firmament and is understanding / through which we know / how to reject the evil / and to choose the good / the spiritual and heavenly love from that which still lingers in the mouth / that tastes of the vain waters! so that the crystal flows in the pure ground / which God’s little fountain discovers for you: do not mix GOD and the world; because this never holds together. Then surely there will follow / what the Savior promised to faith / and from his body or belly the spiritual waters of life shall flow forth into eternal life / whereby the bitter waters are transformed into sweet. For

After the days of repentance have passed / GOD speaks: Let there be a firmament between the waters! that is: all tears of repentance shall cease / and the spirit and the heart shall be strengthened! These first testimonies of love shall be separated from those waters: as those which / though they be holy / nevertheless were born only through the senses. Let a separation occur between these waters and the waters of my grace; so that such may be found pure and without mixtures.

The waters which are above the firmament signify the waters of grace / which are entirely pure, bright, and clear / and so strongly flood a soul / that they cleanse it entirely in an abyss of pure delight <note>German: "Wollust," which in this pietistic context means spiritual bliss or ecstasy rather than carnal lust.</note>. But then the waters of bitterness and affliction are placed at the very bottom: and the uppermost part / which is represented by the region above the firmament / is entirely drowned in a stream of joys; while meanwhile the lowermost part / namely the earth / is filled with sheer bitterness and affliction. From these thus separated waters / namely of the day of comfort and the night of affliction / the second spiritual day has come to be / namely the second step toward inward Christianity.

<meta>This page continues the allegorical and mystical commentary on the first chapter of Genesis. Having previously discussed the creation of the firmament and the separation of the waters on the second day, the text now addresses the gathering of the waters into seas and the appearance of dry land on the third day, interpreting these physical acts as stages in the internal purification and maturation of the human soul.</meta>

# The First Book of Moses. Chapter I.

### 10. And GOD called the dry land Earth; and the gathering together of the waters called he Seas: and GOD saw that it was good.

GOD calls this confluence of the waters "Sea," because it appears as if, through this separation, all sweetness has been withdrawn and has risen into the upper waters; consequently, nothing but bitterness remains in the lower waters. Indeed, this bitterness is so great that these waters are found to be much more bitter afterward than they were before, when they were all still together. When, however, man begins to enter into the knowledge of himself and his lowly and poor origin through this very process, it brings about a great dryness and aridity. This arises because GOD has withdrawn all the waters that covered him—both the salty waters of affliction and sadness, and the sweet heavenly waters. He then draws the sweet waters of grace to Himself in the uppermost region of the soul, without allowing them to come down to the earth; namely, to our lowest parts, where sensuality has its seat. Thus, the dry and arid land must inevitably reveal itself. This is a bitter experience <note>The original German "gehet aber sauer ein" suggests something that is difficult to swallow or a painful realization.</note>, because the waters of bitterness are also present: not to moisten and refresh as they did before, but to communicate their bitterness without refreshment—except when a heavenly dew occasionally falls upon the soul. However, the Sun of Righteousness <note>A common mystical reference to Christ, based on Malachi 4:2.</note> often tends to dry up and lick away this dew immediately. Nevertheless, this dew strengthens and refreshes, sustains and makes one alive.

That GOD looked upon everything as "good" is stated of all the preceding works for this reason: not only because everything that GOD works alone, without our resistance, is always good, and nothing in GOD's works can be corrupted unless the creature mixes something of its own into it; but also, what is more, because in every stage <note>original: "Staffel"</note> in which GOD places the soul, a certain good unique to that stage is to be found; and yet all have their certain time and diverse uses. For when GOD had created the waters, and they were spread over the entire earth, He said it was good. Yet He changed this shortly thereafter and said again that it was good. Thus, what was good and necessary at one time is useless and harmful at another. At one time it is good that this dry and parched earth be flooded with the waters of grace; at another time, however, it is again good that these waters be taken away from it, and that they gather into their own place. Otherwise, if these waters were to remain on the earth at all times, they would ruin it and prevent anything from growing upon it. It is therefore better to let GOD work in the soul without mixing in the confused and over-hasty actions of the creatures. Such creatures either try to keep these waters when GOD withdraws them, or, by making themselves dry, try to cast them away when GOD does not want them removed—under the pretext that their state would thus be purer. O almighty hand of GOD, you must accomplish everything through your holy Word! You command, and so it happens. Your commanding is the doing itself. And everything you do is good. Therefore, we must let our GOD rule. He will make everything better than we can. Oh, what poor creatures we are! We often imagine we want to make things as well as, if not better than, GOD makes them. Therefore, we meddle in everything and always want to have our hands in the work. But we make no progress at all; rather, our own desire to act prevents Him from working. For GOD works upon no other souls than those yielded <note>original: "gelassene Seelen," referring to the mystical concept of *Gelassenheit* or divine resignation.</note> to Him.

<column-break/>

### 11. And GOD said: Let the earth bring forth grass, the herb yielding seed, and the fruit tree yielding fruit after his kind, whose seed is in itself, upon the earth: and it was so.

### 12. And

On the third day, GOD made the dry earth fruitful, so that it brought forth grass and the self-seeding herbs according to their many kinds, and the fruitful trees, which also have their seed within them, through which they can be propagated. Concerning this work, see Psalm 104:12-16. And because this was also brought to an end on this day, a double declaration of goodness <note>original: "Gutpreiſung"</note> followed; just as happened on the sixth day when a double work was created; whereby the creation in these seven primary works is concluded with seven declarations of goodness.

Look now to yourselves, and what kind of fruits you bring forth! For the earth, which drinks the rain that often comes upon it and bears useful herbs, receives a blessing from GOD. But that which bears thorns and thistles is worthless and near to being cursed. Hebrews 6:7, 8.

Whoever, then, through their own fault remains a dry and unfruitful earth, bearing nothing other than what belongs in the fire, shall themselves become food for the fire according to what they have produced. On the other hand, those who prove themselves to be good land and an earth receptive to and hungry for the divine seed have all the more hope of partaking in the land that flows with milk and honey.

If you cannot make yourself into a fruitful earth, then simply submit yourself to Him who can and will prepare and build you up, and follow His voice, with which He constantly calls you and all His creatures out of the evening into the morning and the day.

After the time has come—the hour of GOD's will, who makes the soul capable of being filled or emptied according to His eternal counsel—then GOD commands this dry and parched earth, which seemed entirely useless, to bring forth green herbs. This is its first offspring. The soul is then greatly astonished that the life-giving power has been communicated to it, enabling it to do good works with little effort despite its great dryness. And these plants also have their seed within them, by which they are brought forth and infinitely multiplied. Nevertheless, for now, these are only small, humble herbs—minor works that do not mean much. But they seem great to one who understands nothing greater: especially since he did not expect that such a good could grow for him in his great unfruitfulness. While such a soul believes it possesses the very greatest thing, it is entirely amazed to realize that the same Word which previously brought forth the herbs within it now also brings forth trees, leaves, and fruits. And these are already greater offspring than those of the herbs. These are, therefore, the noblest virtues, which have their seed within themselves, through which a great multitude of other virtues arise. Then the soul begins to recognize its greatness and its nobility, and what it is capable of, as well as what it desires and what it can attain—even if it still sees such things somewhat obscurely. For it has not yet been revealed to the soul how this happens within it, nor who works all these things. It understands only that GOD is the author of these things. Nevertheless, it imagines that He has done all this because of its own faithfulness. Therefore, it must then learn to understand two things well—

---

first, that everything within it is brought forth through the Word, and that without the Word nothing has been brought forth. Therefore, GOD needs nothing but the Word—namely, His Word—to perform these effects. This was the error which Moses committed at the Waters of Strife <note>original: "Haderwasser," referring to Meribah (Exodus 17 and Numbers 20).</note>. He wanted to strike the rock, even though he was only supposed to speak. For he was no longer permitted to accomplish anything with the staff, but rather through the Word, and to work all things in GOD through the self-existent Word. The miracles of those souls who have already progressed far into GOD happen through the Word alone, without any sign or prototype. But souls who still rest in the "gifts" <note>The author distinguishes between souls who cling to the spiritual "gifts" they receive and those who are unified with the Giver (GOD).</note> do not do this. For they still make use of outward works, because the efficacy through the Word has not yet been communicated to them; in that JESUS Christ is communicated to us and formed in us in no other way than in GOD Himself and in a very high manner; which is called a **mystical incarnation**. Therefore, it is impossible for the soul to work through the Word unless it has been given to it in the manner previously described: and then the Word works all things; saying is as much as doing, and doing as much as saying. But if one, out of unfaithfulness, wishes to use the rod or some signs, as one was accustomed to do before, then one displeases GOD greatly.

# Ch. I. The First Book of Moses.

12. And the earth brought forth grass, and herb yielding seed after its kind, and the tree yielding fruit, whose seed was in itself, after its kind. And GOD saw that it was good.

13. And the evening and the morning were the third day.
<margin>Matthew 12:40.</margin>

---

Secondly, the soul must learn that these effects of grace do not occur because of our virtues, but because of our own unworthiness. This is what Mary well recognized when she burst forth in praise of GOD’s mercy, saying He had shown it to her because GOD had regarded the lowliness <note>The original German "Elend" can mean misery, distress, or lowliness.</note> of His handmaiden. He took her nothingness to heart; and this sight produced the Word in her—namely, the image of the Father—which is born in us in no other way than through His gazing upon our nothingness. And as He thus gazes upon us, He begets His Word in us, namely His speech. And by communicating His Word to us, He makes us capable of acting through Him by speaking alone.

This "state of bringing forth" all virtues in the soul constitutes the third day, namely the third stage of the inner life. What is most to be admired here, however, is that all virtues enter such a soul and establish themselves within it without one being able to comprehend how it happens. Because man does nothing in this process except allow himself to be entirely taken over by GOD and allow Him to work within him, he stands amazed that GOD works everything in him and for him—indeed, each thing in its own time. This happens in such an astonishing order that the soul, when it becomes aware of this, cries out: "Oh, how well He has made everything!" You, O eternal and uncreated Wisdom, must perform everything Yourself if it is to be done well. For everything that You are not, or that does not come from You, is all lies, error, and deception!

If one faithfully follows this interpretation, one will sufficiently see the progress of GOD’s workings in souls through Jesus Christ from the very beginning of their conversion, and how necessary it is on the human side not to oppose these works. This is not achieved, as some imagine, through one's own intense activity alone, but rather through a total surrender to the guidance of grace. Grace never leaves those souls it has taken into its protection for a single moment until it has brought them to their happy destination. Therefore, we must let the Spirit of GOD work within us. But it often appears as if man, on the contrary, aims for nothing else than to hinder the Spirit of GOD from working in him. For while we ought to follow the Spirit of GOD through constant self-denial and the surrender of ourselves to His will, it looks as though we wish to go before Him through our own forceful activity and compel Him not to lead us, but to follow us. and because our ways are only error and misery, we seek to mislead this Holy Spirit of GOD into walking the paths we have set before Him, whereas we should leave ourselves to Him to lead us in His ways. Therefore, we are constantly opposed to this Holy Spirit, so that we grieve Him, as the Scripture says, and finally extinguish Him altogether. Gene-

<column-break/>

14. And GOD said, Let there be lights in the firmament of the heaven to divide the day from the night; and let them be for signs, and for seasons, and for days, and years:

15. And let them be for lights in the firmament of the heaven to give light upon the earth. And it was so.

16. And

---

On the fourth day, GOD filled the atmospheric heaven with countless bright-shining lights, which may be an image of the holy angels as inhabitants of the Throne-Heaven, who are therefore also called morning stars in Job 38:7 and "flames of fire" in Psalm 104:4 <note>The text cites Ps 134:4, likely a typographical error for Ps 104:4.</note>. Likewise, the believers are compared to shining stars in Daniel 12:3.

These lights increased the clarity of the light created in the beginning and, moreover, brought a magnificent benefit to the creation in its plants and other creatures by day and night. Therefore, they were appointed as signs of all kinds of natural weather, according to which people could direct themselves in their natural actions and the cultivation of the earth. These were also intended to arrange the four different seasons and finally to measure days and years, as GOD has wisely divided everything into its times, just as He willed to fit and govern everything in nature and in grace in an orderly way. See concerning this day’s work Psalm 19:5-7, 104:19, 136:7-9; Isaiah 40:26; Jeremiah 31:35, 33:20, 25; Job 38:31-33. Regarding the misuse of these signs, see Deuteronomy 18:10, 14; Isaiah 8:19, 47:13; Jeremiah 10:2. Nevertheless, GOD is occasionally accustomed to give such miraculous signs in the sun, moon, and with extraordinary stars, such as the so-called comets. See Joel 2:30-31; Matthew 24:29; Luke 21:25; Joshua 10:12-13; 2 Kings 20:11; Matthew 2:2, 27:45.

Just as heaven and earth are the two first-created <term>Principia</term> <note>original: "Principia," meaning primary principles or fundamental beginnings.</note> and foundations that have water as the third in common, so also the remaining creatures that came from them are of two kinds. One kind is from heaven—that is, fire and water—and from the very <term>spiritual</term> <note>original: "spiritualen," meaning refined or non-material.</note>, weak, and thin light of verse 3, contracted more densely and distinguished into many spheres of light. Such luminous heavenly spheres are the sun and other fixed stars, which are therefore preeminently called stars that have bright flames (Book of Wisdom 17:5). The other kind is contracted more densely from earth and water and distinguished into dark earth-spheres. Such dark earth-spheres are, besides our own ground, the planets, which in themselves have no light or glow, but shine only as much as they are illuminated by the bright-flaming stars. <term>Epistle of Jude, verse 13.</term> For they are not of a fiery-watery or bright-flaming nature. As can be seen through telescopes <note>original: "Fern-Gläser," literally "far-glasses."</note> on the moon (and indeed on other planets), it has its mountains and valleys, earth and water. For this reason, the moon is called a great light in verse 16 only in relation to our earth, for whose sake the Holy Scripture was recorded. For otherwise, the moon in itself is not a great light, but it has the greatest glow on earth after the sun. Therefore, the Hebrew word *Eretz* <note>original: "ארץ" (Eretz), meaning Earth.</note>—

---

—the general word, may aptly apply to all planets; whereas another word is given with a special distinction for the inhabited earth. Otherwise, the division of Scripture would be quite strange, as the one general <term>principle</term> <note>original: "principium"</note> of the whole world, namely the earth, would be counted as a mere speck of dust compared to the other, which is the heaven. Not to mention that the <term>etymological descent</term> <note>original: "Radical-Descendenz"</note> of the word *Eretz*, which according to the opinion of <term>Poole</term>, <term>Piscator</term>, <term>Ainsworth</term>, etc. <note>Refers to 17th-century biblical scholars Matthew Poole, Johannes Piscator, and Henry Ainsworth.</note>, stems from *Ratz* or *Rutz* <note>original: "רץ oder רוץ"</note>, meaning "to run," agrees very well with the purpose of their creation, which is that they should orbit. For because they are in themselves dark and dim bodies, as can be noted on the darkened part of the moon in its waxing and waning, they would otherwise not easily, or not at all, come into view; which is nevertheless the Creator's will and intention.

Now, just as two of the heavenly lights surpass the others in brilliance and glory among us, so also Christ, the Great Light (Isaiah 9:1), who on the fourth great world-day entered His center in the assumed flesh, shines forth as the Sun of Righteousness above all (Malachi 4:2); and the Bride, as the moon (Song of Solomon 6:10), will also surpass all others in clarity. See Revelation 12:1.

And in the same way, in the new creation or renewal of man, GOD places in the heaven of the mind the Understanding as the sun, which illuminates and warms the entire inner world with the rays of GOD's clarity; and the Moon of Reason, the lesser light of human wisdom, to lead us in the affairs of this life; which now shines in the darkness, but not of itself, for it must borrow its light from the Understanding and the light of GOD; and the stars, the affections and inclinations of the mind, which with their course and secret influences govern the earth alongside the sun and moon.

### 8 The First Book of Moses. Chapter I.

**16. And GOD made two great lights; the greater light to rule the day, and the lesser light to rule the night: he made the stars also.**

**17. And GOD set them in the firmament <note>The original German "Veste" refers to the expanse or firmament of heaven.</note> of the heaven to give light upon the earth:**

---

We must, above all things, strive to first become and be called "heavens" ourselves; only then will we receive these most beautiful lights within us. Christ, the light of the world, and His church—which receives her light from Him and thus also becomes a light of the world (Matthew 5:14)—will illuminate us. Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, Moses, David, and all the prophets to whom GOD gave witness that they pleased Him, will shine their light upon us like stars of the first magnitude, both through their example and according to the Spirit. And if we allow ourselves to be made children of light, we shall no longer walk in the darkness and night of ignorance, nor have need of the moon; rather, Christ Himself will illuminate us sufficiently, just as the sun illuminates the day. He will reveal the signs of the times so that we may escape the coming wrath, and so that the Day of the LORD does not overtake us like a thief in the night, but rather that we may obtain the acceptable year of the LORD.

<margin>Proverbs 4:18.</margin>
However, we cannot be enlightened in any other way than by first allowing ourselves to be helped out of our blindness. For no matter how brightly the sun may shine upon a blind man, he will not become seeing because of it, nor be able to enjoy or make use of the light. He must first choose to follow Christ and, with the most inward desire, implore the Son of David for His mercy so that he might see. Then the Sun of Righteousness will not fail to rise for him with healing in its wings. And the more he then draws near to Christ, conducting his walk in the heights and in heaven, and striving for those things which are above where Christ is, the more his path—as that of a righteous man—will shine like the rising morning light, which shines brighter and brighter until the full noon. And especially:

After the third day or stage of the inner life has passed, GOD begins a new state in the soul: namely, the fourth stage of the inner Christian. Here the soul—in which everything until now has occurred in sheer gloom and darkness—begins to receive inner light and many inward enlightenments. In its highest part <note>The "Obersten" refers to the "apex" or highest faculty of the soul in mystical theology.</note> there is nothing but heat and light; it possesses many comprehensible enlightenments alongside the general light. Its state is so bright that, even when it is night for the soul (which is its time of darkness, though a darkness appropriate to its stage), it nevertheless possesses light within itself, even if it is somewhat different from the light of the day. The difference between the light of the day—namely, the more enlightened state—and the light of the night consists in this: through the light of the day, the objects <note>original: "Vorwürffe"; in this context, the distinct things or truths presented to the mind's eye.</note> are distinguished more clearly than the light itself. Many things are recognized, and many truths are revealed, although the nature of the light itself is not recognized because its rays are blinding. But the light of the night reveals almost no objects; it reveals only itself, and that quite clearly. By this, souls in this stage are often deceived, mistaking the night for the day, and the day for the night, when they prefer the light of darkness over the general light—which, although it hides itself behind its own rays, nevertheless reveals all things exactly as they truly are.

This light of the day, which is the eternal Sun, is the light of faith; it does not satisfy as much through its distinctness, even though it is much brighter than all the other stars. The other lights of the night are all the comprehensible clarities, visions, and enlightenments—everything that distinguishes itself and is seen through the night of our ignorance. Nevertheless, these illuminations all come from GOD and are effects of His goodness and power, which we must receive with reverence and humility. But they are very different from one another. Generally, people are so blind that they prefer the light of the night to the light of the day; and by lingering too long among the stars of heaven, which represent these comprehensible clari-

<column-break/>

**18. And to rule over the day and over the night, and to divide the light from the darkness: and GOD saw that it was good.**

**19. And the evening and the morning were the fourth day.**

**20. An...**

---

-ties, visions, enlightenments, and ecstasies, they fail to pass beyond them to lose themselves entirely in the general light of faith. In this way, they are delayed, because through these minor rays—which deceive us—they wish to distinguish all the objects; whereby such things are magnified, altered, or presented to us as entirely unrecognizable. O, what a cruel loss the soul must suffer here! It is one of the most important points of the spiritual life. For if the soul is not instructed regarding these two lights and their difference, it will remain with the light of the night until its death and never enter into the full day of faith, in which truth is found without error or deception.

The rising and falling of these lights represent the "seasons" of the soul—that is, the state in which it finds itself—just as the sun distinguishes seasons and days as it passes through the twelve signs of the solar cycle; the moon does likewise. Thus, the first approach of the internal sun creates the springtime of the spiritual life, which is not yet the eternal spring. Its progress also creates the summer, which is a state full of light and zeal. Finally, through their heat, they bring forth the autumn fruits. But when the sun later withdraws and moves away from us, it leaves us in a cold winter, which distresses us all the more because the previous times were so pleasant to us. This means: the course of these heavenly lights, whether moving forward or backward, indicates the times and conditions of the soul. And just as the sun always finds again the sign in the <term>Zodiac</term> <note>original: "Zodiaco"</note> from which it departed, whether it comes toward us or goes away from us, so the soul finds its GOD again, who is its home and its origin, even though it must experience great darkness when that same light, which had come to it with great strides, withdraws again.

GOD saw that it was good. This signifies that He saw what benefit the soul had drawn from these holy leadings. Therefore, He ends this fourth day or stage so that the soul may enter into another. But if the soul were diligent, how soon would it reach the seventh day! Namely, the rest of GOD within itself. But alas! our unfaithfulness holds us back even at the first day. Because of this, we remain in a terrible chaos all the days of our lives!

It is also to be noted that at each day and stage it is said: "From evening and morning, a day was made." This indicates both the entrance and the exit of each stage. GOD makes this day or stage, which stands out from the others; the beginning of each stage is, as it were, a newly beginning day, and the end of a stage represents a closing day—which, however, does not end except so that a new one may emerge with greater power. Every change of days is mixed with a night, which, as it closes one day, gives birth to the next. O, wondrous mystery of the greatness of GOD over all creatures! Whoever has open eyes for the spiritual light would perceive with exceedingly great pleasure that nothing occurs in the order of nature which does not happen in a certain likeness according to the order of grace in the soul. This gladdens the spirit and reveals to it not only GOD in all His creatures, but also how GOD conducts Himself toward the souls He wishes to draw to Himself. Thus, one sees nothing in nature that does not express something of what has transpired in one's innermost being. And it is very true that man is a small world <note>The "Microcosm" theory: that the human being contains the entire universe in miniature.</note> in which everything that happens in the great world occurs in brief summary. The reason we do not entirely see this is that we are not yet permeated by the light of truth.

<meta>This page continues the spiritual commentary on the first chapter of Genesis, moving from the creation of the heavenly lights on the fourth day to the creation of sea creatures and birds on the fifth day. The author transitions from the "lights of the soul" to the "living movements" of the inner life.</meta>

# Chapter I. The First Book of Moses.

> 20. And GOD said: Let the waters swarm with a swarm of living souls, and let birds fly above the earth, across the face of the firmament of heaven!
> 21. And GOD created the great

---

Just as GOD on the third day created creatures with a growing life <note>referring to plants</note>, and on the fourth day those with a life of movement <note>the heavenly bodies</note>; so on the fifth day He created creatures that would be living souls—that is, those intended to have a soulish, sensitive, and sensory life. From these, He first willed to fill the water and the air with such animals that come forth in great multitude. Among the fish, the great whales are also mentioned as a singular sign of GOD's omnipotence, among which Leviathan is counted in Psalm 104. And thus, this day's work is also praised.

<margin>Psalm 104:18, 25.</margin>
If our mind is enlightened by Christ, the Sun, then it is our duty—and it is the LORD's will for us—that we then bring our good and evil thoughts to light and let them be revealed, like the creeping things of the earth and the winged creatures of the air: so that here too a separation of good and evil may occur. For from the depths of our heart, as if from waters, come both good and wicked thoughts. Thus, we should place both kinds before the face and judgment of GOD, so that we may recognize and distinguish them through His revealing light. Then we may separate from ourselves that which creeps upon the earth and is devoted to earthly lusts and anxieties of the belly, so that the winged part may soar all the more easily and higher above the earth toward heaven, through the movements and pourings-in, the gifts and graces of the Holy Spirit—acting as the *Bahanim* <note>original: "Bahanim"; likely a reference to a mystical interpretation of Hebrew terms for spiritual "beasts" or "powers" used by early ascetic writers</note>, as one of the oldest and most pious Fathers understood this word. For through these we take "wings of a dove" and fly into the face of the firmament, through contemplation and the lifting of the mind above all earthly things. And through this, our soul escapes the snare of the fowler. Thus, if you look upon a woman to lust after her, that is a poisonous toad within you. But if the spirit and sense of moderation and chastity is in us, we will—even when the Egyptian woman <note>A reference to Potiphar's wife attempting to seduce Joseph</note> wants to entice us to love—flee from it as if on wings, leaving the Egyptian clothes in her hand, so that we might only escape her lustful nets. If the desire for another's goods and a love for the deceit of unrighteousness is in you; oh, that is an evil creeping beast! But if we are so minded and natured that even if we have only two mites or pennies, we gladly share them out of mercy; this nature, this sense, is a bird that does not stick to the earth but has its delight in staying in the heights. And so we must learn to test and distinguish ourselves in all the rest.

But the question arises: how is it that GOD nevertheless recognizes and regards everything—the creeping things, even the whales, and the birds—as good? Answer: To the holy and to those who love GOD, all things are good, even that which is contrary to them and seems harmful: because they are able to overcome it, and when they have overcome it, they become partakers of even greater glory with GOD. Just as the poisonous dragon and monstrous Leviathan obtained power to act against Job; he only became the cause of a double glory for him after the victory. For everything he had lost he received back twofold in earthly goods, and without doubt also in heavenly ones. How beautiful and pleasant the radiance of light is would not be so recognized if night and darkness did not come in between. Why are some praised for their chastity, except because others are loathed for their impurity? Why are brave people praised and highly esteemed, except because there are so many faint-hearted and fearful hares? If you take something bitter in hand, the sweet is much sweeter. If you look at something black, the white and bright will appear all the more lovely to you. And so, from the contemplation of evil, the excellence of good shines forth and radiates all the more gloriously. Therefore, it is said of everything: GOD saw that it was good, for the sake of its utility. But it does not say GOD said it was good in its own essence and its archetype.

<column-break/>

> whales, and every living soul that creeps, with which the waters swarmed according to their kind; and every winged bird according to its kind. And GOD saw that it was good.
> 22. And

---

Otherwise, until now, plants have come forth upon the dry and parched earth. One has also seen the lights born in the soul. Namely, both the distinct clarities and the general light of faith: which, although it is indistinct in itself, nevertheless reveals all truths as they are, if only we make use of it to recognize the objects discovered through it, and do not turn our eyes upon the light itself. For if we were to stop to look at the light itself, it would blind us, and would give the eyes of the spirit such qualities that—even though the eyes would be bright—they could not recognize the objects as they are: because they would look quite forced. And in this way, it happens to many souls. Instead of using this light of faith to discover what it wants to show them, they look at the light itself; they want to know what it is and its various effects. Then the eye is blinded: because it has acted against GOD, who only gives this light so that we may run to Him through the path which the light shows us. From this arise all the delusions that occur in the paths of faith. Yet these paths are otherwise so pure, so straight, and so certain, that there is nothing to fear of delusion for the souls upon them—provided they use them in the manner already described. But with those lights that have something pleasant in themselves, it is quite different. For since such lights reveal nothing else without discovering only very few objects, and even then in a very limited way; they cannot reveal things as they are, but only according to our conception, which, according to its liveliness, imagines them only according to what still remains of them, even if they themselves are already gone. One also makes lights for oneself, without wanting to, through the reflection of the mind. The torches of the night are, after all, also imitated by art. But the light of faith is of such a nature that it cannot be imitated: because through its vast conception it swallows up all sensory lights, as it penetrates them all with its clarity. Faith likewise penetrates through everything, so that it can be stopped in nothing but GOD. And therein consists the infallible firmness: namely, when one makes use of it not to look at it, but to always walk forward through it.

To be sure, the soul had felt all these shining graces until then, but its waters had not yet been found living or life-giving. Why do we think it is written that GOD created all sorts of animals in the waters, a different kind of animal according to each kind of water? Because, as we have heard before, there are two kinds of water: sweet and bitter. The bitter ones have been made alive. For it is precisely then that the soul begins to recognize that in bitterness and in death, which takes her away, a seed of life is hidden: and thus this same seed makes the soul love this bitterness; as she considers it more useful for herself than the sweet waters. These bitter waters also bring forth the very greatest, most unusual, and most precious things on the whole earth. Then the soul, because she knows the right distinction, always prefers the bitter over the sweet waters.

The sweetnesses, however, are nonetheless also living and animated. They are no longer mere enlightenments which discover objects without communicating them: but they are life-giving outpourings which bring about a living beginning in the soul. Then she feels herself filled with a recollected life, which she retains even in the midst of her affairs. This life is nothing other than the gentleness <term>Leutseligkeit: a combination of friendliness, humility, and spiritual approachability</term>, which is already to be found at a high level in this soul, and which works an immortal seed in her. This makes the ground of the divine life and the presence of GOD entirely inward. And this is the close, but not yet actual, union.

One also makes lights for oneself / without intending to / through the reflection of the mind. The torches of the night are indeed also imitated by art. But the light of faith is of such a nature / that it cannot be imitated: because through its vast concept it swallows up all sensory lights / in that it penetrates them all with its clarity. Faith likewise penetrates through everything / so that it can be stopped by nothing except GOD. And therein consists the infallible steadfastness / namely, when one makes use of it / not to gaze at it / but to always walk forward through the same.

The soul had indeed felt all these shining graces until then / but its waters had not yet been found living or life-giving. Why do you think it is written / that GOD created all sorts of animals in the waters / according to each kind of water another kind of animal? Because / as we have heard before / there are two kinds of water: sweet and bitter. The bitter ones have been made alive. For exactly then the soul begins to recognize that in bitterness and in death / which takes it away / a seed of life is hidden: and thus this same thing causes / the soul to love this bitterness; in that it considers it more useful for itself than the sweet waters. These bitter waters also bring forth the greatest / most unusual and most precious things / on the whole earth. Then the soul / because it knows the right distinction / always chooses the bitter rather than the sweet waters.

But the sweetnesses are nonetheless also living and ensouled. They are no longer mere illuminations / which discover the objects without communicating them: but they are life-giving outflows which bring about a living beginning in the soul. Then she feels herself filled with an inward life / which she retains even in the midst of her affairs. This life is nothing other than blessedness / which is already to be found in such a soul at a high stage / and which works an immortal seed in her. This makes the ground of the divine life and the presence of GOD quite intimate. And this is the precise / but not yet actual / union.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the first chapter of Genesis, moving from the creation of sea and air creatures on the fifth day to the creation of land animals on the sixth day. The author interprets these physical acts of creation as metaphors for the "inward Christian's" spiritual development.</meta>

->### The First Book of Moses. Ch. I.<-
<meta>catchword: The</meta>

### 22. And GOD blessed them and said: Be fruitful and multiply / and fill the water in the sea / and let the birds multiply upon the earth!
### 23. Then there was evening / and there was morning / the fifth day.

Furthermore, God creates in the ground of the heart <note>German: *Hertzens-Grunde*. In mystical tradition, this refers to the deepest, most essential part of a person where they encounter God.</note> / or rather in the highest peak of the understanding / birds / which fly about in the sanctified air of the Divinity. They represent very high and sublime concepts / which, however, pass by so quickly / that afterwards no trace of them can be seen. And this is the difference between what occurs in faith / and those other illuminations. Namely, the illuminations from faith make themselves understandable / they explain themselves / and remain clear in the understanding. One can recount them whenever one wishes / and recall them at any time. The other illuminations, however, pass by so quickly / that no trace of them remains even in the imagination. Therefore, one cannot envision them again / nor experience their nature. Nevertheless / just as one does not notice birds better than when they are flying in the air / though they always dwell in the air / and are heard there better than they are seen: so do souls possess the illuminations of faith by knowing that they possess them / without distinguishing them except through their song / namely in times of need / when one requires them for speaking / for writing / or for making use of them; and one becomes aware then that one has them / without having previously thought that one had them: just as birds remain hidden / and do not reveal themselves except through their song.

God commands these birds / that they should grow and multiply. They grow into the eternities. Not according to the knowledge of the one who possesses them: because such things are either shut away and hidden in the waters / or they soar in the air / yes, even in the very highest air / so that one loses sight of them down here. The beginning and the end of this fifth state make up the fifth day or stage of the inward Christian.

<column-break/>

### 24. And GOD said: Let the earth bring forth living souls according to their kind! Cattle / creeping things / and wild animals of the earth / according to their kind. And it happened so.
### 25. And

Just as God brought the fish and birds out of the water / so according to chapter 2, verse 19, He also let birds / and here on the sixth day primarily the animals / which like the former are also living souls / come forth in three kinds from the earth as their element. Therefore, they must also return to this, their earthly element / and thus perish / once they have served for the benefit of mankind. Thus God made the wild animals: (as the word <term>Chäjah</term> <note>Hebrew: *chayyah*, meaning a living thing or wild beast.</note> signifies / when it is joined with <term>Behemah</term> <note>Hebrew: *behemah*, usually referring to large quadrupeds or domesticated cattle.</note>:) not that their nature was initially wild and cruel; which arose after the Fall: but that they would gladly dwell in their freedom in the forests. The cattle or tame animals were to be of a quiet and social nature. And the creeping things were also to come forth in great numbers: among which there were surely no pests at that time / which later came forth as a plague from the rotting of creatures because of sin. Psalm 105:30, 31, 34, 35. David also praises this day's work in the wise order / which is to be found among the creatures, Psalm 104:18, 20, 22. / and also rouses these five kinds of living souls to the praise of God in Psalm 148:7, 10. / as part of the fifth and sixth day's work: and so also the first day's work / the heavens in the height together with the angels and all its host; v. 1, 2. the second / the upper waters and the lower under the firmament / from whence fire / hail / snow / vapor and storm winds / arise; v. 4–6, 8. the third / the mountains / hills and trees; v. 9. the fourth / sun and moon and all shining stars; v. 3. and so the conclusion of the sixth / man / in his various gender / age and station; v. 11, 12. and finally His people and His saints / who are nearest to Him. v. 14.

But it does not only behave this way externally / but / just as the external earth is nothing other than a figure and pre-

---

figuration of our heart / as the internal earth; so we find that very same animal kingdom there as well: which is best revealed to us in true knowledge. For there are so many stirrings and movements / inclinations and desires / that everything in the heart lives and moves / as the seat of life. There is joy / there is love / there is hope / there is longing / and other subservient offspring of the heart. And what are these but the cattle and the animals created in the human earth / for the use and service of man and his spirit? Only 

When the highest part of the soul reaches the very highest peak of the most secret sciences / and the fifth day is in its fulfillment / it also seems to the soul that it is no longer attached to the earth; (for in these last days one no longer speaks of the earth / but only of light / knowledge / desire and of love:) namely / when it seems / as if the soul were sunken into a sea of life and into a perfect renunciation of everything earthly: then the soul becomes rightly dismayed / when it sees all kinds of animals coming forth upon its earth / which suppress the soul / and nourish themselves with the beautiful green grass / with which it had adorned itself. Yes, where it had seen itself upon the throne of God / it is now the footstool of the animals. Oh, what a great difference there is between this and the previous state! Nevertheless, God has ordered both of these contrary states in this way. As yet, the soul does not perceive the use of these things: rather, the animals seem to defile the earth / and to take away a part of its beauty; although they are actually its greatest ornament. For these animals are even more noble than the herbs / which previously adorned the earth / and have now become the animals' food. This is the state of man / when it pleases God to raise him to the highest peak of perfection: when He withdraws the beauties / which He has placed in him / from his eyes for a time / in order to let him see only earthly and animal effects. Meanwhile, these are nonetheless living and life-giving effects. The earth / which is the lower part / must also bring forth effects of life. Were then / one might ask / all these plants / with which it was adorned, not ensouled? It is true / they had a growing life / but not a feeling life. This is that life / which is to be imprinted into the inner soul: and indeed no longer for evil / but for good. For here the sensation is given to glorify God. Since nothing is so small and so poor in us / which cannot and should not give some glorification to its God. Such a person now / who for a long time has been unfeeling / is full of wonder that he becomes sensitive again: and this estranges him all the more / because he thought / he had been deprived of his feeling forever. Meanwhile, he must indeed become sensitive again: but his sensation will subsequently be so purified / that he will make use of it not against the will of his Creator / but within that very will.

<margin>(a) Acts 10:14.</margin>
Thus all kinds of animals are created upon the earth. There are predatory and creeping animals. What! should this power of imagination / which previously presented nothing but pleasant / shining / and holy things / this spirit which was filled with such high sciences / find itself full of creeping and dirty animals? Would he not rather say with Peter: (a) I will not do it! I have never eaten anything unclean or common? Yet it was answered to him: Call nothing unclean / what the LORD has cleansed! That is: These things are good / as they proceeded from their Creator; and only our impurity alone defiles them. God makes use of the annoyance which these things awaken in us / to clear out of us everything that is still to be found of the impure in sensuality / so that it may gradually become more spiritual: and He cleanses us / while it appears that He defiles us.

<meta>This page continues the mystical and allegorical commentary on the first chapter of Genesis. The previous page discussed the creation of birds and fish on the fifth day, interpreting them as types of spiritual illuminations and thoughts within the human soul. This page moves into the sixth day: the creation of land animals and the crowning creation of humanity in the image of the Trinity.</meta>

->### Ch. I. The First Book of Moses.<-

## 25. And God made the wild beasts of the earth after their kind / and the cattle after their kind / and every creeping thing of the earth after its kind. And God saw that it was good.

Among these animals, there was also no harmful / predatory / or poisonous creature. For they had nothing but all kinds of green herbs for their nourishment. v. 30. They had not yet tasted blood; the earth was not yet cursed for man's sake; everything stood in perfect divine blessing and love: for adversity / wrath / and bitterness or contraction <note>The author uses "Herbigkeit" (astringency/bitterness), a term often found in Jakob Böhme’s mystical philosophy to describe a quality of divine or natural tension.</note> / were not yet there; and thus no corruption was yet to be felt.

The order of Wisdom is noteworthy in this regard / that the **inner animals** of man were not set to live and walk in man’s heavens; they are ordered neither into the mind nor the will / but their designated dwelling place is in the human heart / in the human earth / to come forth from there and to live therein. There are both wild animals there / lions / bears / wolves / and the like; namely fiery and angry qualities / harsh movements of wrath and zeal / which could become predatory animals: as well as tame horses and fine donkeys / to ride upon / and to guide / govern / and use for one's service according to one's pleasure and free will.

The domestic animals represent our sensory nature: which is very uncomfortable for us / when it revolts against its Creator. But it is also very useful / when it is entirely subject to the one / who made it. Everything in us / when it remains in the order / in which it was created; is good: and can be corrupted by nothing except through the abuse of sin. When these animals came from the hand of God / everything / that was in them / was useful and pleasant: in that they were entirely subject to man / as long as he remained in the order created for him. But they only became contrary to him / because he himself revolted against God. The rebellion of our spirit also brings about the rebellion of our body. But God / whose goodness is infinite / makes use of the uprising of the body against the spirit / in order to make the spirit submissive to Him. And as soon as the spirit is in full obedience to God / the flesh becomes immediately subject to it. Therefore God saw that it was good: because it was highly useful to man for his **annihilation** <note>In this context, "Vernichtigung" refers to the mystical process of self-negation or humbling of the ego before God.</note> / humiliation / and contrition.

One might well wonder / why such states and paths are ascribed to man / before he was created. But one will / if one only pays attention to two things / understand it. The first is / that (as already said) nothing occurred in the macrocosm / which does not also take place in every soul. Thus all paths / which God made use of in the macrocosm / also proceed in man according to the order of his conversion to grace. The other is / that everything that happened in the innocence of the creature before the creation of man / as the one who corrupted such things / proceeds again in this man / so that through grace he might be placed back into the innocence restored more abundantly through the Redeemer. Therefore we find / that / just as the world had 7 ages until its completion / so man has 7 ages of grace / which correspond to the innocence of nature: which when they have been fulfilled in man / make him innocent through grace to such a degree / as is possible in the world. One need have no doubt about this. Because / as St. Paul says / the gift does not behave in the same way as the sin. For since by the sin of one many died / much more has God's grace and gift abounded to many through the grace of one / who is Jesus Christ. Thus / since the redemption of Jesus Christ was much more abundant / it has given back more to man / than sin had robbed from him.

When man has come this far / namely to the restoration of the image of God in him; then his previous corrupted image is entirely set right again. What then is this image of God? It is none other than Jesus Christ / who / as the living image of his Father / was pleased / to express and form himself entirely in man. From this now the purpose of creation and redemption is to be understood. God created everything for man / but man for Himself. And just as God created man after everything else / as the end of all creatures; so also before and after man there was nothing but God. Man was the end of all the rest: but he had no other end than God.

<sig>B 2</sig>

<column-break/>

## 26. And God said: Let us make man in our image / after our likeness / that they may rule over the fish of the sea / and over the birds of the heavens / and over the cattle / and over the whole earth / and over every creeping thing that creeps upon the earth!

## 27. And

Man was the conclusion of the works of God / and therefore of such dignity / that he was created not by way of a command / like the other six days' works / but from the counsel of the Holy Trinity and through the working of the Divine Majesty: therefore he should recognize from the dignity of his first constitution / how much he owed to his Creator; in that the same bestowed upon him such a great preference of dignity immediately in creation; so that he might love the Creator all the more fervently / the more wonderfully he could understand himself to be created by Him. And this counsel was then a revelation of the eternal counsel and purpose that God had / to express His image one day in such creatures: and since now the time had appeared / to put such a thing into work; so the Holy Trinity wished to encourage and prepare itself for this work / for the sake of which all other creatures had been created: therefore the dominion over the same was also handed over to man / to use them for the benefit granted to the creatures by God.

**God said)** By Himself / to Himself / out of Himself / through Himself / with and from Himself / in Himself / out of free will and desire to manifest Himself in creatures.

**Us)** As in Wisdom 11:7. <note>The author likely refers to the Wisdom of Solomon, though the verse citation may vary by edition.</note> God does not speak after the manner of great lords / who speak of themselves in the plural number / as some Jews claim. For in the first 3 monarchies one did not speak so. Also Rabbi Aben-Esra <note>Abraham ibn Ezra (c. 1089–1167), a distinguished Jewish scholar and biblical commentator.</note> himself testifies / that such a manner of speaking is indeed common in the Arabic / but not the Hebrew language. The Holy Spirit does not maintain such pulpit-epic courtesy. So also the Holy Scripture does not recognize this way of speaking: Luther writes very well on this passage. But it must have happened often / <margin>(a) Question 10 on Genesis.</margin> as Theodoret <note>Theodoret of Cyrus (c. 393–457), an influential theologian and bishop of the Early Church.</note> likewise well notes / and especially when He gave the law on Mount Sinai. Why does He not also speak there: "We are your God" etc.?

There is, however, more than one Creator. Ecclesiastes 12:1. The Holy Trinity is included in the word **God** / in the phrase **God said** / and in the word **us**. Where something is spoken / there is the Speaker / the Word that is spoken / and the Spirit of the mouth. The entire Trinity is occupied in the making of the microcosm <note>The "small world," referring to man.</note> and the macrocosm; and indeed in a very special and exceptional way with man. With most other creatures it was only: "God said; Let there be!" and so it was. Of heaven and earth it was said; "God created them": Of sun and moon; "God made the two great lights": But here it is said alone quite gloriously and pompously: **Let us make a man after our image and after our likeness!** Over no creature did God Himself take counsel in this way / as over us: of none did He resolve / to make the same after His image and likeness: none also bears the image of the Holy Trinity in itself but man: How much must depend upon man / because the entire most holy Trinity moved and manifested itself so specially at his origin! Oh, if everyone always considered / how highly man was and still is esteemed before God because of his noble origin; he would deal much better and more carefully both with himself and with other people / than mostly happens! One would not so insult and revile his high origin and beginning / but would show himself according to the same.

## 27. And GOD created man in his own image / in the image of GOD created he him : he created them a male and a female.

---

After some deliberation, GOD created human nature / and adorned it with his image / so that it should occupy that place / and through humility / obedience / praise / love and reverence toward him / adorn and maintain that position / which the evil spirits had lost through their malicious conduct. <note>The author refers to the common mystical belief that humans were created to fill the void in the celestial hierarchy left by the fallen angels.</note>

Foremost, GOD created man in his image and in his form : which is repeated again and again in verse 27 / in order to present to us the importance of this mystery / so that we might explore the knowledge of it by calling upon the Holy Spirit. Enlightened souls / both among the ancients and the moderns / have viewed it thus—specifically in two treatises (a) published in our days—that because man could not be formed directly according to the pure Godhead / he was created according to the image of the **Firstborn of all creatures** <note>original: "Erstgebohrnen vor allen Creaturen"</note>, Colossians 1:15. This is the Son of GOD / who assumed heavenly humanity before the foundation of the world / and appeared in the same to the believers / especially to Jacob. Genesis 32:24, 28. And so Adam, in his first origin, bore the image of the Heavenly / which was afterwards extinguished / and the image of the Earthly / though still within the grace of GOD / took its place; which is discussed in Chapter 2. See 1 Corinthians 15:49. Nevertheless, the Triune GOD himself / as Father, Son, and Spirit / was reflected in man in a manner believable to reason. Of this, some image of the Trinity may still be found in the soul after the Fall / as the soul / the understanding, and the will / or / as others state it / the understanding / the will / and the memory / are one in essence and yet distinct : However, these are not separate subsistences <note>A theological term for distinct persons or individual existences within one essence.</note> / and all unconverted people also present such an image / though they do not for that reason carry the true likeness of GOD in and upon themselves.

<margin>
(a) *The Mystery of the Firstborn of all Creatures* <note>original: "Das Geheimniß des Erstgebohrnen aller Creaturen"</note> : the first dedicated to the King / the second to the Queen of Prussia; both printed at Frankfurt in the year 1711.
(b) Johannes Reuchlin. book 1. *On the Art of the Kabbalah* <note>original Latin: "de arte Kabbal."</note> p. 638. and following.
(c) Buddeus, *Introduction to the History of Hebrew Philosophy* <note>original Latin: "introd. ad hist. Philos. Ebr."</note> num. 52.
</margin>

How the ancient Kabbalists <note>Jewish mystics; Christian scholars of this era often studied "Christian Kabbalah" to find hidden meanings in the Bible.</note> also present a threefold creation of man from the history of creation / and thus man as threefold or triune / and conclude such from the different expressions of Moses; can be read extensively in their works (b). A learned man (c) has recently summarized the sense of the whole matter thus: "The lovers of Mosaic philosophy teach / that man is composed of 3 "parts: namely body / soul and spirit. "The body / they say / we have from the elements / like the animals: "the soul or breath and inhalation from the spirit of the world / "just like those: but the spirit or the mind is from GOD.

Furthermore, GOD created him according to his likeness: namely that this heavenly man should also have an immortal spirit / which stood in the truth / and thus in the perfect knowledge of his Creator / and then also in righteousness and holiness; so that all his thoughts / stirrings, and movements / were holy and righteous from within and without. Thus, the likeness of man to GOD pertains to his essence / and the image pertains more to his form : yet in such a way / that the heavenly body would also have been immortal and incorruptible / although it would still have had to be transformed / in order to reach the constant and greater glory / if he had remained steadfast in the trial of obedience and the unwavering clinging to GOD; then he would have been chosen just like the elect angels and confirmed in his innate glory.

In creating man in his image / GOD impressed into him his image / which was the Word / namely his Son / as he imprinted his Holy Spirit upon him. And just as his delight was to dwell among the children of men : and his Son is the sole object <note>The original "Vorwurff" here means the object toward which an emotion or action is directed.</note> of his pleasure; since he can delight in nothing else but him: (for when GOD has any pleasure in man / it is through his Son:) so it could not be otherwise; he had to create man after his own image / if he were to have pleasure in him; and for that reason, he had to print the image of his Word into him. And this was the end of creation / to imprint in all people the image of the Word / in which the Godhead would be expressed: which could represent it just as a mirror reflects that which is placed before it.

<column-break/>

But since man corrupted this beautiful image through sin / redemption came in between. Because GOD had his pleasure in his Word / he did not want to permit that the people / in whom this image had already been imprinted / should be lost / and at the same time lose forever this image of the Word and the seal of the Godhead: therefore he let his Word set everything right again. For only the Word of GOD could proceed from itself: and no one else but he could do such a thing. Therefore he became man. Just as when a certain object / which is removed from the mirror / can no longer be seen in the mirror / even if it was previously seen therein / as it was still before it / unless it be brought before the mirror again. Therefore JESUS Christ had to come into man / so that man / by never again being able to lose this holy object / would also not lose the image and the sign of the Godhead. This image of GOD is so deeply engraved in man / that he can never lose it again / even if he covers it through sin / disguises it / or even defiles it. And this is precisely what so greatly grieves the great GOD / that man is nevertheless damned for the sake of his sins / and awakens in Him such a desire for the salvation of humanity. Everything that happens in man occurs only / to rediscover and renew this image. And as soon as this is restored / man is once again placed in the state of innocence.

GOD created them / the humans / a male and a female. And yet Eve was not yet there. It is therefore well worth asking / how that can be? And here we must take note of the mystery of the Holy Spirit / who has also been perceived by some believers / ancient and modern / as the heavenly Sophia and Wisdom / who is anointed from eternity / from the beginning / before the beginning of the earth: namely that he / through his divine power / should communicate to all his rational creatures the generative power of other creatures like themselves / in the divine image and likeness. And so the first man was initially created according to both sexes / male and female / in both tinctures <note>A term from alchemy and Böhmean theosophy referring to the essential qualities or spiritual "colors" of a substance; here, the male and female spiritual principles.</note> / just as in GOD all tinctures are undivided / and thus he also bore the image of GOD in this regard. For GOD is a fire / and is also a light / in temperance and sweet unity. According to the former quality, he is called a strong, jealous GOD: but according to the latter, merciful / gracious, and of great kindness; or / as John says / Love. And according to these two qualities, GOD's image showed itself among others in man / as he was created in righteousness and holiness / according to both male and female qualities. The male is fire and wrath: the female is light and love. And just as both qualities are undivided in GOD: so they should also have been and remained undivided in man. Therefore, Holy Scripture expressly testifies here / that man was initially created not in two / but in one person. Just as subsequently / in the separation of the two qualities / the woman was taken out of and from the man. Chapter 2:21-24. Indeed, the great glory and perfection of man consisted initially in such a union of both qualities. For the fire-quality or the masculine did not need to seek the light-quality or the feminine outside of itself / but both were most intimately connected with one another. And when both embraced each other in sweet and pure communion / man had the power / through the movement and strength of the creating Word lying within him / to bring forth an image like himself out of himself / without having need of a preceding animal-like mixing and subsequent painful birth / as is the case now.

And in this impression of the image of the Heavenly / man as male and female would also have drawn this power of generation and birth out of his origin and according to divine order into himself / in order to thus generate and give birth to similar images of the heavenly nature out of himself in great quantity / in such a spiritual manner / which has now remained hidden because of sin / as it now happens by earthly men in an earthly manner. Genesis 5:3. Of which spiritual manner a trace may still be seen in the spiritual birth of the new man / where one also becomes the other's spiritual father and mother.
