18. And **God the Lord** said: It is not good that the man should be alone; I will make him a **helper** who shall be like him.
19. For when **God the Lord** had formed from the earth all kinds of beasts of the field and all kinds of birds of the heavens / then he brought them to the man / to see what he would call them. And

---

God wanted to remind man in this earthly state of his neediness / that he had in some measure departed from God in love / and therefore his solitary state would become unbearable to him. Since everything in creation was good / in that he was both man and woman in a most intimate communion; so it was now not good to leave him alone in this lower earthly hut / separated from his wife in the heavenly image: and so God wished to bring forth his spouse in a similar earthly form as a helper. In order to stir this desire in him all the more / and also to lead him to a clear language / in which he could reveal the thoughts of his heart; he was to proceed / just as God already named some of the most prominent creatures with names / and thus also strive to actually name the remaining creatures with names. In this / as the best naturalist <note>original: "Naturkündiger," meaning one who understands the inner workings of nature</note> he recognized the other creatures according to their innermost essence and properties / he gave an important proof / and gave every animal its name from the deepest insight into its nature / which he thereby presented and described with the most skillful expression.

But if it is asked / in what kind of language this naming occurred / and which language is consequently the oldest of all; one may recognize quite clearly / among other things from the names of the Patriarchs <note>original: "Ertzväter"</note> before the Deluge / which can be explained from no other language than Hebrew / from which they are also derived / that this language was used by Adam and the other Patriarchs. Thus the first man himself is called Adam / because he was formed from earth <note>original: "Adamah," which is the Hebrew word for ground or red earth</note>.

v. 18. (**It is not good**) Necessarily a cause and change must have preceded / something must have happened / why it was not good. For God had indeed created him alone / and placed him in Paradise. And Chapter 1, v. 31 says explicitly: everything was very good. So something else must have come to the good creature of God / who was created alone / whereby it became "not good" to be alone. And what should this be other than the deformation <note>original: "Verbildung," suggesting a loss of the original spiritual form</note> into the animals and their twofold shape and divided properties; and the subsequent inclination / through which he had withdrawn his love from God / and as he saw the creatures around him / and how they loved one another / an inward desire was awakened in him / to also long for something external and creaturely. For this reason God found it good to take Eve out of him / to separate her from him / and to ordain her externally as his helper / in whom he would have his delight / so that he would not let the same go out and break out elsewhere. It was therefore precisely for this reason not good to leave the man alone / who could easily have involved himself with other creatures.

(**make a helper**) God had previously also made him a help / but she was not "before him" <note>meaning external to him</note> so that he might grasp and recognize her with his animal senses; rather she was *in* him. Adam had left this faithful helper in the bridal chamber of his heart / and with his outward-turned senses sought an external animal image for help among the irrational animals / but found no help / which would have been an external object for his now animal-made senses.

Otherwise, this can also be understood of human nature / which God wished to unite with the divine nature in **Jesus Christ** / in the person of the Word / His Son. For since no God could suffer and make satisfaction / and a man was also far too weak to rightfully deserve the redemption of a whole world: so human nature was given to the divine as a helper / in order to achieve the re-

20. And the man gave a name to every cattle and bird of the heavens / and every beast of the field: but for the man / no helper was found who was like him.

demption of the human race perfectly through the God-Man. It is also the image of the communion of Christ and his congregation / which congregation / as a fruitful mother / had to give him many children / as a fruit of his blood; and just like a faithful bride / she had to contribute with him toward her sanctification and salvation.

The power which Adam had over all animals in the state of his innocence is a proof of the subjection of all creatures to man: just as their rebellion against man represents man’s rebellion against God. God leads all animals to Adam / so that he may give them names / which were according to their nature: to show / that he set him as king over the animals as well / as over his powers / senses / and affects <note>emotions or passions</note> / which the innocent man could command without resistance. But sinful man / because he has become subject to his affects / is subject to all others.

Because Adam was the image of **Jesus Christ** / so the animals (which represent the animal part and the inclinations of the mind of man) had to become subject to him in Christ; and the naming belonging to each animal / which Adam gives them / is the testimony / that no one but Jesus Christ alone can make the inclinations of men / which have rebelled through sin / submissive to himself: Just as the birds represent the noblest parts of the soul / its powers / and everything that depends on them. This now could not be restored / except through the grace of the Redeemer.

The Scripture adds / that although Adam / the image of Jesus Christ / had given the animals as well as the birds their proper names / and they were also subject to him as their king / he nevertheless had no helper / who would have been equal to him. This can be understood of Jesus Christ in two ways. Firstly / that although everything was created through him as the eternal Word / and nothing was made without the same / he nevertheless had no helper who was equal to him: because he had only spread his image / or rather the image of his Father / who was the origin and source of all creatures / in the creation of man; but this his image no longer resembled him because of man's corruption. And although human nature in the state of Adam's innocence was a living image of the Word / it was certainly not yet in the perfection as it was in Jesus Christ. Now since God / when he said: *Let us make him a helper who is like him!* aimed at the essential union of the Word and the human nature / which was such a helper that was equal to him / so she should at the same time be such a helper / who should work with him at the redemption of men / which could not be worked without the union of them both / as this was the greatest work of all the works of God. This helper became so similar to him / that out of these two—otherwise very different natures / namely the divine and the human—only one single person became in Jesus Christ.

The second understanding is of Jesus Christ and his Church. Before the Church was born / no helper who was equal to Jesus Christ had been found. But after the Church was formed / she became a true helper of Jesus Christ / and indeed in such a way that she works with him at the salvation of men: in that she has no other will than he has. Could a helper be more similar to him than this holy helper / since she was glorious / without spot / without wrinkle / and without want? But in what way was this helper created?

### Chapter II. The First Book of Moses.

**21. Then GOD the LORD caused a deep sleep to fall upon the man / and he fell asleep; and He took one of his ribs / and closed it up with flesh in its place.**

<margin>Malachi 2:14, 15.</margin>
The creation of the woman is very wonderful and full of mystery; GOD did not wish to create her directly from the earth / but from the man / and specifically from his stronger part, the ribs / which are near the heart. Although here only the physical is mentioned / namely the rib / the flesh and bone; and Adam, according to his desire turned from spirit toward the flesh, recognized only flesh and bone in his Eve: yet the female spirit must also have been separated from Adam at the same time; because it is not read / that GOD breathed a separate, distinct spirit and soul into Eve. Just as here, during a deep sleep, this rib was taken out / the one fundamental origin of fertility separated / and built into a house of heavenly procreative power / which was previously within the man / and afterward indeed outside of him / yet in great union with him in the Image of the Heavenly / created to prevent a greater fall; so it may well be / that in such a sleep / as a sign of weakness and diminished heavenly powers / an exhaustion of the former glorious nature / of which man otherwise knew as little as the holy angels / the <unclear>Adamic?</unclear> <note>original: "araoische," likely a misspelling of "adamische" (Adamic) or "irdische" (earthly)</note> body faded / the heavenly man fell / and an earthly one woke up again. Meanwhile, the man is gladdened / that he sees again a helper in his earthly nature / with whom he could beget a divine seed after his image in chaste union of hearts and bodies.

And concerning the mystery, see Ephesians 5:30-32, where the new man must be born out again into the heavenly image from Christ’s flesh and bones / and that through the power of His divinity / and the spiritual Eve is and will be built from Christ’s side and from His flesh and blood. <margin>John 19:34.</margin>

Whoever, therefore, fears GOD from the heart / and yields himself entirely to His salutary guidance; he receives a true helper like himself / and need not fear / that he will be deceived by an ill-natured woman. Conversely, whoever proceeds according to his own choice without the fear of GOD / and follows the counsel and impulse of his flesh without divine governance; GOD’s wrath lets him find that / which his own false will seeks for his own judgment.

**23. Then the man said: This is at last bone of my bones / and flesh of my flesh! She shall be called Woman <note>original: "Männin," a feminine form of "Mann," mirroring the Hebrew "Ish" and "Ishah"</note> / because she was taken from Man.**

**24. Therefore shall a man leave his father and his mother / and cleave to his wife / and they shall be one flesh.** <gloss>1 Corinthians 6:17</gloss>

**25. And**

---

from His opened side a daughter and a bride / who was so exceedingly beautiful / that nothing could be found in her / which was not pleasing to her Father / who was afterward to become her Bridegroom. The union of Jesus Christ with His Church was so exact / in order to work for the salvation of men with united powers and with the same spirit and will / that / whoever does not belong to His Church / cannot belong to Jesus Christ; and that no one can belong to Jesus Christ / who is not a child of the Church of Christ.

<margin>(a)</margin>
Now, since JESUS Christ was in GOD from the very creation of the world; and all gifts were given to men / after they had need of a Redeemer / in view of the merits of Christ: so the Church was also joined to Him even then / for the rebirth of as many children / as were to be born from the blood of the Redeemer / which in this sense was shed from the beginning of the world / and for the sanctification of all the elect / whom GOD the Father had given to His Son as a gift because of His death.

From the opened side / from the blood and water which flowed from the same / the Church was drawn. This union of Adam and Eve is also the image of the spiritual marriage of souls with Christ JESUS. It happens under the pains of the cross / and not in the sweetness of Mount Tabor <note>Mount Tabor is the traditional site of the Transfiguration, representing spiritual ecstasy versus the suffering of the cross</note>. And this union of souls with their Bridegroom becomes so firm / that Jesus Christ then says: This is flesh of my flesh and bone of my bone. For she even becomes one spirit with the Word / so that she finds nothing but the Word in her. And since she has gone out from Him / she finds herself united with Him without a partition wall / and sees that she has as a husband / Him whom she had as a father. This unity of souls with Jesus Christ is so secret / that / although it is worked in great pain and crucifixions / it nevertheless becomes stronger and stronger through them.

It is written / that GOD gave this woman to Adam. Which indicates / that this unity of the spirit can never be worked by the creature: because it is solely a work of GOD / and not of the human will / which has nothing to do with it except the acceptance and the faithfulness to follow all holy stirrings.

What then must a faithful soul do / to repay that which her Bridegroom has done for her / and to enjoy the joy of the Marriage of the Lamb? She must leave her father and mother / otherwise the spiritual marriage will never be accomplished in her. Who is this father and mother other than the old Adam and the corrupt nature / which one must immediately leave. When one leaves oneself / through self-denial / which works total mortification; then one comes to the Marriage of the Lamb. But one will come to it in no other way. Those, however, who are entirely full of themselves / and who imagine they have reached this spiritual and holy marriage; are deceived beyond measure. And since JESUS Christ had to leave the bosom of His Father / to marry Himself to our nature; do we think / that we can marry ourselves to Him / without leaving ourselves? No: this will not happen in eternity!

# The First Book of Moses. Chapter II.

25. And they were both naked / the man and his wife / and were not ashamed.

There was as yet nothing in them for which they needed to feel shame. For there was nothing else in them but the work of GOD. But GOD’s work is right and praiseworthy. The work of the devil, however / sin and evil desire / brings about a wounded conscience / and thus shame. Thus, man in this his earthly state was initially still in the grace of GOD. Some also concluded from this / that Adam and Eve were not yet fully grown at that time / and as yet knew nothing of procreation. <note>Irenaeus, *Against Heresies*, book 3, chapter 33.</note>

The Christian simplicity of heart / of which the old serpent robbed our first parents / 2 Corinthians 11:3; and still robs their children / is the true nakedness / in which our first parents walked / and yet were not ashamed / until the serpent’s cunning deceived them / and clothed them with fig leaves of knowledge / without the fruit of the spirit and life. In this same garment we walk / until we put on Christ according to the

likeness of His death. For which purpose the LORD afterward clothed our first parents with the skins of dead animals.

This is the state of a soul that has completely abandoned itself. These souls live in such a forgetfulness of themselves / that they are not ashamed of their spiritual nakedness; namely / the extreme poverty of spirit / and the deep detachment <note>original: "Abgekehrtheit" — a technical term in mysticism for turning away from the self and the world to face God alone</note> / into which they have fallen: because they, being entirely swallowed up and lost in GOD / can neither see it nor think of it. This is then a state of transformation / which can rightly be called the state of innocence.

Various traces of a skill and diligence in their natural actions and sensory-soul life / which they possess / are also perceived in the animals: in which GOD's omnipotence and wisdom must be recognized. ### Chapter III. The First Book of Moses (Genesis).

2. Then the woman said to the serpent: We may eat of the fruits of the trees of the garden;
3. But of the fruit of the tree that is in the midst of the garden, God has said: You shall not eat of it, and you shall not touch it, lest you die!

---

To human reason, all these accounts appear strange and wondrous—that God would make and give everything for the good of man, and yet withhold and exempt a single piece. But according to faith and the true spiritual sense, pure, unspeakable wisdom lies hidden beneath them.

We must not imagine this tree in such a crude and fleshly way, as if it were merely a simple plant, without any further significance. It was indeed an external creature, but its foundation and purpose were spiritual, and it belonged properly to the spiritual realm, which permeated the visible world and revealed itself through it.

The tree was, as the earliest Christian teachers recognized, set for the exploration, practice, and testing of Adam—specifically of his obedience and disobedience, as Gregory of Nazianzus <note>original: "Gregorius Nazianzenus," a 4th-century Archbishop and theologian known as "The Theologian."</note> says. God wished to put him to the test, to see if he would persist and remain voluntarily in his simple love, or if he would enter into and involve himself in something different and foreign through the power of his will. For Adam’s heart was meant to hang upon God alone, and all his thoughts and desires were to be directed toward this, his highest good, alone. Therefore, he was to remain in a holy simplicity <note>The German *Einfalt* implies a single-minded, pure devotion, often contrasted with the "multiplicity" of worldly distractions.</note>, wherein he thought of nothing else, nor sought anything with desire, other than GOD.

Even though the knowledge of good might have been permissible for him in itself, it nevertheless became a hindrance because of this primary purpose: because he turned toward something else, if only for a moment, so to speak. For this reason, the Lord prohibited this tree and its consumption.

<margin>v. 3.</margin> Eat not of it) This prohibition from God still contains within it all of God's will for mankind. For all of God’s commandments are comprised in this: Do not eat of it! or: Do not let yourself lust! For at its foundation, this is the same as what God constantly speaks and repeats in the conscience: Love me alone! Do not turn away from me into other things! Do not love what I am not, which cannot satisfy you! Remain with your desire and willpower in me, your best part!

God requires nothing more or further from man, if only he would take heed of this. All blessedness is contained within it. For to love God is the highest blessedness. That is the only thing He wants to have from us and also to give to us.

In this law, which was given to Adam, are given all the commandments that later came forth through Moses.

<column-break/>

4. Then the serpent said to the woman: You shall by no means die the death!
5. For God knows that on the day you eat of it, your eyes will be opened, and you will be like God, and know what is good and evil.
6. And

---

<margin>v. 4. 5.</margin> By no means—but) This word of seduction and false persuasion is still used by the serpent today. For example; the Apostle says: *If we die with him, we shall also live with him.* Romans 6:8; 2 Timothy 2:11, 12. "No," says the serpent, "only believe, and you shall live." Because Holy Scripture testifies everywhere that nothing unclean shall enter the holy city, and the serpent fears that many or all might purify themselves, she persuades all too many that it is a superfluous work, an unnecessary labor; that Christ has long since worked the cleansing of our sins; that it is impossible to be cleansed from them.

God knows etc.) Thus, in temptations, the truth is cunningly interwoven and laced with deceit, so that at first glance (especially when the affections and passions are already tangled in disorder) it is difficult to notice the fraud. It is an undeniable truth: *God knows, etc.* For God knows all things. No less was there a truth in the claim that their eyes would be opened. Just as it was truly not without truth that they would recognize good and evil in a subsequent "mixed state" <note>The author refers to the state of fallen humanity where good and evil are perceived as separate and conflicting, rather than seeing only the unified Good of God.</note>. And this reason likely awakened the desire for knowledge most of all, but did not make its true nature known to her.

The devils or damned spirits knew well from themselves and from their own experience what kind of effect and knowledge would follow from it; as those who had also tasted of the testing-tree of the knowledge of evil, and were thereby deceived and tempted. Had the devils never touched, handled, tasted, or eaten the fruit that grew on this evil tree, they would never have known any evil in their own spirits, any more than the angels of light who remained standing and never had any union or fellowship with this tree, nor tasted of its fruits. But because they lusted after a change, such a change happened to them, and the quality or form of the evil darkness wound itself like a wicked serpent around the neck of their will-spirit: and that is properly the cunning serpent or the serpent-kind. This cunning quality, this subtle spirit, is then called the Seducer; who is always busy tempting, presenting, and introducing or sneaking himself in. And when man occupies himself too much with created things, and does not keep his thoughts constantly turned to God, as is right; then the devil gets the opportunity and power to constantly breathe into him the lust for the earthly fruit of the forbidden tree.

From this we may now recognize who is the first cause of all evil, sin, and misery in the first Adamite man and all his descendants. God, who is the highest good, cannot possibly be the author of evil. The source of all goodness, all salvation, and happiness cannot possibly be the author of misery and anguish, nor consequently of the miserable, wretched, lost state of man. A good tree cannot bring forth evil fruit. The origin must therefore be sought and found elsewhere and outside of God: because in God’s nature there is nothing but eternal goodness and eternal love.

Who else can be the cause of it but the loathsome devil, who sowed sin into man through a pouring out of his nature into Adam's nature. Therefore the Scripture calls him a Tempter, as he tempted the second Adam <note>Jesus Christ.</note>, just as he did the first. He is called a serpent to indicate his subtlety and the creeping of his nature into the mind, the will, and the senses of the first man; whose will was not forced to sin, but acted freely. For the devil was only a persuading cause, who crept with his evil seed through the door of the senses into the man's mind and will, from which seed grew the first movements and inclinations of Adam’s will—the first thought or intent of his mind and will to look upon the forbidden tree and eat from it.

And for this very reason, we must not lay more upon the devil than is his due, nor make him the sole cause and only author of all evil, sin, and misery. He truly can do nothing without our will. If we do not agree and follow him, then all his arrows and murderous plots are in vain. If Eve had not opened her desire and the longing of her will—in which she still stood free toward evil and good—he would never have gained an entrance into her. Had she immediately suppressed the first stirrings and enticements, in the power that she certainly had from God, she would have remained who she was. But it stands sorrowfully written:

### The First Book of Moses. Chapter III.

6. And the woman saw that the tree was good for food, and that it was pleasant to the eyes, and that the tree was desirable to make one wise: so she took of its fruit, and ate, and gave also to her husband with her, and he ate.

<margin>The Devil, as it were, did not want to be believed on his bare word alone, but points to experience itself, so that one might investigate the fruit impartially. But it is precisely in this that his game is won.</margin>

<margin>Here began the love of the world and for created things to arise in the heart of man: the lust of the flesh, in the craving for food; the lust of the eyes, in the delight of the sight; and the pride of life, in the desire for earthly cleverness. <note>original: "1. <margin>Saw.) As soon as man allows his senses to wander toward what is forbidden, the fall is not far off. Through these "windows of the soul," death falls into its innermost parts. Therefore, let everyone watch what they look upon and what they seek in the world.</margin>

<margin>Eve would not have touched the forbidden tree if she had not first looked at it out of carelessness. Therefore, we must consider with what strict governance we should tame our senses against unseemly things, seeing as we are mortal; for even the mother of all living things fell into death because of this.</margin>

<margin>O, guard your heart with all diligence, even through the external senses, which carry such charming images to the mind and thereby lure and awaken it to desire!</margin>

<margin>Tree.) The natural man imagines only a common, natural tree with green leaves: But the Spirit certainly points in this whole history to something further, and presents us in this image—as elsewhere, so also here—with a figurative tree, which represents nothing other than the spirit of this world, which to this day is still an earthly spirit, and therefore brings forth no other fruit, making earthly whoever eats of it.</margin>

<margin>Human learning outside the anointing of the Holy Spirit is the true Tree of Knowledge, which is beautiful and lovely from the outside and has the appearance of making one wise: but it brings death to many and makes them blind, although they think they become seeing through it and already are so.</margin>

<margin>This text should indeed show us that knowledge mostly belongs to the forbidden tree. But why? <margin>Make wise) Adam and Eve wanted to be wise "in the devil's name"; and that is still the plague today: that we want to be wise in the devil's name, says Luther (a).</margin>

7. Then the eyes of both of them were opened, and they became aware that they were naked; and they wove fig leaves together and made themselves aprons.

<insert>These poor deceived ones were put to shame because their eyes were opened through sin, and they thus became aware of a strange form within themselves and saw that they were naked. This they now sought to hide, as it was unbearable to themselves, because they had to appear before GOD. And since the illuminating and sanctifying Spirit had departed from them, and they were thus robbed of their spiritual clothing, lust gained dominion in their members, which then incites to sin. <margin>Fruit) Most insist that they were figs: because these are the sweetest fruit; because the tree also immediately bears both good and bad, or ripe and unripe fruit; and furthermore, our first parents covered themselves with fig leaves immediately after the Fall. <margin>Gave to her husband.) This is the nature of evil: that it powerfully and heatedly seeks to propagate and multiply itself. In sin itself lies this addiction or desire to always make another a partaker of evil so that one is not alone. Satan passed his evil on to Eve, Eve to Adam, etc. Therefore, it is good to cast off all evil or even suspicious company and not to engage in discourses or other opportunities that could lead to evil.</margin>

<margin>And he ate) This was the deadly bite, the cruel mouthful, which introduced earthly life, and through this further the life of sin, and finally the anxious fire-life of hell, along with the eternal curse, death, and damnation. She gives it to her husband, who represents the upper part. He accepts it, she tastes it: and by this very act, he withdraws his will from the will of GOD and His dominion, departs from his blindest surrender, and commits a factual sin.</margin>

### Chapter III. The First Book of Moses.

### 8. And they heard the voice of the LORD God walking in the garden in the cool of the day. Then Adam and his wife hid themselves from
---
By this, they commit two great errors. First, that after the fall they distance themselves even further from God, in that they are ashamed of themselves. Second, that they wish to cover themselves through their own artifice and imagine they can hide through their own cleverness—though such things consist only in the mere practice of minor virtues, resembling weak leaves. To distance oneself from God after the fall is the same as departing from **yieldedness** <note>original: "Gelassenheit" — a central concept in German mysticism meaning a state of letting go of self-will to be open to God</note> in order to submit oneself to human guidance. But God, whose goodness is infinite, seeks such people, calls them back from their turning away, and asks them where they are and what has become of them.

God wishes to judge this apostasy of man while the deed is fresh: namely, that He first hears the man out, and does not immediately condemn him according to His omnipotence and omniscience. Thus, this interrogation did not have the ultimate goal of casting man away entirely, but rather of calling him back again. And so God proved Himself to be <margin>1 Peter 4:19</margin> the **faithful Creator**, who wished to prove His goodness not only in creation, but also in mercy, preservation, restoration, and the setting right of His fallen creature. This interrogation happened toward evening, when the sun’s rays diminish and the air therefore becomes cool. <margin>Song of Solomon 2:17, 4:6</margin> Just as toward the evening of the world, the last great interrogation of all people will be held. And this strong wind went before as a sign of the divine presence, as also happened with Elijah <margin>1 Kings 19:11-12</margin> and with Eliphaz. <margin>Job 4:16</margin> And so the Lord walked in the garden as if in His own house, to prove thereby His gracious presence with His noble creature, man. See Deuteronomy 23:15, Revelation 2/1. <margin>Deuteronomy 23:15, Revelation 2:1</margin>

**The voice of God)** This was a sound of wrath, which penetrated Adam’s conscience like a strong thunder, which confused him and woke him up so that he crept away. Although, certainly, God’s compassion and mercy were also mixed in with it, since it was primarily aimed at Adam's restoration. Yet man first had to be terrified and convinced of the zeal of his Creator against apostasy.

As often as you perceive God’s earnestness and wrath against sin, either in your own conscience or in others, through anxiety, terror, fear, or even external punishments; so often believe for certain that it is God’s voice, that God is thereby expressing His wrath and earnestness—how He can suffer nothing evil, by virtue of His justice.

How few may have yet experienced what a terror God’s voice can strike, how His threatening and wrath penetrate marrow and bone, and so affect and consume the sinner that he feels God is speaking in wrath against him! But those who have experienced it testify of such a voice. <margin>Psalm 29:7</margin>

O, God has means and power enough to cry out to the **secure sinner** <note>Meaning a sinner who feels falsely safe or complacent in their sin</note> and to call into his innermost being with the voice of His justice! Let no one dare to think that God will keep silent and be just like a sinner!

Whoever is wise, let him not wait for the wrath-voice of God, but rather follow His voice of grace and friendly enticement. For He is only too glad when we allow ourselves to be softened by love, and do not first wait for His compulsion and plagues.

Ah, how many a person must first experience God’s terrible wrath-voice on their deathbed, or even after death, how it penetrates the soul like a lightning bolt, so that all their sins first truly dawn on them and appear before them, and they must hear Him whom they did not want to hear in this world!

If you say: "Well, where then can I hear the voice of God? I do not notice God saying anything to me!" Then know that:

You can clearly perceive God’s voice in two ways. Namely, inwardly in your heart, and then also outwardly in His law and Word.

God’s voice is nothing other than the expression of His holy will—what He demands of you and what He wants to give you. That is indeed written into your heart by nature. What is it that often stirs in your heart, that holds your sins before you, that drives you toward the good? Is it not the

voice of God? What accuses you in your thoughts and pronounces judgment upon you for disobedience? What makes you so anxious about it that you often do not know where to turn?

Furthermore, everything that you hear, read, or otherwise think and remember concerning God and His will is God’s own voice. Therefore, hold no word as insignificant: God’s good counsel for you is always hidden behind it.

O, do not neglect a single little word when the Holy Spirit impresses God’s will upon your heart! It is God’s voice that then resounds in your heart. If you let it pass by, who knows if you will be so blessed again! Gather everything up like pearls that wish to promote your salvation!

**In the cool)** Since the first love had been abandoned, and the fire of divine love had grown cold.

God seeks man immediately when the heat of temptation is over and the cool time now comes, when His wrath cools down.

**Hid themselves)** It is always a suspicious state for our soul when it is not engaged in a steady approaching and penetrating into God, but rather withdraws from Him or even hides itself. Either unbelief and mistrust, or else actual disobedience, must have awakened and ruled in the heart. He who does evil hates the light. Man constantly needs God, and when he thus withdraws from God, it is certainly not right with his soul. Rather, who told these two to creep under the trees other than their false heart, which now wanted to withdraw from God for a long time?

The miserable creature acts so foolishly. First, it leaves its faithful God with disobedience. Afterward, when it should hurry back to Him and seek counsel from Him, it runs away from Him even further and hides. O, the wretched blindness into which nature has fallen! Man has now become so mad and foolish that he still thinks his running will help him, and that God will not already find him. <margin>Psalm 139</margin>

If you say: "That does not concern me; I do not run from God; I pray, and go to church, etc." then know:

As often and as much as you make excuses for your sins, or deny, cover, and hush them up; as much as you cannot tolerate God’s light and Word in your conscience: so much do you run from God. For all denying, hypocrisy, and pretense is a fleeing and hiding from God. Amidst all such falsehood, however, you can just as well go to church and pray in your fashion, etc.

See, God is always going after your soul and seeking to grip and seize you in your conscience. You are often caught and snatched like a thief in your wrongdoing by His Holy Spirit, who punishes and reminds you of it on the spot in the midst of the sin. If you then do not stand firm before God and His judgment and accept His chastening, you flee from Him with your will as much as you are able. You cannot indeed escape, but you would like to. Therefore, God takes the will for the deed. You can see that clearly in Adam.

**Called Adam)** The word of reconciliation. Here it meant: Remember from where you have fallen, and repent! <margin>Revelation 2:5</margin> Or the deepest mercy of God, which called the man back again! God did not do that for Lucifer.

God Himself must make the beginning of man's conversion if He does not want to let the creature perish entirely. Men would likely remain far from Him forever if He did not fetch them out and seek them.

Chrysostom <note>John Chrysostom (c. 347–407), an influential Early Church Father known for his preaching</note> presumes that God asked Adam for this reason: so that his sins and falsehood might become manifest.

God saw Adam clearly, but Adam did not see the Lord: his mind and desire were directed toward the creature. Therefore, God had to cry out after him.

This voice or inquiry still resounds by its power even now within us all. How often God asks the soul:

**Where are you?** In the heavenly image, or in the shape of a beast? How do you stand?

If you wish, O man, to escape the angry questioning of God, then learn well to ask yourself without hypocrisy, or to examine your conscience. Ask your "Old Adam" <note>A theological term for the fallen, sinful nature of man</note> diligently: Adam, where are you? How are you living? Are you also crucified with your lusts and desires? Or do you keep going further and further in your apostasy?

It explores the psychological shift from childlike innocence to "slavish fear" and the theological concept of the "garments of light" versus "animalistic flesh."</meta>

<header>The First Book of Moses. Chapter III.</header>

**10. And he said: I heard Your voice in the garden, and I was afraid, because I am naked; and I hid myself.**

He is afraid to appear before GOD because he is naked. This is the false humility of those who withdraw from self-denial <note>original: "Verläugnung" — in this context, the spiritual practice of denying one's ego to submit to God's will</note> when they have fallen, under the pretext that they are not fit to remain in it, nor to have such communion with GOD.

But it must eventually come to the point that man must come before GOD’s face and deal and speak with Him, however long it may take. Therefore, do not withdraw yourself from GOD your Creator, and do not imagine that you will never be allowed to present yourself to Him, or give an account, or that He will not come near you and take hold of you, or urge you to conversation and dealings with Him!

Indeed, it must certainly come to pass that you will be drawn into GOD’s judgment and into His holy presence before His face, whether it happens sooner or later; and you must perceive and suffer GOD’s inquiries and judgments in your conscience, and must give an account of all your doing and leaving undone.

Will you not have to deal and speak with GOD then? Will He not ask you about your affairs? What man will be so clever, so powerful, so cunning, that he could withdraw himself from such dealings with GOD?

What then remains, but that we allow ourselves to be moved by good words in good time, and gradually accustom ourselves to step into GOD’s holy presence and to judge ourselves, and thus settle our affairs with Him in good time, before He is forced to speak with us in anger.

*I was afraid.* From where did this fear come to Adam, who was previously GOD’s bosom child <note>original: "Schooßkind" — a term of endearment for a favored or pampered child, suggesting the intimate relationship Adam had with God before the Fall</note>, and could expect every good thing from the Father? A primary change must indeed have occurred, so that all previous intimacy and close correspondence with GOD was transformed into such great timidity.

The whole of creation was, as it were, shaken and moved by the cruel apostasy. Adam felt this and sensed it with terror in his soul; because the wrath in nature was stirred, and his own being fell into disorder, and his attributes into confusion.

And why is it still the case that people generally have more slavish fear toward GOD than love, trust, and access? Certainly from nothing other than an evil conscience. <margin>Book of Wisdom 17:10-11</margin>

But where does the evil conscience come from? Did GOD create it in man, or give him such a timid, suspicious heart? Oh no! That comes precisely from sin and from the falling away.

Is this not a powerful proof of divine justice against the atheistic, mocking nature that would like to believe it need not fear GOD? Oh, how the most cruel tyrants must tremble and shake before GOD! How all the braggarts and boasters let their pride fall as soon as their conscience wakes up! They cannot dampen it with all their power and pleasure, no matter what they try.

If you do not wish to fear or tremble before GOD one day like a thief before a judge, then learn to respect and revere Him properly in good time, like a child respects his father. Let the Holy Spirit place you in a holy awe of Him all your life in all your affairs; then you need not experience the fear and despair of the damned. Choose for yourself which is best.

*For I am naked.* Yes, indeed he was naked. Oh, how Adam briefly displays the entire abyss of the fall here by confessing his nakedness! Previously, Adam was clothed with light and clarity, and permeated by GOD’s radiance and glory. All of this departed from him at the fall, and thus the coarse, animalistic nature <note>original: "viehische Wesen" — referring to the lower, physical nature of man that became dominant after the loss of spiritual glory</note> broke through, naked and bare. For Adam only put on this coarse earthly flesh after the fall, as the Ancients well recognized (a).

There the fallen man stands before GOD like a worm stripped by murderers, having nothing left but his horrors!

But it does not only concern Adam. The Spirit of GOD generally pronounces the judgment upon all men: They lack the glory. <margin>Romans 3:23</margin>

Whoever then has a shudder for such nakedness of his, and would not wish to be found bare one day before GOD’s judgment; let him look around in good time for another adornment, the wedding garment, which is the new righteousness of JESUS Christ, which faith puts upon the soul; and let him be diligent to put on Christ himself in earnest desire for his salvation: so he will not be cast out among those who must howl and cry in their nakedness.

(a) <note>Latin reference: Gregory of Nazianzus, Oration 1, and from him, the commentator on John Climacus in The Ladder of Paradise, Step 29, number 7.</note>

<column-break/>

**11. And He said: Who told you that you were naked? Have you not eaten of the tree of which I commanded you that you should not eat?**

**12. Then Adam said: The woman whom You gave to be with me, she gave me of the tree, and I ate.**

**13. Then the LORD God said to the woman: Why have you done this? And the woman said: The serpent deceived me, and I ate.**

**14. Then**

Man discovered not only his blindness and evil conscience when he wanted to hide from the omnipresent and omniscient GOD and conceal his disobedience: but he also brought the perversity of his heart to light. When the guilt was presented to him, which he could not deny, he wanted to attribute the cause of it to GOD, who had given him such a helper who had given him the fruit, and he had thus followed her. The woman, however, wants to lay the blame on the serpent, which misled her to this deed with its wonderful speech, so that in the face of this wonder she forgot the commandment of GOD; which is also contained in the emphasis of the word. Thus it has always been dangerous to hold the explicit letter of GOD's work in low regard, and rather to give a hearing to human institutions and interpretations, even under a good appearance: because the serpent knows how to hide behind them very quickly. See <margin>2 Corinthians 11:3, 4, 13–15. Galatians 1:8, 9.</margin>

From the answers of the fallen humans in general, however, learn what an abomination denial is, and how it actually heaps sin upon sin. And yet it is often held to be a completely permissible thing.

*Who told you?* How do you know so much? For you were at first like a child in its innocence and pure simplicity, which does not know whether it is naked or clothed. Whence was that sense so pure and clean, that you only waited for my love, and were without concern for the external? It must indeed be quite different with you, because you so quickly become aware of your externals.

GOD instructs both parties very beautifully, and shows them that they became so naked only because of their disobedience; that they wanted to search out His ways, whereas He had reserved the knowledge of them for Himself alone. For that was exactly what the serpent promised them: namely, that when they had this knowledge, they should be like GOD. When one wants to know where GOD is leading us, and what He intends for us, one reaches into His rights and insults Him thereby. But when one surrenders oneself blindly to Him, one thereby gives Him a right testimony that one loves Him, and also worships Him rightly: because one gives to Him—namely, to GOD—what is His due.

# Chapter III. Genesis (The First Book of Moses)

<sig>D 3</sig>

# 14. Then the LORD God said to the serpent: Because you have done this, you are cursed above all livestock and above all the wild animals of the field! On your belly you shall go, and dust you shall eat all the days of your life!

<margin>Micah 7:17.</margin>

The Lord first condemns Satan—who, much later, was called the "ancient serpent" in Revelation 12:9—who was the author of this Fall and already bore the judgment for his rebellion against God. Thus, the instrument, the serpent, is addressed, which was also to bear a sign of the curse: it would become poisonous and thus an object of loathing. Whereas it may have previously had feet and nourished itself on the green herbs of the earth alongside other animals, its feet were now to shrivel, and it was to crawl on its belly and have dust as its food. This, however, was to have its spiritual fulfillment in Satan, who would now lie under a constant curse and be capable of neither knowing nor being good. For this reason, he is emphatically called "the Evil One" in Matthew 13:19; he was to be cast out from all souls who willingly turn toward God and thrown to the earth under their feet (Romans 16:20; see also Acts 28:5). And so, only the "old man"—the "body of sin"—and then those evil and earthly-minded people were to be his food, where one will become a plague and a terrible judgment to the other.

**And)** From this speech of God, it is evident that God did not withdraw Himself from humanity as completely as He did from the devil. Instead, He willed to instill His Eternal Word, which was from the beginning, into the "Seed of the Woman" and make it effective. In this way, His immeasurable love might again become open and beneficial to fallen humans, provided their souls surrendered themselves back into this covenant of God—a covenant that had stood firm in God’s heart from eternity and now broke forth in the great distress of the Fall.

**I will)** It took a long time before this word of promise was outwardly fulfilled. Many a soul is greatly hindered in faith by the thought that because God does not immediately make true everything He promises, nothing will ever come of it. But we must learn to understand God’s speaking rightly. Namely, His speaking should be the same as the deed itself to us. As soon as He speaks, it happens, even if it does not always immediately fall upon our outward senses. A thousand years are like a day to Him. It is our duty to wait for Him, who has also waited long enough for us.

**I will put enmity)** In speaking this, God also worked through His good Spirit in Eve to bring about the necessary turning of her heart, and thus an earnest hatred toward her committed sin and toward the evil desire instilled by the devil. Therefore, she could not help but become an enemy to the author of her misery, the serpent, so that she renounced the covenant with this deceiver and turned away from his works.

False connections cannot last long if they have no root in God and His truth and righteousness. A person may side with Satan as long as they wish, but God eventually sets enmity between them. Even if people have joined together for evil, they must eventually leave one another. Indeed, by the righteous judgment of God, it often happens that they betray and persecute one another because the foundation of their friendship was evil.

However, our Creator herewith also calls us to the true struggle against the devil. We are to have no more fellowship with the devil and all his nature, works, and pomp. For this is an enmity established by God. Whoever still sides with Satan breaks God’s most beloved order and perverts His holy intention, which He had for our best interests. Those who still find pleasure in sin, and are not disgusted by their own corruption with their whole heart, are doing exactly this. Where there is true earnestness, an eternal hatred against all injustice must immediately arise in the heart through the Holy Spirit in true conversion. From such enmity, the struggle is then zealously continued. Here, no hypocritical compliance with sin is permitted, nor any secret understanding or harmony with the enemy, as if one could also be God’s friend at the same time. No; here a "fundamental hatred" <note>original: "Capital-Haß"</note> is required, which suffers no hypocrisy or pretense.

Do not fear or resist such enmity and such war for long! It has been foreseen and ordained by God, and He Himself has powerfully called us to it through this very pronouncement. We have the most righteous cause against our enemy and a strong protector in the righteous Judge, whose cause this is. We would act foolishly and unaccountably if we abandoned our holy calling and did not persevere with Him who will justify His own cause and stay by us.

**Enmity -- between)** This is a difficult legal process <note>original: "Proceß"</note> that does not end with the parties between whom it first began but is propagated to their descendants.

**Woman)** God diligently names the weaker part of humanity so that one might recognize that it is possible even for a woman, in God, to resist the enemy.

Satan had awakened evil desire in Eve, so that she had become one with him in it. Therefore, God speaks only of the woman (1 Timothy 2:14). God could not let this false unity and friendship between Eve and the serpent stand, for it aimed at nothing but the ruin of the creature. The serpent had breathed its false "desire-plague" into the woman and drawn her to itself through such a false bond. If humanity was to be saved, it first had to be released from these devilish snares. To this end, the beginning had to be made with the woman.

However, there must also be something hidden here regarding both original parents and all fallen men and women: specifically, something taken from the spirit of man and made into a "helper" for him. This can be seen as the senses, understanding, thoughts, and memory of a person, which can be viewed as the feminine part, because in 2 Corinthians 11:3, the senses and thoughts are clearly compared to Eve.

But something even higher and more mysterious is to be understood by this: namely, the "New Eve," the true mother of all living, the Divine Sophia <note>Greek for "Wisdom," often personified in mystical theology.</note>, the Virgin Wisdom, the woman of unfading and ever-verdant youth. All famous women mentioned in Holy Scripture—such as Sarah, Rebecca, Deborah, Jael, and especially the Virgin Mary—were figures and archetypes of her. In her simplicity and purity, she stands in eternal opposition and in a straight line against the colorful and cunning serpent.

<column-break/>

# 15. And I will put enmity between you and the woman, and

> Take this speech of God deeply to heart! You do not know where it may give you great strength today or tomorrow.
> 
> This promise was spoken and imprinted into the hearts of the first humans and into the remaining "spark" of the divine image by the Spirit of God, so that it would be propagated as an eternal covenant to all their descendants. In whichever soul surrendered to it, the struggle between Christ and Satan would begin and be continued until victory and life in God.
> 
> There is no doubt that the serpent itself, despite all its cunning, did not well or fully understand what God meant by this, just as Eve wrongly applied this promise to Cain.
> 
> It is no wonder, then, that even now this text is incomprehensible to nature and reason, even if they can chatter and dispute much about it according to the literal word. For the "veil of Moses" does not let them look into the mystery.
> 
> No one can rightly understand or use it unless they enter into the actual battle of faith against the devil through true repentance and learn to experience in deed what God has spoken herein. Even then, no one will plumb the depths of the mysteries within this.
> 
> In almost every word written here, there are mysteries and wonders of God—indeed, true oceans full of divine love, faithfulness, wisdom, truth, and justice—to be found and perceived by a believing mind.

# The First Book of Moses. Chapter III.

## and between your seed /
## and her seed / the same shall

**Seed)** The serpent's seed is evil inspiration and desire, which we must constantly trample underfoot and smash against the rock of Jesus Christ <note>original: "Fels Jesum Christum." See footnote (a)</note>: all rebellious movements, all false persuasions, along with all lying promises and contradictions against God's Word.

All sins are the direct offspring of the hellish spirit. Therefore, no one should jest with sin. They are all certain demonic powers that inevitably leave behind their effects leading to death and damnation.

<margin>1 John 3:8; John 8:44.</margin>
All unbelieving and unconverted people also belong to this wretched seed. All those who allow themselves to be governed merely by human reason and unbelief are of the devil, or his seed, according to that same corrupted part.

Specifically, those are a false serpent-seed who seek their life and their foundation in falsehood, cunning, and intrigues. For these things are harbored and, as it were, hatched by the ancient serpent like unclean vermin and hellish filth. In this sense, JESUS called the hypocrites and Pharisees "snakes" and "broods of vipers," or the true offspring of the creeping, poisonous, flattering serpent.

Whenever you are pleased with yourself because you can deceive others and make them believe something false, or otherwise obtain something through cunning and take advantage of your neighbor, etc., that is all from the serpent. Indeed, all pretenses, hypocrisies, and subtle deceptions are nothing other than children of darkness.

If you take pleasure in sin and consent to it, you are actually committing adultery with the evil enemy; you are producing new plants for him and his kingdom.

<margin>Psalm 45:7; Genesis 22:18; John 1:9; Romans 2:14-15; Galatians 5:16-17.</margin>
But who is the **Seed of the Woman**? While Christ is generally identified and recognized as such, he is experienced by very few as the Seed of Life and the true crusher of the serpent. In a certain sense he is, and in a certain sense he is not. For it cannot well be said of God the Father that He "placed" enmity against evil into His Son. For otherwise, there must have been a time when the Son had no enmity against evil, but rather friendship with it, before God placed it in him. But the Son of God has eternally possessed, by inheritance, an enmity in all fullness against evil. He is, however, the one who was to arise from the **seed of the virginal woman** by assuming her flesh and blood, so that he might become the source and root of the new birth. He also had to become the root of Adam according to his new life, in which all generations of the earth have been blessed from the beginning: in that God places this divine seed from Christ into the spirit of man as a light that fights against the darkness, as a constant teacher who shows what is good and pleasing to God, and what is evil, against which the spirit must desire and strive.

<margin>1 John 3:8; Romans 16:20; 1 John 3:9.</margin>
Now, since this darkness and the desires of the flesh are the seed of the serpent, which exists in all natural men through sin, Christ wishes to fight against it in all those who allow themselves to be drawn to him through his light within them, and who wish to hate the darkness and apply the power offered to them in their conscience to combat the enemy; and also to destroy the works of the devil within them. He wishes to trample Satan under their feet. His seed shall remain in them, so that they cannot sin.

**The same)** Jerome <note>The influential 4th-century translator of the Latin Vulgate Bible.</note>, and with him the old Latin translation, reads "She" <note>original: "Sie." Referring to the Latin *Ipsa*, often interpreted by the Catholic Church as referring to the Virgin Mary.</note>: by which, without doubt, Wisdom is to be understood. Both are correct: *He* and *she*; she through him—the Church in the power of Christ.

To step on the head of the serpent-seed, of sin, and by the power of that suffering and shed blood which he poured out on the Cross for our redemption.

Thus, this "trampling" within a person is a removal of the devil's violence through the power of faith in JESUS, who breaks and destroys vain thoughts and desires through his suffering and death, and opposes all evil powers in his living, victorious Word—if only the heart inclines toward and holds fast to Christ.

---
<margin>(a) Eucherius, Book 1 on Genesis, Chapter 5.</margin>

<column-break/>

# crush your head, and you
# will

**Head)** Thus the Lord names the primary power of devilish malice: just as the primary power and cunning of an animal reside in its head; indeed, its spirit sits properly in the head. God looks primarily at the wicked and godless plot that Satan had devised against mankind to bring them down from their glory through disobedience. This gruesome invention and trick of the devil—the entire power of sin as the origin of all evil—Christ was to destroy once again.

Furthermore, God understood by this "head," insofar as it had also entered into mankind, the **corrupt power of reason** <note>The author uses "Vernunfft" (Reason) here in a negative sense, referring to human intellect that rebels against spiritual truth.</note>, which is a true brood of the serpent. It constantly resists the form, truth, and love of God within man as long as Christ does not crush it. Yes, certainly, the life of reason is actually the innate falsehood of the serpent, through which it hisses like a serpent's head against the Holy Spirit, spewing venom and poisoning the soul. The head is the true and proper seat of rational cleverness and corrupted senses.

Undeniably, this also includes obstinacy or self-will, self-love, and all self-righteousness and personal choice.

From this, so many monstrosities emerge, as if they were so many heads of a body of sin, all belonging to the serpent. Such are the evil impulses and powers of the spirit, of the earthly mind, and the hunger and desire for vanity, of which the maw of such a head can never be satisfied.

What a "peacock-head" is pride! It seeks to raise itself in man above everything—even above God Himself—and gladly wishes to subject everything to itself. From this, there later spring poisonous envy, murderous backbiting, lying, slander, and abuse.

What a monster in man is the "dragon-head" of wrath, with all its ruthlessness and unrest, as a true power of hell that ignites a person to anger against everything.

But the ancient serpent itself is also the head of all godless and malicious people, whom it leads as a head leads its members, working within them and giving them courage and strength.

As long as Satan retains his "head"—that is, his evil self-will, which has become the origin of sin and evil—the enmity must continue. But it is here announced beforehand, even promised, that Christ shall

**Crush)** This signifies nothing other than a total destruction of the devil and his works by the great Redeemer.

But it is not as the ancient serpent persuades her own brood—upon whom she daily exercises her enmity (Ephesians 2:2)—and as they believe: that all the victory which Christ, the holy Seed of the Woman, obtained over Satan is merely credited to them, and is as essentially and truly theirs as if they had worked it themselves in their own persons. If someone then searches for the basis of this and wants to see proof of it, all they can answer is that they "believe" it—that is, they merely imagine it so. And what will self-love not believe? What we dearly wish for, we easily believe. In this way, man imagines himself to be saved through imagined deeds outside of himself, and that the whole work was done *for* him, while he is nonetheless entirely lost—because meanwhile, the serpent's head remains unbroken within him, and sin remains unkilled in these people.

It is not enough here merely to imagine or say that Christ did it through his suffering and death; the devil’s power in you is not broken by that. Rather, in all truth, JESUS Christ must dwell in each person’s heart through living faith and there, step by step, destroy the devil and his works. Yet all this occurs solely by the power of that suffering and shed blood which he poured out on the Cross for our redemption.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Genesis 3:15, focusing on the second half of the verse ("you shall bruise his heel") and the beginning of the judgments in verses 16 and 17. It transitions from the cosmic battle between the "Seed" to the internal spiritual struggle within the believer.</meta>

# you shall bruise his heel.

It is not enough that Christ performed this once externally in the past; rather, he must continue it and carry out his work of redemption until the end of the world. In Romans 16:20, the continuation of this "bruising" or "trampling" is clearly contained <note>original: "Röm. 16/20." This verse promises that "The God of peace will soon crush Satan under your feet."</note>.

The omnipresent Savior, who is united with his own people, constantly fights within them against all sin through his Holy Spirit. For every good thought and impulse toward faith and obedience, and for every turning away from evil that we notice in our hearts, the Lord JESUS is stepping on the head of the serpent within our soul.

That same Spirit of Christ, which previously broke the serpent's head externally in the person of Christ, must now also dwell in us as a life-giving power and bring the struggle against the devil to victory within each individual soul. Otherwise, Christ would have died in vain if the power of his death did not actually benefit us in our misery and help us triumph over sin, the devil, and hell.

Therefore, whatever serves to weaken and destroy sin is, as it were, Christ’s blessed foot within us, with which he crushes Satan. Even the smallest act of obedience in faith, performed in simplicity and purity, deprives the enemy of his access to the soul, simply because it is Christ doing and working it within the person.

And what better foundation could be offered to us than this: that GOD intends to attack the source of all sorrow—sin—and drive it out of humanity once again?

O, blessed is the one who rightly prepares themselves for this promise and now grants the LORD JESUS the space and freedom to begin this work within them!

Surrender yourself entirely to such grace! Let this "trampling" occur within you incessantly, little by little. Wait confidently and watch how one power of the enemy after another is laid low, until Christ finally puts everything in you under his feet!

O, diligently cling to this "Snake-trampler" <note>original: "Schlangentreter," a poetic title for Christ as the one who fulfills the prophecy of Genesis 3:15.</note> who was appointed for you by the Father back in Paradise; and as often as you feel something evil stirring within you, cry out fervently to him, that he may strike this head with his two-edged sword, the living Word!

For this purpose, Christ must take shape within you, so that he may rise as a victorious Hero in your soul and attack all the powers of the devil with his living Word, driving them out of your soul like the thieves and murderers they are—for they do not belong in the house of GOD, which your heart is meant to be.

Therefore, see to it whether this Hero finds enough of a hearing and enough space in you that he can live and reign there, binding and casting out the dragon with his strong arm through faith, which is the victory over the world and the devil.

Finally, the word *shuf* <note>original: שוף (*shūph*), meaning to bruise, crush, or seize.</note>, to trample or destroy, may—according to its secret meaning—also point to the similar-sounding word *shub* <note>original: שוב (*shūv*), meaning to return or turn back.</note>, to return. Thus, it is a destruction that will ultimately be transformed into a "returning" to the previous state, or some other good condition; only then will the works of the devil truly be called "destroyed" with full emphasis.

<term>Heel (Ferse))</term> This is that which touches the earth: the body and its life. Regarding the person of Christ, it refers to his humanity, since the "Head" of Christ is GOD, and he was put to death according to the flesh (1 Peter 3:18). Regarding his Body <note>In this context, the "Body" refers to the Church or the community of believers.</note> and its outward appearance, it refers to the lowliest and weakest of his followers. Regarding the inner man, it is that part which clings to earthly nature and is therefore easily inclined to stumble and fall. For example, the soul must necessarily allow natural desires to go forth for the maintenance of the body's needs. The serpent pays close attention to these "heels." It observed them even in our LORD (Matthew 4:3). During the entire time of his fasting, one hears nothing from the Tempter. But when he grew hungry, the Tempter came to him. While it is permitted to care for such needs, this very care brings us into danger.

<term>Crush/Trample (Zertreten))</term> There must be and remain a perpetual enmity between the Seed of the woman (Eternal Wisdom) and the seed of the serpent. When the former wishes to shatter the "head" and power of sin in the latter, the latter crushes the "heel" (the part the former has on earth) and persecutes them according to the flesh for their own good. For he who suffers in the flesh ceases from sin (1 Peter 4:1). The serpent continued this by accusing the failings and perversity of their "footsteps"—that is, their conduct, especially at the end of life (which is another meaning of the word)—and thus attacks and surrounds them (Psalm 49:6; Revelation 12:10). He previously kept watch on their heels so that he might snatch their soul (Psalm 56:7).

To this also belong all the murderous stabs of evil judgments, lies, and blasphemies of wicked people, through whom the serpent stings at believers and slanders their footsteps (Psalm 89:51), in that he speaks through his instruments against them as evildoers and insults their good conduct in Christ (1 Peter 3:16; 4:14-16). Against this, we must become hardened and view all these stings as the "marks" of JESUS Christ.

<column-break/>

### 16. To the woman he said: I will create much pain for you when you become pregnant! You shall bear children with pain (a); and you shall have to go about your husband / and he shall rule over you (b).

> (a) John 16:21. Revelation 12:2. (b) Chapter 4:7.

### 17. And

By this, GOD did not intend to announce the full punishment of eternal death belonging to sin, but only some consequences of sin: namely, certain temporal tribulations that should be common to all—both to those who are saved and those who are lost. For the latter, these are meant to be precursors of the eternal curse they must expect with their head, Satan, whose seed they wish to keep within themselves. They do not strive to grasp grace and fight against him, but rather love the darkness and willfully remain in it. For the former, these troubles are meant to be wholesome encouragements to the struggle, in order to fully overcome sin within themselves and become partakers of the victory over Satan and death promised through Christ.

That children should be born in pain indicates that they all became true "Benonis"—that is, children of misery (Chapter 35:18)—who, through the righteous judgment of GOD, become partakers in the misery of their parents. They are born without the created image of GOD, and thus in ignorance and a lack of the sanctifying grace of the Spirit; they are in unholiness and unrighteousness, since all are born in perversity and conceived in sin (Psalm 51:5), and the imagination of the human heart is evil from youth (Chapter 8:21). See also Job 5:7.

Furthermore, women are commanded to be constantly "around" their husbands and to serve them (see this manner of speaking in Chapter 4:7, 15:2, Song of Solomon 7:10); and also to be subject, not assuming any mastery or desire to teach, but to be still. In this way, the woman's initial, ill-fated advice <note>Referring to Eve's suggestion to eat the fruit.</note> was somewhat punished. See 1 Timothy 2:11-12; 1 Corinthians 14:34-35.

<term>Rule over you (Aber dich herrschen))</term> It is noteworthy that the person of the man was not preferred over the person of the woman until after the sin was committed. Before that, equality between them was perfect, and their life, according to the Creator's design, was a glorious image of what occurs in the Trinity. In that mystery, one of the most incomprehensible parts is that the Father and the Son are infinitely equal in their greatness and perfection, and no less so in their majesty; neither "descends" <note>original: "descendiret," meaning to be of lower rank or status.</note> before the other, even though one is the origin of the other. As the holy Fathers say, this is because they are united with each other by an infinite and co-eternal love, which is their very essence. Such a love between two who love each other infinitely must be an infinite enemy to all subjection and dependency.

# The First Book of Moses, Chapter III.

17. And to Adam he said: Because you have listened to the voice of your wife / and eaten from the tree / of which I commanded you and said; you shall not eat of it: so the earth is cursed for your sake! With sor-

---

The man is reproached for his crime / in that he obeyed the woman more than GOD: Therefore, the earth should now be under the curse / so that he should no longer nourish himself from her blessing in pleasure / but now through her degeneration in pain / sorrow and bitter labor. For thus the creature is now subjected to vanity: Romans 8:20. <note>original: "Röm. 8/20."</note> and it is also drawn into the punishment / which man has merited. Chapter 6:13, 8:21. And for this reason, a new heaven and a new earth must now be created / which we expect / in which righteousness dwells. Isaiah 65:17, 2 Peter 3:13. <note>original: "Jes. 65/17. 2. Petr. 3/13."</note> And following this comes the temporal death of the body, common to man and woman and all descendants: which for the reborn should be the conclusion of all tribulations and sufferings; since they then no longer need any struggle within themselves against the enemy / because the sinful body is there entirely annihilated, Romans 6:6. <note>original: "Röm. 6/6."</note> so that they also no longer need to stand on their guard: But for the unreborn, it should be the beginning of the sensation of divine judgment; first in the spirit and in the soul / and then also after the Final Judgment in those bodies resurrected to eternal death. See Ecclesiastes 12:7, Luke 16:23, Daniel 12:2, Matthew 25:41, 46. <note>original: "Pred. 12/7. Luc. 16/23. Dan. 12/2. Matth. 25/41. 46."</note>

<margin>v. 17.</margin> **Cursed**) GOD is in Himself pure goodness / and cannot properly curse. Out of His mouth does not proceed cursing and blessing. He blesses alone / and does not curse. Therefore, He could not instill or introduce any noble seed / or form and condition of barrenness / into the earth; rather, He only told Adam beforehand / that / because Paradise had withdrawn itself on account of his disobedience / barrenness would follow / and this very thing would be the curse / which would cling to it / manifest itself and break forth over this visible earth / so that compared to what it was before, it would be a barren wasteland and heath: and that because the devil and his angels thereby gained power to go in and out of it. Therefore then sorrow / toil and labor / plowing or tilling / digging / sowing and planting / had to follow / if it was to bear anything. Whereas one may boldly imagine from the previous Paradisiacal state an abundance of all nourishing and refreshing things / an imperishable spring / a constantly-increasing power of the earth and its crystalline-pure fruit / and from these the highest adornment and delight / the most refreshing exhaling vapors / emanations and scents / the most beautiful colors playing among one another / etc. all of which offered itself to be enjoyed of its own accord and without effort / and was prepared for humans / to pasture and sustain them with essential powers and food from the pure element in an angelic heavenly manner. But just as man's paradisiacal eating previously happened through a powerful, pleasant drawing-in of the pure gifts and creatures of GOD / as the most beautiful balsamic powers and juices / which nourished and maintained him under pure divine blessing: so afterward his body had to be nourished through coarse food / from which nothing but filth arises.

But this is not all: rather, the announced curse goes and reaches even further / namely so far / that the devil and the fallen angels have gained free access through the fallen outer nature to enter into man's nature / to dwell therein / and to sow their evil seed into him / and also to make their evil weeds grow forth from it: namely fury / wrath / envy / zeal / and similar evil growths and plants / whereby the Evil One established his hellish kingdom within / and impressed his image into the souls and hearts of Adam's descendants.

And so here is also the punishment of the upper part / <note>The "upper part" refers to the human spirit or intellect, which followed the "lower part" (the physical desires/passions) into sin.</note> because it followed the temptation of the lower part and self-love. These traitors are condemned / to till with much toil and little benefit the earth / which was moreover cursed. Namely, this beautiful inward field / which had been tilled by the hand of GOD / gave abundant fruit: but now the same / as soon as it is given into Adam’s hands / bears nothing but thistles.

This is the old, impure, corrupted earth / that lies in a fallen state / in whose place GOD has promised to create a new earth: a dry and parched land / that brings forth nothing else but prickly / harmful / and ruinous plants of darkness / which serve no purpose / but to be fuel for the fire and to be burned: a lean, unfruitful ground and soil / in which there is no fatness / and which bears nothing but grass / hay / stubble / husks and dust / on which the inhabitants live: an evil earth / which the LORD has forsaken / which has become a wild desert and wilderness / wherein neither GOD nor wisdom dwells / nor are any springs of water to be found. This is man’s tested earth / and the land that in its fallen state lies under the curse / threats / and under the judgments of GOD / and is called Egypt, Sodom, and Babylon in the Holy Scripture.

One can see it clearly enough / if one only wishes to turn a serious eye upon it / to examine oneself and one's own corrupted heart. For there man in his deviated and degenerate nature will certainly find nothing else but a heap of weeds / stinking flowers / tasteless disgusting herbs / harsh and bitter plants / prickly roots of bitterness. Not a single plant of GOD's own planting is to be found there anymore. All movements and inclinations / or all thoughts and strivings / of the same are / according to the testimony of the Spirit soon following / only evil / and that without ceasing. It is a hardened and obstinate heart / a stubborn rebellious heart / an uncircumcised heart / whose foreskin must be circumcised. From its abundance come forth evil thoughts / evil words / evil suspicions / murders / adulteries / fornications / thefts / false witness / blasphemies / envy / hatred / wrath / revenge / greed / unchastity / impurity / and the like. Not one good little blade of grass grows forth there / but only poisonous herbs and colocynths. <note>A colocynth is a desert vine known for its extreme bitterness and toxicity.</note> And yet man must eat and live from these herbs / roots and plants / because he has nothing else / on which he may live. Oh, what evil / impure / unhealthy and harmful herbs are found there without number! The herb of wrath / fury / malice and hatred: the herb of evil suspicion or mistrust and envy: the herb of pride / of self-love and selfhood: the herb of the spirit; the herb of impatience / of anxiety / sadness / sorrow and pain: the herb of lust / unchastity and animal bestiality. These are the flowers / herbs and roots / that grow forth from the natural human heart / which is his inward ground and earth. And from these his spirit must eat and live / or die. But how can he / since he eats from such harsh and bitter herbs / roots and plants / be anything other than a fierce / fiery / angry nature / and become a greedy / earthly / worldly-minded and oppressive spirit? For whatever is his nourishment / food and sustenance / of which he eats and lives / from that he also draws its same qualities into himself.

But there are yet other harmful weeds / that grow forth from the earth of the fallen Adam and his heart which has departed from GOD: Namely the herbs of self-righteousness / of own-holiness / of self-willed worship: the herbs of a self-chosen forced outward appearance without inward essence: which make the one who eats of them into a hypocritical mouth-confessor / into a false Christian / into an outward hypocrite / into a mouth-Christian hanging on external knowledge and deeds / into a literal historical-Christian / <note>A "historical-Christian" (Historien-Christ) is a term used to describe someone who believes the historical facts of the Bible but lacks a living, internal spiritual experience.</note> and into a member of the false church.

Such harmful herbs and bitter roots of one's own holiness and self-chosen ways / indeed thistles and thorns / are also found right among the wheat in the partially renewed earth / as long as the mixing lasts. And a well-known example of this manifests itself in the lottery and the judgment that has just occurred here
