<header>The First Book of Moses. Chapter III.</header>

<margin>Judges 6:37. Galatians 3:27. <note>original: "B. Richt. 6/37. Gal. 3/27."</note></margin>
### 21. And GOD the LORD made for Adam and his wife garments of skins / and clothed them.

Humans could find no sufficient covering for the now-befouled coat of the flesh. Their aprons made of fig leaves were not enough. A slaughter had to occur / to provide, as a prototype <note>The author uses the "slaughter" of animals for skins as a "type" or prophetic symbol of the sacrifice of Christ.</note>, such clothes with which not only the now-destitute body / but also the naked soul might be covered.

Some interpreters explain that GOD taught them to make the clothes / which modesty now required. For all art / skill / wisdom, and understanding to make something artistic and laudable / comes from GOD alone. See Exodus 35:30. etc. Others hold that it happened through the service of angels / and thereby stay somewhat closer to the literal text. And whatever comes closest to the literal meaning / is undoubtedly to be preferred here.

GOD intended to show thereby / that such clothes would now be necessary for them outside of Paradise / because through sin their body had become entirely fragile and subject to all kinds of passions / as a shield against the accidents of the air and the weather / and as a means for their nakedness / but chiefly as a sign of the robe of righteousness / which the Messiah intended for us again / and which we should put on in him / to cover our nakedness.

But if the children of Adam wear that which is a testimony of the Fall / and which ought to be worn with proper shame / with amusement and puffing up / and rise up with it in splendor or pride; then that is a new, lamentable fall and such a foolish vanity / whereby one bears witness against oneself / that one has entirely departed from human reason. For just as a thief has little reason to boast of the rope or the chain on the gallows / so too one has little reason to boast of beautiful clothes / which are nothing other than signs of our sin-nakedness. For before man sinned / he had no need to cover himself: because his body was much more beautiful and much more artistically crafted than the most precious fabrics / with which one could cover him / could ever be. Nakedness was a piece of the glory of his blessed life / and suited him as well as the robe of honor of his innate righteousness. But now a very different garment is necessary for us / if we wish to adorn ourselves. There, silk and velvet may not suffice. And that is the beautiful white robe of Christ's innocence. This we should put on daily. He who has this on / to him alone shall it one day be allowed / when the wedding of the Lamb comes / and the King of Heaven appears in his adornment and glorious splendor / to enter the gates of the holy city / and to appear at this royal feast in proper gala attire.

**Of skins)** Of purple-colored sheep / according to Ursinus's opinion. And such a garment should bring to mind / what the Lamb, who was to bear the sin of the world / would do for their benefit / and how they could obtain the true robe of salvation through him.

Therefore, it is worth reflecting / that the Hebrew word given here / **he clothed them** <note>original: "er zohe ihnen an"</note> / through a transposition of the letters also means / **JESUS their Heart.** <note>This refers to a mystical or kabbalistic rearrangement of Hebrew letters, common in Pietist commentary, to find hidden meanings pointing to Christ.</note>

Others / says Bishop Vulcanus, may ask what they will. In the church one sings *Agnus DEI* <note>Latin: "Lamb of GOD"</note>, you Lamb of GOD. Therefore I stay with the lambskins / and remember the lambskins of Adam and Eve / which pointed to Christ / the innocent Lamb of GOD.

But the meaning also refers simultaneously to the killing and conformity with Christ's death / whose innocent life was killed in Adam / as the Lamb that is slain from the foundation of the world. Revelation 13:8.

So then, O you beastly man / clothe your proud flesh with animal skins / and learn here from GOD, with the sinful Adam, the dying away of your sins. Humble yourself / and sit in the dust; into which the flesh / that you now pamper and fatten / must shortly be transformed: Put away your ornaments from you! so that the Lord may know / what he should do to you. Exodus 33:5.

1. Christ is a tree / risen from the earth / and reaching high above all lowly shrubs and herbs of life / yes, life itself. Revelation 2:7. 2. This tree stood in the midst of the garden. The Son of GOD is in the midst of us in his Church / yes, in the midst of the throne. Revelation 7:17. 3. From this tree Adam / overcome by the serpent / was driven away. He who does not overcome / does not get to eat from the wood of life. Revelation 2:7. 4. It is called a tree of life / though in itself it had no life-giving power. In Christ alone is life truly found. John 1. Let us stretch out our hand thither / and long again for that place / from which we, as natural children of Adam, were cast out.

<column-break/>

### 22. And GOD the LORD said: Behold, Adam has become <gloss>(a) Hebrews 2:14. 2 Peter 1:4. 1 John 3:2.</gloss> (a) like one of us / in that he knows Good and Evil; but now / lest he perhaps stretch out his hand / and take also from the tree of life / and eat / and live forever: 23.

GOD shows man his foolish imagination and the deception of Satan / that he could not have attained the wisdom of the Triune GOD through disobedience / since he indeed did not recognize his best interest / and had to experience his evil in deed.

But this is not / as most commonly understand these words / spoken in mockery / as if GOD had reproachfully thrown back at man Satan's lying words from verse 5. Is it safe to attribute such a harsh mocking speech and way of speaking to the most gracious and merciful GOD? since he would then appear / as if the good GOD rejoiced more over the misery of wretched man / than pitied him: and whether it is probable / that the good GOD should alienate all his love and mercy with mockery: let that be left to the contemplation of godly men. At the very least, it must not be understood thus / but it can also mean:

**Adam has been like one of us)** He was like one of us in the image of GOD: and according to that same image he recognized / loved / and embraced the Good; also he recognized / hated / and shunned the Evil. For thus GOD and his Christ know evil. Isaiah 7:15. Merely to recognize the Good is not inherently good: and the mere knowledge of Evil is also not evil. Therefore, knowledge here simultaneously includes a corresponding inclination. And thus the LORD hereby simultaneously hinted at a secret inequality with the state in which man is now / where he knows or recognizes the Good / but does not love it; and recognizes the Evil / but does not hate it.

But besides this, there is another translation of an older and better sense / where the little word **from** or **out of** may indicate a departure / an exclusion / or a separation.

**Adam has become as one [departed] from or out of us)** That is / he has become as one who has gone out from us and our image / and has now learned from his own experience / but also to his own harm / what is good / and how good he found himself in the state of the uncreated divine image / and how evil everything is / how miserably and wretchedly he has corrupted himself.

And this shows us sufficiently / how this knowledge of good and evil / which is the knowledge of the world of GOD in us / preserves the own-life <note>A term often used in mystical theology to describe the selfish, unregenerate nature of man.</note> in us / and prevents its internal death. Therefore GOD sent Adam out of the place of joys; so that he could no longer stretch out his hand toward this tree / and no knowledge would remain / which might prevent his death / and maintain his own-life. For no better medicine could be found for his harm than death. In that he loses his infected own-life through the same / he enters into eternal life / which was healed for him through the innate righteousness. If he did not cast himself off / he could not live to GOD again. From a false humility comes the disturbance and the unrest after a fall into sin: which is often ended with desperation. Where one is greatly distressed and tormented after a fall into sin / there must still be much pride and self-love. Since, on the contrary, it is the fruit of a true humility / to be still and composed in rejection / when one has committed something evil / yes, even if it be something great / in that one gently abandons oneself to GOD / so that one may be rightly judged by him through his mercy / and submits oneself to him as a sacrifice for him to do with us whatever is pleasing to him.

In the tree of life we have a sacrament, lead-

## 23. Then GOD the LORD expelled him from the Garden of Eden / to till the ground from whence he was taken;

## 24. And He drove Adam out / and placed the Cherubim at the east of the Garden of Eden / and that with a flashing sword / which turned this way and that / to guard the way to the tree of life. <margin>Revelation 22:14.</margin>

->The<-

---

Adam and Eve, along with their descendants, were not intended to remain in Paradise forever / but only for a time / as long as the testing of Adam by the serpent should last. However, it was far from God’s intent and opinion / that he should be expelled from it: rather / if he had resisted the temptation / and overcome the devil / he and his entire race would have been taken away from Paradise to occupy the vacant thrones of the fallen angels / and thus would have ascended higher. But instead, because of his base conduct, the most shameful expulsion followed instead of the most glorious exaltation.

And yet, everything God undertook with Adam in this entire process / though it may appear from the outside as a harsh and ungracious proceeding / proceeds from love / not from wrath / and is an effect not of avenging justice for punishment and rejection / but of His chastising love-justice / for the improvement of corrupted human nature. For God is and remains unchangeable Love.

Specifically, so that man would not heap sin upon sin / and presume to secure life for himself in the former way / as when he was still in the first blessed state; God withdrew the Tree of Life from him by actually driving him out of the Garden of Eden. For he could no longer remain in such a blissful place / which was intended to be an image and assurance of the heavenly fatherland / because he had made himself unworthy of it. Therefore, the earth, cursed for the sake of his sin, was assigned to him as a place of work and labor / indeed, as a prison and a stage for the creature subjected to so much misery and vanity because of sin / but also for divine patience / mercy / omnipotence / wisdom, and truth. But God had the way to the Garden and the Tree of Life guarded by His holy hosts / the angels / with the brilliance of a flashing sword / to show man the power of death hanging over him for his terror / so that he might not embolden himself in his sins and guilt to secure life at this tree / but that he must now turn in repentance and faith to the promised Seed of the Woman / as the newly opened source and Tree of Life. See <margin>Numbers 32:31. Revelation 2:7.</margin>

v. 23. 24. Expelled -- drove out) Where to then? It is generally held / that he settled where the city of Damascus is now located.

How long he was in Paradise / is asked and researched by others.

The Silesian nobleman Tschech proves from the analogy and the prototypes <note>A "prototype" or "type" is a person or event in the Old Testament seen as prefiguring something in the New Testament.</note> of Moses and Christ / based on the foundation of Jacob Böhme / that he was in there for 14 days.

Another question arises here concerning the Garden of Eden) Whether it is still in the world? Bellarmine <note>Robert Bellarmine (1542–1621), an influential Jesuit cardinal.</note> has taken pains to prove from the Church Fathers and other teachers / such as Irenaeus, Jerome, Augustine, Theodoret, Bede, Thomas Aquinas, etc. / that Paradise, in its great glory and pleasantness, is still to be found in the world / and was not devastated by the general Flood: since indeed Enoch and Elijah / along with the Saints who rose with Christ / as well as the converted thief on the cross / were found within it. This opinion is also supported by Sixtus of Siena, Justin Martyr, Irenaeus, Tertullian, Isidore, along with Simone Majolo. And although others contradict this / those mentioned are right in a certain sense. For the blessing of the outward creation consisted precisely in this / that Paradise, with its virtue, sap, and power / permeated it: and the curse / which followed upon Adam's disobedience / stems from the fact that Paradise, or the Paradisiacal world, withdrew from it. Thus, Paradise is certainly still in this visible world / but covered and hidden / and will likely remain so / until the Day of Restoration appears:

<column-break/>

and then the inner Paradisiacal world will become outward and visible / whereas the outward visible world will again be swallowed up and become invisible / as it was in the beginning. And so, all the kingdoms of this visible world will then become the kingdoms of GOD and His Christ. Until then, Paradise remains locked and veiled: and thus Adam was driven out of it / needing no other expulsion than for it to be withdrawn from him.

Therefore, Paradise actually still greens through everything on earth: but no unclean, false heart reaches its power and great bliss; God does not cast His pearls before swine: He tests everyone severely first / before He admits them / and deems them worthy to taste a foretaste of what Adam tasted and saw before his fall.

But if you hasten to cross over from sin <unclear>and</unclear> into grace / and hate evil / and lay hold of faith in the Redeemer; then the power of Paradise / that is / God's blessing and life / would again be unlocked for you in earnest repentance / and Christ would take away the Cherub with his striking sword of curse and wrath / and let you come to the pure, harmless enjoyment of all creation. It only depends on one not searching diligently enough / not knocking and persisting with GOD / as to how one might rightly use Him and His creatures: otherwise, the key to Paradise might well be found again / which Christ Jesus has regained. But what are the

Cherubim in v. 24?) Theodoret in his *Questions on Genesis* <note>original: "quæstionibus super Genesin"</note> and Procopius of Gaza made terrifying phantoms and hideous animal shapes out of them / which stood before Paradise.

Augustine and many others hold / that nothing else is understood but angels / who are called "mighty heroes" in Psalm 103:20 / to whom God assigned a visible form of terrifying youths for this work. By

The flashing sword, however, Tertullian understands the *torrid zone* <note>original: "Zonam torridam"</note> / the hot region of the earth / and thus believes / that Paradise was located under the equinoctial line <note>The Equator.</note>. T. Burnet also confesses to this opinion.

To Lyra and Tostatus, this signifies a fire / which broke out from the high mountains / upon which Paradise was situated according to their thoughts / and appeared as a figure around Paradise.

Ambrose says / it is Purgatory <note>original: "Fegfeur"</note>.

And so the "letter" <note>The literal interpretation of scripture.</note> brings nothing but divided opinions: but the "spirit" is life / and in it is truth and certainty and unity.

Franciscus Mercurius van Helmont, in the little book he calls *Some Thoughts on the First 4 Chapters of the First Book of Moses* / gives a spiritual interpretation of this / whose words summarize everything briefly and are as follows:

> "Cherub signifies
> "a boy; because now man, through the stages
> "of age, must go from childhood to manly strength.
> "The flame-like sword is death:
> "as something which is contrary to nature / and does violence to it.
> "For that the sword is a deadly instrument and weapon
> "is well known. Therefore it signifies death: the flames
> "signify pain. For they burn. Pain, however,
> "is an inflammation / or the hot and confused action of a life
> "boiling up through heat / whereby nature attacks the
> "implanted evil with force / and strives to subdue it.
> "The sword is turning, however, because in turn
> "one steps from death to life. And this
> "way will finally lead, through many births of children and
> "repeated dying, to the Tree of Life / that is / to the
> "state of immortality and perfection.

Accordingly, there is no other way to return to the lost glory / than that the soul, through all kinds of secret dying with Christ and through the sharp sword of the Cherub placed before it, should courageously press through / let all the old sensual lusts and false lives that have intruded be cut off / and thus, as a little child stripped of all own-will and possessions, enter into the Kingdom of GOD.

### Chapter IV.

#### The Deeds of the Ungodly and Worldly Men.

<margin>Isaiah 54:5.</margin>
1. And Adam knew his wife Eve/ and she became pregnant/ and bore Cain/ and said: I have obtained the man/ the LORD. <note>The German text uses "den HERrn," suggesting Eve believed her firstborn was the promised divine Savior.</note>

<margin>(a) John 10.</margin>
2. And she continued and bore his brother/ Abel: and Abel became a shepherd of sheep <note>*</note>/ but Cain was a tiller of the ground.

With this first son, Eve wished to show her faith in the promise of the Seed from her/ who should crush the serpent's head/ when she gave him the name of the LORD/ as if she had already received the Lord from heaven <note>1 Corinthians 15:47</note>/ who must be the mighty God/ who would have to overcome this powerful enemy of theirs. This should rightly be placed among the testimonies/ by which the ancient believers wished to make known their hope; and that also concerning the divinity of the Messiah. For

Though she was mistaken in the person/ it shows nonetheless how firmly the word of life in the given promise <note>Chapter 3:15</note> had formed and imprinted itself in the hearts/ so that from then on it became the light/ power/ and guide of the soul/ amidst all misery on earth.

However, just as our mother Eve was deceived in this/ so are and will be in this fantastic age/ which is so powerfully subject to imagination/ many thousands of her children deceived through imagination/ thinking that they are better off than they are in reality. How many there are/ who think themselves exceedingly happy/ when they are actually the most miserable of all! The greatest slaves and vassals of sin nonetheless imagine themselves to be redeemed from sin. How many flatter themselves/ that they have been made kings and priests to God the Father/ and boast of a false gift! Laodicea also thinks/ she is rich and increased with goods; when she is actually wretched/ miserable/ poor and naked. So that one may well cry out <note>Sirach 37:3</note>: O ungodly imagination/ from whence hast thou come in/ to cover the earth with deceit!

Of the daughters/ whom Eve must certainly also have borne/ because otherwise there were no other females/ whom Cain and Seth could have taken in marriage/ none is mentioned by name in Holy Scripture: and little is to be given to the Jewish fables of what they were named(a); it is also just as certain or <insert>traditions/ according to which one was named Azron / and another Awan</insert> <insert>uncertain/ what Irenæus(b), Epiphanius(c) and others/ mention of the</insert> names/ by which they are said to have been called Norea/ Save/ Azuam/ etc. Because the Scripture often makes no mention of many such things/ we may conclude from this/ not without reason/ that in the names and persons/ which it explicitly brings forward/ there is always more than mere history hidden and to be sought.

In the naming of her second son, Eve wished to display a humble recognition of weariness and vanity / how man is subject to vanity/ <note>Psalm 39:6</note> and his thoughts and beginnings are only vanity <note>Psalm 94:11; 62:10</note> upon which neither he nor any other is to rely. <note>Psalm 146:3, 4</note>. And she may have noticed much evil in her first son / if he were indeed born at another time / so that she now wishes to testify / how one is not to rely upon a mere human.

However, the Hebrew text / upon closer consideration of the words/ indicates not unclearly / that at the first birth of Eve, the pious Abel followed the wicked Cain as a twin: just as later Rebecca brought forth the tender and gentle Jacob from her womb together with the rough Esau. Which holily teaches / how already from the beginning/ through the power of the spoken word of the promise of the Woman's Seed/ a mighty wrestling and struggle of the evil and good qualities arose in human procreation; each of which brought forth a fruit of its kind: and indeed the former for the opening of the generation of the wicked; the latter however for the opening of the generation of the pious and the line of the Covenant.

And herein lies something great hidden for God-fearing Christian married couples for their instruction. For although through the common way of child-bearing the blessed Woman's Seed itself may not be brought forth; as He who is born only of Virginal Mothers according to the Spirit/ without the will of the flesh and the lust of man / yet they may / where they strongly move in true faith the word of grace spoken through the first promise / and now also embodied through Christ's incarnation / and through its power struggle against the evil qualities / at least bring forth such children/ who may be capable and receptive of the new heavenly birth from God for the opening of the blessed Woman's Seed: as this is to be seen from the physical genealogy of Christ <note>Matthew 1 and Luke 3</note> as well as from the fact that Israel according to the flesh / for the sake of its origin from the holy fathers regarded in such awakened power of faith / is explicitly called by Paul (d) a naturally good olive tree/ and is set in opposition to the naturally wild olive tree of the Gentiles.

3. AND it came to pass at the end of the year/ that Cain brought to the LORD an offering from the fruits of the ground.

v. 3. At the end of the year) Thus they were thanks-offerings / which they brought / for the blessings / which he had granted them throughout the entire past year. <note>Exodus 23:16</note>. Around this same time even the heathens themselves observe the same custom of sacrificing / and for the same reason: be it that they were moved to it by the passing of a long tradition / or they were directed to this gratitude by learned men / many of whom had seen the writings of Moses; or else they were internally instructed of it by the light within them. For Aristotle (a) thus testifies / that the people of old were accustomed to act and hold sacrifices and gatherings after the gathering of their fruits. It is not easily seen/ however/ what agreement our reason finds between God/ who is a Spirit / and between the fleshly sacrifices; and how thus this sacrificing could have happened from the impulse of nature (b).

These first sacrifices were without doubt performed at divine command: because no self-chosen worship can please God; as Abel's sacrifice was pleasing to him here. <note>Hebrews 11:4</note>. Thus it was at the same time a prototype of the unique sacrifice of Christ as the Firstborn/ and a seal of the righteousness of faith/ which God wished to give in the gracious looking upon his sacrifice. Thus Christ was presented to the faithful Abel in the Spirit / as the Lamb who was slain from the beginning of the world. <note>Revelation 13:8</note>. The sign of this gracious looking/ however/ can very well have been indicated in the burning of the sacrifice by a fire fallen down from heaven/ which was also common thereafter: <note>Leviticus 9:24; Psalm 20:4</note> which Cain did not notice on his own / and which thus moved him to an envious anger. See Isaiah 8:21.

<sig>E 3</sig>

## 6. Then the LORD said to Cain: Why are you so angry / and why has your countenance fallen?

These two verses contain a sermon from the best Preacher to the worst listener. GOTT <note>The original text uses "GOTT" (God) in all capitals to denote the Divine Name.</note> wishes to rebuke him / showing that he was unjustly enraged against his brother / and was grumbling against GOTT himself: for only he is pleasing to Him who does good / and approaches Him in faith and humility; which was lacking in Cain / who was satisfied only with his own imagination and the outward work he had performed / and was not truly concerned with the condition of his heart: for without a repentant / humble, and faithful heart, one cannot please GOTT. GOTT thus shows him the way to the forgiveness of sins; which is to be understood here: (See verses 18, 24, etc.) that if he would strive to do well in a godly life / and always stand on guard against sin / which constantly besets us in our corrupt nature <margin>Hebrews 12:1.</margin> and the enemy / who always goes about / seeking to gain entry into the heart / and seeking to devour us / <margin>Matthew 12:43; 1 Peter 5:8.</margin> so that he might overcome the same / through the power that would be granted to him by GOTT upon his prayer / which is the resistance made in faith in GOTT. This is also a profound divine testimony / that GOTT has placed into all men the promised Seed of the Woman, Christ, as a light and power / to strive against the seed of the serpent within them / and to crush its head in Christ / and thus to rule over it. Now, whoever pays heed to this light within himself / and humbly looks to GOTT for the offered power / and then strives for the good / of which this inner light in the conscience gives testimony; he shall obtain forgiveness of sin / and power / to conquer the sin that constantly waylays us. But whoever does not heed such things / as was afterward shown in Cain / he will finally be mastered by sin and Satan / so that he consents to evil / and becomes and remains a servant of sin. <margin>Romans 6:16; 2 Peter 2:19.</margin>

<column-break/>

## 7. Is it not so: If you do well / there is forgiveness? But if you do not do well / sin lies

**Is it not so?)** This is such an undeniable truth / that even an otherwise ill-intentioned Cain cannot deny it. The presentation was so piercing / that it convicted Cain in his conscience and took him captive. The Spirit of Truth herewith also asks every person's conscience / whether this is not so; whether we have anything grounded to object against this testimony of GOTT; whether we do not find ourselves guilty of failing to follow it; and whether there must not be a true rule in our entire life? However—
Nature does not like to hear this saying: it would rather hear Chapter 3:15 <note>The promise of the Savior.</note>. That is because / it does not want to engage in the struggle against evil / but rather to continue undisturbed in its own will without resistance or battle.
**If you do well / then)** When one is changed from the ground up by the Holy Spirit / and puts on the new man / who is created according to GOTT in true righteousness and holiness; then one is acceptable to the LORD. There GOTT finds again the trace of His first image in Christ JESUS / which was created in us: and that pleases His soul well / so that He has pleasure in us / as a father in his son. Thereafter everything is acceptable to Him / which faith works in us through love. For it is sanctified through the Spirit of holiness. The whole man is in Christ / and there is nothing damnable in him / so long and further as he walks not according to the flesh / but according to the Spirit.
Only believe / all your outward things and postures help you as little as Cain’s sacrifice helped him / if you do not want to become an entirely different person from the ground up and from the inside out / in heart / courage / mind, and all your powers!
The 70 Interpreters <note>original: "70 Dollmetscher"; referring to the Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament.</note>, as well as Augustine, Gregory the Great, and other ancient Latin commentators / and from them the Vulgate <note>original: "Vulgata"; the standard Latin Bible.</note>, render it thus: *If you offer rightly, but do not divide rightly; you have already sinned. Therefore desist from it.* Luther allows this interpretation / but acknowledges with Jerome <note>original: "Hieronymo"; the translator of the Vulgate.</note>, that it is better rendered thus: If you

---

are good or pious / then your sin will be forgiven or lifted. Therefore he quite skillfully draws these two main lessons from this: 1) That nothing pleases GOTT / which does not proceed from faith; 2) that sin is a grievous evil / which is to be lifted only through grace / not through works and sacrifices. He also notes from the 32nd Psalm / where this same Hebrew word stands / that it signifies a lifting / raising / or blotting out of sin / through which the Holy Spirit takes away from man not only the guilt and punishment of sins / but also the dominion of sins / so that they can no longer lie like a burden upon the soul / and make man a slave / as before. And indeed, the Hebrew word comprises within itself 1) Forgiveness of sin; 2) Lifting / namely of the countenance; 3) Receiving what was desired. <margin>Psalm 24:5.</margin>

***If you do not do well*** All outward works count for absolutely nothing before GOTT / unless there is living faith in the heart. GOTT wants the heart to be pious for once / otherwise everything is an abomination to Him / when corrupt nature wants to be pious for itself without His grace / and set up its own righteousness. Truly, one will never get by with that before GOTT! The LORD says: *if you do good / but if you do not do good.* Thus doing good or not doing good does not consist in the offering of the sacrifice / or in the not-offering; but in obedience / which is better than sacrifice / <margin>1 Samuel 15:22.</margin> or other outward worship services.

If you still willfully keep this or that "bosom-sin" <note>A "Schlooß-Sünde" or bosom-sin is a favorite, secret sin that a person is most reluctant to give up.</note>, like Cain; then you are already not pious in God's eyes / even if you were willing to kiss the feet of all the saints <note>original: "Heiligen die Füße wolltest abfressen"; literally "to eat off the feet," an idiom for extreme or fawning displays of devotion.</note> / or wept blood in hypocritical devotion. For your heart is then not upright before GOTT / and thus you are not yet truly pious.

**Many** would like to become better / (because they notice / that their lack of repentance will not do well in the long run /) but they remain hanging onto many a wrong.

As long as you bring sacrifices with Cain in such a state / your piety is an abomination before GOTT / even if it pleased all men / or if the preacher absolved you a hundred times!

True piety is not a hypocritical / externally assumed / forced piety / where one does not become honest or different in the heart / or where one still harbors this or that sin with will and pleasure / or still wants to take along this dishonest profit / or that false and vain pleasure.

Your piety must become something real and universal / so that you gain a desire for everything good without exception / and learn to desist from all evil entirely.

***Sin lies at the door*** This is the harm and just reward of all those who do not want to become entirely different and entirely better / that they must also keep the evil / which they will not leave / around their necks as a punishment.

This is so true and so certainly grounded in experience / that even truly converted people must still feel this misery / as much as they are still stuck in corruption. How many must cry out in the midst of their earnest struggle: *O who will deliver me from this body of death!*

What then will those experience in their conscience / who do not want to become pious at all. They may deny it or hide it as they wish / yet it remains true for all of them what GOTT says here: *sin lies at their door.*

Note this / you many / who think sin is only a thing / that one can get rid of or wipe away in a moment / like perhaps a stain on a garment! Oh no! It rests before the heart / it settles so firmly and deeply into the human will / that great work is required / before one can be rid of it.

Do not be overconfident / dear person / if you happen to stand / so that you are not exactly tempted by sins or grossly led astray! Do not think / when you notice neither evil nor good in you / that you therefore have no more sin! It only lurks like a lion in a cave / and like a mad chain-dog / which indeed seems to sleep / but / before the passerby realizes it / lunges at the soul / and wounds and tears it. Your corruption does not sleep! Satan also does not take a holiday: he is only quiet for a while / to make you secure and to lure you; so that he can all the better ambush and destroy you with his arrows. Just test it in the future with one or another sin / to which you were perhaps formerly accustomed!

<header>The First Book of Moses. Chapter IV.</header>

# Sin at the door: and it shall go around you; but you must rule over it.

### Verse 8. <note>The author likely refers to the final part of verse 7, which in many older German bibles was grouped or numbered differently in commentary.</note>

Sometimes you will notice no evil desire stirring in your heart at all: then you will think you are quite pious; especially when you are perhaps praying, singing, etc. But oh, how sin then rests secretly at the door! And where you do not entirely surrender yourself to GOD, it shall surely fell you before you even realize it.

From where does it often come, that many people commit such heavy offenses, or fall into such wicked cases? Certainly from the security of thinking they could not possibly sin in such a way; yet sin is so near to them—indeed, it is inside their hearts.

Thus sin lies before the heart with its seduction and evil power.

But it also lies there with its accusation and condemnation. It is only a pity that coarse people experience this so little. Yet all willful sinners must become aware of it, even against their will, how near their sins are to them. The barking dog—the bad conscience—soon stirs and shows that it does not sleep with its damnation. As soon as such a sin is rebuked or punished, the person feels it immediately in their conscience. **WHAT** is that other than sin lying at the door? And what makes a sinner so trembling and faint-hearted, so shy, distrustful, and anxious, if not his bad conscience? It does not rest; it accuses him day and night in his own heart, where GOD has His judgment seat, as a foretaste of that terrifying final judgment.

It shall go around you) The LORD speaks here not a word of Abel, but of sin. The Jewish interpreters also take it to mean the "evil inclination" <note>original: "böse Lust," often referring to the Hebrew concept of the *Yetzer hara*.</note> which constantly seeks to weaken and fell a person. Just as it is said of the Devil, that he goes around us and seeks to devour us. And truly, the desire of sin is always directed toward the poor soul; the evil, innate hereditary desire <note>A reference to "original sin."</note> always shoots its wrath and poison against the human; it always hungers for the human will and seeks to become its master. Only pay attention to it in your own life, and enter into a true earnestness against evil: see if you do not notice how everything in the world tries to take your crown. Now money wants to capture you, now beauty and the flesh, now a bit of honor, office, and title, now something even lesser. Your spirit is such a precious thing that everything in this corrupted world woos it and flatters you to win you over.

Some interpreters also note here, not without reason, that in the Hebrew the same turn of phrase is used which the LORD used in Chapter 3:16, where it actually said: "Your desire shall be for your husband," or, "you shall have to go around your husband." Thus also here; its (sin's) will shall follow you: or, toward you shall be its desire, that is, the desire of sin shall be under you. The evil desire, which always seeks to cast you down, shall be in your power, or subject to you: it shall be turned toward you to seek your consent, so that it can do nothing without you. Fundamentally it all agrees, even Luther's translation, which renders it thus:

Do not let it have its will) This happens through the withdrawal of your will, so that you withdraw your agreement from the evil stirrings in your flesh and blood; do not consent to them, but set yourself directly against them and do exactly the opposite. For example: Sin entices you in your heart toward injustice, to take an unfair profit. Then do not merely refrain from the wrong, but do exactly the opposite; act with true uprightness toward your neighbor: then sin must surely retreat and become subject to your good will.

If one is not to let evil have its will, then sin must not be an invincible thing, as the Enemy <note>The Devil.</note> gladly makes people believe. It is indeed nothing small or trivial, but it is also not invincible; rather, it is a thief and murderer who has forced his way into the heart against right and fairness, and must therefore yield against his own thanks and will when a person uses true earnestness.

Oh, how all believers have so earnestly defended themselves against sin! How they have preferred to endure distress and death before they would have consented to a single sin! Should that not also drive us to earnestness, so that we think: if those people did not let sin have its will, then it shall not be allowed to overpower me either! I will defend myself bravely in the name of JESUS Christ: it must finally give way.

But the struggle must be earnest, so that one does not yield to sin for a single moment with their will.

<column-break/>

If you finally want to know what the "will" of sin is or what it wants to have; then just go into your heart and notice what stirs there. There you will find all sorts of evil thoughts and desires rising up, which want to entice you now to injustice and greed, now to evil lust and shame, now to bad company, to hatred, envy, pride, and the like. See, that is what sin wants to have. It, as the Devil's seed and power, wants you to provoke your dear GOD through such profligate ways, to push His grace away from you, to make one wound after another upon your conscience, to offend and grieve your neighbor, and to ruin yourself and others in suffering and soul. Thus, the will of sin is your temporal and eternal destruction and ruin. The Enemy goes about day and night to lead you to this. This will is diametrically opposed to the will of GOD. GOD seeks nothing but your temporal and eternal well-being and all blessing and peace for you and your soul. Conversely, the Enemy wants exactly the opposite. Distinguish now which you ought to choose: and if you do not want to be a contemptible slave to sin, then you must

-> (Rule over it) <- In this, GOD demands nothing other from the wicked Cain than true conversion.

There is thus indeed a strength, ability, or power from the LORD Himself in fallen man to subdue his corruption and to overcome evil with good.

Bernard <note>Saint Bernard of Clairvaux (1090–1153), a Cistercian abbot and influential mystic.</note> records the following thoughts on this passage:

> "It is within us, if only we do not wish to let ourselves
> "be overcome, and no one among us is cast down in this
> "struggle against his will. O Man! your desire
> "is under you, and you shall rule over it. The
> "Enemy can indeed stir up the irritation of temptations;
> "but it is within you whether you will give in or not. It stands
> "in your power whether you want to make your enemy
> "into a slave, so that everything works together for your best.
> "Your victorious enemy ignites in you the desire for food,
> "for vanity, impatience, or even unchastity. If you then
> "do not give your will over to it, you will always be crowned,
> "as often as you resist."

That is a precious testimony right after the Fall of man, that sin shall not always remain MASTER over man, as people commonly imagine—that they must continually be and remain slaves of sin throughout their whole lives, and even remain so gladly because evil pleases them. But it must be true what the Apostles testify: Sin shall not be able to rule over us, so long as we wish to be under grace.

See only that you receive another mind and spirit; thus you will receive at the same time the mastery over sin.

Should you not receive it with joy, that GOD wants to make you so glorious and worthy again as to rule over your worst enemy?

How can anyone be against it when this honor is done for him, that he shall become master over his evil things?

Whoever does not want to rule over sin, over him sin takes the mastery. But whoever does not spare himself, nor cherishes and keeps his sins; he will finally become master over them, so that they can no longer take him captive.

If the LORD Himself provides one with the upper hand and help over sin, yet he himself sells his soul to the slavery of sin and injustice; is that not a mockery and a shame?

Consider how dearly you were bought, and what it cost the Son of GOD to acquire this mastery for you! Why then do you not want to use it now?

Why do you want to remain a servant of sin by force, and a prisoner of your lusts, greed, and pride with your whole will?

All their things are slaveries and servile matters: there is nothing liberal, truly free, or noble about them. Therefore they must indeed be mastered.

All vices have more in common with cattle and servitude, and thus suit only slavish minds.

Should such a noble creature as man is be subjected, even for a moment, to such a monster and shameful abomination—to such an author of the Devil as sin truly is?

<summary>This page provides a theological commentary on God's warning to Cain about sin "crouching at the door." It emphasizes that while sin is a predatory and accusatory force, humans possess the God-given agency and responsibility to resist it through the exercise of will and divine grace.</summary>

It focuses heavily on "typology"—the practice of seeing Old Testament figures like Abel and Cain as "prototypes" for Christ, the Church, the Jewish people, and the ungodly.</meta>

<header>Chapter IV. The First Book of Moses. 39</header>

<margin>
In the field near Damascus. Josephus, Book 1 of *Antiquities*, chapter 3.
</margin>

### 8. Then Cain spoke with his brother Abel. And it came to pass, when they were in the field, that Cain rose up against his brother Abel and slew him. 9. Then

---

**Spoke)** "Let us go out into the field!" <note>original: "Laß uns aufs Feld gehen!"</note> This phrase is still present in the Greek, Samaritan, Syrian, and old Latin translations.

Some people are so hardened and stubborn in their sinful ways that, even if GOD himself preaches to them from heaven, they still refuse to be moved, but willfully and obstinately persist in their path.

When people do not become better, they always become worse through hearing: because they flatter and coddle themselves with an external religious service, as if the mere act of hearing made a person better.

Cain stands here as an example of those stuck in false religion and hypocrisy; who, especially when punished because of their imagined grasp of the truth, very soon break out into quarreling and strife against those who rebuke them, and thereafter hate, persecute, and gladly kill them. See Jude verses 10, 11; 1 John 3:12.

**Cain** means a "possession" <note>Hebrew: *Qayin*</note> and a particular quality of the flesh which desires all natural, human, and divine things and draws them to itself: everything must serve it. Therefore, it is the nature of the flesh to claim everything it does for itself, as if it were pleasing to GOD—indeed, claiming it for itself alone. Thus, when GOD testifies that the simple, pious, and righteous **Abel** pleases Him, the grimace of anger, wrath, and envy burns against him and all the holy prophets, from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zechariah. This disordered desire and the grim, envious neglect or condition of the soul comes from him who was a murderer from the beginning, and who is called *sched* <note>Hebrew: *Shed*, meaning a demon or destroyer</note> by the Jews to this very day. And it is remarkable that the Greek language has also retained the memory of the first murderer’s name in the word which is *kakin* <note>original: "κάκιν", likely referring to *kakia*, meaning wickedness or malice</note>.

**Abel** is (as Philo explains this name) a lamenting, a wailing, and a sighing to GOD, etc. <note>Philo of Alexandria was a Jewish philosopher who often used allegorical interpretations.</note> He was slain in the acre or field; "that is the world," says our Savior, namely the field of the earthly or worldly heart.

->Both give us a remarkable prototype.<-

**I. Abel clearly and distinctly foreshadows Christ.** For:
1) Abel was a shepherd: and so was Christ. John 10.
2) He offered from the firstlings of his flock in faith: Hebrews 11:4. And Christ, who was the firstborn, offered himself as the innocent Lamb of God.
3) Abel offered to GOD from the fat—from the best and the internal organs. Christ did the same.
4) GOD testified from heaven regarding his gift, that it pleased Him because it was done out of faith, Hebrews 11:4; doubtlessly through a fire. Leviticus 9:24. Likewise, the Father often gave testimony of His Son: "This is my beloved Son," etc. Indeed, He gave testimony of Him through the heavens at His death.
5) Abel died a violent death: so did Christ.
6) By his own brother.
7) Out of envy. Out of envy they delivered him up. Matthew 27:18.
8) As is commonly held, while he was still young and unmarried.
9) In the field, under the open sky, outside the tents of Adam. Likewise, Christ died outside Jerusalem.
10) Innocently, only because he was a child of God.
11) His blood cries from the earth for vengeance: but Christ’s blood speaks better than the blood of Abel, Hebrews 12:24, for grace and reconciliation.
12) He is thus the first among those who enter heaven. And Christ has become the firstfruits of those who sleep, who rose incorruptible. 1 Corinthians 15:20.

**II. He is also a prototype of the Church and all believers.**
1. Abel means "vanity": Believers recognize that all things are vain.
2. He offered from the firstlings of his flock in faith: they offer themselves to GOD as the firstlings of His creatures. James 1:18.
3. He offered from the fat, etc.
4. GOD testified from heaven, through a fire, that the sacrifice was pleasing to Him: and here, through the Holy Spirit.
5. Abel was persecuted, envied, and slain: these are as well.

<column-break/>

6. His blood cried out from the earth. The souls of those who were slain for the Word of GOD and the testimony of JESUS cry out with a great voice: "Lord, holy and true! How long do you not judge and avenge our blood on those who dwell on the earth?" Revelation 6:9, 10. Properly, however, it is GOD’s own justice that cries out in this way.

->In Cain, we have a prototype I. of the Jews.<-

1. Cain was a farmer. The Jews loved their fields and agriculture all too much. Luke 14:18, 19.
2. He offered only the fruits of the field—poor things that did not cost much.
3. He was a brother-murderer. 1 John 3:12. Thus the Jews killed Christ, who came from them according to the flesh. Therefore, Matthew 23:35.
4. He was the eldest brother, but evil, and became the last. The Gentiles have been preferred over the Jews.
5. He offered without faith—that is, trusting in himself, without a contrite spirit: which is why GOD did not look upon his sacrifice with grace. So it also went with the Jews.
6. The blood of Abel called for vengeance from the earth upon Cain. See Matthew 23:35. The Jews themselves cry out: "His blood be upon us and our children!"
7. Cain was restless and a fugitive on the earth, and his field was cursed. And these brother-murderers GOD has cast out of their land and scattered under all the ends of heaven. They wander in the land, hard-pressed, looking upward in vain, and seeing only the earth below, finding nothing but distress and darkness. Isaiah 8:21. Their land is desolate and cursed. Malachi 4:6.
8. GOD set a mark upon Cain so that everyone would know him. Namely, GOD preserved him as if he had been marked, keeping him for a slow and long punishment of the conscience, as a terror to the godless. Because of this, he gave himself over to all sorts of pleasures and diversions. The Jews are also marked, and GOD preserves them wonderfully, to the horror of the enemies of Christ.
9. Cain went out from the presence of the LORD and dwelt outside of Eden and Adam’s tents. Thus the Jews are cast out into the uttermost darkness, outside of grace: while Japheth dwells in the tents of Shem, etc. <note>A reference to the Gentiles entering the spiritual inheritance of the Jews.</note>

->II. Of all the Ungodly.<-

1. Cain was a farmer: they love the goods of this world.
2. They offer poor, external things.
3. They kill their brothers according to the flesh: they follow the way of Cain, Jude verse 11, because their works are evil.
4. Cain was the eldest brother, which he perhaps relied upon. Many who persecute their brother rely in vain upon "antiquity" <note>Meaning tradition or long-standing status</note>.
5. They offer without faith, without a contrite spirit, trusting in the work itself.
6. They commit many sins that cry out to heaven.
7. They have a mark upon them so that no one kills them. GOD preserves them so that they may feel the sting of a bad conscience here for a long time.
8. They are outside the true Church and grace.
9. They have a bad conscience.
10. And to divert themselves from it, they build cities after their own names and the names of their children, as Cain built Enoch. Genesis 4:17. See Psalm 49:11.

->What concerns us:<-

I. Let us (1) offer (2) the fat of the kidneys (3) in faith in the Son of GOD. (4) Then GOD will also testify through the Holy Spirit that our works are good and pleasing to Him.
II. Let us not be mistaken when we see (1) that it goes for the children of GOD as it did for Abel. The enmity between the seed of the woman and the seed of the serpent still lasts. (2) GOD will avenge our blood, and that shed since the beginning of Christianity, upon the enemies of Christ.
III. Let us not be like Cain: (1) too devoted to the field and farming; (2) envious toward our neighbor, bloodthirsty and grim. (3) Lest we receive a bad conscience and must be fugitives from the presence of the LORD.

<header>The First Book of Moses. Chapter IV.</header>

9. Then the Lord said to Cain: **Where is your brother Abel?** And he said: **I do not know; am I then my brother’s keeper?**

10. And He said: **What have you done? The voice of your brother’s blood cries out to me from the earth!**
<margin>Genesis 18:20, 21. Chapter 19:13. Luke 22:44.</margin>

11. **And now you are cursed upon the land which has opened its mouth** (a) **to receive your brother’s blood from your hand!**
<margin>(a) Revelation 12:16.</margin>

12. **When you till the land, it shall no longer yield its strength to you; restless and fleeing shall you be upon the earth!**
<margin>Deuteronomy 28:65.</margin>

---

Observe here a representation of divine vengeance, which very quickly stirs in the conscience of the sinner; and the blindness of men, who think they can hide their sins in every way, even from God, before whose eyes everything is naked and exposed. Hebrews 11:4, 12:24; Revelation 6:9; Psalm 116:15. And so the blood, especially of the saints, cries out to God for vengeance, and thus always speaks and bears witness to the malice of their persecutors. Hebrews 11:4, 12:24; Revelation 6:9; Psalm 116:15. <note>The author uses these verses to show that "Abel’s blood" is the prototype for all martyred saints.</note> And so such persecutors bring the curse upon themselves and upon the land in which they have ruled, so that people are rooted out of it, and the land must also experience the curse: just as this was fulfilled upon the Jews after their persecution of Christ and the believers, according to the prophecy of Moses concerning them. Deuteronomy 29:22-28. Now since Cain—whom his conscience convinces of the justice of the divine punishment—wishes to despair, and thereby only murmurs against the justice of God and will not bow beneath it or take refuge in grace; yet God has shown a singular example of long-suffering in him, wishing to lure him to repentance, as He reserved the punishment of Cain for Himself and forbade others from it under a threat of sevenfold great vengeance, while simultaneously giving Cain an extraordinary sign of grace for his protection from men with this decree. See Isaiah 66:19.

v. 10. *The voice — cries*] is interpreted in the Chaldean <note>Original: "Chaldäischen," referring to the Aramaic Targums or translations</note> as follows: The voice of the blood of the descendants or generations that should have come from Abel, calling out. For this reason, it is not without cause that it says *bloods* <note>original: "Geblütern"</note> in the Hebrew. For in killing Abel, Cain had shed the blood of all his descendants, all the possibilities of his children, however many might have sprung from him. This is precisely what makes the sin of murder the most detestable of all others; as the blood-guilt which David also means: and then, because he who takes a life takes away all the good that hangs upon that life.

Otherwise, it is also noted that in this deed committed by Cain, seven sins come together. Namely, there is 1) Envy. 2) Deceit. 3) Murder. 4) Fratricide. 5) The first murder. 6) Grieving the parents, 7) and lying to God.

<column-break/>

13. **But Cain said to the Lord: My iniquity is greater than can be forgiven!** <note>This can also be translated from the Hebrew as "My punishment is greater than I can bear."</note>

14. **Behold, you have driven me out today from the land, and I must hide myself from your face; and I must be restless and fleeing on the earth; and it will happen that whoever finds me will slay me!**

15. **But the Lord said to him: Therefore, whoever slays Cain, it shall be avenged sevenfold. And the Lord set a mark on Cain, so that no one who found him would strike him dead.**

16. **So Cain went out from the presence of the Lord, and dwelt in the land of Nod, toward the east of Eden.**

17. **And**

---

v. 14. *Must — from your face — be fleeing*) What is fleeing from God other than withdrawing oneself from that serenity <note>original: "Gelassenheit," a term often used by mystics like Meister Eckhart to mean yielding to God's will</note> through which one allows oneself to wander in the error of all human ways, and to go astray in the paths of vanity on the earth, since one has left the highest Truth, which is God Himself, and at the same time the infallible connection through which one was bound to Him in total self-denial? Certainly, whoever removes himself even for a moment from the almighty Protector is always exposed to the fury of his enemies.

v. 16. *Nod*] Jerome in his *Hebraic Traditions* <note>original: "Traditionibus Hebr."</note> on the 1st Book of Moses, says the word *Nod* does not signify a certain region, and wishes it to be understood as the state of the fleeing and exiled Cain, so that he remained in no certain place but was always fleeting. He wished to prove this from the Hebrew word <term>נוד</term> <note>Nod</note>, which signifies a fleeing exile, and stems from the word <term>נוד</term> <note>Nud</note>, which means one who wanders to and fro. However, Moses notes that it lay to the east of Eden. And Josephus expands the history further:
> "When he had now traversed many lands with his wife,
> "he finally settled in a place called *Najada*, established a household there, and fathered children. Yet he did not use this punishment for improvement, but rather became worse, following his own lusts and desires even to the detriment of other people, amassing much property through violence and robbery, surrounding himself with all kinds of murderers and scoundrels, and leading them into all evil deeds. Moreover, he also invented weights and measures, and with this abolished the previous old honesty and simplicity of life, and transformed and perverted it into a base and self-serving existence. He was the first to place boundary stones in the field, etc."

->The Septuagint <note>original: "LXX"</note> have rendered it as <term>Ναὶδ</term> <note>Naid</note>.<-

---

It is not unbelievable that such a piece of land is that region in Persia which was previously called *Susiana*, and now *Khuzistan*: since it was located toward the east of Paradise, and is mentioned by the ancient geographer Ptolemy in his description of the land of *Susiana* as a city therein called *Anuchta*, which Huetius <note>Pierre Daniel Huet (1630-1721), a famous French scholar</note> considers to be Cain’s city *Hanoch* <note>Enoch</note>.

Cain had to depart from the community of the Lord and from his father’s face, in whose house faith in the divine promise and the service of God in sacrifices were still maintained. But as he had formerly been devoted to agriculture, he now gave himself over entirely to earthly things and made the beginning of building a city, where the gathered mass of people strove only for lordship over one another, for the violent harming of the same, and for the invention of all kinds of means for this and for lusts, placing their happiness in their outward increase. Hence Lamech among them also fell into polygamy against God’s institution, Malachi 2:14, 15, 16; Matthew 19:4, etc., in order to indulge his lust and violence: since he was doubtless one of those tyrants in Chapter 6:4, who filled the earth with all sorts of outrages, v. 11, and his children also invented the instruments for it, the swords, with which they—doubtless both within and without the city they built, which must have continually grown—would have expanded their wicked reign by slaying both old and young.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Genesis Chapter 4, moving from Cain’s exile to the genealogy of his descendants and the establishment of the first city. # Chapter IV. The First Book of Moses.

**Left Column:**

17. And Cain knew his wife; and she became pregnant and gave birth to Enoch. And he built a city, and named the city after his son’s name, Enoch. <margin>Chapter 46:9.</margin>

18. And to Enoch was born Irad: and Irad fathered Mehujael: and Mehujael fathered Methushael: and Methushael fathered Lamech.

19. And Lamech took for himself two wives: the name of the one was Adah, and the name of the other was Zillah.

---

<margin>Lamech may have boasted of this to his family during a joyful feast—how he need fear no court of law, but had the power in his hands to subject everything to his authority, even at the cost of their lives. And though he may have occasionally suffered wounds and welts, no one was in a position to take revenge on him. Since he had turned the freedom granted to Cain into wantonness, he believed he was in a position to maintain it even more through his own power. Through such a regime of outrage and through lust, the first world drew upon itself the divine judgment, after justice and moderation had, as it were, vanished from the earth.</margin>

<margin>v. 17. Enoch)</margin> The translators <note>The German text uses "Hanoch," a transliteration common in some older German Bibles.</note> have seen fit to call him this, though it is no other name than Enoch, with which his father named him. Thus, ungodly parents can give their like-minded children beautiful names. Better, however, is the counsel of the wise man in Proverbs 22:6.

<margin>Built a city)</margin> Not immediately: For who was to help him build it? Who was to have inhabited it? Rather, it was long afterward, after he had fathered sons and daughters, and sons and daughters had been born to them. It was also no sudden work. Therefore, it does not actually say he "built" [present tense], but he "was building" [imperfect/continuous]. And Moses undoubtedly laid the foundation of a spiritual understanding here with foresight, as Augustine also noted. A man does not become the worst version of himself quickly.

This city of Cain and the City of God began to run their course through birth and death throughout the entire human race. All ungodly men in their various generations who walk in the way of Cain are builders of this city; just as, on the contrary, those who walk in the way of the Lord are builders of His city. Let everyone, therefore, take good care what, how, and with whom they build. For Cain and his builders have the most beautiful appearances and pretenses that can ever be. The name of his son and his city was Enoch—meaning "dedicated" or "consecrated." Also among his descendants are found Mehujael—a "preacher of God"; and Lamech—a "humble man." <note>The author is noting the irony of these godly names appearing in an ungodly lineage.</note> Therefore, it should be of great importance to us to recognize and distinguish the two cities accurately. One is the city of the love of God and of neighbor, Philadelphia <note>original: "Philadelphia," Greek for "brotherly love"</note>, the City of David. The other is the city of the devil; and must therefore be envy, hatred, and lack of love. Men begin to build and inhabit this city when they separate from one another, just as Cain did when he departed from the face of God.

<margin>City of Enoch)</margin> That Huetius <note>Pierre Daniel Huet, a 17th-century French scholar.</note> understands the city of Anuchta, described by Ptolemy in the province of Susiana, to be this city—since the syllable <term>ta</term> is only an addition of the Chaldean language, and thus the actual name is Anuch, which is the same as Enoch—has just been considered.

<column-break/>

**Right Column:**

20. And Adah gave birth to Jabal. He was the father of those who dwell in tents and of those who have livestock.

21. And his brother's name was Jubal. He was the father of all those who play the harp and the pipe.

22. And Zillah also gave birth to Tubal-Cain, a master of all copper and iron smithing. And the sister of Tubal-Cain was Naamah.

23. And Lamech said to his wives: "Adah and Zillah, hear my voice! You wives of Lamech, give ear to my speech! For I have slain men to my wounding, and young men to my bruising."

24. "If Cain shall be avenged sevenfold, then Lamech seventy and sevenfold."

25. And

---

<margin>v. 19. Lamech)</margin> Cain’s faithful and daring successor, who, according to Josephus’ report, fathered 27 sons. He is said to have been entirely devoted to alchemy <note>original: "Chymie," here referring to early chemical/alchemical arts</note>, worked with earthen vessels, and taught such arts to his descendants.

<margin>v. 20. Father/Originator)</margin> Whereas they previously kept the herds in one place, he introduced moving them from one place to another, and thus also adapting their dwellings accordingly. The Scythians did the same afterward.

<margin>Tents)</margin> Their form was this: They set up four wooden poles or columns, and upon and around these they hung curtains or carpets, and made it firm with ropes.

<margin>v. 21. Jubal</margin> carries "jubilation" in his name.

<margin>v. 22. Tubal-Cain)</margin> This is the Vulcan <note>original: "Vulcanus," the Roman god of fire and metalworking.</note> of the poets, and was an experienced naturalist who invented mining and the arts of iron- and goldsmithing.

<margin>Sister of Tubal-Cain, Naamah)</margin> "The Beautiful One," or Venus. <note>The author links biblical figures to Roman mythology.</note>

<margin>v. 20-22. Livestock — Harp-playing — Copper and iron smiths.)</margin> They also devoted themselves to navigation, astrology, and medicine; meanwhile, they loved augury <note>original: "Wahrsagerey aus den Vögeln," divination from birds</note>, prepared poisons, murdered one another, waged wars with each other, gluttonized, drank, blasphemed the godly, and put God entirely out of their sight.

Thus the people of the ancient world—the house or lineage of Cain—were at all times sharp-witted and ingenious in inventing profit and the pleasures of the world, as well as the means and ways to defend and protect themselves in the enjoyment of the same, and to harm others. And therein they lived lustfully until the day the Great Flood came.

<margin>That the Holy Spirit shows</margin> how the seed of Cain were the inventors of these things is a clear proof that these things were the sole work and concern in which the Cainites practiced and spent their time. Whereas, on the other hand, Seth, Enoch, Noah, Shem, and their seed were occupied with divine things. The Cainites were entirely occupied with such things as only concerned this external life. But the Sethites were, and still are, entirely or above all things occupied with the investigation of things that concern the future or divine life. Thus also—

---

If our whole heart, thoughts, and desires are occupied and busy with the things of this external life, with earthly things, how are we better than they? We are exactly what they were: namely, Cainites. For according to a man’s thoughts, will, inclinations, works, and deeds, he is judged; indeed, according to those same things shall be his reward and retribution. Or if one wishes to appeal to Sunday, when one might be occupied with spiritual matters—this is often done sloppily and wickedly enough; and besides, Cain offered sacrifices too. The fear, faith, hope, and love of God must animate our whole life. All our outward professional affairs must receive their sap, power, and life from them.

<margin>Numbers 24:17.</margin>
According to the LORD’S own decree / just as from the fallen, corrupted Adam there came a fallen, corrupted Cain according to his image / so also from the restored and renewed Adam came Seth according to his likeness. Seth alone is named here from Adam / because he was to be the forefather of all believers in the latter days: to whom the name Seth <note>Seth means "appointed" or "substituted."</note> should be all the more significant / because they are not only appointed for a blessing on the new earth / but must also place their special trust in the LORD during the great tribulations that precede it.

<margin>Psalm 73:28. Job 35:10-11.</margin>
Just as GOD also places wisdom / the new image / into the inner being <note>original: "Nieren" (kidneys/reins), historically considered the seat of emotions and wisdom.</note> of all believers.

And indeed, that this likeness of Adam was a righteous likeness and the likeness of God / is revealed clearly and brightly from verses 1 and 2. Thus, just as the sinful Adam begat Cain after his sinful likeness / so the righteous Adam begat Seth after his righteous likeness. For Adam was here recreated through renewal according to the image of GOD. An enlightened teacher says of the common explanation / which assumes it refers to the sinful and corrupted image / "In truth, it is a great misfortune for one who has received a bad name / that among thousands of us, there is not one who may receive a good name again."

Meanwhile, the common opinion can nevertheless be maintained for this reason / because the remnants of corruption are still found even among the reborn / especially in the beginning.

<margin>v. 3. 4.</margin>
**Adam begat Seth / -- and sons and daughters)** Even when this work of marital love remains within its proper boundaries / it is a means wisely ordained by GOD in this time / to bring forth children / whom one can find again in eternity with great pleasure and joy / and present as a true gift of the LORD before the eyes of their Creator.

And so one should rightly build God's temple together / rather than increasing the crowd of godless children through the abuse of procreation / and merely preparing material for the fire. If, however, Christ's love had room in the parents and Christ lived [in them] / then children could again be begotten after GOD'S image.

However, Christian married couples face the danger in their state / that they beget children at such a time and in such a condition where the kingdom of darkness has power / and the spiritual forces of destruction may seize them before / during / and after birth. They would not need to fear this / if such children were ordained to come to light in another and better world.

But if Christian parents succeed with their children / so that they are brought through the corruption of this wicked world unharmed as plants of the kingdom of heaven to triumph; then they are to be considered so much more blessed than others / who might be ordained to bring forth children (who remained hidden within them) outside of such danger perhaps only in a future, better world: because there must be more joy in heaven before GOD and his angels over a single human child who is snatched from the great peril of this evil world through the way of repentance / than over 99 other righteous ones who do not need repentance.

**v. 6-8. Seth** / the third son of Adam / was so highly renowned in his time for his special godliness / that / as Theodoretes <note>Theodoret of Cyrus (c. 393 – c. 458 AD), an influential theologian and bishop.</note> reports / he was called a god on earth / and his sons and descendants were called the sons of GOD / who are said to have invented astronomy and the science of the heavens' course. Some also attribute the invention of the Hebrew letters to him. He is also said to have erected two pillars for the benefit of his descendants / or they themselves did / one of which was made of stone / the other of bricks made of clay / and they engraved their sciences into them / so that they would not be forgotten / and so that neither fire nor water could destroy them / so that / if the brick pillar were destroyed in water / the stone one would remain / and place the recorded things before the eyes of men. For they had heard a prophecy from Adam regarding the destruction of all things / once by fire / the other time by water. The brick pillar is said to have still stood in Syria in the times of Josephus, the Jewish historian.

**Years)** Among other things, the reasons for the long lives of people before the Flood were / that they might have time to contemplate the works of GOD / and especially the word of the first promise / and the covenant of grace established therein / and the divine wisdom contained within: in which two parts their theology consisted. Also / so that they could invent and properly establish all kinds of arts useful for human life / and so that the world might be more fruitfully populated; and also / so that / exhausted by the labor and hardship of this life / they might long for the better [life] after death and rightly prepare themselves.

Some indeed invent very small "lunar years" before the Flood / which lasted only one month / because otherwise the length of life seems too great to them. But instead of such an opinion having any basis / many absurdities follow from it: for example, that some would have begotten children already in their 6th or 7th year / and these patriarchs would not have become older than many in our own time / and none would have reached their hundredth year. Without doubt, the Mosaic years are of one kind and all of the same length. Without doubt, the years here are to be understood in the same way as in the 11th chapter.

Rather, others hold / that many extended their lives to so many hundreds of years because they did not consume meat and all sorts of things / but were content with the plants of the earth and simple foods. They were closer to the first origin / their nature was better and fresher / the food and nourishment simpler / the growths and plants more healing and healthy / the air still purer / and GOD'S grace / works / and wonders / which had to be proclaimed and well-impressed from child to grandchild / as well as the propagation of the human race itself / and especially the mystery of the promised seed of the woman / required it to be so.

> Just as this entire chapter / to which Luke points in the third chapter of his Gospel / has its focus on the lineage of the LORD Christ / which is traced herein from Seth to Shem; so Enos is the second [patriarch] mentioned in this line.

> As a pious and righteous man / he preached alongside his father Seth against the idolatry of Cain and his descendants / took great care regarding divine worship / and established a separation between the godly and the godless. Therefore, particularly in his time, the human race was divided into two parties / which held their own separate assemblies: one called the Sethites or Sethians / the others Cainites / the former also called Children or Sons of GOD / the latter Children or Sons of Men / as fleshly, earthly-minded people, named after their way of life; because the Cainites, already from the time of Cain / of whom it is said / that he went out from the face of the LORD / and thus simultaneously from the fellowship of the Church / had separated themselves from the Sethites not only in spirit but also in location; although they later began to harmonize with each other in evil more than was good / as the following chapter indicates.

<margin>(a) Book 1 on Monasticism.</margin>
> However, although Enos was zealously concerned with the propagation of true religion / he did not for that reason ordain the monastic life / as Bellarmine (a) <note>Robert Bellarmine (1542–1621) was a prominent Jesuit Cardinal; the author here disputes Catholic claims about the ancient origins of monks.</note> and others would have it.
