### Chapter V. The First Book of Moses.
f 3

21. **Enoch** had lived sixty-five years / and fathered **Methuselah**.
22. And **Enoch** walked constantly with **God** / after he fathered **Methuselah** / three hundred years; and fathered sons and daughters.

---

**Enoch** particularly let his light shine through a steady walk before **God** / which the Apostle explains <note>referring to Hebrews 11:5–6</note> as his having pleased **God**, and thus through faith he obtained this testimony; in that same faith he drew near to **God** and sought Him as a rewarder. *Hebrews 11:5, 6*. This constant walking before **God** means to always have **God** before one's eyes in all one's deeds / as the One who sees, knows, and will judge everything; and therefore to follow **God** and not depart from Him / so that one arranges his actions and omissions according to His holy will. It means to constantly keep before oneself the ultimate purpose for which one was created / namely to recognize and praise **God** his Creator and Redeemer / which is true wisdom; and to constantly strive for the means to reach this end / which is true prudence. See *Job 28:28*. Because of his exceptional godliness, **God** also wished to demonstrate a special example of gracious pleasure and reward in him / when he was taken away so that he did not see death / and was not found / though he may have been sought by both believers and unbelievers / because **God** had taken him to Himself. From this, the believers surely received a divine testimony / that their souls would also primarily be taken up by **God** into eternal rest. See *Hebrews 11:5; 2 Kings 2:9, 11, 16, etc.*

**v. 21. Enoch — Methuselah)** He who lived the shortest life on earth before the Deluge <note>the Great Flood</note> fathered the one who lived the longest life among all the fathers. A short life well-lived in the acceptable year of the Lord obtains the longest life / namely, eternal life.

**v. 22, 24. walked with God)** The Hebrew word that expresses "walking" simultaneously signifies constancy and perseverance in the good way of life. And because "walking" is a continuous movement / it indicates here all the more a constant persistence and walking in holiness and righteousness / and thus pleasing **God** / and our own radiating and returning joy, contentment, and pleasure in this constantly persevering walk and the pleasure of **God**. And that such a full meaning was expected by the translators is confirmed by the Apostle in *Hebrews 11:5*.

**Luther** <note>Martin Luther, the Reformer</note> translated this quite well here and regarding Noah; he led a "divine walk" <note>original German: "göttlicher Wandel"</note>; as he otherwise insists in his testimonies upon such a divine life / not only there in eternity / but also here in time / and even deemed it highly necessary to impress it upon children in his Small Catechism.

And that certainly has great significance! Much is required for a divine walk.

The phrase itself implies / that in such a walk one must necessarily stand in His holy fellowship and acquaintance / and it means even more than "walking *before* God." A child walks *before* his father / and always keeps his eyes upon him. But a friend also interacts intimately and familiarly with another.

However, this duty / to walk with **God** and to please Him / and to abound more in such doing / is common to all believers. Just as all the ancestors of **Enoch** / from the restored **Adam** down to him / walked in that very same way of life and holiness; although **Enoch** was the first who was honored with this famous testimony / because he walked more excellently and precisely than others. It is required of us all with every right. For we have the very same **God**. His will is the same; His way is the same.

Just as the **seventh from Adam** (*Epistle of Jude v. 14*) walked / so shall the believers in the "seventh time" <note>an interpretation of the final age of the world as a Sabbath</note> walk holily with **God** on earth / and no less enter into the transformation.

<column-break/>

23. So all the days of **Enoch** were three hundred and sixty-five years.
24. And because **Enoch** constantly walked with **God** / he was no longer present: for **God** had taken him away.

->25. Me-<-

---

**v. 24. was not)** Whoever wishes to walk in the way of life or with **God** / must resolve to be of no regard in this wicked world.

> The people of **God** are His hidden ones. *Psalm 83:3*.

When the Scripture speaks of such people / who walk with **God** and please Him / who continue and persevere in such walking / and find joy and pleasure in such a walk with **God**; and it is said that these are the ones whom the Scripture calls "perfect" / then the immediate question is usually: Where does one find such people? But who would tell such a thing to others / even if one knew of some? Especially since they are often surrounded by the **Cainite race** <note>the "Cainite race" refers to the worldly, ungodly line of descent from Cain</note>.

And how can a pious man / who strives to walk with **God** and to please Him / hope to please the **Cainite race**? They walk contrary ways. **Enoch** and his followers walk on a lonely path / on a narrow and slim track / which few people find / and upon which even fewer walk. And who will love or respect such a person? Who will consider him happy or blessed? Who will desire to be like him? Those who walk in the way of **Cain** / they love those who walk in that same way with them / and hold them in high honor; and they hate those who oppose them therein and walk on a better path. Also, after every higher degree of walking with **God** and of pleasing Him, there arises a higher adversity and more vehement ill-will and displeasure of men against those who thus walk with **God** / and have to walk to please Him: So much so / that if a man were to walk as **Christ** walked / (which is indeed the duty of all men who are in **Christ**) such a person would also be hated just as **Christ** was.

**God had taken him away)** That **Enoch** was translated into Paradise without physical death / has been held as true by many Jewish as well as Christian teachers / although the former mixed the matter with fables.

Thus says **Athanasius** <note>an influential 4th-century Church Father</note>: He was translated into Paradise / and did not see the common death of nature.

It was indeed possible / since **Paul** in his lifetime came into Paradise and was caught up.

Otherwise, in him we have yet another beautiful type <note>a "type" is a historical person or event that foreshadows Jesus Christ</note> of **Christ**.

1. **Enoch** led a divine life: **Christ** could be convicted of no sin.
2. He was a prophet: *Jude v. 14, 15* / and **Christ** was no less a prophet.
3. He was the **seventh from Adam**. *Jude v. 14*. **Christ** was the twice-seventh from **Abraham** to **David** / from **David** to the Babylonian captivity / from there to His birth: *Matthew 1:17* / indeed, the seventieth after **Enoch**.
4. He was taken up body and soul into heaven / and was seen no more. **Christ** likewise.
5. He was the first before the Law / just as **Elijah** was under the Law / and **Christ** under the Gospel. *1 Corinthians 15:20*.
6. The third who departed from the world. For **Adam** and **Abel** were dead <note>meaning their physical presence left the world</note>. Thus **Christ** was the third who thus ascended to heaven.
7. The **seventh from Adam** was taken to heaven through what was arguably the first miracle. **Christ** will draw us to Himself on the "Sabbath of this world" through the last miracle.
8. And indeed after 365 prophetic days or years / as many days as the sun's course describes. Thus **Christ** takes us after the great year and course of the Gospel. *Psalm 19*.

# The First Book of Moses. | Chapter V.

25. **Methuselah** had lived one hundred eighty-seven years / and fathered **Lamech**.
26. And **Methuselah** lived / after he fathered **Lamech** / seven hundred eighty-two years / and fathered sons and daughters.
27. So all the days of **Methuselah** were nine hundred sixty-nine years / and he died.
28. **Lamech** had lived one hundred eighty-two years / and fathered a son.
29. And he called his name **Noah** / and said: This one will comfort us in our work and in the painful labor of our hands / upon the earth / which the **Lord** has cursed.
30. And **Lamech** lived / after he fathered **Noah** / five hundred ninety-five years / and fathered sons and daughters.
31. So all the days of **Lamech** were seven hundred seventy-seven years / and he died.

<note>Commentary on verses 25-31</note>
v. 26. 30. **Lived)** Where? Athanasius Kircher <note>a famous 17th-century Jesuit scholar and polymath</note> in his book *Noah’s Ark* <note>original: "Arca Noë"</note> maintains that the patriarchs resided in the region of Eden where Paradise had been, and he understands Eden to be Assyria—which includes not only Syria and the entire Mount Lebanon, along with the cis-Jordanian part of Judea, but also Babylonia, Mesopotamia, and Armenia. He considers it indisputable that this was the common dwelling of the first patriarchs, and there is hardly anyone who contradicts this.

v. 27. Methuselah brought his life to the highest peak / to 969 years. Thus, no one reached a thousand years / which is reserved for the faithful in the Glorious Kingdom <note>referring to the Millennial reign of Christ</note>. 
Adam and he, with their lifespans, filled the entire time / that lasted between the Creation and the Flood. And because he lived on earth for 243 years at the same time as Adam / he undoubtedly received instruction and knowledge of all things from him / and left this to his descendants / especially to Noah and his sons. 
This man is the first / to whom is attributed the most ancient way of philosophizing / which consists of fables, parables, and proverbs.

**Died)** In several consistent copies, it was found / that Methuselah died 6 years before the Flood; so writes Augustine. However, the Hebrew texts / which one should rightly follow in this matter / testify to the contrary, that he died in the very year / that the Flood came—indeed, only 7 days before / during which Noah mourned him, and for which God waited: as a testimony of the great patience of God in the given span of life / that such time might be used for improvement.

<column-break/>

32. And **Noah** was five hundred years old / and **Noah** fathered **Shem**, **Ham**, and **Japheth**.

<note>Commentary on verse 32</note>
That Noah delayed his marriage until he was 500 years old / gives cause to think / that he may have chosen the single state / in order to care for the things of the Lord, and how he might please the Lord: *1 Corinthians 7:32*. But that he afterwards proceeded to marriage by divine impulse / so that he might become a faithful founding father of the second world after the Flood.

**Shem)** Because he always has precedence / and is named first / whenever the three brothers are mentioned; some wish to conclude / that he was the eldest. But that is not a sufficient reason. If we compare the age of Shem in *Chapter 11:10* / with the age of Noah when he began to father children / here and in *Chapter 7:6*; it is found to be otherwise. For Shem was 100 years old / when he fathered Arphaxad / 2 years after the Flood (*Chapter 11:10*). Now Noah was 600 years old in the year of the Flood (*Chapter 7:6*) / and thus 602 years old two years later. Subtract Shem’s 100 years from this; 502 remains / and so Noah fathered him in the 502nd year of his age. Therefore, Japheth was the firstborn in the 500th year of Noah. Shem, however, is mentioned first / because through him the family of believers was propagated down to Abraham. See *Chapter 10:21*.

The word **Shem** means a **Name**. By the Kabbalists <note>Jewish mystics</note>, Christ is called *Shem haggadol*, *Shem hammichbod*—the Great, the Honorable Name. "He is Shem the Great," says the *Targum of Jerusalem* <note>an Aramaic translation and commentary on the Hebrew Bible</note>.

The number seven of the first patriarchs is the root or "stem-number" / from which the thousand-fold number of Christ’s Kingdom with His saints grows. One need only multiply the ten by itself: ten times ten / and so ten times ten. 
From the multiplication of the faithful, the Kingdom of God becomes full at the end of the world. *Isaiah 60:22, Romans 11:25*. This is reserved for the faithful in the Glorious Kingdom.

<note>Extended commentary at bottom of page</note>

v. 29. **Lamech** indicates here / that one must not spend this life in worldly pleasure / but in the sweat of the brow and the pain of the hands / and thus in repentant recognition of human misery: but that one must also turn to divine rest and comfort / to seek such in the promised Seed of the woman <note>a reference to the future Messiah</note>.

This **Lamech** was quite different from the one who descended from Cain according to *Chapter 4:18-19* / and was a divine prophet. 
After Moses has recounted 7 generations from Cain in the previous chapter / he calculates here 10 generations from Adam to Noah. By this, he clearly signifies / that the good shall finally overcome the evil / and that / after the darkness has passed / the children of light will shine as lights in the world.

**Comforting)** To give refreshment and relief / rest from our work or deed and the toil of our hands. 
To comfort that same age of the time in its work and toil and the curse of the earth is a broad expression / which does not fit this place very well. But he gave relief and rest to his father and his lineage by the removal of the curse from the earth; of which we do not read / that it was even promised from the first time it was laid upon them / until Noah's days. *Chapter 8:21*. And he did that through the invention of certain means / by which the labor of men was eased / and their frustrations sweetened: 1) as he taught them the manner and way to plow the earth / and for that purpose invented the plow and other tools of agriculture; 2) through the planting of the vineyard / and through instruction on how wine should be used.

The true **Noah** <note>Christ</note>, however, gives to **Lamech** / the poor, crushed, and humbled soul / rest from all its work and toil in sins. *Isaiah 61:1, Haggai 2:8, Matthew 11:28*.

v. 31. **died** 5 years before the Flood and before his father, v. 25, 26.

<header>Chap. VI. The First Book of Moses. 47</header>

## Chapter VI.

### The Corruption of the First World.

And it happened / as men began to multiply on the earth / that daughters were born to them.

2. And the children of God saw the daughters of men / that they were beautiful / and took for themselves wives from all whom they chose. <margin>Ezra 9:1, 2.</margin>

3. Then

---

The great corruption / which brought about the downfall of the first world / consisted in the prevailing lusts of the flesh and a haughty life / where one sought to rule over the other. The former was also expressed in the fact that those who called themselves after God / and thereby confessed that they held with God / nevertheless did not marry in the Lord / <margin>1 Cor. 7:39.</margin> so that they might have looked toward the fear of God and faith in the promise / in order to seek the divine seed / to propagate such in their children : but rather they loved only the outward form and beauty / and did not care whether they were given over to pleasures and vices ; whereby prayer is indeed hindered / <margin>1 Pet. 3:7.</margin> without which no blessing can come upon the children. See Chap. 18:19. And such corrupted marriages are also noted by the Savior / that in the last times they would be marrying and giving in marriage / <margin>Matt. 24:38.</margin> namely only according to the perverted lust of the flesh.

And I believe / we have no reason / to look far for examples / or to wait for another time. For what is the intention in most marriages of today’s Christians but impurity / lust / money and property / honor and respect / and the like? And so the procreation does not happen for the benefit of the Kingdom of God. Therefore it has come to pass / that the world has always become worse / and its wickedness always greater. For the life of the parents is generally filled with sins / which / through their evil example / spread of their own accord to their children / who / being raised in evil / increase the number of the wicked. From this has sprung such a perverted and populous propagation of men / that there is no longer any means / to abolish the evil: because every person walks the same perverted path / and habit has turned into a second nature. In this manner / in the use of that which should be holy / there is mostly nothing found but the sin of lewdness and filthiness / in that people behave much more unsuitably therein than the dumb cattle. Here one sees the cause / why the world was condemned : namely because God is no longer known nor loved in marriage.

Nevertheless / the precious name of God must be spread over it all as a cover for shame. The greatest disorder and perversion of all divine will is blasphemously called an ordinance and institution of God and the state of holy matrimony. All this comes from the deception of false teachers / who for the sake of external circumstances <note>original: "accidentien", likely referring to fees or social standing</note> just like the heathen priests approve / bless / and declare everything holy / and even lead the way with their own examples.

<column-break/>

Among all things / which God established in nature / nothing is so holy / as the marital union / which connects people in love through a completely perfect union with one another. If this should not have been / according to the sense and purpose of the Creator ; then God would have let people be born and procreated like fish / or in some other way : which his wisdom and omnipotence could certainly have done. But because he wanted to have in nature a prototype of the union of his powers / and of the perfect covenant that he intended to make with men ; he thus ordained it / that human procreation should happen through the joining of two bodies : so that they might remain continually united to his will through a bond of love / in body as well as in will. But instead of marrying / to reach the twofold goal / which God sets before us ; namely the preservation of a perfect unity among his true children / and the increase of the same through procreation : people commonly marry / only to satisfy their desires. The goal / for which God instituted it / has completely vanished from the memory of those who wish to marry. It is enough for them / if they can satiate their desires. On the rest they do not think / except perhaps by chance.

Thus man perverts all good into evil / and corrupts all things through his sins. Therefore / the current way of people pairing for the sake of procreation is something unclean in the eyes of chaste souls / of which they are ashamed. And in truth / there is likely nothing more unholy than the union of two bodies through the spirit of fleshly desire ; because such is nothing else than a fountain of all sins : just as on the contrary nothing holier is to be found / than a marital union / which happens between two persons / who have dedicated their will to God ; because thereby three things are united / which then are no more than one ; namely the will of God / of the groom / and of the bride. Thus marriage must and should be a heaven on earth.

---

v. 2. **the children of God)** Many Fathers <note>the "Church Fathers" or early Christian theologians</note>, such as Justin Martyr, Irenaeus, Ambrose, Tertullian, Clement of Alexandria, Cyprian, etc. were of the opinion / that the angels had mixed with the female persons on earth / married / and produced a kind of evil spirit from these marriages : and Bebelius (a) thinks / they had been led astray by the translation of the 70 Interpreters <note>the Septuagint</note>, who gave this place as / <margin>the angels of God. <note>original Greek: "οἱ ἄγγελοι τοῦ Θεοῦ"</note></margin> But because it was already thought above / that Seth because of his uncommon godliness was called a god / this way of speaking can without doubt be most comfortably understood according to the letter as the children of Seth / of whom it is also mentioned in Chap. 4:26 / that they began in the times of Enos to call themselves by the name of the LORD.

The children of God are the offspring of his grace in those souls / which in his hands are entirely pure / yet / as soon as they find themselves in man / they become adulterated through the mixing of the creature / as the nature wants to unite its own offspring daringly with grace : and so that it can accomplish this all the more smoothly / it seeks in nature what suits it best. This it then attributes to grace / and what comes from grace it attributes to nature. Hereby GOD is angered / that his grace is thus abused ; he therefore draws it back again / and assures / that his spirit shall no longer be with man ; because he is entirely fleshly and earthly. Therefore he takes back from him everything / that belongs to Him. And because nothing more remains for the creature but the workings of nature / it finds itself so loathsome / that it begins to hate itself greatly. It would also completely despair of regaining the Spirit of GOD / if there were not a light in it / which assured it / that we can go out of ourselves / to enter back into GOD : because for man there is a time / namely a time which God himself shortens / in which man is left to himself / or man is a man ; which is expressed very clearly through these words / the time of man shall only be one hundred and twenty years. As if he wanted to say : I have set limits to the corruption of man. This promise now drives the one who wants to be faithful to his GOD / to rid himself of himself as quickly as possible / through unceasing self-denial. And this is also man’s entire trust after the Fall / that one can eventually die to oneself / through a perfect self-denial.

<margin>(a) in *Antediluvian Ecclesiastical History*. see Sulpicius Severus, *Sacred History*, book 1, chap. 2.</margin>

<header>The First Book of Moses. Chapter VI. 48</header>

# 3. Then the Lord said: My Spirit shall not judge these men forever.

The Lord testifies herewith / that he could not always persist with his Spirit of punishment / especially among these people / who wanted to be called children of God : since they were also only flesh / and thus without Spirit, <margin>Jude 1:19</margin> indeed, they had only fought against the punishing Spirit in Noah / and will have resisted the same with all kinds of excuses / just as it happens in these last corrupted times ; when people are resentful toward those who punish in the gate / that is / publicly / and regard those who teach uprightly as an abomination. <margin>Amos 5:10</margin>

**Said)** This is the next step toward downfall / when it is so stated. This speech once again flowed directly from the mouth of the eternal Creator himself / and is an expression of his innermost heart. Certainly, therefore, all the words must have great significance.

**My Spirit)** By this, various people understand the acts of the created spirit or the soul breathed in by God / as a breath of life / which men did not follow / and therefore had to perish in their mortal flesh / though they should have lived eternally according to the soul. The Jewish interpreters understand the wrath of God under the term "Spirit" : whom Jerome <note>original: "Hieronymus"</note> also followed. But Luther rightly <note>In this context, the archaic German "billig" means justly or rightly.</note> rejects this / because here the Spirit is clearly set in opposition to the flesh. Rather

It is thereby sufficiently given to be recognized / that the eternal Godhead primarily reveals, communicates, and puts itself forward / through the eternal Spirit / which is the divine breath and respiration.

But here the Father / the Word / and the Spirit are together. For what else is it / when it says / And the Lord spoke / but the eternal Word / Jesus Christ / through whom the Father makes known and speaks all his will from the beginning in the world. So then also no other than the eternal Spirit is meant / who proceeds from the Father and the Son / and steps to the hearts of men.

Most people, to be sure, imagine regarding God and his Spirit / either that he is very far from them / or else stands idly by them / and remains like a dead, mute idol. But a person cannot easily inflict greater harm upon themselves / than when they imagine and let themselves be persuaded by Satan / that the Spirit of God is far enough from them / that he does not even concern himself with them / let alone that he must or wants to be so near or even in their heart.

Certainly such a person remains stuck in their corruption / lives according to all self-will and unbroken insolence from day to day / and perceives nothing of the working of God and his Spirit. With that, he is as good as ruined : he remains a slave to the evil spirit and his own desires / which sink him into destruction.

One sees this all too clearly in all those / who live in the world without God as such atheists or ungodly-minded people / how they fall from one vice into another / and can never truly become sober from any. For

If such people believed in or accepted a God / who is closer to them / than they are to themselves ; they would arrange their lives quite differently.

Thus we should never hold this so near and present Spirit in low esteem / or lose sight of him / as flighty nature is quite inclined to do : but rather mirror ourselves in the sad examples of such people / who were not even faithful in natural knowledge / nor became obedient to the Spirit of the Creator. As God’s own testimony here sounds: **My Spirit**

Ah, if people understood / what a blessing it could be for them / if they let themselves be punished <note>In this historical theological context, "punishment" (Bestrafung) often refers to the internal conviction of sin or correction by the Holy Spirit.</note> : how gladly would they let themselves be disciplined by the Holy Spirit ! how dear such punishment would be to them ! No one could make them suspicious of it.

Let no one believe / that he can dispense with such discipline of the Almighty. One can perceive it quite clearly in small children / what they become / if one lets them live for a while without correction. From this one should indeed notice / how necessary the punishment of the Spirit is for us / and how without the same we would be worse than wild animals. Had God not deemed it strictly necessary / he would not have lamented here / that men neglected it ; much less would he have later let them all drown so miserably. But precisely for this reason / because they did not follow words / they had to experience deeds and plagues.

And so the Spirit allows himself to be resisted—but not to be cornered / nor silenced. For one thing, he is no dead, fruitless being / who would let a person go on in their laziness and security. Where he is and finds room / there he urges repentance and faith for salvation.

Whoever does not want this to happen to them / with that person the Spirit of God cannot and will not strive and wear himself out forever / but he finally leaves them / and gives them over to the whims of their own heart / and thus over to the destroyer.

In this we now have a precious testimony / how a man can certainly hinder, grieve, indeed even quench <unclear>and</unclear> push away the Holy Spirit from himself.

<meta>The catchword "richten" at the bottom of the left column connects to the top of the right column, indicating the continuation of the verse fragment being discussed.</meta>

<column-break/>

judge. <note>original: "richten." This term can mean to judge, to rule, or to strive with/straighten out.</note>

Or ; will not judge in eternity in men / or ; shall no longer wrangle and strive with men.

Without doubt, it is observed / that the Holy Spirit is hindered / from carrying out his internal punitive judgments over the evil in men ; in that they quench the Spirit / and suppress his corrections. <margin>Prov. 1:24. etc.</margin>

Natural pride and self-will is mostly to blame / that one does not want to suffer the discipline and conviction of God. For an unbroken, crude person has nothing but a good opinion and imagination of themselves / and also seeks to live according to their own will. Therefore, it cannot be other than vexing to them / when something in them is punished.

But God’s Spirit does not turn away from that / but where he is / there he reproves sin: <margin>John 16:8</margin> His presence and discipline are inseparably linked. <margin>Wisd. 12:1. etc.</margin>

And so you must only learn to experience the Holy Spirit’s punishment in yourself / so that a living testimony against all evil stirs and brings itself forth in your heart from God’s Word and will / which disciplines and scolds you above all / presents and discovers the bad quite thoroughly / and makes the heart anxious and fearful over it.

Blind reason and its leaders generally pass this off as the evil enemy’s temptations and work. But it has its cause / and there is a trick behind it. If they recognized God’s punishments as good / they would indeed be bound to follow them. Because they have no desire for that / they regard others / who still have a feeling / as melancholy / tempted, and foolish : who yet / where they follow the discipline / are indisputably wiser than all their teachers and critics.

Can such an effect then be from the devil / which makes evil loathsome / draws and pulls back from sin / and drives one toward the good ? That is exactly what happens with all whom the Spirit punishes regarding sin.

Only pay attention to it / and you will surely notice it / when you intend something wrong / or long for something evil. The Spirit of God will remind you there / if you only give him a hearing and room ; he will warn you away from it ; he will faithfully warn you / hold before you, put into your mind / and repeat in your heart many passages from the Scripture / so that you should desist from your purpose.

And if you have done, spoken / or even only desired something evil ; you will often become anxious in your heart because of it / even against your will. The wretched pleasure or other advantages / which you enjoyed from the sin / will be made so bitter and so loathsome to you / that you would wish / never to have committed the like.

What else is that but the punishment and discipline of the Holy Spirit ? the wholesome and great work of the eternal divine Spirit ? Is it not clear and evident from this / that the Spirit of God gladly works on all men / and passes by not a single one / whoever he may be / and to whose heart he does not come with his punishment ? For the Lord speaks here of all men / who lived before the Deluge <note>original: "Sündfluth"</note> / let them be as crude and as wicked as they liked / that his Spirit punished them. But he only laments / that they did not want to suffer such a thing.

And precisely therein lies the difference of those men / who here separate into two crowds / one of which lets itself be punished / the other not. Those who do not want to let themselves be punished / they must nonetheless feel the sting of divine justice in their conscience / and against their will retain the bitter memory of divine retribution.

But those who let themselves be punished / for them the first sharp conviction of their sins is transformed into a fatherly, loving discipline and correction of the Spirit of Jesus Christ.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Genesis 6:3 and moves into verse 4. It focuses on the withdrawal of God's Spirit from humanity, the definition of "flesh" as the fallen nature, and a prophetic calculation regarding the 120 years mentioned in the text. judge! since they are also flesh. Yet their days shall be one hundred and twenty years.

Every defiant sinner hears their terrifying judgment here: that the Lord, through His Spirit, labors for a long time even with the disobedient / as He, out of a desire for their salvation, takes the trouble to follow them daily / to accuse and rebuke them in their conscience through their thoughts / and to constantly pronounce the judgment for their sins in their hearts; so that no single person on earth can have an excuse / as if God had not concerned Himself enough, even excessively, for their sake / and had, so to speak, struggled and worn Himself out. But because all effort is in vain for some, and all strikes are for nothing / the resolution finally falls in God's justice / that the punishment of the Spirit and its struggle against evil is withdrawn from such souls in their hearts / and they are left to their own counsel and heart-thoughts for judgment. Surely no more terrible punishment can be imagined than this judgment / even if it seems pleasant to the hardened soul to continue living in self-will.

One of two things must therefore be resolved: Either one must simply comply and agree to submit oneself entirely to the punishment of the Spirit for improvement; or else / one will perish in one's sins / and fall prey to the mockery and wrath of all evil spirits.

Thus, one sin and danger is closely tied to another. He who does not follow the Spirit of God will be abandoned by it. He who loses the Spirit of God lives according to his own will. He who does that is fleshly and

**Flesh)** Not only according to the body / which we received from the Fall, whereas we were previously more spiritual and angelic; but primarily according to the mind and will / which is inclined toward fleshly things / with all desire and approval / and does not long to be torn out of the fleshly state.

Nature that has turned away from God is called "flesh" / because all its senses and affections / its love and drive / yes, even its reason and understanding / only desire and think on fleshly or religious things in a fleshly, unspiritual way and for a fleshly purpose. And according to the sense of the Scripture, the word "flesh" is understood as the whole old, unregenerate human with all his powers / or in a word: "selfhood" <note>German: *Selbstheit*</note> / that is / the self-seeking nature opposed to the Spirit of God / which is full of fleshly love / fleshly joy / hope / fear / etc. These are the affections of the old Adam / and greed / envy / zeal / pride / etc. are the members of the flesh of sin and the bones of the old man / which must be broken. Indeed, even the soul and the spirit / reason and will / are now fleshly in the flesh / thick and coarse / and the flesh has become their master.

**One hundred and twenty years)** But the Great Flood came in the six-hundredth year of Noah / Chapter 7, verses 6 and 11 / and thus a full 20 years earlier. A shortening of the days.

Because it is a determined number / which should rightly have been fulfilled; and yet it was not fulfilled as it was spoken: therefore, according to the hidden prophetic sense, 120 Jubilee years must be understood by this; as Dr. Wasmuth <note>Matthias Wasmuth (1625–1688), a German Hebraist and theologian.</note> also understands it. Thus, 120 Jubilee years together / calculating a Jubilee year at 49 years / make 5,880 years: at which completion the judgments of God upon the antichristian world will break in; which time / according to the calculations of various scholars / falls from the birth of Christ onwards when we write **1739.** For from the beginning of the world until the birth of Christ, 4141 years passed. Add 1739 years to that / and 5880 years result. But if one adds 120 years to this last number of 5880 years / exactly 6000 years emerge. But if one subtracts the 50th year / in which the Jubilee year is celebrated / as one year from every 50; then in the subtraction from 6000 years, 120 years come out.

<column-break/>

### 4. There were giants on the earth in those days; and also after that, when the children of God came in unto the daughters of men, and they bore children to them, these became the mighty ones who were men of renown of old.

### 5. Then

Pride also moved in deeply: in that some misused their very large physical stature / as Providence had allowed / so that among such people who only attended to the flesh, such giants were born / (see Numbers 13:33) others misused their intellect. This happens when the light of the children of God wants to unite with the darkness of the worldly-minded; then only monstrosities result. As one can observe in those who first had a light / and afterwards fell back to the world. From this arises nothing else but such false pretenses and cloaking of all violence in government / and all sorts of sectarianism and lust for power over consciences in the church / among those who also seek fleshly glory and standing among men. See 3 John verses 9 and 10.

**Children of God)** Because the Hebrew words found in verse 2 and here do not occur a single time more in the Scripture to refer to actual natural humans / even of the righteous people / in the same sense; there are others / who, along with the Cabbalists, Theophrastus Paracelsus, and others / understand certain intermediary beings between angels and humans / or inhabitants of the elemental world / of fire / air / water, and earth / who have something in common with both angels and humans / and are distinguished by scholars into good and evil spirits / such as were known under the name of the *Genii* <note>Guardian spirits or tutelary deities.</note> of Socrates, Plato, Pythagoras, Porphyry, Iamblichus, Psellus, Trismegistus, Plotinus, Fludd, Trithemius, etc. Regarding these beings, Thomas Aquinas held the opinion / that the children fathered by them would become magnanimous people and possess heroic natures.

**Giants — Mighty Ones)** Powerful and strong in their own will / turning away from God to attack and oppress others. For at that time, the giants began to use power and violence over the gentle of the earth / and to attack people without fear.

Thus, God's wrath allows the one who proceeds according to his own choice without the fear of God / and who follows the counsel and drive of his flesh without divine governance / to find that which his own false will seeks for his own judgment. When the children of the saints turned their eyes away from the Lord / and with their own disordered lust looked upon the daughters of men / and chose wives for themselves from them; then from such a mixture, tyrants and true worldlings were afterwards fathered on earth. And even today, experience teaches / what fruits grow from it / when the power of a good and holy seed is surrendered to the procreating mother of the corrupted flesh / and two unequal natures are mixed into a monstrous birth.

The giants and monsters of pride come only from the connection of the human with the holy. All the great and famous people of all times are those whom fleshly wisdom has raised up / in that they have hidden such wisdom under a little spirituality. O terrifying monster! There you will see people puffed up by self-esteem and exalted like giants / who have associated some natural gifts with some spiritual habits; and who are nonetheless entirely sunk in nature and in the secret high-esteem of themselves. Nevertheless, these are the most extraordinary and highly regarded people of this world. But those who have entirely annihilated themselves through their self-denial are completely unknown; indeed, they are not even distinguished from other people. But how should they be able to stand out among these great

---

giants / since they are so small / that they seem like ants next to them / whom those others trample underfoot / and often look upon as something useless on the earth! But You, O great God / who resists the proud / and gives Your grace to the humble / You pour the same in abundance into such valleys / which are capable of holding it: while meanwhile the high mountains cannot keep a drop / without letting it fall onto these small valleys; who then also recognize themselves as all the more unworthy of it / as You overwhelm them with it.

# 5. When the LORD saw / that the
# wickedness of man was great on the
# earth / and every imagination of the thought-

God here delivers a very sharp word to our corrupt nature / and leaves it no glory / but rather stops every mouth / so that we must all remain guilty before Him. It says: The LORD
Saw) Thus we may believe with certainty / that our Creator sees into the innermost depths of all our hearts / and knows everything / that is hidden within us / yes, even what a person would not gladly let any other know or notice.
But what did GOD see in the people of that time / and what does He still see in all natural men? Answer:
That the wickedness of man was great) These are actually "wickednesses" / which are the primary focus here / when a person considers evil to be their happiness / and continues in it with full pleasure. Thus many cannot live / unless they are drinking / or gambling / or quarreling / etc. These are ruling and malicious misdeeds / which rule over the person day and night with their full consent. Such wickednesses include the consent of the soul / through which it becomes a slave to sin.
GOD thus primarily condemns the evil will / as that which leans and turns toward sin unforced and voluntarily. And since a person can withdraw their will from it / if they only wish to; so they could also very well live without malice.
But what kind of wickednesses were they / that so provoked and grieved GOD? The ground of their evil heart was unbelief / according to 1 Peter 3:20. In particular, fornications and shameful lusts are reported of them / as well as contempt for the divine will and word / etc. Matthew 24:37.
Whoever now stands in one of these sins / let them expect no other judgment / than this / that they are a malicious person. And even if they were not already surrendered to these sins / it still says further of degenerate humanity / that
**Every imagination of the thoughts of their heart was only evil)** Here you see / that GOD not only knows your outward gestures / speech, and deeds / but also knows and looks through your heart and inward being.
And we know and experience / that by nature the heart is not still for a single moment / that a person is not thinking something or doing something with their mind / or imagining, thinking, and striving for something.
The imagination <note>original: "Dichten"</note> is here not only the sensory life or outward senses of a person / but the will and the desire of the person / the <term>imagination</term> or the power of mental imagery / as Arias Montanus <note>A 16th-century Spanish scholar famous for his literal Latin translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note> well translates it. For the heart is named alongside it / which indicates not only the lower powers of the soul / but primarily the higher ones and the mind. Thus it suggests the building or forming of thoughts / just as a potter builds and makes his vessel; as the Hebrew word <note>Hebrew: "yetzer," meaning form or purpose</note> is actually used in that way. And whoever earnestly pays attention to themselves and their inward being / will perceive / how the imagination of a person according to nature is always forming something and presenting it to the will / which it should grasp / love, and keep. There, reason always has something to imagine and devise / with which it wants to amuse and please the will. One will notice / how the false heart always departs from GOD and His love and harmony with Him; how it only falls upon the earthly and visible with its desires / seeking to hunt down now this profit / now that delight / now a bit of fame / only to maintain its temporal things / to build its barns larger / to have a supply for many years / and so forth. Then such plots go around in the head day and night: one thinks far ahead / and wants to provide for oneself. Therefore the heart is also not still / but consumes and torments itself with its imagining and striving. For example: A lustful person is always imagining such inventions / that suit their desires. If they cannot fulfill it in deed / they at least amuse themselves in fantasy with it / and thus reach for empty shadows. That is called the imagination of the heart. Just let the Holy Spirit search and rule you / and you will notice more in yourself / than you believe now.
My! how should that not hunt and drive us / to have an imagining within us / from GOD Himself. Is it true / that it—is it true / that one's own good works do not count / and to seek it with another / who does it in you / what you are unable to do? For [then] you will [find] / that we should not for that reason fail to pray for another heart; I would not do it either. Rather, this is the mind of God / that we—but rather let ourselves be changed and improved / and no longer for ourselves—

Now your eternal well-being or woe depends on this / that you be thoroughly instructed about yourself. If you do not know your evil heart / then you do not believe it. If you do not believe it / then you also do not want to become better / but rely on your hypocrisy. With that, you are outside of grace / without Spirit / [though] joyful / [yet] without faith; and where then remains your salvation?
Consider then your evil imagination / how you have consumed your beautiful lifetime in vanity! <meta>This page continues the commentary on Genesis Chapter 6, moving from the description of human corruption in verse 5 to God’s emotional response and the resulting decree of judgment in verses 6 and 7. It explores the theological tension between God’s unchanging nature and His "grief" over human sin.</meta>

Chapter VI. The First Book of Moses.

## 6. Then the Lord repented / that he had made man on the earth / and it grieved him in his heart. <margin>Ephesians 4:30.</margin>

**Repented — grieved)** When humans harbor their wickedness / and sin with pleasure and intent; then GOD’s bottomless affection for us humans allows it to be no other way / than that he must lament over it / because he longs so yearningly for our well-being. How could he then remain silent / when he sees / that humans cause and promote their own harm with all their will!

All such ways of speaking in the Scripture should be conducive to our humiliation / that we may be ashamed / that GOD must speak so humanly to us because of our lack of understanding / and that he has such trouble and labor with us / as with such wayward children.

His insatiable love would gladly do all good for us / and yet man will not have it / and will not conform to His order! This must surely affect and move His love. There must be a change in GOD; although not in his essence / yet in his will and purpose / which he had for our good.

He must hold back his love / and must pour out wrath in its place / because the people do not want to be any better.

O, what shall one say / and how may we sufficiently bewail the abominable-perverse nature of our heart!

But what does it help / if one does not want to become honest at the core toward the faithfulness of the faithful Creator! If it does not pain a person / whether he follows GOD or not; then he will also not become sensitive to the sorrow / which GOD has in his heart over all unfaithful souls.

Meanwhile, the Spirit of GOD is provoked by this rebelliousness / and his labor / which he performs on us, is doubled. This truly brings no blessing or grace to man / but rather wrath finally breaks out / just as the Deluge came soon after such pains of GOD; yes, he is then forced to punish / however gladly he would otherwise have spared them.

And so it certainly signifies nothing good / when a person causes GOD his Creator such pain / or lives and walks in such a way / that GOD cannot rejoice in his obedience / but must rather take up the rod. If one walks contrary to Him / then He walks contrary in return: and He can carry it through.

However, disobedience does not only grieve GOD directly / but also indirectly through His own people. Yes, sometimes such sorrow over human falseness toward GOD grows so high in His messengers / that they would have to perish under it / were they not sustained by the joyful Spirit of GOD with living hope in all patience and long-suffering.

And certainly, as our GOD bears sorrow and pain over the sins of ungodly men / so we should rightfully be of the same mind with him; and if we are not / it is not a good sign. <margin>Psalm 119:136, 139, 158.</margin>

Indeed, even over one's own sins, this repenting / this pain of GOD / can awaken nothing other than a divine repentance and sadness in all penitent souls / so that the sinner learns to recognize / how he turns and consumes GOD’s love into a curse.

And let us allow this repentance to be recommended to us / in order to henceforth gladden the one / whom we have caused so much sorrow and pain in our former days. As great as his displeasure over our sins is / so great will also be the joy over our repentance.

<column-break/>

## 7. And the Lord said: I will destroy man / whom I have created / from the earth / from man to the cattle / even to the creeping things / and to the birds of the air! For I repent / that I have made them.

->8. But<-

The expression of Holy Scripture is wonderful. Can GOD repent of anything / or is he capable of sorrow? This is intended to represent / how the misuse of His grace displeases GOD / and how he cannot tolerate the mixing of the flesh and the spirit. GOD has a great desire / to communicate his graces to mankind. His hands are full / to shower them with such. They are / as the Bride says (a) / like golden rings full of turquoises. By this is understood his exceedingly great love / out of which he pours so many graces over us / that he can hold none back. Yet as generous as he is toward us humans / so much does it also vex him / when these graces of his are misused; yes, even / so that he is heartily grieved by it. And why is that? Because (b) he carries all people in his heart; as he says so himself. Therefore, nothing offends him more than ingratitude and the misuse of his grace. What then does GOD do? He takes back everything / that he had given / and takes with the same arm / with which he had favored him / the sword of vengeance / in order to destroy everything in man / that he had worked in the same. Ungrateful man! your pride and self-interest turn your Creator into a GOD of vengeance / and force him / that he can leave nothing of his works / from the smallest to the greatest / unrooted out within you.

**To destroy man)** They had transgressed all human duty; contained in these 3 points / that they should live temperately, justly, and godly: whereas they (1) were unchaste / lustful and lewd. v. 1, 2. (2) They were giants in and on the earth / who in the strength of their own will did everything with injustice and violence; v. 4, 11. And / instead of living godly / as can be seen in v. 5 / the imagination or thoughts of their heart were only evil / and the earth was corrupted before GOD with the defilement of idols. Therefore, the decree finally went out from GOD / the judge of the whole world / because he had long expected their repentance in vain / and was weary of mercy / that the world should be blotted out. <margin>1 Peter 3:20.</margin>

GOD here breaks the staff <note>A reference to the legal tradition where a judge breaks a wooden staff to signify a death sentence has been passed.</note>, as it were, over the first world / and passes the sentence.

This bloody judgment sounds harsh and cruel / yet it is so just / so blameless / and so holy. The very Creator / who created all these people / nourished them so long and kept them alive / now decrees / to miserably destroy and blot them out.

Did eternal Love do that gladly and with joy; or was it not a strange work / a work of his justice / that he could not do otherwise / because the people would not have it otherwise?

Since the people abandoned GOD / and subjected themselves only to men / and looked to their opinion and judgment / and also paid no heed to all the faithful warnings of Noah / so that they might have repented; thus their wickedness and the false wisdom of their heart were publicly brought to light before GOD and men / so that GOD had to intervene / and had to attack the hardness of men with a special judgment. It then took on the appearance / as if GOD / out of inner repentance and pain over his corrupted creature / wanted to destroy the work of his hands: since the people / as far as they were concerned / had rightfully deserved such. Yet grace / which looked upon the promised Seed of the Woman <note>original: "Weibes-Samen"; a reference to the prophecy of the Messiah in Genesis 3:15</note> / could not leave itself without witness / but had mercy on Noah / who took hold of the promise in faith / so that he with his own should be preserved for the propagation of the human race / and also thereby the divine seed / in those who would accept the promise in faith. Therefore he also had to preach to others / so that the eyes of some might yet be opened in the midst of the danger of death / and they might perform heartfelt repentance: so they were indeed judged according to the flesh / in that they perished in the Deluge; but in the spirit they began to live to GOD / and so also according to the spirit were redeemed in his time. See 1 Peter 4:6.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Genesis 6, transitioning from the universal corruption of mankind to the singular exception of Noah. The First Book of Moses. Chapter VI.

# 8. But Noah found grace in the eyes of the LORD.

Among a whole world full of people, only a single, small, simple man is found who attained grace before GOD. But why did he find grace before GOD? The Scripture indicates it with few words, saying: he was righteous. And this righteousness prevented him from stealing anything that belonged to GOD, and from being defiled with the sin of the other people, who were guilty because they acted unrighteously, robbing GOD of what belonged to Him, and making a miserable mixture of nature and corruption out of it.

Further it stands concerning Noah (in the following verse), that he was blameless among all people of the whole world. But from where did this perfection come? It came because he constantly walked with GOD: He surrendered himself to Him and His guidance, remained in His ways and in His presence. This would bring about the perfection of all Christians just as it procured it for Noah, if they only wanted to follow in Noah’s footsteps. But the opposite—namely, the forgetting of God and self-chosen paths—causes all this evil: and are therefore to blame for man’s damnation.

**But)** From this little word it can already be seen that Noah did not walk with the world in its godless course, but earnestly withdrew himself from its charms and examples and was of a different mind than people generally were then. The foundation of his good life was

**Grace)** And not one’s own work and merit. <note>original: "Röm. 11/6" — Romans 11:6</note>. With this, the Holy Spirit cuts off all self-glory from Noah and all people, as if we could change ourselves and make ourselves godly, and attributes everything to pure, unmerited grace. No one is to imagine anything of their own. <note>original: "Eph. 2/8. 9." — Ephesians 2:8-9</note>.

Those who always put off their repentance and think they will surely convert at some point should especially reflect on this. If you, my friend, believe that you must be converted and saved by grace; why then do you not use it while it knocks? Do you know if it will always wait for you whenever you want it? Because you postpone it now, you must indeed believe in fact that you can convert and change yourself without grace one day. But you might fall short in that. Therefore, seek grace today, then you will find it, as Noah

**Found)** Whoever wants to find something must seek it. GOD does not throw pearls before swine; He wants His treasures to be sought. Therefore it does not only say: grace was offered to Noah; or: grace knocked at Noah’s heart; but: he

**Found Grace)** If someone has now found grace, he must necessarily first have sought it right earnestly, prayed for it from GOD, drawn it into his heart, and grasped it with the desire of faith. This was Noah’s finding: a faithful acceptance and taking into oneself of the divine power for life. This prevenient <note>In theology, "prevenient" grace is the grace that comes before any human action to enable a response to God.</note>, reconciling, saving, and converting grace in Christ Jesus could spread in Noah’s heart because he followed it: it could overcome sin in him and work a new life.

And let it be just that in your heart too, if only you desire it. You must only not resist it or hinder its work, much less push the guilt of your impenitence onto it and say: "If I cannot be converted without grace, then it is not up to me, and I cannot become different until grace changes and improves me." For grace is at every moment before the door of your heart. But if you do not let it in so that it can take hold of you, then you will not find it. But if you seek it with all your heart, it will also let itself be found by you.

Oh, first learn to thoroughly recognize your natural misery, then such will surely drive you to hunger and desire for reconciliation and redemption from sins! Oh, how everything that GOD does with you will then become pure unmerited mercy, and you will take up grace as your only life with a contrite and simple heart.

And that is the work of faith: it finds grace with Noah in the throne of grace, or in the reconciliation that happened through JESUS Christ. <note>original: "Ebr. 4/15. 16." — Hebrews 4:15-16</note>.

What you therefore have to seek as the ground and beginning of Christianity is grace, and not right or merit, glory, one's own pretensions or demands before GOD; as nature is far too inclined and quick to make for itself a store of good and a right by which it can be secure. Oh, that serves not to attain grace, but disgrace and wrath!

Therefore learn to go to GOD finely bowed and ask for grace. Do not come before GOD’s throne in your prayer in a natural, brazen, unbroken mind, but humble yourself under His mighty hand, yet without throwing away your confidence.

This is how the dear ancients did it when they had something to seek from GOD. They always spoke of grace and placed this as the foundation in all their discourse with GOD: *Have I found grace in your eyes.*

Follow this pattern, and believe that all your doing and effort is otherwise in vain where you do not lay this as the foundation.

But if you allow a right foundation for your Christianity to be laid therein, then it will also surely endure if you yourself persist in it. For experience testifies that all who early and thoroughly surrendered themselves to grace afterwards grow like trees planted by the water.

This grace will be your essential comfort in all future occurrences: just as Noah floated along on the water with grace and overcame all misery.

<column-break/>

# 9. These are the histories of Noah / Noah was a righteous man / and perfect

But while we read this narrative of a certain pious man, Noah, and how he lived in the world; we must by no means stay with the external history and only form an image of the person. Instead, just as we should seek to direct everything toward improvement, so also should this history serve us for something more for ourselves and give instruction. We must get a living impression of it in the heart and interpret and apply everything to ourselves, and consider whether it also applies to us or not. Then we will have a very blessed advantage from all that was written before. <note>original: "Röm. 15/4" — Romans 15:4</note>.

How then was Noah righteous, and how shall we become righteous according to his example?

No one can interpret this better for us than the Holy Spirit Himself <note>original: "Ebr. 11/ 7." — Hebrews 11:7</note>, where it is said that this righteousness came to him from faith, and thus through grace.

This righteousness given to him by grace he then proved with a righteous walk, which is what the words here specifically aim at: namely, that he was righteous in his whole life.

This righteousness and perfection certainly refer primarily to the true righteousness of a living faith. Only we must rightly understand the true righteousness of faith, so that we do not deceive ourselves and others with a false, merely imagined one. <note>original: "1. Joh. 3/7." — 1 John 3:7</note>.

If you now want to become righteous according to Noah’s example, then examine yourself by the fruits, whether they flow from a true divine righteousness of faith. That is the best way to notice it.

Your righteousness must be better than that of the Pharisees, and must agree with Noah’s: otherwise you will not enter the kingdom of heaven.

And so that you can examine even more precisely whether you are truly righteous or not; think further and sharply whether you are also truly upright in your heart in the work of Christianity, or whether you still hypocritically and falsely act, whether you mean it honestly or falsely. For you can soon notice and know that in yourself, even if you can easily deceive yourself in other things.

Diligently search out what you seek with your things, what you are concerned with in the world, whether you still have your false intentions toward yourself and this and that, and want to assert something that is not purely GOD; or whether you truly intend solely and alone to serve GOD and your neighbor!

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Genesis 6:9, specifically focusing on the character of Noah as "perfect" and his "walk with God" amidst a corrupt generation, followed by the introduction of his three sons and the increasing corruption of the earth.</meta>

### Chapter VI. The First Book of Moses.

...perfect among his generations: Noah walked constantly with GOD.
<margin>Genesis 5:22, 24</margin>

---

Noah was perfect / or / as **Luther** renders it / blameless / without reproach / irreproachable.

Do not be terrified / when you hear the word "perfect," as most people nowadays can hardly tolerate the word anymore, and would rather scratch it out of the Bible. Only learn to understand it correctly / and venture and surrender yourself with all your will into the matter itself: then you will yet thank GOD for having revealed it to you.

"Perfect" here and in almost countless places means the same as sincere / without falsehood / unfeigned and honest.

That such sincerity of heart is necessary for us is more than certain. For upon it rests the entire validity of faith / whether it be unfeigned.

It is possible to attain / if we only will it. One can remain stuck in one's falsehood / or one can let it go. This all happens with deliberation and intent. If one does not want to become sincere toward his GOD / then he remains false by choice. But if one wants to be changed / he need only surrender his heart to GOD.

However, this perfection is certainly to be understood as **Eucherius** <note>Eucherius of Lyon (c. 380–449), a prominent bishop and theologian in Gaul.</note> rightly reminds us concerning this passage: "If no one is without sin, how can **Noah** be righteous?" Thus, some are called perfect / not in the way the saints shall be made perfect in that future immortality / whereby they shall become like the angels of GOD / but as it is possible during this pilgrimage.

And for that reason it is said:

**Among his generations)** That is / above all others in his time and of his lineage; as **Bernard** <note>Bernard of Clairvaux (1090–1153), a French abbot and influential mystic.</note> concludes. Although the Holy Spirit, with these words, may have looked even more toward **Noah's** great honesty and faithfulness / which he proved even toward the godless / since he nevertheless remained steadfast in GOD’S cause among the perverse generation. He is a pattern for us / how we should maintain our honesty toward GOD unmoved, even among the worst rascals. Just as it says further of him: he

**Walked constantly with GOD)** And what else is it but atheism / when one lives along without GOD / as if there were no GOD around and near us.

On the contrary, it is one of the most eminent exercises in Christianity / that one accustoms oneself to walk in GOD’S countenance / and indeed constantly / unmoved: without which all our own work is lost.

Let no one hold it to be impossible / much less a tedious thing / but rather a piece of blessedness. For GOD is indeed the highest blessedness and rest itself. If you now walk with GOD / or have Him as a companion; what better could you wish for in heaven or on earth?

But that you do not believe or experience this happiness is your own fault. You have likely not walked with GOD a single day in your life; much less constantly. Morning and evening you perhaps babbled your prayer / and afterward did not think of Him again the whole day. What then can you experience of the true bliss of a divine walk?

Consider then / with whom you still wish to walk: with GOD, the highest good / or with your worst enemy. One of the two you must have as your guide. Blessed are you / if you choose the best this very day!

But it requires serious and careful watching / day and night / that one pays heed to GOD and His Spirit / never knowingly consenting to anything / that could separate our GOD and us from one another.

To this end, a good means is the true inward prayer of the spirit / or the secret sighing of the heart to GOD; through which one clings to GOD / and penetrates into His holy love: which the Holy Spirit works / when one surrenders the heart to Him / and always lifts it up to Him.

It is also good and blessed / that one diligently places oneself in His holy presence / and / if one has perhaps unexpectedly moved away from it through external things / that one immediately hurries back to it in humility / and never lets oneself be kept away from GOD for long.

This is so far from impossible / that it can even happen during external labor / if only one will take heaven by force / and not choose the earthly over the heavenly. The Holy Spirit certainly stands by / and constantly reminds us / where we fail / if we make a covenant with Him for that reason / and do not grieve Him.

Look at the examples of the ancients / for whom it was also possible! and that in a time / when the way to the sanctuary was not yet opened / and unrighteousness had gained the upper hand: namely, in the days of **Noah**.

GOD let the image of His holy walk be deeply impressed upon our minds / and following His example, let us rest from our own thoughts / cares / negligences and works / and generally from our vain and earthly walk / and walk with GOD / and apply ourselves / to present ourselves proven to GOD and to true righteousness and holiness / and to be blameless in the midst of the perverse and contradictory generation: so that through the grace of our Lord JESUS Christ / the true **Noah** <note>The author likely draws a typological connection: Noah’s name means "rest," and Christ provides the true rest from sin.</note> / we may find favor in the eyes of the Lord at the time of the overflowing Deluge!

<column-break/>

**10. And Noah begat three sons: Shem / Ham / and Japheth.**
**11. But the earth was corrupt before GOD.**

---

**v. 10. Three)** But which was the oldest? For they were not triplets / but **Ham** is called the small one in chapter 9:24. and **Japheth** the greater in chapter 10:21. See chapter 5:32.

The soulful or natural man is **Japheth**. He is in the middle between two. He has something above him; namely the heavenly man **Shem**. He also has something beneath him; namely the beastly nature / as prefigured by **Ham** / and is in itself a zeal and fiery heat in its proper subordinate form / to serve the divine and human nature. This is what **Plotinus** <note>A major Greek-speaking philosopher of the 3rd century, founder of Neoplatonism.</note> also says: namely that in a man there are 3 things / <term>νοῦς</term> <note>original: "noûs" — mind or intellect</note>, <term>ψυχή</term> <note>original: "psychē" — soul</note>, <term>ἐπιθυμία</term> <note>original: "epithymia" — desire or animal appetite</note>, the mind / the soul / the animal nature.

**v. 11. Corrupt)** The corruption of the world is specifically placed in this / that everything was filled with outrage and unrighteous violence: especially arising from those tyrants and famous learned people / who seek to rule over others' bodies / goods and consciences / according to their pleasure. Concerning which corruption Christ also laments in the last times / that unrighteousness shall prevail / and thus love shall grow cold in many. Matthew 24:12. Then the great corruption of the world also consists in this / that men leave the true path of righteousness / and follow their own conceit / as they chose the way to attain salvation according to their own notions / or even throw the salvation of their souls to the wind / and only strive to live according to their fleshly lusts in all luxury and extravagance. See Psalm 81:12 etc. Romans 1:28 etc. 10:2-3.

**Before GOD’S countenance)** The miserable people / who lived so wickedly at that time / likely did not imagine / that GOD searched their being so closely / or paid heed to it. And nature is still minded thus. It does not like GOD’S near presence / alas and it happens; it would rather wish / that GOD were far from it; so that it might carry on its self-will unhindered.

At the very least, the godless man does not believe / that GOD is in earnest against sin / that He pays such close attention and notice to everything / also searching and following all thoughts and stirrings of the soul.

But now each one's conscience testifies / how nothing is hidden from GOD. And how do even the roughest people know to appeal to GOD’S omniscience against their enemies! Thus they should also believe of themselves / that GOD tried all their things and knew them exactly.

But it takes much effort / before even an already convinced man is brought so far by the spirit of discipline / that he earnestly believes / GOD sees all his things. One must thereby learn to live in the constant presence of GOD / and walk before His eyes / as the believers have done: then one will, as it were, become aware every moment / how GOD sees everything. The all-seeing Spirit of GOD will then call such a soul to account / direct / govern and strengthen it over all thoughts / words and works; and the man will acquire a holy awe and reverence for the bright eye of GOD / so that he will not intentionally grieve Him.

# The First Book of Moses. Chapter VI.

### GOD'S Face / and the Earth was full of Outrage.

### 12. And GOD looked upon the earth / and behold, it was corrupt; for all flesh had corrupted its way upon the earth.
<margin>Psalm 14:2, 3.</margin>

---

Primarily, this is the benefit of the all-seeing eye of GOD / that man learns to recognize his sin in its light / as it truly is / and receives a right, living knowledge of his corruption / which is necessary for repentance.

For it is by no means enough / that we know according to the letter / what sin may be / and perhaps even learn a description and verses about it and are able to recite them back.

We find a description here as well; but whom will it help / if one does not learn to apply and interpret all of this to his own actions and omissions? These people before the Great Flood also knew well enough what sin was: but what did it help them? It says:

**The earth was full of outrage)** <note>original: "Frevel," meaning outrageous violence, wickedness, or a violation of divine law.</note> Here, let no one think / as if this is only to be understood as referring to cruel, unheard-of villainies.

We should know / that all other wantonness / insolence / lack of restraint, or the presumption of corrupted nature belongs to it. This is clear from the 4th verse. Without doubt, those same people mostly committed and hid their wickedness under the name of the government <note>original: "Regiment," referring to the ruling authorities or legal systems of the time.</note>. For this is the cunning and malice of worldly people / that they want to maintain and excuse all their unjust / tyrannical, and ungodly things with a certain appearance of legality. And yet, this their doing is called outrage here and elsewhere. <margin>Psalm 73:6.</margin>

Therefore, let no one withdraw himself from this judgment of GOD / who is still conscious of any natural insolence / lack of restraint / and the like / and has not bowed himself entirely under the yoke of the humility and gentleness of JESUS Christ.

It clings far too strongly and long to the evil nature / that one gladly wishes to live insolently without discipline and order / to force one's way through everything / and do everything according to pleasure <note>original: "plaisir"</note> and self-will; especially where one has something to say in the world.

But that was the misdeed of the first world / of the Sodomites / of the Canaanites / of the false Jews, and of all godless despisers / who despised the discipline of the Spirit of GOD / and were so wild and untamed / that GOD saw no other means / than to clear them all out of the way.

<column-break/>

### 13. Then GOD said to Noah: The end of all flesh has come before me

---

<gloss>The LORD God does nothing / unless he reveals his secret to his servants the prophets: <margin>Amos 3:7.</margin> And he especially reveals the judgments and their righteous causes: so that then the earth and all flesh for the sake of man is subjected to vanity / curse, and punishment.</gloss>

What kind of terrifying power of sin is this / which binds GOD himself in His justice / so that He cannot do otherwise than punish! Is that not the inevitable wages of sin / namely death / which has such a grim power over men / that it tears them away and consumes them like bread!

And that is the first true heartache / when sin receives the power and authority to deliver the soul to eternal death through its own unbelief: so that such souls departed in sin must thereafter always feel the power of the same so cruelly / and torment and drag themselves with it.

It was the least of it / that these people were drowned by water. But it was the worst and most unbearable thing for them / that they could not get rid of their sins after death / but were held captive by them / as they had died in impenitence.

For it is a terrifying tyranny and torment of sin over a soul / when it must always feel its shameful desires / how they provoke and torment it / and yet it no longer has space nor time to fulfill them / because it is outside the body; and moreover, it must feel the worm that does not die in its conscience.

But even this is not enough / but sin / which is distressing to hear / also gains power through man's malice over the other poor creatures / who must pay the price for it. Therefore, here GOD speaks of

**The end of all flesh)** and wishes to destroy mankind.

---

Our salvation wants much more to be worked out with fear and trembling: our affairs should be done in humility and modesty / and it behooves us to deal gently with our poor fellow men / even if they should be subjected to us according to the order of things.

Whoever walks before GOD in his own painted freedom or power, proud and lustful / makes himself a true abomination and disgust to the Creator / who can suffer nothing haughty and insolent / but knocks all the powerful from their thrones at the right time.

Therefore, we should watch finely over our own heart / and pay attention to how we do our things in the world. We should finely tame our natural wantonness / and discipline our heart with GOD’S word.

Some people can hide their outrage excellently / and carry out their things craftily and secretly / so that they are not regarded as insolent. Nevertheless, their doing is an outrage before GOD / because GOD looks at the heart / and is a thousand times more an enemy to pretenses. The Spirit of GOD looks into the heart of the false: they cannot hide their outrage from Him. Whatever evil they do with deliberate counsel and with the consent of their will / that is and remains an outrage / a willful sin: and even if they could present themselves as angels in the process / yet this outrage of theirs will fall upon their own heads. They will surely realize it / and one day feel what kind of sin it was!

**v. 12. All flesh)** That is / all people / who were carnally and ungodly minded / (yet not excluding the other creatures on earth / as can be seen from v. 7. /)

**Had corrupted its way)** What does it mean then to corrupt one’s way / and what is the way / that one corrupts through sin?

After mankind fell away from GOD / GOD nevertheless, out of great mercy, could not find it in His heart to do anything other than show them again a way / on which they could become one with GOD again. And that is now His holy will / the guideline of our actions and omissions / insofar as it is contained in the Word of GOD.

GOD did not keep this way secret from us humans / but even wrote it into the hearts of the heathens. And thus this good will of GOD is manifest and known to everyone as a medicinal way / if only he is willing.

He has now set this way before mankind / and calls to them earnestly <margin>Isaiah 30:21.</margin>

Whoever does not now step onto this way with all earnestness from his whole heart / and thus becomes one with GOD’S will; he corrupts that same way: that is; he abandons that divine good ground and seed of the living Word / which GOD has placed in his heart / and does not let the Word / which is implanted in him / come to power and fruit.

Thereby this way is corrupted in such people / that is; it becomes unfruitful / and does not reach the healing purpose / which GOD had intended by it.

Whoever is still fleshly and carnally minded / he is involved in nothing but such corruption / even while he thinks he is best helping and advising himself through greed / guile, and injustice.

Yes, also all secret false ways corrupt and displace for us the right straight way to life.

Whoever is not constantly one with GOD and His will / and keeps the narrow way to life in his heart / he already walks on crooked wandering paths / and will not know nor enjoy the way of peace.

And thereby the right way and the noble treasure of faith is corrupted most of all / when you walk according to your own human law. When you do your own will / and what pleases you; you yourself hinder the blessing / which GOD had intended for you on His ways.
