<meta>This page continues the commentary on Genesis 6, specifically interpreting verse 13 regarding the destruction of the earth and beginning the technical and symbolic description of the Ark's construction in verses 14 through 16.</meta>

# Chapter VI. The First Book of Moses.

For the earth is full of outrage because of them / and behold, I will destroy them with the earth! <margin>Romans 5:21.</margin>

**With the earth)** Thus God did not only destroy the originators of sin / but also the stage upon which they had sinned.

It sounds strange / and yet it is true / that the earth becomes a partaker of the curse of human sins and must pay the price. For even before this, the field was cursed for Adam's sake. Chapter 3:17.

Here one might think: Oh, what can the poor earth or any other creature do / if people misuse them? It is painful enough for them / and they indeed groan over the service of vanity and the perishable nature. Only the one who commits the sins should die and be punished / not the creature. How do the creatures come to this?

But if one goes right to the foundation of divine truth / then the mystery hidden beneath this will be somewhat recognized.

Namely, just as believers sanctify God's creatures and gifts back to the Lord through proper use / so do wicked and natural men profane and corrupt the creature / and turn the good contained therein and placed there by God into evil.

The Scripture calls this "outrage" <note>original: "Frevel," meaning a violent or insolent violation of divine law.</note> and "wantonness," when fallen nature rises up in its vehemence and own power / and descends upon the creature with wrath and pride / misusing it for its own malice / so that the curse becomes manifest and powerful in all things that an impenitent person does. Thus the poor creature is infected / so that both man and his things stand under the wrath of God / and must pay for sin. This is why the creatures mostly perish and die just as man does.

All this, with the help of the Holy Spirit, can give a good insight into the mystery of malice / which is as unknown to nature as the mystery of godliness. It shows us what a contagious, spreading poison sin is in nature / how it eats away like a cancer / and not only incites and seduces toward evil / but also draws others into the punishment and the harm.

The earth here, because of the evil that had happened upon its soil / had to perish with water / and came into an even more wretched form than it had after the Fall but before the Deluge: as many believe that the earth before the Deluge was much better / and was greatly changed by it and stripped of its beauty and fertility / so that God thereafter had to permit humans to eat meat.

And the earth must necessarily have become a good deal lesser, more uneven, and more rugged / because the water necessarily must have destroyed, torn away, and made much unequal. Therefore, some even trace the origin of mountains back only to the Deluge.

Thus the earth upon which we dwell should still today be a "Mirror of Wrath" to us / showing how very powerful sin is in causing destruction. Should this not make all greedy-guts, drunkards, gluttons, and similar sinners / wise enough to stop misusing the creature in such a way?

Certainly, as many drops of beer, wine, brandy, and the like as they swallow into themselves without need for the sake of luxury / so many curses they take into their inner being. Why? Because they force the creature into malice with the heat of their desires and shameful lusts / and give to the creature the love and delight that they owe to God.

If everything must go to ruin for the sake of sin / why then does one not withdraw his heart from vanity / and seek what is more lasting?

Let one therefore recognize from this the cruel power of evil / how far its corruption extends / and let it not be enough to be able to discourse upon it / but see to it that one learns to withdraw from such tyranny / and comes to dwell and live under a higher and more blessed power.

To this, there is no other way than true conversion from former sins. Otherwise, one cannot be quit of the poisonous contagion of sin / unless one entirely withdraws his will from its false dominion / and surrenders himself to the rightful Lord with body, soul, and spirit / with all powers, senses, and endeavors.

<column-break/>

14. **Make yourself a chest <note>The German "Kasten" translates the Hebrew "Thebah" (Ark), emphasizing its shape as a container rather than a ship.</note> of cypress wood; with chambers shall you make the chest: and coat it inside and out with pitch.**

15. **And this is how you shall make it. Three hundred cubits shall be the length of the chest / fifty cubits its width / and thirty cubits its height.**

16. **A window shall you make in the chest / and finish it to a cubit's size from above. And the door of the chest shall you set in its side. You shall make it so that it has a lower, second, and third story.**

17. **For**

**v. 14 Of cypress wood)** It is not yet settled among the learned / whether **Gopher** <note>The original Hebrew term used for the wood of the Ark.</note> is a general word denoting all trees; or whether it means a specific tree. For the latter, some suggest the reason that the word **Gopher** sounds almost like the German **Kiefer** (pine): whereas others maintain that in Syria and Babylonia / where the **Ark of Noah** was presumably built / no pines, or even firs, are to be found; but they hold it rather to be a cypress tree / whose wood is not only very hard and light / but also fatty and resinous / consequently resisting rot / and well-suited for shipbuilding. Just as a sulfur, resin, or pitch called **Gophrid** / mentioned in Genesis 19:24 / is said to flow and come from the cypress tree. Outside of these places, this word is found nowhere else: hence the obscurity of its meaning arises.

**v. 15. 16. Chest) Thebah** in Hebrew / a container / which is the same word used for **Moses'** little basket. It could not be called a ship / because it lacked the most prominent features of one / such as / the bow and stern / mast, sails, rudder, and anchor.

Writers give it different forms. But it had the shape of a human body / when it lies on its back as if dead or sleeping; or even of a coffin. The measurements also correspond exactly to the proportions of the human body. For the width was 1/6th of the length / and the length of the human body also relates as 6 to 1 / and the height from the back through the heart to the top of the chest in a dead or sleeping person is as 10 to 1: just as the width relates to the height of the body at roughly 50 to 30. Our grave and coffin also have approximately such proportions.

Thus, in this figure of the chest is found the mystery of the Incarnation of Christ / and our burial with Him through baptism into death <gloss>(a)</gloss>.

Divine wisdom had Noah construct this wonderful chest in its right symmetry / and division of compartments for so many kinds of animals / and the food for them. He then had to make an opening and entrance / which had to be sufficient for light for the humans / and for entry and exit for all animals / during this heavy Judgment of Wrath. This must be an image of the wonderful preservation in the final Judgments of Wrath / when the believers will be preserved in their chambers and compartments / into which they enter through the door of Christ / and also enjoy Him as the only light / in the midnight / in which all animalistic men find themselves. As **Isaiah** magnificently prophesied of this: <margin>Chapters 26:20, 21. 57:2. 60:8.</margin>

(a) See Augustine, Book 4 of *The City of God*, Chapter 26. <note>original: "vid. Augustin. l. 4. de C. D. c. 26."</note>

# The VII. Chapter.

->Noah's preservation in judgment.<-

And the LORD said to Noah: Go into the Ark / you and your whole house! For I have seen you as righteous before my face in this generation.
2. Of every kind of clean cattle take to yourself seven and seven / the male and his female: but of the cattle that are not clean take two / the male and his female.
3. Likewise of the birds of the heavens seven and seven / the male and the female: to keep seed alive upon the whole earth.

5. An <note>Text continues on next page</note>

---

<insert>
Since God resolved to destroy mankind; He wished to separate the righteous Noah from the unrighteous / and through his faith to condemn the world / and to declare Noah an heir of the righteousness of faith, Hebrews 11:7. But the people of the world, because of their unbelief and lack of repentance / and thus because of their manifest godlessness and chosen false path of righteousness / He wished to destroy.

<margin>v. 17. Flood of waters)</margin> Why did God choose to destroy the earth specifically with water at that time? Surely because the fury and wrath of the Devil had so taken the upper hand that it had, as it were, swallowed all good and all the love of God. Therefore, this fire of wrath had to be broken and quenched by water, so that afterward the Covenant of Grace could be renewed again.

<margin>v. 18-22.</margin> Just as here the Covenant of Grace in Christ was renewed with Noah and all the animals; so too in the great redemption shall all believers rejoice in this / even with the animals / who shall then be liberated from the service of vanity. Romans 8:19, etc.

The LORD blessed the food for so many creatures during its use: and so also believers will not lack it in the great judgments. Isaiah 51:14. But they must also learn from Noah the simple obedience of faith / to behave then in everything according to the LORD’s will. See Matthew 24:15, etc. Luke 17:31, etc. 21:34, 35, 36.

<margin>v. 22.</margin> Some conclude from Holy Scripture and the Church Fathers / that he spent 100 years on the construction / and had taken very many workmen to help.

Before one can be received into the Ark of Salvation / which is God Himself / one must first have fulfilled all His commandments / and have been obedient to Him in everything. Not so much through the external keeping of them / but much more according to the inner purity / which can be obtained in no other way than through the keeping of the law of the Spirit and of life.

<column-break/>

In the whole world there is only a single righteous person <note>This likely refers to Noah as a "type" or precursor to Christ.</note> / who is worthy to enter into the Ark / which is God Himself. Yet there are so many among us who imagine themselves to be found in God. One must be righteous to enter into Him: namely, one must have robbed nothing from God / or restore to Him everything that was stolen; namely, leaving God in Himself with everything that belongs to Him / so that one may remain in one's own "nothingness." This is the righteousness which one must have / in order to be received into the very close union with God.

<margin>v. 1. You --- seen as righteous)</margin> What a glorious testimony! God / as an all-seeing light / had found his heart upright and without falsehood before Him / so that He could take delight and joy in his conduct.

<margin>v. 2.)</margin> Regarding the distinction between clean and unclean animals / one can conclude from this that just as God commanded sacrifice from the beginning / He also indicated which animals should be brought to Him as a sacrifice / those which were also most useful for human nourishment / while others were harmful; in order to set limits to their excess. Though this may not have happened through an express command or prohibition regarding the types of animals / it followed later under the Law in the Old Testament / which was imposed as a yoke / and is now lifted in the New Testament to the extent that man, in the light of God, should make a distinction / between what is beneficial for his preservation in the use of some animals / and conversely what is harmful to other animals / so that he should moderate his desires therein. See Acts 10:10, etc. Romans 14:2, 3. Colossians 2:16, 20. 1 Timothy 4:3, 4, 5. Titus 1:15.

<meta>This page continues the narrative of Genesis 7. The previous page concluded with God's command to Noah to enter the Ark with the animals and his family. This page describes the execution of that command and the beginning of the Great Flood.</meta>

### Ch. VII. The First Book of Moses.

5. And Noah did according to all that the Lord had commanded him. <margin>Ch. 6:22.</margin>

6. And Noah was six hundred years old when the flood of waters was upon the earth.

7. And Noah went in, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him, into the Ark <note>The German "Kasten" literally means a chest or box, emphasizing the vessel's function as a container for preservation rather than a ship for navigation.</note>, because of the waters of the flood.

8. Of clean cattle, and of cattle that are not clean, and of birds, and of everything that creeps upon the ground:

9. They went in two by two to Noah into the Ark, the male and the female; as the Lord had commanded Noah.

10. And it came to pass after seven days, that the waters of the flood came upon the earth.

---

<margin>v. 5.) Noah, as a righteous servant of God, held himself in all his circumstances solely to God and His will. It may have appeared ever so absurd and contrary to reason that he should build a box on dry land and crawl into it with his family; nevertheless, Noah followed the Lord blindly and remained faithful to God in the greatest distress.</margin>

<margin>v. 6.) This obedience of Noah is praised: that through faith, when he received the divine revelation of things not yet seen, he was moved with fear and prepared an Ark for the salvation of his house. See Hebrews 11:7. # The First Book of Moses. Ch. VII.

18. But with you I will establish my covenant: and you shall go into the Ark <note>original: "Kasten"; literally "chest" or "box," implying a vessel of preservation rather than a ship</note>, you and your sons, and your wife, and your sons' wives with you.

<margin>v. 17. Flood of water)</margin> Why did God choose to destroy the earth specifically with water at that time? Surely because the fury and wrath of the devil had so prevailed that it had, as it were, swallowed up all good and all the love of God. Therefore, this fire of wrath had to be broken and extinguished by water, so that afterwards the Covenant of Grace could be renewed once again.
<margin>v. 18-22.</margin> Just as the Covenant of Grace in Christ was renewed here with Noah and all the animals; so too in the great redemption shall all believers rejoice in this, even together with the animals, who shall then be liberated from the service of vanity. <note>See Romans 8:19 and following.</note>
The LORD blessed the food for so many creatures during its use: and so it will also not be lacking for believers in the great judgments. <note>See Isaiah 51:14.</note> But they must also learn from Noah the simple obedience of faith, to behave then in everything according to the LORD'S will. See Matthew 24:15 etc. Luke 17:31 etc. 21:34, 35, 36.
<margin>v. 22.</margin> Some conclude from Holy Scripture and the Church Fathers that he spent 100 years on the construction and took many laborers to help him.
Before one can be received into the Ark of Salvation, which is God Himself, one must first have fulfilled all His commandments and been obedient to Him in everything. Not so much through the external keeping of them, but rather according to the inner purity, which can be maintained in no other way than through the keeping of the law of the Spirit and of life.

### Chapter VII.

->Noah's Preservation in Judgment.<-

And the LORD said to Noah: "Go into the Ark, you and your whole house! For you I have seen to be righteous before my face in this generation.
2. Of every kind of clean cattle take to you by sevens, the male and his female: but of the cattle that are not clean by twos, the male and his female.
3. Likewise of the birds of the heavens by sevens, the male and the female: to keep seed alive upon the whole earth.
4. For in seven days more <margin>(a) v. 10.</margin> I will cause it to rain upon the earth forty days and forty nights, and blot out from the face of the ground every living thing that I have made." <margin>(a) Joshua 6:4, 15.</margin>

---

Since God resolved to blot out mankind, He wanted to separate the righteous Noah from the unrighteous, and through his faith condemn the world, and declare Noah the heir of the righteousness of faith (Hebrews 11:7). However, He wanted to blot out the people of the world because of their unbelief and impenitence, and thus because of their manifest godlessness and chosen false path of righteousness.
In the whole world there is only a single righteous man who is worthy to enter into the Ark, which is God Himself. Yet there are so many among us who imagine themselves to be in God Himself. One must be righteous to enter into Him: namely, one must have robbed God of nothing, or restore to Him everything that was robbed; namely, leaving God in Himself with everything that belongs to Him, so that one may remain in one's own nothingness. This is the righteousness which one must have to be received into the very intimate union with God.
<margin>v. 1. You — seen to be righteous)</margin> Oh, what a magnificent testimony! God, as an all-seeing light, had found his heart upright and without deceit before Him, so that He could delight and rejoice in his conduct.
<margin>v. 2.)</margin> Regarding the distinction between clean and unclean animals, one can conclude from this that just as God commanded sacrifice from the very beginning, He also indicated which animals should be brought to Him as an offering; these were also the most useful to humans for food, while the others were harmful; in this, He also set limits to their immoderation. That which may not have happened through an explicit command or prohibition regarding the types of animals followed later under the Law in the Old Testament, which was imposed as a yoke. It is now lifted in the New Testament to the extent that man himself, in the light of God, may make a distinction as to what is conducive to his preservation in the use of some animals, and conversely what is harmful from other animals, so that he should moderate his desires therein. See Acts 10:10 etc. Romans 14:2 etc. Colossians 2:16, 20. 1 Timothy 4:3, 4, 5. Titus 1:15.

# The First Book of Moses. Ch. VII. 58

**17. When** the flood had now been upon the earth for forty days, the waters increased and lifted up the Ark <note>original: "Kasten"; literally a chest or box</note>, so that it was raised high above the earth.

**18. And** the waters prevailed and increased greatly upon the earth, so that the Ark floated upon the face of the waters.

**19. Indeed**, the waters prevailed so exceedingly upon the earth that all the high mountains under the whole heaven were covered.

**20. Fifteen** cubits <note>original: "Ehlen"; an ancient unit of measurement based on the length of the forearm</note> deep did the waters prevail as the mountains were covered.

v. 17. Forty Days) During these forty days of constant rain and the swelling of the waters, the people saw no rescue; yet this served to bring some to repentance, so that they recognized the justice of God, surrendered their flesh to God's judgment, and thus were preserved according to the spirit. To this end, God—who otherwise could have easily destroyed everything in a single moment—let the waters rise gradually so that they might have time to retreat to the trees and mountains. There, they might come to reflection and still cry out for God's mercy in their great distress. Many undoubtedly did so. Such long-suffering and mercy of God can be inferred from Peter’s words, where he previously spoke of this judgment of the Flood (1 Peter 3:20) and afterward mentions how the Gospel was preached to these dead, who were judged according to the flesh, so that they might live to God according to the spirit and thus be saved (Chapter 4:6).

That God has so often sent floods and excessive rains was done for no other reason than to remind us of the "overflowing" of unrighteousness. The breaking in and flooding of the waters indicates that a breakout and flood of sin had occurred beforehand.

The overflowing flood presupposes an overflowing and abundance of injustice.

Oh, what a general flooding of ungodliness exists in people today! But who pays attention to how powerfully his soul is flooded with his own lusts, which break into his soul like a water-flood and submerge it! The voluptuous person does not consider how deep he has sunk into his beastly lusts, into the slime pits of Siddim <note>A reference to the tar pits mentioned in Genesis 14:10</note>. Does the person who is rich—whether spiritually or worldly—truly consider how his own lusts sink him into ruin and damnation!

v. 19. 20. Mountains) From this, it can be concluded that mountains existed before the Flood and from the time of Creation, rather than having first arisen because of the Flood. Without doubt, the wisdom of God, in restoring the creation that had fallen into disorder through the fall of Lucifer, wished to present a beauty in variety: that here a height, there a depth, here a mountain, there a valley, must be found.

<column-break/>

**21. And** all flesh died that moved upon the earth, including the birds, the cattle, the wild beasts, and every swarming thing that teems upon the earth, and all mankind.

**22. Everything** that had the breath of the spirit of life in its nostrils, of all that was on the dry land, died.

**23. Thus** was destroyed every living thing that was upon the ground, from man to cattle, to the creeping things, and to the birds of the heavens; they were destroyed from the earth. Only Noah remained, and those who were with him in the Ark.

**24. And**

v. 21. All flesh) Hereby a universal Deluge (*) is very clearly indicated, as the mountains under the whole heaven were covered with water fifteen cubits deep. Thus, everything in which there was a living breath and a single movement or sensation—everything that has an independent being within itself by which it can move and reach out—had to give up its spirit, and thus its life and sensation. See Psalm 104:29.

v. 22. what was on the dry land) Through this restriction, it is sufficiently indicated that the judgment and destruction did not affect the fish. They could not perish from the water itself. And because they do not have such a close relationship with man as do the living creatures of the earth, the reason is clear. Therefore, no fish were ever used for sacrifices. And just as the judgments of the end times will specifically affect those who dwell on the earth—that is, the members of the corrupt false church, including the godless poor, like the creeping worms of the earth—so was their prototype directed toward these, and the fish were excluded. The mystery also implies that the fish represent the peoples of heathendom <note>non-Christian nations</note>, who, according to <margin>Ezekiel 47:8, 9.</margin> are to be preserved.

v. 23. Noah alone remained etc.) As the blessed remnant that was left over from the general destruction. All other humans God let go and be snatched away like slaughter-animals, reserved for death and ruin; Noah alone remained unharmed.

All of this must still occur precisely today for all who seek the Lord with their whole heart. For God’s justice gives this special privilege to all the righteous: that He does not kill the righteous with the unrighteous (Chapter 18:25).

If one goes out from the Babel of the world with Noah and separates himself, then God accepts him and preserves him. If he desires no fellowship with the works of darkness, but rather rebukes them, then he need not share in their plagues.

From the beginning of the world, it has always been that believers were not only compassionately preserved from the plagues of the godless but also confidently proclaimed the punishments to others beforehand, seeing their joy in the enemies of God as their wickedness was repaid.

And so it will also go with the righteous and perfect believers of the end times who constantly walk before the face of God. See Isaiah 4:3; 6:11-13. They will not perish through the swelling flood of judgment; rather, those very judgments must be what lifts the Church up (Psalm 46). That which works for evil for the world of the godless works for good for those who love God.

# Ch. VII. The First Book of Moses.

### 24. And the waters prevailed upon the earth one hundred and fifty days.

This is also a beautiful image of what occurs in the inner state, in which everything human and natural—no matter what it may be—must be completely submerged and drowned under the waters of bitterness and sadness. This happens so that <term>Noah</term> <note>Noah is interpreted here as the "Ground of the Soul," the deepest, most essential part of a person that remains faithful to God.</note>, who here represents the ground of the soul, may be preserved alone and pass into GOD Himself. These waters, however, must rise above the highest mountains; namely, the very powers of the soul must be drowned. Although this state appears painful and sorrowful to the one experiencing it, he must take comfort in the fact that sin is drowned along with the sinner, and that no one remains except the righteous one alone: which signifies nothing other than the exceedingly glorified human being, who has been perfectly justified through their loss and annihilation.

The Flood also represents the emotions of the mind and the unrest of this world. Everything in it is drowned, except for those who are in GOD as if in an Ark <note>original: "Kasten"; literally a chest or box, referring to the Ark</note>, where they live securely. Although these are few, they are nonetheless of every kind; namely, of every station, age, and dignity.

Indeed, in this Flood we have
->A prefiguration and image<-
I. of the killing of the old and the resurrection of the new man, or true rebirth.
1. Just as the old world was killed in the Flood, so also here—as in Baptism—the suppression of the old man is signified. Romans 6:3-6.
2. The old world was thereby buried. Colossians 2:12.
3. Noah was preserved in the waters and came forth alive again. Thus the new man rises.
4. The external water could not cleanse people without repentance and faith. *Not the removal of the filth of the flesh.* 1 Peter 3:21.
5. Even the Flood could not preserve them, but rather the power and promise of GOD. So also Baptism has its power from the promise and sealing of GOD.
6. The Flood caused Noah to enter into the Ark with his children: so Baptism leads into the Church.

II. of increasing and decreasing persecutions.
1. Waters signify many peoples, and specifically a power that sits upon many waters and rises against GOD's people.
2. The waters grew and prevailed, covering all high mountains.
3. All flesh perished: few are preserved.
4. These few in the Ark could not be swallowed up.
5. The higher the waters grew, the higher the Ark soared, nearing heaven. And when it was at its highest, it was closest to the end.
6. Finally, the waters subsided and gradually decreased again.
7. Finally, the whole earth became dry and became a new world.

III. of the Last Judgment, insofar as it was a punishment. Luke 17:26, 27.
1. It was a punishment for the old, heated, godless world: and so shall the fire be in the future.
2. Before the Flood, the world was in wickedness; and although Enoch and Noah preached to them, they took no heed until the Flood came. So shall it also be at the coming of the Son of Man.
3. The Flood took away the most, and the fewest were snatched from it. The elect will be snatched out of the fire. 2 Peter 3.
4. The Flood came after the seventh day. Thus, after the 7th age, the general judgment shall also come.

## Chapter VIII.
->Noah’s Departure and Gratitude.<-

<margin>(a) Lev. 26:22.</margin>
THEN GOD remembered Noah, and every wild animal, and all the cattle <gloss>(a)</gloss> that were with him in the Ark; and GOD caused a wind to pass over the earth, and the waters subsided.

### 2. And the fountains of the deep were stopped, along with the windows of heaven, and the rain from heaven was restrained.

### 3. And the waters receded from the earth continually, and the waters decreased at the end of one hundred and fifty days.

### 4. And

---

<margin>v. 1. Then GOD remembered)</margin>
The Scripture speaks of dear GOD in such a wondrous way, as if He had not thought of His friend Noah even once during the Flood, let alone cared for him.
The text speaks as it appeared to human eyes. For Noah was stuck in the greatest distress and danger, was abandoned by all things, and had to look purely at the invisible.
To live in faith is the hardest life of all, as Noah and his sons lived, who were merely clinging to heaven. For the earth was covered with water, so that they had no ground upon which they could set foot: rather, there was only the word of promise, which held them up in such violence of the water.
When the flesh is out of danger, it considers faith to be a very small thing. But those who live in such a struggle and tug of thoughts—namely, when the radiance of divine grace is withdrawn and we stand in sheer darkness or forgetfulness of God—they experience that living by the Word or faith is a much heavier and harder state than if one were a hermit: says Luther.
GOD remembers the ground and center-point of the soul, which He alone, and unknown, had preserved under such a cruel flood.
But why does the Scripture speak here of Noah and the animals, and nothing of his household? Because these were all enclosed in Noah and were all saved in him. Just so, the noblest products of the soul are preserved through their center-point. When God annihilates the center-point of the soul within Himself, He also destroys its effects and powers: which seem as if frozen and dried up, so that they become incapable of their duties. But GOD annihilates them in this way so that He may save them: He saves them only for the sake of the soul. Therefore, no distinction is made among them.
GOD also remembers all the animals, namely everything that belongs to the lower part, to save it from oppression and from drowning.
Then the overflowing of the water ceases: it is then no flood of the waters of grace: they were the waters of wrath and contempt, and the streams of vengeance that overflowed. But oh, kind GOD! You wish to destroy no one but the guilty. You only want to root out sin from its base: and you drown it only so that the righteous might be preserved! This is the beautiful part of the Godhead which has not been made misshapen by corruption. And the Flood is only to drown this corrupted nature, along with the evil it possesses. But God saves what is still good in it and comes from Him: which was prefigured by the animals preserved in the Ark.

# The First Book of Moses. Ch. VIII.

4. And the Ark <note>original: "Kasten"; literally a chest or box, the German term used for Noah's vessel</note> stood still in the seventh month on the seventeenth day of the month, upon the mountains of Ararat.
5. But the waters continued to recede and diminish until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.
6. An <note>Text cut off at edge</note>

---

## In Noah’s Ark, we have once again a beautiful prefiguration of Christ and the Christian Church.

### I. Of Christ.

1. The Ark, in which Noah and his family were preserved, was made of cypress—and thus of "mourning-wood." <note>Cypress was historically associated with mourning and death because it does not regenerate when cut back too far.</note> Christ was made perfect for suffering and through suffering.
2. This Ark was shaped like a human body lying on its back. <margin>Chapter 6:14-17.</margin> So was Christ’s body lowered into the grave so that we might be preserved.
3. It had a door in its side: and Christ’s side was also opened upon the Cross.
4. It had its length, breadth, and height. <margin>Ephesians 3:18.</margin>
5. Men and women entered this Ark. In Christ there is no distinction. <margin>Galatians 3:28.</margin>
6. This Ark was surrendered to the waves of the flood, but not entirely swallowed by them. <margin>Psalms 110:7, 69:1.</margin>
7. Outside of this Ark, no one remained alive. Thus, outside of Christ, there is no salvation. <margin>Acts 4:12.</margin>

### II. Of the Christian Church.

1. An ungodly Canaan <note>Noah's grandson, often interpreted in this tradition as a symbol of the "wicked" within the visible church</note> and all kinds of unclean animals entered the Ark. <margin>Leviticus 7:13.</margin> The Kingdom of Heaven, or the Church, is like a net in which both good and bad fish are caught.
2. Those outside the Ark had to perish. So too, those outside the Church of Christ.
3. The Ark was driven hither and thither by the waters and had no certain place. So it is with the Church Militant <note>The "Church Militant" refers to the Christian church on earth, struggling against sin and spiritual enemies, as opposed to the Church Triumphant in heaven.</note>.
4. It had only one door: and here there is only One Faith.
5. When seven days had passed, the Great Flood came, and those in the Ark were preserved. When the seventh angel has poured out his bowl, then it shall be finished. <margin>Revelation 16:17.</margin> Then the believers will enter into the eternal Sabbath and be preserved from the fire. <margin>2 Peter 3:10.</margin>
6. After the waters fell, the Ark settled upon the high mountains of Ararat. <margin>Also Isaiah 58:14.</margin>
7. On the 17th day of the 7th month, the Ark came to rest. So will the Church yet find rest when all the waters have receded.

<margin>v. 4. 17th day of the 7th month</margin> According to the calculations of Andreas Goldmayer <note>A 17th-century mathematician and astronomer</note>, this should correspond with April 4th of the back-calculated Julian Calendar in the year 1657, which at that time was a Tuesday; on this same calendar day, 2160 years later, Christ rose from the dead on Easter Sunday.

<margin>Mountains of Ararat</margin> The conjectures of most writers suggest that these are the Gordyaean Mountains <note>Located in the region of Corduene, modern-day southeast Turkey</note>, which Holy Scripture calls Ararat. It is said, as the Chaldean historian Berosus writes in Josephus, that a piece of this ship still exists in Armenia at the Gordyaean mountain, from which people scrape off the pitch to carry with them and use as a proven medicine against poison.

> Tavernier <note>Jean-Baptiste Tavernier (1605–1689), a famous French gem merchant and traveler</note> gives the following report in the 4th chapter of his travelogue: "From Erivan to Tabriz, the caravan usually takes 10 days. — The first day's journey goes across a large level field sown with rice, through which a great many small streams flow. On the second day, one continues across this flat field and keeps the mountains of Ararat in sight toward the south, around which a large number of monasteries are built. The Armenians call this mountain *Meseonlar*, which means 'the Mountain of the Ark.' — It is, as it were, separated from the other Armenian mountains, which hang together like a chain, and from the middle up to the peak it is always covered with snow. It is also larger than all the mountains in the region. — As soon as the Armenians catch sight of it, they kiss the earth, lift their eyes to heaven, make a cross, and say several prayers. It should be known, however, that this mountain is often covered with clouds from its middle to its peak for 3 or 4 months at a time."

<column-break/>

[The waters continued to recede] and diminish until the tenth month. In the tenth month, on the first day of the month, the tops of the mountains were seen.

---

> Johann Heinrich Seyfried shares another report from the mouth of a Dutchman in his *Medulla Mirabilium Naturae* <note>The Marrow of Nature's Wonders, 1679</note>: "A Dutchman named Jan Janz Strauß <note>Jan Janszoon Struys, a Dutch traveler who published accounts of his voyages in 1676</note>, who in July 1670 had the opportunity to climb this mountain to cure a hermit, reports that although this mountain is exceedingly high and appears to far exceed all other mountains in height, including the Caucasus, it can indeed be climbed. He reached the aforementioned hermit's cell after five days of riding. Every five miles along the way, he found a peasant with a donkey carrying food and firewood, because it was 'bitterly cold' at night—so cold that by midnight the ice was thick enough for man and horse to cross over it. He and his companion passed through three kinds of clouds. The lowest were misty, thick, and dark; the next ones further up were very cold and covered with snow, even though it was very warm at the foot of the mountain, where the grapes were beginning to ripen. The highest clouds were colder still, so that they always feared they would freeze completely. They spent four days before they overcame the cold and could reach the hermit's dwelling, which was like a small house carved out of a rock. Outside, the weather was as beautiful as anyone could wish—neither hot nor cold, but a constant, moderate warmth. The hermit reported that although he had lived there for 25 years, he had never felt rain, nor even enough wind to move a feather. Further up toward the peak of the mountain, it was said to be even stiller, and no change in the air was ever felt. Upon taking his leave from the hermit, who was an Italian born in Rome (where his father was a very wealthy man), the hermit presented the author with a cross made of wood from Noah's Ark (in which this hermit claimed to have been himself, having cut the wood with his own hands from a chamber), along with a stone which he had likewise broken off with his hands from beneath the Ark where it still rests. From the plain to the cell is said to be about 7 German miles uphill."

Just as the mountain of Ararat may have been the highest upon which the Ark finally settled—after which another seven months and ten days passed (v. 14) until the judgment of the Flood had entirely moved on—so can this be an image of how, in the midst of the final floods of wrath, the believers must first feel the moment of wrath, the hiding of the Lord, and the storms of tribulation for their purification <margin>Isaiah 54:8, 11.</margin>; afterwards, they shall find their rest and refreshment upon the highest mountain of the glorious Kingdom of Christ, which shall then be revealed <margin>Isaiah 2:2.</margin>, until the remaining seven months (of which <margin>Ezekiel writes in Chapter 39:12, 14</margin>) have passed and the earth is entirely cleansed of its abominations. This, along with the five months and the preceding 40 days (which are included in the Flood, when it rained continuously), makes up the time of one year and one month, and one or several days, as mentioned regarding the final plagues of the trumpet of the sixth angel <margin>Revelation 9:15.</margin>. This also teaches us how, with God, the punishments of the wicked and the tribulations of the believers are wisely divided and measured, as the former increase and the latter decrease.

When the saving wind blows upon the soul, it moves it at first in such a way that the soul cannot distinguish whether it blows for its salvation or its destruction. It is then suddenly terrified when it sees that the Ark has settled upon the mountains of Armenia: which is to say, that peace and rest begin to appear on the highest peak of the spirit, where God reveals Himself through a small ray of His Majesty. This then shows the soul that its destruction is not without hope of rescue, but that hope for its salvation is still present.

---

<margin>(a) The dove is the Holy Spirit, who breathes into you the peace of the soul and the rest of the mind. The raven, however, is an image of sin, which departs and does not return, if only the preservation and nature of righteousness is maintained within you. —St. Ambrose. (a)</margin>

Let us look for a moment at what the dove provides us as a prefiguration of the Holy Spirit.

1. It was a pure, loving, peaceful dove that came to Noah upon the water, just as the Holy Spirit came upon Christ. Matthew 3:16.

2. She came to everyone in the Ark at the same time. All members of the Church must become partakers of the Holy Spirit.

3. Noah sent her out after he had gone from the earth into the Ark: and Christ sent the Holy Spirit after He had gone to Heaven.

4. This dove could not rest except in the Ark. Thus, the Holy Spirit does not depart from the Church.

5. On the 7th day the dove came and brought an olive leaf. Likewise, Christ sent the Holy Spirit on the seven-times-seventh day—that is, on the Day of Pentecost <note>original: "Pfingst-Tag / am Mayen-Tag"; Pentecost often falls in May, here linked to the "blossoming" of the Spirit</note>.

6. She brought the olive leaf in her mouth: the Holy Spirit brings the leaf in the Word.

7. This happened at the time of Vespers <note>Evening prayer time</note>. The evening of the world brings much with it.

The ancients also very finely interpreted the raven as a soul that God once hated and then preserved, but which turns back again to the world and its stinking carcasses of the dead, and in doing so forgets its Lord and Benefactor.

The returning dove signifies those souls who indeed go out in their calling before the LORD and must deal with earthly things; but their foot and heart find no resting place therein. Therefore, they soon turn back and keep the olive branch of peace in their hearts as a sign of their grace-filled state.

The raven represents a self-willed and self-working soul that lingers at everything it encounters. Everything is a rest for such a soul, but it is a deceptive rest, because it immediately encounters inconstancy there.

The dove, however, represents the already surrendered and "beaten down" soul, transformed in God <note>A reference to "annihilation," a mystical term for the total surrender of the ego to God’s will</note>, which goes out from God to work outside of itself when it is God’s will. I mean to say that it goes out from its spiritual rest when Noah—who in this place represents God—sets it out for the benefit of its neighbor. Yet, because there is nothing for it on the earth, it finds no level ground there upon which its feet could rest—that is, nothing upon which it could rely. Therefore, it returns again to its spiritual rest without lingering on anything:

<margin>(a) St. Ambrose, *On the Initiation of Mysteries*, chapter 3, and *On Noah*, chapter 17.</margin>

where the spiritual Noah reaches out his hand and takes it back into himself. This represents the state of annihilation, in which the soul finds nothing for itself on the earth.

After seven days—which represent the seven years of perfect annihilation—it is let out of the Ark again. Then it finds just as good a rest everywhere as in the Ark, for the whole world has become God to it. Then it stays everywhere, even though it stays nowhere. And this is the Apostolic life.

It always carries the sign of peace with it, even if it keeps nothing of it for itself. This soul, engaged in the Apostolic life, takes nothing for itself from what it does for God, but brings the olive branch back to Him with exceedingly great faithfulness. And then it, and all its kind who were confined and locked in the Ark, may go out of the same with great confidence; for they no longer need to use any help against the Flood. They are no longer restricted or supported by anything created, and everything is pure salvation for them, even if they have no outward assurance of their blessedness. From this one recognizes that the waters have retreated and that these souls have nothing more to fear in the world—unless through some unfortunate return into themselves they grant entry to unfaithfulness; yet this is difficult in such a state.

Also in the outer world, there will be peace after the passing of God’s judgments over the anti-Christian world, which the Spirit of God, coming over the children of peace in the latter days, will bring with Him. For then the time and the true era <note>original: "Seculum"; the Latin term for an age or era</note> of the Holy Spirit begins, at the evening of the world, when this holy dove, through its Evangelists and messengers of peace, proclaims peace to all the world; as Isaiah speaks of it in Chapter 52:7-8, and as the dove here in prefiguration brings the joyful news with the olive leaf in its mouth: that all waters, and all cruel peoples, and all judgments of God have flowed away and are no longer present.

And so finally the Holy Spirit will reveal Himself with the anointing and the oil of His gifts in glorious measure to all believers, who shall then be purely righteous and shall possess the new earth eternally. Isaiah 60:21, Joel 2:28-29. Then the Wedding Supper of the Lamb shall be held in delightful love upon the renewed earth, and the glorious fruits of the Spirit will reveal themselves richly in all who are drawn to it: the gentle oil of love, joy, peace, longsuffering, gentleness, goodness, faith, meekness, and temperance. Galatians 5:22.

Let us only receive this holy dove in good time with a quiet nature, and not grieve it with a vain and rebellious way of life; so that it may set a firm foot in our hearts with the gentle olive leaf of divine peace.

# The First Book of Moses. Chapter VIII.

## 13. And it came to pass in the six hundred and first year, on the first day of the first month, the waters were dried up from off the earth. Then Noah removed the roof of the Ark <note>original: "Kasten"; literally "chest," the word used for the Ark in German Bibles</note> and looked, and behold, the surface of the ground was dry.

## 14. In the second month, on the twenty-seventh day of the month, the earth was entirely dry.

## 15. Then God spoke, and said to Noah:

## 16. Go out of the Ark, you and your wife, and your sons and your sons' wives with you.

## 17. Bring out with you every living thing that is with you of all flesh—birds and livestock and every creeping thing that creeps on the earth—so that they may move about on the earth, and be fruitful and multiply on the earth.

## 18. So Noah went out, and his sons, and his wife, and his sons' wives with him.

## 19. All the wild animals, all the creeping things, and all the birds, everything that moves upon the earth, went out of the Ark according to their kinds.

After the waters receded, it became dry again; however, at first, the earth was still sticky and muddy. Therefore, it lasted another month and 27 days until the earth was completely dried out of its internal moisture and was thus suitable for habitation again. And so one sees how this judgment of the Great Flood lasted a full year and ten days: as it began on the 17th day of the second month (Chapter 7:11) and ended on the 27th day of the second month.

When God remembers His elect, who cry out to Him day and night amidst the enduring floods of wrath, the Spirit of God will again become active with power within them to gradually drive them <note>This likely refers to driving out the "worldly" or "earthly" nature within the soul</note> from the earth. Meanwhile, they must wait with Noah for the Lord from one morning watch to the next, as spiritual watchmen, and especially for the dawning blessed morning of the "7th time," as the time of redemption.

v. 15-17. This shows how much trouble God takes with those souls who have surrendered themselves to Him, and who wish for nothing but to live in peace in the "Ark" of righteous self-denial. He reminds them of all things at the proper time. In this regard, Noah's caution in sending out the dove might seem useless—or even contrary—to Providence, were it not as full of mystery as it is. Learn, O you souls who are in the Ark by God’s command—namely, in spiritual rest—that you must not go out from there into the "Apostolic life" <note>A life of outward ministry or action</note> without God’s command, which He will show you momentarily through His Providence!

v. 18. **Out)** Into the landscape of Greater Armenia, which is separated from Lesser Armenia by the Euphrates toward the evening <note>westward</note>, and is also called Gordyene <note>An ancient region in Upper Mesopotamia</note>.

Without a doubt, Noah remained on the mountain with his family for a good length of time, as he well knew the state of the world and the earth, until the earth was properly dried and the dead bodies were consumed.

So also, after the great Day of Judgment of this world, the souls kept in their solitude who feared the Lord’s name shall go out at the glorious rising of the "Sun of Righteousness" and salvation under whose wings they shall dwell upon an earth purified of sinners.

<column-break/>

## 20. And Noah built an altar to the LORD, and took of every clean animal and of every clean bird, and offered burnt offerings on the altar.

## 21. An... <note>The text breaks here, likely continuing "And the Lord smelled the soothing aroma"</note>

Since the Lord had so miraculously rescued him and his family from apparent danger of death—in which he had trusted God’s bare word—and now saw himself free again, behold, his spirit burned with desire to love and praise God for it.

Although his heart must have been most occupied internally—sinking itself deeper into God's heart through such an experience of God's faithfulness, and becoming rooted and grounded in His love—it nevertheless broke out externally into certain signs, and his hand and mouth overflowed from that fullness.

Now, however, everyone can easily notice that God took no pleasure in the strangling and burning of livestock, or in other external works of sacrifice. For He declares Himself quite differently in Isaiah 1:11 and elsewhere. Rather, it was actually the intent of God, and of those who sought Him, that humans should learn with all earnestness to surrender themselves and their animalistic desires and characteristics to the fire of Divine Justice, for consumption and purification by the Holy Spirit, in the eternal High Priest Jesus Christ, in whom everything is pleasing to God.

To this end, the ancients took encouragement and stimulation through external sacrifices, whereby the Holy Spirit may have most powerfully reminded them—through the burning and consuming of the sacrificial pieces on the fire—how their self-will, desire-based faith, and the whole "old man" <term>Old Man: A Pauline theological term for the unregenerate, sinful nature of humanity</term> must be gradually put away and consumed.

"If you, O man," says Ephrem Syrus (a), "have no sheep or dove, then simply confess your sins: they shall be for you in place of a burnt offering. If you pray, God will accept it as a calf. If you fall down truly and rightly before Him, He will respect your diligence more than a bullock. Why should you have to buy a sheep, since repentance pleases God better than animals and birds? O the great grace of the Gospel, which has improved the whole Law!"
<margin>(a) Book on Repentance, page 564.</margin>

Accordingly, the work of sacrifice mainly signified the slaughter of desires and the surrender of natural powers. For example, the ram was a symbol of reason, the bull a sign of anger, the goat an indication of evil lust, and so forth. Thus, spiritual sacrifices are not only the mortification of desires and the whole fleshly life—slaughtered by the sword of the Spirit—but also the presentation of all natural powers, which are dedicated to God and burned in the fire of spiritual grace.

We should, however, offer all our things to the Lord—even the greatest—to pray and to leave them to Him. We should bring to Him our faith and our souls, which have their origin not from the earth, but from heaven.

Now, at that time, Noah undoubtedly brought the best that he had to the Lord as a sacrifice, and indeed with a fervent, thankful heart. Therefore, it was so pleasing to the Lord that He accepted it as a...

Chapter VIII. The First Book of Moses. 63

<margin>
Chapters 9:11, 15.
(a) Leviticus 1:9.
</margin>
**21. And when the LORD smelled the soothing aroma (a) / then the LORD said in His heart:**

---

**Soothing aroma)** Can we truly imagine that GOD takes pleasure in the smell of burnt animals? Ephesians 5:2. <note>original: "Lieblichen Geruch"; literally "lovely smell" or "sweet savor." The author references Paul’s letter to the Ephesians, which describes Christ’s sacrifice as a "sweet-smelling aroma" to explain the spiritual rather than physical nature of God’s "smelling."</note>

In the Hebrew, it actually says: the LORD smelled a "scent of rest"; with a deliberate reference and pointer to Noah's name. <note>In Hebrew, the name Noah (Noach) is related to the word for "rest" (nuach). The author is highlighting a linguistic pun in the original text.</note> This is because GOD rested from His anger and His weariness over the sins of mankind and was at peace again. He also found pleasure in Noah's faith and was so truly satisfied and appeased by it that He let His anger go, and love rose up again and overcame His wrath.

Through the Messiah, everything about Noah became pleasant to GOD, because everything was sanctified through faith and prayer: so much so, that even his outward works were something great and good in God’s eyes.

To human reason, it might seem like nothing special that Noah went and lit a fire, burning one or another animal or bird; which, furthermore, does not exactly give off a pleasant smell when burned. And yet, it pleased the LORD well, because it was done in faith in Him.

And all our works, whatever they may be, give off a certain "scent" that rises before God’s face, and is either accepted or rejected by Him. GOD has a certain perception of everything humans do or leave undone, which the Scripture calls "smelling."

If we now desire that our deeds should be pleasant to the LORD our GOD, we must learn to press into the good pleasure of GOD through faith, which He has in His Son. In Him alone must everything be well-pleasing to the Father, because outside of Him, nothing counts before Him. Everything we do or refrain from doing must be offered up to the Father in Christ to become pleasant; outside of Him, everything is merely sin, because it does not come from faith.

If a person does their deeds with a contrite, humble, and confident heart toward GOD in His fear and love, then everything becomes pleasant to the Father in Christ—like a lovely incense that commends itself through the power of the Holy Spirit.

Therefore, everything a true believer does to please and honor GOD is a sweet scent to the Lord, an acceptable service, and a sanctified sacrifice through Christ in the Holy Spirit.

Rightly should we be concerned whether our deeds likewise stir up pleasure in the LORD, and not perhaps disgust and abomination. Did GOD not reject and turn away the Jews with their "shining" sacrifices? <note>A reference to hypocritical religious observance that looks good on the outside but lacks inner faith.</note> And what else is all the faithless worship of hypocrites but an abomination, a foul odor and stench, before GOD?

Oh, if only one could learn to believe that a contrite and broken heart is the best sacrifice that pleases GOD! If only we would let ourselves be convinced by the Holy Spirit that all our affairs would be pleasant to GOD if we only learned to walk in humility and faith with Noah, and did not rush headlong with our hot, proud nature, which spoils everything!

Nothing quiets and satisfies God’s heart like the mind of Christ. When He finds that in us, as He found it in Noah, then GOD is glad to be at peace with us and has only thoughts of peace toward us—as He did here toward Noah, indeed, over the whole world. For in this way, Noah found grace before the LORD not only for his own person, but also for every creature. Such is the power of faith. It is such a power of the Spirit that it wins words from the living GOD even in the midst of the greatest wrath, and opens His heart to Him, so that He forms a gracious decree within Himself for the preservation and sparing of the poor creature. Therefore, GOD spoke in or

**To His heart:)** Namely, to Noah’s heart, to comfort him. For to speak to someone's heart is to comfort them. Isaiah 40:1, 2; Hosea 2:16. And if we understand GOD’s heart, that is His dear Son.

<column-break/>

**I will never again curse the ground because of man; For**

---

**I will -- never again -- For)** A wonderful and entirely extraordinary reason in the eyes of reason: that GOD chooses not to punish precisely because people are evil. One would rather expect the opposite, thinking: for that very reason GOD must strike, because everything is corrupted and malicious.

But our thoughts are not GOD’s thoughts, and His ways are not our ways. Faith alone recognizes and enjoys the fact that GOD is patient and sparing precisely for the sake of human misery.

One can note in the Scriptures that sometimes the sins and the corruption of men, and their confession of them, are presented as a motivating cause for GOD to show mercy. As in Psalm 103:13, 14. In general, the Scripture praises God’s tireless long-suffering toward His creatures, and thus places misery and grace, sin and patience, corruption and sparing, closely together; so that penitent sinners may learn to reconcile and accept them in faith, and apply them well.

For it requires "art" <note>In this context, "art" refers to a spiritual skill or learned discipline.</note> when a person in their distress over sin is to become truly certain that GOD wants to be gracious to them precisely because they are a sinner. On the other hand, how unbelief must be fought against—no one knows this except one who falls into such anguish of conscience and cannot reach GOD’s love. In such distress, one first learns to understand how GOD must spare us precisely because of our deep corruption, so that we do not perish entirely under it. Only then does one truly seek and dig for divine love and patience, and learns to rightly present to GOD in faith how He must be good to us precisely because we are so miserable.

Oh, that is a great mystery, and a true wealth of goodness, patience, and long-suffering! Through this, GOD most wants to make Himself great and glorious, and in this He seeks His greatest honor.

**Curse the ground)** Namely, through a general decree of destruction. For otherwise, GOD has not bound His hands from destroying this or that part, land, or stretch of the earth.

The curse always precedes the outbreak of the punishment itself. The divine order proceeds toward punishment in stages and does not overtake man suddenly. First, GOD forms a resolution; thereafter, He actually pronounces the judgment and the curse; and if no improvement follows, then the punishment is certain.

Thus, we should always be wary of the pronouncement of divine justice and prevent it through repentance and faith; so that GOD is not judged and compelled to break out with a curse instead of a blessing over a land and place.

**For)** Just as timid and trembling souls have no reason to doubt GOD’s goodness and patience—after they can sufficiently recognize from the great example of the first world how GOD does not always contend nor keep His anger forever, nor plague mankind from His heart—so too, bold sinners have no right to twist this into a perverse sense of wantonness, to continue more freely in sin because the grace of GOD is so overflowing and the human condition so corrupt and desperate that even GOD Himself would have no hope of bringing the children of men to any good.

One must therefore be careful not to be led by the little word *For* and the reason given therein to such an interpretation by which a person necessarily abandons all diligence to do good, gives up all hope, and allows their soul to languish. For how can a man have any hope for good if GOD Himself despairs of it?

This can impossibly be the meaning of GOD if we consider the reconciliation that has been made; rather, the words must carry with them a ground of good hope and awaken the soul to an obedient walk with GOD.

Yet, it should not merely be called *for*, but the words may very well be rendered as:

<header>The 1st Book of Moses, Chapter IX.</header>

For the inclination <note>original: "Dichten"; referring to the inner imaginings, thoughts, or impulses of the soul</note> of the human heart is evil from his childhood; and I will never again strike down every living thing as I have done.

22. As long as the earth remains, seedtime and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night shall not cease.

---

<note>The following text is commentary on the preceding verses.</note>

**because the thought of the human heart was evil)** These words are brought forward as a reason why the Lord destroyed the earth this time and dealt so severely with the old world. As for this same reason, the Lord had already decided to punish the old world in Chapter 6:5-7. The only difference here is that it explicitly states: our heart is evil.

**From his childhood on)** From the very first hour, as soon as a living breath is within him.

Many consider their childhood years to be innocent and happy, believing they had done no evil then. Now, in comparison to the growing wickedness of later years—when malice perverts the understanding—those early years might perhaps not have been so full of outward outrage. Nevertheless, it remains certain that the seed of all wickedness lies within the smallest child. Therefore, the Hebrew word also indicates the most tender infancy.

Do not, therefore, hold such flattering thoughts about your younger years, as if they were entirely innocent. Instead, consider not a single hour of your life spent outside the state of conversion and grace to be blessed or pleasing to God, and perform all the more earnest repentance. Indeed, we may well learn to pray with true earnestness: *Remember not the sins of my youth!*

This should also give those involved in the upbringing of children <term>Kinderzucht; the discipline and moral education of children</term> important cause for reflection: that they should attack the "tree of corruption" at its root, and not merely lead the poor children toward outward works and hypocrisy, which only does them more harm. If one believes that their inclinations and inner nature are especially evil in youth, then one will wisely seek to cure the damage from the inside out; one will point them to the ground of their hearts and thereby lay the foundation for a true improvement.

In general, God leads us all together toward the heart, as the center or the foundation of the entire human being and life. As things stand within a person, so are all his actions and omissions. If the spring is unclean, then its outflows cannot be clean.

Should this news then not be more than precious and dear to us—that we now know where we should begin if we wish to turn to God? Namely, at the heart, O man, you must begin to better yourself; otherwise, all your efforts are lost.

See here, God reveals to you the origin of all your misery! You should not spend a long time in vain trying only to chop off the leaves and branches of the tree of corruption, or merely cutting off the weeds at the surface! You must learn to dig deep and begin at the root, if you are concerned with improvement in truth. *The heart is evil*, says God: *Its inclination and striving are evil.* Examine your innermost self in this! Does this judgment of God still apply to you? Have your inclinations and strivings all become good? Consider your falsehood and self-love, which still mingle with everything good. How you ruin everything with secret intentions and impurities!

Therefore, do not only begin to change your life from the outside, but also become better from the inside out. Out of the heart come your wicked things.

Many a man covers up how "excellently" he is converted if he merely puts aside or stops something outwardly—if it even goes that far, and is not simply hidden secretly so that it is not noticed. But see Matthew 23:26. What is accomplished by that, other than keeping an unclean foundation in the heart?

The best advice is that one first takes hold of his heart and lets the Holy Spirit work upon its ground; then, finally, something good will surely come out.

<column-break/>

## Chapter IX.

->The Covenant of Grace renewed with Noah.<-

And God blessed Noah and his sons, and said to them: Be fruitful and multiply, and fill the earth.

2. And the fear of you and the dread of you shall be upon every beast of the earth, and upon every bird of the heavens, in everything that creeps on the ground, and in all the fish of the sea; they are given into your hand.

3. All...

---

<note>The following text is commentary on the preceding verses of Chapter IX.</note>

God promises Noah the blessing for the multiplication of the human race through him, so that the blessed "Seed of the Woman" <note>A reference to the promised Messiah from Genesis 3:15</note>, as the source of all blessing, should be born from his descendants. In this repeated blessing, it is right to remember the blessing following the poured-out bowls of wrath, when children shall be born to the Lord, *more numerous than the dew from the womb of the morning* (Psalm 110). Just as then the animal-like men shall be trampled (Malachi 4:3). <note>The original cites Malachi 3:21, which follows the numbering in some German Bibles; in English Bibles, this is Malachi 4:3.</note> Therefore, God also promises here that wild animals should not harm man, but at the rising of the sun they should make away and betake themselves to their dens, so that man could go about his work without fear (Psalm 104:22-23). Therefore, it is a special judgment when God arms wild animals against men to harm them (Leviticus 26:22; Ezekiel 14:15, 21).

**v. 1. 7. Be fruitful and multiply)** Just as it was undeniably God’s will that the earth should not be or remain desolate and empty, it can just as little (and even much less) be His will that it should multiply merely with vain thorns, thistles, and poisonous, destructive weeds. This pronouncement is by no means intended to mean that every rogue and hypocrite, unbeliever and godless person, should multiply his malicious and cursed seed and in such a way heap up and provoke the righteous curse of His wrath for the Day of Wrath.

Also, not everything spoken by God to Noah the Righteous is simultaneously spoken and commanded to every hypocrite and unbeliever, pagan and "hypocrite-Christian."

Thus the seed of Adam, Noah, Abraham, and Israel could not remain eternally, even according to the flesh, but had to cease in its time—indeed, be rejected—and a completely different seed must be accepted; namely, the seed of Noah according to the Spirit, as the true and only Seed of all promises. When, however, someone's seed is corrupted and deemed unfit, how much more will the fruit growing from it be rejected: since it is impossible to harvest healthy and wholesome grain from a poisoned, unclean seed.

It is therefore lack of understanding and self-conceit upon which all those fortify themselves who, in the propagation of a sinful, malicious, and unrighteous seed, wish to help themselves with this verse and ground themselves upon it while outside the state of grace.

For even if not only this, but much more, is spoken and approved by God, it is nevertheless meant for no one, nor demanded of anyone, except the one who is restored to His divine kind, nature, race, and seed, and to the form of His image.

In that case, however, one multiplies correctly upon the earth when one leads souls to Jesus Christ, both for righteousness and for the inner life.

# Chapter IX. The First Book of Moses.

3. Everything that moves / that lives / shall be your food. As I gave you the green plants, I have given you all of this.
4. However, you shall not eat flesh with its soul / namely, its blood.
5. For I will surely demand your blood for the sake of your souls! From the hand of all animals I will demand it; and from the hand of man / from the hand of every man’s brother / I will demand the soul of man.

<margin>v. 1.</margin> After the tribulations of the Deluge, man is restored to a state of innocence: the fruits of which he now enjoys. This is indicated by the power he is given to rule over the animals and the freedom to eat of everything.

<margin>v. 3.</margin> **that lives / shall be your food)** Many hold the opinion that even before the Flood, the eating of meat was customary and permitted. But their reasons are mostly just conjectures.

<margin>v. 4.</margin> This is one of the seven Laws of Noah, which at that time took the place of the Law, and by which men partially governed themselves; their content together consisted of the following:
> I. You shall not practice idolatry nor worship images;
> II. You shall not misuse the Name of God;
> III. You shall shed no blood;
> IV. You shall flee from incest;
> V. You shall not steal or rob;
> VI. Rather, you shall maintain law and justice;
> VII. You shall not eat a limb from a living animal.

<column-break/>

6. Whoever sheds human blood / by man shall his blood be shed. For He made man in God’s image. <gloss>Chapter 1:26, 27.</gloss>
7. But you, be fruitful and multiply / bring forth abundantly on the earth / and multiply upon it.
8. And

<margin>v. 6.</margin> God intended to forbid the killing of humans very earnestly because man is His property, whom He created in His own image: so that neither the person himself nor anyone else has power over his life; (See Romans 14:7-8) nor should one curse another / or grieve their spirit through hatred. 1 John 3:15. But should a man become a murderer / or should an animal, driven by Satan, kill a man; that should be avenged through a human court. To which end God also intended to establish authorities / and entrust them with the sword for vengeance over such murderers. Romans 13:4. Exodus 21:12, 14, 28, etc. Leviticus 24:17, etc. Now, what is not avenged by men here—especially regarding the "Great Ones" of this world, who have people killed by others in unjust wars / or through unjust death sentences—God will avenge / either in this time / or certainly there in eternity. See 2 Samuel 12:10-11. Psalm 9:13. This should be noted with trembling by the powerful / who value human life so little / sacrificing it to their lusts / since God will indeed demand it of them one day. Revelation 13:10.
And certainly, authorities in general have much to consider regarding those they deal with, even in judgment: namely, that they have before them humans made in God’s image. They should rightly guard themselves against all tyranny, injustice, and other sins against such a noble creature.
And generally, for this reason, it lies upon the consciences of all that they should be kindly disposed toward their servants, children, friends, and...

---

...toward all people, as toward their equals, and further respect and treat their neighbor / however lowly he may be / in their hearts as God's image.

What the Creator forbids here regarding the shedding of human blood, based on this precious foundation, truly applies to all other offenses against our neighbor. For by them, we offend God, the good Creator Himself. Thus, the "image" must still mean something great even after the Fall, and we must not forget or view the first creation of man as abolished, but rather regulate, hold, and conduct ourselves according to it.

Precisely for this reason, even cursing one's neighbor is forbidden in the New Testament on this basis. James 3:9.

And it would be an important question in the New Testament: whether and to what extent this commandment—to have human blood shed for those who have shed the blood of others—remains binding within Christendom.

Even though murder is in a certain sense to be regarded as a greater crime than idolatry, sorcery, blasphemy, etc., which are nonetheless capital crimes and directly offend God: because it shows a greater malice to willfully take the life of one's neighbor / whom one sees / and who is related by the same human nature and other close circumstances; than to sin in this or that way against God / whom one does not see / and from whom one is distant through unbelief: and precisely for this reason, the death penalty for it was determined here by God immediately after the Flood; also, every murderer will find the justice of this punishment within his own conscience: yet, it is not so clearly and distinctly determined and settled as has been assumed for a long time / what kind of justice should be exercised in this regard in the New Testament and among Christians.

The Old Covenant and its economy <note>The "economy" refers to God's specific way of managing or "dispensing" his plan during a particular era of history.</note> indeed required many kinds of slaughter and killing as a foreshadowing, and there it was absolutely necessary that the blood of a willful murderer had to be shed in return: because the blood of the One had not yet been shed who took the guilt of all men upon Himself / and who, being counted among the transgressors between two murderers on the Cross, let His precious blood be shed for the complete reconciliation of all our blood-guilt. Now that this great sacrifice of atonement for our sin has been offered once in the fullness of time / and truly sets free from the guilt of death all those who have seized it with true faith in sincere repentance: should it then not have the power / at the very least to set converted and believing transgressors free from the punishment of death under such circumstances? Since princes and lords take the right and power for themselves to absolve from a deserved death based on far lesser foundations / perhaps in honor of a royal wedding / or at other solemn festivities / and for similar reasons.

Could not the first brother-murderer, Cain, escape the deserved death penalty through a special and extraordinary divine sign of grace as a foreshadowing, after showing regret and penance, even though blood had been shed which cried out against him for vengeance? Chapter 4:13-16. How much more today will a murderer of his neighbor (if he performs true penance) be able to escape the death penalty in the spiritual fulfillment through the actual grace revealed in Christ Jesus, since that blood has been shed which speaks better than Abel’s / and speaks not for vengeance / but for reconciliation. Hebrews 12:24.

Who will speak against this powerful reason?

Meanwhile, in death penalties, God's hidden hand and order are certainly to be recognized; He who rules the world with His wisdom and directs worldly legislators to ordain and carry out that which should happen according to His secret judgments over the malice of men.

Both are God's will and order; but each in its time and in its way. Grace does not abolish Wrath in its order: and Wrath does not abolish Grace in its order. However, since such a great fullness of grace spreads over us through the shed blood of the New Covenant, Grace boasts against Wrath / and is, where it is recognized, to be preferred.

<margin>Revelation 4:3.</margin>
