<note>v. 12. 13. Sign of the covenant — my bow</note> Luther, Brentz, and Melanchthon, Cornelius à Lapide, Pareus, Tasanus, Piscator, Münster, Andreas Rivetus, Johannes Vallesius, Peter Martyr, Musculus, and many others / hold the opinion / that before the Flood no bow was to be seen in the clouds of heaven / and that GOD first created it / when he established this covenant with Noah.

Others, however, argue / with more grounded reasoning / that it existed even before the Flood / but was only here chosen and appointed as a special Sign of Grace: since its causes are natural / and must also have existed before the Flood.

According to the given causes, it is said to arise / when a water-cloud lets its drops fall against the sun / where each and every one of these falling drops catches the rays of the sun in its roundness / as in a mirror / and represents all colors to this wondrous-looking bow / and encourages mankind to remember the love of GOD / because of the covenant made with Noah.

The 3 colors of the rainbow are significant; the yellowish fire-color / the red from blood / and the green from the growing herbs / through which the life in them is indicated: whereby the wrath and fiery zeal of the justice of GOD / and the reconciliation through the blood of Christ / and the hope of eternal life earned thereby / can be brought to the mind of the believer.

And what else does this mean than a sacrament / since this bow is so often called a sign of the covenant / which was namely intended to give assurance of the grace of GOD in JESUS Christ: who for this reason appeared in Ezekiel 1:26–28 and Revelation 4:3, 10:1 with a rainbow.

---

<image-desc>Decorative circular ornament</image-desc>

GOD binds himself to man / and for their sake also to the animals / that he will bear everything with his divine sparing patience until the Final Judgment / so that no more general destruction of men and animals should occur / although in specific judgments great defeats of both often happen / through which men shall be reminded of the final general judgment. And for the assurance of this, he wished to set a sign in the heavens / so that after heavy rains / which should cause men to think of the judgment of the Flood / he then lets a rainbow appear / so that after the preceding dark clouds everything clears up very pleasantly / and they might hold fast to the promised grace in this covenant / which is founded on the Covenant of Grace in Christ / (see Chapter 8:21) / and take their refuge in his promise in Christ. For this covenant is made not so much with the earth and with the animals / as with sinful man / for whose sake the earth and the animals exist. And indeed GOD well knew / that man’s heart is evil from youth upward / and yet he establishes the covenant. Therefore it must necessarily be a Covenant of Grace / not without redemption and forgiveness of sins through the Messiah / in whose faith Noah sacrificed / and became an heir of righteousness. <gloss>Hebrews 11:7.</gloss>

After GOD’s wrath was cooled by the destruction of the evil creatures / behold, his love and goodness broke forth again / which had been, as it were, held back and darkened by sin. And so he still proceeds / when he must visit the iniquity of men out of necessity. He truly grieves / and often punishes sharply / but he also has mercy again / and appeals to his covenant made here with the presentation of this. <gloss>Isaiah 54:7.</gloss>

Such a covenant consists of 4 actions; of which 2 are on GOD’s side: his requisition <term>Erheischung - a formal demand or requirement</term> / which demands something he wants done; and his promise / that after the fulfillment of the obligation he will be our GOD. On man’s side, a counter-promise to GOD’s requirement / in the manner of a humble prayer to GOD; because the parties / who establish the covenant / are entirely unequal: and a counter-requirement. That which GOD requires of man is man's whole duty: <gloss>Exodus 20:1–17</gloss> summarized more briefly in <gloss>Deuteronomy 10:12</gloss> / even shorter in <gloss>Micah 6:8</gloss> / and even shorter in <gloss>Matthew 22:37.</gloss>

How should not everyone now learn to surrender themselves into this holy covenant of GOD with repentance and faith / so that they might enjoy GOD’s patience and longsuffering toward his creatures / and be covered under the same as under the shadow of his wings and in a booth in the evil time!

Certainly / we can all enjoy this covenant / if we only will! Namely, that we let ourselves be preserved from destruction / and surrender ourselves into the promises of GOD with faith and humility for protection against all evil. Above all, the blessed proposal would be worthy of all acceptance / that we might faithfully immerse ourselves in the Covenant of Life / which GOD has opened to all men through his Son for redemption and actually offers.

If GOD here promised / to spare the creature externally from general destruction / how many thousand times more gladly does he spare the soul from spiritual and eternal ruin. Therefore, when this Covenant of Life is offered to us by GOD / and our heart is reminded of it; then faith through the Holy Spirit should be awake / to grasp the Word of Life with joy / and to surrender oneself to GOD anew for life and blessing.

Indeed, this should rightly be man’s most noble work / that he, morning and evening / and always / as it were every moment / renewed the covenant with GOD / sought his love always anew / and thus became and remained partaker of the promise of GOD for life / salvation, and peace.

The eternal Lover of mankind has pleasure in this himself / when we poor earthworms así hunger and thirst after his grace. He seeks his glory in this / that he promises life again to poor repentant sinners / and so gladly does good to them again after their humiliation.

### Ch. IX. The First Book of Moses.

**14.** And it shall come to pass, when I bring clouds over the earth, that the bow shall be seen in the clouds.
**15.** And I will remember my covenant, which is between me and you and every living soul in all flesh: that the waters shall no more become a flood to destroy all flesh.
**16.** When the bow is in the clouds, I will look upon it, to remember the everlasting covenant between God and every living soul in all flesh that is upon the earth.
**17.** Then God said to Noah: This is the sign of the covenant which I have established between me and all flesh that is upon the earth.

<column-break/>

**18.** The sons of Noah who went out of the ark were Shem, Ham, and Japheth. Ham is the father of Canaan.
**19.** These three are the sons of Noah: and from these the whole earth was overspread.
**20.** Noah <note>The text notes that Noah began to be a man of the soil.</note>

From this it is to be seen how Noah fathered no more children after the Great Flood, but rather from these three sons all the inhabitants of the earth were subsequently propagated.

<margin>
Chardin <note>Jean Chardin (1643–1713) was a French jeweler and traveler famous for his ten-volume "The Travels of Sir John Chardin" into Persia and the Near East.</note> relates in his travel description that in the Georgian region of Kartli, not far from the market town of Surami, there is an area called Samtskhe, of which the inhabitants are accustomed to say that Noah turned to live in this region after he left the ark, and that his sons built three castles there. This is also said to be indicated by the Georgian word *Samtskhe*, which is supposed to mean "three castles."
</margin>

Not without reason have learned men, both from Holy Scripture and other writings, concluded that the entire world was divided into three parts according to the number of Noah's sons: to Shem fell the entire Orient with half of the North toward the East; to Ham fell the South; and to Japheth the Western lands with the other half of the North. This division has remained ever since: so that Shem's portion was called Asia, Japheth’s Europe, and Ham’s Land of the Moors or Africa. (a) For from these three sons and their descendants, countless nations and kingdoms arose and were spread and established in the world: from Japheth and his sons in the West and North came the Tartars, Greeks, Germans, Italians, Danes, Scythians, and (if Jewish traditions are to be believed) 200 nations in total; from Ham came the Canaanites, Moors, Egyptians, and 394 nations in total in the South; from Shem, on the other hand, the Oriental peoples: Hebrews, Assyrians, Chaldeans, Syrians, Persians, Armenians, and 406 families in total. (b)

<margin>
(a) Cluver, *Ancient Germany*, Book 1, Chapter 4. <note>Original Latin: "Cluver. l. 1 Germ. antiq. c.4." Philipp Clüver was a 17th-century geographer.</note>
(b) Phil. Glaser, in *Historical Collection*. <note>Original Latin: "Phil. Glaser. in Syngramm. histor." Philipp Glaser was a 17th-century historian.</note>
</margin>

---

-> Let us look a little more closely at this image of Grace. <-

1. The rainbow arises when the sun shines on clouds and vapors. Thus God’s grace appeared when Christ appeared in the flesh, or enlightened the flesh.
2. The rainbow is a harbinger of either good weather or future rain. Upon the covenant established with Christ, "good weather"—a pleasant time—and the Holy Spirit followed and were poured out.
3. In the rainbow, the sun shines through the rising vapors and rain. In the midst of tribulations, those who stand in God's covenant see His friendly face. His grace shines through the mists of temptation: and when they have once endured all the waters of tribulation, it will truly clear up at Christ’s second coming, and a rainbow of eternal grace and mercy will rise. Therefore, He appears with His rainbow above Him at the beginning and conclusion of His kingdom.
4. The rainbow reaches from heaven to earth and unites them. So in Christ, God and humanity—indeed, God and men—are united after He came from heaven to earth.
5. It stands between heaven and earth; it is a mediator between God and men. (1 Timothy 2:5).
6. The bow does not point toward the earth, but toward heaven. <note>This suggests the "weapon" of God's wrath is turned away from humanity.</note> In Christ, the bow of wrath is turned around.
7. At the top, the bow is one; at the bottom, there are two parts. In Christ there is one person; indeed, all is one. Above, we are all one if we stand in the covenant of grace: but here on earth, there is often division.
8. The round form is the most perfect. At the top, the bow is round where it touches the heavens: to indicate that those who belong to the covenant of grace will become perfect above.
9. There is a green color, very pleasant and beneficial to the eyes: signifying God's grace, mercy, and long-suffering, which are pleasant to sinners.
10. There is a bright, shining yellow color, signifying God's strict justice and holiness.
11. These two colors are mixed and tempered by a purple-red <note>Original: "blau-rothen" (blue-red)</note>: signifying that God's mercy and justice are tempered by the blood of Christ and made manifest with it; so that in Christ's blood, we fear and love God.

So let us then, who see His bow, remember His covenant with greater inwardness; for the Jews even now, when they see a rainbow, pray and thank God that He does not bring a flood of water, though they might well deserve it. How much more then should we fear God's justice, love His mercy, and take hold of the blood of Jesus Christ with true faith. Especially since the sign of the covenant only benefits those who are members of the covenant.
And although God still spares the animal-like humans along with the animals—those who often behave like unclean and wild beasts, especially toward believers (see Matthew 7:6, 10:16; 2 Timothy 4:7)—He primarily makes a covenant with those who possess the faith and obedience of Noah, through the most intimate union, when He forms them into His own image. This is the indissoluble spiritual marriage. Therefore, God gives a sign of this covenant and places it in the heavens. Namely, He makes such a soul so immovable and so raised above itself that it can no longer fear the flood; because its transformation makes it as immovable as heaven is unchangeable, and protects it from all assaults. This sign is thus the immovability and the everlasting state of a soul standing in union and transformation.
(Verse 14.) Even if the soul is covered with the clouds of affliction from without, this sign of foundational constancy will nevertheless shine through these clouds: on the contrary, it will be most observed within itself; just as the rainbow is only seen in clouds. This is the infallible mark of a transformed state. For all those who have not yet reached that point have fluctuations from time to time, and their immovability is not constant for all time.

### The First Book of Moses. Chapter IX.

### 20. And Noah began to be a man of the soil, and he planted a vineyard.

According to the opinion of Armenian writers, the city of Nakhchivan <note>original: "Nacsivan"</note> is said to be the oldest in Armenia, built by Noah, who also established his dwelling there after the Deluge. The Armenians also wish to prove from the name of the city that it is the very oldest in that land, and that in the ancient Armenian language, it means "the first dwelling" or "the first settlement." Friedrich Spanheim <note>Friedrich Spanheim (1632–1701) was a noted Calvinist theologian and historian.</note> says the word *Nak Sivan* means as much as "the station of the ship" <note>original: "Navis stationem"</note>.

And although (writes Athanasius Kircher <note>Athanasius Kircher (1602–1680) was a Jesuit polymath who published "Arca Noë" (Noah's Ark) in 1675, a massive work on the Ark and the post-flood world.</note> in *Arca Noë*) Holy Scripture mentions little of Noah’s deeds and actions after the Deluge, sound reason suggests that he did not sit idle, but with the greatest diligence and care populated the world through his lineage, divided it, established orders, and governed the earth, etc. — He left Armenia or the Land of Eden, took with him Japheth with his sons and grandsons, and came first to Greece, and from there to Italy. There he inhabited and ruled the land, which was still empty of inhabitants, and there he instructed his descendants in the foundations of religion, natural science, and other useful arts. Finally, he attained such a name among them that they called him the "Seed of the World," the "Soul of the World," and "Saturn," and even erected columns in his honor.

But so that (writes the aforementioned Kircher elsewhere) no one should think that I invented this out of my own brain; one may look it up in the *Apologies* of the martyr Justin, and in Tertullian, Augustine, Clement of Alexandria, and other commentators on this passage in Genesis. In this, he also appeals to the agreement of all the Rabbis and Arabic writers, and among them he cites Berosus <note>Berosus was a 3rd-century BC Babylonian priest; however, the "Berosus" cited here is likely the "Pseudo-Berosus" published by Annius of Viterbo in 1498, a famous literary forgery that influenced early modern history.</note>.

The words of Berosus, from the 5th book of *Chaldean Antiquities*, are recorded by him as follows: "Nimrod and Bel,
> "who ruled in Babylon, were entirely possessed by a
> "wicked lust for power and a desire to expand their empire.
> "However, as they clearly noticed that the
> "unique Saturn <note>referring to Noah</note>, who held the highest power in Armenia,
> "might resist and halt their criminal undertakings,
> "so that they would have in him an enemy and adversary;
> "they tried everything to find an opportunity
> "to remove him from the way. Sabbatius
> "Saga (as Noah is called there) noticed this, and saw fit

> "hidden for a time in the outermost mountains of Armenia.
> "When Bel had died, and his son
> "Ninus, who succeeded him in the government, was also
> "intent on getting Sabbatius out of the way;
> "Saturn finally considered it advisable to avoid the
> "wicked pursuit, which was not unknown to him,
> "and went with his family to Italy."

Planted vineyards) Like the poets' Janus <note>The Roman god of beginnings and transitions, often depicted with two faces.</note>, from *Sasin*, that is, wine: to whom they also attributed two faces, because Noah had seen the previous and the current world.

Noah is the image of our Lord Jesus Christ, who wishes to build anew our earth, devastated by sin and drowned by the Deluge. Where it was barren, he makes it fruitful.

But how does he build it, and what does he plant upon it? The vine, the image of love. When Jesus Christ enters into a soul that has come into God through the denial of all things, and becomes flesh in the same in a spiritual way; then he plants in it the vine: namely, according to the mind of the Bride <note>A reference to the Song of Solomon, representing the soul's relationship with God.</note>, he orders love. Just as the grape shares everything with others and keeps nothing for itself: So love releases the one who possesses it from everything he has, and does not permit him to possess anything which he does not share with others.

<column-break/>

### 21. And he drank of the wine, and was drunken; and he was uncovered within his tent.

<margin>Gen. 19:33. Eph. 5:18.</margin>
Many wish to cover their own nakedness with his. It may concern the Spirit. 22.

Just as Jesus Christ comes into the soul to make it a partaker of the love of his estates; so he also ensures that the soul carries these in a beautiful order. Jesus Christ has drunk wine: He has drunk the cup to the dregs, and has become drunk from it. This can be understood in two ways. Firstly, regarding the insults which he endured until he was full of them; according to the Prophet: Secondly, regarding the wine of the wrath of God, which was poured upon him because of the sins of mankind. This was the abominable cup which Christ Jesus wished to be spared, when he prayed to God his Father: Is it possible, he says, that this cup may pass? Yet thy will be done.

He looked upon his suffering in two ways: or rather, he made a separation of two kinds of drinks in his cup. The first was of suffering and humiliation, and of this he desired to be filled; just as he testified to his disciples that he longed to eat the Passover lamb with them before his suffering. In this Passover-drink he drank the first cup, and became so drunk from it that from that hour on he thought of nothing else but to go out to meet his enemies. The other drink was the cup of the wrath of God over the sins of men in the Garden. Ah, this was so terrible that it turned the wine into blood when he had drunk it, and he later sweated it out! As if he would say: Ah, eternal Father, thou righteous God, Rewarder of a transgression which would have deserved even more punishment than thou layest upon it! I drink all thy wrath, and transform it into my blood; so that my blood may still thy wrath for the benefit of man! Let the same cup, of my sufferings, pass over to my chosen and blessed ones. For of that alone I say to them: Drink ye all of it, and become drunk, my friends. But let the cup of thy wrath end in me; or let it pass by, so that it may always destroy sin without annihilating the sinner.

When Jesus Christ enters into a soul that is rightly united—living no longer for itself, but in Jesus Christ alone—he completes that which is lacking in its inclinations: that is, he expands this inclination; and commonly he makes such a soul drunk with his first cup. The other cup, however, he reserves for the chosen souls, to whom he gives it to drink at two different times; once when he overthrows and annihilates their own will. Then such a soul feels nothing but contempt and the wrath of God within it. For the second time, when it has become like Jesus Christ. Then it drinks the cup of wrath for the sins of others, as Jesus Christ also did. This it does, however, with great reluctance, because God, as long as this rejection from God lasts, hides from it that it happens for others, and does not reveal it to the soul until he wants to have its consent, or perhaps already has its consent, to be willing to drink it. For God always demands the consent of the soul before he lets it suffer for its neighbor. Whereby the soul is then moved to sacrifice itself entirely to the justice of God and his will.

The nakedness of Noah in his drunkenness represents to us the state of nakedness in which souls—drunk with adversity, the cross, and suffering, as well as those who have drunk the cup of the wrath of God—must find themselves. He keeps them in such a nakedness of all lovely and recognized graces, of all gifts and communications—which served them, as it were, for a garment to cover their confusion—that they finally often appear in a shameful nakedness before

---

their own eyes as well as those of others. In these souls, one sees nothing but weakness and impotence: because they are stripped of the strength of God, all their misery, which was hidden under the abundance of grace, is revealed. Indeed, they seem entirely contemptible in the eyes of men.

This was also the state of Jesus Christ himself on Mount Calvary, who was not satisfied only to drink himself drunk with shame and disgrace, but also willed to be seen naked there. And this nakedness of his, which appeared to be shameful, was a sign of the great nakedness of his soul, which was so great that he himself cried out: My God, my God, why hast thou abandoned me? Thou who art my only support, how hast thou abandoned me! Because he is the example of the nakedness of those souls in the state of sacrifice in which he holds them, he must also be their only comfort.

22. Now when Ham, the father of Canaan, saw his father’s nakedness, he told his two brothers outside.
23. And Shem and Japheth took a garment and laid it upon both their shoulders, and went backward and covered their father’s nakedness; and their faces were turned away, so that they did not see their father’s nakedness.

<margin>Lyra <note>Nicholas of Lyra (c. 1270–1349) was an influential Franciscan teacher and biblical exegete.</note> concludes from this that underpants were unknown at that time.</margin>
Christ has set up his tabernacle <note>original: "Hütte"</note> within us (John 1:14) and has revealed the truth in its nakedness, in the simplicity that is in Christ. This Ham, the father of Canaan—representing the "curved soul" <note>The author uses "curved" to mean a soul bent away from God toward the earth.</note> which is inclined toward the earth and worldly things—notices this truth out in the street. And he does this not without mockery. The naked truth is a thing too poor and contemptible for a hot-headed zealot.

And how unworthily do many still act like him today, who uncover the shame of their "fathers," taking their examples of frailty and weakness in certain works (which they perhaps committed only once) and presenting them as stumbling blocks and offenses to the people of God.

There are, however, two kinds of people who see these souls in their nakedness. The first kind are those who despise them like Ham, grumble over them, make sport of them, and even take occasion to cry out against the Spirit of God when they see that souls, which were once so strong, have now become so weak. The others, however, cover them with the mantle of love by excusing their faults, viewing their origin as a nakedness that came from an over-sweet consumption of the bitter wormwood-wine <note>A metaphor for the intoxicating effects of deep sorrow or divine trial.</note> of affliction and shame, which made them drunk. They view this as an effect of God's goodness, which annihilates sin and everything subject to it within them, so that He alone may remain in them. And these are blessed by God, whereas the first receive the punishment for their boldness. Everything that can be excused must be excused, leaning toward the side of mercy rather than justice.

And how could one not say this, and even more, of the true Shem! Does not the Lord Jesus Christ cover the nakedness of the soul in which He is born? He is the reconciliation (1 John 2:1, 2), the Mercy Seat <note>original: "Gnaden-Deckel"</note>. He covers with the covering of His Spirit (Isaiah 30:1).

<insert>
The mockery of Noah by his youngest son and grandson, Canaan—who was undoubtedly with him—brought a righteous curse upon both father and son, which was to last even unto their late descendants. This serves as a warning that one should not make sport of the failings of the godly, nor reveal them to others to cause contempt; such actions bring God's righteous punishments upon oneself, as one maliciously seeks to make the godly hated and their conduct and correction fruitless. Rather, the example of Shem and Japheth teaches how one should cover the faults of the godly and those in authority, and have patience with them, looking instead at the good that God has placed in them for our benefit; this brings a blessing.

v. 25. **Cursed**) Just as a reward is promised to those who honor their parents, it follows that the transgression of this great commandment must bring a curse as a fitting retribution.

**Be Canaan**) The descendants of Ham are also cursed, but not all of them. For he had more sons than Canaan (Genesis 10:6). Therefore, in Isaiah 19:25, Egypt and Assyria, descending from Mizraim and Cush, are blessed.

**A servant of servants**) It is curious, and at the same time fateful, that the Pope in Rome calls himself by this title <note>The papal title "Servus servorum Dei" (Servant of the servants of God).</note>. In his own opinion, it is for the appearance of humility, but in truth, it is an indication of the curse.

v. 26. **Blessed be**) Or also: Blessed be the God of Shem! And why does Noah burst into blessing the Lord when he intended to bless Shem? Namely, because Shem was most highly blessed when God was blessed, recognized, and acknowledged as the sole author of all his blessing. This is the...

---

<columns>1</columns>

...practice of God's saints (Genesis 28:14, 16). Otherwise, Noah here reveals, in a prophetic spirit, the wonderful governance of God among his descendants.

<margin>
**Servant**) The Septuagint <note>original: "LXX"</note> translates this as "house servant." The Canaanites dwell in you. Outwardly, this is clear and specifically fulfilled in the Gibeonites (Joshua 9:27).
</margin>

v. 27. **God**) The Jews observe here that when Noah blesses Japheth, he uses only the name *Elohim*, as a name known to all nations and peoples. But when Noah blesses Shem, he adds the great name *Jehovah* <note>original: "Jehowäh"</note> to the name *Elohim*. By this, they understand a great privilege for Shem and his sons, the Israelites and Jews—namely, that the specific name of God should be known to them alone.

**Entice**) This is rendered differently by various commentators. Some give it as "persuade," as it is often used in the Proverbs. Most use the word "expand" or "spread out." According to the fullness of the Spirit, the words may allow all three meanings and agree with the truth and the analogy of faith—especially since "enticing" and "persuading" aim at the same thing. Toward what? Toward faith in God and His Christ.

He also "spread him out" when He gave his descendants all the islands and peninsulas, such as England, Ireland, Crete, Sicily, Spain, Italy, Greece, etc.—in a word, all of Europe. This became the most populous of all three parts of the world, the seat of the Greeks and the Roman Empire. He also added Asia Minor and Media, etc., and the vast landscapes to the north, previously inhabited by the Scythians but now by the Tartars.

The Gentiles shall be fellow-heirs and members of the household (Ephesians 3:6, 2:19). Since the time of the Apostles, the faith of our Lord Jesus Christ has flourished most in Europe and in that part of Asia which was Japheth's portion, where the first seven known churches were located. Indeed, this promise made to Japheth is so fulfilled that the descendants of Shem have been cut off, and Japheth dwells in Shem's tents. The Church of the Gentiles bears the name of Israel. Thus, the Greek and Roman monarchies also sprang from Japheth, to whom so many countries and peoples subjected themselves and became their servants.

**Canaan be his servant**) Through his descendants. For these are actually meant by all three names.

The Egyptians have been servants to all nations, and the Canaanites were made servants to Joshua and the Israelites. Indeed, just as the first Canaanites were formerly servants of the Jews, so the Jews, as the last inhabitants of Canaan, have become partakers of the curse because of their unbelief, and have become servants to the descendants of Japheth.

There is, however, also a "Canaan" and a "seed of Canaan" that concerns us much more closely (History of Susanna v. 56; Ezekiel 16:3). The work of Canaan, according to the name’s meaning, is to press down, to humble, to lower, to bend, to make crooked. The body of sin and corruption bends and presses down the soul.

With his nakedness, many wish to cover their own. This may be acceptable to the Spirit.

Just as Jesus Christ comes into the soul / to make it a partaker of his states; so he also makes it so / that the soul bears these in a beautiful order. Jesus Christ has drunk wine: He has drunk the cup to the dregs / and has become drunk from it. This can be understood in two ways. This was the abhorrent cup / which Christ Jesus would gladly have been spared / when he prayed to God his Father: Is it possible / he says / that this cup might pass? Yet your will be done.

He looked at his suffering in two ways: or rather / he made a separation of two kinds of drinks in his cup. In this Passover he drank the first cup / and became so drunk from it / that from that hour on he thought of nothing else / than to go out to meet his enemies. For of that alone I say to them: Drink all of it / and become drunk, my friends. But let the cup of your wrath end in me; or let it pass before them / so that it may everywhere destroy sin / without destroying the sinner along with it.

When Jesus Christ enters into a truly-united soul / no longer living to itself / but in Jesus Christ alone; then he completes that which is lacking in its inclinations: that is / he expands this inclination; and commonly he makes such a soul drunk with his first cup. Then such a soul feels nothing but contempt and the wrath of God within it. For the second time when it has become like Jesus Christ. Then it drinks the cup of wrath for the sins of others / as Jesus Christ also did. This it does, however, with great reluctance because God / as long as this rejection from God lasts / hides from the soul that it happens for others / and does not reveal it until he wants to have its consent / or already has its consent / to be willing to drink it. For God always demands the consent of souls / before he lets them suffer for their neighbor. By which the soul is then moved / to sacrifice itself entirely to the justice of God and his will.

And this his nakedness / which seemed to be shameful / was a sign of the great nakedness of his soul / which was so great / that he himself cried out: My God / my God! why have you forsaken me? You who are my only support / how have you forsaken me! Because he is the example of the nakedness of those souls in the state of sacrifice / in which he keeps himself; he must also be their only comfort.

### Chap. IX. The First Book of Moses.

22. And when Ham, the father of Canaan, saw the nakedness of his father, he told it to his two brothers outside.
23. Then Shem and Japheth took a garment, laid it on both their shoulders, walked backward, and covered their father’s nakedness; and their faces were turned away, so that they did not see their father’s nakedness.

Lyra <note>Nicholas of Lyra (c. 1270–1349), an influential Franciscan teacher whose literal commentaries on the Bible were highly regarded during the Reformation.</note> concludes from this that in those days, people knew nothing of undergarments.

Christ has set up his tabernacle within us <note>John 1:14</note> and discovered Truth in its nakedness—the simplicity that is in Christ. This is what Ham, the father of Canaan (representing the "crooked soul" that is inclined only toward the earth and earthly things), notices out in the street. And he does this not without mockery. Naked truth is a thing too poor and contemptible for a hot-headed zealot.

And how unworthily many still act like him today, who uncover the shame of their "fathers" <note>Referring to spiritual leaders or predecessors.</note> by taking examples of their frailty and weakness—acts they perhaps committed only once—and presenting them as stumbling blocks and offenses to the people of God.

There are, however, two kinds of people who see these souls in their nakedness. The first kind are those who despise them like Ham, grumble about them, make them the butt of their jokes, and even take the opportunity to cry out against the Spirit of God when they see that souls, who were once so strong, have now become so weak. The others, however, cover them with the mantle of love by excusing their faults. They view these faults in their origin as a nakedness that comes from an over-abundance of the bitter "wormwood-wine" of sorrow and disgrace, which has made them drunk. They see this as an act of God's goodness, which annihilates sin and everything subject to it within them, so that He alone may remain in them. These are blessed by God, while the first kind receive the punishment for their boldness. Everything that can be excused must be excused, leaning more toward the side of mercy than toward strict justice.

And how could one not say this, and more, of the true Shem? <note>In this mystical interpretation, Shem is often seen as a "type" or foreshadowing of Christ.</note> Does the Lord Jesus Christ not cover the nakedness of that soul in which He is born? He is the reconciliation <note>1 John 2:1-2</note>, the "Mercy Seat" <term>Gnaden-Deckel (Mercy Seat)</term><note>The golden lid of the Ark of the Covenant, representing the place where God’s grace covers human sin.</note>. He covers with the covering of His Spirit <note>Isaiah 30:1</note>.

24. When Noah awoke from his wine and learned what his younger son had done to him,
25. He said: "Cursed be Canaan! A servant of servants shall he be to his brothers!" <margin>Psalm 78:52</margin>
26. And he said further: "Blessed be the Lord, the God of Shem, and may Canaan be his servant!"
27. "May God allure Japheth, that he may dwell in the tents of Shem, and may Canaan be his servant!"

### 28. Noah

---
The mocking of Noah by his youngest son and grandson, Canaan (who was undoubtedly present with him), drew a righteous curse upon both father and son, which was to last even unto their late descendants. This serves as a warning that one should not make a mockery of the faults of the godly, nor reveal them to others to bring them into contempt. Such behavior brings God’s righteous punishment, as it is a malicious attempt to make the godly hated and to make their conduct and correction unfruitful. Rather, the example of Shem and Japheth teaches how one should cover the faults of the godly and those in authority, having patience with them, and looking instead at the good that God has placed within them for our benefit; this brings a blessing.
---

v. 25. **Cursed**) Just as a reward is promised to those who honor their parents, it follows that the transgression of this great commandment must bring a curse as a fitting retribution.

**Be Canaan**) The descendants of Ham are also cursed, but not all of them. For he had more sons than just Canaan <note>Genesis 10:6</note>. Thus, in Isaiah 19:25, Egypt and Assyria (descending from Mizraim and Cush) are blessed.

**A servant of servants**) It is curious, and at the same time fatal, that the Pope in Rome calls himself by this title <note>original Latin: "servus servorum Dei"</note>. In his own opinion, he does so as a show of humility, but in truth, it is an indication of the curse.

v. 26. **Blessed be**) Or also: "Blessed be the God of Shem!" And why does Noah burst into blessing the Lord when he intended to bless Shem? It is because Shem was most highly blessed at that time when God was blessed, recognized, and acknowledged as the sole author of all his blessings. This is the

<column-break/>

### Practice of the Saints of God.
1 Genesis 28:14, 16. Otherwise, Noah reveals here in a prophetic spirit the wonderful governance of God among his descendants.

**Servant**) The Septuagint <note>original: "LXX," the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament.</note> translates this as "house-servant." The Canaanites dwell within you.

Outwardly, this is clearly and specifically fulfilled in the Gibeonites <note>Joshua 9:27</note>.

v. 27. **God**) The Jews observe here that when Noah blesses Japheth, he uses only the name *Elohim* <note>A more general name for God as Creator.</note>, as a name known to all nations and peoples. But when Noah blesses Shem, he adds the great name *Jehovah* <note>The specific, covenantal name of God revealed to Israel.</note> to the name *Elohim*. By this, they understand a great privilege for Shem and his sons (the Israelites and Jews): that the proper name of God should be known to them alone.

**Allure**) This is translated in various ways by commentators. Some give it as "persuade," as it is often used in the Proverbs. Most use the word "spread out." According to the fullness of the Spirit, the words may tolerate all three meanings and agree with the truth and the "analogy of faith," especially since alluring and persuading aim at the same goal. To what end? To faith in God and His Christ.

He also "spread him out" when He gave his descendants all the islands and peninsulas, such as England, Ireland, Crete, Sicily, Spain, Italy, Greece, etc.—in a word, all of Europe. This became the most populous of all three parts of the world, the seat of the Greeks and the Roman Empire. To this, He added Asia Minor and Media, etc., and the vast territories to the north, which were previously inhabited by the Scythians but are now held by the Tartars.

The Gentiles shall be fellow-heirs and members of the household <note>Ephesians 3:6, 2:19</note>. The faith of our Lord Jesus Christ has flourished most since the time of the Apostles in Europe and in that part of Asia which was Japheth’s portion, where the first seven famous churches were located. Indeed, this promise made to Japheth has been so fulfilled that the descendants of Shem have been cut off, and Japheth now dwells in Shem's tents. The Church of the Gentiles bears the name of Israel. Thus, the Greek and Roman monarchies also sprang from Japheth, to whom so many lands and peoples submitted and became their servants.

**Canaan be his servant**) In his descendants. For these are what is actually meant by all three names.

The Egyptians have been servants to all nations, and the Canaanites were made servants to Joshua and the Israelites. Indeed, just as the first Canaanites were formerly the servants of the Jews, so these latter inhabitants of Canaan <note>Referring to the Jewish people of the author's time or the late Roman era.</note>, because of their unbelief, have shared in the curse and become servants to the descendants of Japheth.

But there is also a "Canaan" and a "seed of Canaan" that concerns us much more closely <note>Story of Susanna v. 56; Ezekiel 16:3</note>. The work of Canaan, according to the meaning of the name, is to press down, to humble, to lower, to bend, and to make crooked. The body of sin and corruption bends and presses down the soul.

### The First Book of Moses. Chap. IX.

28. And Noah lived after the flood three hundred and fifty years.

29. So all the days of Noah were nine hundred and fifty years; and he died.

---

And thus did GOD allow the preacher of righteousness, Noah, to live for another three hundred and fifty <note>original: "vierthalbhundert," an archaic German way of saying three and a half hundred.</note> years among his descendants after the flood, so that he might lay a good foundation for the knowledge of GOD and His ways within them for all future times. See Gen. 18/19.

->In him, we have in conclusion once again a beautiful<-
->foreshadowing of Christ.<- <note>In theology, this is called "typology," where Old Testament figures like Noah are seen as "types" or symbols that predict the life and work of Jesus Christ.</note>

1. His name was Noah, which means, a Comforter. Gen. 5:29. Christ comforts us in all our labor on earth, which the LORD has cursed. *I am your comforter,* he says himself, Isa. 51:12.
2. Noah was a preacher of righteousness. 2 Pet. 2:5. Christ says: *I am he who teaches righteousness.* Isa. 63.
3. Noah walked with God, was a pious man, and found grace before the Lord. Gen. 6:8. *Truly this was a righteous man!* it is said of Christ in Luke 23:47. He increased in age and grace with God.
4. Noah was the King, Priest, and Prophet of his house; and Christ of His Church.
5. *As the days of Noah were,* etc., until he entered the ark; Matt. 24:37. so shall it also be when the Son of Man shall be revealed, and shall enter into the ark <note>original: "Kasten," meaning box or chest, the common term for the Ark in early German Bibles.</note> with the believers.
6. Noah built an ark that the waves of the sea could not overflow; and Christ a congregation that the gates of hell shall not overcome.
7. Herein Noah preserved himself and his small family, consisting of 7 people besides himself; and herein Christ preserves His little flock, which consists of 7 congregations. Rev. 2, 3.
8. The former was built of wood; the Church from the wood of the Cross.
9. Noah offered a burnt offering for a sweet-smelling savor to the Lord. Gen. 8:20, 21. Christ gave Himself up for us as a gift and sacrifice, to God for a sweet-smelling savor. Eph. 5:2.
10. To Noah, God promised that He would henceforth no longer curse the earth, because He had regarded Noah’s sacrifice. Gen. 8:21. *Who is he that condemneth?* Christ is here, who was sacrificed.
11. Noah belonged to both the old and the new world. Christ was likewise to do away with the Old and begin the New.
12. Noah knew that the old world would perish because they did not believe his preaching; and Christ knew that the Jews would die in their sins.
13. Noah was the head and, as it were, the savior of the new world. So is Christ, and in Him everything is new. 2 Cor. 5:17.
14. Just as God established a covenant of grace with Noah and gave him the rainbow as a sacrament and sign; Gen. 9:12. So Christ appeared with the same. Rev. 4:3.
15. Noah planted a vineyard; Gen. 9:20. and Christ maintains a vine in the vineyard which His right hand has planted. Ps. 80.
16. When Noah was drunk, he was exposed, and mocked by Canaan, the son of Ham, Noah’s youngest son. Likewise, though Christ was not drunk with wine, but with the cup of His Father's wrath and with love for us, He was stripped naked and mocked by those dwelling in Canaan.
17. However, the former was covered by Shem and Japheth, and the latter by Nicodemus and Joseph of Arimathea.

## Chapter X.

->The Descendants of Noah.<-

<image-desc>Decorative initial "D" featuring floral and scrollwork patterns.</image-desc>Now these are the descendants of the sons of Noah: Shem, Ham, and Japheth; and sons were born to them after the flood.

->2. The<-

The first sons and grandsons of the three sons of Noah are recounted, from whom the nations later arose. Their names, following these ancestors, were still sufficiently well known in the times of the Old Testament and therefore appear in various places in the writings of the prophets. Ezek. 27, 38:2, 5, 6, 12; Isa. 11:11; Jer. 25:1, 18-25; Num. 24:24, etc. But now that the writings of the Old Testament have come among us Europeans—who can have no such news of the Asian and African peoples because most of them, like our own first ancestors, remained in a wild ignorance and their histories were not written down—these names of the peoples and their descendants remain almost all unknown, or at least uncertain. This is because they have changed through wars, displacements, and the abandoning of their former lands, and have become very mixed. Thus, the spiritual sense must be revealed to us in the prophetic writings to understand which peoples are meant by these names, as the places cited above clearly point to the end times and must be understood in that context alone.

Seventy sons or grandsons of Noah are counted in this chapter from his 3 sons: namely, 14 from Japhet, 30 from Ham, and 26 from Shem. See Gen. 46:27.

Kircherus <note>Athanasius Kircher (1602–1680), a famous Jesuit scholar who wrote on many subjects, including the Tower of Babel.</note> in his book on the Tower of Babel, took the trouble to perform a calculation and research how many people could have been fathered and born from Noah's 3 sons, counting only up to the building of the Tower of Babel. If in the first year after the flood, Noah's sons had fathered 3 sons and 3 daughters together, and continued to do so in the following years up to the 30th—since such children were already fully capable of fathering children themselves due to their age—then in 30 years, 360 people would have been fathered and born from them. These could have increased to 21,600 people by 60 years, and these in turn could easily reach 1,944,000 souls by the 90th year. And so the increase through these up to 120 years, and fully up to the building of the Tower of Babel, would extend to twenty-three thousand three hundred and twenty-eight thousand millions <note>This enormous number reflects early modern attempts to calculate population growth from a single family into a global population.</note>.

### Chap. X. The First Book of Moses.

> **2. The sons of Japheth are; Gomer, and Magog, and Madai, and Javan, and Tubal, and Meshech, and Tiras.**

<margin>Gomer)</margin> This means "a completer" <note>original: "ein Vollender"</note>; he is said to have settled with his people between the two Asian mountains, the Paropamisus and the Imaon, as well as by the rivers Oxus and Ob. See Ezekiel 38:6.

<margin>Magog)</margin> This means "dwelling under a roof." Josephus, Eustathius, Jerome, and Theodoret—according to Bochart (a)—believe Magog to be the father of the Scythians; specifically those Scythians who lived around Mount Caucasus. Indeed, Bochart derives the name Caucasus from the word "Gog."

<margin>Madai)</margin> A "measurer" or "judge" according to the name. By all writers who have dealt with the origin of nations, the Medes are attributed to him. See Isaiah 21:2.

<margin>Javan)</margin> By name, he is called a "deceiver" or "wine-drinker." If one removes the vowels in Hebrew, it can be read as Javan or Ion. Thus, it is certain enough to conclude that from him stem the Ionians or Greeks, who lived in Asia Minor and the many islands of ancient Greece, of which explicit mention is made here in verse 5. And because the Gospel came to these lands among the first—as the seven Asian churches in Revelation 2 and 3 and the other Greek churches to which Paul's epistles were mostly written testify—this shows us the fulfillment of the prophecy regarding Japheth. It shows how his descendants were lured by the preaching of the Gospel so that the spiritual house of God was revealed among them, which previously had been among the descendants of Shem, the children of Eber. See chapter 9:27.

<margin>Tubal)</margin> The Spaniards generally wish to derive their origin from him, which some attempt to prove from the name of the Lusitanian city Setubal (b).

However, because Meshech and Tubal are often placed together in Scripture, especially in Ezekiel 38 and 39, others conclude that Tubal was a people bordering Arabia and Syria. From there, it is suspected they later settled in Tartary, and specifically Siberia, whose capital is still called Tobolsk today. See Ezekiel 32:26 and Chapter 27:13.

<margin>Meshech)</margin> From him, people wish to derive those nations who lived around the Euxine Sea <note>The Euxine Sea is the ancient name for the Black Sea.</note> and are called Moschi.

Kircher (c) believes him to be the founder and father of the Muscovites; although Josephus (d) derives the origin of the Cappadocians from him, because of the name of the very ancient city of Mazaca <note>original: "Mosecha"</note> in that land, which was later called Caesarea. He thinks it possible that Mazaca was the main seat of Meshech, but that from there his descendants turned toward Sarmatia or Scythia, or, as it is called today, Muscovy. Thus, the Cappadocians had their camp on one side of the Euxine Sea, and on the other side, opposite Sarmatia or Scythia, or now Muscovy.

<margin>Tiras)</margin> "Destroyer." From him came the Thracians, as is generally held, who lived where the Turks are now found. They expressed their name truly through their deeds, in that they destroyed and devastated everything. It is also said of them that they ate human flesh and used human skulls as drinking vessels (e).

(c) chap. 9. *Noah’s Ark* <note>original Latin: "Arc. Noae."</note> (d) book 1. *Jewish Antiquities* <note>original German: "Jüd. Gesch."</note> chap. 7.
(e) Bochart. book 3. chap. 2. *Sacred Geography*.

> **3. And the sons of Gomer are; Ashkenaz, and Riphath, and Togarmah.**
> **4. And the sons of Javan are; Elishah, and Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.**

> **5. From these were the islands of the Gentiles divided in their lands; every one after his tongue, after their families, in their nations. 6. And**

<margin>v. 3. The sons of Gomer)</margin> The Jewish historian Josephus (a) claims that from Gomer the Gomerites arose, whom the Greeks later called Galatians. However, Matthew Beroaldus (b) proves that according to Ezekiel 38:6, these must have been a people in Asia situated toward the north <note>original: "Mitternacht," literally midnight, used to denote the North.</note> from the land of the Jews.

Others derive the Cimmerians from them, from whom later the Cimbri and Northern peoples of Europe arose, who occupied a large part of Germany, France, and Britain. Therefore, the English still call themselves "Cymru" <note>original: "Kumern"</note> to this day, and their language "Cymraeg" (c).

<margin>Ashkenaz)</margin> Kircher says (d) that the Germans descend from him, which is attested by almost all the writings of the Rabbis, among whom Germany itself is called Ashkenaz. Cluverius (e) says he is the father of all Celts, and thereby includes everything that reaches from Dalmatia or Illyria, Gaul, Spain, and the British Isles to the North Sea.

<margin>Riphath)</margin> Means "a physician," and is also written as Diphath by Ezra, as Bochart (f) indicates. He is said to have first gone to the province of Paphlagonia in Asia Minor; the people were first called Riphathaeans after him, but later Paphlagonians. After Riphath's descendants had greatly multiplied there, they supposedly turned toward Scythia and Sarmatia. Thus, the Riphäen Mountains <note>A legendary mountain range in ancient geography, sometimes associated with the Urals.</note> were also named after them.

<margin>Togarmah)</margin> Means "bony" or "strong." The Jewish historian Josephus, as Kircher and Bochart attest, attributes Phrygia to him. According to Cluverius's opinion, he turned northward into the great wild forests of what is now called Great Russia or Muscovy, as well as southern Lithuania; the Turks are also said to have come from him. Ezekiel 27:14, 38:6.

<margin>v. 4. Elishah)</margin> "Lamb of God," received the name **Hellas** and **Elles** from the Greeks. To him people attribute the origin of the Greeks and the islanders of the Mediterranean, the Aeolians in Asia Minor, the Morean province of Elis, the land of Silesia and Italy, the Elysian Fields in the Blessed Isles, and even the name of the Hellespont. Ezekiel 27:7.

<margin>Tarshish)</margin> A "searcher of marble," or also "impoverished." Hornius and Bochart attribute the origin of the Kingdom of Spain to him, where the Tyrians and Phoenicians heavily directed their voyages, and where a city near the Pillars of Hercules bears the name Tartessus. The fact that at least the names Spain and Iberia, as it was formerly called, are held to be of Hebrew origin, will perhaps provide an opportunity for further remarks in Romans 15:28.

<margin>Kittim)</margin> Chittim, also Kethim, meaning "trampler" according to his name. Five types of nations are said to have sprung from him or his descendants: 1) The Macedonians and Epirotes; 2) the inhabitants of the island of Cyprus; 3) the Italians, especially the Romans; 4) the province of Cetis in Cilicia; and finally Chios, or even the Indian peoples. Isaiah 23:1. 1 Maccabees 1:1.

<margin>Dodanim)</margin> Called Rhodanim by some. Dr. Matthias (g), Micraelius, and Hornius wish to attribute the building of the city of Dodona in Epirus to him. From the other name, Rhodanim, people conclude that they landed in France by the mouth of the Rhone, which river they named Rhodanus after their own name. Also, the cities of Rouen, Rennes, and Rodez are said to take their names from this.

<margin>v. 5. Islands of the Gentiles)</margin> Among which are counted especially the far-distant ones, such as those of Europe, e.g., Great Britain, Sicily, and the like. For this very reason, the pagans understood Japheth to be Neptune, whom they made the god of the sea. For that name also comes from the very same root word.

### The First Book of Moses. Chap. X.

> **6. And the sons of Ham are: Cush, and Mizraim, and Put, and Canaan.**
> **7. And the sons of Cush are: Seba, and Havilah, and Sabtah, and Raamah, and Sabtecha. And the sons of Raamah are Sheba and Dedan.**

---

<margin>Ezekiel 27:15, 22.</margin>
<margin>Psalm 78:51.</margin>
**v. 6. Ham)** Or Cham; whom the Jews consider an inventor of sorcery, but others hold to be a good chemist <note>original: "Chemicum"</note>. It is said that chemistry <note>original: "Chemie oder Chimic"</note> takes its name from him, as the word signifies Egypt, where Ham and his descendants lived and introduced the chemical arts. <note>The author connects the word "Chemistry" to "Khem," the ancient name for Egypt, which means "the black land."</note>

In the division of the world, however, he was allotted not only Egypt, but all of Africa, and also a large portion of Syria and Arabia.

**Cush)** To him, most writers attribute Ethiopia or the "land of the Moors," while some attribute Arabia. Among the former are nearly all the Hebrews, Greeks, and the common Latin translation <note>The Vulgate</note>, as well as Philo, Josephus, Eusebius, Jerome, Eustathius, the entire choir of the Church Fathers, Athanasius Kircher, etc. Among the latter is only the ancient Chaldean translation of Jonathan. If authority carries weight here, the first interpretation must undoubtedly hold the field.

However, if reason and logic are allowed, the latter view is far preferable and is clearly demonstrated by many passages of Scripture. See Habakkuk 3:7, Job 28:19, Ezekiel 29:10, 30:9, 2 Kings 19:9, 2 Chronicles 21:16, Isaiah 20:4-5. For this name—the land of Cush and the Cushites—is well known from many places in Scripture; but the error of mostly interpreting it as the land of the Moors is primarily attributed to the unfortunate translation of the Seventy Interpreters <note>The Septuagint (LXX), the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</note> and the fabulous tales of the Jewish historian Josephus (a).

Thus, by Cush, one should rather understand Arabia, and by the Cushites, those Arabs who are closest to Egypt. This can be recognized in Zerah, the Arabian king (who is commonly called a king of the Ethiopians) mentioned in 2 Chronicles 14, as well as in Moses' wife, the Midianite woman, in Exodus 2:22.

**Mizraim)** Is often placed near Cush in Scripture because they were neighbors. He is the father of the Egyptians, who are called Mizraim by the Hebrews, as is the land itself. Even today, the capital city Cairo is called *Meser* by the Arabs.

<margin>Psalm 105:23, 106:22.</margin>
Among the descendants of Ham, these were the best-known peoples; hence Egypt is also called the Land of Ham.

This same Mizraim is said to be the Zoroaster or the Osiris known in histories, who continued with great diligence the black arts learned from his father. He is said to have been the first to invent magical characters <note>hieroglyphs or occult symbols</note> and the making of amulets, and to have drawn the stars down from heaven through his incantations and magic songs. For this reason, divine honors were bestowed upon him by the Egyptians (b).

Yet, this Mizraim is said to have had Hermes Trismegistus <note>original: "Mercurium Trismegistum"</note> as his privy counselor and Secretary of State, who, through his wisdom, is said to have restored to a better condition everything that Ham and Mizraim had corrupted and made evil.

**Put)** Regarding him, all writers agree in ascribing to him the entire stretch of Africa from Egypt to the Atlantic Ocean, which today includes the kingdoms of Fez and Morocco.

**v. 7. Seba)** Bochart places him in northern Arabia and derives from him the Sabaeans, who are written in Hebrew with a *Samekh* (ס), and who were said to be tall, large people. Isaiah 44:14.

He also notes (c) that because Moses lists four tribal fathers of this name—two from Ham and two from Shem—three of whom are written with a *Shin* (ש), they must represent four distinct peoples.

**Havilah)** Settled nearest to Babylonia, in Bochart's opinion. This is based on the fact that the Desert of Shur near Egypt and Havilah are placed opposite each other as the outermost borders of Arabia. Genesis 25:18, 1 Samuel 15:7.

**Sabtah)** From him, the Sabathaens—a people in Happy Arabia <note>original: "glückseligen Arabien," referring to Arabia Felix</note>—seem to originate according to Bochart and Bezaldus.

**Raamah)** According to Bochart's opinion, he and his two sons did not settle far from one another, where the city of Rhegma bears his name, and not far from it Dedan (or today, Dadan) in the land of Daden of the same name.

**Sheba)** Here is the other one spelled with a *Shin* (ש), a father of the Sabaeans, who are very famous for their abundance of gold, precious stones, and myrrh. They lived by the Persian Gulf, from whence the Queen of rich Arabia came to Solomon. Psalm 72:10, Isaiah 60:6, Jeremiah 6:20.

<column-break/>

**8. And Cush begat Nimrod: he began to be a mighty one in the earth.**
<margin>Micah 7:2.</margin>
**9. He was a mighty hunter before the LORD: wherefore it is said, Even as Nimrod the mighty hunter before the LORD.**
**10. And...**

---

Among the pious lineage, the Patriarchs themselves were regents over their descendants or children; they were not intent on expanding their borders, but only on enjoying what they possessed in peace.

Nimrod, however, was the first after the Deluge who herded men together as a hunter herds game. Thus, in his time and through his manner, the violent subjection of men under authority began again—the very sin with which the first world <note>the pre-flood world</note> had burdened itself, Chapter 6:4, 13. As the originators of the first violent empires, the Babylonian and Assyrian, they herded men like animals and did not shy away from setting such works in motion under the name of the LORD, forcing them into the false religion they established and compelling them to maintain one language and one mind. Chapter 11:1.

It is certainly remarkable that the most violent and ancient empires and domains sprang from the lineage of Ham, which lay under a curse, just as previously they had sprung from the lineage of Cain.

**v. 8. Cush begat)** From this, the poets fashioned their god Bacchus, from *Bar Cush* <note>Aramaic: "Son of Cush"</note>, and to make it sound better, they called this Nimrod "Bacchus."

And it appears that because so much is specifically reported of him, he surpassed all others in his father's house in pride, insolence, and hardness. He was not satisfied with his rank and degree but claimed for himself a violent tyranny.

Thus, we have in him a clear prototype of the Antichrist:

1. He is named Nimrod, which means "Rebel" or "obstinate," because he rebelled against Noah (who lived 350 years after the flood) and wanted to be a king of his own over his brothers. Likewise, the Antichrist is called "the adversary."

2. He began to be a mighty hunter before the LORD; that is, a great statesman <note>original: "Statist"</note> who knew how to ensnare animals and men with speech and gestures, just as Absalom did. In this way, the final "child of perdition" is described in his deeds and beginnings, his cunning and power, of which Antiochus was also a prototype.

3. The beginning of his kingdom was Babel. And what are Revelation 13 and 17?

4. Just as all great lords, when they are godless statesmen, use justice and religion as a pretext for their evil deeds (2 Samuel 15:3-4, 1 Samuel 15:21), so did Nimrod. He built a city under the name of unity and a single religion, though he was actually seeking his own name, honor, and the like.

5. Nimrod was honored by the Babylonians under the name Jupiter Belus or Baal. Likewise, the Antichrist exalts himself above everything that is called GOD or worship.

10. And the beginning of his kingdom was Babel, and Erech, and Akkad, and Calneh, in the land of Shinar. <margin>Genesis 11:2, 9; Zechariah 5:11.</margin>
11. From that land he went forth into **Assyria**, and built Nineveh, and the streets of the city <note>original: "die Strassen der Stadt," often rendered as Rehoboth-Ir</note>, and Calah.
12. Also Resen <note>original: "Riesen," which in German literally means "Giants," but refers here to the city of Resen</note> between Nineveh and Calah. This is the great city.

---

v. 10.) Regarding the nature of Babylon, Gabriel Caltemark <note>A 16th-century author known for works on geography and theology</note> provides the following report in his book *On the Waters of Paradise* <note>original: "Paradis-Wasser"</note>, chapter 6: "The foundation of this city is laid out in a square form, just as it is divided into four parts, each called by a special name: Babel, Erech, Akkad, and Calneh; it was also settled with four types of inhabitants. The first and most noble were the Patricians <note>original: "Partitii"</note>, from whom the leaders and councilors were chosen. The second were the Knights <note>original: "Equites"</note>, who were used for the knighthood and matters of war. The third were the Commoners <note>original: "Plebeji"</note>, merchants and craftsmen. The fourth were the Farmers or Peasants <note>original: "Agricolæ oder Rustici"</note>, tillers of the field and husbandmen. This city had a circumference of 385 stadia, which is 12 German miles. The ring wall was 32 feet thick; between the towers it was 50, and the towers themselves were 60 cubits high. On the wall, one could easily turn a wagon around. There were 100 city gates, and the houses stood 125 paces or one stadium away from the city wall all around; which space was used for gardens and agriculture."

v. 11. In Assyria) And since this was the dwelling place of the descendants of Shem according to verse 22, he must have made an invasion into it, and thus fallen upon the **Lord's** land itself, no doubt on account of the sins of this people also, just as **God** is accustomed to stir up such 'hunters of men' for that reason.
Built Nineveh) A world of injustice; and Rehoboth) The broad streets of that same city.
We must be very careful to guard against the growth of sins. Evil is of a spreading nature. It begins in the imagination and vain thoughts of the earthly man, which the desire of pleasure follows softly. And because these have deviated from the first correctness and uprightness—where they should have been subject to reason and rational appetite, and these to the law of **God**—they fall ever more into the sensual, and become more and more inclined toward evil: like someone who, in falling from a height, very easily falls deeper and deeper until he comes into the depth of sin, and sinks submerged in sin, dragging down the rational desire, and even reason itself as the governing part of the mind, with him: just like one who is sinking will seize anyone, even his best friend, and drag them down with him. And when reason itself is brought over to Nimrod, the rebellious party, then the faction becomes stronger, so that the heart heaps injustice upon itself and finally takes pleasure in it. Jeremiah 11:15. Then Nimrod, the rebellious heart, has come to Ashur <note>Assyria</note>, his salvation <note>This is a play on words or a spiritual allegory comparing Assyria/Ashur to a false sense of security or "salvation" for the rebellious heart</note>.

13. And Mizraim begat the Ludim <note>original: "Luder"</note>, and the Anamim <note>original: "Anamer"</note>, and the Lehabim <note>original: "Lehaber"</note>, and the Naphtuhim <note>original: "Naphthucher"</note>,

---

v. 13. Ludim) According to Bochartus <note>Samuel Bochart, a 17th-century scholar of biblical geography</note> (a) in the Hebrew language, these are the same as the Ethiopians or "Moors" properly so-called, and Lud is the name of such a land of Ethiopians or Moors; he proves this from those places in Scripture where the Ludim are described as good archers, e.g., Isaiah 66:19, because historically the Moors could not have been better identified by any other mark. Thus, it could also best be settled from Egypt, as from Mizraim. Moreover, the Hebrews wrote in the *Baal Aruch* <note>A famous dictionary of the Talmud and Midrash</note> that the Ludim were cannibals. Hornius <note>Georg Horn, a Dutch historian</note> gives him his support.
Anamim) Bochartus considers these to be those called Nomads, who raised many sheep, lived from them, and clothed themselves in them. In his opinion, *Anam* meant a sheep or cattle among the ancient Egyptians.
Lehabim) These are generally held to be the Libyans, especially those who were closest to Egypt and lived on sandy soil that is completely scorched by great heat. For this reason, they have that name: since *lehaba* in Hebrew signifies both a flame and heat.
Naphtuhim) Bochartus (b) places these in Marmarica, on the Mediterranean Sea. Just as Hornius also believes that the name Neptune originated from this word, because the Egyptians called the seashores *Nephthun*.
v. 14. Pathrusim) Bochartus believes their footsteps are found in the land of Pathros, which he considers to be Thebaid <note>Upper Egypt</note>.
Casluhim) He considers these to be the Colchians (c), whose origin is said to be from Egypt, the name having arisen from the Hebrew and Egyptian *Casluchim*, with the omission of the letter *s* for the sake of difficult pronunciation. Such a long journey could have been drawn, among other reasons, by the wealth of the land, as with others.
Philistines) They occupied the seacoast from Canaan toward Egypt, which land was called Palestine after them. Their borders are described in Joshua 13:3, and they are mentioned very often elsewhere in Scripture.
Caphtorim) Because the origin of the Philistines is traced here from the Casluhim, and elsewhere (d) from the Caphtorim, they are considered with good reason to be neighboring peoples. Most incline toward them being Cappadocians; and this is possible if one specifically understands those who were closest to Colchis.
v. 15. The descendants of Canaan, the youngest son of Ham, who also received the curse with him, are recounted particularly, and how ten to eleven great nations arose from him, receiving their names from his sons. These also had to experience the curse in a special way through their extermination by the children of Israel, to whom **God** gave their land as an inheritance. Chapter 15:20, 21. Exodus 23:23. Then also the spiritual Sidonians, who are mentioned with those of Tyre, along with all the Canaanites who engaged in spiritual huckstering <note>original: "Krämerey," referring to corrupt religious trade</note>, will have to feel the curse upon themselves and their followers at their destruction (see Isaiah 23:1, 2, 12; Ezekiel 26, 27, 28; Jeremiah 47:4; Zechariah 14:21), and especially the spiritual king and prince of Tyre and Sidon in the last times; regarding this, see Ezekiel 28.
Sidon) He built Sidon, the capital in Phoenicia, from which Tyre also later received its founders and inhabitants. It is still called Said today, which means "the catch of fish" <note>Sidon/Saida is related to the root for fishing</note>; just as Bethsaida in Galilee is as much as "the house of the catch of fish."
Heth) He built Hebron, the burial place of Abraham.
The name signifies the fearful ones, or despondency, which resists faith and trust, taking away the courage of the people of Shem to enter into the Holy Land. Numbers 13:30.

### # The First Book of Moses, Chap. X.

<insert>
Shem’s lineage is reported last because it was Moses' intention to proceed in a straight order toward the history of Abraham. From Shem, great nations also arose. But from Arphaxad—from whom the line descends in which the blessing of God given to Shem (Chapter 9:26) later revealed itself in Abraham—one does not read that entire nations arose from him. Rather, the families of the believers were propagated individually; they are called here the children of Heber <note>original: "Heber," referring to the patriarch Eber</note>, and thus Hebrews (Exodus 1:15, 16); and from Jacob onward, the children of Israel; and from the time that the tribe of Judah remained loyal to the House of David, they are called Jews (Esther 2:5, 8:9, etc.). 

According to the ingenious significance of the words, this represents how all believers must first become Hebrews—those who "cross over" from the world to God through true repentance—who then, as the "Israel of God," wrestle and prevail with God in faith (See Genesis 32:28, Galatians 6:16). And so they finally become spiritual Jews, who confess God and the truth with mouth and heart and in all their works with love (See Romans 2:29, Revelation 3:9, John 13:35).

**v. 21. A father of all the children of Eber)** Was Shem not also the father of Elam and Asshur, Lud and Aram, and thus the father of all the children of Elam and Asshur? If we look no further than the literal letter, this is as true of them as of the others. But if we search for who the true children of Eber and the right Hebrews are, we will find that none other than the true Shem was their father. For the children of Eber are those who "pass over" <note>Eber/Heber in Hebrew implies "to cross over" or "pass through"</note> from sin to righteousness, from the flesh into the spirit, and from death into life. Such a one was Abraham (Hebrews 14:13). They are of the circumcision (Colossians 2:11).

Some also hold that the Hebrews were not named after this Eber, the son of Shem, but rather because their fathers lived in Mesopotamia across the Euphrates and later came into the land of Canaan. "Across" <note>original: "Darnach," likely a typo for "Darneb" or a reference to the preposition "beyond"</note> means as much as "on the other side" (As in Joshua 24:2). Yet the former view is more credible.

**v. 22. Elam)** Remained in Asia along with all his brothers. His descendants were initially called Elamites, from whom the Persians later sprang, as most scholars believe (See Daniel 8:2, Acts 2:9).

**Arphaxad)** Bochartus <note>Samuel Bochart (1599–1667), a French Protestant biblical scholar</note> and Hornius <note>Georg Horn (1620–1670), a German historian</note> attribute to him the Assyrian region of Arrapachitis. The name signifies "one who heals the devastation or disturbance," thus hinting at the Messiah.

**Lud)** Almost all agree that the peoples of Asia Minor, known as the Lydians, descend from him.
</insert>

---

**v. 16. Jebusite)** Held Jebus, which was later called Jerusalem, and the fortress of Zion until the times of David. It signifies a people who trample precious truths underfoot like swine trample pearls (Matthew 7:6); who trample the Son of God and the life of God within them under their feet (Hebrews 10:29).

**Amorite)** A bitter people, great babblers, representing the bitterness of envy. <margin>James 3:14.</margin> These initially held the mountains in the land of Judah, but later mostly crossed the Jordan, attacked the Moabites and Ammonites with war, and took away Bashan and Heshbon, and what was between the rivers Jabbok and Arnon. In memory of this victory, a Canaanite poet composed a poem <note>original: "Carmen"</note> which Moses deemed worthy to incorporate into his books. Otherwise, they were people such as Amos describes (a), who equaled cedars in height and oaks in strength.

**Girgashite)** Those who still lived across the Jordan in Christ's time and are called Gergesenes. <margin>Matthew 8:28.</margin> An image of the earthly-minded, who have their primary share in the lake of fire. <margin>Revelation 21.</margin>

**v. 17. Hivite)** Life according to the flesh. According to the Jerusalem Talmud, their dwelling was around Tripoli; but according to Bochart, it was on Mount Hermon. <margin>Joshua 13:3, Judges 3:3.</margin>

**Arkite)** Signifies "persecution" or "persecutor" according to the meaning of the word. <margin>Galatians 4:29.</margin> They held the city of Arka or Arce on Mount Lebanon, which Josephus (b) mentions.

**Sinite)** Legalistic righteousness; also the enmity stirred up by the law in those who are under the law. Some think they lived on Mount Sinai, which Bochart believes was unlikely due to the immense wilderness.

**v. 18. Arvadite)** The reigning sin; the abundance of the curse or the prevailing sins that rule in the mortal body. According to Bochart, they occupied the island of Aradus in the region of Phoenicia, along with a piece of the neighboring land, and were particularly famous as good mariners. <margin>Ezekiel 27:8.</margin>

**Zemarite)** Sheep's clothing; those who walk about in sheep's clothing of false simplicity and self-holiness. Bochart also looks for them on the Phoenician shore.

**Hamathite)** The spirit of wrath, the children of wrath. Their capital city, Hamath, is considered to be Antioch.

**v. 19.)** The sons of the 11 sons of Canaan occupied almost the entire Land of Promise and a part of Syria as far as Damascus; this land was then named after the patriarch Canaan.

**v. 20.)** Just as these peoples inhabited all of Africa and also a large part of Asia—from whom it is quite probably suspected the Americans <note>referring to the Indigenous peoples of the Americas</note> also sprang, as their wild nature may be a sign of such a curse—so too the black and dark sin-nature of the Moors and Saracens or Cushites is noted by the prophets. <margin>Jeremiah 13:23, Amos 9:7.</margin> This may teach us where the spiritual Moors are to be found, as well as the spiritual Egyptians, Babylonians, and Philistines, who at all times have sought to bring people under their physical and spiritual dominion and have always caused all kinds of vexation to the spiritual Israel.
