# The First Book of Moses. Chapter XV.

5. And he led him outside / and said: Look <gloss>(a)</gloss> now toward heaven / and count the stars / if you are able to count them. And he said to him: So shall your offspring be.
<margin>ch. 22:17. (a) Acts 7:11.</margin>

---

**Outside)** Out of his hut / out of the flesh / out of the boundaries of the mere natural order.

**Look — the stars)** Abram was by birth a Chaldean / a people very devoted to astronomy and astrology. Indeed, Abram was also considered by the ancients to have been exceedingly well-versed in this science / and is said to have taught it to the Egyptians.

**If you are able to count them)** Some have nevertheless presumed to count them / and to set a certain number / which amounts to over sixteen or seventeen hundred. However, Galilaeus <note>Galileo Galilei (1564–1642), the famous astronomer whose telescope revolutionized our view of the heavens.</note>, who also undertook this task / and counted over 500 in one degree or another / finally / after becoming weary of it / and nearly blinding himself / had to desist and confess / that there are over ten thousand in our visible hemisphere. Ricciolus <note>Giovanni Battista Riccioli (1598–1671), an Italian Jesuit astronomer.</note> wants to set their number at 2,000,000. But the question will likely remain unresolved; otherwise, GOD would probably not have asked it. For it is clearly given to understand / that it was not possible for Abram to count them. Without doubt, there are many more than we can see. Just as other astronomers tell us of an infinite number of stars. The <term>telescope|original: Guck-Rohr</term> of Galileo discovered a far greater number / than are otherwise visible to us.

**So)** In view of the quantity and quality. Elevated above the earth / through contemplation and meditation on divine things: widely spread / through the extension of love toward all: shining / through the wisdom / that makes the face shine: peaceful / through stillness: moved by the heavenly spirits / angels or powers / through readiness, flexibility, and obedience to the will of God: raining / through instruction and teaching: thundering / through punishment: flowing in / through true generosity: brighter / through a good way of life: appearing small and being great: joined to Christ / and fastened to this firmament: of varying size. There are also wandering stars <note>Planets</note> and fallen stars / as we read. And such are the arrogant / fallen, and degenerate children of Abraham.

The stars shine brightest in the coldest night.

<column-break/>

6. And he believed the LORD / and that he credited to him for righteousness.

7. And

---

The most necessary part of this matter is so fully indicated in these few words / that one must indeed accept them with reverence.

It is to be wished / out of love for the salvation of all men / that they all believed thus and became righteous as Abraham. But Scripture and experience show the opposite.

It is true / all people are by nature and before conversion evil and sinners: and thus Abraham, according to nature, was not to be exempted from the common corruption. But it is also certain and true / that Abraham / when he became righteous / was converted and penitent / and no longer stuck in willful sins.

Had he not immediately gone out from his fatherland and from his kindred at the first call and hint from GOD? Had he not thereby left idolatry and all pagan sins / and converted to the only living GOD with his whole heart? Did he not stand at that time in a sincere exercise of faith / when he held so solely to GOD in the midst of pagan people / and trusted and built upon Him alone? And how GOD tested him through the new promise / which had just then happened to him.

Thus one may also look at all other believers in Scripture / whether a single other person / except through true conversion / has become righteous.

One should then draw the true and correct conclusion for oneself: whether one will ever become righteous otherwise / than when one converts to GOD.

O, for GOD’S sake / yes, for the sake of one's own salvation / let that damnable error go / as if one could indeed be justified / even if one remains in one's old sins with all one's will: whereby one certainly and willfully excludes oneself from Abraham’s blessing!

Let everyone gladly allow the Holy Spirit to write into his heart / what kind of people can become righteous! namely / as mentioned / only the penitent and believing / but not stubborn sinners. These do not even desire to become righteous / at least not in the true order of GOD.

Abraham believed and obeyed first / and thereupon the working and active faith / the obedience of faith / was credited to him for righteousness.

Therefore, one made righteous can as little remain in sin as Abraham could.

And although a sinner is justified immediately at the beginning of his first repentance / just as he is also saved in hope / yet such justification must always proceed in the soul / and always reconcile and intercede for the person anew against all accusations and claims of wrath.

That is why it is written here of the long-converted Abraham only now / that he was made righteous / or his faith was credited to him for righteousness. And this also confirms the majesty of grace in JESUS Christ as inexpressibly precious. For if even one who has reached a great degree of holiness until his end must still always live by grace and allow himself to be justified by GOD; how many thousand times more a beginning and newly-converted Christian.

**Believed the Lord)** Not himself / or other creatures; not his own piety or cleverness: but Him who is over all.

With this highest Good your faith alone shall have to do; in Him alone shall you trust. And how is that possible / where you do not rightly know Him / to whom you are to surrender yourself?

Ah, consider / upon what an immovable foundation you can and must build / if your faith is to be of the right kind!

O, if one could be advised / he would learn to rightly hunger and thirst for righteousness! For this hunger is faith.

What a great pleasure is given to the eternal Creator / when His departed creature gives Him the honor / and entrusts itself to Him again with all its power! And this is also nothing else but faith.

GOD regards faith the most. Thus the faith of such a person / who continues in his self-denial / and subjects himself to the hands of GOD / is more regarded by GOD / than all works of righteousness / which are not supported by such a strong faith: because it is a faith awakened by a fervent love. Then He has enough in the faith and the self-denial: And he needs do nothing else anymore / than live this faith and this self-denial.

But where that happens / there the person yields himself again into GOD’S government / protection / love and grace / into all reconciliation and redemption / as the Savior wishes to accomplish in him. This believing now and this seizing of the grace of GOD in Christ

**He credited for righteousness)** One can easily think / that a great change took place in Abraham / when his faith was credited to him for righteousness. Otherwise, Scripture could not have described such a thing as such a certain, occurred matter. Thus truly much must also occur in you / if you are to experience the great work of justification / even if you cannot express it all.

But that this example of Abraham concerns everyone / who only wishes to believe; is evident from the clear speech of Paul in Romans 4:23.

Just as Luther considers the Epistle to the Romans / from the 4th to the 12th chapter / generally to be a commentary on this verse <gloss>(a)</gloss>.

### Ch. XV. The First Book of Moses. 99

7. And he said to him: I am the LORD / who led you out of Ur of the Chaldeans / to give you this land / to possess it as an inheritance.
8. But he said: Lord LORD / by what shall I know / that I will possess it as an inheritance?
9. And he said to him: Bring me a three-year-old heifer / and a three-year-old goat / and a three-year-old ram / and a turtledove and a young pigeon.
10. And he brought him all these / and divided them in the middle from one another / and laid each part opposite the other: but the birds he did not divide.
11. And the birds of prey came down upon the carcasses / but Abram drove them away.

---

<margin>v. 7. 8.</margin> So that God might test his faith even more / and strengthen it in self-denial; He again gives him new assurances of His promises.
Namely, because this soul is not yet established in faith and self-denial by a permanent state / he wavers / and through unfaithfulness demands signs: although he should have considered / that signs are as much opposed to perfect faith as they are to self-denial; and that / when one fixes the creature upon something created <note>Meaning when a human being relies on physical evidence rather than spiritual promise.</note>, one prevents that same person from relying on God / as upon the grace of the Creator.
Abraham, however, desires to be more closely instructed and assured of the will of God / as to the manner in which his people should come into the hereditary possession of this land.
God wished to give him the assurance and a closer explanation of the fulfillment of the promise through a renewal of the covenant at a special sacrifice; (See Judges 13:12 & etc.) in order to remind the believers / that they should always make and renew the covenant with God at the sacrifice / that they might conduct themselves only as covenant-companions in living faith: then God would fulfill His promise in His own time / even if the same seemed to be delayed for a long time before flesh and blood. For thus it is properly said in Ps. 50:4 <note>original: "Sammlet mir meine Heiligen (Gunst-Genossen) / die den Bund mit mir machen bey dem Opfer." (Gather my saints to me, who make a covenant with me by sacrifice.)</note>.
These sacrificial animals were meant to represent the virtues of the believers / which God demanded from them / as spiritual sacrifices / who had to offer themselves to God with spirit, soul, and body / in faith. These include patience / contentment / bravery; which is nonetheless associated with patience: and friendliness and simplicity; Matthew 10:16. and then purity; since they were pure animals / which consume only pure food: which the believers should diligently practice in their entire conduct. Ch. 8:20. James 4:8. Titus 2:15. That they were killed / testifies to the constant mortification of our lusts and desires: the driving away of the birds of prey signifies the protection of the holy angels and the expulsion of evil spirits from the believers. Ps. 34:8.
And thus God gives Abraham a sign / but in such a way / that He shows therein / that the mistrust displeased Him. For nothing is so contrary to faith and self-denial as signs. The divine moment must decide everything / and the soul must wait for this / without seeing anything / without laboring to see anything of the future / even if it should seem / as if the time for the fulfillment of the promises has already passed. This is also that by which one can avoid deceptions: namely, that one only waits for this moment of God / which is always truthful in its fulfillment.

<column-break/>

12. And it happened as the sun was about to go down / a deep sleep fell upon Abram / and behold / terror and great darkness overcame him.
13. Then He said to Abram: You shall know for certain / that your offspring will be a stranger / in a land that is not theirs; and they must serve them / and they will oppress them / four hundred years. <margin>Exodus 12:40.</margin>
14. But I will also judge the nation / whom they must serve: and after this they shall go out with great possessions.
15. And you shall go to your fathers in peace / you shall be buried at a good old age.
16. But

---

<margin>v. 12.</margin> Abram's sleep signifies how the Church and its watchmen often fall into the sleep of security / and do not perform their office: then God hangs great terrors and temptations in various tribulations and persecutions over the Church to awaken it / so that they might remember God's promises and the time of fulfillment / and call upon God all the more earnestly for them. See Acts 14:22. Isaiah 62:6, 7.
<margin>v. 13.</margin> Just as self-denial and faith move God to give souls great rewards; so that it seems / as if He had nothing else with which to reward these great heroic virtues / than to communicate Himself: so the very slightest mistrust and the desire for outward signs / which are so contrary to these virtues / draw the contempt of God upon themselves / and terrify / so that He threatens the one / whom He previously wished to reward with Himself / and also actually punishes him. Oh, how mysterious this is / and how necessary it was for our instruction! For it is certain / that oftentimes the faults / which are committed against faith or self-denial / when namely one is immediately convinced of the same again / strengthen faith more / through the use which God allows a soul to make of them / than a constant faithfulness / which has never been subject to any weakness.
God gave Abraham a rebuke, as it were / which was directed at his descendants: just as the promises / which He had given him / were likewise established for those same descendants. The fear and the darkness indicate the evil consequences of seeking signs / and the certainties that one seeks in unfaithfulness: which / as they set the soul in fear and doubt / are a hindrance to the grace and the light of God.
<margin>v. 14.</margin> After this they shall go out) This also happened at night / and as it were at the very hour / just as this vision did.
<margin>v. 15.</margin> You shall go to your fathers) From this, many of the Jewish teachers wished to conclude / that the holy fathers of the Old Testament / before the coming of the Messiah, went down into the pit of their place / and did not immediately enter a blessed state / until the appearance of the Messiah / whom they still await: because Abraham's fathers indeed served idols / and thus did not become blessed. (a)
Therefore, a certain place is also believed in by the Roman Catholics / where the departed souls of the fathers of the Old Testament would have gone <note>This refers to the 'Limbus Patrum' or Abraham's Bosom, a concept of a temporary state for the righteous before Christ's resurrection.</note>.

<note>(a) Marsilio Ficino, *On the Christian Religion*, chapter 33.</note>

### Ch. XV. The First Book of Moses. 100

<margin>ch. 18/21.</margin>
> 16. But in the fourth generation they shall come hither again. For the iniquity of the Amorites is not yet full up to this time. 

> 17. And it came to pass, when the sun went down / and it had become dark night / behold, there was a smoking oven / and a flaming torch / that passed between those pieces.

---

v. 16. God does not fail to fulfill His promises / even after He has made things difficult enough beforehand: and after the soul has entered again into the darkness of faith / just as it is written / that after the sun went down / there was a thick smoke / so God renews His covenant with the soul / and continues to show His singular care over it.

<margin>Exodus 6:16-20.</margin>
The four hundred years must be counted from the birth of Isaac / and the four generations from Levi / who moved into Egypt / who fathered Kohath / and he fathered Amram / and he fathered Aaron and Moses / who led Israel out of Egypt / the house of bondage. For otherwise, 400 years do not emerge by a long shot. Kohath / who was also among those / who came with Jacob into Egypt / Gen. 46:11 / lived only 133 years / Ex. 6:18. Amram lived 137 years / v. 20. But Moses was 80 years old / when he negotiated with Pharaoh regarding the departure of the children of Israel / ch. 7:7 / which happened in that very year of the exodus. For Moses died in the last year of Israel's journey in the wilderness / or in the 40th year of their departure. By then he had become 120 years old. Deut. 34:7. But the sum of the years / which these three lived / only makes 350 years. And from that must be subtracted the years / that Kohath lived before his entry into Egypt / and the years he lived after Amram's birth / and the years Amram lived after Moses' birth. <note>The author is reconciling the 400-year prophecy with the shorter lifespans of the four generations listed in the genealogy.</note>

Thus, the meaning of this passage is this: The sojourning of your seed / (which begins with Isaac /) their servitude and affliction / together will last 400 years. For the entire life of Isaac and Jacob was a pilgrimage in foreign lands.

(not yet full) They had not yet come to rest in their sins. <note>original: "noch nicht alle" - literally "not yet all." The sense is that their measure of guilt was not yet complete.</note>

Behold, God waited perhaps several hundred years / before He visited these peoples / until their sins were so great / that they could rise no higher. In this very sense the LORD said in Matt. 23:32: **Fill up then the measure of your fathers!**

After they were settled on their dregs <note>A biblical metaphor for being complacent in sin, like wine left too long on its sediment.</note> / God sent Joshua to root them out.

God also gives sinners a full measure / so that they have no reason to complain about being rushed into judgment. Just as the Egyptians made their measure full with the plagues of the children of Israel / and were likewise visited with many plagues in return.

God has His times / both in goodness and in earnestness. He does not rush His ways therein. He revealed such a mind to His servant Moses / when the people had sinned / Ex. 32:34.

As long as there is still a struggle against the malicious party within us / there is still some hope.

As long as people still walk in the way of sinners / though it be bad enough / there is still some hope. But when they take their seat in the chair of mockers / then destruction comes.

Oh, let everyone submit to the secret ways of divine justice / and let him reflect in his security / whether God might not be giving him a delay and postponement for this reason / because his measure is not yet full! O turn back / before your thorns become ripe / so that the LORD does not snatch you away while you are still fresh! Indeed, wake up properly / and do not wait until the plague is at your throat!

v. 17. Finally, this sacrifice had to be consumed by a fire from heaven / in order to, as it were, seal the promise. See Judges 15:20 <note>original: "Richt. 15 / 20," likely a reference to divine fire, though 13:20 or 6:21 are more common parallels.</note>, Ps. 20:4.

Smoking oven) Made of earth and clay. Job 10:9.

Smoke is a symbol of wrath / also of sadness and darkening; also of prayer.

We should be like this oven of Abraham. (1) Our body is a hut of clay. (2) Christ's Spirit should dwell in us as the fire / for warming and illumination. (3) And so He would also one day awaken our dead corpses.

v. 18. From the river — to the river) The LORD assigned them such natural boundaries of rivers / so that they should not let themselves lust after the desire to rule over other nations / and to expand their land through wars. But Christ's dominion in His glorious kingdom will extend from one sea to another / and from the river to the ends of the earth. Ps. 72:8. There perhaps the Jordan is to be understood / because Christ will prove Himself especially glorious at Jerusalem.

v. 19-21.) Of these 10 nations, God afterwards commanded to exterminate 7 / Deut. 7:1 / so 3 are still missing: of which the Jews believe / that the Messiah would overcome them; and understand by them the Moabites / Ammonites and Edomites: according to Isaiah 11:14 <note>original: "11 / 19" likely refers to the extension of borders in Isaiah 11.</note>. See Ps. 125:3. 129:5. Then Christ will send His angels / and they will gather out of His kingdom all things that offend and those who do iniquity; and will cast them into the fiery furnace: there will be wailing and gnashing of teeth, Matt. 13:41-42. And so the Lord's own property / the whole earth / will be cleansed of all enemies / whose measure of sin will be full.

### Ch. XVI. The First Book of Moses. 101

# Chapter XVI.

->Ishmael’s Birth from Hagar.<-

**U**nd Sarai, Abram’s wife, bore him nothing: but she had an Egyptian maid, and her name was Hagar.

2. And Sarai said to Abram: See now, the Lord has restrained me <note>original: "verschlossen"</note> (a) so that I cannot bear; Please, go in to my maid! Perhaps I may be built up through her. And Abram obeyed the voice of Sarai.
<note>(a) 1 Samuel 1:5. <note>original: "1. Sam. 1/5."</note></note>

3. Then Sarai, Abram’s wife, took the Egyptian Hagar, her servant-maid, after ten years had passed since Abram had lived in the land of Canaan, and gave her to Abram her husband as his wife.

4. And he went in to Hagar, and she became pregnant. When she now saw that she was pregnant, her mistress was despised <note>original: "zu gering"</note> in her eyes.

---

Since Sarai was barren, she comes to the conclusion of her own human reason that perhaps the promise of offspring made to Abraham was not meant to be fulfilled through her, but through another. Thus, she thought she might give her maid to her lord during her lifetime, as the offspring born from her would also belong to her and be under her authority. However, because this was not done in faith, nor according to the divine order which forbids polygamy, she gave her lord and husband an occasion for sin. He, too, was meant to be tested in faith through her barrenness; consequently, both of them brought much domestic trouble <term>Haus-Creutz: literally "house-cross," a common historical German idiom for family suffering or trials</term> upon themselves through this act. This teaches us that we must await divine promises in faith and not seek to put them into effect through our own efforts and according to our own reason. For that yields nothing but calamity when one tries to carry out the Lord’s ways through worldly counsel, even if for a good purpose—though God, in His mercy, finally turns it to good.

**v. 2. Built up)** The figurative meaning of "building up" and "building" the Church is remarkable throughout all of Scripture.

Oh, that everything we do might happen for edification! That we might build up one another and support each other, so that we might become a dwelling place of God through the Spirit.

**v. 3. Ten years)** From this, a custom—indeed, a law—arose among the Jews that if a woman bore no children to her husband in ten years, he could or should take another. If the first wife wished to stay with him and live peacefully with the new one, it was well; if not, he released her with a bill of divorce.

**v. 4-6.)** Here was fulfilled what Solomon says regarding the crimes of the great: "A land is moved by three things, indeed by four, which it cannot bear; and the fourth is: a maidservant when she becomes heir to her mistress." <note>A reference to Proverbs 30:21-23.</note> For this also happens when such a person is taken into the marriage bed during the mistress's lifetime. Just as much unrest arose in Abraham's family through this, which was nevertheless repeatedly turned back by the Lord’s grace, because it was done with good intentions to fulfill the promise.

Our lower part <note>A common mystical interpretation of the "lower soul" or "fleshly mind."</note>, represented here by the woman, which becomes fretful because of its barrenness and its dark and barren path, seeks from external waters what it does not possess itself; it cares nothing for where it finds help, as long as it can have some support.

But it is not long before it feels resentment over this: because this support, which it wanted to use, is a maidservant to whom it has given power over itself, and she misuses that power to despise and mistreat it. Only then does it become aware of its error and complains to the higher part <note>The "higher soul" or "spirit."</note>, which it had made a partner in its crime. The higher part then puts the lower back in its proper place and restores the power that it had allowed to be taken away.

<column-break/>

5. Then Sarai said to Abram: The wrong done to me is your fault! I gave my maid into your bosom; but now that she sees she has become pregnant, I am despised in her eyes. The Lord shall judge between me and you!

6. But Abram said to Sarai: Behold, your maid is in your hand; do with her as it seems good in your eyes. When Sarai then dealt harshly with her, she fled from her presence.

7. But the angel of the Lord found her by a fountain of water in the wilderness, by the fountain on the way to Shur.

8. And

---

Good Hagar had fallen into great outward distress; she went astray in her flight in the wild forest, and likely had great unrest in her conscience because of her bad behavior. Driven into a corner, she might have thought she was now entirely alone and abandoned. But before she expected it, behold, the Angel of the Lord found her in the wilderness.

Ah, how God, with His infinite faithfulness and love, puts our unbelief to shame by so faithfully following after all straying souls and seeking them!

If Eternal Love did not itself make the beginning of our recovery and come before us with its awakening power, one would likely remain turned away from Him forever.

There is such a deep atheism or ungodly sense stuck in man that he does not reflect much upon God. His mind and the "eye of his soul" are directed only toward earthly things, through which God and His work are forgotten and neglected.

Hagar had undoubtedly heard enough about the true God, because she lived in Abraham’s family. Thus, she was not entirely without testimonies of the truth, as can be seen from all her circumstances. Nevertheless, she was so turned away from God and His straight path by the deception of sin that she first became proud over her pregnancy and disregarded her mistress, and afterward even ran away in her own self-will: and thus turned her back on both God and her rightful authority.

One might think: Oh, God will not ask after such a stubborn, proud person or run after her much. But His heart is of a completely different mind toward a poor, straying soul; He indeed hurries and runs after her everywhere at her heels, even into the wilderness—that is, into all the errors into which man plunges himself out of lack of understanding and corruption—and gathers His lost sheep from all over.

### 8. And he said: Hagar, Sarai’s maid, where do you come from? and where are you going? And she said: I am fleeing from my mistress Sarai.
### 9. And the angel of the Lord said to her: Return to your mistress, and humble yourself under her hands.
### 10. Furthermore, the angel of the Lord said to her: I will multiply your offspring greatly, so that they shall not be numbered for multitude.
### 11. Further, the angel of the Lord said to her: Behold, you have become pregnant, and shall bear a son: and you shall call his name Ishmael <note>The name Ishmael means "God hears."</note>; because the Lord has heard your misery.
### 12. And he will be a wild man: his hand will be against everyone, and everyone’s hand against him; and he shall dwell in the presence of all his brothers.

---

God comes to meet you in your desert. He cries out to you in your conscience. He wants to awaken the spark within you and come to your aid with grace.

But this cannot happen unless you let go of your own will and struggle against it with true earnestness. If Hagar had wanted to persist in her stubbornness and not humble herself again under her mistress, she would never have found the right path.

<margin>v. 9.</margin>
Therefore the angel commanded her so earnestly—Return—and humble yourself) It has always been a falling away from God when man does not want to conform to God’s order, but wants to go free and be his own master and ruler; just as Hagar did not want to follow the free woman <note>A reference to Sarah, who represents the "free" promise in Pauline theology (Galatians 4).</note>, but out of pride lived contrary to her mistress, and may well have vigorously tested her patience. This is caused by the self-love of the evil will, in which one allows oneself to be blinded by Satan, to drive forward so boldly in one's lusts, without bit or bridle.

From this, as from an evil mother, only mockery and unbelief are born later, like an Ishmael and a mocker. Thus also false and ungodly people exercise the pious with their resistance; but they cannot come into God's grace until they turn back and humble themselves under God and his friends. And

According to the prophetic sense, this history expresses that those who do not obey the Gospel must eventually come to Sarah or the true Church, which makes one truly free in the Son of God.

<margin>v. 12.</margin>
A wild man) This testimony of divine prophecy is still noticeable today in the descendants of Ishmael, the Saracens or Hagarenes <note>Historical terms for Arab peoples, often used in older European texts to link contemporary populations to biblical origins.</note>, who are mostly the current Turkish subjects and the Arabs, in their wild nature. The Apostle understands by this the wild and fierce nature of man: which becomes all the more fierce when the law wants to subdue it and keep it in check.

Hagar thus represents the multifaceted and active path <note>The "way of works" or human effort.</note> which is preferred over faith, because faith often seems to be unfruitful. Though this path is only the maidservant, as it were, she is nonetheless the mother of a great people in Ishmael; but of a people full of confusion, war, and dispersion, who possess nothing except through weapons. Through this, God repays Hagar for her sorrow.

<column-break/>

### 13. And she called the name of the Lord who spoke to her: You are the God of seeing <note>Original: "du bist der GOTT des Sehens." In Hebrew, *El Roi*.</note>. For she said: Have I also here looked after him who has seen me?
<margin>Luke 1, 48.</margin>
### 14. There-

God looks for us in our misery when we do not think of it and wander in error; so that we also should look back at Him and seek Him out.

This is truly such an unspeakable comfort and refreshment for a humbled heart that one should learn to entice and move others to repentance and faith by contemplating such grace.

<margin>Ps. 94, 7.</margin>
The ungodly person does not believe that God is so near to him with His Spirit. He says in his heart: The Lord does not see it. But a sinner awakened in repentance experiences it very differently.

How shattered and confused <note>original: "confus"</note> this maid must have been in her heart when she ran away from her mistress and did not want to humble herself! And yet she was so powerfully touched and turned around when the angel of the Lord so faithfully came to her aid with counsel and comfort, that she felt God's presence alive within her. And as soon as she complied, broke her will, and wanted to obey by humbling her pride under Sarah—behold, she was helped.

As soon as a soul allows itself to be diverted from the error of its way—indeed, wherever God perceives an honest will that the person will follow—it is already repaid with a glance of grace. The poor, frightened sinner then immediately notices some relief and an encouraging word <note>original: "Zuruf-Einsprechung," a Pietist term for God's inner address to the soul.</note> in his conscience, provided he is willing to follow honestly.

Certainly, we do not come to the vision of God in any other way than by turning back from our wrong paths and our own choices, or whatever else we have chosen in pride, and throwing ourselves truly under God and men.

Let everyone reflect on whether they have ever experienced such a powerful turning of their mind from those wandering paths in their life; that, whereas they previously turned their back on the Lord as if He were not present, they afterwards found themselves so powerfully enclosed in God's presence that they were truly convinced and had to confess that the Lord is a God of seeing.

If you have perhaps asked little after God until now, or even disregarded Him in all your trickery: oh, then let yourself be turned back and toward Him in His presence, and think that God cannot remain God if He were not present everywhere, and thus also to you.

If your atheistic mind—which would like to imagine that there were no judge, no punishment, and thus no God—tries to persuade you that God does not see you: oh, then fight and pray against such lies of the enemy, and see to it that you can say to your Creator in defiance of your flesh:

> You are the God of seeing! as Hagar's saying goes according to the Hebrew; or also: You are a God of gazing! You, Lord, let yourself be seen! Which is at the same time a word of wonder—that God is so gracious and draws so near to humans that He can be seen.

Nothing can sustain faith more powerfully than this reminder: You are the God of seeing!

When the enemies of God and the truth rage, or false friends shoot secretly with their arrows, thinking no one sees it because they have started it so artfully: what then is the conclusion of a sufferer, or what can he better appeal to than the seeing God: You are the God of seeing!

When the inner enemies and one's own corruption make the struggle difficult for faith, what comfort is there where one cannot appeal to this open eye of God and say: You are the God of seeing! You know that I do not want to agree with these enemies!

Should the world also approach with flattering cunning, and even act pious to entice us with trickery out of the narrow way to life, so that we might use their false freedom and conform ourselves to them; oh, how this reminder can strike down such desire when the heart rises to God and remembers in His holy presence: You are the God of seeing! How could I do such a great evil and sin against Him in His presence!

14. Therefore the well was named the Well of the Living One who has looked upon me. See, it is between Kadesh and Bered.

v. 14. Me) As a person worthy of pity and standing in danger, the LORD has

Looked Upon) This "looking upon" consisted partly in correction, and partly in comfort and strengthening. He found her in a state of needing help; and as Hagar praises such a looking-upon, and even names the well of that place after it, she confesses to her own humiliation how necessary God's discipline and improvement were for her. She means to say: "You dear God, you eternal Love, have faithfully sought me and set me right through your gracious gaze toward me!"

Oh, how immeasurably precious should this correcting gaze of God be to us! Truly, God can show you no greater grace than when he brings you back from ruin, even if it does not please the flesh.

Whoever does not want the punishing and correcting gaze of God will also not obtain the comforting one. Indeed, one is not capable of any thorough comfort unless one is first convicted of one's own misery. Therefore, Hagar points to both in this word.

Oh, happy is the person whose eyes are opened in their distress, so that they can perceive this comforting gaze of <term>essential love</term>! <note>Original: *wesentlichen Liebe*. This term refers to God's actual, substantive presence and being, rather than a mere feeling or idea.</note>

When a father calls his child to himself and looks at him kindly, there arises in the child a joy and an awakening to look back at him in love. In the same way, God’s look of love unfailingly works in an instant in the mind of a converted person, so that they turn toward Him with their desire.

An unspeakable joy must have arisen in Hagar's heart, not only because she was rescued in body and deemed worthy of such great promises from the angel, but also because her soul was now set right again and received back into grace. And

So God can make the desert of a previously shattered heart into a lovely <term>Sharon</term> <note>A reference to the Plain of Sharon, a fertile and beautiful region in Israel mentioned in the Bible as a symbol of restoration.</note> and into a pleasure garden, when the Eternal Good shows itself therein and allows itself to be known, tasted, and enjoyed.

One does not think of this during times of temptation—that something so beautiful and glorious should lie hidden in the depths of the soul—when one sees nothing but misery and ruin before and within oneself; when it is as if there is a howling in such a desert, and one evil spirit meets another, offering its hand to storm the poor heart.

But from where else does such light and life come to a converted heart, if not from the gracious and powerful presence of the Highest Good?

Even if it happens afterward, as it did with Hagar, that after such grace one is cast out again or often into the desert (as she had to wander once more with Ishmael; chapter 21), one still knows and experiences that the Living and Walking One is with us.

Oh, that everyone might powerfully experience such a presence, such oversight, and such a bright eye of the Almighty! Then one would keep Him before one's eyes in His holiness and would not consent to any sin.

## Chapter XVII.

->The Institution of Circumcision and the Promise of Isaac.<-

When Abram was ninety-nine years old, the LORD appeared to Abram and said to him: I

<note>The following text is commentary on the preceding verses.</note>

That true piety is nothing superfluous or unnecessary—as the raw, godless world now thinks, making it a mockery, or even calling it an error and heresy—can be seen almost nowhere more clearly than from this very declaration of the eternal living God Himself.

Truly, if a true godly walk were not unavoidably necessary, or were impossible for a right believer, God would not still be so earnestly insisting upon it with this old patriarch in his advanced age. He was already

99 years old? He had walked before God in all truth for so long, and yet God still demanded this of him. What then should He not be able to demand of others, who for the most part have not even begun—or have barely begun—to fear and love Him?

The matter is therefore certain enough: one must become and live godly.

But there remains a more important question: namely, in what true godliness consists. For hypocritical nature also pretends to all kinds of piety, and usually seeks it in appearances, in Pharisaic exercises, statutes, and ceremonies; or, if it is to be called "good," in some external good works.

But God describes godliness here quite differently than reason and the Pharisaic mind do: briefly, but in the most powerful and emphatic way.

Everything consists in living before God's face, and indeed, with a sincere heart.

God shows and praises Himself to Abraham in the most perfect way, in order to win his heart all the more: in that He

Appeared) With this, in addition to and outside of His general presence (as He is near to all creatures), He made Himself known to him in a particular, high way, which was not unusual for Abraham and his like. Conversely, nowadays, this is so much more foreign, unknown, and even hated, that most people will not allow it, but label it as suspicious "fantasizing" or "fanaticism"—just as if God changed, and were not the same today as He was yesterday, if only such sublime and purified hearts were available for it. For certainly, as one of the first teachers (a) clearly confesses, God is not seen by everyone. The heart of man must be clear and pure. God does not appear to those who are entangled in sins, unless they have first purified themselves from everything. But instead of blaming the deficiency and themselves for this, they claim that God no longer wishes to reveal Himself, or that it is not fitting for Him because He is a spirit. But the ancient and pure Church taught quite differently on this matter.

It belongs, indeed, writes Augustine (b), to the divine nature that it cannot be seen; but when He wills, He nevertheless lets Himself be seen. For He indeed appeared to the Patriarchs because He willed to; but to others not, because it did not please Him.

Everything He wills is quite easy for Him, and when it pleases Him, He lets Himself down and transforms Himself, allowing Himself to be seen by those who love Him! in an inaccessible light of glory. Thus, out of great and unspeakable love, He appears to those who are worthy, according to His power. Macarius. (c)

Abraham was such a proven beloved among others; which is why God the LORD spoke to him very diligently and assured him anew of His grace and favor, for a new strengthening in faith and trust. For He never comes empty, whenever and wherever He comes.

In this appearance or revelation of His holy presence, the LORD made such powerful declarations of His perfect counsel, and above all laid a golden foundation for it by presenting His most perfect essence.

<header>The First Book of Moses, Chapter XVII.</header>

# I am the all-sufficient GOD ^(a) / walk constantly ^(b) before my face / and be perfect.

->(a) Ch. 35:11; Exodus 6:3. (b) Psalm 16:8.<-
->2. And<-

---

**I am the all-sufficient GOD** <note>original: *allgenugsame GOTT*; a translation of the Hebrew *El Shaddai*</note>) In this way the eternal Godhead describes Himself, pointing and drawing Abraham’s heart—and our own—with all power away from all other things toward Himself, as if to say:

"Dear one, why does the eye of your mind still gape here and there? What do you still seek among created things, even in the most subtle way? Do you not have eternally enough in Me? Am I not the fountain from which you can draw everything? Look here at Me: It is I! I am that I am! I am the all-sufficient GOD!"

This word truly applies to all of us whenever we notice or become aware of the slightest thing regarding GOD. Indeed, GOD certainly allows Himself to be felt in all things that come before us, calling out to our hearts: "It is I!"

Does He not call out powerfully to every sinner, crying out to them both in their conscience and through the Law: "It is I! I am the LORD your God; you shall have no other gods beside Me!"

And do not GOD’s benefits and the enticements of His love have a powerful voice to testify of Him, that it is He? Even every little blade of grass was created so that GOD might convict us through them; that He alone exists, and besides Him there is no GOD.

We must take all the more notice of this "It is I," because so many false gods announce themselves to our hearts, seeking to steal our love. And yet—

No thing, in heaven or on earth, can echo the true GOD’s words: "I am the all-sufficient GOD!" Rather, this is a privilege, a character, and a title that the eternal GOD possesses entirely alone and proves in deed.

O, what a divine foundation for faith, that we can find in GOD such an all-sufficient source of all good, so that whatever we might think of or desire—provided it is good—it is present in Him!

And thus, this all-sufficient GOD also proves Himself therein to be an **almighty GOD**, because a believing soul can think of or demand nothing good for which it does not find all the capacity in the living GOD.

This all-sufficiency gives to simple faith such a perfect tranquility in GOD that a believing heart is nonetheless satisfied in Him, even if, according to reason or one's own choice, it has obtained nothing yet, or sees others having more.

That the Son of GOD is also indicated here under the name **El Shaddai** <term>El Shaddai: often translated as "God Almighty," but interpreted here as "All-Sufficient"</term> is concluded partly because the Person in this chapter is the same as in the following one, in which the Son of GOD indisputably speaks and acts; and partly because this LORD established the covenant with Abraham: and the author of the covenant has, of course, always been the Messiah. It can also be concluded from the principle that the eternal Father always reveals Himself in the Son and speaks through Him according to His grace, and indeed in a comprehensible human way. Therefore, He also points us to Him in the New Testament, saying that we should hear Him.

And certainly, a hungry soul finds in the heart of the Father—which is JESUS Christ—such perfect sufficiency that, when she renounces everything else, she must necessarily be well, and she cannot or will not go out or hunger for anything else.

Just as one thing flows from another, and "godliness" <note>original: *Gott-seligkeit*, literally "God-blessedness"</note> gets its name from "blessedness" because one is content and blessed in, with, and like GOD; so GOD knew no more blessed counsel or proposal to give Abraham for such a purpose than this:

**walk before my face**) But we cannot walk in this way if we have not first turned toward GOD. For if the wrath of GOD stands like a cloud between you and GOD because of your impenitence, you cannot behold His gracious face. And how then will you be able to live before Him in His grace?

But what else do you think is understood by this

**Face** of the all-perfect Good, than every kind of manifestation and communication by which GOD makes His gracious presence known and

<column-break/>

experienced in the light of the Holy Spirit; through which one then learns to know GOD Himself. Just as one knows, seeks, and finds a friend by their face when one wishes to speak or deal with them.

If you now wish to become truly pious, O man! then begin with repentance or conversion from your ungodly ways, and pray to GOD day and night for His Holy Spirit until He gives you such a strong remembrance and mindfulness of His presence that you cannot forget Him in all your circumstances; and then practice this without growing weary. For—

This walking before GOD’s face is a matter to be sought and recognized more in the power of experience and in daily practice than can be expressed with words. One should simply enter into the matter itself and become eager for it: then one will learn a thousand times more by doing so than through all external descriptions.

And if someone should still ask: how does one practice this? the answer is here from GOD’s own speech: Walk

**Constantly**) Or steadily so. It is a work that requires attention daily, hourly, yes, every moment, alongside all other things. However important other things may seem, this is still much more necessary. Indeed, there is no more necessary exercise in the whole of life than this.

Therefore, GOD insists on an unwavering continuation and faithfulness in it, and means to say:

Walk before my face as much when you must be in company as when you are alone. You will be able to maintain and revere my powerful presence even among other people, if only you hold onto it as your only treasure.

Walk before me with your words as well as in your thoughts, gestures, and works. Speak nothing but what is fitting in my presence; do nothing else either: thus you will be preserved from many a deviation.

Walk also before me in good days as well as in evil days. In good days, do not become overconfident, and do not forget your GOD out of extravagance and lightmindedness. In evil days, keep me all the more before your eyes. For this will be your greatest comfort—when you have me in all want, sorrow, misery, and persecution.

Walk before me in such a way that you do not only seek or honor me here or there, but everywhere in all your corners; so that in your deviations you do not think I am far from you: but rather believe that I am near you.

To arrive at such a constant walk is easy, if only one has a real desire for it. And therefore, it must be presupposed that a person is truly earnest about their salvation, and therefore firmly resolves in GOD to cling fast to Him despite the devil, the flesh, and the world, and their own will.

When this happens sincerely, then through the grace of the Holy Spirit in conversion, such a hunger of faith for Christ and His righteousness will arise that you will not forget Him day or night, but will constantly woo, pray, and beg for His love.

This foundation and walking before GOD then makes a person truly sincere for the first time, so that he seeks to hide nothing, and does not seek to play the hypocrite or lie, when he believes that GOD is so near.

And that is what is also required here in this walk, which in the Hebrew actually means,

**Be perfect**) Do not immediately be repulsed when you hear of "perfection"! GOD demands no more of us than He Himself is willing to work in us. Only understand it correctly according to GOD’s mind, and you will see.

Whoever is so wise as to surrender themselves with all earnestness to such a perfect pattern, and from now on makes a covenant with the GOD of Enoch, Noah, Abraham, and all believers, to walk before Him and with Him: that person goes infallibly on such a path into the eternal light, in which GOD Himself dwells and is blessed!

O LORD, lift up the light of your countenance upon us, and let this Your present face shine upon us and in us for our full recovery!

## 2. And I will make my covenant between me and you / and will multiply you exceedingly.

Here now is a renewal and confirmation of the covenant / which GOD had already made with Abram in Chapter 15. where once again the seed is promised / and at the same time it is shown / that it would not be Ishmael / upon whom the divine promise rested / but another son from Sarai / who was soon to be born. Therefore GOD / after the long span of thirteen years / wished to renew and confirm this covenant before that birth; to show / that the seed from Sarai should properly be the heir of this covenant.

After GOD first displayed his all-sufficiency for all eternal salvation / as also indicated in Chapter 15, 1; and thereby noted the chief duty / which he requires in faith: that one must walk constantly before GOD’s face in holy fear / and seek to do what is pleasing to GOD / as even Enoch and Noah had done; Chapters 5, 24; 6, 9; Hebrews 11, 5, 6, 7. hereafter / that he must be perfect: namely to love GOD with a whole heart and to cling to him / to love all that is good and to hate all that is evil; which also applied here / since he had allowed himself to be led astray by Sarah's human reasoning / toward that which could not be pleasing to GOD; just as Christ also requires this of his covenant-companions / Matthew 5, 48. So GOD assures him anew of his eternal peace with him / and that he should not only be an example of the blessing of all nations / Chapter 12, 2, 3. but also a father of all the blessed among the nations / who should be so incorporated into his seed / which would come from him / namely Christ / that they should be engrafted into his root / and so receive from him the new divine life of the children of GOD / who would therefore also call themselves by his name / so that in the likeness of his faith they might also be saved. See Isaiah 27, 6; 44, 5; Psalm 87, 4, 5, 6; Romans 6, 5; 11, 17, 19; and 4, 11, 12, 16, 17. The new name should also strengthen him in this faith / since the beginning **Ab** and the end **Sam** express the mystery / that he should become **Ab-Zamon** <note>original: *Ab-Zamon*; a mystical or phonetic interpretation of the Hebrew *Av Hamon*, meaning "Father of a Multitude"</note> / that is, a father of a multitude of nations / and that also including their kings. Just as the kings were not only in Judah and Israel / but also those of the Ishmaelites / and the Edomites / among whom finally was Herod’s lineage / and from the children of Keturah / and even to this day among the Oriental peoples / who descend from these nations / and thus from Abraham. So that truly from no other man may more have descended than from him / and he may rightly be called a royal father. From whom also the single and true King of his people / the Messiah / should spring: from whose birth onward it also seems to have ceased / that more kings have come from his seed / so that the obedience of all believers might be directed toward him alone. And

This promise was gloriously fulfilled especially in Christ / since GOD according to Psalm 2, 8. at the beginning of the Gospel gave him the heathen as an inheritance in the conversion of so many nations / who in the three parts of the world / and especially in Europe / have converted to Christ / and thus have become his spiritual seed. And in the end it will be fulfilled with all emphasis / when the ends of the earth shall also be given to him as a seed. Then it shall be said: Praise the LORD all you Gentiles / and extol him all you peoples! etc. Psalm 117. See also Psalm 22, 31, 32; 72, 5, 8, 17.

According to the spirit, GOD promises the soul that has surrendered to him / after he has shown it / that it must be content to please him / since this is the means to attain perfection / that he will unite himself with it and make it fruitful: which is / first to honor it with his union / and afterward to enrich it with the fruits of its own fruitfulness.

O the infinite evangelical blessing / which often extends over many ages from a single believer / who is found faithful! That is truly the grain / namely the Kingdom of GOD / that brings forth thousandfold fruit; and the leaven / that permeates the whole dough.

And thus certainly all blessing of the Gospel depends upon a faithful walk.

Let us only follow the faithful Abraham in this / who immediately / when he heard such words from GOD / fell down—

## 3. Then Abram fell on his face / and GOD talked with him / and said:

## 4. As for me / behold my covenant is with you / and you shall become a father of many nations.

## 5. And your name shall no longer be called Abram / but Abraham shall be your name. For I have made you a father of a multitude of nations.

## 7. And

---

v. 3. *Fell on his face*) To the earth / and thereby acknowledged his unworthiness and GOD’s high goodness.

This soul / after it has learned so much / that it no longer demands signs / thinks only upon / how it may annihilate itself <term>annihilate: in mystical theology, this refers to "annihilation of the self," or total humility and surrender of the ego to God</term>: for it knows / that annihilation is the most certain state / for allowing oneself to be used for the execution of GOD’s decrees / and that the true preparation for the supernatural is nothingness.

Therefore let us also tremble and fall down before the majesty of GOD / as often as we are reminded or assured in our hearts of his gracious approach / and deem ourselves unworthy of such a high visitation. This will preserve us in constant awe and reverence before GOD’s glory / and not easily let us become bold / secure, or light-minded.

Rather, the LORD will draw us ever deeper into himself and his bright divine light / and enclose us more closely in his covenant.

For all those of little faith and the weak should believe for certain / GOD does not let his own be taken from him / who hold to him and his holy presence. He confirms them so through his seal in his firm covenant and foundation / that neither height nor depth may separate them: provided only that one turns away from all unrighteousness and remains in him.

v. 4.) After spiritual annihilation, GOD reveals himself in a much different way / than he did before. For he gives a heart entirely devoted to him the highest and best knowledge of his majesty / which one may have in what concerns him / and also renews the union and his promises.

v. 5. *Abram --- Abraham*) Here belongs the observation of Clement of Alexandria <note>original: *Clementis Alexandrini*</note>, who writes thus (a): When Abraham was still devoted to philosophy and the contemplation of natural and heavenly things / he was called Abram / a high father. Afterward / when he had seen the Son in the spirit / and had known GOD / who is better than the creature; he took on the A / namely the knowledge of the one and only GOD / and was called Abraham / as one who from an investigator of nature had become a wise and godly man / indeed, a friend of GOD.

After the annihilation has occurred / a new name is then also given; a name which no one knows except him who receives it; such a name which the LORD has given from his own mouth / and thus also with the same name everything that was necessary to fulfill this whole intent of GOD.

v. 6.) The promises of a great lineage are further repeated / where the persons included therein are exalted both for their virtues and their status / in that it says; *Kings shall come from you*: and because it says elsewhere; *he is the father of us all*.

7. And I will establish my covenant between me and you / and between your seed after you / throughout their generations / for an everlasting covenant; so that I may be your GOD / and the GOD of your seed after you.
8. And I will give to you and to your seed after you the land wherein you are a stranger / the whole land of Canaan / for an everlasting possession; and I will be their GOD.
9. Furthermore, GOD said to Abraham: You shall therefore keep my covenant / you and your seed after you / in their generations.

The promised eternal possession of the whole land of Canaan was first fulfilled after the Babylonian captivity <note>original: "Babylonischen Gefängniß"</note> / Zechariah 9:2, 5, 6, 7, and will be fulfilled with great emphasis in the glorious kingdom. Zechariah 14:21.

The word **Eternal**, however, is very often understood in Holy Scripture to mean a span of time / which has a certain cycle and end. Exodus 12:14. <note>The author clarifies that "eternal" (ewig) in a biblical context often refers to an age or a specific dispensation rather than infinite time.</note>

GOD assures the surrendered soul <note>original: "gelassene Seele," a term in German Pietism referring to a soul that has yielded its will entirely to God</note> / after it has come so far / and has received the new name / that he wished to be the GOD of that soul and of all surrendered souls who would descend from it in the future. At that point, true constancy lays its firm foundation / and in such a person, no further change is to be expected. GOD says to the soul / that he is its GOD / and this connection / which he has made with it / shall be everlasting / constant, and eternal. He is their GOD / because he commands them with power / and nothing in them resists him anymore / since their will is entirely lost in his; and because they carry out his will here on earth / just as the blessed ones in heaven obey the same.

10. This is my covenant which you shall keep between me and you / and between your seed after you: Every male among you shall be circumcised.
11. And you shall circumcise the flesh of your foreskin. The same shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you.

and through which both the sinful birth was indicted / and the blood of atonement required / as well as the dividing wall among the nations erected / was intended to be a seal of the righteousness of faith / which Abraham already possessed in his previous state / and through which he had already attained righteousness; thus, he did not first become righteous through the work of circumcision; a delusion <note>original: "Wahn"</note> which Paul wishes to remove from the Jews in Romans 4:1, etc.

However, such a painful sign was given / to show / that in the covenant of GOD one must die away from one's old nature, even against its will / and thus circumcise the foreskin of the heart / and should not be stiff-necked. Deuteronomy 10:16, 30:6. Which must therefore happen in the putting off of the sinful body in the flesh / Colossians 2:11, and in the crucifixion of the same together with its lusts and desires. Galatians 5:24.

---

It will be neither unpleasant nor unhelpful / to note here a few of the Jewish customs and antiquities regarding this.

<margin>v. 11. Circumcision</margin> The German Jews of today call it *Judschen* <note>A Yiddish-inflected German term for the rite of circumcision.</note> / and they observe the following ceremonies in Frankfurt. Two days before the circumcision, many women gather in the home of the woman in confinement / and prepare 12 thin wax lights / according to the number of the 12 tribes of Israel. These lights are braided together into one / which is burned during the circumcision before the *Oran Hakkodesch* <gloss>the Holy Ark of the Law</gloss> in the synagogue / and is called the *Judsch*-candle by them.

On Friday evening or the night preceding the day of circumcision, many Jewish men and women come together at the home of the woman in confinement / and congratulate her on the little boy. The most pious among them read and pray / in order to drive away the devils / who are said to especially prey upon the mother and child during this night; as well as to shorten the time for the mother / so that she shall not be grieved / because of the pain her little son must endure the following day in the circumcision. Otherwise, there is eating and drinking throughout the entire night until the bright day: except for the *Mohel* <gloss>the circumciser</gloss>, who is to circumcise the child / who retires home to rest after the meal / in order to better perform the important work the following day. This night is called the Vigil Night <note>original: "Wach-Nacht"</note>. The whole house is then full of lights and nothing but joy. This is called זָכָר <gloss>a male / or / as the Jews pronounce it / Socher, which is as much as / the male's or little boy's meal</gloss>.

During the circumcision / which formerly took place at home / but nowadays is also performed in the school <note>In this period, "Schule" (school) was a common term for the synagogue.</note> / the *Sandyk* <gloss>the companion or godfather</gloss> has the child on his lap.

There must be 2 godparents for every child to be circumcised / a male and a female figure. Thus, one prefers to take a husband and wife: or / if the godmother is a widow / another male person is taken. If the godfather is unmarried or a widower / a maiden is taken for the role / even if it were a little girl of 3 years / as long as she can carry the infant. For the godmother must carry the little boy in her arms across the street to the door of the synagogue / in a procession with other women: then the men take him from her; and after the circumcision, he is given back to her to carry home. The greatest joy of the godmother is / that on the evening before the circumcision she comes dressed up into the women’s synagogue; and / if it is an unmarried girl / (who otherwise may not enter the synagogue / ) she is led in by her mother or another woman. Afterward, she helps to bathe and wash the child on the night before the circumcision. For

A child / who is carried to circumcision / must indeed be washed and cleansed beforehand. Where the slightest impurity is left uncleansed / the child is entirely unfit for such a work: so much so / that / if the child relieves itself <note>original: "seine natürliche Deffnung bekommt"</note> / before it is brought to the *Mohel* or circumciser / or before the foreskin is taken from him / the circumcision cannot be completed / until the child is washed and cleansed anew.

There must be 2 cups of wine at the circumcision. With one, the circumciser rinses and cleanses his mouth / when he has sucked the blood from the circumcised member with the same / and sprinkles it upon the member. The other he uses or blesses before the *Oran Hakkodesch* <gloss>Holy Ark</gloss>, when he blesses the child after the circumcision / and gives him his name; he also sprinkles some of that wine into the child's face / to refresh him.

If ever a banquet <note>original: "Gasterey"</note> is costly and joyful / it is the one after the circumcision / and there must be עשרה <gloss>ten</gloss>, that is / at least 10 Jewish men / who are over 13 years old / present. They also believe / that the word מילה <gloss>Mila, or circumcision</gloss> / commands them to hold such a banquet: interpreting the Hebrew through the initial letters as: משתה יעשה לכל הקרואים <note>original Hebrew phrase translated: "he shall prepare a banquet for all those invited."</note>. On the third day after the circumcision, there is another banquet.

But why GOD placed this covenant of circumcision upon such a member / the wise can easily guess. There is no doubt / that the animal-like way of reproduction resulting from the lamentable Fall / viewed in and of itself, is an abomination to GOD's holiness / and is borne under divine patience until the time of reformation. The future covenant of grace in JESUS Christ aims toward this: that the animal members of earthly lust should first be circumcised in their disorderly outbreaks / and finally be entirely put away and separated from man again.

<header>Chapter XVII. The First Book of Moses.</header>

### 12. And when he is <margin>(a) Lev. 12:3.</margin> (a) eight days old / then every male among you shall be circumcised throughout your generations : whether born in the house / or bought with money / from any stranger / who is not of your seed.

Eight days old) Why at that time and in such tender youth? Maimonides <note>Moses Maimonides (1138–1204) was a preeminent Sephardic Jewish philosopher and scholar.</note> (a) gives the reason. (1) Because / if it were delayed until the boy grew up / he might perhaps no longer wish to do it. (2) Because in childhood he does not feel such great pain as an adult : partly due to the tenderness of his skin / and partly due to his weak imagination <note>The author uses "Einbildungs-Krafft" to mean the mental anticipation of pain.</note>. For the Jews claim that the pain in children passes quickly / and is only a matter of a few days. (3) Because the parents do not yet worry so much about the newborn child / and the power of imagination / which causes the love of parents toward children / is not yet so strong in them. For the love of a father or mother toward their son is not nearly as intense when he is born / as when he begins to be one year old : and they do not love a child of one year as much as a son of six years. Thus, circumcision would often be neglected / because of the parents' tender love for their child. On the other hand, immediately after birth, the power of imagination is still weak / especially in the father / to whom this law was given.

But that it must happen on the eighth day / occurred because all newborn animals are far too weak due to great moisture / and are almost as if they were still in the mother's womb : and this lasts until seven days are ended / after which they first begin to be counted among those who see the air of this world. Exod. 22:30.

In short: God did not want it before the 8th day / because the little boy was still unclean from the mother for seven days after birth and far too tender : He did not want to wait any longer than that / because through this the little boy was received into the covenant of God.

Into the mystery / which God has hidden beneath this / the "veil of Moses" <note>A reference to the idea that those under the Old Testament Law cannot fully see the spiritual truth revealed in Christ.</note> does not allow those under the law to look.

That it had to happen on the eighth day / foreshadows the first day of the week / which is also the eighth / when Christ rose / when the circumcision of the heart was earned through the fellowship of the new life in Christ / which the Lord promised in Deut. 30:6. And since this has been fulfilled / the image of physical circumcision had to cease. Gal. 5:2. etc.

This sign was meanwhile intended to bring the people of circumcision a glory in God and in faith in him / that God would be their God / to whom they should always take their refuge / trust in him / and rejoice in him.

Male) In the male gender, the female should be understood as included under its head.

Strangers) At the circumcision of a stranger and a <term>proselyte</term> <note>original: "Juden-Genossen," meaning a convert to Judaism.</note>, this special blessing was spoken by the circumciser : Blessed be you / LORD our God / King of the world / who has sanctified us with your commandments / and has commanded us to circumcise the strangers / and to draw out the blood of the covenant from them!

The same had to take place in the presence of 3 witnesses.

To the initiation of a proselyte belonged not only circumcision / but also baptism / once the wound from the circumcision was healed : because otherwise the water would have been harmful to the wound. It did not matter what kind of water it was / as long as there was enough of it that he could immerse himself completely in it.

The baptism must not take place at night / nor on the Sabbath / nor on a feast day / and a special small court <note>original: "Klein-Gerichte," likely referring to a Beth Din of three.</note> of three persons had to be present.

After receiving baptism, thanks were given to God the Lord / and a blessing was spoken.

The 3rd initiation ceremony for a new proselyte was a burnt offering / either a bull / or 2 turtledoves / or 2 young pigeons.

<margin>(a) Guide for the Perplexed <note>original: "Mor. Nevoch."</note> part 3. c. 49.</margin>

<column-break/>

### 13. He who is born in your house / or bought with your money / shall certainly be circumcised. Thus shall my covenant be in your flesh / for an everlasting covenant.

### 14. And

The women / who wished to become <term>proselytes of righteousness</term> <note>original: "Fremdlinge der Gerechtigkeit," or Ger Tzedek, full converts who take on all the obligations of the Law.</note> / were only baptized / and were placed in the water up to their necks by other women : and after several laws were recited to them by their appointed witnesses / they immersed themselves entirely under the water ; while the witnesses turned their faces away / when they came out of the water again. Which immersion into water / especially when everything was full of snow and ice in winter / is said to have been so burdensome to many / that some would have liked to see this immersion abolished / especially because of the women in Galilee / who became infertile from the cold water.

The proselytes were also diligently examined before their initiation / and asked / why they wanted to adopt the Jewish religion? Whether they perhaps thought to become rich thereby? Or whether they hoped thereby to come to high positions? Or whether they did it out of fear? If it was a man / they asked him ; whether he had perhaps cast his eyes on an Israelite woman? If it was a woman ; whether she was perhaps infatuated with an Israelite young fellow? If they found no such reasons / it was presented to them / how difficult and tedious the law is to keep ; if they did not look upon the religion in true earnestness alone / they should step back in time. If they would not desist / they were accepted.

If the children were already born before the father became a proselyte / but were still minors ; the boys under 13 / and the girls under 12 years : the father could still have them circumcised and baptized ; and what they lacked in their own consent / the court provided. Yet / when they reached their years of maturity / they could step back in the very hour that they were recognized and declared mature / if they wished. If they did not do it in that same hour / they could not withdraw / but had to remain proselytes.

The children / who were born after their parents' initiation / he could have baptized as he wished / as a proselyte of righteousness / or as a servant / or as a freedman.

If a pregnant woman became a proselyte / she did not need to have her child baptized <note>The child was considered to have been baptized while in the womb during the mother's immersion.</note>.

If a child no longer had a father / and the mother brought it forward ; it was also bought and / where it was a boy / circumcised beforehand.

If someone had captured a small heathen child / he could have it baptized as he wished / as a proselyte of righteousness / or as a servant / or as a freedman.

Bought with money) The servant who was bought / or otherwise obtained and acquired from heathens / was / if he was still a minor / circumcised by force. If the master of such a servant did not want to do it / then the court took charge of it. But if he had come to his years of maturity / he was not circumcised / until he agreed to it. If he did not want to adopt the Jewish religion / the master often exhorted him for a year and a day. If he still did not want to / he had to be sold back to heathens. But if he was bought with the condition / that he should indeed be free from circumcision / but still serve God / like the strangers in the gate <note>Gentiles who followed the Noahide laws but did not fully convert.</note> ; he could serve. But if he did not want that either ; he had to be killed / as one who was not worthy of the day's light.

But if he gladly accepted the Jewish religion / he had to be circumcised and baptized.

At the baptism, the master had to take good care / that the servant did not say to his 3 witnesses / that he was being baptized as a free man. For otherwise he was free / and his master had to set him free / even against his will. Therefore his master bowed him down into the water from above / and did not let him rise / until he said / or the servant himself confessed / that he was being baptized as a servant ; unless it was the case / that his master wanted to release him voluntarily. And when that happened / he was baptized as a freedman / and also called so.

The same was also done with the maidservants.
