38. And Esau said to his father: "Do you then have only this single blessing, my father? Bless me, yes, me too, my father!" And Esau lifted up his voice and wept.

39. Then Isaac his father answered and said to him: "Behold, the fatness of the earth shall be your dwelling, and of the dew of heaven from above!"

40. "And by your sword you shall live, and you shall serve your brother; and it shall happen, when you shall firmly insist upon it, you will tear his yoke from your neck."

---

He received only a physical blessing of a fertile dwelling, and it was announced to him how he would have in common with worldly people the pursuit of violent dominion, the waging of wars, and thus living from such plunder. This, however, is not the inheritance of the children of God. This can be gathered from Jacob’s blessing; for David did not achieve victory through violent warring against his neighbors, but through his heroic protection against his enemies, overcoming them through the blessing of God. It is also prophesied to Esau that he would one day tear the yoke of his brother from his neck: which happened in part in 1 Kings 11:14 <note>This refers to the rebellion of Hadad the Edomite against Solomon.</note>, but more so in the general revolt during the times of Joram, 2 Kings 8:20, 22, at a time when Israel too had cast off the yoke of the Law.

v. 38. **Single Blessing**) *Hi* <note>original: "Hi" — referring to the Hebrew demonstrative pronoun *hu* or *hi* meaning "this"</note>, "this" or "that," is entirely omitted in most translations.

**Also me**) Implicitly, a two-fold blessing is indicated here: one for the heavenly man, the other for the earthly.

v. 39. 40. What is the great difference between Jacob’s and Esau’s blessing, except that the order is reversed, because the order among the brothers was also reversed? And why then does Esau cry out with such a great and bitter cry? And why does he threaten to kill his brother? There must therefore be some difference in this part of Jacob’s blessing. It is notable, however, that the words may also be rendered thus: "Your dwelling shall be *without* the fatness of the earth and *without* the dew of heaven." The Hebrew allows for this interpretation. Psalm 109:24.

Yet the common understanding also has its intended path in the mystery. The fatness of the earth—or of its own physical nature—is given to the earthly man, and the dew of heaven is communicated to him through the heavenly man. And because the service to be rendered to his brother is added as a part of the blessing, it is clear from this that it is a blessing for the earthly man to be subject to the heavenly man.

It is also notable that in Jacob’s blessing, Isaac calls upon the Lord and God; but here, he names none.

Esau or Edom, "the Red," representing red flesh and blood, cannot inherit the kingdom of heaven. Therefore, the spiritual man Jacob takes away the blessing of the firstbirth, whose primary part consists in the heavenly dew of grace, and leaves to the former primarily the earthly element of the visible world, in which the ungodly often fare better and more prosperously than the pious. However, when the same person turns to the heavenly Isaac through true repentance and unfeigned tears of penance, he will also come to a share of the blessing and inheritance of Jacob, and enjoy the dew of heaven with him. Therefore, this follows afterward and stands last in the blessing of Esau.

<column-break/>

41. And Esau bore a grudge against Jacob because of the blessing with which his father had blessed him; and Esau said in his heart: "The days will soon approach when one will mourn for my father; then I will slay my brother Jacob."

42. Then the words of her elder son Esau were told to Rebecca; and she sent and called Jacob, her younger son, and said to him: "Behold, your brother Esau comforts himself concerning you, that he intends to slay you."

43. "And now, my son, obey my voice, and get up, flee to my brother Laban in Haran."

44. "And stay with him a few days, until your brother’s fury turns away;"

45. "Until your brother’s fury turns from you, and he forgets what you have done to him: then I will send for you and have you brought from there. Why should I be deprived of you both at once in one day?"

46. And

---

From this, Esau’s unholy mind becomes clear; he not only married unbelieving women against his parents' will, causing them much grief, but also envied the good that God's providence turned toward his brother. Like a Cain, he burned with a bitter spirit of wrath against his brother, intending to slay him after his father’s death. Thus, God’s rejection is always just, occurring because of a person's evil nature and works, especially when a person tries to force God’s grace—to "defy" God for it, so to speak—and envies others when they can truly boast and rejoice in God's grace. By this, worldly men show that they belong to the "seed of the serpent," who was a murderer from the beginning, and they tend to hate and show hostility toward the pious as the "seed of the woman." See John 8:40, 44.

The privilege which **contemplative souls** <note>Those focused on inward spiritual life and stillness.</note> have over **active ones** <note>Those focused on outward works and religious labor.</note> awakens the envy of the latter; as they, being unable to see the former preferred over them, stir up persecution. This is precisely the true sign that such souls seek themselves in their spiritual labors and do not take only God’s benefit to heart.

But Love shows here its true heavenly wisdom by separating these two brothers because of the difference in their ways. These two ways can indeed exist together when they are united in one person with the submission that God ordains for the best. But they can hardly get along in different persons who do not walk on the same path: because the multiplicity and the hot zeal of **active men** cannot tolerate the simplicity and the stillness of the **contemplative ones**.

It often happens that the **active life** <note>The "active life" refers to a lifestyle of outward service and good works.</note> connects itself with the carnal and sensory life. When one cannot mix prayer with action, one usually goes to work in a very carnal and natural way: and such people are sometimes much more dangerously sunken into their own nature than the clearly manifest sinners. Love—as the mother of both the active and the **contemplative life** <note>The "contemplative life" refers to a life focused on inner prayer and stillness.</note>—laments over this connection, which causes her an exceedingly great pain; it weakens her so much in the soul she possesses that she gradually loses her life over it. Therefore she says: *I am weary of living.* As if she were saying: "I am near my ruin in this soul, because I cannot endure this unhappy mixture."

He renewed and confirmed to this, his younger son, the right of the firstborn given by God—the blessing he had previously given him unknowingly. If you proceed in this way, you will be blessed with a thousandfold blessing and a pure, fruitful offspring."

**Malice of nature** also uses the delights of the spirit for its own ruin, and it is unbelievable how far its plague spreads when it mixes into spiritual things. It is quite different here than in the first souls <note>Referring to those in the beginning stages of spiritual life.</note>. This is why Love cries out: "If Jacob (who is the contemplative soul) unites himself with nature to bring forth works of the flesh and the spirit—which are impure fruits—then I no longer wish to live." It is certain that spiritual people who become carnal again extinguish the life of love more and in a more cruel way than the greatest sinners and imperfect souls do. ## 6. Now when Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to Padan-aram in Syria to take a wife from there; and that as he blessed him, he gave him a charge, saying, "You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan";
<margin>Hosea 12:12.</margin>
## 7. And that Jacob had obeyed his father and his mother and was gone to Padan-aram in Syria;
## 8. And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father;
## 9. Then went Esau unto Ishmael, and took Mahalath the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham’s son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife, in addition to the wives he already had.

---

It appears that Esau did this to some extent to please his father and to reconcile with him by taking a wife from the daughters of Ishmael. These were of a similar nature and way of life to himself, and as the saying goes, "like seeks like." However, he does not consider whether he might be offending God with this **polygamy** <note>original: "Vielweiberey"; the practice of having multiple wives simultaneously.</note>. In this way, natural men—those acting only on their human impulses—never find the right path to truly satisfy or reconcile themselves with God and the people they have offended. He should have demonstrated a reconciled heart toward his father's parents so that they might have called Jacob back home, as Rebecca had imagined. <margin>Chapter 27:45.</margin>

v. 9. **To Ishmael)** This means to the Ishmaelites, or the House of Ishmael, which was then ruled by the eldest brother, Nebajoth. For that Ishmael himself had already been dead for 14 years is proven by the chronology: Ishmael lived 137 years; <margin>Chapter 25:17.</margin> Isaac fathered Jacob and Esau in the 60th year of his life. Jacob went to Syria in the 77th year of his life. These years together make 137 years. But Ishmael was born 14 years before Isaac.

**Mahalath)** Who was also called Basemath, as seen in Chapter 36:3.

<column-break/>

## 10. And Jacob went out (*) from Beersheba, and went toward Haran. <margin>(a) John 16:23.</margin>
## 11. And...

---

God wished to reveal His kingdom and glory to Jacob; this could not happen at home amidst earthly things and comfortable days. Therefore, he had to travel into a foreign land and leave everything behind. Indeed:

Observe the condition Jacob was in when he became worthy to behold God and His angels. He had, after all, the assurance that he would one day be master of the house as the firstborn and inherit everything. And yet, in obedience, he left everything and went away stripped and poor, with only a staff.

This is a precious **model** <note>original: "Vorbild"; a type or prophetic pattern.</note> of how our soul, if it wishes to soar to God, must be torn away from all temporal things so that it may penetrate into God freely and unhindered!

This does not mean one must immediately throw everything away and run away physically; rather, we must withdraw our hearts, desires, and attachments from the vanishing essence of this world, even while the "outer man" remains in his external calling, station, or trade.

If we are truly earnest about lifting or soaring our heart to God, we must first think about what we must lay aside so that we are properly fit for the task.

He who wishes to climb high must not have a heavy burden around his neck; otherwise, he makes it difficult or impossible for himself.

Now, everything earthly and transitory is such a leaden weight upon our soul, which does not allow the spirit to rise but always drags it down and bends it toward the earth. The heavy clod of the earth naturally keeps the heart imprisoned in low and trivial things, like a stone tied to the foot of a bird so that it cannot use its wings.

Let everyone judge for themselves whether it is not highly necessary to cast off the burden of earthly desires above all things, and to make the heart empty and free so that it can fly up to God unhindered.

God wants our love, delight, and pleasure for Himself alone. If we are to give these to Him, we must necessarily withdraw them from the earthly and learn to become **pilgrims** <note>original: "Pilgrime"; here used spiritually to mean someone whose true home is in heaven, not on earth.</note> in our hearts, even while we still live in the world.

This truly requires attention and struggle! One must keep as sharp an eye on one’s heart as one would on a thief; for at every moment, it wants to steal the love intended for dear God and give it to a creature. Everything else also lies in wait for us, seeking to capture our mental faculties and flood them with vanity.

Yet the Holy Spirit is so faithful that He constantly draws people inward and seeks to lure them away from earthliness. In this, God uses various means, especially all kinds of tribulations, through which vanity is made loathsome, disgusting, or bitter to us, so that we do not easily touch it with pleasure again or encumber ourselves with it.

Scarcely had Jacob received the blessing from his father—that he should be the rightful heir and lord in his father’s house—when adversity arrived in heaps. He had to wander into **misery** <note>original: "Elend"; in older German, this word specifically refers to being "out of the land" or in exile, as well as being in a state of distress.</note> away from his brother’s wrath and persecution at his parents' command. It appeared as though all the great promises and blessings would now fall into a well and be lost.

What a clear picture this is of the state of the "newborn babes" in the spirit! Scarcely do they gain access to the promises of grace and blessing in Christ, when they are informed by the Father Himself and His Spirit that they must leave the house of the "Old Adam" with their hearts and become pilgrims on earth. This is because the world and its prince pursue them, seeking to rob them of their barely-begun spiritual life.

Meanwhile, in all such lessons, there is this precious advantage: that everything is intended for the salvation of our souls. God thus turns away the great wrath of the dragon or the "hellish Esau" from us—precisely so that we can later inherit the blessing and not perish in the bloom of our conversion. For this purpose, many a glimpse of God's grace must strengthen His children.

Had Jacob not been alone and forsaken in a foreign land, he might not have been so capable of receiving God’s great demonstrations of grace. And:

If we do not allow ourselves to be made lonely in spirit and separated from worldly vanities, we will not taste how friendly the Lord is. For two kinds of kingdoms cannot rule in one heart: the earthly and the heavenly, Christ and **Mammon** <note>A biblical term for wealth or material greed personified as a false god.</note>.

We should think diligently on this, especially during prayer: that we do not first gather a heart full of vanities and follies and then expect to lift that heart to God. How is it possible to find or reach God and His light then? Such people remain far from the eternal Good, even if they chatter away from prayer books and heap up God’s wrath.

In such a manner, one will never behold God. For that is granted only to pure souls who quiet their hearts before God and thus approach Him with a collected and cleared spirit.

<header>Chapter XXVIII. The First Book of Moses.</header>

### 11. And he came upon a certain place, and stayed there all night, because the sun was set; and he took of the stones of that place, and put them for his pillows, and lay down in that place to sleep.

---

**Stayed there all night)** The soul that is in love with God and united with Him finds nothing that can disturb its rest in Him. Its running does not hinder its rest, nor does its resting hinder its journey. Jacob stops along the way and makes his night camp there. He takes the stones of the place and puts them under his head; among them, he chooses one specifically for his pillow. This stone, however, signifies Jesus Christ, his only support. He sleeps quite peacefully upon the earth, because it was the promised land of rest and <term>contemplation</term> <note>original: "Beschaulichkeit"; a state of deep spiritual focus or meditative prayer</note> for his spiritual lineage—namely, for all contemplative souls who would rather sleep on this earth, even though it is hard, than anywhere else.

Such have always been the children of so holy a father, as they said through David (a): *How can we sing the Lord’s song in a foreign land?* How should we be able to rest in a life of many distractions, we who are born for the unity and rest of contemplation?

Jacob falls asleep and enters into an ecstasy after the sun has set. The <term>overpowering grace</term> <note>original: "Übermach"</note> that leads a soul into the pure divine light comes only through the extinguishing of natural light; that which has been acquired through human effort must give way to that which is to be poured in by God.

**Took of the stones — put them for his pillows)** It is noteworthy how the great patriarchs, who are to be regarded as princes, managed with such meager and poor means on their journey. By this, they shame and rebuke the pomp and the grand <term>entourages</term> <note>original: "Depesen"; referring to the elaborate baggage and official ceremony of travelers</note> that are customarily made during the travels of great lords, or even by private individuals.

**Lay down in that place to sleep)** And thus, in the simplest manner, just as he found it, he desired no luxury or softness for his flesh. And in this mindset and conduct, God shared Himself with him.

Jacob slept on the earth and had a stone for a pillow; and precisely then was he deemed worthy to see a vision that was superhuman—so writes an ancient teacher (b) regarding this, as he exhorts us to moderation in sleep.

If we wish to enjoy the gracious visitation of God, then simplicity and self-denial must be, as it were, our pillow, not luxury and disorder. We must learn to be content with what is there, just as Jacob adapted to all poverty, even though he was the son of a rich man.

Wisdom governs her lovers in an innocent, unaffected way of life, where one enjoys God's gifts only according to necessity, and not for excess or splendor, which comes from the Fall.

A hard stone is often the best pillow. That is: when we do not treat our flesh tenderly and foolishly, or let it idle in the bed of luxury and self-love, we are the quickest to wake up and carry out God's command.

We must let our senses and own desires rest and not let them keep the upper hand if we wish to enjoy God.

Especially when a person feels a longing and impulse to deal with God in prayer and good meditations; there, the outer man with the earthly senses and distractions should rightly submit and become as if sleeping or dead, so that the spirit can soar all the more freely. For amidst the noise of foreign and coarse thoughts and images, God and His truth cannot be rightly recognized, much less the mysteries of His kingdom.

<column-break/>

### 12. And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder

---

->**Ladder**<-

We shall find occasion to speak of dreams at another time; but for now, let us direct our eyes toward Jacob’s

**Ladder)** There is so much to be said of this ladder that we shall already make the beginning here.

God let him, as it were, catch a glimpse of Paradise here in his solitude and pilgrimage: just as God sometimes knows how to refresh His own in such adversities—even in prisons and other sorrowful places—with such lovely revelations, and to truly open heaven in their hearts.

God must present spiritual, heavenly things to us with images, otherwise we would not understand them at all.

According to the consensus of all ancient Christian interpreters, it is certain—as Luther also notes—that the mystery of the <term>Incarnation</term> <note>original: "Menschwerdung"; God becoming human</note> of the Son of God was prefigured herein. For the Savior Himself applied it to Himself and His presence in humanity in John 1:51.

Yes, truly, it is none other than the eternal Reconciler of God and men, who reconciles, unites, and brings together the earth with heaven, the Creator with His creatures; who is emphatically this ladder, who was on earth according to the flesh, and in heaven according to His divinity; and thus in heaven and on earth at the same time. John 3:13.

Thus, this image points to the almighty, eternal, essential Word of the Father, Jesus Christ; how the same would also outwardly surrender Himself into our human nature and assume it, and thus bring our human nature back into the heavenly nature, and reunite the earth with heaven; beyond which no greater condescension has happened or ever will happen.

Furthermore, through the ladder, this vision represents this eternal Word, Jesus Christ, as He fills heaven and earth in His glorified state in an invisible way, reaching from one end to the other; as He who binds and unites all things again with one another and with God. Wisdom 18:16.

There is no doubt that this ladder finally aims at and points to the eternal unity and communion of the new earth with heaven, which the Lord will create in the revelation of His glory, when He will restore the first purity and harmony or communion of the lower world with the upper, according to so many clear promises in the Holy Scriptures. There, then, without any doubt, will be a closer and clearer communion of the saints with the angels.

The matter is therefore certain enough in itself: that Jesus Christ is the true way to God. John 14:6.

But the question remains: where should a longing soul find this ladder, this way and access to God? For there are very dangerous errors regarding this most necessary matter, whereby many remain far from God all their lives.

How easy, how near, how short the way to God is to be found! You need only turn into your heart, need only seek God and His kingdom in the interior; thus you find it. External things are good guides to Christ, but Christ Himself is the true Jacob’s ladder to the Father: and He primarily wants to be found inwardly in the heart; internally He also wants to show and teach us the way itself.

Everything that announces itself in your heart as lovely charms toward prayer, toward true obedience of the spirit, toward a longing for the eternal and a disdain for the world; that is truly from the true light of Jesus Christ. There, His Spirit shows you, as it were, one rung of grace after another, how you should gradually let yourself be led up to the true fatherland.

---

Sleeping on the journey signifies resting from the love of temporal things during the passage of this life, and closing the eyes of the mind to the pleasure of visible things during the course of fleeting days: so says Gregory the Great (c) very beautifully.

Oh, this is as necessary to a spiritual pilgrim as daily bread! One will also notice that the Spirit of discipline works unceasingly toward this, and that one has no rest in his heart where he involves himself in earthly things while yet wishing to seek God. God necessarily withdraws from such hearts that let themselves be tossed about by the waves of earthly belly-cares and lusts. In the still waters of the heart alone can God reflect Himself as a light.

# The First Book of Moses. Chapter XXVIII.

6. Now when Esau saw that Isaac had blessed Jacob, and sent him away to Padan in Syria <note>original: "Padan in Syrien"; commonly known as Padan-aram</note> to take a wife from there; and that as he blessed him, he gave him a charge, saying: You shall not take a wife from the daughters of Canaan;
7. And that Jacob had obeyed his father and his mother, and was gone to Padan in Syria; <margin>Hosea 12:12</margin>
8. And Esau seeing that the daughters of Canaan pleased his father Isaac poorly:
9. Then Esau went to Ishmael, and took Mahalath, the daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son, the sister of Nebajoth, to be his wife in addition to the wives he had.

---

It appears Esau did this to please his father to some extent, hoping to reconcile with him by taking a wife from Ishmael's daughters—one who was of the same nature and way of life as himself, since like-minded people gladly associate with their own kind. However, he does not consider whether he offends GOD with this <term>polygamy</term> <note>original: "Vielweiberey"</note>. In this way, natural-minded people never find the right path to truly satisfy and reconcile themselves with GOD and the people they have offended. He should have demonstrated a reconciled heart toward Jacob to his parents, so that they might have called Jacob back home, as Rebekah had imagined. (Chapter 27:45).

**verse 9. To Ishmael)** That is, to the Ishmaelites, or the house of Ishmael, which the eldest brother Nebajoth then ruled. For that Ishmael himself had already been dead for 14 years at that time is proven by the <term>chronology</term> <note>original: "Zeit-Rechnung"</note> as follows: Ishmael lived 137 years (Chapter 25:17). Isaac fathered Jacob and Esau in the 60th year of his age. Jacob went to Syria in the 77th year of his age. These years together make 137 years. But Ishmael was born 14 years before Isaac.

**Mahalath)** Who was also called Basemath, as seen in Chapter 36:3.

<column-break/>

10. And Jacob went out (a) from Beersheba, and traveled toward Haran. <margin>(a) John 16:28</margin>
11. And

GOD wanted to reveal His kingdom and glory to Jacob: this could not happen at home amidst earthly things and during easy days. Therefore, he had to travel into foreign lands and leave everything behind. Indeed:

Consider the condition of Jacob in which he became worthy to behold GOD and His angels. He already had the assurance that he should one day be master of the house as the firstborn and inherit everything; and yet, in obedience, he left it all and went away destitute and poor with only a staff.

He is a precious model of how our soul, if it wishes to soar to GOD, must be torn loose from all temporal things so that it may penetrate into GOD, free and unhindered!

This does not mean one must immediately throw everything away and run away externally; rather, we must withdraw our hearts, desires, and attachments from the vanishing essence of this world, even if the outer person remains in their external calling, station, or trade.

If it is our true earnest desire to lift or swing our hearts up to GOD, then we must think above all else of what we must first cast off so that we are properly fit for it.

Whoever wishes to climb high must not have a heavy burden upon their neck; otherwise, they make it difficult or impossible for themselves.

Now, everything earthly and transitory is such a lead-heavy burden upon our souls, which does not allow the mind to rise but always pulls it down and bows it toward the earth. The heavy clod of earth naturally holds the heart captive in low and trivial things, like a stone tied to a bird's foot so that it cannot use its wings.

Let each person judge for themselves whether it is not highly necessary to cast off the burden of earthly desires above all things and to make the heart empty and free, so that it may fly up to GOD unhindered.

GOD wants to have our love, delight, and pleasure for Himself alone. If we are to give these to Him, we must necessarily withdraw them from the earthly and learn in our hearts to become pilgrims, even while we still live in the world.

This truly requires attention and struggle! One must keep as sharp an eye on one’s heart as on a thief, for every moment it seeks to steal its love from the dear GOD and give it to a creature. Everything else also lies in wait for us, seeking to capture our mental powers and flood them with vanity.

Yet the Holy Spirit is so faithful that He constantly draws people inward and seeks to lure them away from earthliness. In this, GOD uses various means, primarily all kinds of tribulations, through which vanity is made loathsome, disgusting, or bitter to us, so that we do not easily touch it again with pleasure or drape ourselves in it.

Hardly had Jacob received the blessing from his father—that he should be the rightful heir and lord in his father's house—when adversity immediately arrived in heaps. He had to wander into misery at his parents' command to escape his brother's wrath and persecution; thus, it appeared as though all the great promises and blessings would now <term>fail entirely</term> <note>original: "in Brunnen fallen"; literally "fall into the well," an idiom for coming to nothing</note>.

What a clear image this is of the state of "newborn babes" in the spirit! Hardly do they gain access to the promises of grace and blessings in Christ before they are informed by the Father Himself and His Spirit that they must depart from the house of the "Old Adam" with their hearts and become pilgrims on earth—because the world and its prince pursue them and want to rob them of the spiritual life they have barely begun.

Meanwhile, in all such lessons, there is this precious advantage: that everything is intended for the salvation of our souls. GOD thus turns the great wrath of the dragon or the "hellish Esau" away from us specifically so that we can inherit the blessing afterward and not perish in the bloom of our conversion. For this reason, many a "glimpse of grace" must strengthen GOD's children.

If Jacob had not been alone and forsaken in a foreign land, he might not have become so capable of receiving GOD's great demonstrations of grace. And:

If we do not allow ourselves to become solitary in our minds and separated from worldly vanities, we will not taste how friendly the Lord is. Because two kinds of kingdoms cannot rule in one heart: the earthly and the heavenly, Christ and Mammon.

May we think diligently upon this, especially during prayer: that we do not first gather a heart so full of vanities and follies and then expect to lift that heart to GOD. How is it possible to find or reach GOD and His light then? Such people remain far from the eternal Good, even if they constantly babble from prayer books and heap up GOD's wrath.

In such a manner, one will never behold GOD. For that is granted only to pure souls who quiet their hearts before GOD and thus approach GOD with a collected and cleared spirit.

# Ch. XXVIII. The First Book of Moses.

### 11. And he came upon a certain place, and stayed there overnight; for the sun had set. And he took one of the stones of that place, and put it at his head, and lay down in that same place to sleep.

**Stayed there overnight)** The soul that is in love with and thus united with its GOD finds nothing that can disturb it in its rest in Him. Its running does not prevent its rest, nor does its resting prevent its wandering. Jacob stops along the way and makes his night quarters there. He takes stones there and puts them under his head; among them, he especially chooses one to be his head-pillow. This stone, however, signifies JESUS Christ, his only support. He sleeps quite peacefully upon the earth because it was the promised earth of rest and <term>contemplation</term> <note>original: "Beschaulickeit"</note> for his spiritual lineage: namely, for all contemplative souls who would rather sleep upon this earth, even if it is hard, than anywhere else.

Of such a kind were always the children of such a holy father, in that they said through David (a): **How can we sing the LORD's song in a foreign land?** How should we be able to rest in a multi-faceted life <note>original: "vermannigfaltigten Leben"; referring to a life distracted by many worldly cares</note>, we who are born for the unity and the rest of contemplation?

Jacob falls asleep and enters into an ecstasy after the setting of the sun. The abundance that leads a soul into the pure divine light comes only through the extinguishing of the natural light; and that which has been acquired must make room for that which is to be poured in.

**Took of the stones — put at his head)** It is noteworthy how the great Patriarchs, who were to be regarded as princes, managed so poorly and meagerly on their travels: thereby shaming and punishing the pomp and the great expenses that are usually made during the travels of great lords, or even by private individuals.

**Lay down in that same place to sleep)** and thus in the simplest way, just as he found it; he desired no luxury or softness for his flesh. And in this mindset and conduct, GOD communicated Himself to him.

Jacob slept on the earth and had a stone for a head-pillow; and just then he was deemed worthy to see a vision that was superhuman: so writes an ancient teacher (b) regarding this, when he exhorts toward moderation in sleep.

If we wish to enjoy the gracious visitation of GOD, then simplicity and self-denial must be, as it were, our rest-pillow, not luxury and disorder. We must learn to be content with what is there: just as Jacob adjusted himself to all poverty, even though he was the son of a rich man.

Wisdom governs her lovers in an innocent, unaffected way of life, where one enjoys the gifts of GOD only according to necessity, and not for excess or splendor, which comes from the Fall.

A hard stone is often the best rest-pillow. That is: if we do not treat our flesh tenderly and foolishly, or let it idle in the bed of luxury and self-love, then we are quickest to wake up and carry out GOD's command.

We must let our senses and own desires rest and let nothing keep the upper hand if we wish to enjoy GOD.

Especially where a person finds a longing and impulse to deal with GOD in prayer and good meditations; there the outer man with the earthly senses and distractions should rightly succumb and become as if sleeping or dead, so that the spirit can soar all the more freely. For amidst the noise of foreign and coarse thoughts and images, one cannot rightly know GOD and His truth, much less the mysteries of His kingdom.

To sleep on the journey means to rest from the love of temporal things during the passage of this life, and to close the eyes of the mind to the pleasure of visible things during the course of the fleeting days: as Gregory the Great (c) says very beautifully.

Oh, this is as necessary to a spiritual pilgrim as daily bread! One will also notice that the spirit of discipline works incessantly toward this, and that one has no rest in his heart where one involves oneself in the earthly and yet wishes to seek GOD. GOD necessarily withdraws Himself from such hearts that let themselves be driven about by the waves of earthly belly-cares and lusts. In the still waters of the heart alone can GOD reflect Himself as a light.

Wisdom governs her lovers in an innocent, unaffected way of life, where one enjoys the gifts of GOD only according to necessity, and not for excess or splendor, which comes from the Fall.

A hard stone is often the best resting-pillow. That is: when we do not treat our flesh tenderly and foolishly, or let it grow lazy in the bed of luxury and self-love, we are the quickest to wake up and carry out GOD's command.

We must let our senses and own desires rest and not let them have the upper hand if we wish to enjoy GOD.

In particular, where a person finds a longing and impulse to deal with GOD in prayer and good meditations, there the outer man with the earthly senses and distractions should rightly succumb and become as if sleeping or dead, so that the spirit can soar all the more freely. For amidst the noise of foreign and coarse thoughts and images, nothing of GOD and His truth can be rightly recognized, much less the mysteries of His kingdom.

<margin>(c) Gregory the Great, *Moral Reflections on Job*, Book V, ch. 22, p. 420. Vol. II of his works.</margin>
**To sleep on the journey** signifies resting from the love of temporal things during the passage of this life, and closing the eyes of the mind to the pleasure of visible things during the running of these fleeting days: as Gregory the Great (c) says very beautifully.

Oh, this is as necessary for a spiritual pilgrim as daily bread! One will also notice that the Spirit of discipline works ceaselessly toward this, and that one has no peace in one's heart if one involves oneself in earthly things while still wishing to seek GOD. GOD necessarily withdraws from such hearts that let themselves be tossed about by the waves of earthly worldly cares and lusts. GOD can only be reflected as a light in the still waters of the heart.

<column-break/>

12. And he dreamed, and behold, a ladder

->Ladder<-

We will find occasion to speak of dreams at another time; but for now, we want to fix our eyes on Jacob’s
**Ladder)** There is so much to say about this ladder that we shall make a beginning here.

GOD let him, as it were, catch a glimpse of Paradise in this his solitude and pilgrimage: just as GOD knows how to refresh His own in such adversities, even in prisons and other sorrowful places, with such lovely revelations, and to truly open heaven in their hearts.

GOD must present spiritual, heavenly matters to us with images; otherwise, we would not understand them at all.

According to the consensus of all ancient Christian interpreters, it is certain—as Luther also notes—that the mystery of the Incarnation <note>the "becoming human"</note> of the Son of GOD was foreshadowed here. For even the Savior Himself applied it to Himself and His presence in humanity in John 1:51.

Yes, truly, it is none other than the eternal Reconciler of GOD and men, who reconciles, unites, and brings together the earth with heaven, and the Creator with His creatures; He who is emphatically this ladder, who was on earth according to the flesh, and in heaven according to His divinity; and thus in heaven and on earth at the same time. John 3:13.

Thus, this image points to the almighty, eternal, essential Word of the Father, Jesus Christ, and how that same Word would also manifest outwardly in our human nature and take it upon Himself, and thus bring our human nature back into the heavenly being, and reunite the earth with heaven again; than which no greater condescension has ever happened or will ever happen.

Furthermore, through the ladder, this vision represents this eternal Word, Jesus Christ, as He, in His glorified state, invisibly fills heaven and earth and reaches from one end to the other; as that which connects and unites all things again with one another and with GOD. Wisdom 18:16.

There is no doubt that this ladder ultimately aims at and points to that unity and communion of the new earth with heaven, which the Lord will create in the revelation of His glory, when He will restore the original purity and harmony or communion of the lower world with the upper one, according to so many clear promises in the Holy Scriptures. Then, without any doubt, there will also be a closer and clearer communion of the saints with the angels.

The matter is therefore certain enough in itself: that Jesus Christ is the true way to GOD. John 14:6.

But the question now remains: where should an eager soul find this ladder, this way and access to GOD? For there are very dangerous errors regarding this most necessary matter, through which many remain far from GOD all their lives.

How easy, how near, how short the way to GOD is to be found! You only need to turn into your heart; you only need to seek GOD and His kingdom within; then you will find it. External things are good guides to Christ, but Christ Himself is the true Jacob’s Ladder to the Father; and He primarily wants to be found inwardly in the heart; inwardly He also wants to show and teach us the way itself.

Everything that manifests in your heart as lovely enticements to prayer, to true obedience of the spirit, to the longing for the eternal and the disdain of the world—that is truly from the true light, Jesus Christ. There His Spirit shows you, as it were, one rung of grace after another, how you should gradually let yourself be led up to the true fatherland.

The First Book of Moses. Ch. XXVIII.

# The ladder was set up on the earth / and 
# its top touched the heavens (a)

<margin>(a) Matthew 6:10. Ephesians 1:10.</margin>

Oh, how near this divine heavenly ladder often stands before and at your heart! How blessed it is for your soul if you make use of what you notice of the divine pull and impulse within you! Eternal life is hidden in every step!

Just let your longing be open to the Holy Spirit, and hasten out from all things with your mind: what does it matter—you will find heaven opened within you in Christ, which sin had once locked shut! For where GOD is, there is His heaven: and where heaven is, there is GOD. If GOD is now in you, then you also have His heaven in your heart.

Oh, if only one learned to believe how simple and straight the way to GOD is, and how near the Kingdom of God always is to everyone: oh, how one would hold fast to Him with joy and experience that He is not a GOD of the far distance!

But how does it work with this ladder? Namely, the soul must let all evil go and long for the true light: thus, in such longing, it receives an opening of the Kingdom of Heaven in its heart and a divine pull toward grace, so that it now expects all good from GOD, and thus in faith is led by the hand <note>German: *gehandleiter*, a metaphor for being guided step-by-step as if by a railing or a steadying hand.</note> toward grace. Romans 5:2.

Do you see now the true Jacob’s Ladder? Is that not the access to the Father of which the first Christians testified? And can you not find this in your heart?

So, this one thing remains the most necessary: to constantly long for Jesus, to turn oneself into Him and His holy name, to seek, ask, and take everything in Him, to think of Jesus without ceasing, and to let Jesus become all in all within oneself.

Whoever turns to this holy Jacob’s Ladder in faith in the Son of GOD truly finds heaven with its whole host coming toward them, which is the joy of the angels in heaven over such a repentant sinner.

Just as a high ladder is not climbed without difficulty, so the entire way of Christianity is such a long and heavy heavenly ladder that must be reached and climbed over amidst many struggles and tribulations. Especially since the corrupted flesh, which still clings to us, always wants to pull back with its heaviness from the ascending desire for heaven. Meanwhile, we are lured to such an ascent even in the midst of the greatest affliction, just as Jacob was deemed worthy of such a glorious vision in the midst of his <term>exilio<note>Latin: exile; referring to Jacob's flight from his brother Esau.</note></term>.

And so we also rightly understand the ascent and how it happens. Namely, as heaven and the way to it are inward and spiritual, so must the ascent also be; so that our thoughts and desires need not first turn toward some foreign or far-distant place, but rather that one gathers oneself with all one's strength in one's heart, or withdraws the senses and all desires and thoughts from everything else, so that they do not wander from Christ: thus one ascends inwardly to GOD.

But how difficult and tedious this is to the ungodly mind of the "old man" <note>A biblical term referring to the unregenerate, sinful nature of a person before spiritual transformation.</note>, common words and works demonstrate. As soon as one hears of drawing near or having fellowship with GOD, one gapes upward toward the external sky and the stars, and depicts the eternal divine Being to oneself and others as an idol locked up in heaven. One wants to have Him from the outside in, though He is already in the heart and everywhere, indeed filling all things.

Hopefully it is understood well enough for our daily practice if we note that it is nothing other than the pure, living hunger of faith for GOD.

As many divine fruits as faith produces in its own, so many steps are, as it were, to be seen on such a heavenly ladder. For everything that God's Spirit works draws and pulls us into His kingdom; and indeed, the longer the deeper, the more the more hidden.

Bernard <note>referring to St. Bernard of Clairvaux (1090–1153), a Cistercian abbot and influential mystic.</note> (b) names four kinds of steps. 1) To the heart, in which one learns to fear GOD: 2) in the heart, where one perceives Him as a counselor: 3) from the heart, where He is sought as a bridegroom: 4) above the heart, where one contemplates. But who wants to set a goal or number for such ways and leadings

<column-break/>

# and behold the angels of GOD ascended 
# and descended on it. Book of Wisdom 10:10.

13. And

of GOD, how He leads His own into Himself? His ways are inexpressible, and even he who experiences them cannot think them out. It is and remains a hidden mystery of the Kingdom of GOD, which is given to be known in reality and power only to those who love Him, but to others only in parables.

Who, for example, can express even the single way of humiliation that GOD walks with a single soul? How many and varied steps are found there? How wonderfully GOD plays with some! And though it seems to go more and more into humiliation and nothingness with Him, these are actually nothing but steps toward exaltation. That may well be called a reverse and wondrous ladder, where the steps bring one down and yet lead upward.

The Lord Jesus Himself entered into His glory on this strange ladder of humiliation, and now He lures us all upon it after Him. Blessed is he who faithfully follows Him and thus, against all reason, climbs and reaches glory! The deeper it goes downward with our "old Adam," the more certainly we ascend with Christ and reign with him over all enemies. We will then not regret His labor, no matter how bitter it may have become for us. After the arduous ascent to our first fatherland follows eternal rest.

Oh, how sweet it may be when the true heavenly ladder, Jesus Christ, is present in the final struggle of death—just as He was for Jacob in the dark night—and shows the poor tired soul the right path out of this lower world into the upper kingdom of peace! How joyfully one may then fully ascend from one step of grace to another into the very heart of God the Father!

Where the inward kingdom of GOD and Christ is opened to us, together with the beautiful paradise that Christ has won; it makes us forget all sorrow even here, all earthly things become dung <note>original: *Koth*, literally "excrement" or "mud," used here in the Pauline sense (Phil 3:8) to describe things of no value compared to Christ.</note> in our eyes, and the spirit rests alone in its origin. How should we then not apply all our strength to it! Blessed is he who is daily found before GOD therein, knocking and seeking, until the entrance into the eternal kingdom is abundantly provided to him! There it is then good to rest.

Therefore, let one practice in time the ascending and lifting up of his heart to the perfect light in his heart; seek and use that as his constant guide, and hold steadfastly to the rungs and steps of the holy discipline and leading of the Holy Spirit: thus at the end of faith one will find heaven open with all its blessedness.

**The angels of GOD)** That these allowed themselves to be seen there is a very singular and lovely representation of how, through Christ’s merit, the believers are also brought back into the fellowship of the angels, and that the angelic and heavenly powers, which were closed by the Fall, should again be opened and become useful in the minds of those who are "born from above." This, however, can only be known and enjoyed through experience.

And we may recognize how the access to the heavenly kingdom and its citizens shall not remain barred to us, but that converts and believers can even here already come and be in the company of many thousands of angels; and that thus the entire heavenly court stands open to faith, and will be opened even more in the future, the more gloriously Christ is acknowledged in His glory.

**Ascended and descended on it)** This angelic ascending and descending undoubtedly contains a great mystery within it, and shows particularly the activity of these holy spirits which they demonstrate in the restoration of the creatures. For this reason, they have also desired to look into the incarnation of Jesus and to lower themselves to it: just as they, on the other hand, also ascend to the contemplation, worship, and praise of GOD. Thus they also carry our prayers and alms or good works up before GOD, and from Him down to us new grace and new light from above.

To see the angels ascending and descending means to contemplate the citizens of the upper fatherland, with what great love they cling to their origin by ascending above themselves; and with what compassionate love they have lowered themselves to our weakness: so says Gregory the Great <term>Gregorius M.<note>Latin: *Gregorius Magnus*, refers to Pope Gregory I (c. 540–604 AD), known for his writings on the spiritual life.</note></term>.

## 13. And behold, the **Lord** stood upon it / and spoke: **I am the Lord / the God of Abraham your father / and the God of Isaac; the land whereon you lie / I will give to you and to your seed.**

<margin>Jacob took such a promise so faithfully into his heart / that he later repeated it to Joseph on his deathbed / and strengthened him therewith. ch. 48:4.</margin>
the **Lord** stood upon it) This ladder / which with its uppermost part serves as a place of rest for **God** / indicates the steps / that one must climb / in order to attain rest in **God** Himself through the rest of contemplation <term>Beschaulichkeit: a state of quiet, prayerful meditation</term>. The distance between is great. Yet even angelic souls climb up and down: because the steps / by which one climbs up / often become steps for climbing down / both in appearance and in truth. To such a soul / however / all things are equal; as it can draw an excellent benefit from this / namely by leaving everything that concerns it to **God**. The highest peak of this ladder is in Heaven / in **God** Himself. Just as a ladder is of no more use to one who has already climbed as high as he desired / so these steps / which represent the various means for climbing up and down to **God** / cease / as soon as one has come to Him Himself.

But should He / who supports the whole world and sustains it through His mighty arm / be able to lean on anything? Yes, certainly. For since He has His pleasure in those souls who have attained to a perfect rest and to the last step of their origin / which is **God** / through the loss of all means and through a total annihilation <note>original: "Vernichtung" – a mystical term for the emptying of the self/ego to make room for God</note> / to rest; why should **God** not also rest with pleasure in a soul / that rests in nothing but Him? This is called resting in Himself: because such a soul possesses nothing outside of Him.

There are indeed precious enough things / which happened to Jacob and his successors in and through the fellowship of angels: but it is not yet the best and highest thing. Angelic powers / radiance / and joy / are still far from being divine. For they ascend and descend / and are still subject to change and decrease.

But this is the greatest bliss / that **God** Himself shows Himself on the path and ascent to the heavenly life and invites everyone / whoever wants to have Him.

To that end, He stands at the top of the heavenly ladder / and thereby gives clear assurance / how He is ready / out of undisguised love to descend with His benefits and powers as if on a ladder to the wretched and fallen / and to step into their misery.

The **Lord** stood at the top of the ladder / that He might reach His hands to the weary / and might incite those ascending to labor with His gaze. Therefore the place is called **Bethel** or **God’s House** <note>Hebrew: *Beth-El*</note> / in which one daily climbs up and down. Sinners indeed reach the previous step again / when they [wash away their filth with tears].

Just as one who wants to help another who has fallen into the mud must himself go down into the mud / and thus save him; so **God** in Christ lets Himself so willingly into all our misery / and seeks thereby to help us out with power.

For thus this mystery-filled ladder also teaches us / that **God** leaned upon the uppermost part / so that / just as souls / after they went out from Him through creation / come to the earth of an impure life upon the rungs of this descent; so also / in order to reach Him again / they must climb back up the path on which they went down. These thoughts have moved many full of mystery <term>Geheimnißreiche: mystics or those seeking hidden spiritual truths</term> to say / that / if the soul wished to attain again to a true unity in **God** / it must first have come back into the pure state of its creation. This is to be understood as the loss of all stains and self-interest. Through this ladder it is very well expressed / since / when one wants to go back to **God** / one must climb back up the same steps / which one climbed down during the fall from the same: which is also quite natural.

The **God** of Abraham and the **God** of Isaac) That true **God** / who formerly gave and essentially communicated Himself to Abraham and Isaac as their **God** and Good / from whom they perfectly obtained everything / that could make them blessed and favored in time and eternity.

Oh, what a highly precious and worthy word of assurance lies herein / that the eternal Good / essential Love / **God** Himself / wants to communicate and give Himself to all those / who fix their eye of faith upon Him / and wait for Him!

The land --- will I give -- to you) **God’s** condescension extends even to physical things for all those who receive the same precious faith with Jacob.

Yes, certainly this is also a blessing to the children of **God** / and works together for their best / when their necessity casts no anxious care or torment upon them in the true service of the Spirit. Therefore one should not think lightly of it / where one can serve the **Lord** without distraction amidst the circumstances of the other: as the patriarchs applied it to their greatest advantage and growth. For since **God** promised it to them / it must certainly have been something good; because **God** can and will give nothing but good.

<column-break/>

## 14. And your seed shall be as the dust of the earth / and you shall break forth toward the West and toward the East / and toward the North and toward the South : and in you shall all the families of the earth be blessed / and in **your seed.** ch. 22:18.

## 15. And

As the dust) The phrase / the dust of the earth / can be understood both according to the quantity and the quality of this people. According to the number, **God** promises / that it should become so numerous / that this people should be found in all places / and that converted people would dwell everywhere. Which has certainly come to pass / and is and will remain eternally true. For there is no place / in which such a person is not to be found. According to their nature / they are such annihilated souls / that they are turned into the dust of their nothingness. Therefore the Scripture does not say: they shall be increased as much as the dust / or even more. For that would only express the exceedingly great number. Rather it says; like the dust: which represents their annihilation very well.

In you -- and in your seed) In the seed as the cause and source of the blessing; in Jacob / and so also in Abraham and Isaac / but as in a model and example / in whose footsteps all believers should tread.

This serves for all those who hunger for Christ according to the true ground of faith as a blessed assurance / how the merciful Creator has lowered Himself to us in the most loving way in the mystery-filled incarnation of His Son / in which **God’s** kindness and love for humanity is perfectly displayed.

Truly this is the most wonderful descent of the whole love of **God** / which has so graciously visited us in our fall / and now still works around us daily / to reunite us with His eternal kingdom / and to receive us therein as citizens of heaven.

This may have comforted the good Jacob most powerfully on his difficult pilgrim’s journey: because he felt well the misery of the fallen creature. And it is still that which refreshes and supports such souls / who are weary of this misery and their impurity / and long for something eternal.

To such, Christ’s condescension is an infinite ground of comfort / that this eternal Good / which once clothed itself in our poor flesh and blood / still daily lets itself down / and wants to be with us / and to help us out of all misery ever more. What can be more joyful / if one only hears it with faith? How much more blessed is it / where one experiences it daily!

For holy people may fall / if they become negligent: and sinners reach the former step again / if they wash away their filth with tears. <margin>Jerome.</margin>

-># The First Book of Moses, Ch. XXVIII.<-

15. **And behold, I am with you / and will keep you everywhere you go / and will bring you back into this land. For I will not leave you / until I have done that which I have spoken to you.**

I am with you!) Oh, what a most binding and gracious assurance!

God's Holy Spirit still makes such promises alive in times of need for those who believe in His name / and who, like Jacob, cling to Him alone.

It can powerfully strengthen and awaken faith when the Holy Spirit can make the heart certain that God wants to be so near / so intimate / so communal with us / as with His friends / who have and may take every right / every claim / to His love in faith / just as a child relies on his father who is present / or a subject relies on his mighty protector.

It is certainly an incomparably sweet thing when God is with someone; upon this, it is entirely safe and blessed to place all confidence.

Whoever knows God as eternal life / as essential joy / peace, and blessedness; he may also know the happiness of a soul with / by / and in whom this eternal Good resides.

Whoever has God with him truly and without deception / has everything with and by him that can calm, purify, and make him blessed. His soul need desire nothing that he should not find essentially and perfectly / as well as constantly and eternally. For there is nothing but communicativeness and expansion in the good God / who gives Himself and His life as gladly as a mother gives milk to her child.

How joyfully / how comforted one can walk through this evil world when it can truly and fundamentally be said: The Lord is with me! How David dared to stand against all enemies with this! <margin>Ps. 118 / 6 7.</margin>

<column-break/>

16. **Now when Jacob awoke from his sleep / he spoke:**

Not that he should not have known of God's omnipresence: Rather, because such souls who stand at this level are so swallowed up in peace and unity / and faith leads them so purely / that they possess God without thinking about it / and without having any conscious knowledge of it / except for occasional moments in which He reveals Himself a little; which is as if they were waking up again from a very deep sleep. Faith and <term>Gelassenheit: a state of yieldedness or letting go of self-will</term> make them blind; just as the sun blinds one when looking at it: so that they can distinguish nothing of Him. It is like when one lives in the air and inhales it without thinking about it / both that one lives in it and that one draws it into oneself: because one does not pay attention to it. Although such souls are entirely permeated by God / they do not think of it: because God hides from them what they are. Therefore, these ways are called "mysterious ways" / which means incomprehensible and secret.

But God is so gracious / according to the beautiful example in the text / and convinces us through His actual trials how near He and His heaven are to us / when He lets us feel and perceive such things in a certain way.

But one must first wake up / as Jacob <margin>Eph. 5/14</margin> awoke from his sleep: that is / to become sober from all foreign and ungodly things / which hinder God's holy communication. For such people who remain drowned in their affects and desires can certainly not perceive divine grace / so that no truth finds a place with them.

---

**will keep you**) God's protection on the way was indispensable to him in his current state; in which he traveled all alone in the midst of the heathens' land toward unknown people / and did not know how things would go for him further.

Even if we do not hover in exactly the same external uncertainty / we are nevertheless not out of danger. What external accidents may happen to a person in an instant! And moreover, our soul has enough distress and pursuit from so many enemies on this short pilgrimage in the midst of the land of the heathens / or on the corrupted earth among evil people.

Whoever does not believe or know his danger may yet be poorly converted. For in conversion, God opens the eyes so that one gradually perceives his dangers and enemies.

When the various dangers become apparent to a cautioned soul / it might well perish from fear / did it not learn to know a sufficient protection and refuge. But then God's preservation from within and without is dear and precious to us / once we have been in the claws of the enemies a few times / or at least have experienced their threats / like Jacob from Esau. Then the promise of God is so sweet to us / and we see that He did not give it to us out of boredom.

But it is a great pleasure to the dear Father in heaven when we trust Him in this. He very gladly points all the faint-hearted, fearful, and weak to His guarding heart / wherein He protects and watches / always striving for us / so that we lack nothing.

Though Jacob must flee from Esau / his physical brother; he nevertheless has **JESUS Christ** / the firstborn among many brothers / as a companion / who lets him feel His presence both in waking and sleeping / and still graciously reveals Himself to His own when they must flee from Esau. As He also shows through the words:

**will keep you /— and bring you back)** shows that it is He who leads the souls entrusted to Him in all their ways: until He leads them back into Himself / as the place of their origin. For that is the true Land of Promise / the true Rest of Canaan / into which **JESUS** wants to bring us back if we entrust ourselves to His faithful guidance.

And what is more blessed than experiencing this? It is truly nothing but eternal life / which regenerates man and makes him heavenly-minded. For **JESUS** / the heart and life of the Father / has come to make us divine again. Whoever follows Him daily dies to the earthly life / and daily keeps his ascension with **JESUS Christ** / and thus fulfills the will of the Son / who wants us to be where He is / and to be translated with Him into the heavenly being.

Oh, well for those who soar up to Christ with their whole heart and mind! They shall find Him as they desire Him.

**I will not leave you!**) Oh, the invaluable faithfulness of God and His Son! For His love does not allow Him to leave us; He will not let us go until He has perfectly blessed us. Let one learn to look into the heart of the dear Savior / how it burns with desire for our blessing / how deeply He bows and holds to us!

In times of need / especially the final one / this may well be the only lasting ground of true rest and contentment. Then it may be a most precious jewel / if a soul has well-trodden Jacob's path of faith in life / and has since torn itself away from the earthly with all its strength.

If one is faithful in small things / one comes to greater things / and in due time climbs with Jacob after all purifications to the summit / where one inherits everything when one has left everything.

One should only follow the **Lord** / who still calls down to His own from the top of the ladder / that they should not grow weary / but should climb after Him with fresh vigor.

<meta>This page continues the spiritual commentary on Genesis 28, specifically focusing on Jacob's reaction after waking from his vision of the ladder and receiving God's promise of protection.</meta>

Chapter XXVIII. The First Book of Moses. 179

# "Surely the **LORD** (a) is in this place / and I knew it not!"
<margin>(a) Acts 16:10. Revelation 21:3.</margin>

-> 17. And <-

---

**Surely the Lord is in this place!) God** allows believers to sense His loving presence in a certain spiritual way / so that they are divinely assured of it.

**The Lord)** After all those blessings with which the **Lord** had overwhelmed **Jacob** / **Jacob** did not look at the blessings / much less at himself; but at the **Lord** / the author of them.

<margin>(a) <note>original: "Serm. 6. in Dedic. Eccl."</note> Sermon 6 on the Dedication of a Church.</margin>
**In this place)** Although **God** is in all places / it is nonetheless said specifically; *Our Father / who art in the heavens;* because He manifests His presence there differently and in a special manner. Among the wicked, He is present as long-suffering and punishing; among the elect, as active and helping; among the saints, as nourishing and resting; etc. Where He rests, there He is as a bridegroom. So says **Bernard** (a) regarding this text. <note>Saint Bernard of Clairvaux (1090–1153) was a highly influential mystic and abbot.</note>

**I knew it not)** All people well know that **God**, in His infinite essence, is present everywhere. For this is written into the heart alongside the natural knowledge of **God**. Even if atheists and <term>Epicureans</term> <note>Followers of Epicurus; here used as a label for those who live for worldly pleasure and deny divine providence.</note> wish to deny it through their deeds / their own conscience secretly contradicts them / and convicts them of **God’s** omnipresence.

But that **God** is present in a particular way among the generation of the godly with His love, favor, and power / essentially and effectively; to this belongs a faith / which the **Holy Spirit** works. To such an extent / that even believers must often remind and awaken themselves in such faith. This is also the meaning here regarding **Jacob**.

We must look upon good **Jacob** here as a poor refugee / who was stuck in great distress / because he had to travel into a foreign land to escape his brother. In such anxiety, he did not know / that the **Lord** was so near to him according to His special presence. Therefore, he here sincerely confessed his ignorance and faint-heartedness.

Oh, if only one could learn great honesty from this dear man / so that we also might gladly confess our lack of experience / wherever we find it in ourselves regarding this or that spiritual ground of truth! He admitted it so confidently / that he had not known or so considered and taken to heart **God’s** presence for his comfort. And that was no shame to him / but a great help toward further enlightenment.

**Surely it is no shame for the oldest person /** if he recognizes and confesses his blindness regarding the kingdom of **God**. But it is a shame before **GOD** and His own / if someone wishes to learn nothing further / but out of pride acts / as if he already knew everything / as if one should not tell him / because he is too learned / too old / too noble / for that, etc.

Many people are not well instructed in their youth. For many, it would have turned out better / if they had had the opportunity. Therefore, no one should be ashamed to confess: I did not know this or that; I did not understand that better.

What we know of **God** is, in any case, the least of it. We must learn every day from the wisdom of **God** / and yet we will likely always remain students.

It is good then / to stand firm in faith through the **Holy Spirit** in one's heart against all future trials and attacks / believing that **God** is always incomprehensibly near to us with His love as with His heaven. It will certainly be necessary / that one learns to practice this point quite diligently / so that one may be rooted and grounded deeply enough in **God’s** present light: in order to endure / when storms of physical and spiritual distress rise up against it. For

The old serpent / who seeks to seduce the whole world / not only keeps the blind and unhappy minds in common idolatry / so that they do not want to know **God’s** presence / and diligently shut their eyes to it: their language is; *There is no God:* and; *God does not see it:* thinking / like ignorant children / that if they only cover their eyes so that no one sees them / then they are not seen either. Rather, he also often seeks to darken the light in good souls regarding this / and to lead them astray.

<column-break/>

It is impossible to say / how the enemy works against this / to make the soul doubt the grace-filled presence of **God**. And

It is certainly no small distress / when well-meaning souls in sudden sorrow do not know or cannot believe, like **Jacob** / that the **LORD** is also in their place. They think: **God** is only with this or that person / who does not suffer so; but from them He has departed far away.

<margin>Isaiah 49:14.</margin>
This is where all the complaints about **God’s** abandonment lead. *Isaiah 49:14.*

Whoever now wishes to ward off or even overcome such strong temptations: he truly needs / to diligently practice the ground of faith / how near **God** is to all who seek Him; and how, beyond His general presence / according to which He is also present to His enemies / He has promised a special grace-filled presence to His elect.

But it requires watching over one's own heart / so that one learns to practice what **Asaph** said in *Psalm 73:23.* This

Practice brings experience / so that one becomes more and more aware / how **God** is so near / in a way one had not previously known or recognized.

Just as **Jacob** confesses his faint-heartedness and lack of practice / so he recognizes, on the other hand, **God’s** faithfulness and constancy / who had not departed from him for even a moment. And with this, the knowledge of **God** grew greatly in him / so that in the future he learned to venture more upon his ever-present **God**; as his following life story proves.

Just as **Jacob** indeed knew of **God’s** presence before / but yet was not convinced of it with such certainty / until after this vision: So **God** gladly wants to lead us further and further in the knowledge of Him and in communion / so that we should grow more toward the power of the image of **God** / and thus toward the new birth / after the knowledge of the truth has once dawned within us.

**Gregory the Great**, where he shows / how those who begin to love and serve **God** / have not yet come to the contemplation of **God** / and are therefore only prepared for it little by little / speaks very emphatically of this matter (a) / that they finally notice through the experience of the internal vision / how they had not previously known whom they served. **Jacob** also could not doubt before his sleep / that **God** was there; because he well knew / that **God** is everywhere: but because he then learned to know Him even more perfectly / he said; previously he had not known it / as he had not recognized Him so precisely and intimately. He marveled at the form of the inner light / into which he was first received; and recognized through the experience of the revealed beauty / how much he had previously not known. For through faith we recognize **God** as if by a rumor: but through the love of contemplation / that which had previously been known to us only by rumor is revealed to us / as if through the discovery of His presence.

In truth, it is no different with souls / who are still inexperienced in the inward way to **God** and His kingdom. They often content themselves for a long time with knowing / that **God** is present everywhere. Indeed / when suffering begins / the heart can hardly believe / that He is near. When **God** then draws closer / and shows special signs of His loving presence; behold, it is then said: I did not know / that the **Lord** is with me. So precisely / so intimately / I have not yet experienced His near faithfulness.

Then one believes certainly and truly for the first time / what one otherwise only believed from hearsay / and had not yet experienced. Indeed

One should only believe certainly / that **God** confirms His near, friendly presence ever more through trials / if we only believe / that it is He / who speaks with us. According to His general Creator-presence, He will also offer Himself to us as a Redeemer / as a Friend / as a Counselor / indeed as everything in everything. One step always follows the other; and finally, He gives Himself to the soul as its bread, treasure, and life / to eat and to enjoy.

<margin>(a) <note>original: "L. II. Expos. in 1. Reg. c. 3. p. 77. Tom. I. Opp."</note> Book 2, Exposition on 1 Kings, Chapter 3, page 77, Volume 1 of the Works.</margin>
