<meta>This page continues the narrative of Genesis 48, where the aging patriarch Jacob (Israel) prepares to bless his grandsons, Ephraim and Manasseh. The previous page established Jacob’s intent to adopt these sons of Joseph as his own, placing them on equal footing with his eldest sons, Reuben and Simeon.</meta>

<header>Chapter XLVIII. The First Book of Moses.</header>

### 13. Then Joseph took them both, Ephraim in his right hand toward Israel’s left hand, and Manasseh in his left hand toward Israel’s right hand, and brought them near to him.

### 14. But Israel stretched out his right hand and laid it upon Ephraim’s (a) head, although he was the younger; and his left hand upon Manasseh’s head: he guided his hands knowingly, even though Manasseh was the firstborn.
<margin>(a) Jeremiah 31:9.</margin>

### 15. And he blessed Joseph, and said:

v. 14. Here we read of the first instance of the **laying on of hands**, a ceremony which was thereafter used in various acts; specifically, as seen here for a blessing, but also for the imparting of other divine gifts and the commissioning of persons into important offices. See Deuteronomy 34:9, Numbers 8:10, Matthew 19:13, Acts 8:17, etc. Such customs may certainly be imitated in simplicity for edification, but they must not be misused in a superstitious manner, as if the gifts were imparted solely through the physical act itself. <note>The author cautions against "sacramentalism"—the belief that the physical gesture has power independent of God's will.</note>

Through this laying on of Jacob's hands, God showed once again how, for holy and wise reasons, He often places the elder below the younger and prefers the latter over the former: as with Cain and Abel, Japheth and Shem, Haran and Abraham, Ishmael and Isaac, Esau and Jacob, and others besides, such as Moses, David, and Solomon, who were also among the youngest. By this, God wishes to show that man should not claim any privilege by nature—or by any kind of gift—as his own property or use it to exalt himself. Otherwise, for holy and hidden reasons, God can very quickly prefer others who are lesser, or who do not possess such privileges and gifts. See Matthew 19:30.

The crossing of the hands which Israel performed was thus not without **mystery**. He gave the right of the firstborn to the lesser state: because the closer we draw to God, the more childlike we must become; and the greater we are in our own eyes and the eyes of men, the smaller we are before God. Therefore, Jacob said through the prophetic spirit that the smaller shall be preferred over the larger. And Jesus Christ Himself (a) frequently held this before us.
<margin>(a) Matthew 18:3, 5 and Chapter 19:13, 14.</margin>

This laying on of Jacob's hands thus occurred **crosswise**. The foundation of all blessing is in the crucified Jesus. This was quite beautifully prefigured among the ancient Hebrews, where the High Priest was anointed with holy oil on his forehead in the form of a cross. <note>This is a common "typological" interpretation, where Old Testament events are seen as symbols or "types" of New Testament truths—in this case, the shape of Jacob's crossed arms representing the Cross.</note>

v. 15. **He blessed Joseph**) Just as Jacob did not give his blessing to his eldest sons first, but rather to Joseph, the younger, as the most obedient and pleasing: so we must also take care that we do not forfeit or diminish the primary right of blessing as Esau and Jacob’s [other] sons did. For

even if one occasionally gains a temporal blessing from it, as Jacob's sons did, the Eternal Father might nevertheless be moved to give the preference—and at the same time a greater blessing—to others who have pleased Him better through faith and obedience; whereas those who act as recklessly as Simeon and Levi might find the blessing disregarded.

<column-break/>

### The God, before whose face my fathers, Abraham and Isaac, constantly walked; the God, who has shepherded me from my beginning until this day; 16.

In these words, Jacob expresses that the most **Holy Trinity** is and remains the sole and perfect origin of all blessing and goodness; as is also witnessed in other places by the threefold repetition. Numbers 6:23. <note>Early modern commentators often looked for "hints" of the Trinity in the Old Testament, such as whenever God is mentioned three times in a row.</note>

Thus Jacob, out of a living enjoyment [of God], praises the eternal God and Father as the **fountain of blessing**, who has not only revealed Himself to him but has truly shared Himself with him.

First, this fountain must make itself known to a soul before it can share itself. For an unknown thing cannot be enjoyed with benefit. And who can draw water from a well that he neither sees nor knows?

So Jacob presupposed this: that he and his fathers had first recognized God in a living way; and specifically as He had revealed Himself to them. For it is a very special description of God’s powerful revelation when he says:

**The God before or in whose face my fathers constantly walked**) Whoever is to walk in God’s face and presence must necessarily have become aware of such a face. In the true foundation, this happens when God allows faith to experience His gracious presence; which in the Scripture is called His "countenance," by which one can know God and become aware of how near and good He is to us. Psalm 67:2.

In this bright-shining face and light of the Father, Jacob walked with his fathers, just as the Lord Himself desired. Chapter 17:1. And

Dear reader, why did Jacob here name the Eternal Father in no other way than by His countenance, in which one must walk? Was he not looking thereby at the voluntary **obedience of faith**, in which Abraham and Isaac were entirely at one with God’s will, and thus walked in a divine harmony with His Spirit? Into this will, united with God, Jacob also turned his own will, which is the power of the entire New Covenant, and thus the fountain of blessing in the **Messiah**.

Oh, how this should spur everyone to seek the Lord’s face more zealously and constantly than before! Especially since God’s Spirit places it so easily before us and testifies throughout the entire Scripture how near the divine light is to everyone, and how it only depends on whether we are willing to turn the "face" of our mind toward this Face or not. For

the fact that God’s presence is seldom—or only weakly—noticed and enjoyed is the fault of man’s fluttering mind, which, like an unstable bird, is always wandering off and will not remain unshifted in the right dwelling. But if we wish to have God’s friendly face, and therein His eternal blessing, we must learn with the Patriarchs to walk constantly before God, and to remain standing in His present light in holy awe and reverence even in all our doing and leaving.

In this way, and no other, can the Eternal Father truly communicate Himself in His blessing, as the godly Jacob further praises Him, having experienced it in a divine walk, describing Him as a communicating fountain:

**The God who has sheperded me etc.**) He places the communication of the blessing in "shepherding," and looks partly to God’s physical provision, but partly and primarily to the internal shepherding of his immortal part [the soul].

---

It is certainly also a precious blessing to a believer when he can take his temporal necessities from God’s hand in faith. Thus, in physical preservation, unspeakable wonders of God occur; but these are not esteemed because they happen daily and seem insignificant to proud reason.

One also rarely recognizes with Jacob that God nourishes and shepherds us "until this day"; instead, one thinks one must provide for oneself, and thereby falls into ungodly pride and idolatry.

Yet, this was not the true primary blessing for Jacob; rather, one sees from his manifold tribulations that God always made the creaturely world distasteful and bitter to him, in order to make him long for something more permanent.

And who would doubt this, when one considers how thirstily the good ancestors—feeling the weight of the Fall and the Curse—longed for the perfect blessing in the Messiah? As those who, in the light of the Spirit, knew very well what great salvation was intended for them in Christ.

Thus they also became partakers of such promises through faith, as they waited for the Redeemer. And in this eternal comfort of the Gospel, whoever wishes may be even more deeply strengthened, if he learns from Jacob’s words that this fountain of blessing is in the Son of the Father—for which reason, and no other, he refers to the "redeeming Angel."

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Genesis 48, specifically focusing on verse 16, where Jacob invokes "the Angel" to bless his grandsons. The previous page discussed the ritual of the laying on of hands and God’s tendency to favor the younger over the elder.</meta>

<header>The First Book of Moses. Ch. XLVIII.</header>

# 16. The Angel <gloss>(a)</gloss> who has redeemed me from all evil: bless the boys; and let my name be named upon them, and the name of my fathers, Abraham and Isaac; and let them increase like fish into a multitude in the midst of the land.
<margin>(a) Job 33:23, 24.</margin>
<margin>17. Then</margin>

---

**The Angel who has redeemed me)** Here Jacob expressly names him with the proper title of the Messiah: his <term>Goel</term> <note>Hebrew: *Go’el*, a kinsman-redeemer who protects and vindicates family members.</note>, his Redeemer; and indeed a Redeemer

**From all evil)** This universal work of redemption, which spreads over everything, cannot possibly be attributed to a created angel or spirit in such absolute terms. Furthermore, the Scripture primarily and properly attributes this title to the only Savior: Exodus 3:8, Isaiah 63:9, Hosea 13:14, Job 19:25, etc. Indeed—

Jacob designates this Angel in the Hebrew as a specific Person with a distinct demonstrative particle. 

It is this very Angel—the one who had guided him, tested him, and called him until now (Chapter 30:11, 13; 32:24)—whom he invokes. And indeed—

This invocation for a blessing can apply to no one other than the Son of God, because both God Himself and this Angel are petitioned for the blessing simultaneously and with equal reverence and worship. Therefore, he cannot be an ordinary angel. Otherwise, Jacob would have distinguished him from the Deity itself with some specific sign.

These reasons are neither invented nor forced; they are found in the clear words of the text, and therefore they can provide a more certain conviction of the Savior's glory. Even some of the Jewish commentators admit something of this.

The early Christians also had no doubt about this. "Scripture does not fail," says **Tertullian** <gloss>(a)</gloss>, "to call an Angel 'God' and God an 'Angel'." For when Jacob wished to bless the sons of Joseph, Ephraim and Manasseh, he spoke—having placed his hands crosswise upon their heads: "God who has fed me," etc. But then he places that same Angel, whom he had called God, at the very end of his speech to name the Person of whom he spoke, saying: "May he bless the boys." For if he had intended a different, created angel, he would have included two persons in the plural number. But now, he uses the singular number for one person in the blessing, wishing it to be understood that God and the Angel are one.

The ancient fathers also point out a fine reason why Christ is called an "Angel" (or Messenger). Namely, it refers to his prophetic office of teaching, by virtue of which he proclaims all the counsel of the Father from His bosom and thus glorifies the Father in the hearts of believers. <gloss>(b)</gloss>

And certainly, this has its precious foundation in the matter itself and in lived experience. For is He not always such a great Envoy and "Angel of Counsel," who, as the eternal Word, reveals Himself with the Father to His own, and makes known to them the Scripture and the entire will of God? Who can rightly understand or enjoy even the smallest part of their salvation without Him?

Is He not also the only Redeemer, of whom Jacob could boast with such divine certainty that He leaves no evil behind from which He does not truly redeem him?

But what do we think Jacob considered to be "true evil"? Was it perhaps merely temporal inconveniences, shame, or physical loss? Or was it not rather all the fruits of the Fall, which he still felt within himself from original sin with misery and pain? Ah, indeed, like Paul, he considered that the worst evil, and rejoiced in faith that such a great and perfect Savior was given to him by the Father against it—of whom he could say in full hope: "The Lord will deliver me from every evil work and preserve me for His heavenly kingdom!" (2 Timothy 4:18).

<note>(a) original Latin: *Lib. de Trinit. c. 27. p. 740.* (Tertullian's *On the Trinity*). Also see Cyril of Alexandria, *Thesaurus*, Assert. 12, p. 116, and *Glaphyra in Genesis*, p. 210. Athanasius, *Orations against the Arians*, 4, p. 464, Vol I.</note>
<note>(b) original Latin: *Gregor. Nyff. Orat. XI. adv. Eunom. p. 699. T. II.* (Gregory of Nyssa, *Against Eunomius*).</note>

<column-break/>

Observe with wonder how the essential blessing of Christ consists precisely in this work of redemption! For the curse rests upon sin, as a transgression of the law. Whoever takes away the curse is necessarily also a fountain or source of blessing. And this is the blessing that God has spread over all the nations on earth.

One must strive earnestly for this faith, so that this Fountain of Blessing may well up with pure salvation and blessing for all who thirst for it, and so that He may still be worshiped in everyone’s heart. As often as we feel the Father drawing our heart toward Christ, it is as Peter spoke to the Jews <gloss>(a)</gloss>: "God has sent His servant Jesus (as a messenger or Angel) to bless you, in turning every one of you from your iniquities." There one sees in what manner and in what order Christ wishes to redeem and bless us: namely, in that we turn ourselves away from the iniquities that brought the curse upon us. This is the true power and fruit of redemption from all evil: when we cast out from the soul through faith (which purifies the heart) that which brought the curse upon us.

To the extent that the Lord Jesus overcomes evil within us, His redemption becomes powerful in us. And by this, everyone can notice whether and how much blessing they have from Christ. Life and deeds must prove it. We must become aware in ourselves whether we are becoming free of the curse, one after another, or not—just as a prisoner realizes he is free by the falling away of his chains.

May the Spirit of Christ open everyone’s eyes to seek and perceive this infinite blessing of redemption! Oh, that especially those whose hearts are heavy with sin might learn to look constantly upon this great Angel of Redemption, who was so eagerly embraced by the ancients and drunk from as the purest source of God's love!

**Bless)** All of God’s blessing is a creative word, which He speaks so that it happens, and commands so that it stands fast.

But the Creator speaks and makes everything through the Spirit or breath of His mouth: not only in the first creation, but also in preservation.

Where the Spirit of blessing finds suitable vessels of grace, He pours Himself into them all the more richly, however few of them there may be in the world.

It follows naturally that our heart, mouth, and everything will overflow with that which fills it; and that only those who are themselves blessed of the Lord are fit to bless others and share a blessing out of their own fullness.

If we wish our springs to flow out into the streets, according to the Spirit's command, then our own fountain must first be blessed (Proverbs 5:16, etc.).

This should then powerfully bind us to draw in the pure breath of God into our souls with persistent thirst of faith, as from a pure source. For—

Herein lies our well-being or woe: what kind of vessels or hearts this Fountain of Blessing finds in us—whether they stay still for the influence of His Spirit, whether they make themselves pure and ready, and allow themselves to be cleared of all "foreign waters" or not.

**That my name be named in them)** By this he does not only mean that they should remember his faith in the true God, who gave him the name "Israel" from the true God, to constantly remember the glorious struggle with God (who wishes to be overcome through the prayer of His own and moved to share the blessing; see Isaiah 14:1, Jeremiah 14:9); but also that they themselves should be counted as part of Israel.

<note>(a) Acts 3:26.</note>

<header>Chapter XLVIII. The First Book of Moses.</header>

17. Then, when Joseph saw that his father laid his right hand upon Ephraim’s head, it displeased him; and he took hold of his father’s hand to remove it from Ephraim’s head onto Manasseh’s head.
18. And Joseph said to his father: Not so, my father! For this one is the firstborn <margin>(a) Gen. 25:33.</margin>. Lay your right hand upon his head.
19. But his father refused and said: I know it, my son, I know it! This one shall also become a people, and he also shall be great: but truly his younger brother shall be greater than he, and his seed shall become a multitude of nations.

<note>There is a great mystery hidden in the fact that Joseph so dearly wished to grant the birthright to Manasseh, while Jacob would not be moved. God intended to show that He would first choose a younger Ephraim from among the Gentiles <note>original: "Heyden"</note>, who would recognize the Messiah come in the flesh and be born of Him as His first son. Conversely, the elder Manasseh—representing the Jews—would, according to this name, "forget" their Savior and thus be placed behind, only reaching the knowledge of the Messiah at the very last. Yet, the Lord would also convert thousands from among them, just as ten thousands have been converted from the Gentiles. See Deuteronomy 33:17. This Kingdom of Christ, composed of Gentiles and Jews, will first increase greatly in "spiritual Egypt" and thereafter come into a mighty pressure, so that they might then truly turn in faith to the promised glorious Kingdom, to be led out and redeemed from this spiritual Egypt; then the "fullness of the Gentiles" shall enter, and "all Israel shall be saved"; to which the following blessing over the whole "Israel of God" among the 12 mystical tribes belongs.</note>

<note>In this act, Jacob did not look at the beginning, but at the end: who would remain steadfast until the end.</note>

<note>That an unchangeable earnestness is required to maintain this eternal blessing—which otherwise can be as easily spilled as precious water in a shaken vessel—is shown by the sad example of these two tribes of Israel, Ephraim and Manasseh.</note>

<column-break/>

20. So he blessed them on that day, saying: In you shall Israel bless themselves, saying; God make you like Ephraim and like Manasseh! And so he set Ephraim before Manasseh.
21. And Israel said to Joseph: Behold, I die, and God will be with you, and will bring you again into the land of your fathers.
22. Moreover, I have given to you one portion of land above your brothers, which I took out of the hand of the Amorites with my sword and with my bow.

<note>v. 20. Jacob here pronounced a precious blessing over them both; but how long did it last? Do not the prophets raise many laments over these tribes, regarding how shamefully Ephraim fell away from the Lord and was punished, and how one tribe envied and persecuted the other?</note>

<note>v. 22. The piece of land which Jacob bequeathed to Joseph in advance as a sign of special affection was the plot of ground he had bought from Shechem, Chapter 33:19. He later had to maintain this before God through his prayer and supplication—which were his "spiritual sword and bow," as it is also rendered by the oldest Chaldean translator <note>This refers to the Targum, an Aramaic paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible, which often interprets "sword and bow" as "prayer and petition."</note>. God protected him against the Amorites (by which name all the peoples of Canaan are called, Chapter 15:16) and let His terror fall upon these enemies so they did not harm him. Chapter 34:30, 35:5. Therefore, Joseph undoubtedly wished to be buried here. Joshua 24:32. The 70 interpreters <note>The Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament.</note> also expressly call this piece of land "Shechem."</note>

<note>Believers should learn from this how they ought to protect their bodies and goods against all adversaries: namely, with their prayer and supplication to GOD, so that His Word might be their sword and His power their bow; with which they might healthfully wound and overcome their enemies. See Psalm 18:33, 35, 36, etc.</note>

<note>Kingdoms and dominions should learn that the salvation of the Lord is the true walls and bulwarks. Isaiah 26:1. If they cannot take comfort in that, they will certainly be put to shame in the day of distress despite all their physical preparations.</note>

# Chapter XLIX.
->Jacob’s Prophecy and Death.<-

1. AND Jacob called his sons and said: Gather yourselves together, that I may tell you that which shall befall you in the last times!

<note>Jacob was driven by the Spirit of God to present and interpret the divine counsel to his sons: what would befall them at the "end of days" which God had appointed for the dispensation <term>dispensation: a divine ordering of worldly affairs</term> of the Old Testament. This dispensation was to take place among his physical seed, after which another dispensation of the New Testament would arise, wherein the spiritual seed—the "Israel of God" (Galatians 6:16)—would stand up. Under this, various events would occur in certain successions of time, which would mostly correspond with the mysterious names of the tribes. Therefore, one must seek these various events and their changes within the believers of the New Testament and apply these prophecies to them, as will become clear from the following explanations.</note>

<note>Thus Jacob also showed his sons that which was to happen regarding the inward Kingdom and the coming of Jesus Christ.</note>

<column-break/>

2. Gather yourselves together and hear, you sons of Jacob; and listen to your father Israel!
3. Now—

<note>v. 2. This entire prophecy is regarded by the Hebrews as a song.</note>

<note>It took place upon his deathbed, when it was undoubtedly his greatest earnestness to lay out the foundation of his faith to his children, and indeed before all people. Therefore, he necessarily spoke the mysteries of the truth of God with a complete foundation through the Holy Spirit and with great certainty.</note>

---

<note>But because Jacob himself gives us to understand that one must seek the fulfillment of his prophecy—according to verse 1—"In the last times," the opening of these prophecies in full knowledge will likely not be made known until the "time of refreshing" before the face of the Lord, when Jacob dwells securely in his descendants in the promised land.</note>

# The First Book of Moses. Chapter XLIX.

<margin>(a) Deuteronomy 21:17.</margin>
3. Reuben, you are my firstborn, my strength (a) and the beginning of my power, the most excellent in dignity and the most excellent in strength!

4. Because of your unstable mind, like water, you shall not have the preeminence! For you went up to your father's bed: then you defiled it; he went up to my couch.

Thus Reuben was deprived of the dignity and prestige due to him by his birthright, as well as the power flowing from it and the double portion of inheritance, because of the incest he committed, in which he gave free rein to his evil lusts and did not seek to restrain them. See 1 Chronicles 5:1-2. In a spiritual sense, he represents the Jews at the end of the days of the Old Testament, who indeed saw the "Son" in the flesh (according to the meaning of the word Reuben, "See, a son"), but would not believe in Him, as they had defiled themselves with spiritual incest through their alliances with the Romans; the accusation of which can be seen in more detail especially in Hosea 2:3-15. See also James 4:4 and Romans 9:24-26. Therefore, for the most part, they have been cast out from this birthright in the grace of God, and it has been given to the believers from among the Gentiles <note>original: "Heyden"</note>, whom God has accepted as the firstfruits of His grace under the New Testament. See Romans 15:9-12 and 16:4-5.

v. 3. **The beginning of my power)** Or also "of my sorrow and my care," over which I have had to grieve.

v. 4. **You shall not have the preeminence)** God does not ordain or measure the privilege of the birthright according to the physical and external birth of children, as we have already observed from several examples; rather, He bestows it upon the one who is worthy of it and who fits into God's order—one who recognizes the birthright in its true high nobility and holds it in high esteem and honor.

O, what an eternal and immeasurably important glory can be forfeited for a short-lived pleasure! It is also forfeited by many who consider the honor of the saints and the lot of the righteous as something small and insignificant.

Yet, whoever wishes to do so may! There are already others who will take with both hands what they reject! But—

O, how great is the loss of such a privilege! The damage is irreparable! It is in vain that Esau cries out loudly before his father!

Therefore, think, O human, of your Father and your Fatherland! Think of your nobility, how highly it is esteemed! How could you make the members of Christ into the members of a harlot? How could you fail to preserve the privilege that God intended and assigned for you!

**Father's bed -- defiled)** When he "went up," this occurred. And the holy marriage-bed of Christ, in which He lay with the first Christians, has also been soiled and contaminated with foreign teachings and impure human traditions, after men behaved loftily and a spiritual "Reubenite" and son of Christendom even set himself in Christ's place as a vicar.

<column-break/>

5. Simeon and Levi were brothers; their daggers were weapons of violence.

<margin>(a) Psalm 16:9.</margin>
6. Let my soul not enter into their counsel (a); let my honor not be united in their assembly! For in their anger they slew the man, and in their self-will they hamstrung the ox.

7. Cursed be their anger, for it is so fierce; and their wrath, for it has been so cruel! I will divide them in Jacob, and I will scatter them in Israel!

8. Judah

Simeon and Levi, who were also brothers in malice, had to hear their father's loathing of the bloodthirsty deed they committed against the Shechemites <note>See Genesis 34</note>, which Jacob had not yet forgotten! In a physical sense, it was meant to be avenged so that they would receive no special inheritance among the tribes in the land of Canaan: thus Simeon dwelt within the tribe of Judah, Joshua 19:1, whereby his hot-headedness and power were broken; and Levi, because of the priesthood, received no physical inheritance in the land. And although the priesthood was entrusted to them, the curse over their "counsel" manifested itself even in this dignity among their descendants, when the high priests, scribes, and elders—who may have been from both Levi and Simeon—assembled against Christ, Matthew 26:3-4, 57. For in their anger they slew "the man," the Lord <note>original: "den HErrn," referencing Genesis 4:1</note>, and "the ox"—namely He who presented Himself as a sacrifice—and they "hamstrung" Him by opening almost all of His veins of blood.

According to the hidden meaning, the two brothers represent the corrupted state of the Church and the Government when they unite. These two are of one mind against the truly godly and unite against them: just as the scribes and Pharisees united with Pilate against Christ, and as in the future final time the Antichristian Beast will unite with the False Prophet against the two witnesses and other confessors of Christ, just as they have united as a prelude against them in all past times.

These are also the wind and the waves, among which a wicked union arises as a prelude, creating a storm on the sea against Christ and His disciples in the ship. For the winds represent the false teachers and wicked clergy who stir up the waves of the sea—the civil authorities—and both then storm together against the little ship of Christ.

v. 5. **Weapons of violence)** The pen and tongue are also weapons of violence through books of shame and slanders.

v. 6. **Not in their assembly)** The Prince of Peace, Christ, who does not fight with fleshly weapons and who rules and bears the world with great forbearance, does not wish to "smell" <note>Meaning to take pleasure in or be present at</note> such communities where bloodthirsty counsels are held and executed; for He alone has the "quiet ones in the land" as His temple wherein He dwells.

**Hamstrung the ox)** Others translate this as "the walls" or "the foundation," meaning they tore it down.

v. 7. **Cursed be their anger and wrath)** The question arises: is a blessing pronounced here over these three sons of Jacob, as verse 28 says was done for all twelve? Answer: The curse is directed at the deeds, not the persons, as with Cain and his father, the serpent. Indeed, they were blessed in their descendants. Furthermore, verse 28 thoughtfully mentions the "tribes," not the "sons." And Levi received a special blessing later when he was very zealous against the makers and worshipers of the golden calf.

**Scatter in Israel)** So that they could instruct the people in the Law.

Therefore, many Hebrews believe that the teachers in the children's schools were from the tribe of Simeon, while the tribe of Levi was for the adults (a).

<header>Chapter XLIX. The First Book of Moses.</header>

<margin>(a) Colossians 2:15.</margin>
### 8. Judah, you are he! Your brothers shall praise you! Your hand shall be on the neck of your enemies (a)! Your father's sons shall bow down before you!

---

After Jacob had spoken of the fallen state of man and his corruption through his first three sons and tribes, he now begins to prophesy concerning the Kingdom of the Messiah.

While Jacob’s speeches seem to aim at the outward condition of this tribe, if one looks deeper into the mystery itself with an enlightened understanding, many wonders of the Lord Jesus open up within it, which are not easily exhausted.

To Judah is granted the dominion among all the tribes, and it was decreed that from him the Prince over them should be taken. 1 Chronicles 5:2. This began to find its fulfillment after the death of Joshua, when Judah was chosen by the Lord to lead the wars of the Lord; Judges 1:1,2. This was a great honor, through which Judah stepped into the place and dignity of the firstborn. This was fulfilled even further according to the letter with the subsequent kingdom established in David and his family. However, according to the spiritual sense, it is fulfilled in Christ, the Lord of David, who willed to be born from this tribe and the loins of David. In Him, the promise of the seed of Abraham—in whom all nations and families of the earth should be blessed—was to come to its full completion. Then all true Israelites and believers would laud and praise Him as the true Prince of Victory over the serpent, the enemy of Christ and all believers, whose head He would crush as the promised Seed of the Woman. Therefore, they would also bow before Him with humble adoration, which is due to Christ as the true God. See Psalm 45:12, 95:6, 97:7.

In the following verses, the actual nature of the time of His coming is clearly expressed, and the most prominent events that would happen with Christ are recounted. First, the kingdom in the family of David would cease; following that, the Jews would still retain their judges and lawgivers who would be born from among them—such as the kings of the Hasmoneans <note>The Hasmonean dynasty were leaders of the Jewish rebellion against the Seleucid Empire in the 2nd century BCE.</note> from the tribe of Levi, and finally the High Council <note>The Sanhedrin, the supreme judicial and religious body of the Jews.</note>, which was occupied by natural-born Jews. And though finally Herod, an Edomite <note>A descendant of Esau, rather than Jacob; thus an "outsider" king.</note>, and Pilate, a Roman, ruled over them, the High Council of High Priests and Elders still held authority over the Law, and were permitted to give laws and judge according to them. Then the time came that these too should cease and come to an end. But before this would happen, the true Peacemaker <note>German: "Friedenmacher," a translation of the Hebrew "Shiloh" in verse 10.</note> should come, who would bring about spiritual rest and the refreshing of souls, and finally also physical rest in His glorious kingdom. Regarding the former, see Matthew 11:29; regarding the latter, Hebrews 4:9, etc., Psalm 72, Isaiah 2:4, 11:5-9, 10, 54:13. After this, Jews and Gentiles, Scythians and barbarians, would finally long for Him, receive Him in faith, and obey Him. Regarding the Jews, see Malachi 3:1, which is to be understood of those among them who hoped for the Kingdom of God: Luke 2:25. Regarding the Gentiles, Haggai 2:8, where He is called the desire of all nations. And finally, regarding the wildest of peoples, see Psalm 68:32, Isaiah 66:19, Colossians 3:11.

**You are he)** You are the right man; it is granted to you by the grace of God that you shall be the forefather of the Messiah. He wishes to say, as it were: I have looked around here and there to see who among you all it would be. Thus I have found, through the reminder of the Holy Spirit, that it is you.

To Reuben, it was said through the spirit of prophecy that he would flow away like water; but to Judah, in whom Jesus Christ was enclosed as the Head of all who return to God, the assurance is given: his brothers—who represent godly but not yet spiritual men—should praise him. He shall rule in Jesus Christ over his enemies, who has annihilated everything. For truly spiritual souls possess no power of their own; all their strength stands in God alone.

<margin>(a) John 4:23.</margin>
**Your father's sons)** by which he, as it seems, wishes to distinguish him from his other brothers, indicates that he speaks of those souls entirely devoted to the supreme will of God, who are the true sons of Israel, who (a) will worship God in a service pleasing to Him. For these worshippers alone will [praise] Him in the—

<column-break/>

<margin>(a) Isaiah 29:1.</margin>
### 9. Judah is a young lion (a)! From the prey, my son, you have gone up! He has knelt down and couched as a lion, yes, like an old lion: who will rouse him up?

---

Just as in the physical kingdom of David, he first had to fight with all his enemies round about like a strong lion; but afterward, in his old age, and especially in the times of Solomon, he couched and settled into rest so that no nation dared to rise against Israel or disturb it in its rest: See 1 Kings 4:21, 25. So this has found its fulfillment especially in Christ's kingdom, who, as the Lion of the tribe of Judah (Revelation 5:5), must first fight in His Kingdom of the Cross against all His Antichristian enemies, until all of them are made a footstool for His feet in His glorious kingdom. Psalm 110.

This prophecy of Jacob over Judah sparkles like a bright gemstone, not only in this chapter but in the whole First Book of Moses, indeed in the entire Old Testament.

Moses recorded this over 400 years before its fulfillment, before a trace of a Jewish kingdom even existed. And when the time of fulfillment finally came, how wondrously did it begin! Saul became king from the tribe of Benjamin; yet he had to be removed first. Who would have thought then that a king from Judah should be taken from behind the sheep? And indeed after so many contrary troubles, without any human help or preparation? Did not everything happen to the end that this prophecy might be fulfilled in the tribe of Judah? Did not this Kingdom of Judah have to stand firm for over 400 years afterward, despite the rebellion of the 10 tribes, until the Babylonian captivity? And although many changes occurred afterward, the government as the Lawgiver was not allowed to vanish, but remained for 700 years with the Great Council until the times of Christ, who is the true Lion of God.

**The word Lion** indicates His strength. But he calls Judah a young lion to show that his strength is in his Father (in Jesus Christ) and in his nature. His Father is his Son, and his Son is his Father. It is the invincible Lion.

**From the prey you have gone up)** Because you have enclosed within yourself the blood of the Son of God, through whom everything, both heaven and earth, must be won.

But to show that he speaks of those who have returned to God, who take the prey because they remain victorious in all things, he interprets it thus: **My son)** in that you rest in a spiritual sleep, you have laid yourself down in God as a lion and lioness, who fear nothing; for they are full of courage and strength. For the lion rests confidently because of his strength; and this soul relies entirely on God, who is her strength. Therefore he adds: **Who would wake him up?** As if to say: Who would be so bold as to go where this soul is found? Could all of hell disturb the peace of a soul that stands in God in her permanent state?

This lying down can also be understood as the rest of the Word, which became flesh in Mary. For He laid Himself in her holy loins like a lion in his den.

Indeed, has not this young lion, the eternal Son, lowered Himself and submitted to all suffering and shame in human nature?

Just as the Spirit of God spoke to Samuel when he was moved by Him to anoint David as king by God's command: Arise and anoint him! For this is he.

# Chapter XLIX. The First Book of Moses.

### 8. Judah, you are the one! Your brothers will praise you! Your hand will be on the neck of your enemies <margin>(a) Colossians 2:15.</margin> (a)! Before you your father's sons will bow!

---

Therefore, they would also bow before Him with humble adoration, which is due to Christ as the true God. See Psalm 45:12, 95:6, 97:7.

In the following verses, the actual nature of the time of His coming is clearly expressed, and even the most prominent events that would occur regarding Christ are recounted. First, the kingdom in the family of David would cease; following that, the Jews would still retain their judges and lawgivers who would be born from among them, such as the kings from the Hasmoneans <note>The Hasmonean dynasty ruled Judea from c. 140 BC to 37 BC.</note> who were of the tribe of Levi, and finally the High Council <note>The Sanhedrin.</note>, which was occupied by natural-born Jews. And although finally Herod (an Edomite) and Pilate (a Roman) ruled over them, the High Council of the high priests and elders still held authority over the Law, and were permitted to give laws and judge according to them. Then the time came that these, too, should cease and come to an end. Before this happened, the true Peacemaker <note>A translation of "Shiloh," often interpreted in this era as "the one who brings peace."</note> was to come, who would bring about the spiritual rest and refreshment of souls, and finally also physical rest in His glorious kingdom. Regarding the former, see Matthew 11:29; and regarding the latter, Hebrews 4:9, etc., Psalm 72, Isaiah 2:4, 11:5–9, 10, 54:13. For Him, Jews and Gentiles, Scythians and barbarians <note>A reference to the list of nations in Colossians 3:11, representing the "wildest" or most distant peoples.</note> would finally long, and they would receive Him in faith and obey Him. Regarding the Jews, see Malachi 3:1, which is to be understood of those among them who hoped for the kingdom of God: Luke 2:25. Regarding the Gentiles, Haggai 2:8, where He is called the "Desire of all Nations." And finally, regarding the wildest peoples, see Psalm 68:32, Isaiah 66:19, Colossians 3:11.

**You are the one)** You are the right man; it is bestowed upon you by the grace of God that you shall be the forefather of the Messiah. He means to say, as it were: I have looked here and there to see who among you all it might be. Now, through the reminder of the Holy Spirit, I find that it is you.

To Reuben, it was said through the spirit of prophecy that he would flow away like water; but to Judah, in whom Jesus Christ—as the Head of all the "turned-in" <note>German: *Eingekehrten*. Refers to souls who have turned inward to focus on their spiritual life with God; a common Pietist term.</note>—was enclosed, the assurance is given that his brothers (representing godly but not yet spiritual people) should praise him; he shall rule in Jesus Christ over his enemies, He who has annihilated all things. For the truly spiritual souls possess no strength of their own; all their strength stands in God alone.

**Your father's sons)** By which, it seems, he wishes to distinguish him from his other brothers; it indicates that he speaks of those souls entirely devoted to the supreme will of God, who are the true sons of Israel, who will <margin>(a) John 4:23.</margin> (a) worship God in a service pleasing to Him.

<column-break/>

### 9. Judah is a young lion <margin>(a) Isaiah 29:1.</margin> (a)! From the prey, my son, you have gone up! He has knelt down and couched like a lion, yes, like an old lion: who will make him rise up?

---

Just as in the physical kingdom of David, he first had to struggle with all his enemies round about like a strong lion, but afterwards in his old age, and especially in the times of Solomon, he lay down and went to rest, so that no nation dared to rise up against Israel and disturb it in its rest (see 1 Kings 4:21, 25); so this has especially found its fulfillment in Christ's kingdom. He, as the Lion of the tribe of Judah (Revelation 5:5), must first struggle in His Kingdom of the Cross against all His anti-Christian enemies until all of them are made the footstool of His feet in His glorious kingdom. Psalm 110.

This prophecy of Jacob over Judah sparkles like a bright gemstone, not only in this chapter but in the entire First Book of Moses, and indeed in the entire Old Testament.

Moses recorded this over 400 years before its fulfillment, before a single trace of a Jewish kingdom existed. And when the time of fulfillment finally came, how wondrously it began! Saul became king from the tribe of Benjamin; yet he had to be cleared away first. Who would have thought then that a king from Judah should be taken from behind the sheep? And indeed, after so many adverse troubles, without any human help or arrangement? Did not everything happen to the end that this prophecy might be fulfilled in the tribe of Judah? Did not this kingdom of Judah thereafter have to stand firm for over 400 years, despite the defection of the ten tribes, until the Babylonian captivity? And although many changes occurred afterward, the government as the "Lawgiver" could not vanish, but remained for nearly 700 years with the Great Council until the times of Christ, who is the true Lion of God.

**The word Lion** indicates his strength. But he calls Judah a "young lion" to show that his power is in his Father (in Jesus Christ) and in his nature. His Father is his Son, and his Son is his Father. It is the invincible lion.

**From the prey you have gone up)** Because you have enclosed within you the blood of a God, through whom everything, both heaven and earth, must be won.

But to show that he speaks of the "turned-in" souls who take the prey because they retain the victory in all things, he interprets it thus: My son, while you rest in a spiritual sleep, you have laid yourself down in God as a lion and a lioness who fear nothing, in that they are full of courage and strength. For the lion rests confidently because of his strength; and this soul relies entirely on God, who is her strength. Therefore he adds: "Who would wake him up?" As if he would say: Who would be so bold as to go where this soul is found? Could all of hell disturb the rest of a soul that stands in God in her permanent state?

**This lying down** can also be understood of the rest of the Word, which became flesh in Mary. For He laid Himself in her holy loins, like a lion in his den.

Yes, has not this young lion, the eternal Son, lowered Himself and submitted Himself in human nature to all suffering and shame?

Just as the Spirit of God spoke to Samuel when he was moved by Him to anoint David as king by God's command: "Arise and anoint him! For this is he!"

# Chapter XLIX. The First Book of Moses.

### 10. The scepter shall not depart from Judah, nor a lawgiver from between his feet, until Shiloh comes (a); and to him shall the obedience of the peoples be.

<margin>(a) Hebrews 7:14.</margin>
<margin>II.</margin>

The scepter will always remain with his house; for in this state, he is the Lord of the entire world, as his kingdom exists in God alone. He possesses within himself the state of simplicity and unity—a whole kingdom—by possessing that inward peace which makes him master over the inclinations of his soul.

But when he who is to be sent arrives—which shall occur through the spiritual incarnation, where the Word is given in the state of transformation—then this kingdom shall be taken away again. For when a soul no longer possesses itself, Jesus Christ possesses everything within it; whereby all possessions and kingdoms are reunited in Him. He is also the one for whom the nations wait, and thus also those souls who are called to share in this happiness.

According to the literal sense and the common idiom of the Hebrews, this refers to the government, majesty, and dominion which the tribe of Judah received over the other tribes through David.

Such government always remained among the Jews until the time of Christ, even though they had not had a king for a long time before then. For the "scepter" does not merely signify a royal office, but generally a manner of government. This is seen in abundance from the addition in which Jacob explains himself:

<term>Nor a lawgiver</term> <note>original: "noch ein Gesez-Geber"</note>) Which can be understood as both spiritual and worldly government, but especially as the administration of justice in the Great Council <note>The Sanhedrin</note> at Jerusalem.

<term>That which comes from between his feet</term> <note>original: "Der zwischen seinen Füssen hervorgekommen"</note>) According to the modest expression of the Scriptures, this simply means one's descendants.

Accordingly, Jacob's clear meaning is this: the Jews should not completely and utterly lose their own government until the time of the Messiah arrives.

<term>Until</term> <note>original: "Bis daß"</note>) But when Shiloh comes, the scepter of the "old man" falls, and the "law of sin" which is in our members ceases; and when Christ comes, He brings His scepter and sword with Him, with which He kills the Beast and the Antichrist within us.

When Christ was born in the flesh, the scepter departed from the Maccabean tribe and passed to Herod, an Edomite.

<term>Shiloh comes</term> <note>original: "Der Siloh komme"</note>) "Yavo Shilo" <note>Hebrew: יבא שילה</note> makes, by <term>Gematria</term> <note>A system of assigning numerical values to Hebrew letters to find hidden connections between words</note>, the same total as "Mashiach" <note>Hebrew: משיח, the Messiah</note>.

**Numerical Calculation:**

| Phrase: "Yavo Shilo" (Shiloh shall come) | Value | | Word: "Mashiach" (Messiah) | Value |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| Yod (י) | 10 | | Mem (מ) | 40 |
| Bet (ב) | 2 | | Shin (ש) | 300 |
| Aleph (א) | 1 | | Yod (י) | 10 |
| Shin (ש) | 300 | | Chet (ח) | 8 |
| Yod (י) | 10 | | | |
| Lamed (ל) | 30 | | | |
| He (ה) | 5 | | | |

From this, it is concluded that the Shiloh who is to come is none other than the Messiah. And:

It is indisputably certain to a heart in which the Holy Spirit dwells that he is speaking of the true Savior, Jesus Christ.

Conversely, unbelief among Jews and hypocritical Christians seeks to call all of this into doubt.

Therefore, there are many kinds of disputes among the learned regarding this "Shiloh." But one must not waste time with what does not serve to strengthen faith and for edification.

The most necessary things to note here—in order to ground oneself in the truth of Jesus Christ against today’s atheistic world, which so plausibly calls everything into doubt, and to learn to recognize the true Messiah even according to outward history and circumstances—are the following:

1) That the Jews, as much as they might wish to twist and obscure this passage, have never been able to falsify it in the Bible; rather, one finds this word unchanged throughout all Hebrew Bibles. Even their own Masoretes <note>Scholars who preserved the Hebrew text</note> expressly admit concerning it that it is written here alone with these letters (שילה) and nowhere else in the Old Testament.

2) Its meaning, as many interpret it, is "peaceful," "peace-making," or "salvation-bringing."

<column-break/>

This is in itself a precious name for the Lord Messiah: which all who are weary and heavy-laden experience when they come to Him and let Him help them. For truly He alone, the Savior, creates rest for our souls—yes, salvation and peace—if we only desire it. He is the "Hero" <note>German: "Held"</note>, as Luther translates it, and the "Breaker-through," not only in His suffering and death but also always in the eventual and actual rescue of His believers from all their enemies.

Furthermore, "Shiloh" can also mean a "child," "fruit of the body," or "son." For Christ is indeed the child born to us and the son given to us (Isaiah 9:6).

This is certain not only regarding His human nature, according to which He took such a lowly beginning as the smallest child, but Christ may also be called Shiloh here as the eternal Son of God. For:

Regarding this word, even the ancient Hebrew book called the <term>Zohar</term> <note>A foundational work of Jewish mysticism or Kabbalah</note> notes that it is written with a *Yod* (י) and a *He* (ה), indicating the Divine Name.

3) It is also worth considering how the Seventy Translators <note>The Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament</note> render this word: namely, *apokeimena* <note>Greek: ἀποκείμενα, meaning "the things laid up" or "reserved"</note>. For it is more than certain regarding the Messiah or anointed Redeemer that He is the "rightful deposit," the "reserved one," or the "hope of the Gentiles." He is indeed the highest treasure, in whom lies everything necessary for all poor and hungry hearts, as they well experience; yes, to whom everything is assigned and reserved by the Father, especially all the glory of His kingdom.

Although the most honest and ancient Jews gladly accepted this prophecy as referring to the Messiah, many—especially the modern Rabbis—seek all sorts of wretched excuses and put forward absurd things, so that they understand "Shiloh" to mean sometimes Saul, sometimes Jeroboam, sometimes Nebuchadnezzar, and other persons.

But their objections are so forced and nonsensical that they themselves cannot agree among each other what the "scepter" is or who "Shiloh" might be.

It can be enough for us that the older and best Rabbis understood no one else by it but the Messiah.

This Messiah did indeed come at the very time when the Jewish government ceased. For history shows it as clear as day that exactly around the time when Christ was to come in the flesh, Pompey made the Jewish land a province and took away the Jews' high courts. A few years after Christ's birth, Vespasian completely destroyed Jerusalem and, with it, the entire Jewish Republic.

That this prophecy does not determine a specific year, but only the general era of time, can be seen from this: it does not say "at the Messiah's coming the government shall immediately cease," but rather "the scepter shall not be removed *until* the Hero comes." And so, the total removal could still be delayed for a few years.

This is thus an excellent testimony against all unbelievers who do not believe in the Son and deny that Jesus came in the flesh—whether they be Jews or other mockers among the so-called Christians.

<term>To him shall the obedience of the peoples be</term> <note>original: "Demselben werden die Völcker gehorsamen"</note>) It was indeed a great thing that the Apostles won so many Gentiles and nations for Christ Jesus, their Lord and Master, and drew them into the obedience of faith; which has not entirely ceased throughout all the centuries since. But the gathering of the nations will only truly begin when the "fullness" enters and "all Israel" shall be saved. For if the beginning is so great, and the fall of the Jews has given such a rich harvest of the Gentiles, how great will it be when the whole lump of dough is leavened!

Submission and obedience are and remain an inseparable and inevitable power and fruit of faith: so that whichever nation or soul submits to the Lord Christ, the same undoubtedly believes in Him. But whoever does not obey Him is unbelieving.

From the word *Yikkahat* <note>Hebrew: יקהת, translated as "obedience" or "gathering"</note>, a certain Jew is said to have cleverly noted which peoples would submit to and obey Shiloh: namely **Y** (י) Jews [Juden], **P** (פ) Christians [Christen], **H** (ה) Heathens [Heyden], **T** (ת) Turks [Türcken], under which names all peoples of the world are comprised (a).

<margin>(a) Pfeiffer, *Critica Sacra*, Chapter 7, Lecture 1, Paragraph 7.</margin>

# Chapter XLIX. The First Book of Moses.

**11. He will bind his foal to the vine / and his donkey’s colt to the choice vine. He will wash his garment <gloss>(a)</gloss> in wine / and his cloak in the blood of grapes.**

<margin>(a) Revelation 19:13.</margin>

Among the most distinguished events that would happen to Christ, his suffering is primarily reported here: how he would first make his royal entry upon a donkey and upon a foal, the colt of a donkey; as Zechariah later prophesied with more extensive detail in chapter 9:9, which then stood tied to a vine, of which there were many on the Mount of Olives. Here, the donkey signifies the Jews sighing under the burden and yoke of the Law, and the wild foal signifies the Gentiles, whom Christ also wishes to rule through His Spirit: all of which was fulfilled according to the literal word in Matthew 21:2, etc. Thus, the poor Jews are to be pitied in their blindness, as they are unable to recognize the fulfillment of such a clear prophecy. Following this, His suffering itself followed, when He also trod the <term>winepress of God's wrath</term> <note>A biblical metaphor for divine judgment and the intense suffering of Christ, where "treading grapes" represents the shedding of blood.</note>, so that His clothes and His entire body were sprinkled with blood (Isaiah 63:2-3). This happened first to Christ, and later will also happen in His great vengeance over the nations, when His spiritual body—the believers—will be sprinkled with blood in their suffering and martyrdom. See Revelation 6:12 regarding this, and Revelation 19:19-20 regarding the nations it will also strike.

*He will)* make the wild and unruly Gentiles, like a wild unruly foal, into His members, and bind them to the vine—which is He Himself (Romans 5:18-19)—and finally also bring in the son or the descendants of the burdened donkey—the Jewish people who until now have been very heavily burdened with the Mosaic Law. Our Savior will succeed with them at His second coming in what He did not wish to accomplish at His first coming.

*Foal)* The Hebrew word generally means a young animal and is mostly used for young donkeys. The other word actually signifies a burdened

*Donkey)* who is accustomed to carrying and has been constantly broken and tamed under heavy burdens. Whose

*Son)* however, indicates the same nature as the one whose son he is called.

What mysteries of the Kingdom of Christ are not hidden under these parables!

Has not corrupt nature become so entirely beast-like that it cannot recover unless the Savior binds it to Himself and His divine love, and in repentance accustoms it again to drink the wine of His grace and joys? Did not the Son of <term>God</term> bind and unite our humanity with Himself for that very purpose?

Now, whoever diligently allows himself to be bound to this vine through the bond of pure faith, and sucks the noble juice of the love of <term>God</term> from the noble branch, certainly remains standing in this true vine as a newly grafted branch; he turns green and brings forth his fruit. There his Father cleanses him, so that he may bring forth more fruit.

But those who separate themselves from the Redeemer ordained for them through self-will and unbelief are cast out and wither away from divine power until they are eventually cast into the fire.

Since Christ has put on human nature as His garment, He gladly performs this mercy on every soul: that He washes it in the wine of His love—namely, in His shed blood—and separates it from the mire of sin. He washed His cloak in the blood of grapes when He covered fallen humanity against the wrath of <term>God</term>, shedding His precious blood over it so that His holy body was overflowing with it; and indeed, all out of the most fervent love for us humans.

This wine is thus nothing other than the blood of Jesus Christ. Just as souls have no purity of their own, nor possess any worthiness that they should claim for themselves, but everything is in Jesus Christ; so they expect nothing from themselves, nor from any power of their own. Instead, everything within them—no matter how impure it may be—is purified through the grape-blood of Christ, which has been under the winepress and has communicated itself to His friends under the form of wine. Therefore, these souls washed in the blood of Jesus Christ need fear nothing. For this, their Savior, is also, according to

<column-break/>

**12. He is ruddier of eyes than wine, and whiter of teeth than milk.**

**13. Zebulun will dwell at the haven of the sea; yes, he will be at the haven of ships, and his border will be at Sidon.**

**14. Issa-** <note>Catchword for Issachar, continued on the next page.</note>

---

v. 12. Ruddier of eyes than wine) That is: The desire of His heart and the watchfulness over our souls makes Him burning and fiery, and yet at the same time lovely and sweet, like red wine that goes down smoothly for a thirsty soul; according to the speech of the Song of Solomon.

This signifies the greatness of His compassion, which looks upon the misery of men in order to redeem them from it. They also represent His knowledge, which is paired with compassion and is entirely immersed in holy love.

The purity of His works, prefigured by the teeth, surpasses everything one might say about them, because they were performed in innocence. This is said with the words: He is

Whiter of teeth than milk) He is so hungry for the salvation of men that this will of the Father is truly His food, which He grasps with the longing of His heart as if with teeth; and He also teaches His own how they should in turn eat and drink Him in His love, and indeed with white or innocent teeth of the mouth of faith.

All of this is not only prophesied here by the spirit of prophecy but was also understood thus by the ancient Christians <gloss>(a)</gloss>; and indeed for the purpose that we all might be reached and enticed to hasten to this great Bringer of Salvation and allow ourselves to be saved by Him; whose eyes otherwise also look in wrath like the oriental ruddy wine, and like red flames of fire: Revelation 1:14. This was first proven in the vengeance upon the Jews in their destruction, and will finally be fulfilled in the vengeance upon the Antichrist, the Beast, and the False Prophet. His milk-white teeth, however, may also be an image of the pure Apostolic teachers, who first broke open the shells of the Law and ceremonies, as it were, and showed the kernel of the promise in Christ to the believers, and thus chewed the spiritual food, so to speak, for the beginning believers from among the Jews and Gentiles: just as the symbol of teeth is also taken for teachers in Song of Solomon 4:2 and 6:6.

Judah then also represents the first Apostolic Church of Jews and Gentiles, who partly saw the Shiloh in the flesh and looked upon His suffering with their eyes, also experienced His vengeance upon the Jews, and were themselves the white teeth who, as mentioned, prepared the food of the Gospel quite purely for the nourishment of the whole Church.

v. 13. The literal Zebulun lived by the sea, which may have taken its name from the prominent city of Sidon; but the spiritual Zebulun in the New Testament represents the <term>Church of Smyrna</term> <note>The second of the seven churches in Revelation; the commentator uses a "periodist" view where biblical tribes correspond to eras of church history.</note>, which followed the first Apostolic and Ephesian churches, and had its dwelling mostly by the sea in Asia Minor, Greece, and Illyria, as far as Paul had filled everything with the Gospel (Romans 15:19), of whose voyages for the sake of the Gospel the Book of Acts testifies more extensively.

Where the tribe of Zebulun was situated is also found described in Joshua.

Because he had his territory by the sea, he conducted his commerce with ships and fish, and especially enjoyed his blessing from that.

The Savior stayed frequently in this tribe, as seen in Matthew 4:13, 20.

### The First Book of Moses. Chapter XLIX.

**14. Issachar will be a donkey of strong bones / who will lie down between two burdens.**

**15. For he saw the rest that it was good / and the land that it was pleasant : then he bowed his shoulder to carry / and has become a servant to land-tribute.** 1 Kings 5:13, 14.

**v. 14, 15.** Of the physical state of the literal Issachar, we have no specific historical record / but we do have one of the spiritual Issachar, referring to the previously mentioned <term>Pergamene Church</term> <note>The third of the seven churches in Revelation 2:12-17, historically interpreted here as the era when the Roman Empire accepted Christianity.</note> / when the great figures of the world confessed to Christianity; at that time the Church indeed achieved a physical strength through the great multitude / which, however, was also weighed down by earthly burdens : and as they, along with the teachers, grew fond of earthly goods and pleasures / they also had to accept the yoke of men from the Bishops / Archbishops / Patriarchs / and the like / who were appointed in the Church / as the entire so-called <term>Clergy</term> <note>original: "Clerisey"</note> began to become a truly subservient labor-force; indeed, a true Issachar / who according to the spiritual meaning can represent a hireling / since they almost all looked toward the temporal reward of honors and property.

**v. 16. Dan will judge his people / like any other of the tribes of Israel.**

**v. 16.** Regarding the history of the physical Dan and the remaining tribes / these are difficult to find : so that we must look immediately to the mystical sense of the spiritual Dan / as one tribe after another was born under the spiritual Israel of the New Testament / at which time such events especially occurred.

Now follows the <term>Thyatiran Congregation</term> <note>The fourth church of Revelation 2:18-29, often associated by commentators of this era with the medieval church and the rise of corruption.</note> / in which the Antichrist was born. And concerning Dan, it is worth considering / that he was born of the maidservant / who afterwards became an adulteress; Genesis 30:5, 35:22. and that he was the first to practice public idolatry in his tribe; Judges 18. and that he is not found among the sealed of the twelve tribes of Israel in the New Testament. Revelation 7. All of which corresponds well to the Antichrist / the beast and the false prophet.

He then wanted to be like the first among the tribes of spiritual Israel in the New Testament / as this meaning can also lie in the words / as if he were the only one / to whom the office of judge over all others belonged; since he also set himself up as the supreme judge in all matters of faith in the entire Church. He is the <term>crooked serpent</term> <note>original Latin: "serpens tortuosus"</note>, according to Isaiah 27:1. namely the wretched instrument / through which the ancient serpent / Satan / pursued this spiritual Israel / the people of the New Testament / on the way and narrow path to eternity / and so corrupted and filled it with human laws / that because of this the Spirit of Christ departed from the majority / who otherwise would have led them into all truth / so that they now plunge into ruin on the broad path without the governing Spirit of Christ. See 2 Corinthians 11:3.

Here the light has now dawned for many believers and witnesses of the truth / so that they recognized the great corruption in the Church of Christ / and yearned for the salvation of God / which will come at the end of days / when the Lord will consume this lawless one with the spirit of His mouth / and destroy him by the appearance of His coming. 2 Thessalonians 2:8.

Dan is the first of the maidservants / who attributed the self-willed nature of a good intention to Jacob.

The words of Jacob are very deep in this pronouncement.

Judge) Samson was from the lineage of Dan / and a judge in Israel.

**17. Dan will be a serpent on the way / an adder on the path / that bites the horse's heels / so that its rider falls backward.**

**18. For**

Dan) It may well not have happened in vain / that whereas Jacob otherwise used no tribe's name twice in the prophecy / he nevertheless repeats the name of Dan here : and thus, without doubt, it was indicated / that even so, some from the lineage of Dan / in whom there would be something good / should yet come forth. Therefore, in the final time, the tribe of Dan receives / during the establishment and restoration of the Kingdom of Israel / its lot in the Jewish land / where it comes to lie toward the north; Ezekiel 48:1. although it must be satisfied with getting its lot furthest removed from Jerusalem / compared to the other tribes. They thus still receive their part and lot in the flourishing Church on earth / and become judges like other tribes in Israel : but to the upper Church of the heavenly Jerusalem, none comes from those who initially entered into Christianity from such a tribe; because they became Antichrists within it.

Accordingly, the name of Dan, set down twice, distinguishes one sort and kind of Danites from the other / of which something good is prophesied for one / but hard things are spoken of the other.

Serpent) Thus in the final time, Dan will be like two kinds of such serpents / which hide themselves secretly beside the path / upon which people commonly walk / and then unexpectedly and cunningly / as if flying up / spring forth / and bite the horse in the heel / so that the rider must fall down. Samson also did this in a certain measure to the Philistines. For he never / like other leaders and judges / had soldiers and armed men with him; instead, he always attacked his enemies entirely alone in a concealed and deceitful manner / and unexpectedly dealt them a blow. Therefore Jerome, although without basis, is of the opinion / that these words of Jacob refer to him alone.

On the way) of life / which he entered / when he accepted the faith in Jesus.

And in this respect it may well be possible / that one / who stands in the midst of Christianity / unknown to himself / could come from Jewish extraction, and indeed from the lineage of Dan / from which / according to the opinion of the Fathers / the Antichrist would subsequently arise.

<meta>This page continues the exposition of Jacob’s blessings in Genesis 49, shifting from the specific tribal prophecy of Dan to a sudden, prayerful interjection in verse 18. The author interprets this as a profound Christological moment where Jacob, near death, looks past the earthly tribal divisions toward the coming Messiah.</meta>

### Chapter XLIX. The First Book of Moses.

## 18. I wait for your salvation, O LORD!

<margin>Psalm 119:166. Luke 2:30.</margin>
<margin>19. Gad</margin>

The most prominent circumstances of this statement can show us a great deal of good.

The man who spoke it had been long practiced in suffering, in patience, hope, and faith. Who would now doubt that he let this speech be heard from the deepest ground of his heart, and indeed out of total certainty?

Since he had spoken only plainly in the two preceding prophecies, he turns here, at this most important matter—the very sum of the New Covenant—to the Lord his God Himself, and addresses Him longingly. With his short statement, he expresses both his innermost wish for the Messiah and his living hope and prophetic certainty and prophecy of the same. For such types of prophesying are not rare in the Scripture, where something future is presented in the form of a wish.

Now, whoever knows from history and considers the manifold sufferings of this faithful Jacob can easily believe that he must have looked around most longingly for his deliverance. He had recognized and borne his natural misery all the days of his life, had to fight hard against many spiritual enemies, and also endured many deep humiliations in his spirit under the chastening hand of the Almighty. Thus, he had also become thoroughly worn down and softened <note>original: "mürbe," meaning softened or tenderized by life's trials</note> from the outside under so many adversities. For what misery had he not experienced through his wives and most of his children! What lessons he had to learn through the hostility of Esau, Laban, and other enemies! As he now also saw temporal death before his eyes, and recognized for himself and his children—indeed for the whole world—a rescue and redemption from the Fall and from all the consequences of the Fall as so indispensable and highly necessary; behold, he finally broke out into this wish!

Added to this was the almost immediate occasion that he had thought of the tribe of Dan in the previous words: where, upon the memory of the wicked serpent-mind <note>Referring to the prophecy in Gen 49:17 where Dan is called a serpent</note>, he may have found cause to sigh for the true <term>Serpent-Crusher</term> <note>original: "Schlangen-Treter." A reference to Genesis 3:15, the first promise of the Messiah who would crush the head of the serpent.</note>.

Now, for what did Jacob look, hope, or wait?

> **On your salvation, o LORD!** he says.

After physical help, he had neither desire nor cause to look about: rather, his spirit now, at the departure of his life, indisputably stretched out only for eternal salvation.

Jacob's expression shows clearly enough that he understands no one else by this "salvation" than the future Savior. For although all other help and rescue from God may not be excluded—which is very often called "salvation," especially in the Psalms—an enlightened heart soon understands that dear Jacob was concerned with a much higher way of making whole <note>original: "Heylmachung"</note>. He longed for something more perfect and certain that could truly satisfy his sighing soul.

In temporal matters, he had finally received enough help from his God and experienced many a wonder of God upon himself and his kin, indeed even had many revelations and appearances. All such help is also to be accepted with thanks in its part. But it could not fully content him without the Eternal. His heart looked around for an even nobler part and salvation that reached deeper and could satisfy his innermost ground.

Thus, the eyes of his pure faith looked, with the word "Salvation," solely and alone upon that blessed Seed of the Woman who was already promised in Paradise, as the Lamb that was slain from the beginning. This one he names with great emphasis as **Salvation** itself, and not only a bringer of salvation or a Savior: to show that he hopes and wishes to enjoy Him entirely and completely with all His perfect work of redemption.

Yes, one should note and see how precisely dear Jacob expresses the person of the Messiah here! He uses in the Hebrew the word from which the name **JESUS** comes, in whom alone we shall be saved, and the reason why it was given to Him is this: *For He will save His people* or heal them *from their sins.* Matthew 1:21 <note>The OCR cites Matthew 1:14, but the author is quoting 1:21</note>. Jacob means this JESUS here as the true and only bringer of salvation, the rescuer and healer, the life-giver or awakener, who was to help out of sickness, distress, and death: all of which this precious word in Hebrew holds within itself—indeed, a thousand times more than all tongues may ever express or all miserable ones may experience.

<column-break/>

Everyone here ought to open the eyes of their mind and test in faith whether they believe as faithfully in the Jesus who has already come as Jacob did here before His coming in the flesh. See with what fervor he expresses the salvation-worthy name **JESUS** here: let one learn to practice it thus in good and bad days.

Without any doubt, the dear combatant of faith, who had wrestled with God and men, felt such a power of life and salvation from this most holy name within himself, which permeated him like a balm and confirmed him in the Father's love, especially in the time of tribulations.

As many as rightly recognize Jesus Christ through the Holy Spirit know with divine certainty that herein lies the true redemption and the healing of all our damage, when the Son of God, through this very communication of His salvation-worthy name Jesus, makes His acquired goods of salvation our own for our use. Only then does one see what kind of salvation Jacob sought, and what high cause he had to long and sigh for it until death, the foretaste of which he had often enjoyed. For just as no one can become eager for it unless they have first tasted what the anguish of sin brings.

Jacob calls this salvation the "Lord's salvation," whom he addresses with his whole heart: *On your salvation, O LORD!* Not on miserable human help or that of other creatures; not on pathetic comforters or false lights and saviors: but on the salvation that flows from You, O great **JEHOVAH**, You sole true God!

**I wait**, says Jacob, and thereby expresses the state of his innermost heart, in which the Holy Spirit worked faith.

According to nature and the Fall, Jacob, as well as all men, would have had only death and the curse to expect. But since he now expects salvation instead, it is clear what a faithful "waiting" this must have been.

The Hebrew word that he uses actually expresses a waiting where one is set upon or intent on a thing with great earnestness and desire, but especially with full confidence, and aims and presses toward it with all might: which "waiting" in the Scripture is contrasted with mistrust and impatience, where one does not want to wait for the time and thus misses the help, or at least spoils and neglects it.

Good Jacob was indeed thoroughly practiced in such waiting. He had so often and for so many long years had to wait for temporal rescue: how much more should he have waited for eternal salvation!

O, how a soul that knows its misery longs for salvation and for the actual liberation from sins and from the whole service of vanity! <note>A reference to Romans 8:20-21, the "bondage of vanity" or "corruption."</note> That then requires time before the naughtiness of the old man decreases and dies. Therefore, it is a matter of waiting for it with Jacob.

So faith also waits in the New Testament for the salvation of God. For when we rightly feel our distress in this world and the corruption, we long, with the whole sighing creation under the service of vanity, for the full fulfillment of the redemption acquired for us through Christ. For which Paul also waited after the work of redemption was done: *The Lord will deliver me from every evil!*

Such waiting is as little in vain as was Jacob's. For faith was in him, and is still in all upright <term>Jacobites</term> <note>In this pietist context, "Jacobites" refers to true spiritual believers who, like Jacob, wrestle with God and wait for His salvation, rather than the political followers of King James.</note>, a certain, essential ground of things hoped for and expected, and a divine conviction of the whole salvation that one does not see physically. Hebrews 11:1.

We will then only rightly learn the lesson of the faith of JESUS and—because this happens most certainly in temptations and tribulation—ask the Father that He grant us at all times that spirit of faith which Jacob had, not only in all his tribulations, but also especially in his last hours. How confidently did this teach him to wait for the making-whole of his and all souls! And indeed, not with an idle waiting of spiritual laziness, but with a living hope which he had in the Lord's promises, in which he reminded Him of the fulfillment.

If sin now becomes powerful in you, if your own impotence meets your eyes everywhere, so that you perceive nothing less than salvation or rescue; there learn with all the desire of faith to press into the redemption of Jesus Christ—all the more certainly since that which Jacob still hoped for has now been accomplished.
