<meta>This page continues the prophetic blessings of Jacob from Genesis 49. Having previously addressed Dan and interrupted with a prayer for salvation, the text now moves through the tribes of Gad, Asher, and Naphtali, correlating them with the stages of church history (the Seven Churches of Revelation) before focusing extensively on the blessing of Joseph as a type for the coming Kingdom of Christ.</meta>

<page-num>274</page-num>
<header>The First Book of Moses. Chap. XLIX.</header>

### 19. Gad shall be attacked by warring troops; but he shall attack their rear in troop-like fashion.
### 20. From Asher: his bread shall be fat; for he shall provide royal delights.
### 21. Naphtali is a let-loose hind, who gives beautiful speeches.

v. 19. The spiritual Gad represents the period of the Church of Sardis <note>The author follows a common Pietist tradition of interpreting the Seven Churches of Revelation 2-3 as successive ages of church history; Sardis is often linked to the post-Reformation era</note>, when the testimony of truth arose through several witnesses, joined by the greats of this world. Consequently, they were attacked with wars and resisted with external weapons; thus, in this time, very heavy religious wars have broken out time and again.

And when Israel is finally on the march and takes possession of its land again in the last days according to God's promise, then one will first see how Gad, as a bellicose people, will be so well-armed.

v. 20. Asher, therefore, represents the Philadelphian Church <note>The "Church of Brotherly Love," often viewed by Pietists as the ideal spiritual community</note>, where the spiritual bread of life, the heavenly manna, has again revealed itself in great abundance. This occurs through the deep, precious truths that were unlocked and perceived through the "open door" in this congregation. Then, the testimony of the glorious Kingdom of Christ shows and offers us the magnificent royal delights of spiritual goods, and the believers are invited to the Wedding of the Lamb. Thus, they are the true Asher, which means "Blessed." For blessed are those who are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb. Rev. 19:9.

v. 21. Naphtali represents the godly in the Laodicean Church who will take to heart the punishments and chastisements of the Lord in the last days—with which God will also begin at His house, 1 Peter 4:17—and therefore become zealous and repent. Thus, they will open the door to the Savior who stands there knocking, by taking the beautiful speeches of His voice to heart. He will then enter into them and hold the supper with them, and they with Him. Rev. 3:19-20. These will also be made inwardly free by Him from all human laws and ordinances, so that they are compared to hinds in the forest in their freedom. Likewise, believers are compared to the hinds of the field in Song of Solomon 2:7 and 3:5, and Christ Himself to a roe and a young hart in Song of Solomon 2:17 and 8:14.

Moreover, the name Naphtali is rich in mystery according to its meaning, which signifies a "struggle" or "wrestling." Gen. 30:8. This is because these believers must maintain a great struggle for their freedom against the external church, and often even against the "good people" within it—their own brothers and sisters. Many persecutions are drawn upon them, so that they become, with their Head, a "Hind of the Morning" <note>original: "Hindin der Morgenröthe," a reference to the title of Psalm 22</note>, which was said by the Jews to refer to the early dawn, and also of His first childhood, and as soon as He came forward publicly with His testimony. He often withdrew into the forests and wildernesses, and there delivered beautiful speeches to the people—specifically to the weary and heavy-laden who struggle and fight against their corruption. Therefore, most interpreters apply this particularly to Christ, as He wished to stay at Capernaum, which lay in the tribe of Naphtali, as a regular dwelling place. Matt. 4:13, 15. This blessed Fifth Monarchy <note>A biblical concept from the Book of Daniel referring to the final, eternal Kingdom of God that succeeds the four earthly empires</note> will follow this, resting upon His chosen bride and the firstborn, who will be the true Nazirites and "separated ones" among their brothers, who will reign with Christ for all eternity. See Dan. 2:44, 7:27.

v. 22. Shoots) Joshua and Gideon, Elijah, Elisha, Micah, etc., are of his lineage and seed.

v. 23-24. The resigned soul remains in its strength, even if it is surrounded by weakness, because it has set the bow of its strength upon the Most High, who is its God. But when the years of its trials and its captivity are over, the hands of God—the Almighty in Jacob—loosen its arms and hands and make them fit for great things.

v. 24. From whence is the Shepherd) This can be understood in two ways. First, that when his hands are loosened, the Shepherd comes out of such a deliverance. For only when the soul has been made truly free again through resurrection and renewal does it become truly fit to lead others. The second way is that from the Mighty One of Jacob, who is God, the Leader of the inner people has come—namely, Jesus Christ, the true Shepherd.

The Stone of Israel) By this, the Foundation is understood. This is likewise Jesus Christ, the cornerstone of the spiritual house, which would have neither worthiness nor stability if it were not founded upon Jesus Christ, the firm stone and rock, but rather upon the sand of one's own inventions.

<column-break/>

### 22. A fruitful vine is Joseph, a fruitful vine by a spring. Of those shoots, each one goes over the wall.
### 23. And although the archers embittered him and shot at him, and hated him;
### 24. Yet his bow remains stiff, and the arms of his hands were strengthened through the hands of the Mighty One in Jacob: from whence is the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel.

Joseph thus represents the believers at the dawning of the glorious Kingdom of Christ. They will emerge in great numbers, so that before one realizes it, they suddenly stand there as a great people, born in secret by the Spirit of God. Isa. 66:7-9. Thus, they will be the fruitful vine in the vineyard of the Lord, whose shoots will go over the wall, in that they overcome all obstacles. They will join David in singing the song of praise in its fulfillment, as contained in the eighteenth Psalm, when the Lord had rescued him from the hand of all his enemies; for with his God he had leaped over a wall, v. 30, and He made his feet like the feet of harts and set him on high places, v. 34. To this end, the believers of the previous time were prepared as "free hinds." Also, the Lord will equip the believers of this time with strength for the struggle, and God will cast down those who set themselves against them; He will give their enemies over to flight, so that they shall destroy those who hate them. v. 40-41. See also Deut. 33:27-29.

And here, Christ will gloriously reveal Himself as the Mighty One in Jacob, who has crowned His people with victory and will now reveal Himself as the Shepherd and Stone who has become the cornerstone. Ps. 118:22. He will now pasture His believers fully on green, grassy meadows and lead them to the still waters, Ps. 23:1, where He Himself will take charge of His flock and lead them to the best pastures. He will let them lie down in gentle folds and grant them fat pastures upon the mountains of Israel. Ezek. 34:11, 14. Then the glorious blessings will be revealed which are reserved for these believers in such a glorious Kingdom of Christ, which will surpass all previous blessings: namely, first and foremost, the heavenly blessing in the full pouring out of the Holy Spirit over all flesh, Joel 2:28. Of this, only the blessed firstfruits have been felt from the first Pentecost of the New Testament onward, but then the full harvest will be here on earth. The earth will also then be greatly blessed with all its growth; they will also bear children in great blessing and raise them likewise. Such prophecies are presented very clearly by Isaiah regarding the believers of the last time in this blessed Kingdom. Chap. 65:17-25.

These are precisely the "eternal hills" for which the believers long, which will endure into all eternity. Their blessing will come upon this Joseph, the true "always-increaser" <note>original: "semper-Augustum," a Latin title for the Emperor, here applied spiritually to Christ</note> and augmenter of His kingdom. The physical Augustus, under whom Christ chose to be born (Luke 2:1, etc.), was but an image of this. Under him, the Roman Empire—the greatest among the four world-empires and monarchies—was in its highest bloom. That bloom will remain for all eternity upon Christ as the Head, and upon His chosen bride and the firstborn, who will be the true Nazirites and separated ones among their brothers, who will reign with Christ for all eternity. See Dan. 2:44, 7:27.

<header>Ch. XLIX. The First Book of Moses.</header>

25. From your father's **GOD**, who shall help you; and from the Almighty, who shall bless you with blessings of heaven from above, with blessings of the deep that lies beneath, with blessings of the breasts and of the womb!

26. The blessings of your father exceed the blessings of my parents, even to the desire of the eternal hills: they shall come upon the head of **Joseph**, and upon the crown of the one set apart from among his brothers!

<margin>Deut. 33:16. 1 Chron. 5:1, 2. Rom. 8:29.</margin>
v. 25. The **GOD** of your father, the **GOD** of Israel and of all truly resigned souls <note>original: "Gelassenen" — a key term in German Pietism referring to those who have surrendered their will entirely to God</note>, and the Almighty, to whom nothing is difficult, He will shower you with blessings from above, and also with blessings of the deep that lies beneath! This is to say: that they shall not only attain the graces and endearments of heaven—which are typically given in the state of passion, love, and light where surely everything comes from above, as the certainty of it is shared—but also the blessing of the lowest hells; namely, the temptations and misery which are the inheritance of the abyss. This can also be understood as the inward hell through which such chosen souls (at least some) must pass. Even with all their consequences and hellish vapors (which contain nothing but terror and loathing), a blessing—indeed, an even greater blessing than the former—is won by those who draw from it the benefit that **GOD** intends.

The latter blessing is perceived in two ways: first, that of the breasts, where the milk flowing from them represents the ease of helping spiritual children on these paths and nourishing them with this spiritual milk of contemplation <term>contemplation: a high state of prayer and quiet focus on the divine</term>; the second is that of the womb, by which he understands the bringing forth of these very spiritual children in **JESUS** Christ. For the grace of spiritual birth is one thing, and the nurturing and care of the same is another. One gives birth in **JESUS** Christ but cannot nourish; another nourishes but cannot give birth. However, both together make up the perfection of the Apostolic ways; therefore, this so perfect blessing has been reserved for **Joseph**, who stands in this state.

v. 26. The blessings which **Jacob** gives to his son **Joseph** are distinct from those **Jacob** received from his fathers: because they were established through faith and through the resignation <note>original: "Gelassenheit"</note> from which he had his origin, and this must properly sustain the blessing. He also assures through these words that his ancestors walked in these same leadings and received such an extraordinary blessing through the prelude of their lives, until the desire of these souls—who, because of the high degree of their holiness, seemed like the mountains and hills—would be fulfilled and brought into one, where all desire is lost.

The truest sense, however, is likely that the example of the ancestors must sustain the resigned soul in its peculiar paths until **JESUS** Christ, the Desire of the Saints, should come; who then should be not only the preacher but also the true pattern and example of this; and until the soul should possess Him without mediation—even the most holy mediation—through the spiritual incarnation that takes place within the soul.

<margin>(a) Rev. 1:8.</margin>
This blessing shall be upon the head of **Joseph**; because, although **Joseph** is highly exalted in the secret life, **JESUS** Christ is nonetheless infinitely more exalted therein: and there is nothing so highly exalted that is not under Him; since He (a) is the beginning and the end of all leadings. Every age also receives its particular blessing from Him; for the faithful in every age have been led by **Christ’s** Spirit into all truth necessary for them at that time, and have been mightily protected from enemies and false brothers.

<column-break/>

27. **Benjamin** shall raven as a wolf. In the morning he shall devour the prey, and at night he shall divide the spoil.

28. All these are the twelve tribes of **Israel**: and this is what their father spoke to them when he blessed them; every one according to his blessing, so he blessed them.
<meta>catchword: 29 And</meta>

v. 27. **Benjamin** represents the believers in the glorious kingdom and until the end of the same; who in the beginning will have the strong, and so all the mighty, as prey with and in **Christ**, their Head (Isa. 53:12). Then they will execute vengeance upon the heathens and their kings, according to the judgment that is written; which is the honor that all His saints shall have (Ps. 149:7-9). Then shall the merchandise and hire of the spiritual **Cyrus** be holy to the **LORD**, which can no longer be gathered and hidden for protection; instead, this spiritual **Benjamin**—who by meaning shall be the sons of the right hand of the **LORD** (see Ps. 118:15-16)—who dwell before the **LORD**, they shall receive their merchandise as a prey, so that they may eat and be satisfied, and have lasting clothing (Isa. 23:18; see also Ezek. 39:10). In the evening, however, at the conclusion of this new earth, they shall divide and carry away the spoil in blessed eternity, when the twelve tribes of the mystical **Israel**, who were born throughout the time of the Old and New Testament, shall be led as the adorned bride to her husband **JESUS** Christ, to infinitely praise and glorify **GOD** and **Christ** in the new heaven and upon the new earth in the heavenly Jerusalem for all the eternities of eternities (Rev. 21:1-2 etc.).

Regarding this, **Tertullian** (a) writes to me, "the first book of Moses has already promised **Paul** to me. For among those figures and prophetic sayings, **Jacob** foresaw here that **Paul** would come from the tribe of **Benjamin**: who was indeed a ravening wolf in the morning; that is, in his early years he devastated the flock of the **LORD** as a persecutor of the Church; but later in the evening he divided the spoil; that is, in his later years he pastured the sheep of **Christ** as a teacher of the Gentiles. If such mysterious explanations of the figures do not please you, it is at least certain that I perceive in **Paul** such an order in the Acts of the Apostles, which you also cannot deny." <note>original: "L. 5. adv. Marcion. c. 1." — Tertullian, *Against Marcion*, Book 5, Chapter 1</note>

The Hebrews explain this prophecy of **Jacob** as referring to the altar of burnt offering, which was in the tribe of **Benjamin**, and which, through its constant fire, would devour many sacrifices morning and evening like a wild beast, of which the priests should also have their portion. And perhaps that naughty woman mentioned in a Talmudic tractate (b), by the name of **Miriam bat Bilgah** <note>original: "Maria Bilga Tochter"</note>, had this in mind; she went into the Temple, struck the altar with her slipper, and said: "O you wolf! you wolf! how long will you consume the goods and treasures of the children of **Israel**?"

When kings, princes, lords, and other powerful ones carry lions, unicorns, horses, eagles, and the like in their coats of arms, they should strive, like **Christ**, to acquire the virtues of these animals in their hearts, or whatever else meaningful can be noted in their actions: as for example, the eagle soars upward toward the sun and carefully warms and protects its young. But they should especially guard themselves against the wolf, loathe it, and flee from its wild, predatory nature; according to which such animals are images of tyrants and beastly-minded men; just as the devil himself is called a roaring lion (1 Pet. 5:8). Therefore, the worldly kingdoms are called mountains of prey because of their great general corruption (Ps. 76:5).

v. 28. Thus the believers of all times have their particular dispensations according to the wise government of **Christ**, and

### **19. Gad shall be raided by troops of war; but he shall raid their rear in troop-like fashion.**

### **20. From Asher: his bread shall be fat; for he shall yield royal delights.**

### **21. Naphtali is a let-loose hind, who gives beautiful speeches.**

v. 19. The spiritual Gad belongs to the era of the church at Sardis <note>The author follows a tradition identifying the seven churches of Revelation 2-3 as historical periods. Sardis is often associated by these commentators with the post-Reformation period</note>, when the testimony of truth arose through several witnesses, joined by the greats of this world. Consequently, they were attacked with wars and resisted with outward weapons; thus, very heavy Wars of Religion broke out during this time. And when Israel is on the march and takes back its land in the final time, according to the promise of **GOD**, then it will first be seen how Gad, as a warlike people, shall be so well-equipped.

v. 20. Asher represents the Philadelphian congregation, where the spiritual bread of life, the heavenly manna, has again revealed itself in great abundance through the deep, precious truths that were unlocked and perceived through the "open door" in this congregation. Then the testimony of the glorious Kingdom of Christ shows and offers us the magnificent royal delights of spiritual goods, and the believers are invited to the Marriage of the Lamb. Thus, they are the true Asher, which means "Blessed." For "Blessed are those who are called to the marriage supper of the Lamb" (Rev. 19:9).

v. 21. Naphtali represents the godly in the Laodicean congregation who will take to heart the punishments and chastisements of the Lord in the final time—with which **GOD** will begin at His own house (1 Pet. 4:17)—and will therefore become zealous and repent. Thus, they will open the door to the Savior who stands there knocking, by taking the beautiful speeches of His voice to heart. He will then enter into them and hold the supper with them, and they with Him (Rev. 3:19-20). These will then be made inwardly free by Him from all human decrees and ordinances, so that they are compared to the hinds in the forest in their freedom. In the same way, believers are compared to the hinds of the field (Song of Sol. 2:7, 3:5), and Christ himself to a roe and a young stag (Song of Sol. 2:17, 8:14).

Furthermore, the name Naphtali is rich in mystery according to its meaning, which signifies "a struggle" or "a fight" (Gen. 30:8). This is because these believers must maintain a great struggle for the sake of their freedom against the outward church—and often even against the "good people" within it, their own brothers and sisters. Many persecutions are drawn upon them, so that with their Head [Christ] they become a "Hind of the Dawn" <note>original: "Hindin der Morgenröthe" — referring to the Hebrew title of Psalm 22, *Ayelet HaShachar*</note>, of whom it was said early on by the Jews, even from His earliest childhood, as soon as He publicly came forward with His testimony. He often withdrew into the forests and wildernesses and there delivered beautiful speeches to the people, specifically to the weary and heavy-laden who struggle and fight against their own corruption. Therefore, most interpreters apply this particularly to Christ, as He chose to stay at Capernaum—which lay in the tribe of Naphtali—as a regular dwelling (Matt. 4:13, 15). Upon this, the blessed Fifth Monarchy <note>A theological concept of a final, godly world empire following the four earthly empires of Daniel’s prophecy</note> shall follow, and upon His chosen Bride and the firstborn, who shall be those who reign with Christ for all eternity.

<column-break/>

### **22. Joseph is a fruitful vine, a fruitful vine by a spring. Of its shoots, each one goes over the wall.**

### **23. And although the archers embittered him, shot at him, and hated him;**

### **24. Yet his bow remains stiff, and the arms of his hands were made firm by the hands of the Mighty One of Jacob: from whence is the Shepherd, the Stone of Israel.**

Joseph represents the believers at the dawn of the glorious Kingdom of Christ, who will stand forth in great numbers. Before anyone realizes it, they will suddenly appear as a great people whom the Spirit of **GOD** has birthed in secret (Isa. 66:7-9). Thus, they shall be the fruitful vine in the vineyard of the Lord, whose shoots go over the wall by overcoming all obstacles. Like David, they will strike up the song of praise in its fulfillment, as contained in the eighteenth Psalm, when the Lord had rescued him from the hand of all his enemies. For with his **GOD**, he leaped over a wall (v. 30); He made his feet like those of a deer and set him upon high places (v. 34)—for which the believers of the previous era were prepared as "free hinds." Also, the Lord will equip the believers of this time with strength for the fight, and **GOD** will cast down those who oppose them: He will give them their enemies in flight, that they may destroy those who hate them (v. 40-41). See also Deut. 33:27-29. And here Christ will gloriously reveal Himself as the Mighty One in Jacob, who has crowned His people with victory. He will now reveal Himself as the Shepherd and the Stone who has become the cornerstone (Ps. 118:22), and who will now graze His believers fully on green, grassy meadows and lead them to still waters (Ps. 23:1-2). He Himself will take charge of His flock and lead them to the best pastures; He will let them lie down in gentle folds and grant them fat pastures on the mountains of Israel (Ezek. 34:11, 14). There the magnificent blessings will be revealed, which are reserved for these believers in such a glorious Kingdom of Christ, which shall surpass all previous blessings. Namely, first and foremost, the heavenly blessing in the full outpouring of the Holy Spirit over all flesh (Joel 2:28), of which only the blessed first-fruits have been felt since the first Pentecost of the New Testament; then, however, the full harvest shall be here on earth. The earth itself will also be greatly blessed with all its growth; they will also generate children in great blessing and raise them likewise. Such prophecies are presented very clearly by Isaiah regarding the believers of the final time in this blessed Kingdom (Ch. 65:17-25). These are precisely the "eternal hills" for which the believers long, which will last into all eternity. Their blessing will come upon this Joseph, the true *Imper-Augustum* <note>original: "Vermehrer" — a play on the name Joseph (meaning "he shall add/increase") and the title of the Emperor Augustus (from *augere*, "to increase")</note> and Enlarger of His kingdom. The physical Augustus, under whom Christ willed to be born (Luke 2:1, etc.), was an image of this. Under him, the Roman Empire—as the greatest among the four world empires—was in its highest bloom. This bloom will remain for all eternity upon Christ as the Head; they shall be the true Nazirites and separated ones among their brothers. See Dan. 2:44, 7:27.

v. 22. **Shoots**) Joshua and Gideon, Elijah, Elisha, Micah, etc., are from his lineage and seed.

v. 23. 24. The resigned soul <note>original: "gelassene Seele"</note> remains in her strength, though she be surrounded by weakness, because she has set the bow of her strength upon the Most High, who is her God. But when the years of her trials and her captivity are over, the hands of **GOD**—who is the Almighty in Jacob—loosen her arms and hands and make them fit for great things.

v. 24. **From whence is the Shepherd**) This can be understood in two ways. One is that when his hands are freed, the Shepherd comes out of such a redemption. For once the soul has been made truly free again through resurrection and renewal, it becomes truly fit to lead others. The other way is that from the Mighty One of Jacob, who is **GOD**, the leader of the inner people—namely Jesus Christ, the true Shepherd—has come.

**The Stone of Israel**) By this, the Foundation is understood. This is likewise Jesus Christ, the foundation stone of the spiritual house. It would have neither worthiness nor stability if it were not founded on Jesus Christ, the best stone and rock, but rather on the sand of one's own inventions.

### Chapter XLIX. The First Book of Moses.

25. From the GOD of your father, who will help you, and from the Almighty, who will bless you, with blessings of heaven from above, with blessings of the abyss that lies beneath, with blessings of the breasts and of the womb!

26. The blessings of your father exceed the blessings of my parents, even unto the desire of the everlasting hills! They shall come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the head of him who was separate from his brothers!

<margin>Deuteronomy 33:16. 1 Chronicles 5:1–2. Romans 8:29.</margin>
v. 25. The GOD of your father, the GOD of Israel and of all truly yielded souls <note>original: "Gelassenen" — a key term in German mysticism referring to those who have surrendered their self-will to God</note>, and the Almighty, for whom nothing is difficult—He will shower you with blessings from above, and also with blessings of the abyss that lies beneath! This is as much as to say: that they shall obtain not only the graces and endearments of heaven, which are usually given in the state of passions, love, and light, where certainly everything comes down from above as the certainty of it is communicated; but also the blessing of the lowest hells, namely the temptations and the misery which is the inheritance of the abyss. It can also be understood as the inward hell through which such chosen souls (at least some) must pass; which, with all its consequences and hellish vapors (containing nothing but terror and loathsomeness), nevertheless results in a blessing—indeed an even greater blessing than the former—to those who draw the profit from it that **GOD** intends.

The latter blessing is perceived in two ways: the first of the breasts; the milk coming from them represents the ease of helping spiritual children in these ways and nourishing them with this spiritual milk of contemplation: the second of the womb; by which he understands the bringing forth of these very spiritual children in **JESUS** Christ. For the grace of spiritual birth is one thing, and the nourishment and care of the same is another. One gives birth in **JESUS** Christ but cannot nourish; another nourishes but cannot give birth: yet both together constitute the perfection of the Apostolic ways; and therefore this so perfect blessing has been reserved for Joseph, who stands in this state.

v. 26. The blessings that Jacob gives to his son Joseph are distinct from those Jacob received from his fathers: because they were established through faith and through the yieldedness from which he had his origin, and this must properly sustain the blessing. He also assures through these words that his ancestors walked in these very same leadings and received such an extraordinary blessing through the prelude of their lives, until the desire of these souls—which, because of the high degree of their holiness, seemed like mountains and hills—would be fulfilled and brought into one, where all desire loses itself.

However, the truest sense is likely that the example of the forefathers must sustain yielded souls in their singular ways until Jesus Christ, the Desire of the Saints, should come; who then should be not only the preacher but also the true pattern and example of this: and until the soul should stand in Him without any means—even if they were the holiest means—through the spiritual incarnation that takes place within the soul.

This blessing shall be upon the head of Joseph; because, although Joseph is highly exalted in the hidden life, **JESUS** Christ is nonetheless infinitely more exalted therein: and there is nothing so highly exalted that is not under Him; because He <gloss>(a)</gloss> is the beginning and the end of all leadings. <margin>(a) Revelation 1:8.</margin>

likewise, every age receives its particular blessing from Him; since the believers in every age are led by the Spirit of Christ into all truth necessary for them for that time, and have been mightily protected from enemies and false brothers.

Benjamin represents the believers in the glorious kingdom and until the end of the same, who in the beginning—the strong ones, and all the powerful, with and in Christ, their head—shall have the prey: Isaiah 3:12. when they shall execute vengeance upon the heathens and their kings, according to the judgment that is written; which is the honor that all His saints shall have. Psalm 149:7, 8, 9. Then the merchandise and the hire of the harlot of the spiritual Cyrus <note>The "spiritual Cyrus" refers to Christ as a liberator, typified by the historical King Cyrus who freed the Israelites from Babylon</note> shall be holy to the **LORD**, which can no longer be gathered and hidden for protection; but this spiritual Benjamin, who by meaning shall be the sons of the right hand of the **LORD**, (see Psalm 118:15, 16) who dwell before the **LORD**, they shall receive their merchandise as a prey, so that they may eat and be satisfied, and have lasting clothing. Isaiah 23:18. See also Ezekiel 39:10. But in the evening, at the conclusion also of this new earth, they shall divide and carry away the spoil in the blessed eternity, when the twelve tribes of the mystical Israel, who have been born throughout all time in the Old and New Testaments, shall be led as the adorned bride to her husband **JESUS** Christ, to praise and glorify **GOD** and Christ infinitely in the new heaven and upon the new earth in the heavenly Jerusalem for all eternity of eternities. Revelation 21:1, 2. etc.

Regarding this, Tertullian writes <gloss>(a)</gloss>, "the first book of Moses has already promised me Paul." For among "those figures and prophetic sayings, Jacob here foresaw that Paul would come forth from the tribe of Benjamin: who indeed was a ravenous wolf in the morning, that is, in his early years he laid waste the flock of the **LORD** as a persecutor of the church; but afterward in the evening he divided the spoil, that is, in his later years he pastured the sheep of Christ as a teacher of the Gentiles." If such mysterious explanations of the figures do not please one, it is at least certain that "I perceive such an order in the Acts of the Apostles concerning Paul, which you also cannot deny."

The Hebrews explain this prophecy of Jacob as referring to the altar of burnt offering, which was to be in the tribe of Benjamin and, through its constant fire, would devour many sacrifices morning and evening like a wild beast, of which the priests should also have their portion. And perhaps that naughty woman mentioned in a Talmudic tractate <gloss>(b)</gloss>, named Maria the daughter of Bilga, had this in mind; who went into the Temple, struck the altar with her slipper, and said: "O you wolf! you wolf! how long will you consume the goods and treasures of the children of Israel?"

While kings, princes, lords, and other powerful ones otherwise carry lions, unicorns, horses, eagles, and the like in their coats of arms; they should, like Christ, strive to obtain the virtues of these animals in their hearts, or whatever else of significance can be noted in their actions: as for example, the eagle soars upward toward the sun and carefully cherishes and protects its young. They should, however, especially beware of the wolf, abhor it, and flee the wild, predatory nature: according to which such animals are images of tyrants and beastly-minded people; just as the devil himself is called a roaring lion. 1 Peter 5:8. Therefore also the world-kingdoms, because of their general great corruption, are called mountains of prey. Psalm 76:5.

29. And he commanded them and said to them: I am to be gathered to my people; bury me with my fathers in the cave that is on the field of Ephron the Hittite:
30. In the cave that is on the field of Machpelah, which lies opposite Mamre in the land of Canaan; which Abraham bought together with the field from Ephron the Hittite for a hereditary burial place.
31. There they buried Abraham and Sarah, his wife. There they buried Isaac and Rebecca, his wife. There I also buried Leah.
32. The field and the cave that is therein is a property purchased from the children of Heth.
33. And when Jacob had finished commanding his sons, he drew his feet together upon the bed, and he gave up the ghost, and was gathered to his people.

---

<margin>v. 29–32.</margin> Jacob wished to be buried in the land of Canaan, in the ancestral burial place purchased by Abraham; where the three blessed patriarchs—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—were buried with their three lawful wives—Sarah, Rebecca, and Leah. This was because Leah was Jacob's first, and therefore by Providence also his lawful wife, from whom Judah, the ancestor of Christ, was born. Consequently, neither Rachel, nor the two handmaids Zilpah and Bilhah, much less Hagar or Keturah, were to be placed there. Thus, the triple lineage of the beloved friends of GOD was to rest here, in order to encourage the children of Israel, their descendants, to have faith in this promised inheritance and to urge them toward its possession. It may also have been indicated to them here that they should produce their offspring in chaste marriages: for while GOD bore with the secondary marriages of their ancestors, Abraham and Jacob, in patience, He took no pleasure in them; therefore these other wives were not laid beside their husbands. See Malachi 2:14, 15, 16 and Matthew 19:3–9.

The Jews ingeniously show from the letters of the word **ישראל** <note>original: "ISRAEL"</note> the names of those who entered this grave: namely Isaac and Jacob, Sarah, Rebecca, Abraham, and Leah. (a)

<margin>v. 33.</margin> This was a very gentle and blessed departure, as Jacob was first able to present the divine decree with full understanding through the Spirit of GOD, and then immediately commend and give up his spirit into the hands of GOD. See Luke 23:46.

(a) Wagenseil in *Sota*, p. 217. <note>Refers to Johann Christoph Wagenseil’s commentary on the Talmudic tractate "Sotah."</note>

...raisins, embalmed, washed, wrapped in fine linen, and thus preserved in coffins.

This custom was very common among both the ancient Egyptians and the Hebrews. Whether the latter learned it from the former, or vice versa, is not as easily discernable from antiquity as the fact that the most important part was performed using salt, which was the sole basis and cause for such embalming. Even today, such embalmed bodies are found in the Egyptian fields (which are called **mummies** in the pharmacies), coated with a delicate balsam or gum, like a pure and bright varnish, by which the sulfurous, salty substance that causes the preservation of the body was held and bound, so that they could not weather away and the body finally crumble to ash.

<margin>v. 3. Forty days—seventy days</margin> They likely spent the 40 days with constant daily anointing of the body with the most precious oil, and then the remaining 30 days with the customary funeral lamentation; just as such a month of mourning was also observed for Aaron (Numbers 20:29) and Moses (Deuteronomy 34:8).

### Chapter 50. The First Book of Moses.

4. And when the days of his mourning were past, Joseph spoke to the house of Pharaoh, saying: If I have now found grace in your eyes, speak, I pray you, in the ears of Pharaoh, saying:

5. My father made me swear, saying: Behold, I die! In my grave, which I have bought for myself in the land of Canaan, there shall you bury me. Now therefore, let me go up, I pray you, and bury my father, and I will come again.

6. And Pharaoh said: Go up, and bury your father, according as he made you swear.

7. And Joseph went up to bury his father; and with him went up all the servants of Pharaoh, the elders of his house, and all the elders of the land of Egypt:

8. And all the house of Joseph, and his brothers, and his father's house; only their little ones, and their flocks, and their herds, they left in the land of Goshen.

9. And there went up with him both chariots and horsemen; and it was a very great company <note>literally "army" or "host"</note>.

10. And they came to the threshing floor of Atad, which is beyond the Jordan; there they mourned with a very great and sore lamentation; and he made a mourning for his father for seven days.

<gloss>Job 2:13; Ezekiel 3:15.</gloss>

14. And Joseph returned into Egypt, he, and his brothers, and all that went up with him to bury his father, after he had buried his father.

---

<margin>v. 5. Joseph cites the oath given to his father so that it might not be interpreted as pride or mistrust—as if he did not wish to bury his father among them [the Egyptians].</margin>
**Which I have bought for myself**) Abraham had purchased the ancestral burial place, Chapter 23, and here the same is said of Jacob: Since it is possible that he bought something additional to it, or had the ancestral purchase confirmed; or perhaps the basis of possession is cited here to show it is a purchased property, which the inhabitants of the land would grant back to them, even though they had already been staying in Egypt outside the land of Canaan for 17 years.

<margin>v. 10. 11. Among the faithful, mourning cries should be spent with prayers and godly contemplations of the gracious and wonderful guidance of God toward the deceased: for which, otherwise, no ceremonies at all are necessary; rather, everything else is merely a vain and sinful worldly display, which should be entirely omitted in the New Testament, as it is to be counted among the very corrupt customs of all Christendom.</margin>
**Threshing floor of Atad**) This place is said to be located three "stones" <note>milestones</note>—that is, half a German mile <note>approximately 2.3 miles or 3.7 km</note>—from Jericho, according to the writings of Jerome, and was called Bethagla in his time.

Now, if Moses wrote his books in the land of Midian, as Eusebius <note>original: "(a) L. 7. de Præp. Evang." — Book 7 of *Preparation for the Gospel*</note> believes, or in Egypt, or even the first book on Mount Sinai; then this place would not have been "beyond" but "on this side" of the Jordan to him. For it lies near the Dead Sea, ten miles further from Egypt than Hebron.

Therefore, it is also clear that Joseph did not take the most direct path on such a journey, but traveled a detour of up to 32 German miles through the Arabian desert, so that the Dead Sea lay on his left hand and he took his way across the Jordan. He did this so that he would not have to pass through the land of the Edomites and Philistines, who would undoubtedly have refused him passage through their territory because he traveled with a great army. Otherwise, he would have had to travel only 38 miles from On in Egypt by the most direct path to Hebron, whereas by this route he had to travel up to 70 miles.

<margin>v. 13. Cave of the field) That these faithful patriarchs wished to be buried in a cave, and yet there in the open field, indicates that this is the simplest and best way to be buried: so that, according to the powerful word of God, one can all the sooner return to dust (Ezekiel 3:19; Ecclesiastes 12:7) and thus the seed is entrusted to the earth for the spiritual body (1 Corinthians 15:42, 43, 44). All other methods currently practiced, such as embalming bodies, or allowing oneself to be placed in a coffin above ground, or desiring to be buried in churches—even under the altars and in the choirs—are nothing but human inventions that give rise to superstition and cannot coexist with the knowledge of the New Testament.</margin>

# The First Book of Moses. Chapter 50.

15. And when Joseph’s brothers saw that their father was dead, they said: "Perhaps Joseph will hold a grudge against us and certainly repay us for all the evil that we did to him."

16. Therefore, they sent a message to Joseph, saying: "Your father commanded before his death, saying:

17. 'Thus shall you say to Joseph: I pray you, forgive the transgression of your brothers and their sin, for they did evil to you!' Now, we pray you, forgive the transgression of the servants of the God of your father!" But Joseph wept when they spoke these things to him.

18. And his brothers also went and fell down before him, and said: "Behold, we are your servants!"

A guilty conscience is an ever-gnawing worm <note>A traditional metaphor for the persistent sting of remorse or guilt.</note> that stirs whenever the opportunity arises, as long as one has not yet attained the true peace of God in the soul through faith; namely, that peace which is born in a repentant heart, receiving the assurance that one's sins are forgiven. Once forgiven, these sins can no longer be held against us by anyone, nor can anyone harm us without God's will.
The pretext that Joseph’s brothers seize upon—as if Jacob had requested such forgiveness from Joseph—reveals their own restless spirits. Jacob likely already felt assured of Joseph's reconciled heart, but the brothers show they had not yet truly humbled themselves before God or earnestly repented of this sin.
These Hebrew brothers feared Joseph’s revenge because they did not recognize the magnanimity of those in whom God alone reigns, who gladly forget all insulting words directed at them. This fear also moved them to call themselves "servants of the God of Jacob," Joseph’s father, so that he might forgive them all the sooner. Furthermore, they well knew that nothing was more powerful to such a holy man than to remind him of God, especially under the image of such a beloved father.
Joseph, however, who was already established in the state of God's will—which is the highest perfection—speaks to them as a man experienced in these ways and says: "All has happened according to the will of God, which no man can resist." He adds: "Do not fear! Can we then resist this holy will, which leads without stumbling, and which even makes use of the evil intentions of men to reach its goal, transforming evil into good and elevating the soul through that which was intended to humble it?" Even sin itself, which by its nature is harmful to us, becomes useful in the hand of God, because He (a) knows how to turn everything to the best.
> O you holy will, from which everything has its origin, and in which everything concludes as its end! Why do you not have many souls who surrender themselves so completely to your commands?

Should anyone today or tomorrow experience a similar humbling of their enemies, they should conduct themselves well according to Joseph's example. He met his formerly worst enemies in the most friendly manner, so much so that he wept at their address.
<margin>(a) Romans 8:28.</margin>
(1) When an evil report has gone out; (2) we must be humbled before we come to honor; (3) especially worship Christ, who sustains us, feeds us, and leads us to God, before His throne of grace. Although our sins brought Him to misery, He still forgives us when we repent, so that we need not fear.
The conclusion is this: that in the end, good maintains the victory and is stronger than evil. Therefore, one should side with the strongest party and cling to that which is good!

# Chapter 50. The First Book of Moses.
<meta>Catchword: v. 21. Ah</meta>

20. You indeed intended evil against
me (*); God intended it for good /
---
<margin>(a) Ps. 21:11 <note>The German text cites Ps. 21/12; in most English Bibles, this corresponds to Psalm 21:11 regarding the "mischievous device" of enemies.</note></margin>
Whoever notices what deep mysteries of truth,
wisdom, and the love of God lie hidden beneath these words,
with which Joseph brought God’s purpose to the minds
of his brothers regarding his sale!

If we humans still stood in our original innocence,
no one would have anything adverse to fear from another.
One human would not think evil against another, nor
inflict it upon him. For GOD had made all things very good, and the
well-made creature also acted well toward one another. But

The devil has sown his envy and wrath into humanity,
and thereby poisoned the mind and will, so that now after
the Fall, one seeks the ruin of the other. From this come
evil thoughts against one's neighbor, and from those
thoughts come harmful counsel and intentions against others.

**You)** These are not pagan people or barbarians,
nor are they strangers and unknowns who are unrelated to him or
opposed to his teachings. Rather, they are Jacob’s
sons, the seed of such a holy and righteous man,
servants of GOD, as they call themselves in verse 17, and—what
surpasses everything—Joseph’s biological brothers.

How heavy is this prefiguration, that Christ first had to
suffer at the hands of his own people, and afterwards that all
his members <note>A common Pietist term for the "limbs" or individual believers making up the body of Christ.</note> would have to endure the most from those
who also profess the Christian religion!

However, all such outward attacks are almost minor, and
are easily overlooked compared to the internal enemies, which
seek to undo all divine guidance and tokens of grace
in a willing soul in a thousand different ways.

All such enemies, from within and without, fundamentally
mean evil toward the soul. Therefore, we must truly learn to answer
them confidently, as Joseph did his brothers: You
intend evil against me.

Certainly, they intended it poorly enough, in that they
sought to murder their innocent brother entirely.
As they themselves call this thinking and intention of theirs "wickedness"
in verse 15. For although they could not fulfill it in deed—
so that Joseph would have lost his life—nevertheless their
entire mind and will tended toward it, so that in their hearts they
had already struck him dead: indeed, their thinking was truly
a fratricide before GOD’s righteous eyes.

Since the good Joseph clearly recognized all the malice and horrors
of his enemies, how, do we think, might he not have sighed
and cried out to GOD the Almighty, that He might help him!
And oh, how the Lord heard him, and transformed
all that evil counsel into good!

**God intended it for good)** or considered, ordained,
arranged it. It was already a precious help that God
revealed and exposed the evil thoughts: and it was even
more that He transformed them into good.

God’s justice annihilates all evil thoughts against
His chosen ones at the right time.

The wise Joseph did not attribute all this good to himself, but
to GOD, out of the profound humility of his well-practiced heart.

This eternal GOD, in His deep truth and wisdom,
actually transformed and arranged all the evil plots against him
into good through His own good plans.

No one in heaven or on earth possesses this art but the
Lord alone: He alone can let evil
turn out to a good end. Yes, what is even more, at His
command, evil itself must actually cooperate for the good
of those who love God. *Rom. 8:28.*

How then did the LORD intend it for good with Joseph?
Or how did He arrange the evil thoughts for good? Answer:
By the fact that He suited all such tribulations to Joseph for his
purification, so that after sufficient humbling, he could bear
the greatest matters of honor and government with wisdom
and lowliness, and consequently help his entire lineage.

O how healthy for this man was all that mockery,
rejection, and plague! How powerfully all of that, from his youth,
disabused him of the world's shame and seduction,
so that he followed not his flesh and blood, but the Spirit of
GOD, and thus grew in grace in secret
under the Cross!

Furthermore, GOD arranged it so that in the midst of his misery,
certain people always had to become favorable to the good man
and help him along; indeed, that in the dungeon he became
acquainted with and liked by the court servants, and was
afterwards recommended to the King by one of them. Were
those not good thoughts of GOD over the evil thoughts of the brothers?

<column-break/>

to do as it is this day, to
save much people alive. 21.
---
Had Joseph not been sold by his brothers and
afterward imprisoned, he would never have become so great a
lord. But he did not become a great lord in order to
practice pride and luxury. Oh no, GOD did not have such
thoughts about him! But rather that he might spread
GOD's glory.

Notice then, with whom GOD intends to make things good!
Namely, with Joseph, with a sufferer: not with one
who wants to help and provide for himself. If you stand in the "press"
<note>Likely referring to a wine-press, a common metaphor for intense suffering or crushing pressure.</note>,
under internal or external distress, persecution, and the like;
then think that you are in the very state in which GOD
wants to make it good. Just wrap yourself in suffering and endure:
all the evil thoughts of enemies must cooperate for your good!

If it were not so, that GOD could make something good
even out of something evil; then GOD could not do all things.
Now, however, He even arranges sins for good: not
that He wants the evil itself; but rather, when He
foresees the sin, His wisdom and goodness work so that something
good follows from it.

Since Joseph’s brothers had so atrociously sinned against him,
who could have thought then that it should turn out
to a good end? Reason might think: Now
these people will all be uprooted and punished! But how
far were GOD’s thoughts from human ones! Instead
of punishment, GOD brought about through this very thing pure
rescue and salvation; and indeed, not only for the old Jacob, but also for
these murderous brothers.

O the great depth of the riches of divine love
and wisdom! How this eternal light goes directly
against human ways! How this eternal love works,
even in the greatest deviations, toward pure rescue,
restoration, and healing! Who can reach the wonders
and mysteries that lie hidden herein!

Who would still doubt the good thoughts of GOD over himself,
even if men thought nothing but evil! Who would not
learn to recognize in faith how wonderful GOD’s
counsel is, and how gloriously He carries it out! *Isa. 28:29.*

This is the most precious way to the glory of GOD
and to our exaltation in GOD. To this end, even our
worst enemies themselves must help us with their evil plots.
They must train and maintain us in prayer,
in trust, in hoping for the invisible.
In doing so, they grant us the greatest advantage,
against all their thanks and will.

Blessed is he who learns to find himself in this way that is
contrary to reason, even if he should be mocked for a long time
by his own and others' reason! One should only endure:
what does it matter? Will it not be best for those
who seek to pull through and help themselves not with evil plots,
but with faith?

It certainly requires waiting, to endure quietly
under all the shame and derision of adversaries,
like Joseph, who even at the beginning of his exaltation
did not once reveal the wickedness of his brothers to his father,
nor take revenge on them.

The best counsel for those who must yield and bend
among false brothers, or even public persecutors,
is: commit your ways to the LORD and hope in Him;
leave yourself and everything to Him who can distinguish
evil from good.

Only remain pious and innocent in the process, and hold yourself
upright, like Joseph. For such people, it must turn out well in the end.
Never has a single human being entered into glory
without resistance and testing.

Even the same Midianites or worldly masters to whom
Joseph was sold, often had to be helpful to him, so that
Joseph was brought before Pharaoh, and the malice of the false
brothers was later revealed. To such an extent do treachery and
falsehood get caught in their own net that they set for others.
And these are all mysteries of divine justice.

O that all those would consider it, who think like Joseph’s
brothers that their cunning shall help them through, that their
patrons, their idols, their conspirators will protect them;
those who bind themselves together with loose cords to do
harm and to oppress their neighbor, who is intolerable
to them because of the truth! Devise a plan; it
will come to nothing, if only Immanuel is with us!
*Isa. 8:10.*

# The Second Book of Moses.

In this book, the great work of God is narrated / how, according to his gracious promise, he led the descendants of Abraham out of Egypt / and the heavy servitude <note>The German "Dienstbarkeit" refers to the state of being a servant or slave; here it denotes the period of Israelite slavery.</note> which he had previously foretold to them / and rescued them from the cruelty of Pharaoh with a mighty arm. For this reason, this book is also called by the Greek name *Exodus* <note>original: "Exodus"</note>, which means / the Departure / because the children of Israel went out of Egypt / after God had first allowed them to fall into heavy tribulations under the King / in response to which he then visited the King with his people and land with heavy plagues / of which there were ten / these were carried out through the service of Moses / who / having been preserved by the wonderful governance of God in his childhood / had come to great honors with the King / but afterwards / being persecuted by him / had to leave Egypt / and was there called again by God / to lead the children of Israel out of Egypt. Chapters 1–11.

In memory of this wonderful departure and redemption, God instituted for them a mysterious feast / which they were to perform annually with the slaughter of a lamb in every house / and consume the same together: where they also had to smear their doorposts with its blood / to show / that they, along with all believers, should be redeemed from the power of Satan and the servitude of sin through the blood of the true sacrificial Lamb provided by God / his dear Son <note>This is a "typological" interpretation, a common practice in historical Bible commentaries where events in the Old Testament are seen as symbols or "types" foreshadowing the life of Jesus Christ in the New Testament.</note>. Chapter 12.

Following this is the wonderful journey and provision in the wilderness / where God first redeemed them from the wrath of Pharaoh / who pursued and reached them with his army: by leading his people through the sea / which he split before them and allowed to dry up; and when the enemies were so bold as to pursue them into the sea / they were drowned in the same: for which great redemption they then praised God with one accord. Furthermore, it was God's wise counsel / to lead them through a wilderness / and there to test them with hunger and thirst: but when their unbelieving heart revealed itself / they were nonetheless fed by God with bread from heaven and with quails / and were given to drink with water / which was brought forth from the rock. Wherein Christ once again / as the bread that would come from heaven / and give life to the world / and as the rock of salvation / from which the water of life would flow / intended to be prefigured. Furthermore, God also granted him a victory against the Amalekites / and through the advice of Moses's father-in-law / who followed him into the wilderness / and brought his wife and children to Moses / he allowed the governance of the people to be established through 70 elders. Chapters 13–18.

Afterward, God gave the people a law of ten commandments / in which the duties of love toward God and neighbor were presented: over which God also wished to make a covenant with the people / to bind them to obedience and holiness; through which, however, they were directed to the Covenant of Grace in the blood of Jesus Christ / to seek from this the forgiveness of sins and the power for sanctification. Along with this, some other laws / regarding physical dealings and punishments for certain vices / were added; because God wished to rule the people through immediate laws from him / as his special people. Chapters 18–24.

Specifically, God commanded this people to set up a certain sanctuary <note>referring to the Tabernacle or "Tent of Meeting"</note> / in which he should be served by the tribe of Levi with certain sacrifices and at certain times. Through which the only High Priest, Christ, with his once-for-all valid sacrifice / and that in the mysterious time of the New Testament / which should be a constant feast and remembrance of all God's benefits / was prefigured. Chapters 25–31.

During the time that Moses received such commands from God on the mountain / the people fell into a terrible sin of idolatry with the calf / because they wanted to have visible gods / just as they may have already fallen into the idolatry of that land while in Egypt / where such an idol / namely an ox / which they called Apis <term>Apis: An ancient Egyptian deity represented as a bull, symbolizing fertility and strength.</term> / was worshipped. Whereat God became so fiercely angry / that he wanted to destroy the people / if Moses had not prayed to God for them: who, however, allowed this sin to be avenged to some extent with the slaying of 3000 men / and thereafter promised the further leading of the people through the Angel of the Covenant, Christ. Chapters 32–34.

Following this, the construction of the sanctuary according to all its pieces is described very specifically / and that much more extensively than the works of creation: because the works of grace far surpass the works of nature. And finally, this completed Tabernacle <note>original: "Hütte des Stiffts"</note> was visibly filled with the glory of God. Chapters 35–40.

This book fits beautifully in sequence as the second after the first: in that it confirms the truth of the promises of the first—concerning the multiplication of Abraham’s descendants and the possession of the land of Canaan—within and through their fulfillment.

Just as in the first book of Moses <note>Genesis</note> great mysteries of the future lie hidden within the types of external histories, and all come together in Christ: so too in this second book of Moses lie such wonders and mysteries of Christ and His Church. Thus, Augustine rightly said that the New Testament is hidden in the Old, and the Old is revealed in the New; this book is cited twenty-five times in the New Testament, and Stephen—the first martyr of the New Testament—gives what is essentially an explanation of it in the Acts of the Apostles.

<margin>(a) In the dedication to the Commentary on Exodus.</margin>
There are indeed some who lack understanding, and perhaps not a few, writes Johannes Brenz (a) <note>Johannes Brenz (1499–1570) was a prominent German Reformer who wrote extensively on the Old Testament.</note>, who consider the labor spent in reading or explaining the books of Moses to be superfluous. They believe these books do not concern Christians, as disciples of the Gospel, because the name of Christ or the Gospel is not contained therein in express words. But if anyone examines these books with the right spirit, he will certainly find Christ and His Gospel enough within them: perhaps not as clearly, yet just as essentially and truly as in the books of the New Testament. For anyone who thinks that in the Second Book of Moses nothing is treated but Jewish matters foreign to Christianity would certainly be the most ignorant judge of biblical books. Since Christ and His Gospel are so diligently taught and illuminated there, if one wanted to give the subject matter its proper name, one would have to say that this book is a Christian Catechism <note>A manual of religious instruction</note> rather than the "Second Book of Moses." For

<margin>(b) To Honoratus, on the Profit of Believing, chapter 3.</margin>
What is the Passover Lamb and its ceremonies other than a sermon on Christ and His death on the cross? Is it not about the work of redemption connected to it, the power of His blood, and our participation in it? This is indeed the clear Gospel of Christ. To say nothing of the water from the rock or the manna from heaven: these placed Christ before the eyes of the believers of old. Even the Law of the Ten Commandments, through which comes the knowledge of sin, is a schoolmaster <note>The German "Zuchtmeister" (Greek: paidagōgos) refers to a guardian or tutor who guides a child; here it refers to the Law leading believers to Christ.</note> who drives us to Christ as a mediator. Let Aaron the High Priest then step forward, with all his sacrifices, his holy garments, and the other sacred furnishings: Christ and His Gospel will shine forth everywhere and be offered to us. What an excellent image is painted before our eyes of the state of the Church Militant <note>The "Church Militant" refers to the Church on earth, which is currently engaged in a spiritual struggle against sin and evil.</note>! How accurately the thorn-covered path to the eternal rest of the heavenly Canaan is drawn for us! So much so that Augustine (b) judged with good reason: if we were to diligently consider the resting places and camps of the people of Israel, and the nature of those places indicated in this book, we would perceive great wonders of the heavenly journey within them. How beautifully are the believers here reminded above all of the glorious exodus from spiritual Egypt, where a heavy servitude of both body and soul prevails in almost all places. Though tribulations will befall the believers in the final times, God will also eventually come with His plagues upon the enemies and lead His people out from among them with a mighty arm; but He will powerfully destroy those enemies, like Pharaoh and his army. It also indicates how God will lead His own into a wilderness during the great tribulations of the end times, but will also wonderfully sustain and refresh them there, granting them victory against the hellish Amalekites <note>The Amalekites were ancient enemies of Israel; here they represent spiritual foes or demonic forces.</note> in their many temptations. Revelation 12, 13–17. Finally, the true, permanent sanctuary will be gloriously erected in their souls and in their midst, where all these prototypes will be presented in their perfect essence. Then it will be said with emphasis:

> Behold, the tabernacle of God is with men, and he will dwell with them, and they shall be his people, and God himself shall be with them, and be their God!

v. 1. And) It may not be without reason that the first four books of Moses are joined together by the conjunction "And," just as most historical books also have it; even the First Book of Joshua is linked to the books of Moses by the same word. Likewise, the two prophets Jeremiah and Ezekiel, as well as Obadiah and Jonah, are joined together: to show, among other things, that these matters are interconnected and should be considered in succession.

v. 2-4. It is not without mystery that the order of the twelve patriarchs appears changed so often. One order is found at their birth, another when they moved into Egypt, another when they moved out of Egypt, another at the division of the land of Canaan, another when they set up camp, etc. For these twelve patriarchs prefigure the twelve fatherhoods in the heavens and the patriarchs of the spiritual sons of Israel.

v. 2-7. Here the twelve tribes are repeated together again, as they were first born of the two wives and afterwards of the two handmaids, just as in Genesis 35:23–26. This is to show that, just as only seventy souls of them were first in Egypt, so from those same souls there subsequently arose the great nation of more than six hundred thousand men over twenty years of age who went into the army—not counting women and children—within two hundred years through God's blessing in the great fertility of the children of Israel. They brought forth in such abundance that they must have often given birth to twins, triplets, quadruplets, or even quintuplets, as is said to have already happened among the Egyptians. <gloss>(a)</gloss> Naturalists <gloss>(b)</gloss> shall testify that there are seven chambers of conception <note>A common medieval and early modern medical belief that the uterus was divided into seven distinct cells or "chambers."</note>, in each of which a perfect birth could be formed and born into the world: which, because of the number seven, would also be significant in the spiritual birth of the faithful in the seven secret eras. Therefore, not only the land of Goshen but also the surrounding land of Egypt was filled with them, and, so to speak, swarmed with Israelites; so much so that the king began to harbor suspicion.

v. 6. 7. As long as Joseph lived, no mention is made of the multiplication of the children of Israel. We may boldly believe that not one iota <note>original: "Jota," referring to the smallest letter of the Greek alphabet</note>, not a stroke or a tittle in the Scripture is without mystery. Before our Joseph, Jesus Christ, died, his disciples were very few. But after He had tasted death for all, how great did the number of believers become! If the grain of wheat had not fallen into the earth and died, it would have remained unfruitful. But now that it has passed through death, what a fruitful multiplication has arisen from it!

v. 7. Fruitful) Philo says, with reasons that are quite probable, that the removal of the foreskin through circumcision contributed much to this.

<column-break/>

8. Then a new king arose over Egypt who did not know Joseph.
9. And he said to his people: "Behold, the people of the children of Israel are greater and more powerful than we!"
10. "Come, let us deal wisely with them, lest they multiply. Otherwise, it might happen that if a war should arise, they too might join our enemies, and fight against us, and depart out of the land."
11. And

---

v. 8. New King) But this is not the one who was still living at the exodus of the children of Israel; rather, he was a predecessor, and is said to have been named Amenophis, as Eusebius calls him. 
It appears this new king was from a different family, who then tend to disregard the beneficial decrees of their predecessors, and even to hold the previous faithful servants or their descendants in low esteem, even if they have served the land and people well. Indeed, even sons tend to pay little heed to the decrees of their parents. 
Therefore, in all one's actions, one should seek only to serve God and His church; then one retains in Christ a faithful and constant Lord, who will reward faithful service with eternal grace and will not forsake the seed of the righteous. See 1 Kings 12:8; Psalm 37:25, 28.

v. 9. 10. Worldly wisdom always seeks to hinder, or even to suppress, that which is good. And then the few believers must become a sacrifice to their bitter envy: then it is said, as when the Pharisees persuaded themselves regarding Christ: "If we let him alone, everyone will believe in him. Then the Romans will come and take away both our land and our nation." John 11:48. But here too, no wisdom, no understanding, no counsel avails against the Lord. Proverbs 21:30.
But who is the king in Egypt who knows Joseph? And who is the king who does not know him and wants to know nothing of him? Answer: When the Lord rules us, and our mind is enlightened by the Lord; when we keep Christ in our memory: then the Spirit, as long as He lives in Egypt—that is, in our flesh—leads the government in righteousness. But when our mind has lost the memory of Him, has turned away from God, and wants to know nothing of Christ; then the wisdom of the flesh follows in the government, which is an enmity against God, and takes counsel with its people—the fleshly lusts and vices—to suppress the seed of Israel: and the spirit of the world, which does not know the merits of Joseph or Christ, is then the ruler in our flesh.

<margin>(a) Ps. 105:24.</margin>

<column-break/>

13. And the Egyptians ruthlessly compelled the children of Israel to serve.
14. And they made their lives bitter with hard service in mortar <note>original: "Thon" - clay or wet earth used for building</note> and in bricks, and with all manner of service in the field; in all the service they compelled them to do, they acted with ruthlessness.

->15. And<-

---

The great burdens and plagues with which God allowed the children of Israel to be afflicted were a righteous judgment because of their idolatry, into which they had fallen while in Egypt. Thus, they had strayed from the path of their godly ancestors and followed the heathens among whom they lived. See Joshua 24:14, Ezekiel 20:7, 8, 23:3, and Amos 5.
In this way, persecutions are commonly the righteous judgments of God, through which God watches over His people when they wander onto the erring paths of the world; thus they must be disciplined and awakened. Yet the Lord knows how to preserve His own under such pressure, and even to increase them, just as happened with the early Christians. Hence it is said: the blood of the martyrs was the seed of the Church.

**v. 11. Pithom)** As **Kircher** (a) <note>Athanasius Kircher (1602–1680) was a famous Jesuit scholar and polymath who wrote extensively on Egyptian hieroglyphs and history.</note> notes, this city received its name from a monstrous serpent that emerged from the marshy morass of the Nile and caused great slaughter among men and cattle.

**v. 12. Spread out)** Besides the fact that the Hebrew word signifies breaking out like water, which tears down all dams and banks built to contain it, this also refers to the great growth and multiplication of both children and possessions.
In this, **Israel** according to the flesh prefigured the "Israel of God," who is supported by the power of God's grace. The Lord says that the oppressions of His people are like the waters of **Noah**. **Micah 7:15.** As the waters of Noah broke out, so was the Ark supported. Where the sufferings of Christ abound, there also comfort through Christ abounds. **2 Cor. 1:5.**
Therefore, do not let your courage sink, O you **Israel of God!** Though the Egyptian burdens and hardships be great, be strong and carry yourself like a palm tree, **Ps. 92:13.** which grows against the weight that is placed upon it.

<column-break/>

When things happen in Christendom such that taxes and burdens are increased, and people are made into serfs burdened with constant forced labor, then it takes on the true form of the spiritual **Egypt**, over which the plagues of the seven bowls of wrath will also be poured out.
**God** has not been content to give extraordinary examples of His guidance in individual people—the souls who have surrendered themselves to Him; He also wishes to give such examples in an entire people who are united in those same ways. He does this so that His chosen (a) <note>original: "auserwählt" - the elect or chosen ones</note> people may learn through a general, and thus more visible, prototype that everything must necessarily pass through this.

No one is exempt from this; it is necessary that all who are called to the hidden life (which is actually the "chosen people") pass through captivity and conversion. Was anything more fortunate than this people as long as **Joseph** lived? The very best of the entire kingdom was for them. Yet now they are in captivity, held more harshly than all other prisoners. All souls who are to be led through this path are, at the beginning of the spiritual life, placed in infinite and unspeakable delights. For on earth there are none equal to the heavenly ones that these people partake in. However, after **God** has assured Himself of this people's loyalty through so many benefits, He must also let them feel the hard captivity. And no one can remain exempt from it: because **Jesus Christ**, as the First among the Chosen and the Head of those who have surrendered themselves, was willing to leave His Father’s bosom (b) <note>original: "Schooß seines Vaters" - the heart or presence of the Father</note> to become the greatest captive among all men.

All must go through this way. The holy Patriarchs are the images of what was to be fulfilled in **Jesus Christ**. The saints of the New Covenant are likewise the imitations of it. But the Savior is the holy pattern and original of them all.
<margin>(a) in Oedipus <note>referring to Kircher’s work *Oedipus Aegyptiacus*</note></margin>

But why must all pass through this? Is it so that

---

they may remain so miserable forever? No: rather, it is so that they may possess the land promised to **Abraham**, **Isaac**, and **Jacob**. This Promised Land is nothing other than the possession of God. Oh, what should one not do to possess such a thing! And what sufferings are worthy compared to this possession?
**God** makes use of **Pharaoh** to bring these souls into captivity. But he is not alone in this office: He gives them taskmasters. Men, devils, and nature are the Egyptians to whom one is subjected. They burden these poor people with work, thinking to hinder their multiplication by oppressing them.

Even today, people still work in this way. They think to stifle the inner life through persecution and by speaking ill of it. But it is precisely then that it multiplies most. The more those people who teach such things are slandered, persecuted, and defamed, the more others join themselves to them to walk in these ways; it grows and multiplies even under persecution, just as the Church was strengthened and spread through the blood of the martyrs. The devils themselves join in with their cruel persecutions. And this is precisely the most painful part in the beginning, because of the weakness of nature, which wants to sink under the weight. But the more such a soul is burdened from all sides with weakness and misery, the more it rises up, like the palm tree, and multiplies.

The very hardest persecution for this people is that, after being raised in such a noble manner in communion with **God** and at His table, it sees itself forced to work in the earth <note>symbolizing worldly or base concerns</note>, just as one otherwise works in gold and silver, and to work for the sake of the earth. All its work is only earth: it seems to have become entirely nature and earth. Then the enemies mock the soul when they see it at such work, which is so contrary to its birth, upbringing, and hope. Such mockery and hatred from the people of this world has always tested souls standing in prayer. But a day will come on which they (c) will recognize their own folly and the wisdom of the pious.
