The Second Book of Moses. Chapter XIX.

# 5. And now, if you will diligently obey my voice and keep my covenant, then you shall be my special possession above all peoples! For the whole earth is mine.

# 6. And you shall be to me a kingdom of priests and a holy nation. These are the words that you shall speak to the children of Israel.

v. 5. You shall be my special possession above all peoples) In this way, God had taken for Himself a particular possession <note>original: "Eigenthum," referring to a treasured property</note> from among all peoples: (1) the people of Israel; (2) from among them, the tribe of Levi for His service; (3) from the clean animals, the firstborn for His sacrifice; (4) from the whole earth, the land of Canaan; (5) for the sustenance of His servants from this land, the tithes; (6) for His sanctuary, in which He was to be served and where He wished, as it were, to dwell, the Temple and the city of Jerusalem; (7) from time specifically, the Sabbath and the remaining feasts. See Psalm 114:2.

This expresses very well how, although all peoples belong to God, nevertheless the inner people <note>The "inner people" refers to those who are spiritually devoted, a common theme in Pietist thought</note> belong to Him in a quite extraordinary way. God says this inner people shall belong to Him as His own property and shall be acquired by Him in a special manner. This means that if one could truly practice self-negation <note>original: "vernichtigen," meaning to make oneself nothing before God</note>, one would become God's own in such a way that no other people but this one alone should have a share in it. No other way but this can have such a privilege. God also says that they shall be set apart for Him among all other peoples. He who names "all" excludes nothing.

Now, what God desires from this people who are so dear to Him—so that they may attain such a high standing—is only that they obey Him and remain in the way of yieldedness <note>original: "Gelassenheit," a central mystical term meaning a state of surrender, calmness, and letting go of self-will</note>.

The phrase *keep my covenant* is as much as saying: Remain in union with me.

v. 6. You shall be to me a kingdom of priests) Or a kingdom of the priests. This great glory of the people of Israel—that they should be a kingdom whose subjects were nothing but priests, who all should have the right to approach God to enjoy His blessed fellowship—was greatly obscured, if not entirely lost, through the sin of idolatry with the [golden] calf. For afterward, God took the tribe of Levi and Aaron in particular for such priestly dignity and excluded the remaining tribes from it. See Ezekiel 20:26. To which dignity the believers of the New Testament have attained once again. 1 Peter 2:9. Revelation 1:6, 5:10.

Without any doubt, it is also the will of God, and has been His intention and meaning from the beginning, that such a priesthood should be the general office or service of all His faithful and obedient people. Therefore, it is also promised here to Israel under the condition of obedience. Had they been faithful in such obedience, then this promise would undoubtedly have been fulfilled. But after they fell through idolatry, as mentioned, in Chapter 32, God chose—at that prompting—the tribe of Levi, which remained faithful at that time. But after these also became covenant-breakers, this promise was not only spread further—namely, to all repentant, believing, and obedient people—but it is also said in 1 Peter 2:9 and Revelation 1:6, 5:10 that it is indeed fulfilled. May God grant, however, that it may be fulfilled in us.

The "Kingdom" indicates, even according to the letter, the absolute power of God which He has over the yielded souls who do not resist Him. He is an absolute Lord over them, so that they themselves can no longer be lords. But with others, who possess themselves, He has a different relationship. For since they are free because of their own liberty and full of their own will, they desire many good things which God does not want, and only permits because of their weakness. But He rules as a mighty Lord over those who no longer have a will of their own. Therefore, when He taught His disciples to pray and said to them that they should ask that His kingdom might come—that is, that He alone might rule over them—He added: "and that His will be done, on earth as it is in heaven." As if they should have said thereby: "When this shall have happened, O Lord, then your will will be done here on earth as the saints do it above in heaven—without resistance, without wavering, without exception or delay." Therefore, in the Gospel, these two petitions are also enclosed in one verse.

A holy nation) One specially dedicated. When all the wickedness of man is destroyed within him, nothing but the holiness of God will remain. Then it will be a holy people to God, but not of itself. God also does not say simply, "you shall be a holy people," but "you shall be a holy people *to me*." And this is what He says to His dear leaders: "This is what you shall say to my precious, yielded ones."

<column-break/>

# 7. And Moses came and called for the elders of the people and laid before them all these words which the Lord had commanded him.

# 8. And all the people answered together and spoke: All that the Lord has spoken, we will do. And Moses brought the words of the people back to the Lord.

# 9. And the Lord spoke to Moses: Behold, I will come to you in a thick cloud, so that the people may hear when I speak with you, and believe you forever. So Moses announced the words of the people to the Lord.

<meta>10. Furthermore</meta>

v. 8. All the people answered together: — All — we will do.) They were quite ready with the promise of obedience and were thus unmindful of the great corruption and impotence <note>original: "Ohnmacht," meaning powerlessness or fainting</note> of the human heart. They should instead have recognized their misery—how the spirit is indeed willing but the flesh is weak—so that they should have asked God for the strength and grace for obedience. See Deuteronomy 5:27-29.

This unanimous agreement of the whole people beautifully expresses the surrender and sacrifice that souls make of themselves toward the ways that are set before them. God is so good that He always proceeds in this manner with those whom He wishes to lead into the ways of darkness and the Cross. Namely, He first presents these ways to them; afterward, He requests their agreement. For although He is the supreme Ruler, He nevertheless leads us with <margin>(a) Wisdom 12:18</margin> great (a) restraint <note>original: "Zurückhaltung," implying a respectful holding back</note>, as if He were honoring our freedom.

But alas! How rare it is to find some who surrender themselves entirely when this state has come! Almost everyone then forgets that they agreed and sacrificed themselves entirely to it. It also happens that the zeal and speed with which they perform their sacrifice cause them to forget their weakness and misery, and they answer like this people: "we will do everything!" But if they considered their weakness and their yieldedness at that very same time, these would teach them sufficiently that they can do nothing of themselves, and that through yieldedness they have divested themselves of all will in order to leave themselves entirely to God. They should rather have said: "May the Lord let everything be performed for us! Then we will do everything. For our faithfulness is in Him, just like everything else; and of ourselves, we are nothing but impotence and sin." This confidence and this leaning on oneself is a secret presumption, which always brings some sin—either great or small, depending on how far it has spread—in its wake.

v. 9. In a thick cloud) The darkness of the clouds indicates how God wants His inner people to believe solely based on faith, and not on evidence—founding themselves on the belief that He speaks through providence.

So that the people may believe you) God wants faith in His servants, the prophets, to be presented along with faith in Him, so that He is also honored in His ministers and messengers. See Chapter 14:31. Matthew 10:40, 41.

### Cap. XIX. The Second Book of Moses.

10. Further the LORD spoke to Moses: Go to the people and sanctify them today and tomorrow, that they may wash their clothes, <margin>Rev. 7:14.</margin>
11. And be ready for the third day. For on the third day the LORD will descend before the eyes of all the people upon Mount Sinai.
12. And make a boundary around the people, and say: Guard yourselves from climbing the mountain or touching its edge! Anyone who touches the mountain shall surely be put to death. <margin>Heb. 12:20. etc.</margin>

<column-break/>

13. No hand shall touch him; rather he shall surely be stoned or shot with a projectile. Whether it be a beast or a man, he shall not live! When the horn sounds slowly, then they shall climb up the mountain.
14. Then Moses went down from the mountain to the people and sanctified the people, and they washed their clothes.
15. And he spoke to the people: Be ready for three days; you shall not approach a woman. <margin>1 Sam. 21:4.</margin>
**16. And**

---

<margin>v. 10. Sanctify them)</margin> This sanctification commanded by God is a new purity, in order to enter into a new state of a new law of pure love.
<margin>today and tomorrow)</margin> Under the Law and the Gospel, in the Old and New Testaments.
<margin>v. 11. On the third day)</margin> Just as the Holy Trinity <note>original: "H. Drey-Zahl," the Holy Three-Number</note> is founded in the Godhead itself, and the same has revealed itself in three different ways under the names of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit: so also, according to these and their properties, offices, and works, there are 3 distinct times or days that follow one after another, and to each of which one is specifically assigned, according to the foundation of Holy Scripture.
The first time, of the Law or the Old Testament, was of the Father or the Ancient of Days, in which JESUS Christ was "yesterday" (Heb. 13:8) among the types and figures. When this time was fulfilled, God sent His Son (Gal. 4:4). And then appeared the day that Abraham desired to see, and he saw it in the spirit (John 8:56), which is the "Today" of JESUS Christ. In view of this, He is also called in Isaiah 9:6-7 a Father of the future age, namely that which should follow the one in which he spoke.
And the time itself is called in 2 Cor. 6:2 the day of salvation. But of no time and day is more prophesied in Holy Scripture than of the last day of judgment. That is now the day of the Holy Spirit, for which we wait, and at which the Savior aims in the words: "When the Comforter comes, he will rebuke the world" (John 16:8).
From which we may conclude that He shall carry out the office of Judge of the world (Isa. 4:4, 28:6).
Since the LORD especially praised this to Ezra (a), that He showed His servant Moses on Mount Sinai, alongside other mysteries, the secrets and the end of the times: so we may certainly believe that here, under the "third day," something further is seen and something quite secret is indicated.
That is now the Pentecost-Day of the Holy Spirit, the day of the second coming of Christ in the Spirit, when the fiery Law of Love of God shall be transfigured in the spirit. The prophet Hosea (b) also looked toward this when he prophesied in the spirit: "The LORD makes us alive after two days: He will raise us up again on the third day, that we shall live before Him."
Just as to each of the previous 2 days or times a special holy man was appointed as a visible and human leader who made the beginning of the covenant in their time; as here through Moses the Law was given, but through Christ in the second time the Gospel was proclaimed and its mystery revealed: so the third and last time shall be started by the prophet Elijah, whom God, according to the testimony of Malachi (c), will send before the great and terrible day of the LORD comes.
Whoever can grasp it, let him grasp it, think further on the matter, and use it as a key that will serve him well throughout the understanding of Holy Scripture!
<margin>v. 12. Make a boundary)</margin> As it appears from v. 24, a certain landmark or border was made of wood, or stones, or piled-up sand.
By this it was signified that free access to God through the Messiah was not yet manifest (Heb. 7:19, 10:19, etc.).
Moses, who had passed through the state of death, is led up the mountain where God is, as the beginning of this pure love. But because he was already purified, he was brought even to the source.
But for all others, it must cost them their life if they only approach the mountain or touch it; just as the LORD says: (d) "No man shall see me as long as he lives."

<column-break/>

<margin>v. 13. But what kind of death shall he die? Ah,</margin> not by the hand of a man, but through the shots of those arrows which You will pull against the heart, which cannot yet purely love You, O You God of my heart! without losing its own life. You will strike it to the ground with stones, because such a heart—since it would not allow itself to be struck down and softened by so many benefits with which You preceded it—is no better than a stony heart; and it is necessary that, as You have said to it through Your prophet (a), You take the stony heart from it to give it a heart of flesh, which loves You purely, a submissive and tractable heart, a pure and new heart.
**So shall those -- climb up)** But yet no further than the set limit of the boundary allowed, which therefore seems to have been made not down in the plain but at the root of the mountain, so that the people still had to climb upward somewhat and were permitted to come onto the mountain in their time, but not all the way up.
<margin>v. 14. 15. The outward cleansing of clothes should</margin> bring to the people's minds the inner purity of souls and sanctification, without which no one may see the LORD, and thus also may not approach Him (Heb. 12:14).
And there they should also abstain from women, because through innate lack of restraint the flesh can very easily be defiled; therefore, in special devotional exercises and humiliations, believers should apply themselves to all moderation. See Heb. 10:22, 23; 1 Cor. 7:5.
Since the Fall, man has become so animalistic in his members as well as in his will and desires, that he is often moved against his will by his violent and almost senseless imagination, so that he is ashamed of himself and has a secret testimony within him that it is an abomination before God's holy eyes—who would have man holy and pure—and is also a shame before men, by whom such desire is considered a great imperfection even according to reason. And this is undoubtedly the reason why God so often earnestly commanded total abstinence from such works before holy actions.
(a) Ezek. 11:19.

**The Second Book of Moses. Chapter XIX.**

**16. And it happened on the third day, when it was morning, that there arose a thundering (a) and lightning and a heavy cloud upon the mountain (b) and a very strong sound of a trumpet. All the people who were in the camp were terrified.**
<margin>(a) 1 Sam. 12:18. (b) Heb. 12:18. Job 38:1.</margin>

**17. And Moses led the people out of the camp to meet God (a), and they stood at the foot of the mountain.**
<margin>(a) Heb. 13:12-13.</margin>

**18. But the whole of Mount Sinai smoked; because the Lord descended upon it with fire: and its smoke went up like the smoke of a furnace (a), and the whole mountain trembled greatly.**
<margin>(a) Rev. 9:2.</margin>

---

This very terrifying and fearful preparation for the giving of the Law—which, according to the testimony of the Apostle, caused even Moses himself to shake and tremble—was an indication of the curse still resting upon sin. This curse, which was to be rebuked to some degree by the whole Law given on Mount Sinai, also had to be publicly proclaimed on Mount Ebal (Deut. 11:28-29, 27:13, etc.). Therefore, the Apostle notes the great difference between the giving of the Law on Sinai, which occurred with such fearful signs, and how the Law of the New Testament was given through the pouring out of the Holy Spirit in a loving manner in the region of Mount Zion in Jerusalem. There, God willed to imprint His law by His Spirit into the hearts of the believers and thereby promote their sanctification. Thus, we are now exhorted to approach the throne of grace with boldness and to ask God for the workings of the Spirit in our hearts, and not to refuse the Word that is now to be spoken to our hearts from heaven; so that through this we may be carefully moved to serve God and to please Him with discipline and fear. See Heb. 12:18-28, 10:19-25, Jer. 31:31-34, etc.

<margin>(a) Mark 3:17.</margin>
*v. 16. There arose a thundering etc.*) One imagines that the Word of God is pure sweetness: and it is also true, when one looks at it in itself, or when it is accompanied by a pleasant outpouring of grace; which then makes it entirely sweet and pleasant at the beginning of the spiritual life. But to those souls who stand at this stage—oh, to them it is full of terror and nothing but pure bitterness. Therefore, it was heard thus by John: and when he received the new name, having previously heard this thundering of the Word, he was called (a) a Son of Thunder <note>The author refers to "Boanerges," the title given to James and John.</note>.

*All the people — were terrified*) What wonder was it, since one can hardly read without shuddering and great inward reverence rising in the heart, with what great solemnity God published His Law.

*v. 18. Descended*) God is the center <note>original: "Centro"</note> or the innermost part of all: He is also the highest above all: He dwells in heaven, which is a pure, lovely, and refreshing outflow from Himself. The circumference or the perimeter of visible matter, however, is the outermost and thus the lowest, because it is the furthest from the Highest and from the spiritual essence of God as the center. Thus, when God is said to "descend," it means that He then visibly revealed Himself to us in or near the circumference or the outermost part of visible matter, since we are so closely bound to material bodies. And thus He also "ascends" again when He withdraws such visible revelation from us.

When God first appeared to Moses, He would not allow him to approach the fire in which He was without taking the shoes off his feet. But today, God leads Moses himself into the fire in which He was, because of the purity of his love, which had grown unto infinity. When He appeared to this faithful servant back then, it also happened in fire, to give him His benevolence and pure love. But now that He wishes to communicate the Law of pure love, He also appears to the children of Israel in the fire itself of love, since He is love itself. It could be no small fire that could ignite so many hearts.

From where does it come, O my Love, that you look so terrible here? Ah! It is only so to those who see you only from the outside and not in the workings of pure love. To these, because they look at things only superficially, she seems quite cruel toward those souls who surrender themselves to God. But certainly, inwardly and in itself, he <note>referring to God/Love</note> is very pleasant to the heart that is entirely abandoned to him.

<column-break/>

**19. And the sound of the trumpet increased and became very strong: Moses spoke, and God answered him with a voice.**

**20. When the Lord had come down upon Mount Sinai, on the peak of the mountain; then the Lord called Moses to the peak of the mountain, and Moses went up.**

**21. Then**

---

*v. 19. Moses spoke, and God answered*) What a pleasant conversation! God speaks with the soul, and the soul speaks back! The soul speaks with God, and God likewise listens! But there is even more communion of the soul with God for which no witnesses are necessary. Therefore God lets such a soul—

*v. 20. Climb to the peak of the Mountain of Love, namely to the highest peak of pure love: that is, she is taken up into God himself; but in such a high and excellent way that everything one might say about it is not to be compared with it.*

Then everything that had remained in the exterior itself, or in the lowest part of the human being, is changed and renewed through this pure love. Then this person is made spiritual, not only internally but also externally. O you holy fire! You have the power to renew the whole earth. These souls—or rather, this single soul among so many thousands of saints—goes not only onto this mountain, but also onto its highest peak or eminence: because she necessarily had to gather a great store of this pure love, both for herself and for all others. It was necessary that she draw from this fountain of fire, so that as a fiery furnace she could communicate this holy fire to such a great people. Ah, Moses, you have surely changed your standing! Before this, when you were in your humility of holy exercises, you judged yourself unworthy to speak to a king and to the people of Israel. But now, in your deepest <term>Gelassenheit: a state of surrendered calmness and letting-go of the self</term>, you have no trouble or resistance in climbing to the highest step in God, to speak so familiarly with Him, and to become His chosen vessel, full of Himself. This is because annihilation <note>original: "Vernichtung"</note> causes a person to no longer look at themselves, nor to heed their lowliness anymore; and because they are thus below all lowliness, they are for that very reason above all height.

That Mount Sinai otherwise has, so to speak, only one root but two peaks has already been touched upon somewhat above: one of which, from the setting of the sun, was called Horeb, from the wilderness and desert; the other, however, faced toward the rising of the sun and was called Sinai, from the thorns growing frequently there: and otherwise this part is far higher than the former, and also very difficult to climb. For its height is said to extend to 700 steps, not including the places where one walks level. Therefore, according to the testimony of della Valle <note>Pietro Della Valle, a famous 17th-century Italian traveler</note>, it is a half-day's journey up—or, as Thevenot (a) <note>Jean de Thévenot, a French traveler</note> reports, it is 3 hours' walk high.
<margin>(a) in the 27th chapter of the 2nd book of his Oriental Travels</margin>

# Chapter XX.
## The Giving of the Law on Sinai.

And God spoke all these words and said:

<gloss>God spoke all these words: that is; the Angel of the Covenant, Christ Himself, who is the true God, and who, as the Mediator between His Father and the people, wished to present to them the order of salvation. In this order they must stand if they are to be God's people in deed and wish to comfort themselves with His gracious gifts. For as it is written: God was in Christ, reconciling the world to Himself (2 Corinthians 5:19); so it is also said: God was in Christ and gave the law on Mount Sinai through Him. See Acts 7:35-38.</gloss>
<gloss>He was surrounded by many thousands of holy angels (Deuteronomy 33:2) as their Head, to whom all the angelic hosts had to stand at His service. Therefore the Apostle notes that it was spoken through angels (Galatians 3:19, Hebrews 2:2, and Acts 7:53)—namely, through their active arrangements, appearing as flames of fire or flaming torches around the throne of God, and thus seen in that form by the people (v. 18, compared with Psalm 104:4). Yet it was actually the Lord Himself who spoke from the midst of the host of angels surrounding Him. These are called "Ten Words" in Chapter 34:28 because they were the ten principal commandments upon which God specifically wished to make His covenant with them (Deuteronomy 4:13). He wished to present the most excellent primary duties: love toward God and love toward one's neighbor—which God requires just as much as love for Himself. Only through the observation of these could they participate in the grace of God in the Mediator. Not that they could be saved through the works of such a law, but that through love, which was the core of this law, they should demonstrate that their faith in the promise made to the fathers was of the right kind, coming from a sincere heart that cannot help but love the benevolent God in return, and for God's sake, also love their fellow human beings.</gloss>
<gloss>...were subjected to the bondage of sin; into which man fell as into a house of servitude through the guilt of his own disobedience, having been cast out of the paradise of freedom.</gloss>
<gloss>You cannot hear this voice as long as you are in Egypt. Even having escaped from it, you do not hear it immediately; for it is then still too early. Even when you have come to Marah, to Elim, and to Rephidim <note>These are stops on the Israelites' journey representing stages of spiritual testing.</note>, you are still not yet judged fit to hear these words. Rather, only after much endured toil and bitter labor, sorrow and vexation, and after many overcome temptations, will you receive the new law of love from your God. Thus the law will be renewed in you, or explained and transfigured anew in the new essence of the Spirit.</gloss>

<column-break/>

24. And the Lord said to him: Go, get down; afterward you shall come up, and Aaron with you. But the priests and the people shall not break through to come up to the Lord, lest He break out against them.
25. And Moses went down to the people and told them.

<gloss>v. 24. Aaron with you. But the priests — not) Oh, how good it is to be united with such holy souls! They receive the very thing they obtain for themselves also for those who are united with them. Although the whole people of Israel were united with Moses as with a father, Aaron was nevertheless joined to him in an exceptional way; he was, as it were, associated with the fatherhood of Moses, as no one else was in this manner. There are also people whom God connects in this way between two alone in the union of a fatherhood: and all others who are joined with them...</gloss>

2. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.
3. You

<gloss>God wishes to give us to understand with these opening words: on one hand, that He is and wishes to be our highest friend, ally, and reward, offering Himself to us for that purpose; on the other hand, that the Ten Commandments are now no longer a prescription of a Covenant of Works, but of a Covenant of Grace, in which faith is required from the very beginning in the One who says:</gloss>
<gloss>I am the Lord) The JEHOVAH <note>A rendering of the Tetragrammaton, emphasizing God's eternal, self-sufficient existence.</note>, the single, inaccessible life and light: but also specifically</gloss>
<gloss>Your) reconciled in Christ JESUS</gloss>
<gloss>God) Who, through revelation and communication, wishes to become specifically your own possession.</gloss>
<gloss>Who else is meant here but Jesus Christ in particular, the Lawgiver Himself? Just as the commandments themselves relate primarily to Him, more of which will be heard in what follows. God cannot be called our God in any other way than in Him, in whom we become acceptable to God and His children.</gloss>
<gloss>But if one thinks the following words do not apply to us, because we are not the ones whom the Lord</gloss>
<gloss>Brought out of the land of Egypt:) Oh, then one unfortunately betrays oneself that they are still stuck in the thickest Egyptian darkness, knowing nothing of redemption, nor having been rescued from the heavy yoke and hand of the harsh taskmasters!</gloss>
<gloss>If these words do not concern you, then God does not concern you, and you do not concern God: He is not your God, and you have no part in Him.</gloss>
<gloss>God speaks these words to those who despise the spiritual Egypt—that is, the present world—looking upon it with their backs turned and having left it in their minds; those who no longer serve the Egyptians, whom they served in the state of...</gloss>
<gloss>Indeed, what is to be said of Egypt? Even if you have already escaped from it, you do not hear these words immediately: you must first have gone through the Red Sea; and even then it is still too early. Even when you have come to Marah, to Elim, and to Rephidim; you are still not yet judged fit to hear these words. Rather, only after much endured toil and bitter labor, sorrow and vexation, and after many overcome temptations, will you receive the new law of love from your God. <meta>This page continues the commentary on Exodus 20. While the previous page established the setting of the Giving of the Law at Sinai through a Christological lens—identifying the "Angel of the Covenant" as Christ—this page begins the specific exposition of the Commandments. <header>The Second Book of Moses. Chapter XX.</header>

### 3. You shall have no other gods before my face.

First, GOD wants man to direct the love, fear, and trust—which he should have for Him, the true GOD, alone—toward no creature. For GOD sees all things; before His face, even the innermost stirrings of the heart are revealed. It is a belittling of GOD when a creature turns away from the Creator toward fellow-creatures to expect pleasure, comfort, and protection from them. See Job 31:24-28, Ephesians 5:5, Philippians 3:19.

God wants to be loved not just more than everything else, but solely and purely—that is, for His own sake. He desires that we trust Him and seek our salvation, pleasure, joy, and comfort in Him alone. Even in physical and spiritual matters, one should not despise the means <note>The "means" refers to earthly tools like medicine or rituals used by God</note>, yet one must not make an idol out of those means either.

"Other gods" are therefore all those things upon which our faith, love, and hope are placed outside of the true God.

Is not, for example, Astaroth, the goddess of the Sidonians—that is, goods and riches—worshipped to this very day, and more than ever before?

<margin>Revelry <note>original: "κῶμος"</note>, gluttony, and drunkenness, Romans 13:13.</margin>
What is Chemosh, the abomination of the Moabites, other than the revelry of these latter times, which is worshipped day and night?

Are there not so many "Baalim," or ruling lusts, that they cannot all be counted?

And what shall be said of the inward Anti-Christ, who has seated himself as God in the temple of the heart, and who sets himself up as the "opposing anointing" <note>The author contrasts a false spiritual influence (the "opposing anointing") with the true Holy Spirit</note> which teaches lies, against the true anointing of the Spirit of Christ, who leads into all truth?

**Before my face)** others translate this (a) as *outside* or *beside* my face; still others (b) as *upon* my face. All of these have a good and correct meaning, and none contradicts the others. For:

The Son of God is "God’s Face"; as seen for example in Exodus 33:14-15 compared with chapter 34:9. Also, in the priestly blessing of Numbers 6:25-27, it is indicated clearly enough that the Holy Spirit may also be so named. The reason for this name is that the Father is known in the Son, and not otherwise than in the light of the Holy Spirit, just as a person is recognized by their face.

Outside of or beside this Triune God, we shall have no others—no foreign gods, no "after-gods" <note>counterfeit or lesser gods</note>—all of which cover and darken the face of God, or Christ within us, whenever they come upon or over it.

Look now to how you stand before God in this regard, and search to the very bottom whether you have any foreign gods within you; see if they do not lie over the Lord’s face and hide it from you! Isaiah 59:2. Truly, everything to which the heart is attached without the Lord and His righteousness—whatever it may be—is a foreign, a false god! Because the Lord alone should be loved with our whole heart.

> (a) Thus the Jewish scholar Rabbi Bechai himself, in his commentary on this passage, explains these words: You shall have no other gods besides Him who is my face.
> (b) Arias Montanus <note>A 16th-century Spanish Orientalist and editor of the Antwerp Polyglot Bible</note>

<column-break/>

### 4. You shall not make for yourself a carved image or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is on the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.

### 5. You shall not bow down to them nor serve them. For I, the Lord your God, am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me: Psalms 109:9, 13, 14.

### 6. And showing mercy to many thousands; namely, those who love me and keep my commandments.

7. You

God also forbids man from setting before his eyes any external shape or image—either of Him, the true God, or any other self-chosen idol. Man must not imagine that by bowing before such a mute, dead idol, he has shown honor to his Creator or his self-fashioned god. Rather, he should strive to seek God in the innermost depths of his heart, to love, fear, and trust Him there, so as to serve Him in spirit and truth, and thus expect all help and protection from Him. See Psalm 115, Habakkuk 2:18, 19, 20.

Where this does not happen, "other gods" appear. This includes everything that the imagination itself turns into a god, ascribing to it a divinity or something that belongs only to the true God: such as fear, faith, hope, love, etc.

Whatever a man thus devises for himself as a god is either a created thing or a man's own mere imagination, which he often has even concerning the true God.

Whether it is a creature or a human invention, the divinity of that creature or invention depends entirely on the man; it is, in fact, an idol—though not until the man thinks it is a god and holds it as such in his mind. 1 Corinthians 8:4.

Thus, according to His will expressed here, God permits:

**No carved image)** of any creature for the purpose of showing it honor, worshipping it, or calling upon it.

Only Christ, the image of the invisible God, is the one in whom God is served in the purest way, and without whom we may not approach Him, as He is a consuming fire. But all other images He will not suffer or permit—

God wants them abolished, wherever they may be.

**Any likeness)** Even if it were only painted for that purpose, regardless of what it was modeled after.

If no image or likeness of any creature was allowed to be made for worship or veneration, then it was least of all permitted to be done of God Himself. On one hand, because it is simply impossible. Isaiah 40:18-25. For who can represent the infinite Spirit in a body? On the other hand, nothing but offense can arise from it, providing an occasion for something unseemly to be attributed to God in one's thoughts. Such things provoke the Lord to jealousy. Therefore He says:

**v. 5. I the Lord your God am a jealous God)** And so all chastisements and plagues—indeed, all the ways of God—cry out with power into the secure hearts: "O man, consider that it is I who warns you, I who strikes you, so that you may accept discipline, recognize my hand, and bow beneath it!" I am a jealous God! I am the one who punishes sins! Just as, conversely, all the benefits and tender enticements of God testify of Him, that it is He who then:

**v. 6. Shows mercy to many thousands)** For this purpose, surely, every little blade of grass was created: so that God might convince us through them that He alone is God, and besides Him there is no other.

Just as God so earnestly testifies of Himself and His essence—that He is and what He is—so we should rightly respond with a humble echo of a contrite spirit: "Yes, dear God, it is I; I am the most ungrateful, disobedient creature; I am a sinful man!"

How healthy this will be for our souls if we truly take note of this "I am" and answer correctly! For so many false gods announce themselves to our hearts, wanting to steal our love.

But we see here how much God looks for and seeks only those who:

**Love Him)** And we look at the words following immediately, in which He defines what "loving Him" consists of, and who those are whom He recognizes as His lovers: namely, those who:

**Keep my commandments)** And here again it is clear as day that Christ, and His Spirit and grace, are included in the Law. For without Him, it is impossible to keep God's commandments, and without Him, it is also impossible for God to do us good.

Those who accept and "put on" Christ also obtain His Spirit with Him, through which they are made so willing that they gladly act according to His commandments.

# 7. You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain! For the Lord will not leave him unpunished who takes His name in vain.

With this, God forbids man from speaking or thinking of Him and divine matters in a vain and frivolous manner. Instead, one should do so with due fear, honor, and devotion, so as not to become a partaker of the heavy punishment of such a majestic and almighty God, who will not allow the honor of His name to pass unavenged. See Leviticus 24:10, etc.

<term>Name</term> in Holy Scripture refers to everything found and recognized in a person, through which they are made even more clearly known and praised: for example, all attributes, virtues, works, words, sons, etc. For through these, someone becomes revealed and known for who they are, and is also praised and glorified. And indeed,

The <term>Name of the Lord</term> must be something great and holy: because the saints fearfully reminded God of it when they prayed, and God invokes it when He wishes to confirm something. "Lord, be gracious for Your <term>Name's</term> sake!" they say. And when God speaks, "For My <term>Name's</term> sake I will be gracious," He can remind Himself of nothing higher or holier.

In particular, this Name is understood to be the Son of God, to whom this commandment may especially refer. He is the one of whom the Father says in the following chapter 23:21: "My Name is in his innermost being." <note>original: "Mein Name iſt in ſeinem Innerſten." This is a Christological interpretation of the "Angel of the Lord" in Exodus 23.</note>

One must therefore take great care not to treat this great and glorious name improperly. God desires that one should not even

<term>Take it in vain</term>. And what does that mean? Commonly, it is understood as cursing, swearing, blasphemy, or other frivolous and dissolute misuse of God's name. But that is by far not the full meaning of these words.

A wife bears the name of her husband, and the bride or Church of Christ bears the name of her Lord and Head, as does every member of the same. This should not happen in a vain, false, or lying way, without being grounded in the truth.

And what else is primarily meant by this, in a word, than <term>Hypocrisy</term>—all false assumptions and appearances of godliness, all false, invented, and imitated holiness?

God's name is therefore misused and dishonored not only when one carries it habitually and in vain in an impure mouth, or when one lacks proper thoughts or speech regarding God's virtues, omniscience, wisdom, omnipotence, omnipresence, justice, and mercy; but also when one prays to God without devotion, approaching Him only with the lips. This is true especially and above all when one calls oneself by God's name—such as Israel, God's children, or Christians—in a vain and hypocritical manner while the reality is the opposite. As in 2 Timothy 2:19: when one allows the name of Jesus, the Savior and Redeemer, to serve as a false security, and does not live and walk as a member and brother of Christ, while nevertheless boasting of being a child of God and of the redemption and brotherhood of Christ.

This is not only the most natural and proper understanding suggested by the words themselves, but it is also indicated by the following: The Lord will

<term>Not leave him unpunished</term> or, as some translate from the Hebrew, <term>not cleanse</term>. <note>The Hebrew word "naqah" can mean both "to leave unpunished" and "to be clean/pure."</note> Since the commandment is directed against hypocrisy, and the ultimate goal of the Law and the Gospel is to make man pure as God is pure, and holy as He is holy, the Lord threatens that He will not cleanse one who usurps God's name and covers themselves with an outward appearance of holiness, but does not desire to have the indwelling, essential holiness. This is a deserved reward and the specific punishment of hypocrites, who do everything they do only for show, and therefore love images and forms, gestures and ceremonies, relying on outward services. They boast and pride themselves as if they were indeed God's people in truth simply because they consider themselves as such. It is just for the most holy God not to cleanse such people from their sins, because they neither desire nor seek true and essential righteousness. He gives them exactly what they seek and desire: namely, a reputation and respect among men, as if they were pure, just, and holy. Thus, they receive their reward! <note>A reference to Matthew 6:2, "Verily I say unto you, they have their reward."</note>

God's Name is and signifies God's Essence, and it requires essence, sincerity, deed, and truth from all who bear His name. And

Therefore, do not so easily give yourself out to be God's covenant-partner, people, servant, child, a Christian, priest, or apostle, where you are not so in deed. For one should not joke with God.

<column-break/>

# 8. Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. 9. Six [days you shall labor...]

Because the Lord created heaven and earth in six days and ceased or rested on the seventh day, man is commanded to work six days and rest on the seventh. The reason is that man was created in the image and likeness of his God. When man fell from that state, he was invited back to it: so that he might follow his God in doing and not-doing, and in the renewal of his work, in laboring and resting. Just as our God had His going-out through the six days and rested on the seventh day, so fallen man has his return to God through his six days of labor and rests on the seventh. In this way, man returns after the conclusion of his six days and comes to the spiritual seventh; and thus both God and man meet each other at the Sabbath of true rest. God goes out from Himself through six stages and rests on the seventh; and man goes out of himself through six days and also rests on the seventh day.

But because two things are to be considered in rest—resting *from* something and resting *in* something—the first rest is that with Christ according to the flesh, that we die in and with Christ and cease from sin; the other rest is in Christ according to the spirit, when we return to God.

This is the purpose of God's institution, for which He blessed and sanctified the seventh day. All men from Adam onward should have known and continued this, as it was initially made known to them (Genesis 2:2-3), had not the great corruption and forgetfulness of the true God and His service brought men into such neglect of keeping this day holy. Therefore, God specifically wished to reinforce this first institution for His people here by commanding them to "remember" it. See Isaiah 58:13-14, Ezekiel 20:11-12, 20, etc.

The Jews otherwise maintain, according to Selden's account <margin>(a) Book 3 of *On Natural Law and the Law of Nations according to the Teachings of the Hebrews*, chapters 9, 10, 11.</margin> <note>John Selden (1584–1654) was an English jurist and scholar of Jewish law. The Latin title cited is *De Jure Naturali et Gentium juxta Disciplinam Ebraeorum*.</note>, that the Sabbath was given only to the Jews alone, just as it was first given on the seventh day after their departure from Egypt when they camped in Marah, shortly before the giving of the Law. And one can agree with them in both respects to a certain degree. For

That the Patriarchs kept an outward rest of the seventh day as a commandment from the Lord—of this one finds at least not the slightest trace. On the other hand, it is frequently mentioned from the times of Moses onward.

Concerning Adam, one reads only of one commandment that was not inscribed in the natural conscience of all men: namely, not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. If the prohibition regarding the Sabbath had bound the first man, it would have had to be given to him as explicitly as the one regarding the tree. Likewise, in the rest of the entire history of the Patriarchs, nothing is to be found concerning the Sabbath. Although one reads that Abel, Noah, Abraham, and Jacob offered sacrifices, it is never added that this occurred on the Sabbath.

It is also nowhere indicated in Scripture that God demanded such rest from His believers at that time with even a single word, or testified to a pleasure in such a way of sanctification, or was angered by any negligence in this regard, etc.

But by the time Moses wrote this history and these books, the Sabbath had certainly already been instituted.

Since, however, many Christian men and even quite a few of the ancient Church teachers are of the opinion that it was instituted by God immediately after Creation, and that the institution is clearly contained in those words: "God sanctified it," it is best that in the face of such differing opinions, one should leave the other to the Lord, and each meanwhile seek to have an abundance of faith and love.

## 3. You shall have no other gods before my face.

First, GOD wants man to never turn the love, fear, and trust—which he should have for the true GOD alone—toward any creature. For GOD sees this; all the innermost stirrings of the heart are manifest before His face. It is a belittlement of GOD when the creature turns away from the Creator and toward his fellow-creatures to expect pleasure, comfort, and protection from them. See Job 31:24-28, Ephesians 5:5, and Philippians 3:19.

GOD wants to be loved not just more than everything else, but alone and purely—that is, for His own sake. He desires that man trust Him and seek his salvation, pleasure, joy, and comfort in Him alone. While one should not despise the practical means for physical and spiritual needs, one must not make an idol out of those means either.

<margin>Is not, for example, Ashtaroth <note>Ashtaroth was a Canaanite goddess; here the author uses her as a symbol for material wealth.</note>, the goddess of the Sidonians—that is, goods and riches—worshiped to this very day, and more than ever before?</margin>
Accordingly, "other gods" are all those things upon which our faith, love, and hope are set outside of the true GOD.

Are there not so many <term>Baalim</term> <note>The plural of Baal; here used to represent various "mastering" passions.</note> or ruling lusts that they cannot all be counted?

What shall we say of the inward Anti-Christ, who has seated himself as GOD in the temple of the heart? He sets himself up as the "adverse anointing" <note>The author contrasts the "false" spirit of the world with the "true" anointing of the Holy Spirit.</note> which teaches lies, opposing the true anointing of the Spirit of Christ, who leads into all truth.

**Before my face**) Others translate this as (a) "besides and alongside my face," and still others (b) "upon my face." All have a good and correct meaning, and none contradicts the other. For:

The Son of GOD is GOD’s "Face" (or Presence); as can be seen, for example, in Exodus 33:14-15, compared with chapter 34:9. In the priestly blessing of Numbers 6:25-27, it is clearly indicated that the Holy Spirit may also be so named. The reason for this name is that the Father is recognized in the Son, and only through the light of the Holy Spirit, just as one recognizes a person by their face.

Outside or alongside this triune GOD, we should have no other, no foreign, no "imitation" gods, all of which cover and darken the Face of GOD—or Christ within us—whenever they come upon or over it.

See to it now, how you stand before GOD in this regard, and search to the very bottom whether you have any foreign gods within you; see if they do not lie over the Lord’s face and hide it from you! Isaiah 59:2. Truly, everything upon which the heart is fixed without the Lord and His righteousness—whatever it may be—is a foreign, false god! Because the Lord alone should be loved with our whole heart.

## 4. You shall not make for yourself a carved image or any likeness of anything that is in heaven above, or that is on the earth beneath, or that is in the water under the earth.

## 5. You shall not bow down to them nor serve them. For I the Lord your God am a jealous God, visiting the iniquity of the fathers upon the children to the third and fourth generation of those who hate me: <margin>Psalm 109:9, 13, 14.</margin>

## 6. And showing mercy to many thousands; namely, to those who love me and keep my commandments.

<margin>7. You</margin>
GOD also forbids man from placing any external form or image before his eyes—whether of Him, the true GOD, or any other self-chosen idol. Man should not imagine that by bowing before such a mute, dead idol, he has shown honor to his Creator or to a god of his own making. Rather, he should strive to seek GOD in the innermost depths of his heart, and there love Him, fear Him, and trust in Him, so as to serve Him in spirit and truth, and thus expect all help and protection from Him. See <margin>Psalm 115, Habakkuk 2:18-20.</margin>

Where this does not happen, "other gods" arise: this includes everything that your own imagination turns into a god, attributing to it divinity or something that belongs only to the true GOD—such as fear, faith, hope, love, etc.

Whatever man thus devises for himself as a god is either a created thing or a man's own mere imagination, which he often has even concerning the true GOD.

Whether it is a creature or a human invention and discovery, the "divinity" of that creature or invention depends entirely on the person. It is in fact an idol; but it does not become so until the person thinks it is a god and holds it as such in his mind. 1 Corinthians 8:4.

According to His will expressed here, GOD does not permit:

**A carved image**) of any creature for the purpose of bestowing honor upon it, worshiping it, or calling upon it.

Only Christ, the image of the invisible GOD, is the one in whom GOD is served in the purest way, and without whom we may not approach Him, who is a consuming fire. But GOD wants all other images abolished, wherever they may be. He will not even suffer or permit:

**Any likeness**) Even if it were painted only for that purpose, regardless of what it was taken from.

If no image or likeness of any creature was to be made for worship or veneration, it was least of all permitted for GOD Himself. On one hand, because one cannot (Isaiah 40:18-25)—for who can represent the infinite Spirit in a body? On the other hand, nothing but offense can arise from giving occasion for GOD to be imagined in the thoughts as something unseemly. This then provokes the Lord to jealousy. Therefore He says:

**v. 5. I the Lord your God am a jealous God**) And thus all chastisements and plagues—indeed, all of God's ways—cry out with power into secure hearts: "O man, consider that it is I who warn you, I who strike you, so that you might accept discipline, recognize my hand, and bow beneath it!" I am a jealous GOD! I am He who punishes sins! Conversely, all of God's benefits and the lures of His love testify of Him, that He is the one who:

**v. 6. Shows mercy to many thousands**) To this end, surely every blade of grass was created: that GOD might convince us through them that He alone is GOD, and besides Him there is no other.

Just as GOD so earnestly testifies of Himself and His essence—that He is and what He is—so we should rightly respond with a humble echo of a contrite spirit: "Yes, dear GOD, it is I; I am the most ungrateful, most disobedient creature; I am a sinful man!"

How healthy this will be for our souls, if we truly take note of this "I am" and answer it rightly! For so many false gods announce themselves to our hearts and wish to steal our love.

We see here, however, how much GOD watches for this, seeking only those who:

**Love Him**) And we see from the words immediately following what He considers "loving Him," and whom He recognizes as His lovers: namely, those who

**Keep His commandments**) And here again it is clear and bright that Christ, and His Spirit and grace, are included in the Law. For without Him, it is impossible to keep the commandments of GOD, and without Him, it is also impossible for GOD to do us good.

But those who receive and put on Christ also obtain His Spirit with Him, through whom they are made so willing that they gladly act according to His commandments.

**Chapter XX. The Second Book of Moses.**

**7. You shall not take the name of the LORD your God in vain! For the LORD will not leave him unpunished who takes His name in vain.**

By this, God forbids man from speaking or thinking of Him and divine matters in a vain and frivolous way. Instead, one should do so with due fear, reverence, and devotion, so as not to become a partaker of the heavy punishment of such a majestic and almighty God, who will not let the honor of His name go unpunished. See Leviticus 24:10, etc.

*Name* in Holy Scripture means everything that is found and recognized in someone, through which such a person is made even more manifest, known, and praised: for example, all attributes, virtues, works, words, sons, etc. For through these, someone becomes revealed and known for who they are, and is also praised and glorified. And indeed,

The *Name of the LORD* must be something great and holy: because the saints primarily remind God of it when they pray, and God brings it up when He wishes to solemnly affirm something. *Lord, be gracious for Your name's sake!* they say. And when God says: *For my name's sake I will be gracious:* He can remind Himself of nothing higher or holier.

In particular, the *Son of God* is understood through this name, to whom this commandment may also specifically apply. He is the one of whom the Father says in the following chapter 23:21: *My name is in His innermost being.* <note>The author connects the "Name of God" directly to the person of Jesus Christ, suggesting that to misuse the name is to misuse the revelation of the Son.</note>

One must therefore take great care not to treat this great and glorious name improperly. God desires that one should not even

*Take it in vain)* And what does that mean? Generally, it is understood as cursing, swearing, blasphemy, or other frivolous and careless misuse of God's name; but that is by far not the full meaning of these words.

A wife bears the *name of her husband*, and the bride or Church of Christ bears the name of her Lord and Head, and every member of the same does as well. This should not happen in vain, falsely, or deceitfully, without being grounded in the truth.

And what else is primarily meant by this, in a word, than *hypocrisy*—all false assumptions and appearances of godliness, all false, fictional, and imitated holiness?

God's name is therefore misused and dishonored not only when one carries it out of habit in a vain and unclean mouth, or when one does not hold proper thoughts or speeches regarding God's virtues, omniscience, wisdom, omnipotence, omnipresence, justice, and mercy; but also when one prays to God without devotion and approaches Him only with the lips; but especially and most of all, when one calls oneself by God's name in a vain and hypocritical way—such as Israel, God's children, or Christians—while the opposite is true. According to 2 Timothy 2:19: when one allows the name of Jesus, the Savior and Redeemer, to serve as a false sense of security, and does not live and walk as a member and brother of Christ, while nevertheless boasting of being a child of God and of the redemption and brotherhood of Christ.

This is not only the most natural and proper understanding suggested by the words, but the following also points toward it: *The LORD will*

*Not leave him unpunished)* Or, as some translate from the Hebrew, *not cleanse him.* <note>The Hebrew word "naqah" can mean both "to leave unpunished" and "to be clean" or "innocent."</note> Because this commandment is directed against hypocrisy, and the ultimate goal of the Law and the Gospel is to make man clean, as God is clean, and holy as He is holy; thus the Lord threatens that He will not cleanse one who usurps God's name and covers himself with an outward appearance of holiness but does not desire to have the indwelling, essential holiness. And that is a deserved reward and the specific punishment of hypocrites, who do everything they do only for appearance's sake, and therefore love images and forms, gestures and ceremonies, resting in outward services, boasting and defying as if they were indeed and in truth God's people because they consider and present themselves as such. It is just for the most holy God not to cleanse such people from their sins because they do not desire or seek true and essential righteousness; and to give them, moreover, what they seek and desire: namely, a reputation and respect among men, as if they were clean, righteous, and holy. Thus, they receive their reward!

God's name is and signifies God's essence, and it requires from all who bear His name essence, purity, deed, and truth. And

Therefore, do not so easily give yourself out to be God's covenant-partner, people, servant, child, a Christian, priest, and apostle, where you are not so in deed. For one should not jest with God.

<column-break/>

**8. Remember the Sabbath day, to keep it holy. 9. Six [days you shall labor...]**

Because the Lord created heaven and earth in 6 days and ceased or rested on the 7th day, man is commanded to work for 6 days and to rest on the 7th. The reason is that man was created in the image and likeness of his God. When man fell from that state, he was invited back to it: so that he might follow his God in doing and not doing, in the re-renewal of his work, and in working and resting. Just as our God had His going out through the 6 days and rested on the 7th day: so fallen man has his return to God through his 6 days of work and rests on the 7th. In this way, man returns after the conclusion of his 6 days and comes to the spiritual seventh: and thus both God and he meet each other on the Sabbath of true rest. God goes out from Himself through 6 degrees and rests on the 7th: and man goes out of himself through 6 days and also rests on the 7th day.

But because two things are to be considered in rest—namely, *resting from something* and *resting in something*—the first rest is that with Christ according to the flesh, that we die in and with Christ and cease from sins; the other rest is in Christ according to the Spirit, when we return into God.

That is the purpose of God's institution, for which He blessed and sanctified the 7th day. All men from Adam onwards should have known and continued this, as it was initially made known to them in Genesis 2:2-3, had not the great corruption and forgetfulness of the true God and His service brought men into such neglect of observing this day holily. Therefore, God wanted to particularly impress this first institution upon His people here again through a *remembrance*. See Isaiah 58:13-14, Ezekiel 20:11-12, 20, etc.

<margin>(a) <note>original: "i. 3. de J. N. & G. Hebr. c. 9. 10. 11." refers to John Selden's "On the Natural Law and Nations according to the Hebrew Discipline," Book 3, chapters 9-11.</note></margin>

The Jews otherwise believe, according to Meldenius's report (a), that the Sabbath was given only to the Jews alone, just as it was first given on the 7th day after their departure from Egypt when they camped in Marah, shortly before the giving of the Law. And one can agree with them in both respects to a certain extent. For

That the Patriarchs <note>The biblical fathers before the time of Moses, such as Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.</note> kept an outward rest of the 7th day as a commandment from the Lord; of that one finds at the very least not the slightest trace. On the other hand, it is frequently mentioned from the times of Moses onward.

Regarding Adam, one reads only of one such commandment that was not inscribed in the natural conscience of all men: namely, not to eat from the tree of the knowledge of good and evil. If, however, the prohibition of the Sabbath had bound the first man, it would have had to be given to him as expressly as that regarding the tree. Similarly, nothing of the Sabbath is to be found in the rest of the entire history of the patriarchs. Although one reads that Abel, Abraham, and Jacob offered sacrifices; it is nevertheless never added that it happened on the Sabbath.

It is also nowhere indicated in Scripture that God demanded such rest from His believers at that time with a single word, or showed pleasure in such a type of sanctification, or was angered by negligence in this, etc.

But when Moses wrote this history and these books, the Sabbath was certainly already established.

Because, however, many Christian men, and even not a few of the ancient Church teachers, are of the opinion that it was established by God immediately after Creation, and that the institution is clearly contained in those words—God sanctified it—it is best that, in the face of such different opinions, one should leave the other to the Lord, and each should meanwhile seek to have an abundance of faith and love.

->### The Second Book of Moses. Chapter XX.<-

[Column 1]

**9. Six days you shall labor, and do all your work.**

**10. But the seventh day is a Sabbath to the LORD your God; in it you shall do no work: neither you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your manservant, nor your maidservant, nor your cattle, nor your stranger who is within your gates.**

**11. For in six days the LORD made heaven and earth, the sea, and all that is in them, and rested on the seventh day. Therefore the LORD blessed the Sabbath day, and hallowed it.**

Since it is not naturally instilled in our conscience to divide the year into weeks or seven-day periods, nor that one specific day must be used to serve God in a special way; and because this established seventh day—which we now call Saturday or the Eve of Sunday—has been abolished and was only a sign, sacrament, or shadow (as it is called by Moses in Exodus 31:13 and by Paul in Colossians 2:17; although according to another opinion, these were the Sabbaths of the other feasts and not the Sabbath of the seventh day); and since the strict law regarding precise abstinence from all work (Exodus 35:3) is no longer binding: some conclude from this that this commandment was also ceremonial in nature, given only to the Jews and belonging to the Jewish church order.

But because the Law is spiritual, and this commandment simultaneously drives one toward sanctification—thereby clearly pointing to the Holy Spirit and the seventh "time of rest" into which man must enter through the holy number seven—and since the rest of the soul and the mind is the goal toward which God views everything regarding man, and toward which all His works aim (about which even the pagans knew how to write many beautiful things), it is certainly a general duty of mankind to seek this goal. One should be mindful of such rest by ceasing physical labor and other excesses on the first—and yet also recurring—seventh day introduced by God's providence.

The right way to remember this rest, however, is to *remain in rest*. There is no other sanctification than to find peace within the Rest itself; because it is the rest of God within Himself: God within the annihilated soul <note>original: "vernichtigten Seelen." This refers to the mystical concept of the "self" being made nothing so that God can fill the person entirely.</note>, and the soul in God.

These three types of rest are distinct, however, and must be explained.

**The first rest** is the rest of God in the soul: namely, when the soul has attained unity with the will of God and reached a "secret state"; He then remains in the soul and rests within it, just as the Son of God assures us (a): *If anyone loves me,* he says, *he will keep my word; and my Father will love him, and we will come to him and make our home with him.*

**The rest of the soul in God** occurs after the resurrection,
<note>This text appears to continue at the bottom of Column 2 due to the original printing layout.</note>
she finds her rest perfectly in Him. Then her pains and
annoyances have passed away forever. Before this,
God indeed found His rest in the soul, because it was
delivered from sin and its will was aligned with the will of God;
yet the soul still did not find its rest in God,
since it walked in a very uncertain, vexing, and anxious
path. It finds its true rest no sooner
than when it has come to God: where it then remains in a
peaceful and constant state that is subject to no changes.
There it also finds its own rest, and something still remains there for it;
which is the actual rest of the creature in God, which has also
been recognized and found to be so.

**The rest of God in Himself** is the rest He takes in a completely annihilated soul; where, after everything that was in the creature has disappeared, nothing remains but God, who rests within Himself. This is not for the sake of the creature; for since the creature has passed entirely into God, it feels no rest that is distinct from this rest of God; rather, it is for His sake. For since He—through the complete surrender <term>Gelassenheit: a key spiritual term meaning "yieldedness" or "letting go" of the self</term> of the creature—had taken back everything that belonged to Him, He remains all in all, according to the pronouncement (b) of the great Apostle: And this is the rest of God in God.

<column-break/>

[Column 2]

**12. Honor your father and your mother, that your days may be long in the land which the LORD your God gives you. 13. You...**

God now also wished to plant love among men by emphasizing various duties, so that He might first root out the weeds planted by sin—hatred, impurity, earthly-mindedness, and greed.

The order is noteworthy and consists of a double *ternary* <note>original: "ternario" — a grouping of three.</note> or number of three, and a double intention toward one's neighbor: one part concerns the person of the neighbor, and the other concerns what the neighbor possesses.

First, God wanted to bring men into such an order that children should be devoted to their parents with respectful obedience. Under this, God later intended for authorities and teachers to be included, so that one should be subject and obedient to them in all reasonable things; whom God would then equip with wisdom if they would call upon Him for it: so that people might be maintained in good order and peace among one another.

"Father" thus means here everyone who is in such a position as Adam was in regard to his wife, children, and grandchildren; he was not only their biological father, grandfather, and father-in-law, but also their lord, master, king, priest, teacher, and eldest wise leader; likewise the man from whom the woman came, and whose father he was, as it were. Consequently, through the term

**Mother)** not only a natural biological mother is meant, but everyone who is like the first Eve in regard to her children and descendants: a grandmother, mother-in-law, mistress, lady, queen, or an old, godly, wise, and prudent woman. Thus, through both together, we are to understand

**Father and Mother)** All superiors: including, besides those mentioned above, cousins, stepfathers, guardians, princes, lower judges, and all who surpass us in dignity, years, wisdom, and godliness. Genesis 45:8, 1 Timothy 5:1. These people one shall

**Honor)** That is: to deem them worthy of love, loyalty, reverence, obedience, and fear; as well as patience with their failings and the keeping silent about them: and thus to recognize their precedence.

From this honor the mother is so little excluded that, if she possessed more understanding, skill, and godliness, she might even take precedence. Leviticus 19:3, Proverbs 8:32-36.

Now, just as this commandment is the first of the second tablet <note>The Ten Commandments were traditionally divided into two stone tablets: the first four commandments (duties to God) and the last six (duties to fellow man).</note>, so it flows from the first commandment of the first tablet. There is the true Father over all that is called children in heaven and on earth: and here the image of the Father is presented for honor. This is also why this is called the first commandment with a promise. Ephesians 6:2. This promise is expressed here by the lengthening of days

**In the land that -- God gives)** Canaan was a prefiguration and pledge of Heaven, in which everyone desired to live long for that reason, and because the Messiah was to come and be seen in that very land.

->### Chapter XX. The Second Book of Moses.<-

### 13. You shall not kill.
<margin>James 2:11</margin>
### 14. You shall not commit adultery.
### 15. You shall not steal.

In these first two verses, God intended to care for the human body, so that it might be harmed by no one; and then also in regard to the wife, who has become one body with the husband, that the marriage might likewise not be defiled or damaged through adultery.

<margin>v. 13. Kill)</margin> Or more accurately, murder. For not all killing is forbidden <note>The author distinguishes between lawful killing—such as state execution or self-defense—and "murder," which is always a violation of the Law.</note>. But murder is always wrong and against the Law: as it may be committed both against oneself and against one's neighbor, in both soul and body.

All those who lead godless lives, violate their own consciences, and postpone their repentance become murderers of themselves and their own souls. They murder the neighbor's soul by tormenting them with unjust deeds, causing them offense and stumbling blocks, and leading them into the pit and destruction with false teaching or ungodly conduct and bad examples. <margin>John 10:8</margin>

So also do they become murderers of their own bodies who recklessly put themselves in danger, harm their health, and so on. They murder the neighbor’s body by failing to protect, help, warn, or rescue them from danger when they are able—whether it be pain, sickness, or the distress of hunger, fire, or water, or danger from murderers or others—and especially when they pressure someone to drink to excess <note>original: "Nöthigen zum Trincken"</note>; which is an abomination that should not even be known in Christendom, yet is perhaps nowhere so well-known as among those un-Christian heroes of drinking.

According to the spiritual sense—which Christ and his Apostles understood and explained better than the blind Pharisees and scribes—every internal root of manslaughter is likewise forbidden: all loveless and malicious thoughts, all envy, revenge, fury, and implacability; all tinder of wrath, drunkenness, gambling, etc.; and all initial external sparks and works of envy and hatred, such as angry gestures, defiance, boasting, and so on.

<margin>v. 14. Commit adultery)</margin> This includes loving the world and its things, turning one's heart from the Creator to the creatures and clinging to them, preferring the external to the internal; pampering the flesh and thereby stifling the Spirit; using the creature unnecessarily according to your carnal will and for pleasure; or also clinging too strongly to someone who fears GOD. For all of this is contrary to the will of GOD, and because it makes the person so defiled unfit for the love of GOD and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit, it is harmful to the person themselves. It includes all types of carnal impurity or all defilements of the body along with every root, inclination, and tinder of the same—such as drunkenness, daily indulgence in luxury, excess of food, sleep, and idleness, etc.

<margin>v. 15. Do not steal)</margin> With this, God also intended to care for the neighbor's possessions and goods, so that these should not be taken from them, but that each might enjoy what is theirs in safety.

Just as with murder, stealing can occur both against oneself and against the neighbor, or even against both at once, and in many ways.

This includes all kinds of overreaching in trade and business; false coinage; unjust weights, measures, or scales; deceptive, useless, or over-expensive goods; unfair usury; selling at too high a price; wages for labor that are too high, too low, or withheld from craftsmen, day laborers, servants, and maids; negligence by the same, or others, in their service; concealment or denial of debts, of things entrusted, or of overpayment; the diminishing, damaging, or destruction of a neighbor's property; the acceptance or begging for unnecessary alms, as well as the acceptance of bribes and gifts; the overly harsh oppression and burdening of subjects; the practice of vain and useless arts; greed and the refusal of help which one owes to the neighbor—a debt of injustice that clings to all who desire to be rich.

Theft is committed against oneself and the neighbor simultaneously through laziness and idleness, and through the squandering of one's own goods on excessive clothing, gambling, gluttony, drunkenness, etc.

<note>The following paragraph appears at the bottom left, seemingly as a repeated or misplaced fragment of the right column text.</note>
then his children of lies, because they agree with him therein. Lies to their neighbor. But we have not so learned Christ, since we are taught in him, as the truth, and nothing but truth, is in Jesus. Eph. 4:20, 21.

<column-break/>

### 16. You shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
### 17. Let

Thus God also did not want the neighbor to be offended in his good name and reputation, whereby his spirit is offended and grieved.

Just as we ourselves and the love for ourselves are the rule and yardstick for the love of the neighbor and how we should behave toward him, so we must always begin here with ourselves. And thus one can also speak against oneself

Bear false witness) When one, for example, accuses and despises oneself from no good motive; or when one excuses oneself against better knowledge and conscience; or when one praises oneself or one's deeds and affairs too much.

Against the neighbor, however, it can and does happen both publicly and secretly, both in the church and from the pulpit as well as in common life: for example, when authorities pass an unjust judgment or judge too hastily before they have investigated everything; or when accusers, witnesses, advocates, etc. speak too much or too little, with unfair exaggeration or belittling of the matter. It also happens through abusive and blasphemous writings among the learned. And

It can also happen secretly when one criticizes, slanders, or speaks ill of the neighbor behind his back; but also when one flatters him and thereby causes him a harmful fall. Likewise, when one lies and deceives, or when one interprets a neighbor’s speech poorly. And he who tolerates slanderers, detractors, and flatterers around him and lets them speak to the neighbor's discredit also gives others cause to apply themselves to new tales, lies, slandering, and belittling.

Here someone might ask, just as that man asked concerning the point about the neighbor: "Who is then my neighbor?" to justify himself and say: "May we not speak what is true? The testimony of another’s actions and behavior is a true testimony: I do him no wrong; I speak the truth!" Answer: A person may speak the truth, and nothing but the truth, and yet speak evil. Rightly, the rule of the Law and the Prophets, indeed of Christ and his Gospel, should first be observed: "Whatever you want people to do to you, do also to them." That which Doeg said in 1 Samuel 22:9-10 was true; nevertheless, David calls it a lie in Psalm 52:4.

Therefore, if this commandment is to be satisfied, one should rightly, as far as possible, interpret everything about the neighbor for the best: for example, that this or that happened perhaps out of haste and not intentionally, or might even be approved by us if we knew all the circumstances. What cannot be interpreted for the best should rather be rebuked to his face with appropriate gentleness out of love for his improvement. Leviticus 19:17.

Before oneself, one should be honest, upright, truthful, and non-deceptive in words and gestures. One should never give cause to speak ill of him by leading a scandalous life. The neighbor's virtues and praise should not be kept silent, or belittled and diminished, but recognized and praised with love and joy; yet at the same time, one should not make an idol out of him, nor praise him too much or more than he deserves. The best thing is to speak little of oneself—of one’s faults, arrangements, intentions, affairs, deeds, etc.—as well as of others. James 1:19. One should defend the slandered neighbor and not be quick to believe when something bad is told about him.

In short: One should not judge any person and his ways and opinions without divine light.

Because the Law is spiritual, it aims even further. And toward what? Christ is the Truth and the one who is true. 1 John 5:20. And those who believe in Him and love Him are in Him who is true, and He speaks in them and testifies to them what is true; and they agree with His testimony. And from that same testimony of truth, they speak the truth also to their neighbor: and thus their "Yes" is yes, and conversely their "No" is no. And these are the right and genuine sons of Jacob: namely, truthful people. Genesis 42:11. Oh, that we all who call ourselves Christians might be of such a number! But the devil is a liar and the father of lies and liars. John 8:44. He dictates and teaches his lies to them, and they become

And out of that same evil treasure of their heart, they also speak lies to their neighbor. But we have not so learned Christ, as many of us as have heard Him and are taught in Him, as the truth, and nothing but truth, is in Jesus. Ephesians 4:20-21.
