# The Third Book of Moses. Chapter VII.

8. And the priest who offers anyone’s **burnt offering**, the skin of the burnt offering which he has offered shall belong to him, the priest.
9. And every **grain offering** <note>original: "Speisopffer"; refers to offerings of flour or bread</note> that is baked in the oven, and everything prepared on the **griddle** or in the pan, shall belong to him, the priest who offers it.
10. And every grain offering, whether mixed with oil or dry, shall belong to all the sons of Aaron; to one as much as the other.
11. And this is the law of the **peace offering** <note>original: "Danckopffer"; a sacrifice of thanksgiving or fellowship</note> that shall be offered to the **LORD**.
12. If one offers it as a **praise offering**, then he shall offer with the praise offering unleavened cakes mixed with oil, and unleavened wafers spread with oil: and the cakes mixed with oil shall be made of roasted fine flour.

---

v. 8. **The skin — to the priest)** This suggests that the priest stands, as it were, in the person of the sinner who brings the sacrifice, in order to give himself over to reconciliation through the slaughter of his sacrifice in the death of this sacrificial animal. This found its perfect fulfillment in Christ, who clothed himself in our weak flesh and thus presented himself in our person to his Father as the only valid sacrifice of atonement and gave himself unto death. Thus, through faith, all his suffering becomes our own, as if we had suffered death ourselves and thereby satisfied the justice of God. Indeed, since he surrendered himself to God as a burnt offering in his whole life with perfect obedience and consumed all his soulful and bodily powers in such obedience, this is also credited to us; because he appeared here as the <term>guarantor<note>original: "Bürge"; a legal term for one who takes on the debt or obligation of another</note></term> in our person, fulfilled the obedience of the law for us, and suffered as a sin and guilt offering for us. See 2 Corinthians 5:21; Hebrews 2:14.

v. 9. **In the oven — on the griddle — in the pan)** Origen <note>Latin: "homilia 5 in Leviticum" — refers to the 5th sermon on Leviticus by the early church father Origen</note> interprets these three kinds of preparation as the threefold understanding of Holy Scripture and the words of God: the historical or literal, the ethical or moral, and the spiritual, hidden, and deeper sense. The oven, by its form, contained the deeper and hidden things; the pan held that which may be well understood and interpreted through frequent turning; the griddle held what lay open before everyone's eyes.

v. 10. **Dry)** Such as the grain offering of a poor man, which he brought as a sin offering.
**To all the sons of Aaron / to one as much as the other)** Many interpreters understand and apply this also to the preceding verse and every grain offering, which belonged to whoever offered it, no matter who he was; one had as much right to it as the other, provided he was the one offering it. For the priests were divided into different orders, and each had his certain day to offer. Whatever fell to him on that day belonged to him.

v. 11. **The peace offerings were of two kinds.** First, a praise offering, where one gave thanks to God for blessings received and confessed this before God—as is the meaning of the word—and thus praised God for it. See Psalm 103:2.

v. 12. **One)** But who is he that brings a praise offering, other than he who ensures that God is lauded and praised in and over all his actions, and thus fulfills in and through himself what our Savior said <note>Latin: "Matthaei 5:16" — refers to the Gospel of Matthew</note>: "Let them see your good works and praise your Father in heaven."

<column-break/>

13. Along with the cakes, he shall offer **leavened bread** with his sacrifice, along with the sacrifice of the praise offering of his peace offering.
14. And of it he shall offer one from the whole sacrifice as a **heave offering** <note>original: "Heb-opffer"; a portion lifted up and presented to God, then given to the priest</note> to the **LORD**: it shall belong to the priest who sprinkles the blood of the peace offering.
15. And the meat of the sacrifice of the praise offering of his peace offering shall be eaten on the day of his sacrifice: nothing of it shall be left over until the morning.
16. And

---

v. 13. In addition to the usual grain offering, it was also permitted to bring a cake of leavened bread, whereas otherwise no leaven could be offered. This was partly because it was intended for a meal where such bread is used for ordinary nourishment; but partly, in a hidden sense, it might be suggested that God still bears the imperfections and faults of men in such thanksgivings. For example, when some, out of good intentions, offer things to God to give him praise and thanks, which do not actually serve to praise or serve God, God overlooks what happens out of ignorance and looks instead at the willing heart. Yet, this can also certainly be applied to what believers in old times used and bequeathed for the adornment of churches, the founding of religious orders, and many such things that flowed from the "leaven" of outward service invented by men and from the imagination of supposed good works; that in this, God regarded the mind of the founders and overlooked the error in the works themselves. However, this cannot be as pleasing now in the greater light of knowledge, according to which one should distinguish between that by which Christ is honored in his members, or whatever else redounds to his honor and is promoted thereby. In such things, He will certainly also graciously overlook the leaven of accompanying weaknesses, provided that vanity and other perverse intentions—as such impurity—do not defile it; for such things must not be present at all in these peace and praise offerings.

v. 14. From each kind of bread, one cake was given to the **LORD**.

v. 15. **The meat — shall — be eaten)** But it was not roasted—as the spoiled sons of Eli wanted the meat prepared raw (1 Samuel 2:15)—but always boiled.
Of this meat, not only did the priests have their portion, but those who brought the sacrifice also kept a portion, and likely the largest part.
This showed, however, that the common people were also permitted to eat of it, and thus came into the fellowship of the altar. It served as an assurance of how they received their share of reconciliation through the sacrifices made by the priests, and were now invited here to a closer fellowship of God's grace in the eating of such sacrifices (1 Corinthians 10:18). Since all sacrifices have now ceased in the New Testament, there remains the single peace offering which Christ instituted in the **Holy Supper** <note>the Eucharist or Communion</note> in his memory, through which believers are invited to the fellowship of his sacrifice—and thus with Christ, the true altar himself—and then also to the fellowship of love with one another. Therefore, the Apostle compares this fellowship in the Lord's Supper with that of the peace offerings of Israel according to the flesh (1 Corinthians 10:16, 17, 18).

It concludes by linking the Old Testament fellowship meals to the Christian sacrament of Holy Communion.</summary>

### Chapter VII. The Third Book of Moses.

16. And if the sacrifice of his offering is a **vow** or a **voluntary offering**, it shall be eaten on the day that he offers his sacrifice, and on the next day what remains of it shall also be eaten.
17. But what remains of the flesh of the sacrifice on the third day shall be burned with fire.
18. But if any of the flesh of his **thanksgiving sacrifice** <note>original: "Danck-Opffer"; a type of peace offering</note> is eaten on the third day, it shall not be accepted; it shall not be credited to him who offered it; it shall be an abomination: and the soul that eats of it shall bear its iniquity.
19. And the flesh that touches anything unclean shall not be eaten; it shall be burned with fire. But as for the rest of the flesh, everyone who is clean may eat of it.
20. And the soul that eats flesh from the sacrifice of the thanksgiving offerings which belong to the **Lord**, while their uncleanness is upon them, that soul shall be **cut off** <note>A severe biblical punishment implying excommunication or divine judgment</note> from its people.

---

v. 16. The second kind of thanksgiving offering, or the voluntary offerings and vows, was made to ask God for a future benefit. Regarding this, see Jacob's vow in Genesis 28:20-21.
v. 17. **Shall be burned on the 3rd day**) Specifically, at home.
v. 18. **Shall not be credited**) It will be as if he had offered nothing; it is in vain: he will have no benefit from it, but rather harm. See Numbers 18:27.
v. 19-21. Nothing unclean was allowed to come near it, nor could an unclean person eat of it. This shows that even in the thanksgiving offering of the **Holy Supper** <note>original: "heiligen Abendmahl"; the Eucharist</note>, no worldly mark should be kept, nor should an unclean, worldly person be admitted to it; otherwise, such a person will experience the divine judgment of being "cut off." See 1 Corinthians 11:30, where unworthy guests were visited by the Lord with sickness and even physical death.
This is what is specifically and most properly understood through this: namely, that an unworthy guest or companion at the table of the Lord’s Supper, who carries his uncleanness upon him—namely, the animal nature, which is nothing other than the desires of anger and lust—and wishes to communicate and have fellowship with the Lord while in the uncleanness of his animal lusts and inclinations, and thus eat of the **thanksgiving sacrifice of the Supper** <note>original: "*sacrificio eucharistico*"; Latin for "eucharistic sacrifice"</note>, eats death and judgment upon himself.
"Flesh" <note>original: "Fleisch"</note> otherwise means, as is well known, "strong food" in the Scriptures; as opposed to the **milk of children** and the **herbs of the weak**. And so, the "holy flesh" is nothing other than the Word of God. It can easily happen that this is touched by something unclean. If someone held a correct and pure doctrine regarding God and the mystery of the Holy Trinity, or other things, but denied, for example, the resurrection of the flesh, or held an impure doctrine regarding it: then the "holy flesh" of the good doctrine would also become unclean through this. Such flesh should then not be eaten.

<sig>Nn n</sig>

<column-break/>

21. And if a soul touches anything unclean, whether it be the uncleanness of a man or an unclean beast, or any unclean abomination, and eats of the flesh of the sacrifice of the thanksgiving offerings which belong to the **Lord**; that soul shall be cut off from its people.
22. And the **Lord** spoke to Moses, saying:
23. Speak to the children of Israel and say: You shall eat no **fat** of an ox, or lamb, or goat.
24. But the fat of a carcass <note>an animal that died of itself</note> and the fat of a beast torn by predators may be used for all kinds of work; but you shall certainly not eat it.
25. For whoever eats the fat of the beast from which he has offered a **fire offering** <note>original: "Feuropffer"; a sacrifice consumed by fire</note> to the Lord; the soul that has eaten it shall be cut off from its people.
26. You shall also eat no blood at all in any of your dwellings, whether of bird or of beast.
27. Whatever soul eats any blood, that soul shall be cut off from its people.
28. And

---

The prohibition of fat and blood is so often reinforced (see Chapter 3:17, etc.) to show how the Spirit from these **types** <note>original: "Fürbildern"; prophetic symbols or prefigurations</note> and the true reconciliation were not yet present. See Chapter 17:11. Now that both have appeared, the use of them is permitted, just as here the fat of a carcass or a torn beast was permitted for other uses.
v. 23. **Of an ox, lamb, or goat**) Only of these three; they were allowed to eat it from other clean animals.
v. 24. **Of the carcass**) Of the three types of sacrificial animals.
v. 25. **Eats fat of the beast**) That which could be separated from the meat without tearing the flesh, and which was otherwise offered in sacrifices, even if it were slaughtered at home for the household.
v. 26. **Of bird or of beast**) The blood of fish and locusts, say the Hebrews, was not forbidden to them.
v. 27. The Law gives a reason elsewhere why eating blood is forbidden: because the life of the animal is in the blood. If we search for a deeper meaning of the Law, it was the Lord's intention to prevent bloodthirstiness, so that men might not be inclined to love and shed blood.
We should have no fellowship with the animal life: neither in the lustful desire of lewdness and luxury, nor in the angry desire of cruelty and grimness. See Ecclesiastes 11:10.

### The Third Book of Moses. Chapter VII.

28. And the **LORD** spoke to Moses, saying:
29. Speak to the children of Israel and say: Whoever wishes to offer the sacrifice of his **thanksgiving offering** <note>original: "Danckopffer"; often translated as a peace offering or fellowship offering</note> to the **LORD** shall bring his offering to the **LORD** from the sacrifice of his thanksgiving offering.
30. His own hands shall bring the offerings made by fire to the **LORD**: namely, he shall bring the fat along with the breast; the breast, to **wave** it as a **wave offering** <note>original: "Webopffer"; a ritual where the priest moved the offering horizontally</note> before the face of the **LORD**.
31. And the priest shall burn the fat on the altar, and the breast shall belong to Aaron and his sons.
32. And the right shoulder you shall give to the priest as a **heave offering** <note>original: "Hebopffer"; a ritual where the offering was lifted vertically</note> from the sacrifices of your thanksgiving offerings.

The thanksgiving offering could be brought in three cases. First, every person had to bring his thanksgiving offering on all feast days: and these were properly the peace offerings. After that, one could bring one in various circumstances: either when **GOD** had helped someone recover from a sickness, or had shown him goodness in another way; or else it could happen voluntarily or out of a vow, when one sought to persevere in a request to **GOD**. Finally, there was also a mandatory thanksgiving offering that a Nazirite <note>A person consecrated to God by a special vow of separation</note> had to bring at his purification.

v. 29. Whoever now wished to bring such an offering, whether of cattle, sheep, or goats, male or female; he was to bring it himself with a willing and joyful heart, so that **GOD** and the priests might properly receive their portion of it.

Thus he must be healthy; he must perceive the salvation of **GOD** within himself, and the goodness of **GOD** must move him to gratitude. As long as the leper is sick and leprous, he cannot bring this offering.

v. 30. **His hands**) must be stretched out. But as long as your hands draw inward and hold back from giving, and are only stretched out to take; then you are leprous and unfit for this sacrifice. And

Although prayers can also be made by others for us, whom we ask in humility to move **GOD** all the more to hear us; yet we must primarily pour out the same before **GOD** ourselves: and just as in the previous sacrifices the hands had to be laid upon the head of the sacrifice, Chapter 1:4, 3:8, 4:4, 15, 24, 29, so these also had to be actually brought with one’s own hands; to show how we ourselves must pay our due gratitude and give to **GOD** from what is ours, not through strangers or from the goods of others, as the rich and prominent are accustomed to do.

**The fat**) which belonged to **GOD**, was placed in a bowl, which the one offering took into his hands along with the fat,

**To wave**) Then the priest placed his hand under the other's hand, and thus "waved" <note>original: "webte"</note> this fat together with the one who gave it, toward all four winds in a cross-shape, from East to West, and from North to South.

v. 31. Thereupon the priest received it from the other, brought it to the altar, salted it in the middle of the ascent, carried it from there up to the hearth, and poured it onto the fire.

The priests and the one who brought the sacrifice shared the meat.

The priests had the very best: namely, the breast. And with all right, indeed according to all duty, an elect breast also belongs to them, which should be full of divine wisdom and understanding, indeed full of **GOD** Himself.

v. 32. Just as the breast is the best part of the animal, so also formerly the shoulder was counted among the best pieces.

<column-break/>

33. Whoever among the sons of Aaron offers the blood of the thanksgiving offerings and the fat, to him shall the right shoulder belong as his portion.
<margin>(a) Exodus 29:27.</margin>
34. For the **wave-breast** (a) and the **heave-shoulder** I have taken from the children of Israel, from the sacrifices of their thanksgiving offerings, and have given them to Aaron the priest and to his sons as an eternal statute from the children of Israel.
35. This is the **anointing** <note>original: "Salbung"; here referring to the portion allotted to the priests by virtue of their consecration</note> of Aaron and the anointing of his sons from the offerings of the **LORD** made by fire, on the day when they were allowed to draw near to serve in the priest’s office before the **LORD**:
36. Which the **LORD** commanded to be given to them, on the day that he had them anointed, from the children of Israel. It is an eternal statute among their descendants.
37. This is the law of the **burnt offering**, the **grain offering**, and the **sin offering**, and the **guilt offering**, and the **ordination offering** <note>original: "Fülle-opfer"; literally "offering of fullness," referring to the installation of priests</note>, and the sacrifice of the thanksgiving offerings:
38. Which the **LORD** commanded Moses on Mount Sinai, on the day when he commanded the children of Israel to offer their sacrifices to the **LORD** in the wilderness of Sinai.

v. 33. From this, the right shoulder belonged primarily to those priests who sprinkled the blood, etc.

The remainder belonged to those who brought the sacrifice.

v. 34. Just as the fat was waved, so it also happened with the breast: the shoulder, however, was lifted up high. Then the priest and the one who gave the sacrifice both lifted and waved together.

This priestly portion was intended to teach the priests how they should dedicate their hearts to the people in sincere love, and offer their shoulders to bear their burdens. All of which shall then be a glorious example to the ministers of the New Testament, how they should be minded toward the congregation over which **GOD** has set them as overseers: wherein the true High Priest, Christ, has gone before us, who wishes to set His own as a seal upon His heart and breast, and as a seal upon His arm and shoulder. Song of Solomon 8:6.

v. 35. 36. These pieces are called the anointing of the priests because they were their right, which was linked with the anointing. Love and patience are both gifts of the anointing, for which the ministers of the Gospel must apply themselves through prayer, so that they may be provided with them from above.

v. 37. 38. Thus, from burnt offerings, except for the skin, **GOD** the **LORD** had everything for Himself alone, and the priests got nothing of it to eat, much less those who brought the burnt offering. In sin and guilt offerings, as well as in grain offerings and the thanksgiving offerings of the whole congregation, **GOD** and the priests shared: but those who brought them again had nothing. But in the thanksgiving offerings of individual persons, all three had their share: **GOD**, the priests, and those who brought the thanksgiving offering.

**The ordination offering**) the initiation into the priesthood is mentioned here, although in the preceding parts regarding Aaron <unclear>mention</unclear> <unclear>is</unclear> <unclear>made</unclear> in this third book, because the five books of Moses were divided by others in this way, and not by him himself, and he had already dealt with it in Exodus 29.

Chapter VIII. The Third Book of Moses.

# The VIII. Chapter.

->The Consecration of Aaron and his Sons and of the Sanctuary.<-

AND the **LORD** spoke to Moses, saying:
2. Take Aaron and his sons with him / and the garments and the anointing oil / and the bull for the sin offering / and the two rams / and the basket with unleavened bread;
3. And assemble the whole congregation before the door of the Tabernacle of the Meeting <note>original: "Hütten der Zusammenkunft"; also known as the Tent of Meeting</note>.
4. And Moses did as the **LORD** commanded him / and the congregation assembled before the door of the Tabernacle of the Meeting.
5. And Moses spoke to the congregation: This is the word that the **LORD** has commanded to be done.
6. And Moses had Aaron and his sons come forward / and washed them with water.

---

v. 1-3. Here that very thing is now orderly put into effect which was ordained above in the 2nd Book of Moses <note>Exodus</note>, Chapters 28 and 29.

To these things, those who wish to be Christians must pay all the more careful attention, because all who shall be found worthy of this name are likewise chosen for a holy priesthood.

The first High Priest, Aaron, was consecrated with special ceremonies, which consisted of washing, the putting on of the high-priestly garments, the anointing with the holy anointing oil, and a special sacrifice: which occurred publicly in the presence of the entire people in the forecourt. According to the statement of the Hebrews <note>Jewish tradition</note>, all these ceremonies were not observed at the consecration of subsequent High Priests; rather, for seven consecutive days, the garments were put on the new High Priest and taken off again toward evening, and he was anointed with the anointing oil on all seven days for as long as it [the oil] was available. (a) Thus, in this first one more than in the following ones, the prototype of Christ is to be sought.

v. 4. 5. Moses, as the servant of **GOD** who was faithful in all his house and administration (Hebrews 3:2), proved his faithfulness also in this consecration festival of the filling-offering <note>original: "Füll-Opffers"; referring to the "offering of ordination" or "filling of hands"</note>, and directed himself precisely in all clauses according to how he had received the command from **GOD**, and carried the same out faithfully according to all circumstances.

**As the LORD had commanded him to do**) This is for us an example to follow, that we should do it precisely as the **LORD** has commanded.

v. 6. The washing was the first thing, and this first time it is said to have occurred not only on the hands and feet, but on the whole body. (b)

You must before all things be washed, if other garments are to be put on you than those you inherited from your old father Adam. Therefore wash and purify yourselves, as the Spirit requires through the Prophet (c)! Let yourself be washed by Moses himself, and have your spots and blemishes removed through the Law of **GOD**. Indeed, let yourself be washed by Christ himself into the new being of the Spirit, and be purified from the old being of the flesh through the water-bath in the word, so that you may have fellowship with him. For whoever is not washed by him personally has no part with him (d) <note>original footnote cites "Job 13:8," which is a typographical error in the source for John 13:8</note>, and cannot put on the Lord Jesus either. But as many as are baptized with his baptism of the Spirit have put on Christ (e): and those who have put on Christ are truly baptized. If we also wish to offer to **GOD** a worthy sacrifice, Christ must wash our hands and feet, our desires and works, for that purpose. Afterward, we must be clothed with all those virtues which the ornamental and mystery-rich garments signified.

<column-break/>

7. And he put the tunic <note>original: "Unter-Rock"</note> upon him, and girded him with the sash <note>original: "Gürtel"</note>, and put the robe <note>original: "Ober-Rock"</note> upon him, and put the ephod <note>original: "Leibrock"; a priestly vest-like garment</note> upon him, and girded him with the skillfully woven band of the ephod, and bound it unto him therewith;
8. And he put the breastpiece <note>original: "Brustschildlein"</note> upon him, and put into the breastpiece the <term>Urim and the Thummim</term> <note>Sacred objects used by the High Priest to determine God's will; often translated as "Lights and Perfections"</note>.
9. And he set the turban <note>original: "Hut"</note> upon his head, and set upon the turban, over against his face, the golden plate of the holy crown, just as the **LORD** had commanded Moses.
<margin>Exodus 28:39.</margin>

10. And

---

v. 7. 8. Much has already been shown concerning the high-priestly and priestly garments in the 2nd Book of Moses <note>Exodus</note>, so it is unnecessary to repeat it here. The rest must be saved for another opportunity.

v. 9. Here the High Priest stands in his full regalia and in the fullness of his splendor, so that he lacks no piece.

I. In general, note regarding these garments:
1) That they were ornamental and distinguished, which brought an air of dignity to the High Priest. Thus Christ was to be worthy above all Levitical priests, clothed with the adornment of all required qualities.
2) They were of blue, red, and white color;
3) Of gold, wool, and fine linen: which signifies Christ's eternity, divine holiness, and innocence.

II. In general, these garments also signify the believers of the Christian Church, whom Christ has put on and wrapped around himself like an ornament. Isaiah 49:18.
1. As these were the High Priest’s ornament;
2. And as these were blue and red in color: so are the believers lovely, and must often fight even unto blood.
3. The High Priest wrapped them around himself, united himself with them, and took care of them: So does Christ for us. Who shall separate us from his love and from his body?

III. We have a perfect High Priest who lacks no piece, in whom all the adornment of the priestly garments is fulfilled. Righteousness and Truth is his sash. The holy crown, the Urim and Thummim, and the breastpiece with the stones, are now manifested in essence in the royal, prophetic, and priestly threefold office of Christ. That sustains us, presents us before **GOD**, is light and justice, has all power, and sanctifies our unholiness.

IV. We also should rightly be provided, as kings, prophets, and priests, with crowns, Urim, and the breastplate of faith and love, (1) who are ready for good works, and (2) carry others in our hearts and before **GOD** through intercession and Christian love, (3) also shine before them and reveal **GOD’s** will, and (4) have before our hearts and foreheads these words: *Holiness to the LORD*.

### The Third Book of Moses. Chapter VIII.

**10.** And Moses took the anointing oil / and anointed the dwelling <note>the Tabernacle or "Mishkan"</note> and all that was therein / and hallowed these same things. <margin>Exodus 29:21, 37; chapter 40:9.</margin>

**11.** And he sprinkled some of it upon the altar seven times / and anointed the altar with all its vessels / and the wash basin with its base / that he might hallow them.

**12.** And he poured some of the anointing oil upon Aaron’s head / and anointed him / that he might hallow him. <margin>Exodus 29:7; 30:30; 40:13.</margin>

**13.** And Moses had Aaron’s sons come forward / and put the tunics <note>or "under-coats"</note> upon them / and girded them with sashes / and bound caps <note>headdresses or bonnets</note> upon them / just as the **LORD** had commanded Moses.

<margin>(a) Book 3 of the *Antiquities*, Chapter 9. <note>original: "l. 3. Antiq. c. 9." Referring to the work of the Jewish historian Flavius Josephus.</note></margin>
v. 10. **Anointed and hallowed)** Josephus writes (a) / that Moses also sprinkled all these things with the blood of the slaughtered sacrificial animals / and hallowed them with blood: which Paul also confirms in Hebrews 9:21.
v. 11. **Seven times)** This is to indicate the sevenfold mystery of the anointing in the seven gifts of the Holy Spirit / which are given in the most supreme way to Christ Jesus / and through him as the Head also to all his living members / to each according to the measure of Christ’s gift / of which Isaiah 11:2 speaks. It also refers to the seven different times and periods or eternities / in which Christ, as the Altar, should serve to make those who had sinned clean again, according to their guilt.
v. 12. **Poured some of the anointing oil upon Aaron’s head)** By this, the anointing of the true High Priest, Christ, was made known / about which we read in Psalm 133:2. He received the Holy Spirit from his heavenly Father without measure. John 3:34. The anointing of Christ at Bethany also pointed toward this / when the entire vessel of precious ointment was poured upon his head. Mark 14:3.
However, we must not stop here / but look toward the consecration of the ministers of the New Testament; how their nature should be according to the instruction of the Spirit in these symbols. Here, first, the fitness for this office / and the necessary gifts of the Spirit for the same / should be examined; which is the intent of the wish in Psalm 132:9: *Let your priests be clothed with righteousness / and let your saints shout for joy!* This also gives cause for the anointing of the congregation / that many among them may also partake in it / and all holy exercises among them / such as the preaching of the Word / prayer, and the use of the Sacraments / shall not be without anointing and blessing. And by this, it must also be recognized / who are the true members of Christ. For
Just as this anointing oil flowed from Aaron’s head down onto his clothes / as is said in Psalm 133 / so it also flows down from Christ onto all who belong to him / and so back to Aaron's head / that is / to the highest peak of our spirit / from where it will flow down into all our powers / even to the hem of our garment / that is / into our bodily or sensory feelings.
v. 13. **Just as the priestly garments in general** were symbols of the virtues / attributes, and benefits of Christ; so one should also generally note here / that now all distinctive holy priestly garments should cease: having fulfilled their meaning. Therefore, the people are no longer to be distinguished from others or declared more unholy / as Christ and the Apostles wore common clothes. There is no certain special habit / black or white / long or short / cloak or collar / cap or cowl / to be seen, ordained, or left behind: rather, he clothed and still clothes his disciples and servants with the clothing / that he himself wore: that is, innocence of life / humility / gentleness / goodness / kindness / contempt for the world / endurance of all hardship / love and faithfulness toward all people / chastity and purity / sobriety and temperance.

<column-break/>

**14.** And he had the bull for the sin offering brought forward / and Aaron with his sons laid their hands upon the head of the bull for the sin offering.

**15.** And it was slaughtered: and Moses took the blood and put it on the horns of the altar round about with his finger / and purified the altar / and poured the blood at the base of the altar / and hallowed it so that he made atonement for it.

**16.** And

---

> The three offerings of the consecration (the sin offering / burnt offering, and the filling offering <note>original: "Füllopfer"; also known as the ordination offering or peace offering of consecration</note>) / make it known that / just as the priests should constantly exercise themselves in repentance, faith, and love / so this would also be the main summary of the office of an evangelical teacher / to primarily and always urge this upon the congregation / so that hearts might be sprinkled with the blood of Christ for righteousness and also for sanctification.

v. 14. **All who wish to be priests in this time of grace** / or pass themselves off as Christians / (for that is the same thing) are strictly bound / to offer a repentant life to God.
For the bull figuratively signifies our flesh / upon which we lay our hands on the head / that is / we must submit ourselves with free will and confess / to follow Christ in repentance / abstinence, and resistance against everything that pleases the flesh.
v. 15. **Thus shall our bull be slaughtered** / and the flesh shall give up its spirit / which shows its life in lusts and desires. Our blood / that is / our natural life / which is in the blood / will follow the finger of Christ / or the power of his touch / with which he moves us inwardly and thus we follow the movement of God / and we, in his power, overcome the disorderly movements of the flesh. And if we thus follow his impulse and movement / our blood will grow more cold and die away / and Christ will dip his fingers more and more into it / or unite his powers in our deadened nature / and finally, through the pouring out of all the remaining blood / or the complete mortification of the entire old Adam-life, he will strengthen, hallow, and seal our inward life.
**Upon the horns of the altar)** By this, the Scripture understands—when it speaks of sin offerings whose hide, dung, and flesh were burned outside the camp—the horns of the Altar of Incense. For only those sin offerings were burned outside the camp whose blood entered the Holy Place. Chapter 6:30; Hebrews 13:11.
**Purified)** Hallowed and set apart from all common use / through the smearing with the holy anointing oil and the sprinkling with blood. Exodus 29:36-37.
**The Altar — Base of the Altar)** Here the Altar of Burnt Offering is meant.
Both our altars / of the heart and of the will / in the unity of the heart and the freedom of the will / must be hallowed. In all Israel, there was no more than one Altar of Burnt Offering and one Altar of Incense: so also should we all be of one will and one love and one freedom in Christ / one heart and one soul. Acts 4. And so all our deeds will be hallowed from faith through prayer / and receive their worthiness from Christ’s merit.
**Poured the blood at the base)** The mortification of one's own life and humiliation in repentance must precede / before one can give oneself as a burnt offering / which must burn entirely in love. From humble lowering, the highly worthy ascent to God is born / which is connected with reverence and love.

because there is no longer a specific offering / altar / and priest / other than in the inward spirit, no longer to be distinguished and declared more unholy. There is no certain special habit / black or white / long or short / which Christ ordained for his apostles / or these others / to wear.

### Chapter VIII. The Third Book of Moses.

**16.** And he took all the fat that was on the inwards / and the caul <note>The fatty membrane or "omentum" covering the liver</note> of the liver / and the two kidneys with their fat / and Moses burned it upon the altar.

**17.** But the bullock with its hide and its flesh and its dung he burned with fire outside the camp / as the **LORD** had commanded Moses.

<margin>
The Holy Spirit explains the mystery of the bullock to mean that **JESUS** was represented hereby / who / just as the blood of those animals was brought into the Holy Place for sin / and their bodies burned outside the camp / so he also had to sanctify the people through his own blood / and thus also suffered outside the gate. Hebrews 13:11, 12. We had deserved to be eternally cast out from the communion of **GOD** / and so also from heaven : thus Christ has now primarily earned for his believers / who go out with him outside the camp of the sinful world and bear his reproach / that they may be prepared as priests for a holy congregation / and be brought into the Most Holy Place ; for whom he also daily intercedes / and thus perfectly reconciles them before the heavenly Father. Therefore he is called a Savior of all men / but especially of those who believe / 1 Timothy 4:10.
</margin>

**v. 16.** In the inwards <note>the internal organs or "entrails"</note> of our body / as is well known / our natural life is sustained by external food and drink and by harmony with the elements. Just so is our supernatural life sustained in the inwards of our spirit / that is / in the powers of our souls / by the internal nourishment of divine grace in holy works and the harmony of the will with **GOD**. All the fat now / that grows out of us from this lovely food / we must offer up and burn to **God** in love : all growth in grace / all strength of the spirit ; also all the "fat" of internal taste and delight : especially the caul of the liver / or the delight arising from love. For love is never without taste.

The entire warmth or heat of nature has its origin in the liver. For that is the place of fire / whose heat transforms food and drink into flesh and blood. It also shares its heat with the brain / the eyes and all the senses. It gives life and warmth to all the limbs. To this liver corresponds our full or loving power / in which there is also a living fire / namely love. The caul <note>the "net"</note> of this loving power / in which it is wrapped with its love / is spiritual joy. And this is, as it were, an internal fat / which we should always offer to the glory of **GOD**.

The kidneys <note>or "reins"</note> are a poison, tinder, and sustenance for lust. Therefore **GOD** wills / that these also with their fat / in the suppression of all fleshly desire / shall be offered and burned out through the fire of divine love.

**v. 17.** The hide <note>the skin</note> may signify the outward works of repentance / which one should not perform so that one is seen by people / Matthew 6. so that the temptation of vain glory does not strike us.

So should we also burn the flesh at the same time / that is / in all our works flee the praise of people in our intention. For as the flesh is covered with the skin / so does the intention lie within the works. He who performs his works in secret / but yet wishes / that they were manifest / and he thereby might be more honored ; he indeed burns his hide / but not with the flesh at the same time : and therefore his sacrifice is not pleasing to **God** / and is useless to himself.

The dung of our sacrifice, however, depicts the perverse and disordered inclinations / which we have in us either by nature or through previous evil habits ; which we should secretly overcome and suppress in ourselves for **GOD's** glory / so that no one may perceive our imperfection.

These burnings must nevertheless take place in a clean place / and have a pure conscience as their foundation. For this must above all things be purified from all sins before the eyes of the Divine Majesty through true, fundamental repentance. Thus the sacrifice for sin is completed.

<column-break/>

**18.** And he brought forward the ram for the burnt offering / and Aaron with his sons laid their hands upon the ram’s head.

**19.** And it was slaughtered; and Moses sprinkled the blood all around upon the altar.

**20.** And he cut the ram into its pieces / and Moses burned the head and the pieces and the fat.

**21.** And he washed the inwards and the legs with water / and Moses burned the whole ram upon the altar. That was a burnt offering for a sweet-smelling savor: it is an offering made by fire unto the **LORD** / as the **LORD** had commanded Moses.

->**22.**<-

<margin>
Just as holiness is the decoration and ornament of every priest / so it is necessary above all things / if we wish to attain the same / that we offer up our senses and animal nature to **God** through repentance / and reject all comfort of the world / and also overcome all disordered desires and inclinations of our flesh.
</margin>

Afterwards it is also necessary / that we deny our inner powers and spiritual nature in the faith of the Son of **GOD** and bring them to the altar of **God**. Through this we shall attain a constant clinging with love to **GOD** and a happy victory of him / and pass by all comfort of the creatures.

**v. 18.** When we have offered up our body / our flesh and its animal life / as our bullock / through repentance to **God** ; then our nature becomes soft / gentle and innocent / like a lamb or sheep. With that same innocence we must now also draw near in **GOD'S** presence / and with a free will and mind offer ourselves entirely to **GOD** to be burned in his love.

**v. 19.** In this sacrifice and its slaughtering our nature must be so completely put to death / that in all gifts and exercises we seek nothing else nor look upon anything else / than that we may burn entirely in his love. For if we seek our comfort and convenience in something that is not **GOD** / then we live according to nature : and as long as we do not love something purely for **GOD'S** sake / we cannot offer ourselves entirely as a burnt offering of divine love.

**Upon the altar all around)** Or / against the altar / at the altar all around / at its lowest chest / where the net or grating was.

**v. 20. The fat)** Not the "stocking" <note>likely referring to a piece of fatty membrane</note> / as the translation of Luther gives it. (a)

**v. 21.** When now the inwards of our conscience have been washed away from all guilt / and the legs of our powers and desires from all disordered lust and inclination / with pure water ; then our Moses will lay these our purified inwards and our well-ordered desires upon the cut flesh of all our internal virtues / and thus offer up this whole sacrifice together with the head in the communion of his love to **GOD**. Oh, that will then give a pleasing savor before the **LORD** our **GOD**!

### Chapter VIII. The Third Book of Moses.

31. And Moses spoke to Aaron and to his sons: Cook the meat before the door of the Tabernacle of Meeting / and eat it there. Along with it, also eat the bread that is in the basket of the <term>consecration offering<note>original: "Füll-opffers," literally "filling-offering." 34. As has been done on this day. The **LORD** has commanded to do this / to make atonement for you.

---

Just as the priests were granted their sustenance from the offerings / as they also received such quite richly from the tithes and firstfruits; so too has Christ ordained this sustenance for the ministers of the Gospel / when he said to his Apostles / how they should expect such from their listeners: a worker is worthy of his food; Matthew 10:10. Wherever a child of peace was in a house / there they should remain / and eat and drink what they have in that same house: for a worker is worthy of his wages. And further: And wherever you enter a city / and they receive you / there eat what is set before you. Luke 10:7–8. How much more then is this to be understood of a congregation / to whose service in the Word a person is called.

Just as the priests had to remain for the first seven days in one stretch day and night before the door of the Tabernacle of Meeting; so this is meant to teach us / how we are bound all the time of our life to wait upon the charge of the **LORD** at the spiritual Tabernacle / which he has commanded us / as the **LORD** himself testified under this symbol: No one who has laid his hand to the plow / and looks back / is fit for the kingdom of **GOD**. Luke 9:62. Which would also have its punishment / just as death was threatened here / which **GOD** would worthily send.

While this is correct according to the spiritual sense / that faithful servants of Christ must never cease from the watch before his Church with prayer and sighing for its welfare: yet physical exercise in the proclamation of the Word cannot always be demanded of them because of their age and weakness of body / as can be seen regarding this in Numbers 8:25–26. <note>In the referenced passage of Numbers, Levites were permitted to retire from heavy labor at age fifty, though they continued to assist their brothers.</note>

# Chapter IX.
->Aaron’s First Service.<-

And it happened on the eighth day / that Moses called Aaron and his sons / and the elders in Israel;

2. And he spoke to Aaron: Take for yourself a calf / a young bull / for a sin offering / and a ram for a burnt offering / which are without blemish / and bring them before the face of the **LORD**.

4. And an ox and a ram for a peace offering / to sacrifice before the face of the **LORD** / and a grain offering mixed with oil. For today the **LORD** will appear to you.

7. And

---

**v. 1. On the 8th day)** Just as the setting up of the Tabernacle occurred in the second year on the first day of the first month / Exodus 40:17. and soon after in the same month the consecration of Aaron and his sons followed for seven days: Chapter 8:33. so hereupon on the eighth day the first service of the Old Testament was performed in the public assembly of the elders and the people; and that / as is not otherwise to be presumed / on the Sabbath / when the regular assembly had to be. Leviticus 23:3.

**v. 2–4.** And thus herewith a prescription for the regular sacrificial service on the Sabbath was given / where the priests first had to make atonement for themselves with a sin offering and burnt offering / and afterward the people with the very same and then also with a grain and peace offering.

**v. 5.** So that the entire service was spent with the preparation of these offerings / and the prayers accompanying them.

The priest was then reminded herewith first to think of his sins with repentant confession of the same before **GOD** / and then to strengthen his faith in the grace of **GOD** / which at that time was offered in these types <note>The author uses "types" or "pre-figures" to suggest the Old Testament rituals point toward future Christian truths.</note> of the offerings / which all aimed at the single sacrifice of Christ.

**v. 6.** The appearance of the glory of **GOD** on this day was also promised in a special degree and sign: with which **GOD** wished to assure / that he would appear among them with his grace at their public assemblies. See Exodus 20:24. But there is a condition attached:

**Then the glory of the LORD will appear to you)** There is a word to be done / which the **LORD** commanded to be observed. And this word is near us: namely in our heart. Deuteronomy 30:14. Romans 10:8. If that is not respected and established with obedience / it will afterward be said: I do not like to smell <note>A reference to Amos 5:21, where God rejects the "soothing aroma" of sacrifices if they are not accompanied by justice and obedience.</note> in your assembly!

<insert>
This should now teach us, regarding service in spirit and in truth within the assembly of New Testament believers, how teachers/ministers should first rightly prepare themselves for the proclamation of the Word: namely, with humble recognition and confession of their sins and their unfitness for such a great work, where one is to present the <term>mysteries of salvation<note>Refers to deep theological truths regarding how humanity is saved through Christ.</note></term> to the people. This cannot happen in a healing way except through divine light, holiness of heart, and fervent love for one's neighbor. This grace, however, is obtained only by a humble heart that first humbles itself before **God** in prayer and calls upon **God** for this grace.

Furthermore, the burnt offering represents the faithful meditation on the mysteries which are then to be presented according to the occasion of the time and other circumstances. While there is a promise that in extraordinary cases the **Lord** will give His servants what they should speak in that hour <note>original: "Matth. 10/19. 20."</note>, this does not abolish the necessary preparation through such investigation of divine mysteries under the invocation of the Holy Spirit. But whoever follows only his own reason in this, and relies on his own intellect or the work of others, seeking only to commit it to memory—he is not fit for the important office of declaring the <term>atonement<note>original: "Versöhnung." In a New Testament context, this refers to the reconciliation between God and humanity through Jesus.</note></term> achieved in the New Testament, nor for providing useful instruction on how one may become a partaker of it. 
Colossians 2:6-7. This should also occur during instruction from spiritual and lovely hymns. Colossians 3:15-17.

15. Afterward, he brought forward the people’s offering and took the goat of the sin offering that was for the people, and slaughtered it, and prepared it as a sin offering just like the previous one.

16. And he brought forward the burnt offering and prepared it according to the law.

17. And he brought forward the <term>grain offering<note>original: "Speisopffer," literally "food offering." In the Mosaic law, this was an offering of flour and oil, symbolizing the fruits of one's labor offered to God.</note></term> and filled his hand with it, and burned it upon the altar, in addition to the morning’s burnt offering.

18. Then he slaughtered the ox and the ram as a <term>thank offering<note>original: "Danckopffer," often translated as "peace offering" (Hebrew: *shelamim*). It was a communal meal symbolizing fellowship between God, the priest, and the worshiper.</note></term> that was for the people, and Aaron's sons delivered the blood to him, and he sprinkled it all around the altar.

---

<insert>
From this <term>figure<note>A "figure" or "type" is an Old Testament person or event seen as a symbolic foreshadowing of New Testament truths.</note></term> we may learn what we owe to **God**, our superiors, ourselves, and our neighbors. For these offerings were partly for **God** alone, partly for the priests, and partly for themselves for fellowship with one another. The root and the beginning or the ground of all true conversion and godliness is self-knowledge, in which we must offer up to **God** a contrite heart and a broken spirit over the misery of our sins.

v. 15. The sin offering of the congregation was either a young bull or a male goat. However, the Hebrews write more extensively that when the Scripture speaks of the sin offering of the whole congregation, it must be understood not as one piece, but as twelve bulls or goats—one for each tribe. By this, the people were likewise first directed toward a repentant recognition and confession of their sins, and then 

v. 16. In the burnt offering, they were directed toward the faithful contemplation of the grace of **God** offered to them in the sacrifices, whereby they were exhorted to the constant observation of the covenant with **God**. Therefore, these are called the "saints who make a covenant with **God** by sacrifice" <note>original: "Ps. 50/5," quoting Psalm 50:5.</note>, as it is so precisely stated.

v. 17. Afterward, the grain offering was to remind them of the gifts of love commanded by **God**, which they should contribute not only for the sustenance of the priests but were also bound to refresh their needy brothers with.

v. 18. Finally, the thank offering reminded them of the gratitude owed to **God**, who invited them to fellowship in the typical atonement made through the sacrifice—and thus also with Himself in the enjoyment of the holy meal—and wished to exhort them to a godly walk, to praise **God** for all His benefits through obedience to all His commandments. See Psalms 50:8–23 and 116:12–19, where these duties of godliness are especially emphasized in connection with thank offerings.

All of this presents to us the essential parts of spiritual service within the assembly itself: that in all things, the humble confession of sins must constantly occur and be emphasized. Afterward, people must always be instructed in the mystery of Christ’s sacrifice, and how it must be claimed through faith; then the mysteries of faith must always be explained to the believers to bring them to growth in the living knowledge of Christ. Finally, they are also awakened to love and charity toward the needy, just as the Apostolic custom intended and was maintained in the congregations—that one collects something for the poor. 1 Corinthians 16:1-2. And finally, we must constantly encourage one another toward an active faith through love and good works, so that we may be found abundantly thankful in faith. See Hebrews 10:24-25, and in prayers with psalms and hymns of praise, etc.

### Chapter IX. The Third Book of Moses (Leviticus)

19. As also all the fat of the ox and of the ram / the tail / and the diaphragm / and the kidneys and the lobe of the liver.
20. And they laid all the fat upon the breasts / and ignited all the fat upon the altar.
21. But the breasts and the right shoulder **Aaron** waved as a wave offering before the face of the **Lord** / as **Moses** had commanded.
<margin>(a) Sirach 50:22.</margin>
22. And **Aaron** lifted (a) up his hands toward the people and blessed them / and stepped down / once he had performed the sin offering and the burnt offering and the peace offering.

<margin>v. 19. 20.</margin>
However, we must not linger upon any taste, sensation, or delight that may arise from such spiritual exercises / but rather return all of it to the **Lord** in the fire of divine love. For this reason, **God** willed it as an eternal law among the children of Israel / that they should ignite and burn all the fat of the sacrifices. For the fat—alongside other things already indicated—represents all that which we love either naturally or supernaturally. We must then love and use these things not for our own pleasure or convenience / nor according to our innate natural inclination and desire / but solely for **God’s** sake and for **God’s** honor and service. Just as for this same reason we should deny and surrender the desires of the flesh and the inclinations of nature / which are summarized in the kidneys and the lobe of the liver. If we accomplish this and surrender to **God** / He then gives us His fire for it: then fat and fire are united / and burn upon the altar of **God** in the unity of our heart / and we feel peace between us and **God** / yes, our righteousness and the peace of **God** kiss each other / as the Psalmist says in Psalm 84 <note>original: "Pf. 84", though modern Bibles cite this as Psalm 85:10</note>.

<margin>v. 21.</margin>
If we now demonstrate a constant and untiring zeal in this, so that the fire of our altar burns well; then our breast will be expanded more and more in love / and our shoulder will be so prepared and strengthened under the form of the cross in the mind of **Jesus** Christ / that he will show himself obedient in us even unto death on the cross. Philippians 2:8.

<margin>v. 22.</margin>
Finally, the service was concluded with the imparting of the blessing / after these three principal types of offerings were performed: there he blessed the people with hands raised toward **God** / to entreat the blessing from the Source; for which the instruction was given by the **Lord** in Numbers 6:23. See Psalm 121:1-2.

The hands were held during the blessing in such a way that the palms were turned toward the earth / and the outer side toward heaven. Also, the right hand was held a little higher than the left (a). The fingers were stretched apart from one another.

However, the blessing of others is nothing other than placing the name of the **Lord** upon someone / that is / drawing **God’s** grace and mercy to oneself / so that it can also be shared with others; as the Hebrews themselves understand it (b). From this it follows what Hesychius the Priest <note>original: "Isychius Presbyter", a 5th-century theologian</note> (c) wrote, not without purpose, regarding this our text: >Not only **Aaron** / but also **Moses** / blessed the people; so that we may learn / how the priests do not give the blessing out of their own power / but insofar as they bear Christ’s image / so far can they give the fullness of the blessing / for the sake of Him who is within them. For the law indicates this (in the following verse) / how **Moses** was also included in the blessing / because the image of the **Lord** was entrusted to him. Therefore, not only is a priest fit to impart the blessing / but also every righteous person / who has Christ within them / and shows the image of his **Lord** in a good walk of life with **Moses**.

Stepped down) Namely, from the altar. And so there must indeed have been an ascent to the altar / even though it was not supposed to be made of steps or stairs. Exodus 20:26.

<column-break/>

23. Then **Moses** and **Aaron** went into the Tabernacle of the Congregation / afterward they came out / and blessed the people. And the Glory <note>original: "Herzlichkeit", often used in this period to translate the Hebrew *Kabod* or divine splendor</note> of the **Lord** appeared to all the people.
<margin>Exodus 24:17.</margin>

24. Then a fire went out (c) from before the face of the **Lord** and consumed the burnt offering and all the fat upon the altar. And all the people saw it and shouted for joy / and they fell on their faces.

<margin>(a) Lev. 10:2. 1 Kings 18:24.</margin>
<margin>v. 23.</margin>
After the blessing was imparted to the people, **Aaron** went with **Moses** into the Holy Place; without doubt to once again offer their thanksgiving and petition for further blessing before **God**. Whereupon they both imparted the blessing to the people / and afterward were deemed worthy of the appearance of the Glory of **God** in the sending down of the divine fire / which, as a sign of grace and favor toward the sacrifice (Psalm 20:4. Genesis 4:4.) ignited everything on the altar / and was afterward very carefully preserved. Chapter 6:2. The same occurred afterward at the dedication of the Temple. 2 Chronicles 7:1. Such fire was supposedly found again afterward in the second Temple by Nehemiah, 2 Maccabees 1:18, and according to their claim, was always maintained by the Jews.

This then indicates / how the assembly of the believers should also be concluded with the wishing of this blessing / after the source of blessing was revealed in Christ / who came down from heaven / and imparted the same to us; who also went again into the Holy Place / and then let the fire of the Holy Spirit descend upon his Apostles / where divided tongues were seen over them as if they were fiery: Acts 2:3. Which fire afterward also came upon the believers in fervent love / whereby they all became of one heart and one soul / and were thus, so to speak, melted together: Acts 4:32. Which fire, however, has not been as carefully preserved before the church as was fitting; in that they have left their first love: Revelation 2:4. Which is now almost entirely extinguished through the iniquity taking the upper hand in these last times / even in most believers through the temptation that has broken in everywhere.

We must now, after the passed seven times of the militant kingdom of Christ here on earth, once again wait for the appearance of our true High Priest **Jesus** Christ / when the holy fire of love will be found again and poured out over all flesh; Joel 2. so that the whole earth shall be full of the Glory of the **Lord**. Psalm 8:2, 10. Isaiah 6:3.

<margin>v. 24.</margin>
Everything that a human can do for themselves / is to provide the sacrificial animals: but others, as priests, must slaughter these / arrange them / and place the fire of love alongside them. And when this has then happened / he has exhausted his own strength / and can do nothing else / but go back into himself / to let **God** work.

When, however, the soul has attained a certain state of purity / **God** sends a consuming fire / which goes out from His face / that is / from Himself / who is the true love: and this fire consumes the burnt offering / and burns everything that had remained in the human of himself / annihilates it and turns it to ashes. And this is the completion of the total annihilation <note>A mystical term referring to the soul's ego being completely surrendered to God</note> / which can be worked by nothing other than **God** Himself / and through the fire of His face / which is the purest and most disinterested love.

# The Third Book of Moses. Chap. X.

## Chapter X.

->The Judgment upon Nadab and Abihu.<-

And the sons of Aaron, Nadab and Abihu, took each his censer and put fire therein / and laid incense thereon / and brought a strange fire before the face of the LORD / which he had not commanded them.

<margin>Num. 16:20, 35.</margin>
2. Then a fire went out from the face of the LORD and consumed them / so that they died before the face of the LORD.

---

This very strict and sobering judgment of God upon the two sons of Aaron was quite likely brought about through their own self-will immediately after the completion of this first service / in that they undertook this repeated and superfluous burning of incense without an express command / and presumed they could do as they pleased / even though in this service everything was to be performed exactly according to the instruction of the LORD. Thus it is called

*v. 1. A strange fire)* / not only because it was not taken from the altar / from the fire that had fallen from heaven; but also because it was taken out of their own impulse and intended to be brought before the LORD. With this, GOD intended to strike terror into all priests / and likewise the people / in the beginning / so that they would not dare to change anything in the instruction of His service or arrange it according to their own pleasure.

Nothing pleases the LORD / except what He Himself has commanded / and what has come from Him. He considers only His own gifts / and what He Himself has worked and ignited in us through His Holy Spirit / as the pure holy fire / to be acceptable.

One should also consider this today / as there is still so much self-chosen worship <note>original: "selbst-erwählten Gottesdienstes"; often called "will-worship," referring to religious practices invented by humans rather than commanded by God.</note> everywhere / despite one person always disapproving of it in another / so that almost nothing but strange fire is to be seen everywhere. Whatever one cannot recommend to the consciences of men through the Scripture and grounds from the Scripture / one usually wants to force through by a heated, self-willed, impetuous zeal based on one's own credit and belief.

In this way, the entire following practice up to the present day is unfortunately prefigured by the names of these two young priests. For

**Nadab** is as much as "voluntary" / and signifies one's own will and choice in divine worship.

**Abihu**, however, means "the father himself" / and points to those who not only appeal to the authority of the fathers / but also cling to the religion which they have inherited from their fathers and ancestors / and thus follow after their fathers / even if they are no longer in the light.

*v. 2. And this then also ignites the fire of God’s wrath* / so that it consumes so many through public and special plagues here and there / as it did here the sons of Aaron. For

GOD is so jealous of His honor and His pure love / that He can suffer no strange fire; such as that which is not taken from His altar / that is / in Himself. Between these there is no middle ground: one must burn either with His love / or with His wrath.

No soul dedicated to GOD / and who has surrendered itself to Him / indeed no soul which He has called to serve Him through the pure sacrifice / can admit either strange or self-love or self-interest; otherwise it dies instantly: and indeed it dies through the fire which goes out from the LORD. For both the fire of His justice and His love go out from Him. And this death happens / when one goes out from his station <note>referring to one's spiritual calling or state of grace.</note>. For this unfaithfulness is a true death to the purity of this very station / which befalls it in the presence of the LORD / even in its life: in that it ceases to live for Him as much as it wants to live for itself; dying to the perfection of the divine life by as much as it does not desire to die to its own love.

<column-break/>

<margin>Num.</margin>
3. Then Moses said to Aaron: This is what the LORD spoke and said: I will be sanctified in those who draw near to me / and before all the people I will be glorified! And Aaron remained silent.

---

With this, Moses especially reminds and warns the priests / that God wishes to be sanctified through obedience in them / who have particularly obtained the grace to draw near to GOD in the service of the priesthood / and that they must lead all others with a good example in this; and / if He were therefore offended by them through disobedience / He would then have to show a special example of punishment upon them / just as He would be a consuming fire to all wanton transgressors of His commandments. Heb. 12:29. See also Num. 16:5. and elsewhere / where the Levites wanted to presume the priestly office against God’s commandment.

*Those who draw near to me)* Or also / those who are near to me. For the Hebrew word <note>original: "קָרַב" (qarav)</note> is particularly to be understood of those / who are near to GOD in kinship: which then applies to His priests in a special way / who are to be near to GOD through a holy life / just as the seven princes were to Ahasuerus. Esth. 1:14. Ezek. 42:13.

And although it is also said of the people / that they are near to GOD; Ps. 148:14. yet the priests are precisely those / through whom the people must become near to GOD / and thus in a special degree of preference. For the priest's office is / to be a mediator between GOD and the people / says Chrysostom <note>John Chrysostom (c. 347–407 AD), an influential Early Church Father known for his preaching.</note>, and to make intercession for the people. And because the priests are and should be such middlemen / they must also fairly shine forth higher in godliness and holiness than the people / and be in some measure like the great High Priest and Intercessor / the LORD Jesus. Such intercessors were Noah / Samuel / Daniel / Job and others / who were all nearer to GOD. For the service or the office alone does not make the intercessor acceptable before GOD / but rather the sobriety and temperance / the righteousness / holiness and godliness of the one who bears the office. Otherwise, those who should be near through their office may / for lack of the proper qualities that make them fit for their office / be very far from Him. This very thing was the condition and fall of the two priests Nadab and Abihu.

The matter concerns you, you priests! you who through your station and profession are or should be nearer to GOD than others / His intimate and secret friends; whose office is / to be middlemen between GOD and His people / to kindle incense for our GOD / to offer prayer and intercession for the people. From you it is therefore expected / that you should be purer / more spiritual / soberer / more righteous and more godly / than the other people. For a man must be righteous / whose prayer shall avail much. James 5:16. And intercession is such a kind of prayer / which must avail very much: because it is done for the priest himself and for the whole congregation. Therefore it is fitting and necessary / that a priest or leader of the people be an excellently righteous and fervent man: in order to obtain, as an agent <note>representative or advocate</note> before GOD, grace and mercy for himself and the people; especially at a time / when GOD is perhaps very angry. Therefore it must not be said of such: Like people, so the priest. Hos. 4:9. They must not be nearer to Mammon than to the true GOD: not draw near to GOD with the mouth / while the heart is far from Him: least of all run after and be fond of being near to wine and strong drink. Oh, how shall such escape the righteous judgment of GOD! The LORD will be sanctified either in those who should be near Him / or through those who should be near Him.

### Chap. X. The Third Book of Moses. 475

4. And Moses called Mishael and Elzaphan / the sons of Uzziel / the uncle of Aaron / and spoke to them: Step forward and carry your brothers out from the sanctuary to a place outside the camp.
5. And they stepped forward and carried them out in their tunics <note>The original German "Röcken" refers to the long linen priestly garments.</note> to a place outside the camp / just as Moses had spoken.
<margin>(a) chap. 21 / 10-12.</margin>
6. Then Moses spoke to Aaron and to Eleazar and to Ithamar / his sons: You shall not uncover your heads <gloss>(a)</gloss> / nor tear your clothes / so that you do not die / and so that He does not become angry with the entire congregation! But your brothers, the whole house of Israel / shall bewail the burning / which the LORD has kindled.
7. And you shall not go out from the door of the Tent of Meeting / lest you die! For the oil of the LORD’s anointing is upon you. And they did according to the word of Moses.

---

v. 4. Mishael / Elzaphan / Uzziel) these are all names / in which the name of God (El) is contained.
v. 5. In their tunics) The linen ones. Therefore they could not have been burned to ashes / as some claim / along with their clothes. The fire burned their bodies / but not their clothes. It was a kind of thunder <note>Likely referring to lightning, which was historically associated with the sound of thunder.</note>: which does not burn the chest / but melts the money inside it; which does not consume the flesh / but consumes the bones. And
this is the nature of the spiritual judgments of God / which God carries out under the Gospel; which were prefigured by those under the Law / but are more terrible than those. They do not touch the bodies of men so much / but rather seize their souls. Such is the contempt for the Word and the commandments of God. From which may the good and merciful God deliver us!
v. 6. Aaron with his sons had to show no sign of mourning toward them / but remain undisturbed in their service; to thereby acknowledge the righteous judgment of God: which Israel, however, should take to heart as a warning / and bewail their miserable condition; so as to guard themselves against similar disobedience toward God.
God does not want / that among the priests and Levites / who are to be the most dedicated to God / one should be allowed to mourn those people / who have withdrawn themselves from God: but rather that the sanctified souls should stand on the side of divine justice / without any human self-interest or intent. As soon as they were to commit this unfaithfulness / they would immediately fall from their standing / even if under a good appearance / and deserve the same punishments. One must exercise an inviolable loyalty / if one does not wish to take back something / in a matter where one had already surrendered oneself to God. Common souls may indeed grieve over some loss through the feeling of compassion; and this is held as a good sign in them / and can indeed be so / when such sorrow is worked through love or another reasonable emotion / even if it might be human: But the souls of whom we have spoken must only uniquely
v. 7. He adds: you shall not return again into yourself / or go out from the door of the Tent of Meeting for the sake of any particular benefit / which belongs to God alone / and in which you must remain enclosed at all times. If you linger in any self-willed reflection / you will die and fall from your standing: because He does not want / that you / who are sanctified to the LORD through the holy anointing oil / which is the inextinguishable sign of a soul that has reached God / should take part in the sorrow and the benefit of common souls even by a single glance.

<column-break/>

8. And the LORD spoke to Aaron, saying:
<margin>(a) Judges 13/14.</margin>
9. You shall drink no wine nor strong drink <gloss>(a)</gloss> / you and your sons with you / when you go into the Tent of Meeting / so that you do not die. That shall be an eternal statute among your descendants.
<margin>Ezekiel 44/23.</margin>
10. Both to make a distinction between the holy and the unholy / and between the unclean and the clean:
11. And to teach the children of Israel all the statutes / which the LORD has spoken to you through the service of Moses.

---

It may be / that these fire-bearers overloaded themselves with wine during the meal of the thank-offering / and thus came to this reckless act. Therefore all strong drink was forbidden to be enjoyed at the time / when they were to attend to the priestly office: in order to perform such holy service in all sobriety and attentiveness without the slightest clouding of the mind. Which should now also primarily remind the teachers in the New Testament / how temperance and sobriety are to be observed at all times / but especially the abstinence from strong drink before the proclamation of the Word / so that no disorderly affection may be stirred up thereby. Therefore it is highly punishable / where a teacher under some pretext will take brandy <note>original: "Brandwein"</note> and the like / when one can assist the weak nature in other ways. Just as it is also a punishable habit of the listeners / to enjoy such drinks before hearing / whereby they make themselves incapable of all edifying hearing / and unworthy of divine grace.
v. 9. You shall) Because good laws are prompted by bad customs / it is very much to be presumed / as some of the Jewish teachers do not hesitate to affirm / that Nadab and Abihu overindulged in wine / which made them frivolous and presumptuous.
No such person who has become like an animal shall touch the mountain of the LORD / or be found among priests and teachers of the people.
Drink no wine) Just as sobriety is the mother of all virtues / so drunkenness is the mother of all vice and all disorder. Therefore those who are to be examples to the flock should most rightly guard themselves against it.
v. 10. To make a distinction between the unclean and clean) Oh, how necessary it is still for spiritual priests in the New Covenant / both in body and spirit, not to become drunk with any false love! For the pure life of God never associates itself with anything unclean. Everything must go / under whatever appearance it might disguise itself and try to devour the false life.
O, well is he who learns to lead a sober and watchful life in God's presence / so that he may be worthy to serve the LORD constantly and unhindered / according to 1 Corinthians 7:35.
v. 11. To teach the children of Israel) The people of God / that they also may become a people that is near to God / a priestly generation; and that their body may be the temple of the Holy Spirit / which we have from God / and are not our own / and therefore should glorify God in our body and in our spirit / which and because they are God’s. 1 Corinthians 6:19-20.
and look solely to the benefit of God.
