# Ch. XXV. The Third Book of Moses.

8. And you shall count seven Sabbath years, seven times seven years; and the time of the seven Sabbath years shall be forty-nine years to you.

9. Then you shall cause the trumpet's sound to go around in the seventh month, on the tenth day of the month: on the Day of Atonement, you shall let the trumpet go throughout all your land.

---

**v. 8.** When seven Sabbath years—making forty-nine years—had passed, the fiftieth year was also to be hallowed as a second great Sabbath year, just like the previous one, and the land was to be left uncultivated. 
Just as the six days of creation and the following seventh day were an image of the 7,000 years <note>Many early modern theologians believed human history would last 7,000 years, mirroring the creation week</note>, so these 7,000 years are in turn an image of a greater 7 times 7,000 years, which are called the "Ages of Ages" in Holy Scripture. For 
because everything is not yet brought to rest with the seventh millennium, other spans of time must still flow until the goal is reached, where everything shall finally rest in God, and God will be all in all. 
And here the view is truly "perspectival" <note>Meaning it requires a long-range spiritual vision rather than a short-sighted literal one</note>, where a brief sight is not sufficient to reach the meaning of the Spirit. 

**v. 9.** They then had to announce the year by a trumpet on the great Day of Atonement <note>Yom Kippur</note>. And because this trumpet was a "Jubilee horn" (Joshua 6:5), which is thought to signify a ram—from whose horns the trumpets were made, hence they are called Jubilee or ram-trumpets in verses 4, 6, and 13—and since the sound of the angel trumpeting in the air at the giving of the Law also had such a sound, it is given as a *Jobel* or ram-horn, or simply a horn. Thus this year is now called a Jubilee year (a); although the derivation from the meaning of the word <term>Hobil</term> <note>original: *Hobil*, meaning "to bring back" or "restore"</note>, "to bring," is also very thought-provoking, because everything was then brought back to its former state. And if it does indeed signify a ram, then it signifies the Lamb <note>Christ</note> when He shall come with the voice of the archangel and the trumpet of God, when the glorious liberty of the children of God shall be revealed. See 1 Thessalonians 4:16; Revelation 14:1, etc.

**The trumpet's sound)** For this reason, others derive the word *Jobel* from Jubal, the inventor of musical instruments. This may be what Luther looked toward when he used "Resounding Year" <note>original: *Hall-Jahr*</note> for Jubilee year.
However, it more properly means: the joyful shout of the trumpet. 
As soon as the 50th year began, namely precisely 
**In the seventh month on the tenth -- (Day of Atonement)** and thus on the 10th day after the beginning of the civil year, the Jubilee year was blown everywhere, according to the testimony of the Hebrews—not in the 49th year beforehand, as some wish, contrary to all Hebrew tradition—and it was held immediately thereafter, so that it lasted a full year until the tenth day of the 51st year. 

Atonement aims at the rest and peace of God, which were to be introduced through Christ’s shed blood; therefore, it happens in the number seven, as the number of rest, in which God the Lord also rested from all His works. Just as the Jubilee or Resounding Year, which consisted of seven times seven completed years, had to be observed precisely on the Day of Atonement in the 7th month. 
Now, just as the number ten flows back into the number one and becomes one: so there may well lie a reason here that in its own time, and after the rotation of certain ages, everything shall come back to God, the eternal Unity—from whom it branched out and departed into "twoness" through sin—and shall become one with Him, that which had multiplied into division and scattering. 

(a) Thus the Hebrews almost unanimously hold that *Jobel* is an Arabic word and signifies a ram, and therefore this year was named after the ram-horns. See <note>original: Buxtorf. Lex. 10. And you shall hallow the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty throughout the land to all who dwell therein. It shall be a Jubilee year for you; then each of you shall return to his possession, and each of you shall return to his family.

11. That is the Jubilee year: the fiftieth year shall be for you. You shall not sow, nor reap what grows of itself, nor gather from the unpruned vines.

---

**v. 10. You shall hallow it)** The court did this publicly and said: This year shall be hallowed to the Lord. 
**Proclaim liberty)** That is, to indicate by the blowing of horns throughout the entire land that the land and the servants now have their freedom. It is not to be called a "Year of Release" <note>original: *Erlaß-Jahr*</note>, as Luther translated it; for that was the name given to the 7th year for the release of debts, which did not happen in the 50th or Jubilee year, as many groundlessly believe. (a)

**v. 11. It shall be the fiftieth year)** Some indeed suggest (b) that the 49th year was the Jubilee year, because otherwise two Sabbath years would have followed one after the other. They claim that designating it as the 50th year is a manner of speaking, just as we call a week eight days, even though it has only seven. They also argue God usually counts other years by the number 49: such as Daniel's 70 weeks, which by such a calculation were nothing other than 10 Jubilee years, namely 10 times 49 or 490 years. 

Against this, however, others (c) appeal to the express letter of the Scripture, where the 49th year is always contrasted with the 50th in the text. They also prove that otherwise two Jubilee years would have to be counted in 50 years, or one Jubilee year would be counted twice; and in the first Jubilee year, there would have been none before it that could have been counted. This is also the opinion of all the Hebrews, who hold the 49th year to be a simple Sabbath year, but the 50th to be a Jubilee year, and that the beginning of the count for the following Sabbath years was made again from the 51st year.

**v. 12. The Jubilee year shall be holy to you)** However, from Moses until the Babylonian Captivity, it was suspended, as it fell out of practice (d). Yet the Jubilee years were still counted because of the 7th year, so that no confusion would arise; otherwise, that year could easily have been counted as the first year following the Year of Release, when in fact not the 50th, but the 51st, was the first year in the count. Today, however, they no longer count them at all. 

**You shall eat its produce directly from the field)** Since it was an easy thing for God to bless the 48th year so that they might have had enough not only in the 49th, but also in the 50th; and there is also no doubt that He would have done so and given such overflowing abundance that they could well have made it into the 51st year.

# The Third Book of Moses. Chapter XXV.

## Chapter XXV.

->Regarding the Year of Rest and Jubilee, and the Poor.<-

And the Lord spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:
2. Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land which I give you, then the land shall keep a Sabbath rest unto the Lord.
3. Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather in its produce.
4. But in the seventh year, the land shall have a Sabbath of rest, a Sabbath unto the Lord: you shall neither sow your field nor prune your vineyard.

---

This commandment regarding the Year of Rest <note>The Sabbatical Year or *Shmita*</note> has already been briefly introduced in Exodus 23:10-11, where it is specifically noted that the poor among them should then eat what grew of itself—namely, from the seeds that fell naturally and from the unpruned vines, which they had to allow to grow freely. These are specifically named here as "set apart" because they were not regularly tended or pruned, just as the Nazirites <note>Nazirites were individuals consecrated to God who, among other vows, did not cut their hair</note> had to do with their hair. Here, however, the fruits are still left to the owners and their families, provided that, according to the previous commandment, they also granted the poor a free right to enjoy such fruits according to their need.

**v. 2. Into the land — which I give you)** The Jews who lived elsewhere, outside the land of Canaan, were not obligated to let their land rest. <margin>(a) See Hottinger, *On Hebrew Law*, no. 69.</margin>

**The Land)** This wording does not seem to favor the opinion that gardens were exempt from this rule, as some have claimed. <margin>(b) Vinar. on this passage. Quistorp on Exodus 23:10. Hottinger, in the place cited.</margin>

**v. 3. Six years)** Just as God worked for six days in His creation and brought forth something special on each day, and also assigned man work-days of that same number; so here He already allows a prophetic perspective to be seen. He orders the number of years according to the number of days, so that the latter become an image of the former. For 
the wisdom of God consists in this: that He first lets certain images precede in order to represent something even greater and more secret, as He—according to the order of time—becomes greater and greater in His works. This is not to say He can become greater in Himself, but rather in His effects which He demonstrates in His creatures, in which He and His eternal Son (through whom He brought forth all things) work continually.

**v. 4. Just as the 7th day of the week was holy to God the Lord and was a Sabbath or Day of Rest, so every 7th year had to be holy to God the Lord and be a Sabbath or Year of Rest, in which both the land and those who farmed it were to rest.**

**In the 7th year)** This year did not begin with the month of *Nisan* <note>Nisan falls in March/April; it is the first month of the religious calendar</note>, by which all other festivals in the year were regulated; rather, it began with the month of *Tisri* <note>Tishrei falls in September/October</note>, when the civil year began. This was for the benefit of the land; because in *Nisan* the grain everywhere has only just become truly ripe, and thus in many places the fruits of the sixth year—which were meant to provide abundantly for the following year—would have remained standing in the fields if the rest had begun in *Nisan*. The month of *Tisri* was also most suitable because the Jubilee Year was to begin in that same month.

<column-break/>

5. What grows of itself after your harvest you shall not reap, and the grapes of your unpruned vines you shall not gather; it shall be a year of rest for the land.
6. And what the Sabbath of the land brings forth shall be food for you: namely for you, and for your male servant, and for your female servant, and for your hired hand, and for your guest who stays with you. <margin>Exodus 12:45.</margin>
7. And for your cattle and for the wild animals that are in your land, all its produce shall be for food.

---

**v. 5. What grows of itself after your harvest)** This refers to the grain of the 6th year that may have fallen during cutting, binding, sweeping, loading, or transport, taking root in the earth and sprouting in the following year, as often happens in many ways.

**v. 6. 7. All of this was offered up freely.**
The master of the house might indeed eat of what grew on his property, and also take some home with him to keep and share with his family, provided that some of that fruit still remained in the field or on the trees. But if there was nothing left in the field, he had to give away what he had at home for the common good. If someone had sold any of it, the money received for it also had to be given away. <margin>(a) See Lightfoot, *Chorographical Century* [on] Matthew, Preface, ch. 1. Buxtorf, *Talmudic Lexicon*, under the word *Ba'al* <note>original Hebrew: בעל, meaning 'Owner' or 'Master'</note>.</margin>

If someone kept something for himself alone and sought to profit from it, he was regarded as dishonest and deemed unfit to give testimony in court.

No one had anything of their own from the land; rather, everything was common property. The poor, strangers, widows, and orphans—even the cattle and the wild animals in the field—had just as much right to consume all fruits and plants as the person on whose land they grew. If someone plucked a grape from his vineyard, it was not done as if they were his own grapes belonging to him, but from the general grapes that belonged to everyone.

Just as the Lord wished to free them from all otherwise imposed labor in farming the land in the seventh year, so in this Year of Rest He wished to give the believers an image of the desired rest of the people of God in the glorious Kingdom of Christ in the final seventh millennium from the creation of the world (Hebrews 4:9; Revelation 20:6). Since we have already put more than seven hundred years of the sixth millennium behind us, and the timing must be fulfilled precisely according to the number the prophets indicated, we should be encouraged to contemplate this in faith. As this is described, among other places, in the final chapters of Isaiah from chapter 60 onwards, they will build houses there, plant vineyards, and otherwise work (Chapter 65:21, etc.), but it will not happen with such toil and under the curse, but with pure joy and much blessing, which they will have in all their work. See v. 21.

Then the creature, which is subjected to vanity—not willingly, but for the sake of Him who subjected it—will be made free in hope from the bondage of corruption into the glorious freedom of the children of God (Romans 8:20, 21 and Chapter 13:5). Thus, that heavy servitude among men, where the lives of farmers and others are made bitter (Job 31:39), will cease, and everyone will dwell in quiet rest under his vine and fig tree (Micah 4:4).

# Chapter XXV.

->Concerning the Year of Rest and Jubilee, and the Poor.<-

AND the LORD spoke to Moses on Mount Sinai, saying:
2. Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When you come into the land that I give you, then the land shall rest a Sabbath to the LORD.
3. Six years you shall sow your field, and six years you shall prune your vineyard and gather in its fruit.
4. But in the seventh year the land shall have a Sabbath of rest, a Sabbath to the LORD: you shall not sow your field, nor prune your vineyard.

This commandment regarding the Year of Rest was already briefly set forth in Exodus 23:10–11, where it was specifically mentioned that the poor among them should then eat what grew of itself—namely, from the fallen seeds and from the unpruned vines. These vines had to be allowed to grow freely and are specifically called "separated" <note>original: *abgesonderte*</note> here because they were not properly tended or pruned, just as the <term>Nazirites</term> <note>Nazirites were individuals who took a vow of separation to God, during which time they were forbidden from cutting their hair or consuming grape products.</note> had to do with their hair. **v. 2. Into the land — that I give you)** The Jews who lived elsewhere, outside the land of Canaan, were not obligated to let their land rest. <note>original Latin: *vid. Hottinger. de jur. Hebr. n. 69.* — See Hottinger, *On Hebrew Law*, no. 69.</note>

**The Land)** This does not seem to favor the opinion of some who claim that gardens were exempted from this law. <note>original Latin: *Vinar. ad h. l. Quistorp. ad Exod. 23, 10.* — Vinarius on this passage; Quistorp on Exodus 23:10.</note>

**v. 3. Six years)** Just as God worked for six days in His creation and brought forth something special on each day, and also assigned man work-days according to that number; so here He allows a perspective-like <note>This "perspective-like" view suggests that physical laws act as a "foreshadowing" or a visual aid for larger spiritual truths.</note> meaning to be seen. By ordering the number of years according to the number of days, the latter becomes an image of the former. For

In this consists the wisdom of God: that He first lets certain images precede in order to represent something even greater and more secret. He becomes ever greater and greater in His works according to the order of times—not that He can become greater in Himself, but in His effects, which He demonstrates in His creatures, through which He and His eternal Son (through whom He brought forth all things) work continually.

**v. 4.** Just as the seventh day of the week was holy to the LORD God and was a Sabbath or day of rest, so every seventh year had to be holy to the LORD God and a Sabbath or year of rest, in which both the land and those who cultivate it were to rest.

**In the seventh year)** This year did not begin in the month of Nisan <note>The first month of the religious calendar, occurring in Spring.</note>, by which all other festivals in the year were determined; rather, it began in the month of Tisri <note>The seventh month of the religious calendar, occurring in Autumn, marking the start of the civil year.</note>, when the civil year began. This was for the benefit of the land; for in Nisan the grain has only just become truly ripe everywhere, and thus in many places the fruits of the sixth year (which were meant to provide abundantly for the following year) would have remained standing in the fields if the rest had begun in Nisan. The month of Tisri was also most suitable because the Jubilee year was to begin in that same month.

<column-break/>

5. What grows of its own accord after your harvest you shall not reap, and the grapes of your unpruned vines you shall not gather; it shall be a year of rest for the land.
6. And what the Sabbath of the land brings forth shall be food for you: namely for you, and for your male servant, and for your female servant, and for your hired laborer, and for your sojourner who stays with you. (Exodus 12:45)
7. And for your cattle and for the wild animals that are in your land, all its yield shall be for food.

**v. 5. Of its own accord after your harvest)** This refers to grain from the sixth year that fell out during cutting, binding, stacking, loading, or hauling, took root in the earth, and then sprouted in the seventh year, as often happens in many ways.

**v. 6, 7. All of this was made freely available.**

The head of the household could indeed eat of what grew on his land, and also take some home with him and keep it, and share it with his family, as long as some of that fruit still remained on the land or on the trees. But once there was nothing left in the field, he had to give away what he had at home for the common good. If anyone had sold any of it, the money received for it also had to be given for the common good. <note>original Latin: *vid. Lightfoot. cent. chorogr. Matth. præm. c. 1. Buxtorff. Lex. Talm. voc. עָבַר* — See Lightfoot, *Chorographical Century, Preface to Matthew*, ch. 1; Buxtorf, *Talmudic Lexicon* under the word *avar* (meaning "to pass over" or "transgress").</note>

If someone kept something for himself alone and sought to profit from it, he was regarded as dishonest and deemed unfit to give testimony in court.

No one had anything of their own from the land; rather, everything was common property. The poor, strangers, widows, and orphans—even the cattle and the wild animals in the field—had just as much right to consume all fruits and plants as the one on whose land they grew. If, for example, someone plucked a grape from his vineyard, he did not do so from his own grapes that belonged to him, but from the common grapes that belonged to everyone.

Just as the Lord wanted to free them from all otherwise imposed labor of cultivating the land in the seventh year, He intended in this Year of Rest to give the believers an image of the desired rest of the people of GOD in the glorious kingdom of Christ. This refers to the final seventh millennium <note>original: *siebenden Tausend der Jahre* — a reference to the "Chiliastic" belief that history would last 6,000 years followed by a 1,000-year Sabbath reign.</note> from the creation of the world (Hebrews 4:9; Revelation 20:6). As we have now moved more than seven hundred years into the sixth millennium <note>This note suggests the commentary was written around 1700 AD, based on a chronology dating creation to approximately 4000 BC.</note>, and although things must be fulfilled precisely according to the number indicated by the prophets, one should rightly be encouraged to contemplate this in faith. As this is described, among other places, in the final chapters of Isaiah from chapter 60 onwards, they shall then build houses, plant vineyards, and otherwise work (Chapter 65:21, etc.); but such things will not be done with hardship or under the curse, but with pure delight and much blessing, which they shall have in all their labor. See v. 21.

Then the creature—which is subjected to futility, not willingly, but because of Him who subjected it, and that in hope—will be made free from the bondage of corruption into the glorious liberty of the children of GOD (Romans 8:20, 21; and Wisdom 13:5). Thus, that heavy servitude among men, where life is made bitter for plowmen and others (Job 31:39), shall cease, and everyone will dwell in quiet rest under his vine and fig tree (Micah 4:4).

### Chapter XXV. The Third Book of Moses.

**8. And you shall count seven Sabbatical years <note>original: *Ruhe-Jahre* - literally "years of rest."</note> for yourself, seven times seven years; and the time of the seven Sabbatical years shall make forty-nine years for you.**

**9. Then you shall cause the trumpet’s sound to go around in the seventh month, on the tenth of the month: on the Day of Atonement you shall cause the trumpet to go around in your whole land.**

<margin>v. 8.</margin> When seven Sabbatical years—making forty-nine years—had passed, then the fiftieth year was also to be celebrated as a second great year of rest, just like the previous one, and the land was to be left uncultivated.

Just as the six days of creation and the following seventh day were an image of 7,000 years, so too are the 7,000 years an image of a greater seven times 7,000 years, which in Holy Scripture are called "Eternities of Eternities." Because

Since everything is not yet brought to rest within the seventh millennium, other cycles of time must flow until the goal is reached, where everything shall finally rest in God, and God will be all in all.

And here the view is truly perspectival <note>The author suggests a "prophetic perspective" where events in the near future mirror much larger cosmic timelines.</note>, where a short-sighted vision is not suited to reach the sense of the Spirit.

<margin>v. 9.</margin> They then had to announce the year with a trumpet on the great Day of Atonement. And because this trumpet was a "Jubilee horn" (Joshua 6:5), which is thought to signify a ram—from whose horns the trumpets were made—they are also called "Jubilee" or "ram-trumpets" in verses 4, 6, and 13. And since the sound of the angel trumpeting in the air at the giving of the Law also had such a sound—where a *Jobel* or ram’s horn, or simply a horn, is mentioned—this year is now called a Jubilee Year <term>Jubal/Jobel: A Hebrew term likely meaning "ram" or "ram's horn," but also associated with a "shout" or "bringing back."</term> (a); although the derivation from the meaning of the word <term>Hobil</term> <note>original: *Hobil* - to bring back or lead back.</note> is also very thought-provoking, because everything was then brought back to its previous state. And if it does indeed signify a ram, then it signifies the Lamb <note>Refers to Christ as the Lamb of God.</note>, when He shall come with the voice of the Archangel and the trumpet of God, when the glorious freedom of the children of God shall be revealed. See 1 Thessalonians 4:16, Revelation 14:1, etc.

**The Trumpet’s Sound)** For this reason, others derive the word *Jobel* from *Jubal*, the inventor of musical instruments. This may have been what Luther looked toward, as he often used the term "Resounding Year" <note>original: *Hall-Jahr* - Luther's specific translation for Jubilee, emphasizing the sound of the announcement.</note> for the Jubilee Year.

However, it more properly means: the joyful, shouting sound of the trumpet.

As soon as the 50th year began, precisely

**In the seventh month on the tenth — Day of Atonement)** and thus on the 10th day after the beginning of the civil year, then, according to the testimony of the Hebrews, the Jubilee year was blown [announced] everywhere—not in the 49th year beforehand, as some claim against the opinion of all Hebrews—and it was held immediately thereafter, so that it lasted a full year until the tenth of the 51st year.

The Atonement points to the rest and peace of God, which were to be introduced through the shed blood of Christ: therefore it occurs in the number seven, as the number of rest, in which God the Lord also rested from all His works. Likewise, the Jubilee or "Resounding Year," which consisted of seven times seven completed years, had to be observed on the very Day of Atonement in the 7th month.

Now, just as the number ten flows back into the first number and becomes one: so there may well be a reason here that, in its own time and after the cycle of certain ages, everything shall come back to God, the eternal Unity, from which it had split and gone out into duality through sin, and shall become one with Him, whatever had multiplied into division and scattering.

<margin>(a)</margin> Thus the Hebrews almost unanimously hold that *Jobel* is an Arabic word and signifies a ram, and therefore this year was so named after the ram-horns. <note>original: *vid. Boxtorf. Lex. Hebr. voc. יובל. Sigon. de rep. Hebr. l. 2. c. 15. Goodwin. Mof. & Aar. l. 3. c. 10. & Reitz. not. 1.* — See Buxtorf, *Hebrew Lexicon*, word: *Yovel*; Sigonius, *On the Hebrew Republic*, Book 2, Chapter 15; Goodwin, *Moses and Aaron*, Book 3, Chapter 10; and Reitz, note 1.</note>

**10. And you shall sanctify the fiftieth year, and proclaim liberty in the land to all who dwell therein. It shall be a Jubilee Year for you: then each of you shall return to his possession, and each shall return to his family.**

**11. That is the Jubilee Year: it shall be the fiftieth year for you. You shall not sow, nor reap what grows of itself therein, nor gather from the unpruned vines.**

**12. For it is the Jubilee Year; it shall be holy to you: you shall eat the produce thereof from the field.**

<margin>v. 10. You shall sanctify it)</margin> This the court did publicly, saying: This year shall be sanctified to the Lord.

**Proclaim liberty)** That is, to indicate throughout the whole land with the blowing of horns that field-servants and domestic servants now have their freedom: not to call it a "Year of Release" <note>original: *Erlaß-Jahr*</note>, as Luther translated it; for that was the name given to the 7th year for the release of debts, which did not happen in the 50th or Jubilee Year, as many hold without basis. (a)

<margin>v. 11. It shall be the fiftieth year)</margin> Some indeed claim (b) that the 49th year was the Jubilee Year, because otherwise two Sabbath years would have followed one another. They argue that it is called the 50th year as a manner of speaking, just as we call a week eight days, even though it has only seven. They also argue that God tends to calculate other years by the number 49: such as the 70 weeks of Daniel, which according to such calculation were nothing other than 10 Jubilee years—namely 10 times 49, or 490 years. On the other hand, others (c) appeal to the express letter of Scripture, where the 49th year is constantly contrasted with the 50th in the text, and they also prove it by the fact that otherwise two Jubilee years would have to be counted every 50 years, or one Jubilee year would be counted twice; and since with the first Jubilee year, there would have been none before it that could have been counted. All Hebrews are also of this opinion, holding the 49th year for a simple Sabbatical year, and the 50th for a Jubilee year, and that from the 51st year the counting began again for the following Sabbatical years.

<margin>v. 12. The Jubilee Year shall be holy to you)</margin> It was celebrated from Moses until the Babylonian captivity, after which it fell out of practice (d). However, the Jubilee years were still counted because of the 7th year, so that no confusion would arise, because otherwise that year could easily have been counted as the first year following the Year of Release, when in fact it was not the 50th, but the 51st, that was the first again in the counting. Today, however, they no longer count them at all.

**You shall eat the produce from the field)** Since it was a light thing for God to bless the 48th year so that they had enough not only in the 49th but also in the 50th; and there is also no doubt that He did so, and gave such great abundance that they were well able to manage until the 51st year.

<meta>This page continues the theological commentary on the Jubilee Year (Leviticus 25), expanding from the historical laws of Israel into a mystical, "universalist" interpretation of cosmic history. ### Chapter XXV. The Third Book of Moses.

### 13. In this Jubilee Year, each of you shall return to his property.

Just as the Jubilee Year and the Sabbatical or Release Year <note>original: *Erlaß-Jahr* - the year of debts being cancelled every seven years.</note> were similar in these regards, they were also distinct in other matters. For in the Jubilee Year, every person returned to his property and to what was his own, which did not happen in the Release Year.

But here we might well cry out: Oh, what a depth of the wisdom and knowledge of God! For the mysteries hidden beneath this are very great, which God the Lord in these last times—as the six great work-days <note>The author refers to the common early modern belief that the world would last 6,000 years, corresponding to the six days of creation, before the final Sabbath.</note> run to their end—reveals with power to the children of wisdom. And just as He gave His blessing twofold in the sixth year, so too in this sixth great age He will pour out the wealth of His knowledge with much blessing, so that many will come upon the mysteries of Scripture and find great understanding therein. From this rich knowledge, one can also conclude that the last times are at hand. For God does not diminish in revealing His wonders but comes forth ever more gloriously; whereas the enemy begins his works grandly, but in the end, it all turns to clay <note>original: *Laim* - mud or loam, implying a weak or crumbling foundation.</note>.

First and foremost, in this year, this great mystery was presented to the believers—as many enlightened souls in our times now see—that this refers to the great restoration <note>term: *Wiederbringung* - also known as *Apokatastasis*, the theological doctrine that all beings will eventually be reconciled to God.</note> of all rational creatures. After the passage of seven eternities—the duration of which is known to God alone, and in each of which a rest will be revealed for souls who have been stuck in labor and misery—this restoration will then extend quite universally. Then, with power, God will be "all in all" (1 Corinthians 15:28), and thus everyone will return to the possession of God as their origin. By this, they will also return to their fatherly property of eternal bliss in heaven and to the freedom of the children of God, once they have first, like the Prodigal Son, tasted the husks with the swine—the unclean spirits—in the hellish eternities of torment (Luke 15:16).

It is also worth considering that the first Jubilee Year under this law occurred approximately in the year 2500 from the creation of the world, by which time 50 Jubilee cycles had already passed. This shows how the years are precisely measured by God, for everything will happen in its time; just as this great universal reconciliation, as the end and conclusion of all God's works, will occur when it is powerfully fulfilled that Christ has become the reconciliation for the sins of the whole world (1 John 2:2). Therefore, this Jubilee Year was also trumpeted on the great Day of Atonement and began at the same time. And

Why is that which is so mysteriously contained here, and so credibly discovered by some enlightened and diligent searchers of Scripture, considered unbelievable by many? Namely, that in this holy number seven, according to its deep meaning and the multiplication or continuous increase, the times of the eternities and the entire duration until the complete restoration of the whole creation lie hidden.

It is indeed indisputable that the Law is spiritual—or at least it should be indisputable, as Paul also believed (Romans 7:14)—and that consequently great mysteries lie hidden under all its symbolic things.

Thus, these are good, holy, and irreproachable thoughts, which certainly agree well with the analogy of faith, when some hold that in eternity—which encompasses certain divided and determined durations—the complete cycle of cleansing for the whole creature is prefigured, and will resemble a great Sabbatical year of seven times 7,000 years (making 49,000 years) until the great Jubilee Year, the 50,000th, when everyone shall return to their property and inheritance.

<column-break/>

### 14. When

But how these times and years are to be calculated, one does not wish to take it upon oneself to determine. Rather, with the hoped-for approval of the fair reader—and a request for this fairness in reception, which allows everything to come before it for testing, even if one is only bound to keep the good—one wishes only to add the thoughts of a secret lover of wisdom <margin>(a) Author of the work *Mago-Cabbalistic & Theosophic*, Chapter 6, Part 1.</margin> <note>This refers to Georg von Welling (1655–1727), a famous alchemist and theosophist whose work *Opus Mago-Cabbalisticum* influenced figures like Goethe.</note> (a), whose other views are left to stand on their own. According to his explanation, this number seven and the duration of the eternities until the Jubilee Year contains five million, seven hundred sixty-four thousand, eight hundred and one years, according to the following calculation:

| :--- | :--- | :--- |

| 2 | 49 times 7 | 343 |
| 3 | 343 times 7 | 2,401 |

| 6 | 117,649 times 7 | 823,543 |
| 7 | 823,543 times 7 | 5,764,801 |

<margin>* "Let no one be misled by this, as if one meant exactly such earthly years and times as we have now. However, one must use a more comprehensible word, because one cannot find another way to determine the duration of damnation in the New Jerusalem after the destruction of our visible, transitory world."</margin>

> "Namely, after fifty-times-one hundred thousand [5,000,000] as the great Fall- and Jubilee Year, and again seven hundred thousand years*, gradually all human creatures who lay in damnation will once more reach their property and eternal inheritance. In the remaining sixty-four thousand and eight hundred years, however, the fallen angels [shall]. In the final single year (according to this author's insight), the fallen son of the morning <note>original: *Sohn der Morgenröthe* - Lucifer.</note> (Lucifer), as the origin of all corruption, will stand quite bare and alone in the very last and most cruel torment and total abandonment by all damned humans and evil spirits. He must endure the suffering and torment of the whole creation in quite imperceptible wrath and unfathomable torture, and feel truly what it is to be separated from the source of light and life and to be entirely alone; until he finally recognizes his malice and fall, and—through the never-ending divine mercy in Jesus Christ—may receive [grace], and thus also once more reach grace, his property and inheritance, his first dominion, light, and glory. And so shall be completed the determined mysteries of this stewardship, where God is all in all, the devil shall be no more, nor shall death and hell be found; but in this wonderful reversal, everything will again be perfectly purified and remain partaking of all joy and bliss at the point of rest—that is, in God—forever and without any ceasing. For

> "That such great times of determined torment must exist, the holy text elsewhere gives enough to recognize, where it is so often found 'from eternity into the eternities' <note>original: *von Ewigkeit in die Ewigkeiten* - a literal translation of the Hebrew/Greek idioms for "forever and ever."</note> or 'from the times into the times'; that is, in an incomprehensible sequence. From the frequent repetition of these terrifying words, one can conclude that it must be so.

> "Because these times are not comprehensible or speakable except in numbers—for the signs that signal the difference between day and night, as well as all years and times, will then be no more—we can have no correct concept of these determined times and eternities through our transitory times."

v. 14–16. They had to arrange the sale of their goods according to the years remaining until the Jubilee Year, selling it either more dearly or more cheaply because it would be returned to the original owner sooner or later.

v. 17. **Fear your God**) He sees and detests all deceptive cunning and oppressive force committed against a neighbor—which causes them distress—and He will certainly avenge all such schemes and overreachings, or any other harshness in trade and conduct. For this very reason, the fear of God is held up here, because such things are commonly practiced by those who possess greater power over others.

v. 18. 19. **So that you may dwell safely in the land**) Learn here what makes you secure against all hostile attacks and invasions. Truly, it is not strong walls, not good castles and bolts, nor many armed men! It is nothing other than obedience to God's command. Through this, you come under the protection of the Most High and into the land where one can dwell safely: which will also be fulfilled outwardly in a special degree in the seventh millennium <note>The author is referring to the "Sabbath of the World," a belief that after 6,000 years of history, a 1,000-year period of peace (the Millennium) would follow.</note>. Ezekiel 39:26; Joel 2:21, 26.

v. 20. **If you should say**) Either with the mouth or in the heart and thoughts, which God knows: for the distrustful heart is very easily overtaken by such worries about sustenance.

v. 21. But a gracious God, who is so generous in His promises! Behold, He promises 

**the yield of three years in the sixth year**) and thus a greater blessing by omitting the sowing than if they had sown, and even greater than they actually needed.

**22. You shall sow the eighth year and eat from the old yield; until the ninth year, until its yield comes in, you shall eat of the old.**

**23. Therefore, the land shall not be sold into eternal ownership: for the land is mine; for you are strangers and sojourners with me.** <margin>Psalm 39:12.</margin>

**25. If**

v. 22. For they did not need any of the grain from the sixth year until the ninth year, because they could sow again in the eighth year and also harvest.

But how does this promise reconcile with its fulfillment, since the yield of the sixth year was often so poor that the seventh year became a miserable, sorrowful year for them? **Answer:** All of God's physical promises are grounded in and refer to the obedience of mankind. Even if it is not always explicitly stated, it is always understood. If obedience is missing, is it any wonder that the promises also fail to appear and are revoked by God?

v. 23. **You are strangers and sojourners with me**) How precious is God's goodness and truth in this, and how powerfully can this detach the mind of an obedient child from everything that is transitory, if the Holy Spirit can lay and strengthen this foundation living within us!

Nature, having turned away from God, settles itself in all things, regards everything as its own property, and turns vanity into nothing but eternal and permanent things in its imagination. Since the Fall, such an adhesive, false nature lies in the heart, seeking its only life and pleasure in the senses and reason, wandering and spreading so far into earthly things that it possesses, uses, loves, speaks, and thinks of everything with a sense of "ownership." This poison has flooded the entire creation and made everything damnable and full of hellish fire.

What closer, surer, and more blessed way out of such miserable slavery and captivity could Eternal Grace in Christ have invented than making this temporal life merely a passage, a journey, or a pilgrimage for us? He has presented it as such so that we should never linger in it with our spirits but always hasten toward the Fatherland.

The Eternal House-Father <note>A term for God the Creator as the master of the household of the world.</note> calls out to all inhabitants of this earth: Oh you people, look around you and see where you are, and where time is rushing you! Truly, you are in an inn, where you have but one or two nights to lodge; after that, you must depart.

Nothing of all that you see is yours. Everything belongs to the Master of the House, who has lent it to you. You are not to take your goods or your provisions as your own property; otherwise, you will be condemned as thieves and robbers.

Do not make a long calculation <note>original: *facit* - a Latin term used in German for a sum or accounting result.</note> for yourselves here, as if you intended to boast and feast forever on foreign goods! Behold, your hour is soon up: Arise, and prepare yourselves for the exit!

Blessed then is he who does not gape at apparent vanities, but as a called pilgrim of the earth and citizen of heaven, keeps his spirit ready to return to God, his origin! Thus, one brings a joyful conscience even into old age, and blessed eternity finally swallows up the brief time of suffering with infinite joy and triumph, where there will be an eternal day without darkness or change in the infinite light of divine glory.

The spirit longs for this, and the beginning seeks its end again; the pilgrim his Fatherland, the guest his rightful dwelling, the bird its nest; so that God may be all in all eternally.

v. 24. **A redemption**) For the benefit of the poor, so that everyone could finally regain his ancestral inheritance.

### The Third Book of Moses. Chapter XXV. 546

25. If your brother becomes impoverished and sells some of his property, then his redeemer <note>original: "Einlöser"; refers to the 'Go’el' or next-of-kin responsible for recovering family land</note>, who is closest to him, shall come so that he may redeem what his brother has sold.

26. But if someone has no redeemer, and his hand reaches enough <note>meaning he gains the means</note> so that he finds as much as is sufficient for his redemption;

27. Then he shall calculate the years since he sold it, and he shall give back what is remaining to the man to whom he sold it, so that he may return to his property.

28. But if his hand does not find as much as is enough to give back to him, then what he sold shall remain in the hand of the one who bought it until the Jubilee Year; in the Jubilee Year it shall be released, and he shall return to his property.

29. And if someone sells a dwelling house in a walled city, his right of redemption shall last until the year of its sale is ended. For one full year, his right of redemption shall last.

---

<margin>v. 25. The closest) Relative.</margin>
With this, GOD intended to establish love among the Israelites, so that they should take care of their poor brother. See Ruth 2:20 and 4:4.

<margin>v. 26. His hand reaches) Through inheritance or in another way.</margin>
v. 27. The redemption could occur if 2 years had passed after the purchase: for the buyer could keep it for at least that long.

v. 28. If the sold piece of land or field could not be redeemed, it remained with the buyer until the Jubilee Year; at that time it went out free again and returned to its first owner, who had sold it out of necessity, without the payment of a single cent <note>original: "Heller"; a very small historical coin</note>, even if the buyer had already sold it to another, and that person to a third.

v. 29. What was special, however, was that although all rural estates, and even houses in villages, could be redeemed again: a dwelling house in a walled city could not be redeemed again after the one-year period; and thus it was not released in the Jubilee Year either, but was lost forever. This was intended to teach them to walk carefully in civil society so as not to forfeit such freedoms, and whatever other reasons there may have been.
However, of greater weight is the mystery that some enlightened souls see here: that if someone sells their portion in the heavenly Jerusalem—to which all the firstborn shall attain—through wanton disregard for such a birthright and the love of earthly pleasures, like Esau, they will be unable to reach this citizenship of the firstborn in the holy and great city (Revelation 21:2-10) for all eternity. Instead, they must be deprived of it forever, even though all are called to it and the right was earned for them through Christ.

**One year shall his right of redemption last**) This is an image of the time of grace or the year of salvation, which lasts as long as it is called "Today."

<column-break/>

30. But if it is not redeemed until a full year is complete for him, then the house which is in a city that has walls shall belong to the one who bought it as a permanent possession for his descendants; it shall not be released in the Jubilee Year.

31. But if it is one of the houses in the villages that have no walls around them, it shall be counted as the field of the land: it shall have the right of redemption and be released in the Jubilee Year.

32. As for the cities of the Levites, namely the houses in the cities of their possession, the Levites shall have an eternal right of redemption.

33. And if someone purchases <note>literally: "appropriates"</note> from the Levites, then the sold house or city of his possession shall be released in the Jubilee Year. For the houses in the cities of the Levites are their possession among the children of Israel.

34. But the field of the suburbs of their cities shall not be sold; for they shall have that as an eternal possession.

---

v. 30. **If it is not redeemed**) This refers to when true repentance and the obedience of faith in Christ regarding the right of the birthright [does not] occur.
Another receives such a "bishopric" <note>referring to a position of oversight or inheritance</note>, and he [cannot] get back his mystical house, which he could have had in the upper Jerusalem, even at the restoration of all things. Instead, he must be content with a lesser place and measure of salvation, as if in the countryside.

**The house**) Paul clearly names this to us in 2 Corinthians 5:1; thus we may recognize how this ordinance concerns us, for whom otherwise the Law was written; (these are the words of Origen <note>original Latin: "Origenis"</note> (a) [so that] we might follow it rightly, not being permitted to possess rural estates nor [houses] in the cities—and why do I say houses? Not even several coats, nor much money.

v. 31. **According to the field of the land**) Like a sold field or piece of land.

v. 32. 33. But there was something even more special with the houses of the Levites.

**In the cities of their possession**) That is, in the cities that were assigned to them as their own. For otherwise they could well, and partly had to, live in other cities.

v. 34. **The field of the suburb**) Landis understands this as the 1000 cubits closest to the city and the common pasture; whereas Hanameel sold Jeremiah a field near the city of Anathoth. Jeremiah 32:7, 8.
Regarding the mystery hidden beneath this, Origen requires a priestly mind and a Levitical state. And according to the spiritual understanding—as he further speaks—a mind dedicated to GOD is called a priest; but "Levi" is the one who unceasingly clings to GOD and stands ready at His beck and will. Let us first become such people, then more can be said of this, and it will also reveal itself.

### Chapter XXV. The Third Book of Moses. 547

35. And if your brother becomes poor, so that his hand falters beside you; then you shall take him in, whether he be a stranger or a sojourner, so that he may live beside you.

36. You shall take no usury <note>original: "Wucher"</note> nor interest <note>original: "Uebersatz"; refers to a surcharge or profit on goods</note> from him, but you shall fear your God, so that your brother may live beside you.

37. You shall not give him your money for usury, nor provide your food for interest. (a) Ps. 15:5.

38. I am the LORD your God, who led you out of the land of Egypt, to give you the land of Canaan, and to be your God.

39. And if your brother becomes poor beside you, so that he sells himself to you; you shall not let him perform the service of a slave <note>original: "Knechts-Dienste"; refers to harsh or degrading labor</note>.

40. He shall be with you as a hired hand, or as a sojourner: he shall serve with you until the Jubilee Year.

41. Then he shall go out from you, he and his children with him, and shall return to his own kin, and to the possession of his fathers he shall come again.

<margin>v. 35-38. Regarding the poor)</margin> How this commandment is to be observed toward the poor, and that one should not pinch any extra profit from the fruits of nourishment; this has already been dealt with above in Exodus 22:25. We should indeed remember the many spiritual and physical blessings that the Lord has shown us, and therefore strive only to be good stewards of His gifts. In this, we should be mindful of the Savior's faithful exhortation in Luke 16:9-12.

<margin>v. 39 etc. God wanted)</margin> God wanted to preserve the families in their possessions, which had fallen to them in the distribution of the land of Canaan, and also to preserve their freedom: and if both should indeed have been lost, yet in the fiftieth year every man was to come again to his possession and to his family in freedom.

<margin>v. 40. Until the Jubilee Year)</margin> Yet if someone from his kinship wished to redeem him, he could be released sooner: and if his master wished to set him free out of compassion, he was also free to do so. If the master died and left no male heir, the servant was also made free by such a death.

<margin>v. 41. Then he shall go out)</margin> As soon as the 50th year began, from the first of Tishri <note>the first month of the Hebrew civil year</note> until the Festival of Atonement, they were indeed not yet entirely free, but they no longer served their master; rather, they were in good spirits and wore wreaths upon their heads. But as soon as the 10th of Tishri or the Day of Atonement came, and the horns were blown, every Israelite man-servant, as well as maid-servant, went out—regardless of how they had entered service, whether they had sold themselves out of poverty or been assigned to someone by the authorities because of theft—even if their years of service were not yet finished, and even those servants who had had their ears pierced and had previously not desired to leave their masters, went free and clear back home, and thus each returned to his family.
Whoever had a wife and children took them freely with him (a).

(a) <note>original: "vid. Joseph. l. 4. Antiq. c. 8. Cun. l. 1. de rep. Hebr. c. 2."</note> See Flavius Josephus, *Antiquities of the Jews*, Book 4, Chapter 8. Cunaeus, *On the Hebrew Republic*, Book 1, Chapter 2.

<column-break/>

42. For they are my servants, whom I led out of the land of Egypt: they shall not be sold as a slave is sold.

43. You shall not rule over him with severity, but fear your God. Eph. 6:9. Philem. v. 16.

44. But your man-servant and your maid-servant, whom you wish to have, you shall buy as servants and maids from the very heathens who are around you.

45. Also from the children of the sojourners who stay with you, from them you may buy them, and from their kin that is with you, whom they have fathered in your land; these you shall have as a possession.

46. And you may make yourselves owners of them for your children after you, that they may inherit the possession: these you may let serve forever. But over your brothers, the children of Israel, there shall no one rule over the other with severity.

47. And

<margin>v. 42. For)</margin> The LORD God wanted to call His people to be a free people, over whom He would rule as King, and He wanted no slaves or bondservants <note>original: "Knechte oder Leibeigene"</note>, as Luther translates it, under His reign. See Jeremiah 2:14, John 8:33. Therefore also the priests among them were to be like fathers in their families, explaining the laws of the Lord to them and exhorting them to follow them. And then there were the elders, who were to maintain such laws and punish wrongdoers. But they finally burdened themselves with a king, and thereby greatly injured their own freedom and rejected the loving, fatherly government of God; regarding this, read 1 Samuel 8. Nevertheless, the Lord did not want them to be kept as slaves or bondservants, either by kings or much less by their neighbors and brothers, nor should the poor be ruled with severity.

<margin>v. 44. From the heathens)</margin> They were permitted to keep true slaves, who were either bought or born in the house to heathen bond-maids who had not yet accepted the Jewish religion.

<margin>v. 45. Also from the children of the sojourners)</margin> Or "strangers in the gate," as they were called, of whom it is spoken elsewhere.

<margin>v. 46. Such servants and maids)</margin> Such servants and maids remained bondservants and had no benefit from the Jubilee Year.
**But over your brothers no one shall rule over the other with severity**) Which in the New Testament should teach us all the more that neither Christian authorities nor others should hold believers—or even those who confess the name of Christ—as such slaves and bondservants, but rather sweep out this heathen leaven <note>a metaphor for corrupting influence</note> and magnanimously abandon such heathen laws, since the rule of Christ binds them all, and they cannot withdraw from it, because they are all brothers who wish to be saved through Him; Matthew 23:8. Yet for this reason, believers can still be authorities and subjects, and each must observe their duties; both sides should strive to become only faithful servants of God, Romans 6:22, and of Jesus Christ, the King of all kings and Lord of all lords, who wishes to hold us not as servants, but as friends. John 15:14-15. See also 1 Corinthians 7:23, 12:13.

> This all pointed toward Christ and toward our redemption from our spiritual bondage under impurity and unrighteousness. Luke 4:18. The Savior knew it best.

<margin>v. 47-49.</margin>

<margin>v. 54.</margin>

Since we are all so impoverished through sin and sluggishness that we cannot help ourselves in the least.

<margin>v. 55.</margin>
> Oh, better to serve the rightful Lord than to be stuck in such shameful servitude! Better a prisoner of GOD and one bound to Jesus Christ than a contemptible servant of the devil and a slave to one's desires!
> Oh, that is a happy captivity, the captivity of the souls surrendered to GOD! They are never freer than the more they find themselves in this captivity. To be a prisoner of GOD is to depend so much on Him through the gift of freedom which one has given back to Him, that one can no longer use this free will except in submission to His own movements. GOD commands as the Supreme One, and the soul resists Him no more. It feels indeed that it is a prisoner: but it is such a sweet captivity that it does not desire to be otherwise, and prefers such captivity far above all the freedoms of the world. And the more this captivity grows, the more its freedom grows as well. For the creature can never be truly free except when it is entirely immersed in the will of its Creator.

# Chapter XXVI. The Third Book of Moses.

**3. If you walk in my statutes, and keep my commandments, and do them;**

**4. Then I will give you your rains in their season, and the land shall yield its increase, and the trees of the field shall yield their fruit.**

<margin>Deuteronomy 12:10.</margin>
**5. And your threshing-time shall reach unto the vintage, and the vintage shall reach unto the sowing-time; and you shall eat your bread to the full, and dwell in your land safely.**

Here, God now promises His physical blessing as a pledge of the spiritual and heavenly. For godliness <note>German: *Gottseligkeit*</note> has at all times the promise of this life and of that which is to come. 1 Timothy 4:8. Nevertheless, believers in the New Testament must, above all things, strive after the spiritual blessing in heavenly goods in Christ, Ephesians 1:3, and precisely not look upon the physical, seeing as the Apostles and many dear believers lived in great poverty and heavy tribulations.

However, if the Law—as the Jews and many following their mindset would have the Scriptures understood—is to be understood not spiritually, but only carnally or literally; then there is no doubt that when it is observed according to the letter, it also bestows such blessings upon those who do so. But if the Law is spiritual, as Paul believed, then it must without doubt also be observed spiritually, and therefore a spiritual reward of blessing must be hoped for; just as, conversely, the curses of a spiritual law are not intended physically.

**v. 3. Keep my commandments)** Not only in the book, nor only in the memory; but that you *do* them.

**v. 4. Your rains)** These are thus special rains for a special people. For

If these were merely common rains promised to those who keep God’s commandments, how would it be that the same rain appears in its season even for those who do *not* keep God’s commandment, and these rains are common to one as to the other in the world? Now, if the unrighteous receives a share in this just as the righteous does, and perhaps even has the most enjoyment of it, how then could such a special reward of blessing be contained herein for those who keep God’s commandment? That God lets it rain over the righteous and the unrighteous is more than certain. For the Savior said it Himself (a). Even if the Jew does not accept this because the Lord Jesus said it, it must be enough for you, who let yourself be called a Christian after His name; and you cannot view as a special blessing that which the unrighteous has in common with the righteous. We must therefore look for such a rain in Holy Scripture which is granted to the saints and believers alone, and of which the clouds are commanded that they should not give such over the unrighteous.

**The land shall)** be a good land, and bring forth fruit thirty, sixty, and a hundredfold. Matthew 13:23.

**v. 5. Bread to the full)** In earthly matters, the godless often receive much more of this, whereas the righteous must sometimes go hungry. What does Paul say in 1 Corinthians 4:11 and 2 Corinthians 11:27? But if it is understood according to the sense of Wisdom (b), of the bread spoken of in John 6, then no doubt remains.

**Shall dwell safely)** Because abundance is a dangerous lure, and often draws in foreign guests and enemies who want to share with us and thereby hinder peaceful possession, He frees His people from fear of such danger through the promise that He will provide them with peace and security.

(a) Matthew 5:45.
(b) Proverbs 13:25.

<column-break/>

<margin>(a) Proverbs 3:24-25.</margin>
**6. And I will give peace in the land, so that you shall sleep, and none shall make you afraid: and I will rid the land of evil beasts, and no sword shall go through your land.**

<margin>(a) Psalm 18:40-41.</margin>
**7. And you shall chase your enemies (a), and they shall fall before you by the sword.**

**8. And five of you shall chase a hundred, and a hundred of you shall chase ten thousand. Then your enemies shall fall before you by the sword.**

**9. And** <note>The text breaks off here at the catchword for the next page.</note>

---

**v. 6. I will give peace)** What kind of peace? As the world gives? Not at all. John 14:27. Under the law of the new covenant, He gives instead the sword. Matthew 10:34. But He gives His peace, which surpasses all understanding. Philippians 4:7.

What better can be understood by the general peace, which God intends to establish for those who keep His commandments, than the general peace of the mind's inclinations and powers <note>German: *Gemüths-Neigungen und Kräfte*</note>, with which He graces those who surrender themselves entirely to Him? They labor for a time in active ways, and think to bring about the peace of their inclinations through a holy keeping of these commandments of God; but without success. Yet God, in view of their labor and godly pursuit, gives them—through His immeasurable grace, by placing them into the prayer of quiet <note>German: *Gebeht der Ruhe*, a term for a state of mystical contemplation</note>—not only peace from some inclinations, but from all, and also adds the peace of those powers which are in such a sweet and deep sleep that nothing can distress them. All threats of creatures, and everything else that might be said to them—namely, that they would lose themselves through these ways, and that they remained entirely idle in them—can no longer turn them away from it, nor cause them to make another resolution.

**No terror)** For if I fear God, I fear nothing else. Therefore the righteous is as bold as a young lion, Proverbs 28:1, and for that reason does not fear the lion that walks about, nor the dragon, nor his angels; nor is he terrified by the dread of the night. Psalm 91:5.

**The evil beasts)** Because our peace may be disturbed either by an internal evil or from without, the Lord promises safety in view of both.

Physical animals are otherwise actually neither evil nor good in themselves, but became so to man only through the Fall: but that is a wicked beast which deceived our first parents and also slinks into Paradise. And that is an evil beast against which Peter warns us in 1 Peter 5:8.

**v. 7. You shall chase your enemies)** What kind of enemies, other than the devil and his angels themselves, the evil and unclean spirits. How we can chase them, James also tells us in chapter 4:7. Resist the devil, and he will flee from you.

**v. 8. Five)** Who are these five? Answer: The innocent virgins <note>a reference to the Five Wise Virgins of Matthew 25</note>. If we are of their number, we shall chase a hundredfold. Through the wise speeches and convincing words of a brave soldier of Jesus Christ, a whole multitude of deadly contradictors is overcome and put to flight.

**By the sword)** of the Spirit, the Word of God, which is sharper than any two-edged sword.

<margin>v. 9. I will turn toward you</margin> Like the sun shining upon the crops. Oh, what a great benefit it is / when the LORD turns toward someone! Peter could speak of this / who was already half lost / when he had denied the Lord: but came back to himself / when the Lord turned toward him.

<margin>v. 10. it is assured</margin> that in obedience one should not find it necessary / to hoard the old store for another year; because such an abundance should exist / that one would cast out the old even in the presence of the new / because new blessing and new grace would always be expected.

<margin>Of the old store</margin> <note>German: *Vom Firnen* refers to produce from previous years.</note> From the old provisions. These are the prefigurative scriptural passages of the Old Testament.

<margin>Before the New</margin> To the Gospel / the spiritual law / the new spiritual food of JESUS Christ / who.

<margin>My soul</margin> that is / Christ; says Origen (a): just as he is also called the Word of God / the Wisdom of God / the Arm and the Power of God. And in such a way "my soul" is the same as "my Son."

<margin>No loathing of you</margin> God is so good / that he never casts us away / unless we first leave him through our own unfaithfulness.

<margin>v. 12. He goes with the soul; and she always with him.</margin> He especially testifies to her / that he is her God and her protector: and this is an excellent communion of love.

<margin>v. 13. I have broken the bars of your yoke</margin> In place of which he lays his gentle yoke / of faith / of love / and of hope.

<margin>Walking upright</margin> There is nothing more unjust / than to bring the believers of the New Testament under a heavy yoke of servitude / when they should be able to lift up their heads with a joyful spirit to the praise of God.

...withdrawn from obedience / so she feels a thousand plagues because of it. <unclear>She</unclear> and made her victorious over her enemies; so that she again enters into her own <unclear>powers</unclear> weaknesses and stumblings. <margin>v. 16.</margin> The drying up or wasting of the eyes is taken here as the annihilation of divine enlightenment / which is brought about by an imagined fire and heat / which one creates for oneself. And then the soul faints / because one sows in vain / and works much without fruit.

<margin>v. 14.</margin> 14. But if you will not obey me / and will not do all these commandments;

There are two mainsprings <note>German: *Senn-Adern*, literally "sinews" or "tendons," used here as the driving forces of governance.</note> of common governance / by which the great Law-giver binds his people to obedience; from which earthly law-givers have also taken an example: namely rewards and punishments. However, it is the will of the LORD / that we should rather allow ourselves to be won over by the first of these two. He also knows well the form of the heart / which he has made / and knows / that we naturally prefer to be drawn with the cords of a man / namely with the bonds of love. Hosea 11:4. And therefore he would then certainly prefer / that his goodness should gently lead us to repentance and penance / rather than that we / like a dumb irrational beast / should have need of compulsion. Psalm 32:8, 9. This is God's way and manner with Jews and Gentiles.

<margin>v. 14. 15. 16. But if the so great goodness of God cannot win us / to keep us in the way of his commandments / but we wish to deviate from him; then he hedges our way with thorns. Hosea 2:6. If his mercies can gain nothing from us / then he sends his judgments. If the offered rewards will not persuade us / then he distresses us with his punishments. Yes / if lighter tribulations will not move us / then he sends heavier ones. And that is the chief content / sense and meaning / of this chapter.</margin>

Now, when it is announced here / that disobedience / which is the sin of witchcraft, 1 Samuel 15:23, should be visited with all kinds of physical curses and judgments / which is a harbinger of eternal judgment; this is understood to mean not only coarse and abominable sins / but also when one deals with God only in a casual manner: namely when one wants to serve him in such a way / that one will not allow anything to be taken away from the lusts of one's flesh; which is nothing else than serving God and Mammon and one's belly / and cannot stand together. See Matthew 6:24. Philippians 3:18, 19.

The soul has no sooner withdrawn itself from the obedience owed to God / than she feels a thousand plagues because of it. She withdraws from that composure in God / who would have fought for her and could have made her mindful of her own powers / in which she nevertheless encounters nothing but weaknesses and stumblings. She is weakened even by her own strength / upon which she relies / so that / without even fighting / as soon as she only catches sight of her enemies / she falls. She is so full and so confused by her vain anxieties after her unfaithfulness / that she flees / even though no one pursues her. Whereby she then removes herself more and more from simplicity and union with her God / the further she proceeds in her own exercises / and sinks into her own powers.

# Chapter XXVI. The Third Book of Moses.

**18. But if, despite all this, you will not obey me / then I will punish you seven times more for your sins.**

**19. And I will break the pride of your strength / and I will make your heaven like iron and your land like bronze.**

<margin>v. 18.</margin> Now God speaks to those who are utterly abandoned / those who truly do not return to their own works: but who nonetheless do not obey him / refusing to trust him in the things he commands / and failing to let themselves be led according to his will through the incomprehensible ways of Wisdom; for they fear they might surrender themselves too much to God. Then he lets them feel his hand seven times more than he otherwise would for their sins: in that he lets them experience such weaknesses and trials as he would not impose even upon the greatest of sinners; for the punishment or purification of such sinners is postponed until the next life: but these souls, chosen by God, he pulls back from their <term>self-will</term> <note>German: *Eigenheit*; refers to the spiritual ego or the tendency to rely on oneself rather than God</note> with heavy hammer blows and through terrible suffering. And thus, such great sufferings, as they are described in the spiritual life, arise only from this self-will; they are also beautifully recorded in various places of the Holy Scripture.

Here one may express what it means to be punished seven times more severely / and how dearly God makes one pay—even with interest—for a small misstep through the appearance of a sin / and often through sin itself: and how ghastly self-will / pride / and self-righteousness are before God; so that it commonly happens that he allows either stumblings / or the appearance of them / so that their pride may be dampened thereby! For this is a mystery reserved for his judgment alone. Is this not what St. Paul expresses when he says <margin>(a) 2. Cor. 12 / 7.</margin> (a): "Lest I should be exalted above measure through the abundance of the revelations / there was given to me a thorn in my flesh / namely, the messenger of Satan / to buffet me with fists." As if he wanted to say: So that I do not claim God's graces as my own / an experience of the uttermost misery teaches me what I am of myself / and keeps me in total nakedness even in the midst of these very high and holy graces.

<margin>v. 19.</margin> The first tenderness of pride / which is broken here / is the self-complacency that the soul has in its gifts and graces and in its own strength. The second is the tenderness caused in it by self-will / which places a real obstacle in the way of the soul's union with God.

Now, so that this pride and self-will may be destroyed / God closes the heaven before such a soul; it becomes like iron to them; no pleasant dew flows from it for them; God seems to have nothing but harshness for them: It seems as if he no longer wishes to hear them / but rather to cast them away. The soul now finds not the slightest comfort / neither in heaven nor on earth. For the earth has become like bronze to it / in that it can no longer taste its sweetness. Then the soul finds itself in a most piteous state / as experience sufficiently shows.

However, those people who feel these pains can hardly believe that they come only from their self-will / and that what they see as great trials from God are merely the pains of self-will / which they do not recognize. They need only to surrender themselves / and let go of all resistance / giving themselves over without exception and without fear into the hands of God; not through a formal and comprehensible surrender / which still provides some support / but truly / so that they give themselves over without wavering to the whole will of God / and allow themselves to be robbed of everything good without moving or resisting / also enduring all attacks of the enemy without any fear; being assured that God alone can strike down all our enemies: But as soon as we enter into any self-defense / that would already be enough to make us fall at their mere approach.

<column-break/>

**20. And your strength shall be spent in vain / for your land shall not yield its increase / and the trees of the land shall not bring their fruit.**
<margin>Habakkuk 3 / 17.</margin>

**21. And if you walk contrary to me / and will not consent to obey me; I will bring seven times more plagues upon you according to your sins.**

**22. And I will send wild animals (a) of the field among you / which shall rob you of your children / and destroy your cattle / and make you few in number; and your streets shall be desolate.** <margin>(a) Deuteronomy 32 / 24.</margin>

**23.**

It is therefore possible that the Lord may repeatedly impose punishments upon his people / and that sevenfold more than before / and yet his people still will not be obedient: which the Lord actually anticipates here / and therefore says:

<margin>v. 21.</margin> (If you walk contrary to me) When something happens to us differently than we wanted / supposed / thought, or imagined / and without our expectation; such a thing is said to happen by chance or "contrary" <note>German: *zufälliger Weise*; the author plays on the meaning of "coincidence" or "casually" vs. "contrary to."</note>. Now, since the will of the Lord is that we should keep his commandments and walk in his ways with our whole heart and will; it happens, on the contrary, quite often that when a person does what is commanded / it is done as if beyond their purpose and intention / or casually / as if in passing.

Or it is also / as the learned Jews explain it / to walk with God in such a way that whatever one encounters from him / one attributes to accidental chance and blind luck: just as there are many blind worshippers of such a goddess <note>The Roman goddess Fortuna</note> even among Christians: from whom the thought should be far removed that one should imagine any accidental or "chance" outcome in regard to God; but rather / that he foresees all things / and wisely disposes and orders them / even those which seem accidental and by chance to man.

(Will not consent) If you have a desire / heart, and will / not to obey me. God looks through our heart and will at our feet and conduct. He looks at the delight or the displeasure of the heart.

The most high God created man as a noble and free creature / with power and ability to act / this or that / or even to do things contrary to these: and because all things between God and man are handled in the manner of a covenant / the conditions of the same always presuppose free agents who enter into the covenant; and therein lies my possibility to keep the covenant or to break it: just as for that reason both rewards and punishments are attached. For otherwise / man would be unjustly punished for that which could not have been avoided; and improperly rewarded for that which could not have been done otherwise. And thus there would be neither merit nor punishment / neither sin nor righteousness. All persuasions and dissuasions / all counsels / exhortations / admonitions / all promises and threats / punishments and warnings / all commands / all prohibitions / in a word / all the workings of God upon the human will / which would then in fact no longer be a will / all laws of God and men / would in such a case all be null and void / useless and in vain / indeed a pure delusion and shadow-boxing.

(Plagues — according to sins) In proportion to the sins and upon the sins; also according to the quality and kind of the sins. Thus he gladly punishes greed with plundering / pride with banishment / hardness with fire / luxury with want / worldly joy with terror / hypocrisy with the destruction of churches / etc.
