# The Third Book of Moses [Leviticus]. Chapter XXVI.

**23. And if by these things you will not be reformed by me / and walk with me in such a casual manner / <note>German: *zufälliger Weise*. While often translated as "contrary" in Bibles, the author here interprets it as "incidental" or "by chance," meaning a lack of serious intention.</note>**

**24. Then will I also walk with you in such a casual manner / and**

The Lord our God pays close attention to the form and inclinations of our hearts / whether we are with him or against him; and / even if we are with him / whether it happens with a firm purpose of the heart / or only in a casual manner / as if the service of God and walking with him were a side-project <term>side-project</term><note>German: *Nebenwerck*; a secondary task or minor matter compared to one's main business.</note> or something that could be performed only superficially and as if in passing.

And here the perversity of the human heart is to be wondered at and lamented / that it pursues vain and transitory things with such earnestness and zeal / and conversely disregards lasting / constant / and eternally-enduring things; making the former its main business and most noble affair / and the latter its side-project. For how does one not pursue such things with the utmost concern / which in the final end may be of no use at all! And yet one pays little heed to the things / which can truly be of use / so that in truth one should seek nothing else but them.

It is therefore not only highly-just and rational / but also God’s great love / goodness / and mercy / that he requires of his people / that they should walk with him with a whole and perfect heart; not at random and in a casual manner / however it comes. And so it must then also be possible / to walk with God thus / through the grace of God / without whom we can do nothing / but through whom we can do all things / <note>Philippians 4:13</note>. so that one keeps his commandments and does them; just as on the other hand the opposite is possible / that one does not walk with him: so that therefore no preceding necessity finds a place here / that would determine or force us to walk or not to walk with God in the way of his commandments.

However, God also assures the souls of whom verses 18 and 19 spoke / that / if they would proceed further in their resistance / so as not to let themselves be led by him wherever he wished; then he would also increase their punishment: He would not be satisfied with merely not hearing them / and being harsh toward them / nor with heaven being implacable to them / nor with the dew no longer falling upon them; but he himself would be opposed to them. Oh, if one only knew / what that was / to have God against oneself / and what kind of terrible torments one must endure because of it; oh, what would one not rather resolve / than to let it come to this extreme misery! Job / when he felt the weight of such a cruel abandonment / lamented miserably <margin>(a) Job 7:20.</margin> / that / because God was opposed to him / he could no longer bear himself. But the creature is so self-interested / that it would rather endure all of this / than to deny a virtue / for which it lives. It even believes / it deserves something by it / that it endures so many pains to preserve such virtues. But it is shamefully deceived; in that it loses the essential virtue thereby / because it wants to keep the apparent one: whereas it should rather let this apparent virtue go / so that it might obtain the essential one.

v. 24. **Then will I also with you so)** Just as purpose and chance are opposed to one another / so it may be said of the Lord / that he walks as it were in a casual manner with men / when his gracious purpose and intention are not directed toward them. And thus he lets it rain over the just and the unjust. To the former he gives beneficial rain with purpose and out of good intention; but to the latter just as it happens by chance.

What comfort can that bring / if one, like the rich man in <note>Luke 16:25</note> / receives good things from an angry God / when it does not stem from God's good will toward us / and from his purpose to do us good / but as if by chance?

A righteous child has no joy in all that his father gives him / unless he receives it with a blessing. And what joy can we ever draw from that which our heavenly Father gives us / if it does not come with a blessing?

<column-break/>

**I will also strike you seven times more for your sins;**

**25. And I will bring the sword upon you / which shall execute the vengeance of the covenant / so that you shall gather yourselves into your cities: then I will send the pestilence among you / and you shall be delivered into the hand of the enemy.**

**26. When I break the staff of bread among you / then ten women shall bake your bread in one oven / and shall bring back your bread by weight; and you shall eat / but not be satisfied. <margin>Haggai 1:6.</margin>**

<margin>27. An...</margin>
The repeated strikes / with which God chastises the soul because of its resistance / are weaknesses which have some fellowship with mortal sins / and with which he burdens the soul so that it might despair of its own strength / and be moved to surrender itself entirely to him. It seems to the soul itself / that it is nothing more than pride <note>German: *Hoffart*; a traditional word for vanity or arrogance</note>. All its thoughts / words / and works / are full of it. It feels more temptations than before / toward the earth / and toward that to which it clings. It believes itself to be full of impurity from head to foot. It is plagued with resentment and envy against those who belong to God with greater surrender. It loses all mortifications <term>mortifications</term><note>German: *Enttöttungen*; the spiritual practice of "dying to the self" or subduing worldly desires.</note> / and it appears to it / as if it were entirely fleshly. It can fit into nothing / nor maintain itself: and the more it tries to do so / the less it succeeds. A certain imagined hatred / which it cannot overcome / grieves it: yes, it often seems to it / as if it were moving against God. The anger / which for a long time seemed dead in the soul / wakes up again; and moments of rashness arise instantly.

All those spiritual people / who have not surrendered themselves / admit this: one more / another less; according to the degree of their self-will / and the decree of God for their rescue. And the higher a soul has been elevated through the flow of God's gifts / the deeper is its fall through the experience of such tribulations. Indeed, all those who are dedicated to the "hidden death" <note>A mystical term for the total annihilation of the ego.</note> go / as was said / through this. And that is because / they may be as faithful as they wish / they nonetheless resist / without thinking of it; in that they (because they are not yet enlightened) seek to place their faithfulness in their resistance: while they wonder at their sluggishness and laziness in all good things / since they can do almost nothing good anymore; and now take up spiritual things with such coldness / though they had previously applied themselves to them with very great zeal.

v. 25. **Sword -- Vengeance of the Covenant)** This sword of vengeance of the covenant is a knife of separation / which God puts into the soul / to distinguish the two parts / the highest and the lowest part / without which the soul would always struggle in conflict. Oh, then this separation of the soul makes for mighty death-pangs! When it sees itself thus in need / it runs into the "cities" / to find some rescue for itself: that is; it seeks some supports in external works / in the practice of virtues / in fellowship with the servants of God / in the enjoyment of the holy sacraments. But all of this does not ease its burden: because the grace of this stage is a grace of death <term>grace of death</term><note>German: *Gnade des Todes*; a paradoxical concept where God's "grace" is experienced as the painful death of the old self.</note> / and therefore must also cause an increase of loss / so that the soul sees itself delivered into the hands of its enemies by that very means / though for its highest benefit.

v. 26. God breaks the strength of our bread / when / instead of finding comfort in the Holy Supper and similar external means / we find nothing but utter tastelessness and new pains in them. This is a severe trial for a good soul / which has a great esteem and reverence for the holy sacrament / and all such things; and it is all the more so / because it does not find itself finished with this spiritual martyrdom / but on the contrary / even more empty.

# Cap. XXVI. The III. Book of Moses [Leviticus]. 553

**27. And if you will not for all this obey me / and walk with me in such a casual manner;**
**28. Then I will also walk with you in fury in a casual manner / and I will also chastise you seven times more for your sins:**

When God sees that this soul / which he desires to have for himself alone / is still more opposed to him; he does not only move against it / but he increases its pains even further / and moves against it with fury. Oh, then the soul no longer knows what will become of itself! For God breaks it in his fury / just as Job (a) had experienced; and its anguish becomes infinitely greater than can be expressed. Nevertheless, it is certain / that our Self-will <term>Self-will</term><note>German: *Eigenheit*. In mystical theology, this refers to the ego, or the part of the human will that insists on its own way rather than submitting to the Divine.</note> is the only cause of all this / at least commonly so: although it is also true / that God also imposes anguish according to his almighty power / so that the purest souls may experience inward suffering; just as Jesus and Mary suffered: and that St. Paul also often burned with pain and sorrow (b) / which suffering was caused by his zeal for the glory of God and for the salvation of his brothers. But these kinds of suffering are so pure and so calm / that they may well be called entirely spiritual sufferings. The other pains / however / which are caused by Self-will / are commonly accompanied by some confusion and unrest: in that they are like a devouring fire / which through a strong and deep activity makes known the rust and impurity / which still remained to be consumed. With this intention, King and Prophet David also [entreated] God / that he (c) would not rebuke him in his anger / nor chasten him in his hot displeasure.

Now as the resistances persist / the more the pains are doubled / and then God increases the evil. For the second time it was only external blows because of sins according to their distinction: But now they are seven wounds because of the sins. What until now was only on the surface / now seems to have taken over the entire interior / and thus to have deep wounds. Oh, what a great difference there is between wounds and blows / and how well those know it who have experienced it! To appearance they are indeed the same trials / since they always occur regarding the seven aforementioned deadly sins: But how greatly their piercing depth differs!

**v. 28. Will walk with you in fury in a casual manner)** For it is fitting for the Judge of all the world / to lead back all those / who walk inordinately with their God / and to bring them into the order of justice.

God is always good and the highest good / but also just / indeed strict in the punishment of unjust and perverse men. He is / as one of the Fathers writes / by his nature solely good / but casually also strict / because of sin: and when his people deal with him as if everything happened only by chance / and do not look to him as the cause of everything; then he will also meet them in the heat / anger, and fury of such "accidental" adverse events: so that one might take his judgments to heart / learn righteousness / and accustom oneself to walking with him with a full purpose of heart.

In this matter the choice indeed stands with us / and God forces us to nothing: but our greatest danger also rests upon it / if God has accepted us as his people / made himself known to us / and also allowed us to recognize and taste both the evil and the good through experience / and we in this case yet waver and limp before our best friend / if we walk with our GOD uncertainly / haphazardly, and casually / just as it happens to come.

So then let whoever will / yes, let all false Christians / who are blinded by their sins and injustices / walk with the true God in a casual manner: but as for us / who know what respect is due to God / and have learned Christ differently / as truth and an upright nature is in him / let us walk with the Lord our GOD with a full purpose of heart!

(a) Job 16:10. (b) Rom. 9:2. (c) Ps. 6:2. <unclear>Urstiv.</unclear> *Sacred Qualities, part 2, book 3, chapter 8.*

God brings everything in the aforementioned soul into disorder. Its cities / which are its external and internal senses and its powers / are set into such a devastation / which turns them into a solitude.

The center / and the very deepest part of the soul / which is the sanctuary / must be destroyed and brought to nothing. Not the slightest image of holiness remains in it any longer; and the GOD / who previously dwelt within it / is no longer inside. Oh, then it is time / that this sanctuary (which nevertheless served as an intermediary between God and the soul) be completely destroyed / so that nothing of it remains! Oh, what a cruel blow the soul suffers through the loss of this sanctuary! Yet this is still something good in the midst of its misfortune / and a means for its improvement: which indeed might seem too hard / but in truth is only too fortunate. For there no hope remains for the soul anymore. Oh, who could only grasp such a thing! And yet it is this destruction of the sanctuary and the center of the soul / which soon brings an end to all trials.

**v. 33. Among the heathen)** They indeed came to know the Assyrians and Babylonians / and finally the Romans / in such a manner.

## 23. And if you will not be corrected by me by these things, and will walk with me in such a casual manner:

## 24. Then I will also walk with you in such a casual manner / and

The Lord our God pays close attention to the state and inclinations of our heart, whether we are with him or against him; and, if we are with him, whether it happens with a settled purpose of the heart, or only in a casual manner <note>original: "zufälliger Weise." This refers to a heart that is indifferent or treats devotion as an incidental thing rather than a priority.</note>, as if the service of God and walking with him were a side-work or such a matter that could be performed only superficially and as if in passing.

And here we must wonder at and lament the perversity of the human heart / which chases after vain and temporary things with such earnestness and zeal, and yet regards lasting, constant, and eternal things as insignificant; making the former its primary work and chief concern, and the latter its secondary business. For how one chases after such things with the utmost concern, which in the end may be of no use! And yet pays little heed to the things which can be of use then / so that in truth one should seek nothing else but those very things.

It is therefore not only highly fitting and rational / but also God's great love, goodness, and mercy / that he requires of his people / that they should walk with him with a full and perfect heart; not by chance or in a casual manner, just as it comes. And so it must also be possible / thus to walk with God / through the grace of God, without whom we can do nothing / and through whom we can do all things / Phil. 4:13. that one may keep his commandments and do them; just as, conversely, the opposite is also possible / that one does not thus walk with him: so that no preceding necessity finds a place here / which would determine or force us to walk or not to walk with God in the way of his commandments.

God also assures the souls spoken of in verses 18 and 19 / that, if they should continue further in their resistance / so as not to let themselves be led by him where he wished to go; then he would also increase their punishment: He would not be satisfied with not hearing them, and being harsh toward them, nor that the heavens should be implacable toward them, nor that no more dew should fall upon them; but he himself would be contrary to them. Oh, if one only knew what it was to have God against oneself, and what terrible torments one must endure because of it; oh, what would one not rather resolve to do / than to let it come to this extreme misery! Job, who felt the weight of such a cruel abandonment, lamented miserably <margin>(a) Job 7:20.</margin> that, because God was against him / he could no longer bear himself. But the human race <unclear>race</unclear> is so self-interested / that it would rather endure all this / than renounce a virtue to which it clings. It believes, rather, that it deserves something by enduring so many pains to preserve such virtues. But it is shamefully deceived; by losing the essential virtue because it wishes to keep the outward appearance: whereas it should rather let go of this apparent virtue / so that it might obtain the essential one.

v. 24. I also with you so) Just as purpose and chance are opposed to one another / so it may be said of the Lord / that he walks as if in a casual manner with men / when his gracious purpose and intention are not directed toward them. And thus he lets it rain upon the just and the unjust. To the former he gives convenient rain with purpose and out of good intention; but to the latter just as it happens to fall.

But what comfort can that bring / if one receives good things, like the rich man in Luke 16:25, with an angry God / if it does not proceed from God's good will toward us, and from his purpose to do us good / but as if by chance?

A righteous child has no joy in all that his father gives him / unless he receives it with a blessing. And what joy can we ever draw from what our heavenly Father gives us / if it does not come with a blessing?

<column-break/>

## I will also strike you seven times more for your sins;

## 25. And I will bring the sword upon you, which shall execute the vengeance of the covenant, so that you shall gather yourselves into your cities: there I will send the pestilence among you, and you shall be delivered into the hand of the enemy.

## 26. When I break the staff of bread for you / ten women shall bake your bread in one oven / and deliver your bread again by weight; and you shall eat, but not be satisfied. Hag. 1:6.

The repeated blows with which God chastises the soul because of its resistance / are weaknesses which have some commonality with mortal sins / and by which the soul is burdened so that it may despair of its own strength / and be moved to surrender itself entirely to him. It seems to the soul itself that it is nothing more than pride. All its thoughts, words, and works are full of it. It feels more attachments than before to the earth / and to that which it clings to. It believes itself full of impurity from head to foot. It is plagued with grudge and envy against those who belong to God with greater surrender. It loses all self-mortification / and it seems to it as if it were entirely carnal. It can restrain itself in nothing, nor maintain itself: and the more it tries to do so / the less it succeeds. A certain imagined hatred, which it cannot overcome, troubles it: yes, it often seems to the soul as if it were moving against God. Anger, which had seemed dead for a long time / wakes up again; and sudden impulses arise in an instant.

All spiritual people / who do not surrender themselves / belong here: one more, another less; according to the measure of their <term>Selfhood</term> <note>German: *Eigenheit*. The stubborn part of the human ego.</note> and the counsel of God for their purification. And the higher a soul has been elevated through the flow of God's gifts / the deeper is its fall through the experience of such distresses. Indeed, all those who are devoted to the <term>Secret Death</term> <note>German: *geheimen Tod*. A mystical term for the total dying-away of the ego to God.</note> go through this, as was said. And that is because / however free they may wish to be / they nevertheless resist without thinking about it; in that they (because they are not yet enlightened) seek to place their faithfulness in their resistance: while they wonder at their sluggishness and laziness toward everything good, as they can do almost nothing good anymore; indeed, they are annoyed to find themselves taking up spiritual things with such coldness / when previously they had applied themselves to them with very great zeal.

v. 25. Sword -- Vengeance of the Covenant) This legal sword of the covenant is a knife of separation / which God puts into the soul / to distinguish the two parts, the upper and the lower part / without which the soul would always be in conflict. Then this separation of the soul causes violent death-agonies! When it sees itself thus distressed / it runs into the "cities" to find some rescue in itself: that is, it seeks some pieces in outward works, in the practice of virtues, in fellowship with the servants of God / in the enjoyment of the holy sacraments. But all this does not relieve it: because the grace of this stage is a grace of death / and can only cause an increase in the sense of being lost / so that it sees itself delivered into the hands of its enemies / although for its highest benefit.

v. 26. God breaks the strength <note>original: "Kraft" or "Stab."</note> of our bread when / instead of finding comfort in the Holy Supper and similar outward means / we find nothing but tastelessness and new pains in them. This is a severe trial for a good soul / which has a great esteem and reverence for the holy sacrament and all such things; and all the more so / because it does not find itself satisfied by this spiritual hunger / but on the contrary, even more empty.

27. And if through this you will not obey me / and walk with me in such a casual manner;

28. Then I will also walk with you in fury in a casual manner / and I will also chastise you seven times more for your sins:

When God sees that this soul / which he wants to have for himself alone / is even more set against him; then he does not just go against her / but he increases her pains even more / and goes against her with fury. Ah, then she no longer knows what will become of her! For God breaks her in his fury / as Job (a) had experienced; and her anguish becomes infinitely greater than can be expressed. Nevertheless, it is certain / that our self-will <note>original: "Eigenheit." In pietistic writing, this refers to the "ego" or the stubborn insistence on one's own desires over God's.</note> is the only cause of all this / at least commonly: although it is also true / that God also imposes anguish according to his omnipotence / so that the purest souls may feel inward suffering; just as Jesus and Mary suffered such things: and that St. Paul also often burned with pain and sorrow (b) / which suffering his zeal for the glory of God and for the salvation of his brothers caused him. But these kinds of suffering are so pure and so calm / that one may well call them entirely spiritual sufferings. The other pains / which are caused by self-will / are commonly accompanied by some confusion and restlessness: in that they are like a consuming fire / which through a strong and deep operation makes known the rust and the impurity / which still remained to be consumed. With this in mind, the King and Prophet David also prayed to God / that he (c) would not punish him in his anger / and not chastise him in his fury.

Now as the resistances persist / the more the pains redouble / and then God increases the evil. For the second time, it was only outward blows because of sins according to their distinction: But now they are seven wounds because of those sins. What until now was only on the surface / now seems to have taken over the entire inward being / and thus to have deep wounds. Oh, what a great difference there is between wounds and blows / and how well those know it who have experienced it! To outward appearance, they are indeed the same trials / in that they always occur regarding the seven aforementioned capital sins: But how different is their penetration!

v. 28. **Will walk with you in fury in a casual manner)** For it is fitting for the Judge of all the world / to lead back all those / who walk in a disorderly way with their God / and to bring them into the order of justice.

God is always good and the highest good / but also just / yes, severe in the punishment of unjust and perverse people. He is / as one of the Fathers writes / by his nature merely good / but in a casual way <note>original: "zufälliger Weise." Here used in a philosophical sense: God is essentially good, but His severity is a "circumstantial" response necessitated by human sin.</note> also severe / because of sin: and if his people deal with him as if everything happened only by chance / and do not see him as the cause of everything; then he will also encounter them in the heat / anger, and fury of such "chance" adverse occurrences: so that one might take his judgments to heart / learn justice / and accustom oneself to walking with him with a full purpose of heart.

In this, the choice indeed lies with us / and God forces us to nothing: but our greatest danger also rests upon it / if God has accepted us as his people / made himself known to us / and allowed us to know and taste both the evil and the good through experience / and we in this case yet waver and limp before our best friend / when we walk with our God in an uncertain, accidental, and casual manner / just as it happens.

So let whoever wants / yes, let all false Christians / who are blinded by their sins and injustices / walk with the true God in a casual manner: but let us / who know what respect is due to God / and have learned reverence / how in him is truth and a truly created essence / walk with the Lord our God with a full purpose of heart!

## The XXVII. Chapter.
->The valuation of vowed things.<-

And the LORD spoke to Moses / and said:
2. Speak to the children of Israel and say to them: When someone makes a special vow / the persons shall belong to the LORD according to your valuation.
3. Your valuation of a male from twenty years old up to sixty years old shall be: your valuation shall be fifty silver shekels <note>original: "Seckel." A shekel was a standard unit of weight and currency in ancient Israel.</note> according to the shekel of the sanctuary.
4. But if it is a female / then your valuation shall be thirty shekels.
5. If it is from five years old up to twenty years old / your valuation of a male shall be twenty shekels / and of a female ten shekels.
6. And if it is from one month old up to five years old / your valuation of a male shall be five silver shekels / and for a female your valuation shall be three silver shekels.
7. And if it is from sixty years old and upward / if it is a male / then your valuation shall be fifteen shekels / and for a female ten shekels.
8. But if he is too poor for your valuation / then he shall present himself before the priest / and the priest shall value him: according to what the hand of him who vowed can reach / the priest shall value him.

---

<insert>
A vow is when someone dedicates themselves, their family, or their property to the LORD, in order to be rescued from a certain distress / or to become a partaker of a special benefit.
These promises depend on a person's free will / and God is willing to accept them / but the person must then consider his duty / to indeed fulfill them / lest he be punished by God for his unfaithfulness. Ecclesiastes 5:3-4.
</insert>

<column-break/>

9. And if it is an animal / of which one can bring an offering to the LORD; everything that one gives of it to the LORD / shall be holy.
10. One shall not exchange it nor change it / a good for a bad / or a bad for a good. But if one does indeed change one animal for another / then both it and what was exchanged for it shall be holy.
11. But if it is any kind of unclean animal / of which one may not bring an offering to the LORD; then he shall set the animal before the priest:
12. And the priest shall value it / between good and bad; according to your valuation by the priest, so shall it be.
13. And if he indeed wishes to redeem it / then he shall add a fifth part to it above your valuation.
14. And when someone sanctifies his house / so that it is holy to the LORD; the priest shall value it / between good and bad: as he / the priest / shall have valued it / so shall it remain.
15. And if he who sanctified it wishes to redeem his house / he shall add the fifth part of the money according to your valuation to it; then it shall be his.
16. And if someone sanctifies part of the field of his inheritance to the LORD / then your valuation shall be according to its seed. The seed of a homer <note>A dry measure equivalent to about 220 liters.</note> of barley shall be valued at fifty silver shekels.
17. When

Whatever was vowed to the LORD, whether clean or unclean animals / or houses and estates; that had to be handed over / or / where one wished to keep it / the value of the same and a fifth part added to it / had to be given as a kind of penalty for the change of heart.
If, for example, another buyer gave 100 according to the valuation / he had to give 120 / and / where another gave 1000 / give 1200.
And because the inherited estates became free again in the Year of Jubilee / the valuation of them had to be set and paid according to the number of years.

In this, God also wished to teach us / how we are likewise bound to put our promises to our neighbor into action; otherwise God will also know how to punish the unfaithfulness committed against the neighbor.

This then aimed primarily at the betrothal <note>original: "Verlobung." Here used in the sense of a spiritual vow or commitment.</note> that one owes to God in Christ / when one also promises oneself to Him / to be rescued from the distress of eternal damnation / and to become a partaker of eternal salvation through Him. <note>Commentary on the text above</note>

Here, believers must also be faithful / and pay attention in their inner selves to their impulse, regarding what they might feel moved in their interior to apply from their wealth to the honor of God / so that they then also diligently endeavor to promise and keep the same faithfully: just as the good deed of the believers in Macedonia is praised in 2 Corinthians 8:3 etc. And in this regard, the pious ancients were also very eager to make such rich foundations from what remained to them / through which, according to their understanding, they intended in sincerity to promote God’s honor / which also would not have been without a blessing on their souls: of which, however, the examples in our very earthly-minded times are very rare / and therefore little blessing is mostly to be felt in families.

# The Fourth Book of Moses,

Which among the Hebrews takes its name from the word in the first verse / which in German is given as **"in the wilderness"** <note>original: "in der Wüsten"; the Hebrew name for the book is *Bamidbar*</note> / and, in accordance with this name, provides a detailed description before the other books of what occurred in the desert / and thereby simultaneously presents the symbolic state of the Church / as long as it remains in the wilderness.

And because this book also deals extensively with counts; such as the census of the entire people in Chapter 1 / that of the Levites in Chapter 3 / who were to represent the firstborn / and the 42 encampments in Chapter 33: it received the name from the **Septuagint** <note>The "LXX" or seventy translators of the Greek Old Testament.</note> in Greek / and from them also in Latin / that it be called **"The Numbering"** <note>Latin: *Numeri*; English: *Numbers*</note>. Just as **Jerome** <note>original: "Hieronymus"</note> (a) also judged / that the mysteries of the entire calculation are contained therein.

<margin>(a) to Paulinus</margin>

That Moses, next to GOD, is the author and writer of the same / is demonstrated by the commentators from Deuteronomy 31:24, John 3:14, and 5:46–47 / against those who wish to attribute it to **Ezra** or some other person / because, in part, Moses is often spoken of in the third person; which, however, also occurs in the second, third, and fifth books of Moses: and in part because a certain **"Book of the Wars of the LORD"** is cited therein / which was not yet written in Moses' time; regarding which more can be said in its proper place.

Indeed, ceremonial statutes still appear in this book / just as the people of the Old Testament, as the counterpart, certainly deal with more than enough ceremonies and statutes in the still-enduring wilderness: but the primary purpose is the preparation of Israel for their march toward the land of **Canaan**. Therefore also

The primary content is the journey of the Israelites through the wilderness from Mount Sinai to the Jordan / and comprises / as reckoned by some / a history of the accounts of Moses and the Hebrews spanning 38 years, 9 months, and 20 days / from the second month of the second year of their departure from Egypt until nearly the death of Moses and the end of the journeys. Along with this are recounted the various trials and manifold falls into sin of the people / and the resulting judgments of GOD / as well as the diverse dangers and blessings of GOD / between Mount Sinai and the promised land.

The judgments occurring herein are, according to their order, these: (1) The people's craving for meat brings a great plague upon their necks. Ch. 11. (2) **Miriam** is struck with leprosy because of her rebelliousness against Moses. Ch. 12. (3) According to the firm decree of GOD, all men who marched out of Egypt must die in the wilderness. Ch. 14. (4) A man / who gathered wood on the Sabbath / is stoned. Ch. 15. (5) The company of **Korah** is swallowed alive by the earth / and the entire congregation is nearly completely destroyed for their rage against this judgment. Ch. 16. (6) The grumbling is punished with the bites of fiery serpents: Ch. 21. (7) and a great multitude is slain because of idolatry and harlotry with the Moabites. Ch. 25.

Aiming toward **Christ**, one finds symbolic figures in the **Nazirites** / as those consecrated to GOD; the confirmation of Moses in his prophetic office against all opposition; the blossoming rod of **Aaron**; the bronze serpent; and the installation of **Joshua** in Moses' stead / just as the Law gave way to Christ: and then the glorious prophecy of **Balaam**. Ch. 24. Just as Christ then also points us to this book in John 3.

The general order of it is otherwise / that / after the divine service and the Church order were first established / the state of the commonwealth and the government of the people now follow / and the primary purpose therein is the revelation of the truth, justice, and grace of GOD in governing His own in this world, shown in so many examples and in all of Israel / as a clear prototype of the Church engaged in its pilgrimage: Thus the entire book may consist of roughly 3 main divisions, which are: 1) The arrangement and preparations for the march of the Israelites; up to Chapter 10. 2) The progress from Mount Sinai to the Moabite wilderness and the borders of the land of Canaan; up to Chapter 22. 3) The encampment and whatever else occurred shortly before the taking of the promised land; until the end.

And here the truth of Christ’s saying manifests: **Many are called, but few are chosen!** since the bodies of most fell in the wilderness of this world because of unbelief. For

What was written therein previously / was written as a prototype and a warning for those / upon whom the end of the world has come. Just as the temptations, stumblings, and judgments / depicted here / have already sufficiently manifested among us / and will manifest even more / as we still have the passage through the Jordan of the great temptation (Rev. 3:10) before us.

The Fourth Book of Moses. Chapter 1.

# Chapter 1.

->The numbering of the people, excluding the Levites.<-

**A**nd the LORD spoke to Moses in the wilderness of Sinai, in the tent of meeting, on the first day of the second month, in the second year after they had come out of the land of Egypt, saying:
**2.** Take the sum of the whole congregation of the sons of Israel, according to their families, according to their fathers' houses, with the count of names, every male, head by head;
**3.** From twenty years old and upward, everyone who goes out to the army

<note>v. 1.</note> *On the first day of the second month in the second year*) Thus, only one month has passed since the setting up of the Sanctuary <note>The Tabernacle</note> until this muster, when the camp of Israel was to be properly organized. See Exodus 40:17.
<note>v. 2.</note> *Count of the names*) Come here, all you who have a resolute spirit, to serve the Lord of Hosts in deed and truth as noble Israelites, and to be part of His militia; come here and let yourselves be inscribed as faithful people in His registry and muster-roll!
All His soldiers must be of the male sex, in view of dignity, strength, and brave courage. Yet this should not be to the disadvantage of the female sex in spiritual warfare, as if to exclude them from it. For there have been, and still are, and will yet be found brave "manly" women of that same sex to lead the Lord's wars. See Exodus 38:8 and Galatians 3:28.
Just as Christian bravery is signified here by the male sex, so it is also regarded in the required age.
<note>v. 3.</note> *From twenty years*) At this age, the Lord requires the strength of a youth in a soldier who is to fight against internal and spiritual enemies.
And what can be better understood by the number twenty than the Law of God doubled or twofold in its number? The Ten Commandments alone in the letter belong to a child and one who is still immature. But the Law is also spiritual. Romans 7:14. This Law brings life, strength, and power with it. Romans 8:2 and 1 John 2:14.
*And upward*) But how much "upward"? Answer: Scripture nowhere limits this, nor does it set a goal or end to the duty and service of the Christian warrior.
In this, there is a great difference between earthly and internal soldiering: in the former, the age of sixty years brings exemption from war. But in the Christian war and struggle against spiritual enemies, age brings no exemption. Paul, though he was already old, was still a soldier of Jesus Christ. However, there are all too many who, when they are oppressed by age, only then begin to learn the use of spiritual weapons and want to deny themselves and their lusts when they can no longer practice them.
*Everyone*) whoever has a good will and seeks to come out of spiritual Egypt.
*Goes out to the army*) Or also, as others understand it, everyone who "went out," namely from Egypt, in conformity with the first verse and Chapter 26:4. Thus, the focus here would not be on the army or the host, but on the redemption from Egypt.
The redemption from Egypt is of no use to those for whom a ransom was indeed paid for redemption, but who meanwhile remain in their slavery and in Egypt; it is only for those who come out from there and serve their Redeemer in His wars. Luke 1:74–75.

<note>v. 3 cont.</note> ...just as it is also the duty and office of the Evangelical priest in spiritual warfare. Ephesians 6:10–18.
<note>v. 4.</note> These had their assistants and helpers, who were captains or distinguished men.

<column-break/>

in Israel. You and Aaron shall count them according to their hosts.
**4.** And there shall be a man from each tribe with you: namely, a man who is a head in his father's house.
**5.** These [names follow...]

<note>Israel</note> means strength and overcoming with God, and God is the strength of Israel. 1 Samuel 15:29. His warriors must be strong in the Lord and in the power of His might. This is what is looked for in the muster.
*Count*) Or—because this word is too general for the subject of this and the following chapter—rather "inspect" or "muster"; whereby it is not only a matter of the number, but also looking at how fit and prepared for war the people are. For the Lord requires capable warriors who are brave and stouthearted. Deuteronomy 20:3, 8.
Those who are of no account stand like zeros and are not counted. But the Lord’s warriors are all counted and chosen.
But not everyone is worthy of the divine counting, as Origen <note>An early Christian scholar, c. 184–253 AD</note> says (a); rather, those who are to be included in God's number are marked with certain prerogatives. Thus, women are not included, nor any servant, nor anyone from the "mixed multitude" of Egyptians who marched out; but only Israelites alone. And even of those, not all, but only those from twenty years and upward. The younger age of children was not considered fit for the counting, except in the case of the firstborn or the priestly and Levite state. These things are not without further meaning. As long as you remain a child in divine understanding, you do not count as a man. When you have outgrown the "children's shoes" of vanity and folly, and put away what is childish and silly; when you have become such a youth who overcomes the Wicked One and walks in the strength of Israel: then you will also be reckoned in the divine counting. As long as a womanly softness or an Egyptian mind remains in us, we are not recognized as fit to be accepted into the holy number written by God; whereas those who belong to it are not only counted themselves, but even their hairs are numbered. Matthew 10:30.
But why were they not counted immediately when they went out from Egypt? Answer: Pharaoh was still pursuing them then. They were not even counted when they had already gone through the Red Sea and come into the wilderness. For they were not yet tested, nor yet attacked by enemies. They first had to fight with Amalek and overcome him. And yet they were still not counted. For one victory does not settle it. And even though they had eaten manna and drunk water from the rock, they were still not counted then. First, the Tabernacle had to be built, the Law given, the sacrifices ordered, and the cleansing and sanctification emphasized; only then did the time for counting come.
Write this, O reader, double and triple into your heart, and learn what you must pass through, what you must endure, and what temptations and struggles you must experience if you want to be reckoned among the living in Jerusalem, and counted among the holy families and tribes; for which, in the Ambrosian Hymn of Praise <note>The Te Deum</note>, "Lord God, we praise Thee," it is prayed for the Church with these words: "Let them be numbered with Thy saints in eternal glory."
*According to their hosts*) He who wishes to serve in the spiritual war must unite himself with the host of Israel, with the Church of Christ, which is an army with banners set in battle array (Song of Solomon 6:3 <note>6:4 in many English bibles</note>); so that he may receive and impart her strength.
*You and Aaron*) For who is more fit for this than Moses, the king (Deuteronomy 33:5), who according to his name is "one who draws out"; and Aaron the High Priest, whose office is to instruct and exhort the Lord's warriors, and whose duty is in spiritual warfare. Ephesians 6:10–18.

### Chapter 1. The Fourth Book of Moses. 559

5. And these are the names of the men who shall stand with you: Of Reuben, **Elizur** the son of **Shedeur**.
6. Of Simeon, **Shelumiel** the son of **Zurishaddai**.
7. Of Judah, **Nahshon** the son of **Amminadab**.
8. Of Issachar, **Nethanel** the son of **Zuar**.
9. Of Zebulun, **Eliab** the son of **Helon**.
10. Of the children of Joseph: of Ephraim, **Elishama** the son of **Ammihud**; of Manasseh, **Gamaliel** the son of **Pedahzur**.
11. Of Benjamin, **Abidan** the son of **Gideoni**.
12. Of Dan, **Ahiezer** the son of **Ammishaddai**.

---

There is no doubt that all these names contain something great and secret within them, as the Lord is accustomed to expressing the essence of a thing through its name. In the meantime, we wish to provide some meaning here based on the characteristics of the Hebrew language.

**v. 5. Elizur)** That is, "My God is the Rock"; and the Rock is Christ. <note>original: 1. Cor. 10/4</note> His father is **Shedeur)** "The Light of the Almighty."

The light of wisdom and counsel, and the rock of power and strength, are two primary necessities for holy warfare. <note>original: 2. Kings 18:20</note>

**v. 6. Shelumiel)** "God is my reward," the wages of the spiritual soldiers, Abraham's payment after his war. <note>original: Gen. 15:1</note> He was the son of **Zurishaddai)** "The Almighty" or "the All-Sufficient is my Rock."

The Psalmist puts both together in Psalm 73:26.

**v. 7. Nahshon)** "Experience," an experienced soldier; the son of **Amminadab)** "My noble and willing people." Deborah and Barak sang of such people in Judges 5:9.

**v. 8. Nethanel)** "The gift of God," the son of **Zuar)** "the little one," the humble one. <note>original: 1. Peter 5:5</note>

**v. 9. Eliab)** "My God is the Father," the strong God. **Helon)** "mighty and strong."

**v. 10. Elishama)** "My God has heard," or "the hearing and obedience of God"; the son of **Ammihud)** that is, "glory of my people"; a figure of Him who is the true glory of His people Israel. <note>original: Luke 2:32</note>

**Gamliel)** or **Gamaliel**, "God is my reward." He is the rewarder of everyone who diligently seeks Him. <note>original: Heb. 11:6</note> He is the son of **Pedahzur)** "of the Rock," who is Christ the Redeemer.

**v. 11. Abidan)** "My Father is the judge"; namely, God the Father, who is a judge of all, and of every righteous cause for which one conducts His wars; the son of **Gideoni)** "He who tramples down, breaks down, and cuts off injustice," according to the original meaning.

**v. 12. Ahiezer)** "The helper of his brother"; according to Joab's speech to his brother Abishai in 1 Chronicles 19:12. We should help one another against pride and deceit. Such a faithful brother is the son of **Ammishaddai)** "the people of the Almighty." Those who fight against spiritual enemies must still be like this.

**v. 13. Pagiel)** He who encounters God, and whom God encounters in return: just like Melchizedek and Abraham. <note>original: Heb. 7:1</note> See Isaiah 64:5. Or also, he who makes intercession with God for the people; as the word also signifies, and is used of Christ in Isaiah 53:12. **Ocran)** He who troubles the enemies of Israel.

**v. 14. Eliasaph)** "God will cause to grow, increase, or add": namely, courage, strength, and knowledge. Just as he is the son of **Deuel)** "the knowledge of God." Paul puts both together in Colossians 1:10. This man is called **Reuel**, "the friend of God," in chapter 2:14, according to the frequent exchange of the letters D and R <note>A common linguistic shift in ancient Hebrew scripts</note>.

**v. 15. Ahira)** "A friendly brother" or "brotherly friend," is the son of **Enan)** that is, "their eyes," acting as a watchman or sergeant of the army. <note>original: Num. 10:29–31</note>

**v. 17.** Through this, it is emphatically signified and made known what kind of people the soldiers of Jesus Christ must be: namely, just such as Moses, Aaron, and their assistants were; or such as their names, which prophesy good things, clearly indicate they were. For how could others choose or approve the Lord’s soldiers unless they themselves were like them to a considerable degree?

*Those expressly mentioned by name*) The Lord knows every leader of His kingdom by name.

**v. 18.** And He also has the names of every one of His lowliest warriors, who stand among the others, written in heaven.

**v. 19.** The people of Israel were mustered three times: in the first year after they had eaten the Passover lamb and come out of Egypt (Exodus 30:12–13); here for the second time; and in chapter 26 for the third time.

---

In the first census—which was conducted for the purpose of the tax for the atonement of their souls in the very first year, as mentioned in Exodus 30:12 and 38:26—the Levites were included in the count. Here, however, in the second census, they are not. They certainly needed to pay something for the atonement of their souls, but here they were to remain exempt from military service.

Just as the number there was 603,550 (Exodus 38:26), it matches here again exactly. From this, we should note the wonderful providence of God among men, who determines all of them in their certain number.

<column-break/>

48. And the LORD spoke to Moses, saying:

49. Only the tribe of **Levi** you shall not number, nor take the sum of them among the sons of Israel.

50. But you shall appoint the Levites over the **Dwelling of the Testimony** <note>The "Dwelling of the Testimony" refers to the Tabernacle, the portable sanctuary that housed the stone tablets of the Ten Commandments.</note>, and over all its furnishings, and over everything that belongs to it. They shall carry the Dwelling and all its furnishings; and they shall attend to it, and shall camp around the Dwelling.

<margin>Chapter 3, verses 10, 38.</margin>
51. And when the Dwelling is to set out, the Levites shall take it down; and when the Dwelling is to be set up, the Levites shall raise it. But the stranger <note>A "stranger" here refers to anyone who is not a Levite.</note> who approaches shall be put to death.

52. And the children of Israel shall camp, each in his own camp, and each by his own standard <note>A "standard" (German: *Panier*) was a tribal banner or flag used for organization.</note> according to their armies.

53. But the Levites shall camp around the Dwelling of the Testimony, so that no wrath comes upon the congregation of the children of Israel; and the Levites shall keep watch over the Dwelling of the Testimony.

54. And the children of Israel did so; according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses, so they did.

---

**Verse 51. The Levites shall take down and set up the Dwelling)** Only then, and at no other time, did the Levites enter the Dwelling, and only when everything was wrapped up. For they were not permitted to look upon the holy vessels uncovered, nor to touch them even when covered, but only the carrying poles. See Chapter 4, verse 4, etc.

**Verse 52. Each in his own camp)** Everything was very orderly arranged in the camp, with streets, markets, stalls, and even workshops for all kinds of professions, as if it were a city. <margin>(a) Josephus, Book 3, *Antiquities*, Chapter 11; see also Exodus 32:27.</margin>

**Verse 53.** The Levites were to be, so to speak, the bodyguard of God, their King, so that no one from the rest of the people might come too close to God out of a lack of reverence. However, everyone could approach God with their sacrifices through the Levites and then the priests—serving as lower and upper ministers, respectively. These sacrifices were like petitions which they allowed these ministers to present to God. This was meant to be a proof that the access to God into the Sanctuary was not yet revealed as long as this first Tabernacle and the subsequent Temple stood (Hebrews 9:6, 9), until the prophecy of Jeremiah 30:21 would be fulfilled.

**Verse 54.** Just as the Israelites did what the LORD had commanded them through Moses, it is very unfitting for those who call themselves Christians that they do not do what God has commanded them through Christ, but rather let it stop at merely hearing and knowing. A brief summary of what He has commanded us can be found in Matthew 5, 6, and 7, by which everyone can easily test themselves to see if they are a doer of the Word or not.

# The Second Chapter.
### The Military Order of the Children of Israel.

AND the LORD spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying:
2. The children of Israel shall each camp by his own standard, with the signs according to their fathers' house: they shall camp around and opposite the Tabernacle of the Meeting.

<margin>A.</margin>
Just as the previous chapter contained the counting and muster, so here we find the positioning and order.

By this, GOD wanted to show how he is not a GOD of disorder, but of peace, so that everything should proceed in an orderly and honorable manner among His people: just as this should also rightly be maintained now in the churches of the New Testament among all congregations; 1 Corinthians 14:33, 40. For as it was then, so it is now truly the **Church Militant** <note>The term "Church Militant" refers to the Christians on earth who are struggling against sin and the devil, as opposed to the "Church Triumphant" in heaven.</note> here on earth, and we should all strive to be found as good soldiers of JESUS Christ, 2 Timothy 2:3. We must have the whole armor of GOD at hand, and thus, with these spiritual weapons of our knighthood, we must strive to overcome our powerful enemies and the "fortresses of the heights of reason." Ephesians 6:11; 2 Corinthians 10:3, 4, 5.

v. 2. They had to camp around the Tabernacle, facing it from all sides; and as is believed from Joshua 3:4, they were to be about 2000 cubits <note>original: "Ehlen"</note> away from it; and that in a square: which is believed to have been about 12 miles in length and breadth.

But when GOD the LORD ordains something of this nature, one may certainly believe that He is not concerned with the outward appearance alone—though that too is not without wisdom—but that His mind always intends a hidden mystery beneath it. In this, His Word is recognized as great: that whereas humans, with their words, express their entire meaning understandably, the LORD always hiddenly includes something more and deeper in His speeches. Whoever has once rightly grasped this principle of truth will not so easily grow weary in reading Holy Scripture, nor will they skip over it; but rather they will penetrate ever deeper, and—if he earnestly calls upon the LORD for His Spirit—he will indeed seek and make no mysteries where none exist, but neither will he so easily pass over them where they are.

<margin>B.</margin>
Around the Tabernacle) Where else should children be but around their father; the servants but around their lord; the disciples but around their master; the subjects but around their prince, the King of Saints; the younger brothers of Christ but around their elder brother?

The Jews themselves expand the explanation here to the Gentiles as well, and extend it to all nations that live around the Holy Land, which was the center of the then-inhabited world: Psalm 74:12. This is for the shaming of all those who, in their goodness, want to restrict GOD to the narrow boundaries of their own party, and will not allow Him to be good to anyone else but those they choose. But our GOD has His own circuits. His peoples are all around Him, and among them all, the one who fears Him and does right is pleasing to Him throughout the whole world. Acts 10:35.

<margin>C.</margin>
Just as the people of GOD are around Him, so He is also around them, Psalm 125:2; Zechariah 2:4. Indeed, He is in their very midst. He walks with them like a father among his children, as a king in the midst of his people. Psalm 46:5; Matthew 18:20. Indeed, He is even closer. "There is one among you whom you do not know." John 1:26; 2 Corinthians 13:5.

<margin>D.</margin>
Opposite) Facing the tent of the Commander-in-Chief, facing the main guard; as servants who stand ready to receive the word of command, to go wherever He orders them to go, and to do what He desires of them, and to do what He commands them to do, like the centurion's servant in Matthew 8:9.

There must be an equality between the Church Militant and the heavenly host, mentioned in Daniel 7:10.

<margin>E.</margin>
The spiritual **Eve**, the Church of GOD, the mother of all living, is created to be a helper, as it were, for Him. Genesis 2:18. The LORD has chosen a "masculine virgin" <note>The author uses "männliche Jungfrau" to describe a church that is both pure and brave or strong like a soldier.</note>, a brave bride, that she should stand before Him. Ephesians 1:4.

<column-break/>

3. And those who camp toward the East, toward the rising sun, shall be the standard of the camp of Judah according to their armies; and the prince of the sons of Judah, Nahshon the son of Amminadab:
4. And his army, namely those numbered of them, seventy-four thousand and six hundred.
5. And those who camp next to him shall be the tribe of Issachar, and the prince of the sons of Issachar, Nethanel the son of Zuar:
6. And his army, namely those numbered of him, fifty-four thousand and four hundred.

8. And his army, namely those numbered of him, fifty-seven thousand and four hundred.

10. The

<meta>This page begins Chapter 2 of the Fourth Book of Moses (Numbers), detailing the specific layout and military organization of the Israelite camp around the Tabernacle. # The Fourth Book of Moses. Chapter II.

### Chapter II.
->The Military Order of the Children of Israel.<-

**AND** the Lord spoke to Moses and to Aaron, saying:
2. The children of Israel shall camp, every man by his own standard, with the emblems of their fathers' house: they shall camp round about the Tabernacle of the Meeting, facing it.

Just as the previous chapter contained the counting and muster, here we find the positioning and order.
By this, God wished to show that He is not a God of disorder, but of peace, so that everything should proceed in an orderly and honorable fashion among His people: just as today in the Church of the New Testament, this should rightfully be maintained in all congregations (1 Corinthians 14:33, 40). For as it was then, so it is now: the Church on earth is truly the <term>Church Militant</term> <note>original: "streitende Kirche," referring to the church on earth struggling against sin and spiritual enemies</note>, and we should all strive to be found as good soldiers of Jesus Christ (2 Timothy 2:3). We must have the whole armor of God at hand, and thus, with these spiritual weapons of our knighthood, we must strive to overcome our powerful enemies and the strongholds of the heights of reason (Ephesians 6:11; 2 Corinthians 10:3, 4, 5).
v. 2. They had to camp facing the Tabernacle and all around it—and, as is thought from Joshua 3:4, about 2,000 cubits away from it. This was in a square, which is believed to have been about 12 miles in length and width.
When the Lord God ordains something of this nature, one may certainly believe that He is concerned not only with the outward form—though that itself is not without wisdom—but that His mind always includes a hidden mystery within it. In this, His Word is recognized as great: while humans usually express their entire meaning understandably with their words, the Lord, in His speeches, always includes more and deeper things hidden within. Whoever has once truly grasped this principle of truth will not easily become weary of reading Holy Scripture, nor will they skip over things; rather, they will penetrate ever deeper. If one earnestly calls upon the Lord for His Spirit, one will not seek or invent mysteries where none exist, but neither will one so easily overlook them where they are.
(Around the Tabernacle) Where else should the children be but around their father; the servants but around their lord; the disciples but around their master; the subjects but around their prince, the King of Saints; the younger brothers of Christ but around their elder brother?
The Jews themselves here extend the explanation even to the Gentiles, stretching it to all nations who dwell around the Holy Land, which was the center of the world inhabited at that time (Psalm 74:12). This is to the shame of all those who, in their goodness, want to restrict God within the narrow borders of their own party, and do not want to allow Him to be good toward anyone else but those they choose. But our God has His own circles. His peoples are all around Him, and among all of them throughout the whole world, the one who fears Him and does right is acceptable to Him (Acts 10:35).
Just as the people of God are around Him, so He is also around them (Psalm 125:2; Zechariah 2:4); indeed, He is right in their midst. He moves among them like a father among his children, as a king in the midst of his people (Psalm 46:5; Matthew 18:20). Indeed, He is even closer: "There is one among you whom you do not know" (John 1:26; 2 Corinthians 13:5).
(Facing it) Facing the tent of the supreme commander, across from the main guard; like servants who stand ready to receive the word of command, to go wherever He has commanded them to go, to come when He desires it of them, and to do what He bids them to do, like the centurion’s servant in Matthew 8:9.
There must be a similarity between the Church Militant and the heavenly host, as spoken of in Daniel 7:10.
The spiritual Eve, the Church of God, the mother of all living, is created to be a helpmate, as it were, for Him (Genesis 2:18). The Lord has chosen a manly virgin, a brave bride, that she should stand before Him (Ephesians 1:4).

<column-break/>

3. And those who camp toward the East, toward the rising of the sun, shall be the standard of the camp of Judah according to their armies; and the prince of the sons of Judah shall be Nahshon, the son of Amminadab:
4. And his army, namely those numbered of them, are seventy-four thousand and six hundred.
5. And those who camp next to him shall be the tribe of Issachar, and the prince of the sons of Issachar, Nethanel, the son of Zuar:
6. And his army, namely those numbered of them, are fifty-four thousand and four hundred.
7. The tribe of Zebulun, and the prince of the sons of Zebulun, Eliab, the son of Helon:
8. And his army, namely those numbered of them, are fifty-seven thousand and four hundred.
9. All those numbered from the camp of Judah are one hundred and eighty-six thousand and four hundred according to their armies: these shall set out first.
<meta>The catchword "10. D" refers to the start of verse 10 on the following page: "10. Das Panier..." (10. The standard...).</meta>

---

v. 3. (Toward the East <note>original: "Gegen Morgen," literally "toward the morning"</note>) On this eastern side were also the tents of Moses and Aaron (Chapter 3:38).
Christ is the true Morning Star and our guide to eternal life; therefore His tribe and lineage had to camp toward the East and at the very front. He is the Dayspring from on high (Luke 1:78) and the one who must have preeminence in all things, as our predecessor, king, and breaker of the way (Micah 2:13).
(The standard of the camp of Judah) On their banner, as the Jews say, a lion was depicted, with the inscription from Chapter 10:35.
v. 4. (74,600) God honors and increases the tribe from which Christ wishes to come. Therefore, this tribe is not only the first but also has the largest number and the most people.
v. 5. (Next to him) But, as the commentators believe—those who maintain this—not in the middle, although this tribe of Judah holds the center in the narrative and arrangement; for Judah had to have the first rank, and for that reason and for the sake of preference, the center was his due. Just as banners also belong in the center. And so Issachar was assigned to his right side.
v. 6. (His numbered ones) Those of Issachar are those who, according to the meaning of the name, "remember the Lord."
v. 7. (Zebulun) is, according to the name, a "dwelling of strength."
v. 8. Therefore, his army and his numbered ones are suited to the Lion of the tribe of Judah.
v. 9. (Camp of Judah 186,400 — shall set out first.) The first and the last camps were the strongest, so that Judah had the preference, from whom the Messiah and the royal dignity were to arise.

<header>The IV. Book of Moses. Ch. II.</header>

32. These are those numbered of the children of Israel by the house of their fathers: all those numbered of the camps according to their hosts were six hundred thousand and three thousand and five hundred and fifty.
33. But the Levites were not numbered among the children of Israel / as the LORD had commanded Moses.
34. And the children of Israel did so: according to all that the LORD had commanded Moses / so they camped according to their standards / and so they set out / each according to his family / according to the house of his fathers.

---

v. 32. Here, for the third time, the number 603,550 is repeated—which is said to be the exact sum of the root letters of the five books of Moses <note>This refers to Gematria, a Jewish system of assigning numerical value to letters to find deeper meanings</note>—having already been indicated in Chapter 1:46 and Exodus 38:26. Through this, the LORD intended to show His precise care for His people, demonstrating how He knows His own (2 Timothy 2:19) and has recorded them all by name in His muster roll—that is, in the Book of Life (Philippians 4:3), much like a general or field commander. 
Similarly, the mystery-laden number of 144,000 also appears three times: Revelation 7:4, 14:1, and 14:3.

v. 33. The Levites were exempted from military service; therefore, they were not included in the military order of the children of Israel.

v. 34. **So they camped -- and so they set out**) Thus we have here a prototype of the "Cherubic chariot" <note>A reference to Ezekiel's vision of God's throne-chariot surrounded by living creatures</note> with the many thousands who surround the LORD and stand at His service. Within is the Tabernacle of the Sanctuary along with the Ark of the Covenant, where Jesus Christ is present yesterday, today, and forever, issuing commands to the people through Moses and Aaron. Around this Ark, the four great army leaders are found in their tents as "Cherubic heroes," and around them, in turn, camps the great multitude of the Israelite people.

Whenever GOD intends to execute judgment, He goes to the field in this manner. Just as it happened here against the Canaanites, so it shall happen in the last days against the Antichrist. An attentive reader will perceive a mysterious agreement between the formation of the Israelite camp in the wilderness and what the Apostle John saw and made known in his heavenly Revelation, chapters 4, 5, and 7.

Therefore, some believe, not without reason, that Ezekiel’s Cherubim were modeled after these standards (Ezekiel 1:10). <margin>(a)</margin>

For things on earth are ordered according to those in the heavens. Thus, it is believable that the upper Cherubic chariot—upon which the Son of GOD presented Himself in the form of a Son of Man—was the original after which the camp and its four Cherubic commanders were modeled.

Because of this, the main standard of the fourth camp is said to have borne the image of an Eagle.

Thus, one sign would be taken from the wild animals [Lion], one from the tame animals [Ox], one from the birds [Eagle], and one from the human race [Man]. Although the Jews also ascribe—perhaps only by conjecture—certain animal names to the smaller standards of the other tribes, saying that, for example, Issachar had a donkey, Dan a snake, Naphtali a doe, and Benjamin a wolf, according to Genesis 49:14, 17, 21, and 27.

The Hebrews also write that each main banner had a color corresponding to the gemstone of that tribe in the high priest's breastplate. For example, Reuben would have had a red banner, as his stone was red—a sardius. They also say the names of the three patriarchs—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—were divided here so that the first letter of each name <note>The Hebrew letter 'Aleph' (א)</note> stood on the first banner; on the second, the next letters <note>The Hebrew letters 'Yod, Tzadi, Het' (יצח) for Isaac</note>, and so forth. <margin>(b)</margin> In this, the division of the Hebrews is not to be dismissed.

# The III. Chapter.
->The establishment of the Levites and the exchange for the firstborn.<-

AND these are the generations of Aaron and Moses / on the day that the LORD spoke with Moses on Mount Sinai;
2. And these are the names of the sons of Aaron: The firstborn Nadab / then Abihu / Eleazar and Ithamar.
3. These are the names of the sons of Aaron / the priests who were anointed / whose hand was filled <note>A Hebrew idiom meaning "to be ordained" or "consecrated" for service</note> / to minister in the priest's office.
4. But Nadab and Abihu died before the LORD / when they offered strange fire before the LORD in the wilderness of Sinai / and they had no sons. And Eleazar and Ithamar ministered in the priest's office in the sight of their father Aaron.

---

v. 1. 2. Recorded here are the sons of Aaron and the relatives of Moses—who was from the Kohathites, of the family of Amram, who was his and Aaron’s father—along with their duties: as the priestly office was inherited by Aaron’s descendants, but not the regency <note>The civil leadership or governorship</note> which Moses had exercised (Deuteronomy 33:5).

v. 3. **whose hand was filled**) The priest’s hand was filled with gifts and offerings that were to be sacrificed to GOD: more of which can be learned best from the first institution and consecration of the priests in Exodus 29.

In this manner, "filling the hand" represents the giving of possession of heavenly goods, over which GOD has made Christ the High Priest (Hebrews 9:11) and placed all things into His hand (John 3:35), which He now also does for His believers when He gives them the pledge of the Holy Spirit. We have various kinds of gifts to offer to our GOD, which the great High Priest has placed into our hands. Indeed, it is believed that some have more than enough to sacrifice regarding their own will.

**One**) No one is named here, neither Moses nor Aaron, as the one who fills the priest's hand. For the LORD alone is He who can make a priest. The LORD may fill whose hand He will, and speak through whom He will: But

No one must take the priestly office into his own hand until it has been given into his hand by the LORD, just as Christ did not glorify Himself to be made a High Priest (Hebrews 5:4, 5).

And without doubt, it was the will of GOD and His purpose and intention from the beginning that such a priesthood should be the general office or service of all His people.

v. 4. The sons of Aaron had to administer their office before their father and in his sight, so that they could be guided by their father in the proper administration of their service. This can teach us that it is well done when younger ministers stand by older ministers of the Word, so that the latter may give the former all good guidance, and the former may follow the latter.

Just as the Levites were handed over entirely to the priests for their service / and were thus subordinate; so it is also unavoidable in our present state of human weakness / that among the ministers of the Word, the elders / or those who have some advantage in spiritual gifts / should be placed over others / over whom they must at least have oversight / so that such men may faithfully fulfill their office. This can be counted among the human ordinances / to which one may submit for the Lord’s sake / 1 Peter 2:13. provided the office is administered not against / but according to the Lord’s will: where the greatest should behave as the youngest / and he who leads like one who serves; Luke 22:24, etc. and where they are to remember / that they are fellow elders / who should not rule over the flock / much less over their fellow elders: 1 Peter 5:3. which even Peter had to write / who sometimes seems to have been preferred by the Lord / and to whom the dignity of tending Christ’s flock was especially commanded; John 21. this is now indeed also claimed by those / who wish to be his successors and high priests; but they are little mindful of this admonition.

v. 12. **From the midst)** He who never deviates either to the right or to the left / can best be said to be in the middle. This, however, is primarily Christ; John 1:26. and thereafter those who are closest to him. **instead of all the firstborn)** Natural rights and physical birth count for little with God; rather, it is the preference of the heart: just as one may see in the case of Jacob and Esau.

**who open the womb)** and are also first begotten by the father. See Deuteronomy 21:15, etc.

and were priests; and those who did not descend from Aaron, Izhar) Who is also called Amminadab.

The Levites had much to do at the Tabernacle, especially in the wilderness, and had to take care of and transport all the equipment when traveling.

So that everything would proceed in an orderly fashion, each family knew exactly what it was supposed to do.

v. 23. **Westward**) On the side where the Most Holy Place was, along with the two tribes from the sons of Rachel: Ephraim, Manasseh, and Benjamin.

v. 24. **Eliasaph**) Thus, he had the same name as the prince of the tribe of Gad.

v. 25. 26. The Gershonites had all the soft items in their care: the colorful coverings woven with Cherubim and flowers, the goat-hair <term>camlet</term> coverings, and the red and blue skin coverings, the curtain that served in front of the Holy Place, the hangings, and the ropes with which they were fastened to the stakes in the ground.

v. 27. The fact that the Kohathites, who were otherwise from the second son of Levi, were entrusted with the most prominent items of the sanctuary happened because Moses and Aaron, and thus the priests, were chosen from among them. And it certainly stands within God’s power to prefer one family over another in this regard, so that they may perform the nobler services for their neighbor.

v. 30. **Elizaphan**) Of him it is otherwise noted that he is listed elsewhere as the middle one among the sons of Uzziel; thus, it seems he was not made prince because of birthright; just as their father was the youngest son of Kohath. ### Chapter III. The Fourth Book of Moses. <note>The Fourth Book of Moses is the traditional name for the Book of Numbers.</note>

37. And the pillars of the court round about with their bases, and their pegs and their cords.

38. But before the dwelling toward the East, before the Tabernacle of the Meeting toward the sunrise, Moses and Aaron and his sons shall encamp, who keep the charge of the sanctuary for the charge of the children of Israel. And the stranger who comes near shall be put to death. <margin>v. 10. ch. 1:51. 18:22.</margin>

39. All those numbered of the Levites, whom Moses and Aaron numbered according to their families, by the command of the Lord, all the males from a month old and upward, were twenty-two thousand. <margin>ch. 4:48.</margin>

---

<margin>v. 37. The pillars of the court) 56 in total.</margin>
<margin>Their pegs) or copper stakes, which were driven into the earth and to which the hangings were fastened. Likewise</margin>
<margin>Their cords) which hung from the pillars and were used to tie the hangings firmly to them.</margin>
Because these pieces were not few in number, and were not light but heavy, they were assigned 4 transport wagons with 8 oxen, upon which they could load these items. <note>This refers to the logistics of moving the Tabernacle through the desert.</note>

The Gershonites and Merarites also dismantled the dwelling when it was time to travel, and set it up again when they were to rest.

<margin>v. 38. Before the dwelling toward the East — Moses and Aaron etc.) So that they might be very close to the entrance of the Tabernacle and could attend to their office there.</margin>

<margin>v. 39. 22,000) This number does not match the specific numbers of the three tribes of the Levites in verses 22, 28, and 34, which add up to 22,300. Since one cannot say that a round number of a thousand was intended—otherwise, the excess of 273 firstborn would also have been rounded—some believe that these 300 were the firstborn of the Levites themselves. They could not be used to "buy back" or redeem others because they already belonged to the Lord as firstborn, just as the rest of the tribe did.</margin>

The fact that three orders were established in the service of the sanctuary and the Tabernacle can represent to us how three kinds of ministries were specifically ordained by the Holy Spirit in the spiritual sanctuary of the New Testament Church. For first, as priests, there are the overseers, who are also called shepherds and teachers; and then also elders who labor in the word and doctrine, 1 Timothy 3:1, etc., 5:17. These may be compared to the Kohathites, so that Christ might take shape in souls, and thus the spiritual light and bread and the gift of prayer may be born and nurtured in hearts. Afterward, there are the deacons or servants, who should properly manage the office of catechists and school-servants: 1 Timothy 3:8, etc. These are comparable to the Gershonites, who were to prepare the "outer tent," as it were, through good discipline and useful instruction, so that later the inner things could be more fittingly placed therein through public preaching. And finally, there should be those appointed to the external necessity of temporal goods, for the maintenance of the outward service and the poor, following the example of the Apostles, as seen in Acts 6. These are comparable to the Merarites, who carried the pillars and boards as the support of the physical dwelling; in the same way, these must care for physical maintenance. These are now called by various names according to the different customs and ministries in the congregations. All must see to it that they serve the Lord in their entrusted office with all faithfulness and sincerity of heart. And there is no doubt that in the Church Above <note>The Heavenly Church</note>, things proceed just as orderly in the temple of God. Thus, as the upper is, so also the lower—in its shadow—is entirely uniform with it.

40. And the **LORD** said to Moses: Number all the firstborn of the males among the children of Israel, from a month old and upward, and take the number of their names.

41. And you shall take the Levites for me, **I am the LORD**, instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel; and the cattle of the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the cattle of the children of Israel.

42. And Moses numbered, as the Lord commanded him, all the firstborn among the children of Israel.

43. And all the firstborn males by the number of names, from a month old and upward, of those that were numbered of them, were twenty-two thousand two hundred and seventy-three.

44. And the **LORD** spoke to Moses, saying:

45. Take the Levites instead of all the firstborn among the children of Israel, and the cattle of the Levites instead of their cattle, that the Levites may be mine: **I am the LORD**.
