## The Fifth Chapter.

->The repetition of the Ten Commandments and the obligation to follow them.<-

And Moses called all Israel and said to them: Hear, O Israel, the statutes and the judgments which I speak in your ears today, and learn them, and keep them, so that you may act according to them.
2. The **LORD** our **God** made a covenant with us at Horeb.
3. The **LORD** did not make this covenant with our fathers, but with us, who are all here today and alive together.

---

v. 1. (To all Israel — Hear, O Israel). If we also wish to belong to the "Israel of God" and the spiritual seed of Abraham, we must truly have open ears for this discourse and take what is said to heart. For although the "shadow" <note>the ceremonial laws and rituals of the Old Testament</note> has passed away in Christ, the kernel and the essence of the entire Law given by Moses remains today just as it was yesterday. <note>original: "Matth. 5/ 17. Röm. 3/ 4." Referring to Matthew 5:17, where Jesus states he came not to abolish the Law but to fulfill it, and Romans 3:4 regarding God's faithfulness.</note>

v. 2, 3. (A covenant with us — not with our fathers). This covenant indicates the breadth of God's power and His glorious goodness. For although He had raised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to the greatest manifestations of grace—and that to such a high degree of perfection—and they themselves gave such faithful demonstrations of their faith and love; yet they did not have such an intimate covenant with God. This is the glory of our God, who cannot raise a creature so high that He is not able to reveal even more to others. He does not measure His special graces strictly according to human merit. For who was holier than these excellent Patriarchs? The Israelite people were not yet their equal by far. Ah, it happens so that His power may be further spread, for He takes pleasure in always showing even greater and more intimate kindnesses: and often more so to sinners than to the saints who have always stood in His righteousness.

However, there is another cause for such special graces and this precise covenant which God made with Moses, and not with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham. This cause is: because these tribal fathers and Patriarchs were called only to the "spiritual birth" <note>the beginning of the faith lineage</note>, but not to the "pastoral office" <note>the active leadership and governance of a people</note>. Thus, they did not require such an exact covenant, as they did not yet need such a detailed experience of the inner ways.

Otherwise, it should be noted that there are three kinds of souls: some to whom God gives many children, but at a distance, and who are still only in the sprouting of their seed; just as the Christians were enclosed in the blood of the martyrs. These are sanctified in God as much as possible, yet He has called them only to such a distant bringing-forth; He gives them a great number of children through His grace, of whom they have no personal knowledge, as only a few are known to them.

There are others who do not "give birth" in Jesus Christ <note>meaning they do not initiate the conversion of others</note>, but nonetheless hold the office of preachers, so that they help those already-formed souls whom God sends to them; to whom they then communicate the necessary light and knowledge regarding these matters, and instruct them in what they are told.

Finally, there is a third kind, who are chosen to give birth to other souls, to raise them, and to lead them to the most perfect state. God therefore makes them "universal apostles," who give birth, baptize, instruct, and provide bread and milk—and even medicines—according to the necessity of each soul; and who, just as Moses first did, lead the souls through the wilderness of faith and bring them into God.

<column-break/>

4. The **LORD** spoke with you face to face on the mountain from the midst of the fire.
5. I stood at that time between the **LORD** and you, to show you the word of the **LORD**. For you were afraid of the fire and did not go up the mountain; and He said:
6. I

---

<insert>
Thus, God makes a special and indeed the most intimate covenant with these people that has ever been, because they are called to the bringing-forth, upbringing, and leading to perfection. The "conception" happens when one departs from Egypt or from worldly muddle. The "upbringing" leads them into the wilderness of faith. And the "completion" causes them to enter into the Promised Land, which is their end.
</insert>

v. 4. For this reason, God unites Himself in a very precise way with these souls, more so than with others, so that He looks upon them face to face: that is, He unites them with Himself essentially, essence to essence, and draws them into the truth of His being, so that as they lead others, they may not be deceived.

But although God has made this essential union with them, He nevertheless allows the father and shepherd to pass through the very same path where he is to lead the others, so that he may be spared nothing: so that in the light of his experience, he may have no doubt nor wavering. For let a person be ever so enlightened—yes, let him stand in the divine light as much as he will—if he has not come through the path himself, he can never know in truth what it is. The reason for this is that one is easily deceived in the telling of things, and the tongue cannot express everything that the soul experiences. And so, the experience of another cannot make the soul understand, nor—when counsel is sought—enable it to see into the truth: because men are instructed, and God never permits them to fully reveal what they say; and all the less so because they do not even know themselves, especially in that highest state where their innermost self is very hidden from them, so they can say even less of it.

A person who has the same illness as another will understand it much better than one who has not yet experienced this illness and who only sees it from the outside; for the light of experience is something quite different from the light of sight. Just as those people who have endured the very same pains are much better able to give proven and helpful remedies; and through the description given to them, they can recognize the beginning, progress, and end, and finally the present state of those who wish to use their counsel.

v. 5. These very leaders also serve as guiding stars and mediators. As judges, to clearly judge everything according to the will of God: and as mediators to lead souls to their perfection.

<gloss>I)</gloss> Just as God rescued Moses from the danger of the water—which can be called a certain kind of shipwreck—so that he could be the leader of His people: so it often happens that God takes people whom He has pulled out of the abyss of sin, in order to make from them truly choice leaders of souls.

<summary>Moses begins his second sermon by reminding Israel of the unique, living covenant made at Horeb, acting as a mediator between the people and God's fire. The commentary interprets Moses as a prototype for spiritual leaders who must personally experience the "wilderness of faith" to effectively guide others to perfection.</summary>

v. 6. This is not found everywhere in the Catechisms alongside the Ten Commandments. "I do not know," reasoned a famous French theologian (a) <note>Referring to Jean d'Espagne (1591–1659), a prominent Protestant theologian.</note> about this, "what moved them to tear down the frontispiece of the Law of God. For—

1) If one wishes to be regarded as keeping all the words that God spoke when He publicly proclaimed this Law, why then does one scratch out the very first ones?
2) These are indeed the foundation of the entire Law, which show who the Legislator is, and by what right He has to command. Thus, they cannot be left out, unless one wishes to withdraw the principle upon which the Law of the Ten Commandments is built.
3) The understanding of the 1st Commandment is not whole or complete without these words that go before it, and upon which it entirely depends. These first words are the soul of this commandment and cannot be separated from it. There is also no right understanding if one begins the Ten Commandments without this preface. For the word *other* in the following verse presupposes that the Law has already spoken of a God who excludes the others. And therefore, one must express this first.
4) In addition to all these deficiencies, there is a far more peculiar one, namely an error in theology, by which all Christians are wronged. When God says: "I am the LORD your God," it is the same as if He said: "I am the LORD your Savior." In such a way God speaks with those to whom He offers salvation. These words are Evangelical <note>meaning they pertain to the Gospel or "Good News" of grace rather than just the demand of the Law</note>. God established the Gospel at the entrance of the Law. Why? If the Gospel did not speak first, the Law would drive us back and oppress us as people who stand under the curse. Therefore, those do not even know what they are doing who present the Ten Commandments without these first words, which grant us access and confidence in the Legislator's mercy.
Test everything, and keep that which is good.

v. 8. 9. 2) The making of images: 3) The showing of honor in two ways.
If now no image of any likeness of creatures is to be made, how much more is it something ungodly to form God in wood or stone, whose likeness no one has ever easily seen; or to place before the eyes and imagination of men paintings and images of God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, whereby thoughts are drawn down to bodily and sensory things, and a false concept of God is grasped, which does not agree with the truth that He is a Spirit.

Our God is jealous, and will suffer no other gods; no images or paramours <note>original: "Buler," meaning lovers or adulterous distractions from God</note> beside Him.

Origen (a) <note>Original Latin note refers to Origen's 8th Homily on Exodus, Chapter 20.</note>, who holds the view that God would be accused of injustice if one wished to understand this according to the letter, gives a graceful explanation according to the inner sense, which is not to be rejected, yet also must not exclude the outer understanding of the letter. He who sins and does the will of the devil is certainly of the father the devil, according to John 8:44, and his seed is in him, just as the seed of God is in him who does not sin: 1 John 3:9. In such a way now, the devil with his angels, who are to be viewed as fathers in the seduction and persuasion of man, are not punished in this world for such sins. Therefore he said there to Christ: "Have you come to torment us before the time?" But the children, who have allowed themselves to be seduced by him and be spiritually begotten, are visited, disciplined, and scourged.

Accordingly, it is still to be viewed as a grace and benefit, which does not happen to the devils, when God, for the sake of sins, allows His earnestness and zeal to be seen and felt in this time. How then can there be anything unjust on God's side in this? There is nothing unjust in God if He, for the evil children of ungodly parents

Who hate Him) for that is indeed what is spoken of, allows them to pay for their parents' iniquity: and what should be unjust in this, since no temporal punishment is so great that it does not deserve a thousandfold that which is more than worthy of eternal punishment; and no one may prescribe to God how He should punish those who hate Him? Also, no guilt is to be attributed to God if, through a disordered and improper procreation by conscientious parents, an infirmity or evil is born into children, which in such a case they have their parents to thank for: So there will be even less of anything unjust in God if He allows all this to happen for improvement, for reflection, and for the preservation and protection of man, if only one applies it to that purpose and allows it to bear fruit.

v. 10. Many thousands) Thus mercy exceeds judgment by many degrees.

Love me and keep my commandments) For that is fundamentally one and the same; 1 John 5:3. and the sum total of the commandment is love from a pure heart and from a good conscience and from <term>unfeigned faith</term> <note>original: "ungefarbtem Glauben," a sincere faith without hypocrisy</note>. 1 Tim. 1:5. And

The main purpose and the main sum of God's entire mind in His Law is this: Since God wished to make man subject to His Law, He first shows him the graces He has given him: So that this Law might not seem difficult to him; and that he might grasp a living confidence that this so kind God, who had rescued him from the house of bondage, would not place him under the yoke anew: but that He, on the contrary, would grant His grace and the necessary strength to keep His commands; just as He clearly promises elsewhere (b). "I will," He says, "send my Spirit into your midst, and will make you walk in my commandments, and keep my laws, so that you may do good works." Indeed, even so much that He Himself would work His Law in us who would let Him work without resistance.

For this reason also comes His first commandment, to have no other gods beside Him. Which means as much as: that one should not, in order to keep His Law, rely on any foreign power, but solely on His own: because He is both a strong God, who can do all things through His power, and a jealous God: who does not want anyone to imagine that He wants to share this power with him; nor that one should ascribe the keeping of His commandments to any other power than His own, nor to any other
<sig>Tttt 2</sig>
loyalty, nor violence, nor art.

The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter V.

### The Fifth Chapter.

->Repetition of the ten commandments and the bond associated with them.<-

And Moses called all Israel, and said unto them: Hear, O Israel, the statutes and judgments which I speak in your ears this day, that ye may learn them, and keep, and do them.
2. The Lord our God made a covenant with us in Horeb.
3. The Lord made not this covenant with our fathers, but with us, even us, who are all of us here alive this day.

<margin>
v. 1. All Israel — Hear, O Israel) If we wish to belong to the Israel of God and the spiritual seed of Abraham, we must truly have open ears for this discourse and take it to heart. For although the shadow <note>original: "Schatten" — referring to the Old Testament ceremonial laws</note> has passed away in Christ, the core and the essence of the entire law given by Moses remains today as much as yesterday. Matthew 5:17. Romans 3:4.
</margin>

<margin>
v. 2. 3. A covenant with us — not with our fathers) This covenant demonstrates the vastness of God's power and His glorious goodness. For although He had raised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob to the highest manifestations of grace, and to such a high state of perfection—and they themselves gave such faithful evidence of their faith and love—they nonetheless did not have such a close covenant with God. This is the glory of our God, who cannot raise a creature so high that He could not reveal even more to others. He does not measure His special graces strictly according to a person's worthiness. For who was holier than these excellent Patriarchs? The Israelite people were not nearly their equals. Ah, it happens so that His power may be spread abroad all the more, that He takes pleasure at all times in showing even greater and more intimate kindnesses: and this indeed often more to sinners than to saints who have always stood in His righteousness.
</margin>

But there is yet another reason for such special graces and this very precise covenant which God made with Moses, and not with Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham. This reason is that these Forefathers and Patriarchs were called only to spiritual birth, but not to the Office of the Shepherd <note>the pastoral or leadership role</note>: thus they did not require such a precise covenant, as they also did not need such a precise experience of the inner requirements of the path.

Otherwise, it should be noted that there are three kinds of souls: some to whom God gives many children, but at a distance, and who only stand in the sprouting of their seed; just as the Christians were enclosed in the blood of the martyrs. These are sanctified in God as much as possible: those whom He has called only to such a distant bringing-forth, and to whom He indeed gives a great multitude of children through His grace, of whom they have no personal knowledge, as only a few are known to them.

There are others who do not give birth in Jesus Christ, but nevertheless observe the office of preachers, so that they help those already-formed souls whom God sends to them; to whom they then communicate the necessary light and knowledge for this matter, and instruct them in what must be said to them.

Finally, there is a third kind, who are chosen to give birth to other souls, to raise them, and to bring them to the most perfect state; whom God therefore makes general Apostles, who give birth, baptize, instruct, and give bread and milk, as well as medicines, according to the necessity of each soul; and who, just as Moses first did, lead the souls through the wilderness of faith and bring them into God.

<column-break/>

4. The Lord talked with you face to face in the mount out of the midst of the fire.
5. I stood between the Lord and you at that time, to show you the word of the Lord: for ye were afraid by reason of the fire, and went not up into the mount; and he said:
6.

<insert>
Thus God makes a special and indeed the most intimate covenant with these people that has ever been held, because they are called to the bringing-forth, upbringing, and leading to perfection. The procreation happens when one steps out of Egypt or out of the confusion. The upbringing leads them into the wilderness of faith: And the completion makes them enter into the Promised Land, which is their end.
</insert>

<margin>
v. 4. Therefore God unites Himself in a very great way with these souls, more than usually with others, so that they behold Him face to face: that is; He unites them with Himself essentially, from essence to essence, and at the same time takes them into the truth of His being, so that they, in leading others, may not be deceived.
</margin>

But although God has made this essential union with them, He nonetheless lets the father and shepherd go through that very same path where he is to lead the others—to spare him somewhat—so that he may have no doubt or wavering in the light of experience. For even if a person were so enlightened and stood in the divine light as much as he wished, if he has not come through the path himself, he can never know in truth what it is. The reason for this is that one is deceived by the mere narration of things, and that the tongue cannot express everything that the soul experiences. And so too, the experience of another cannot make the soul understand, nor—when counsel is sought—put it into the truth: because people are different, and God also never permits them to reveal all that they are capable of knowing; and all the less so, as they do not even know themselves, especially in that high state in which their innermost being is very hidden from them, so they can say all the less about it.

A person who has the same illness as another will understand it much better than someone who has not yet experienced this illness, and who only sees such an illness from the outside: since in experience there is something much different than the light of the spirit. Just as also such people who have endured the very same pains are much sooner in the position to give protective and healing remedies for it, and can recognize a description given to them of its beginning, progress, and end—and finally the present state of those who wish to use their counsel.

<margin>
v. 5. These same leaders also serve as arbitrators and as mediators. As arbitrators, to judge clearly what the will of God is: and as mediators, to lead the souls to their perfection.
</margin>

(I) Just as God rescued Moses from the power of the water, which could have become a certain kind of shipwreck, so that he could be the leader of His people: so it likewise often happens that God takes people whom He has drawn out of the abyss of sin, to make from them truly select leaders of souls.

<margin>v. 6. This [preface] is not found everywhere alongside the Ten Commandments in the Catechisms. "I do not know," reasons a famous French theologian (a) about this, "what moved them to tear down the front facade of the Law of God." For:</margin>
<margin>(a) Jean d'Espagne <note>A 17th-century French Protestant theologian known for his works on the Decalogue.</note></margin>

" 1) If one wishes to be regarded as keeping all the words that God spoke when He publicly proclaimed this Law, why then does one scratch out the very first ones?
" 2) These words are indeed the foundation of the entire Law, showing who this Legislator is and by what right He has to command. Thus, they cannot be omitted unless one wishes to withdraw the fundamental principle upon which the Law of the Ten Commandments is built.
" 3) The meaning of the 1st Commandment is not whole or complete without these words that go before it and upon which it entirely depends. These first words are the soul of this commandment and cannot be separated from it. There is also no correct understanding if one begins the Ten Commandments without this preface. For the word *other* in the following verse assumes as a basis that the Law has already spoken of a God who excludes the others. Therefore, one must express this first.
" 4) Beside all these deficiencies, there is an even stranger one, namely a theological error by which all Christians are wronged. When God says: "I am the Lord your God," it is as much as if He said: "I am the Lord your Savior." In this manner, God speaks to those to whom He indicates salvation. These words are Evangelical <note>Meaning they belong to the "Gospel" or "Good News" of grace rather than the "Law" of demands.</note>. God has fastened the Gospel to the entrance of the Law. Why? If the Gospel did not speak first, the Law would drive us back and oppress us as people who are under the curse.
" Therefore, those who present the Ten Commandments without these first words—which provide us access to and confidence in the Legislator's mercy—do not even know what they are doing.
->Test everything, and retain that which is good.<-
v. 7. None) It is noteworthy that four negations occur here regarding this matter, and thus just as many types of actions in the veneration or service of God are forbidden. 1) Through the "having" of other gods, primarily the internal foundation is addressed:
v. 8. 9. 2) The making of images: 3) the showing of honor of two kinds.
Now, if no image of any form of the creatures is to be made, it is even more ungodly to fashion God in wood or stone—whose form no one has easily seen—or to place before the eyes and imagination of men paintings and images of God the Father, Son, and Holy Spirit, whereby thoughts are pulled down to physical and sensory things and conceive a false notion of God that does not agree with the truth that He is a Spirit.

**10. And showing mercy unto many thousands; namely to those who love me and keep my commandments.**

<margin>v. 9. I the Lord your God am a jealous God) Our God is jealous <note>original: "jaloux"</note> and will suffer no other gods, no images, and no paramours beside Himself.</margin>
<margin>Visiting iniquity) Through all kinds of harsh means, rods, and blows, to make it loathsome to them. But why</margin>
<margin>Upon the children) and not upon the fathers themselves? Or, if also upon them, why not upon the fathers alone who have sinned?</margin>

Origen (a), who is of the opinion that God would be accused of injustice if one were to understand this according to the letter, gives a neat explanation according to the inner sense, which should not be rejected, yet also must not exclude the outer understanding of the letter. Whoever sins and does the will of the devil is certainly of the father the devil, according to John 8:44, and his seed is in him, just as the seed of God is in him who does not sin, 1 John 3:9. In this manner, then, the devil with his angels—who are to be regarded as fathers in the seduction and persuasion of man—is not punished in this world for such sins. Therefore he said there to Christ: "Have you come to torment us before the time?" But the children, who have allowed themselves to be seduced by him and be spiritually begotten, are visited, disciplined, and scourged.
Therefore, it is still to be regarded as a grace and a benefit—which does not happen to the devils—when God allows His earnestness and zeal to be seen and felt in this time for the sake of sins. And how then can there be anything unjust on God's side in this? There is nothing unjust in God if He lets the wicked children of godless parents
Who hate Him) for that is indeed what is being discussed, pay for the misdeeds of their parents: and what should be unjust in this, since no temporal punishment is so great that it does not deserve a thousandfold that which is more than worthy of eternal punishment; and God may not be prescribed by anyone how He is to punish those who hate Him? Also, no guilt is to be attributed to God if, through a disordered and improper way of procreation by unscrupulous parents, an infirmity or evil is born into children, which in such a case they have their parents to thank for: So there will be even less of anything unjust in God if He allows all this to happen and occur for the improvement, for the reflection, and for the preservation of every person, provided one only applies it to that end and lets it work upon oneself.
v. 10. Many thousands) Thus mercy exceeds judgment by many degrees.
Love me and keep my commandments) For that is fundamentally one and the same; 1 John 5:3. And the main sum of the commandment is love from a pure heart and from a good conscience and from unfeigned faith. 1 Timothy 1:5. And
The main purpose and the main sum of God's entire meaning in His Law is this: After God wished to make man subject to His Law, He first indicates to him the graces He has given him: so that this Law might not seem difficult to him; and that he could take a living confidence that this so-kind God, who had rescued him from the house of bondage, would not put him under the yoke anew: but that He, on the contrary, would bestow His grace and the necessary strengths to keep His commands; just as He clearly promises it elsewhere (b). I will, He says, send my Spirit into your midst, and will make you walk in my commandments and keep my laws, so that you may do good works. Yes, even so much so that He Himself wishes to fulfill His Law in those who yield themselves entirely to Him and would let Him work in them without resistance.
From this cause also stems His first commandment, to have no other gods beside Him. Which means as much as: that one should, in order to keep His Law, rely on no foreign power, but solely on His own: because He is both a strong God, who can do all through His power, and also a jealous God: who does not want anyone to imagine that He would share this power with another; nor that one should ascribe the keeping of His commandments to any other power than His own, nor to any other faithfulness, nor violence, nor art.

<header>The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter V.</header>

### 11. You shall not take the name of the Lord your God in vain! For the Lord will not leave him unpunished who takes His name in vain.

### 12. Observe the Sabbath day, to keep it holy, as the Lord your God has commanded you.

### 13. Six days you shall labor and do all your work:

v. 11. Just as the name of God is taken in vain in many ways, both coarse and subtle, there is perhaps no way more common—indeed, almost universal—than when the godless world thinks and speaks of God's mercy as if God had no justice or holiness, and therefore sins recklessly against Him. It is also taken in vain when one lives and walks in a way that seems to deny one or all of God's virtues, especially His omniscience, omnipresence, holiness, and justice; and also when one misuses God's Word, which speaks of God and His virtues and makes them known. And

How dissolutely do all hypocritical people handle God's name, and what a poor opinion they must have of it, when it must serve all their base intentions—a small bit of property, a little honor, or lust! Must not God and His name be a cover for almost all sins and vices for them? Whatever a hypocrite does, no matter how evil, he spreads God's name over it to maintain it as just and fair. But God will certainly not <gloss>leave such a person unpunished</gloss> <note>original: "Ungeſtraft laſſen"; the author notes this can also mean to not "cleanse" or "clear" the person of guilt.</note>.

How then could outward works or the performance of due duties and obligations, in which the name of God is invoked, cleanse a person from his sin? These are certainly far too powerless.

It is, moreover, worth the effort to examine ourselves to see what kind of name each of us carries: whether it is the name of your God and His Christ, or another; and if it is God's name, whether it is carried in earnestness and purity, or in vain and falsely.

v. 12. It is wonderful how the Sabbath, which should signify nothing other than rest to us, has been able to become a stone of stumbling and a rock of offense: so much so that restless men have made a restless workday out of this day of rest, and have conducted a long, bitter dispute—for which many a ready pen has been sharpened—over the question: whether one is obligated to observe a certain 7th day in the days of the New Testament by virtue of this commandment? Why do we always dig so much into the images and external ceremonies, and not rather press through the shadows to the true body, which is God in Christ Jesus? Why should one Sabbath not begin where the other ends?

v. 13. When we have rested for one day, shall we then sail across the wide, restless sea of this world for the following six days? Do we think that we would not be so blessed if we had the whole world as a temple, all time as a Sabbath, all creatures as our lessons, and God Himself as our teacher?

<margin>(a) Homily 35.</margin>
> "In the shadow of the law," writes Saint Macarius (a) <note>Macarius of Egypt (c. 300–391), a monk and teacher known for spiritual homilies.</note>, "which was given through Moses, God commanded that everyone should rest on the Sabbath and do no work. This, however, was a prototype and shadow of the true Sabbath which the Lord grants to a soul. For the soul which is deemed worthy to be free from shameful and impure thoughts keeps its true Sabbath and rests in the true rest, having become still and free from all works of darkness. For although they then rested bodily according to the prototype of the Sabbath, their souls were yet bound to wickedness. This true Sabbath, however, is the true rest of the soul, which is still and purified from the thoughts of Satan."

<column-break/>

### 14. But the seventh day is a Sabbath to the Lord your God: in it you shall do no work, neither you, nor your son, nor your daughter, nor your male servant, nor your female servant, nor your ox, nor your donkey, nor any of your livestock, nor your stranger who is within your gates; that your male servant and your female servant may rest as well as you.

### 15. And you shall remember that you were a slave in the land of Egypt, and the Lord your God brought you out from there with a mighty hand and with an outstretched arm. Therefore the Lord your God commanded you to keep the Sabbath day.

### 16. Honor your father and your mother, as the Lord your God has commanded you, that your days may be long, and that it may go well with you in the land which the Lord your God is giving you.

> v. 14. "Just as He then commanded that even the irrational animals must rest on the Sabbath, so that an ox would not be pulled under the yoke and the donkey would carry no burden: likewise, when the Lord comes, He makes those called the 'souls in the gate'—or residents of the land or house—rest from the burdens of sin and impure thoughts."

The stranger within your gates: These were those who simply renounced idolatry and accepted the 7 Laws of Noah <note>The Noachide Laws: a set of moral imperatives traditionally viewed as binding on all humanity.</note>, but were not circumcised. These were called 'Strangers in the Gate,' or residents of the land or house, because as such they were permitted to dwell among the children of Israel in Canaan.

<margin>(a) Selden, *On Natural Law and the Law of Nations*, book 3, chapters 10, pages 4, 5, 8, 11, 12.</margin>
These were then not to be kept at work by the Israelites as servants on the Sabbath, though otherwise, they could and had to work for their own benefit on the Sabbath day, because the Israelite laws did not concern them. (a)

v. 15. The soul was sold into slavery under harsh masters, and the Lord relieved it of the unbearable burdens of its vain and impure thoughts, took away the heavy yoke of the works of unrighteousness, and set it free after it had worked itself weary in the thoughts of vanity. Therefore, it should observe and preserve this rest as a holy Sabbath: whereas, by contrast, the connection to the Exodus from Egyptian bondage has no place among believers, because the figurative unrest of the Exodus from Egyptian bondage mentioned here also finds no place.

Since meanwhile the labor of service for repentance (Genesis 3:17, 19) and Egyptian bondage still continue in the kingdoms of the world, the body should also praise God with its rest, and such rest should be granted to subjects and servants and not be infringed upon.

v. 16. Honor your father and mother, in order that (which is to say, in what manner): According to the spirit, this is as much as saying: Follow your Eternal Wisdom, or His Spirit and Word, which you should not resist but obey, for your well-being and true life.

## 17. You shall not kill.
## 18. And you shall not commit adultery.
## 19. And you shall not steal.
## 20. And you shall not bear false witness against your neighbor.
<margin>Ps. 15:3.</margin>
## 21. And you shall not covet (a) your neighbor's wife / and you shall not desire your neighbor's house / his field, nor his manservant, nor his maidservant / his ox, nor his donkey / nor anything that is your neighbor's. <margin>(a) Rom. 7:7.</margin>

---

<margin>v. 17</margin> **You shall not kill)** or rather, murder. For since this prohibition does not mean a judicial act, nor what happens by accident, <margin>Deut. 19:4, 5.</margin> nor when an animal is slaughtered for the sustenance of man—all of which are types of killing—but rather a premeditated malice of the will; therefore, such is best distinguished from the former by the word "murder." <note>The author distinguishes between the general German verb *töten* (to kill) and *morden* (to murder), arguing that the commandment specifically targets the internal "malice of the will" rather than legal execution or accidental death.</note>

Since we are now in this fifth book of Moses, following the purpose of the preface, to consider these matters more according to the spirit, the question arises here:

What is spiritual murder? Answer: It is committed (1) against your own soul, Prov. 6:32, 29:24. <margin>Job 5:2.</margin> (2) against your neighbor, Matt. 5:21, 22; 1 John 3:15. (3) against GOD or the divine nature and the Lord Christ. Rev. 13:8; 1 Cor. 15:3; Hebr. 6:6. And according to this, so much is said herewith:

You shall not hinder, quench, or suppress God's image and Spirit in yourself or others through sins, evil examples, mockery, or persecution, etc.

<margin>v. 18. &c.</margin> **And — And — And — And)** Just as various books of Scripture are linked together at their beginnings by conjunctions—as the first four books of Moses are linked together, the book of Joshua with the fifth book of Moses, the book of Judges with Joshua, the little book of Ruth with the former, and with this the books of Samuel, etc.—so also here different commandments are linked together and united as members. From this it follows that if one of them is broken, the entire will and law of GOD is broken and desecrated, and the authority of the lawgiver is despised. James 2:10, 11.

Consider this well, whoever you are, and therefore conscientiously observe all and every commandment of GOD, and guard yourself with all diligence that you break or transgress none of them!

<margin>v. 19.</margin> **You shall not steal)** GOD is a Lord of all things. To Him belongs your heart, affections, life, time, children, husband, wife, limbs, goods, etc. Everything is to be employed for no other reason than for His sake and for His honor and service. Mark well what stealing is!

<margin>v. 21.</margin> **The commandment regarding lust** <note>In this context, "lust" (Lust) refers to the internal "coveting" or "desire" mentioned in the tenth commandment.</note> reaches the very deepest and shows most clearly that the law is spiritual: which we know from Paul, even if we otherwise could not or would not recognize it, who therefore makes the conclusion in Romans 7:7–14. Therefore, we should all the more search for and pay attention to the spiritual understanding of the law. So that the same may be better grasped by us, we shall summarize it briefly.

<column-break/>

## 22. These words the Lord spoke to your whole assembly on the mountain, out of the midst of the fire, the clouds, and the darkness (a), with a great voice, and He added nothing more, and He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me. <margin>(a) Hebr. 12:18.</margin>
## 23. And it happened, when you heard the voice out of the midst of the darkness, while the mountain burned with fire, that you came near to me, all the heads of your tribes and your elders;
## 24. And you said: Behold, the Lord our GOD has shown us His glory and His majesty, and we have heard His voice out of the midst of the fire! This day we have seen that GOD speaks with man, and he remains alive.
## 25. And

---

<margin>v. 22.</margin> **These words)** therefore require of us, in the secret sense of GOD:

I) That we should love nothing but Him alone, and everything else only for His sake.

II) That we should not think that GOD is like the thoughts and imaginations that our reason and our darkened understanding make of Him.

III) That we should not boast of His name, covenant, knowledge, grace, and sonship in vain, if we do not wish to put such things to right use and bear appropriate fruits.

IV) That we should cease to work, act, and live according to our own will; so that GOD may work, act, and live in and through us.

V) That we should honor the word, the will, and the good inspirations of GOD: because He wishes to spiritually regenerate us thereby and make new creatures out of us: so that we may live a long time on earth, or in the world that He wishes to give us—that is, that we may enjoy eternal life.

VI) That we should not kill the divine image within us, nor rob our souls of spiritual life through sin, nor kill the soul of our neighbor through a heathenish, worldly, and evil life.

VII) That we should not make use of or employ any creature out of mere lust, without the will of GOD: because such is an adultery of the heart.

VIII) That we should not rob GOD, to whom everything already belongs, of our goods, love, time, labor, and our life, by not applying them for Him alone.

IX) That we should judge no one from ourselves and without divine light: because otherwise, since we are stuck in darkness and blindness, we would judge falsely.

X) That we should be content with what we have and desire no more: because all other desire, as a form of lust, is forbidden.

<margin>v. 23. 24.</margin> When souls find themselves on the passive path of enlightenment, <note>The "passive path" (leidender Weg) is a term from mystical theology referring to a stage where the soul stops trying to reach God through its own efforts and instead suffers or "undergoes" the transformative work of God's light.</note> GOD shows them His glory, indeed even speaks to them, and they understand His voice from the midst of the inward fire which ignites them. All this, however, is worked such that life is still left to them. They have seen and heard all this; and yet they still live: because these states do not require death. For these are graces that are proportioned to their capacity. But as soon as they have reached this point, they believe they have already traversed all internal states; and because they possess a living light and a great happiness, they imagine that they are already through all the states of death of which they were told, or that such things are only their own imaginations; indeed, they even become offended by this and think they have already arrived in GOD, without having come through the terrible wildernesses and through the very outermost trials that were mentioned to them. Oh, how terribly they deceive themselves, and what a great difference there is between those communications which spare life, and those which work death! <note>The author warns that initial spiritual "highs" or illuminations are not the final goal; the "death" of the old self is a much more rigorous process that follows these initial graces.</note>

# The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter V.

25. And now why should we die, so that this great fire consumes us? If we continue to hear the voice of the LORD our GOD any longer, then we shall surely die!

26. For what is all flesh, that it might hear the voice of the living GOD speaking out of the midst of the fire, as we have, and remain alive?

27. Go near, and hear all that the LORD our GOD shall say; and speak you to us all that the LORD our GOD shall speak to you: so we will hear and do it.

The first word of GOD, and the communications which accompany it, are graces that work within the powers <note>The "powers" (*Kräffte*) refers to the faculties of the soul, such as reason and will, in the language of 18th-century German mysticism.</note>, maintaining the fire of love in the will, and imparting a greater life rather than the stroke of death. The second word, however, is heard in the very center <note>original: *Mittelpunct*</note>, and it causes death. For this Word is the <insert>(a)</insert> voice of one crying in the wilderness: Prepare the way of the LORD, and make his paths straight! because GOD himself wishes to come; no longer through his gifts, but through himself; and he wishes to come not into the powers, but into the center, through an essential union. This Word now, which is to precede such a great state, must be a word of death, so that it truly brings about the dying away <note>The term *Absterben* (dying away/mortification) is a technical term in Pietism referring to the process of the ego or "old man" dying so that the soul can be reborn in God.</note> of the soul from itself: Just as the body must necessarily die if it is to enter heaven—indeed, it must even rot in order to rise again on the last day—likewise the soul must die to all things in order to come into heaven, which is GOD himself.

When love has once reached a high degree, and its ignition has become very great, then the soul must die through the consumption of this fire itself: for it is no longer a moderate fire which cannot consume nor turn to ashes as before; but it has then increased so much that it must consume everything, without anything being able to escape it. One can no longer resist it; one must die: and when GOD speaks with this second, so burning voice, which does not only melt the soul (as the Bride <insert>(b)</insert> once felt), but kills and annihilates it, then the soul must perish through its burning. The prototype of this is clear enough where St. Peter says <insert>(c)</insert> that at the end of the world all elements shall melt through the heat of fire, and that the earth and all its works shall be burned: because this fire must necessarily prepare man for the complete day of eternity.

The day of time is seen and felt as soon as the newborn child has opened its eyes, even if it must grow in years before it can grasp such daylight. Thus, as soon as a soul is reborn to grace, it enjoys the beauty of such grace as soon as its eyes are merely opened: But it cannot distinguish this light of grace until it has progressed within it. This is all the temporal day, which requires neither death nor the consumption of fire. But to enter into the eternal day, which is GOD himself, it is necessary that the fire consume everything: either here on earth, or after death. And this is essentially and irreputably so. Because if GOD is to give himself, and one is to enter into him, one must possess a purely divine purity—taken from within him—which consumes and nullifies everything impure, self-centered, or limited found in the creature, which hinders the pure-divine living within it from flowing out into GOD: Which St. Paul <insert>(d)</insert> calls a swallowing up of all that is mortal within us by life. So that this created good—let it be as highly exalted as it will—does not cause death, but rather GOD himself, as the author of such grace. The eternal day, the light of glory, the source and essence of life, must necessarily bring death before it can bring the soul into its eternal day, which is he himself.

<column-break/>

28. But when the LORD heard the voice of your words when you spoke to me, the LORD said to me: I have heard the voice of the words of this people, which they have spoken to you: They have done well in all that they have spoken.

29. Oh, that they had such a heart to fear me, and to keep all my commandments all the days; that it might go well with them and their children for eternity!

30. Go and say to them: Return to your huts.

31. But you, stand here by me, and I will speak to you all the commandments and the statutes and the laws which you shall teach them; that they may keep them in the land that I give them to possess as an inheritance. <margin>Deuteronomy 6:1.</margin>

32. So<unclear>...</unclear>

---

v. 28. **The voice of words)** is mentioned here a second time by the LORD with great significance, whereby the all-seeing eye of Wisdom—searching to the very depths—perceived an honest and serious intent of the heart and will. It was only a voice, a sound, a mere tone. Just as it happens, for example, with most Christians when they speak of improvement as penitents in confessionals, or otherwise try to satisfy GOD with words in their morning and evening prayers, table graces, and the like: It is only a voice of words, quite neatly composed according to a certain form, of which the heart knows little or nothing.

**They have spoken well)** To have *done* as they *spoke* would have been better. The tongue promises much, but the heart does not desire to do it.

v. 29. **Oh, that they had such a heart)** GOD does not look so much at man's outward confession, or at what they promise with the mouth; but rather at the shape and condition of their hearts and the entire ground of the soul <note>The *Seelen-Grund* is a mystical concept referring to the deepest, most essential part of the human spirit where God dwells.</note>. And therefore we must not be satisfied or have enough with offering the Lord JESUS a little devotion, or a prayer and song, or an outward church-going; but we must sacrifice and surrender to him our heart and the innermost ground of the will.

v. 30. **Return to your huts)** Because it is not necessary that they remain standing here assembled until all the remaining laws are also given.

v. 31. **But you, stand here — so I will speak to you)** Namely, there is another time, besides the one mentioned above, in which one can hear the voice of GOD without dying: and this is when one has already died. Just as the blessed in heaven will behold GOD, although they can no longer die: since they have risen again and are not to die again, being made like the angels. Therefore Moses could speak with GOD, and receive his words, and remain constantly with him; because he had, in a mystical way, died and risen again.

The Lord our God is an altogether excellent Lawgiver. He has given commandments, and he is still commanding them. Other lawgivers, once they have published their laws, leave them to the people to observe at their own peril. The Lord our God does not do so. He has given laws and commandments, and he is still always giving them. When the carpenter has built a house, he no longer cares for it. When a ship-builder has built a ship, it no longer concerns him afterward whether it sinks or swims. When the gardener has planted a vineyard, he leaves it to the weather and the ordinary providence of God. But when our most gracious God has done something of the kind in a spiritual way, he has nevertheless not done it in such a way that he would not still be always doing it.

From this appears the great goodness, love, and care of our God toward his people. He is at all times instructing, teaching, admonishing, punishing, improving, disciplining, comforting, encouraging, warning, and performing everything else of a fatherly lawgiver and teacher, as one who is such yesterday, today, and forever.

# 4. Hear, Israel / the **LORD** our **God** is one **LORD**.
<margin>1 Corinthians 8:4.</margin>

With this, the unity of **God** is impressed upon **Israel** / that there is only one divine Being / who is one in understanding and will / even though the traces of the three witnesses in the one Being itself are found here in the three divine names / **LORD** / **God** / **LORD** / and otherwise in the blessing <margin>Numbers 6:24, 25, 26.</margin> where the notes should be consulted / and in other places of the Old Testament / they are sufficiently to be found; and such was afterwards clearly revealed in the New Testament. <margin>Matthew 28:19. 1 John 5:7.</margin>

And so there is also one world that was created in time / and is harmoniously governed by the One and Triune **God** / and had to be redeemed only once by the one Son of **God** / and so for all eternity will be maintained and governed in harmony for His praise by the one **Lord** and **God**.

For this reason, the one and most excellent commandment is added here / as the source both of the other excellent commandment of love for one's neighbor / as well as all remaining commandments of the duties of love / toward **God** / ourselves and our neighbor / how man should behave toward his sole Origin and Sustainer: namely, that he should surrender himself to Him with spirit / which is understood by the heart / soul and body / according to all its capacity and strength. <margin>Matthew 22:37. Mark 12:29.</margin>

**Hear Israel)** It is surprising / that the Jews / who otherwise do not misuse their holy things with speech as Christians do / yet / just as Christians through a shameful misuse call the name of **Jesus** in vain / in sudden terror or wonder / through similar misuse / especially the women / immediately have the words **Shema Yisrael** <note>original: "Schemo Jisroel"</note> in their mouths / and have become so accustomed to this / that even the otherwise cautious secret Jews in Spain and Portugal have incautiously let these words slip (a) / and were thereby recognized as Jews / and dragged away to the punishment of fire.

Otherwise, they also want to drive away the "alp" <note>A folkloric supernatural creature, similar to a succubus or incubus, thought to cause nightmares or sleep paralysis.</note> or the night-pressure and ghosts with these words / and otherwise perform many superstitious things with them.

->**The LORD)** The Father.<-
->**Our God)** The Son / Immanuel / **God** with us.<-
->**The LORD)** The Spirit. <margin>2 Corinthians 3:17.</margin><-
->**One single LORD)** But a threefold expression / gradual revelation / degree or manner of being in the Godhead. And<-

Should not the main verse of the New Testament concerning the Holy Trinity, 1 John 5:7, be taken from these words? John says 3; Moses shows and counts these 3 for us; the **LORD** / our **God** / the **LORD**. John says / they are one; Moses speaks **Echad** <note>Hebrew: אחד</note> / one. For among the Hebrews both the masculine and the feminine are used instead of the neuter gender, which they do not have. John says; these 3 bear witness. In all Hebrew Bibles the last letter of the first word **Shema** <note>Hebrew: שמע</note> and the last of the last word **Echad** <note>Hebrew: אחד</note> are written large. Now the Jews say / as can be found in the margin of the great Buxtorf Bible: Put these 2 large letters **Ayin** <note>Hebrew: ע</note> and **Dalet** <note>Hebrew: ד</note> together / and the word **Ed** <note>Hebrew: עד</note> Witness comes out.

Although this verse is more a confession of faith than a prayer / it is nevertheless used by the Jews in all needs and cases as a prayer / and called the **Shema** <note>original: "Schemoh"</note>.

The Jews can also, in reading this verse, draw out the last word **Echad** <note>One</note> for a half or even a whole hour with singing: they also turn their head toward the 4 parts of the world at the last letter **Dalet** / which indicates the number 4.

Namely, a general duty and obligation is required here from all nations and peoples / who inhabit the 4 parts of the world. The capital letter on the word "Hear" is a numeral-letter / and signifies the 70 nations / which are indicated in chapter 32:8 / and may be counted up in Genesis 10. Thereupon follows this general duty of all 70 nations / who inhabit the 4 parts of the world.

<margin>(a) Christoph Arnold, notes on Wagenseil's *Sota*, page 1195.</margin>

<column-break/>

# 5. And you shall love the **LORD** your **God** with all your heart and with all your soul and with all your might.
<margin>6. L.</margin>

Thus, our whole spirit together with soul and body must be surrendered to **God** in heartfelt love. The understanding must have its highest delight in the knowledge of **God** and His mysteries. The will must only desire what is **God's** will. And the body's business must be directed toward the glory of **God**. <margin>Colossians 3:17.</margin>

**With all your heart -- soul and all your might)** With your whole judgment / will and conscience; likewise / with your most tender affection / desire / pleasure and joy: as also with all bodily members and other goods.

**God** / who created the whole human being / also requires the whole human being in His love. He must be loved wholly and sincerely / so that our heart inclines with love to no thing except only to **God** / nor delights itself in anything except in Him. For whoever loves something alongside or before **God** / and yet not for **God's** sake; he already loves Him less than he should (a).

If we hold back a part of our heart / soul / mind or powers / and do not love **God** with it / then we love it more than our **God** / and value our **God** less than that same thing / whatever it may be.

Therefore, the requirement to love **God** with all one's heart / means this much: that one should allow no single desire / whether one's own or another's / to find room in oneself except for Him alone and in Him / let it be as holy and highly exalted as it may. As long as one does not love **God** above utility / let it be as great as it may / or virtue / or salvation / or eternity; it is certain / that one does not love Him with all one's heart: because then one can still love more. And who would doubt / that he should not love more generously / who loves without expecting any utility / than when one seeks one's own utility in loving. The natural light testifies / which all people <unclear>possess</unclear> / who certainly hold that they would be loved much more / the less the one who loves them enjoys a utility from it / and thus find / that he loves them out of pure benevolence. Thus he / who loves **God** for the sake of utility / does not love Him with all his heart / even if he loves Him from the heart; because he loves his own utility alongside **God**.

Each one who loves his soul alongside **God** / and fears to lose it / who would gladly see it adorned with divine gifts and enriched in great virtues out of care and self-love: that same person does not love **God** with all his soul: because he so gladly wants to keep his soul in his divine love / and pushes down something of the love-owed-to-**God** onto it.

He who excludes anything / and does not lose everything for his **God's** sake; he does not love Him with all his might: because he would love Him even more strongly / if he abandoned himself to His leading without the slightest exception. He who says "with all your might" / has the highest love / which fills the whole space of the soul: and one must not think / it is enough / to offer **God** only a pure sacrifice of his temporal life and powers / when one should also offer up his eternal life and eternal powers with it.

O commandment of pure perfect love! one can hardly find you kept according to all your right under heaven! Yet you must be kept by us in your full perfection / if we want to come into heaven. This complete keeping is also commonly found only at the door of heaven / after such a complete purification of the soul has first / either in this life or in that one / allowed it to be born: And as soon as such keeping allows itself to be found in its complete perfection after this life / then the entrance into Paradise must be opened to them. For then nothing can stop a soul / which sees in its purity / from pouring itself out eternally into **God** / who is now truly its **God** and its All / since He has become entirely its love.

<margin>(a) Idiota <note>A pen name for the 14th-century mystic Raymundus Jordanus.</note> in *Contemplations*, chapter 12.</margin>

# Chapter VI. The Fifth Book of Moses [Deuteronomy]. 709

### 6. And these words / which I command you today / shall be in your heart:
<margin>chapter 11:18. Jeremiah 31:33.</margin>

### 7. And you shall instill <note>German: *einschärffen*, literally "to sharpen into" or inculcate</note> them into your children (a) and speak of them / when you sit in your house and when you walk on the road / and when you lie down and when you rise up:
<margin>(a) Genesis 18:19. Psalm 78:2 and following. Tobit 4. Ephesians 6:4.</margin>

This commandment should be written in the heart / so that the hand would observe it in its actions; it would be the right ornament and forehead-jewelry of man / with which they were accustomed to adorn themselves; and it would be the blessing in their houses and in their cities / and thus just as much / as if it were bound on the hand / hung on the head and neck / and written on the posts of the doors and gates. Job 31:35, 36. Song of Solomon 8:6. Proverbs 3:3, 6:21, 7:3. Which the Pharisees understood in a superstitious, physical way / and made wide "reminder-slips" <note>German: *Denck-Zettel*, referring to phylacteries</note> on their clothes. Matthew 23:5. Just as the natural man always wants to please GOD with external things / whereas with these figures of speech He desires only the inner work of the heart. Proverbs 23:26.

**v. 6. These words)** All of God’s commandments / but primarily the immediately preceding first and great commandment of love / which according to its power contains all the others within itself. These very words / and no others: not such teachings that are merely human commandments.

Without doubt Moses foresaw / that such a generation would come / who would set aside the commandments of GOD / and promote the traditions of men instead. Mark 7:8.

**Today)** Just as "yesterday" refers to the Law / and "today" to the Gospel: Hebrews 13:8. Thus, through the frequent repetition of this word in this matter, it is indicated / that these are Evangelical words.

**Shall be in the heart)** That one actually thinks of them / has them present in the mind / will / and inclinations / and is ready and willing to do them.

**They will no longer be written on stones:** They are too hard and thick / to be able to contain such things. They must be engraved in the hearts. For the heart alone can contain this lesson. The language of love is learned from love itself / and love teaches how to love. O You God of Love / You can instruct us rightly / to love You in purity! You alone teach the believing and faithful souls the pure law of Your love / which is entirely freed from all self-love / and which those who still love themselves cannot understand. It is truly the law of the heart / which is recognized only by the heart: and not the stony law / which / because of its resistance / cannot contain such a law that makes a soul so soft and pliable to all the will of GOD / whatever it may be / and whatever it may cost: because a loving heart sets aside all self-interest / only to think of that which concerns its Friend. This is the law / that tears our whole heart away from itself / to give it entirely to GOD and let it rest in GOD: which fleshly love has almost pulled into its own laws / by saying / that the heart is more where it loves / than where it moves. GOD has given Himself to man / to make His love all the more known to him: And man surrenders himself entirely to GOD / to give Him testimonies of his love: And when he has come to this happy restoration / then one can no longer distinguish / whether GOD is our heart / or whether our heart is GOD.

**v. 7. Your children)** Those who are begotten of GOD through the immortal seed of the Word / as disciples.

**Instill)** Through more and more frequent repetition and drumming-in of these words.

The 5th Book of Moses [Deuteronomy] may well take its name <note>Deuteronomy means "Second Law" or "Repetition of the Law"</note> from this instilling and repetition. For it seems throughout to be nothing else / and the most noble conclusion / at which it is mainly aimed / is everywhere / that we should hear the voice of the Lord / be obedient to His commandments, and do them.

To whet or sharpen <note>referring to the German *einschärffen*</note> is nothing other than rubbing off the rust and making the tool bright-shining and sharp.

<margin>2 Chronicles 15:14.</margin>

---

**v. 8. As a sign)** Against this strives the mark of the beast on the hand and forehead, Revelation 13:16 / when one strives for honor and wealth in this world by keeping human commandments.

**On your hand -- between your eyes)** On these words are still based the <term>Tephillin</term> <note>Hebrew: phylacteries</note>, <term>phylacteria</term> <note>Latin: amulets or prayer boxes</note> or reminder-slips of the Jews today / which they must put on every day during morning prayer.

These consist of 4 square pieces of wood / one of which has 4 small compartments / which is bound in front on the forehead / the other has only one small compartment / which is bound on the thick flesh of the left arm. In said small compartments are placed special slips of clean parchment / on which various biblical verses are written with special ceremonies / such as (1) from Exodus 13:1-11. (2) Exodus 13:11-17. (3) Deuteronomy 6:4-10. (4) Deuteronomy 11:13-22. Attached to these two is a strap of Cordovan or other clean leather with a loop: specifically on the first / which is bound around the head / and is called by them <term>Tephillin Shel Rosh</term> <note>Hebrew: Phylactery of the Head</note>, <term>precatoria capitis</term> <note>Latin: prayer-device of the head</note> / there is a knob or knot with a double ד <note>The Hebrew letter Dalet</note> / which comes to be at the back of the head / and the square housing / on which a ש <note>The Hebrew letter Shin</note> stands on the outside / comes to stand in front on the forehead. On the other strap around the arm, a knot is tied in the manner of a י <note>The Hebrew letter Yod</note>.

These <term>Tephillin</term> they consider especially holy. Inasmuch as they not only carry them in special bags / but also must otherwise be clean and pure of body / if they wish to put them on.

**v. 9. On the posts of your house)** Therefore one still sees on almost all doorposts of Jewish houses certain reminder-slips of parchment attached / called <term>Mezuzah</term> <note>Hebrew: doorpost</note> / on which they are accustomed to write several biblical words and other superstitious things / and for this reason they refer back to this passage.

# The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter VI. 710

### 14. You shall not follow other gods / from the gods of the peoples who are round about you;

### 15. For the LORD your GOD is a jealous <note>The German *eiferiger* implies both "zealous" and "jealous"—a passionate intensity that demands total exclusivity.</note> GOD among you: lest the anger of the LORD your GOD burn against you and destroy you from off the face of the earth.

### 16. You shall not test the LORD your GOD / just as you tested him at Massah.

<margin>v. 14. 16.</margin> Prosperity very easily causes one to forget GOD / and to choose other gods for oneself: namely the world and men / so that one might keep them as friends / and thus be able to live according to the perverse lusts of the flesh. And then, lack and want cause one to mistrust GOD / as happened at Massah / and to attempt to help oneself with other forbidden means / and thereby set aside GOD’s presence / wisdom / omnipotence and goodness. See Chapter 8:11 etc. and Proverbs 30:8-9.

<margin>v. 15.</margin> GOD is jealous over the heart of man; indeed, He wants it entirely / and not half. Jealousy can tolerate no companion / even if it were a king. He also desires nothing else / even if it were the very best of things. And it is this very jealousy which prompts Him to strip the soul bare / and to lead it through such harsh conditions; so that / once it remains stripped of all innate and acquired goods / it may be free of everything / and can then find itself in a state to receive the love of GOD. Whoever loves only the virtues / gifts and benefits of GOD for their own sake; that person is not worthy of GOD. Oh! Is GOD not lovely enough / to give Him our whole heart: and also not great enough / to possess it all alone / without one wishing to possess anything alongside Him?

In order that we might now love Him with this highest love / and so that He might preserve us Himself; He remains in our midst. Thus we must also be zealous for GOD / and without mercy tear out of our hearts everything that wishes to dwell therein alongside Him. How blessed is he / who recognizes the generosity of pure love! He may imagine / that he can speak of and comprehend the very best things regarding it; yet he will never truly recognize it / until he has experienced it: and he does not experience it / until it has drawn him out of himself / to place him in GOD through that secret ecstasy <note>German: *Entzückung*, often used in mystical literature to describe a state of being "carried away" by divine love.</note> / which can be understood by none other than those in whom such a placement occurs / as they are then quite astonished / that they are only just then beginning to recognize the true unselfishness and generosity of love / which they had supposed they recognized many years before.

Every person who has been established in the Truth recognizes and experiences the jealousy of GOD so strongly / that he reserves nothing of his own / be it ever so small: And if he should perhaps claim something for himself / oh, with what a severe punishment would this infidelity be punished! Those who have once experienced the jealousy of a GOD / they would be able to say things of it / which should make one tremble with horror. And the more He wishes to have a heart for Himself / the more He is jealous over it. The Bridegroom is more jealous with his Bride / than with her maidservants: and when He once admits a soul to His bridal-bed / oh GOD, then He does not suffer the slightest thing upon her / but tears everything away from her without mercy.

<margin>v. 16.</margin> You shall not test GOD) GOD may be tested in many ways. In His wisdom. Psalm 73:11. In His truth. 2 Kings 7:2. In His goodness and providence over us. Matthew 4:6-7. In His power. Numbers 11:4-5. Psalm 78:19-20. Numbers 14:22. In His omnipresence. Exodus 17:7. Toward which the latter two are primarily aimed in the following words:

As you (in your fathers / tested Him) So that / although every testing by the fathers may be meant here / nonetheless the one regarding His omnipresence and power is to be understood primarily and specifically.

<column-break/>

### 17. You shall keep with all diligence the commandments of the LORD your GOD / and His testimonies and His statutes / which He has commanded you.

### 18. That you do what is right and good in the eyes of the LORD; so that it may go well with you / and you may enter and possess as an inheritance the good land that the LORD swore to your fathers:

### 19. That He may drive out all your enemies from before your face / just as the LORD has spoken.

The law / word and will of GOD must be put into practice / and consists of duties / which must be learned by us / and not merely imagined / or fantasized about / as if they had been done by someone else in our place. How often we may read such a thing in this book! And so it sounds consistently until the end of Holy Scripture. See Chapter 15:1; 19:9. James 1:22. Revelation 22:14. And

Should not an honest soul gain every desire to enter into such a blessed way of life / and be converted from the heart / since pure grace and promise are laid upon him and his own? How could one then view the will of GOD merely as such a tedious or harsh law / that would be neither possible nor useful to keep?

<margin>v. 17.</margin> But what is more horrifying / than that one must say / that the commandments of the Devil are kept with greater diligence than the commandments of the Lord! For what is more zealously held with mouth and heart / and in deed more zealously shown in obedience than these teachings of the unclean spirit:

1. That one should fear men / love the world / and trust oneself; and
2. serve these in GOD’s place.
3. That one should use and profane the name of GOD in all sorts of ways.
4. That one should spend six days with greed and choosing in the cares of sustenance; but on the seventh serve the devil / pride / strolling / drinking / gambling and idleness / and thereby simultaneously serve one's belly; but for appearance's sake / according to custom / keep and attend external worship / sing and read / and yet leave Him only the heart <note>The author is being satirical here; "leave Him only the heart" implies a hollow ritual where the heart is not actually engaged.</note>.
5. That one should obey and follow parents and superiors in nothing except in sins and an evil life.
6. That one should meet one's neighbor with mercilessness / envy / enmity / anger and bitterness.
7. That one should consider fornication and adultery a "gallant affair" <note>German: *Galanterie*, suggesting that people treat serious sins as mere fashionable social pastimes.</note> / and think even less of saying shameful words and jesting speech.
8. That one should strive after that which is on earth / and seek one's own profit to the neighbor's harm.
9. That one should always reproach something of his neighbor improperly. And finally
10. That one should let lusts rule freely within oneself.

Regarding this, may GOD bring a holy shudder within us / so that we may respect His rights <unclear>higher</unclear> than we have until now.

<margin>v. 18.</margin> What is right and good in the eyes of the LORD) In his actions / man should look only to GOD / what might be right and well-pleasing before Him: but not to the lust of his own heart or to the actions of other men / what they do in his time / and what the ancestors have done. See Chapter 12:8, 25. Psalm 49:14, 20.

<margin>v. 19.</margin> With this, preparation is made for the following chapter / where such expulsion of the <term>heathen</term> <note>original: *heyndischen*, an archaic form of *heidnischen*</note> and hostile Canaanite peoples will occur with power as the main work. For in this is also shown the jealousy of the LORD our GOD / who has shown us so much grace / that we should be thankful to Him for it all the days of our lives / and demonstrate and prove this gratitude not only with words and with the mouth / but much more in deed and truth / with a most simple obedience / in the observation of His commandments. Now, so that this may happen all the better and more steadily / GOD will have nothing left remaining / whereby the enemies might gain access to us.
