# Chapter VI. The Fifth Book of Moses <note>Deuteronomy</note>. 711

20. When your son asks you tomorrow and says: What are these testimonies and these statutes and these rights / which the LORD our GOD has commanded you?
21. Then you shall say to your son: We were slaves of Pharaoh in Egypt / and the LORD led us out of Egypt with a strong hand;
22. And the LORD did great and terrible signs and wonders in Egypt / upon Pharaoh and upon all his house before our eyes:

These are the best conversations / instructions and reports / that we should give our children daily: that we seek to instruct them in the ways of the LORD / and not only lead them to GOD’s Word / but also make known to them what we ourselves have experienced of GOD’s wonderful ways in our own lives and in our families; so that they might learn / how GOD always rewards the good in us and ours with grace / but also punishes the evil / and how wonderfully He has led / protected and preserved us: of which there will be enough material in every generation / if only one would pay attention to GOD’s ways toward us. See Genesis 12:26, 13:14, Joshua 4.

May GOD grant / that we all might take these words of our Creator truly to heart for such a purpose / that through the power of the Holy Spirit we diligently practice GOD’s Word in our houses / and let our children do nothing in the morning and evening before saying an earnest prayer.

One should rather skimp on food / and bring a Bible into the house / which is better than all prayer books / to diligently read it with one's own / and always apply what one reads to oneself.

If one cares daily for the needs of the body / why would one leave his soul and the souls of his family unprovided for with the Word of GOD / which can feed and satisfy them as immortal spirits?

But therein one must also guard against empty chatter / or superfluous Pharisaic talk / reading or hearing / where one does not have and show a complete earnestness / in the Holy Spirit. One should speak and read nothing / until one has sighed to GOD for His good Spirit. Even if there are few words / there is all the more power. Our word shall be yes, yes / short and good / so that we do not fall into hypocrisy.

One will observe GOD’s mind even more closely / if one constantly insists on the practice and the deed in all things good / so that one actually desires to become obedient with one's family to the pattern of teaching. For

Outward hearing and learning is ultimately easy: but everything must be transformed into life and become true in us / according to what we recognize.

Since such a heavy duty lies especially upon those who have children / that they should lead others to GOD / whom GOD has given them and bound to their souls; so they may consider / how blamelessly they must shine before them / as true spiritual house-priests <term>house-priests: a concept in Pietism where the father or head of household acts as a minister to his own family</term> and house-preachers / who themselves must not become reprobate.

For this it is necessary / that one personally practices daily repentance and penance / believes in the Lord JESUS without hypocrisy / and follows His Holy Spirit with an honest mind. Truly / in such daily exercises of repentance one will also use more earnestness with his children / and also awaken true divine blessing and transformation of their hearts.

The poor children are indeed as corrupted by the Fall as the elders / and one has as much natural desire for good as the other. Therefore one would act most blessedly / if one turned back with them / and became like children. If one surrendered oneself daily more to GOD with one's family / and thus in earnest first laid the true foundation of faith anew with his children; then one might well build his house of salvation upon the rock of Christ / and not on the sand of hypocrisy and false imaginings.

<column-break/>

23. And he led us out from there / that he might bring us in to give us the land that he had sworn to our fathers.
24. And the LORD commanded us to do all these statutes / that we fear the LORD our GOD; that it may be well with us all our days / to keep us alive / as it is this day.
25. And it will be righteousness for us / when we shall be careful to do all this commandment before the face of the LORD our GOD / just as he has commanded us.

->Romans 3:24.<-

->The<- <note>Catchword for the next section</note>

If one had first turned his heart rightly to GOD / then one would also be powerful and blessed in prayer and supplication for his poor children; just as they are in great need of it / because they are stuck in great danger / distress and corruption / in body and soul.

In this let one now test his prayers / whether they have been sufficient / to ask for something right and blessed for them before GOD.

The Holy Spirit must be the first and last here / that one asks for Him and receives Him into the heart from GOD. He will surely anoint and make one powerful / so that one can offer up one's family to the Lord with impact.

But without the Holy Spirit one will neither believe rightly for oneself and come to JESUS Christ / nor much less be able to lead others to Him. All our things are lost and nothing / if GOD does not do / speak and accomplish it in and through us.

But if our heart first becomes full of faith and love for GOD / then our mouth will also overflow of its own accord toward our children. One will always bring forth all kinds of good admonitions from the good treasure of his heart / warnings and corrections / which are wholesome for them. One will be able to give them so many blessed reports of GOD and His will / of this and that temptation and snare of the devil / which one has experienced oneself / etc. Then it will be our delight / to give them, as it were, with every bite of bread a good reminder as food for their souls / and to plant the Word rightly in them / as a seed of eternity that has become living and fruit-bearing in ourselves. Our heart will burn with love for their souls / and it will then also become true in us / what GOD says of Abraham in Genesis 18:18.

But how can one rightly show the way to his poor children and convince them what it means to become godly / and how one must set about it / if one wants to come to GOD / when one has not yet experienced or rightly practiced it oneself? Where will the power / impact / and wisdom / come from / which is so necessary / if one does not receive it through the Holy Spirit? Does one not think / that children soon notice it / if we are not in right earnest about GOD and His will?

Oh, it soon shows itself / whether something is said with a right foundation or earnestness! But if one only babbles and hypocritically recites something to the children *pro forma* <note>original: "pro forma"; meaning "for the sake of form" or "as a formality"</note> and for appearance's sake / then the children will follow in hypocrisy / and also learn to make mere chatter out of GOD’s Word / like the elders. From this preserve us, dear Lord GOD!

v. 24. **That it may be well with us**) When we serve GOD / we serve ourselves much more: for we receive all the benefit from it. Job 35:7. Psalm 16:2, 3.

v. 25. **To us for righteousness**) Moses indeed described righteousness from the Law / how man could come to life: but because man finds nothing but impotence in himself / to fulfill this righteousness; he must turn to Christ and His Spirit / that he might obtain in Him the righteousness from faith. See Chapter 24:13. Romans 8:3-4, 10:4-11.

# Chapter VII.

->The extermination of the Canaanites and their abominations.<-

**W**hen the LORD your GOD shall have brought you into the land where you are going to possess it as an inheritance, and shall have rooted out many nations before your face; the Hittites, and the Girgashites, and the Amorites, and the Canaanites, and the Perizzites, and the Hivites, and the Jebusites <gloss>(a)</gloss> seven nations that are greater and stronger than you:
<margin>(a) Genesis 10:15 etc., 15:19; Exodus 33:2, 34:11.</margin>

2. And the LORD your GOD shall deliver them before you, so that you strike them: then you shall utterly ban them <note>The Hebrew term "herem" implies total devotion to destruction or divine exclusion.</note>; you shall make no covenant with them, nor show them mercy: <gloss>Exodus 34:12, 15.</gloss>

---

Just as strictly, believers in the New Testament are forbidden from associating with all depraved people who still live in their pagan state, even if they wish to be regarded as Christians because of their outward confession to Christ, and thus in deed, if not in words, call themselves brothers. 1 Corinthians 5:9 etc. With such unbelievers and people living in injustice and darkness, the holy people belonging to our Lord Jesus Christ shall have no fellowship. 2 Corinthians 6:14 etc.

The people who are His own possession shall in no way unite themselves with those nations of Canaan, who are expressed here by name, and therein at the same time their characteristics; by these, however, all false powers and all worldly lusts in us are signified, along with all those people who allow themselves to be ruled by the same.

**Hittites** are the fearful ones, who are unfit for faith and have no ground of trust within themselves. These are the first here, and also the first to be excluded from the holy city, and in contrast, the first part in the pit is assigned to them.

**Girgashites** are those who estrange themselves from God and the life that is from Him through earthly-mindedness.

**Amorites** are chatterers and everything that stems from the root of bitterness.

**Canaanites** are those who are bowed down, bent down into themselves, and are lovers of themselves.

**Perizzites** are those who live on in false security.

**Hivites** depict the ungodly life: and

**The Jebusites** are such people, thoughts, and lusts which trample underfoot the divine truths, the pearls, the Son of God himself, and the life of God within them.

The number seven of the nations is quite remarkable. Rupertus <note>Rupert of Deutz, a 12th-century theologian.</note> relates it to the 7 evil spirits which the Savior also mentions in the Gospel (a): others also to the 7 capital and deadly sins; 1) Greed, 2) Pride, 3) Envy, 4) Wrath, 5) Unchastity, 6) Gluttony and Drunkenness, 7) Sloth or Vanity. Just as the Beast in the Revelation appears with 7 heads.

v. 2. These must all together be struck, banned, annihilated, and rooted out without any grace or mercy. And

This justice must be carried out not on others, but on ourselves.

If we root out all the bitter roots, then our field becomes clean. If we sweep out the leaven from every corner, then we become a sweet dough.

If even one traitor remains in us, we may not dwell in safety.

The Lord wants the members that are on earth to be put to death. We should not rest until we have rooted them all out: so that there may be peace in our entire region. Our "old man" <note>A Pauline term for the unregenerate human nature.</note> does not improve. The body of sins must cease: land and body must be sanctified to the LORD.
<gloss>(a) Luke 11:26.</gloss>

<column-break/>

3. And you shall not intermarry with them. Your daughter you shall not give to his son, and his daughter you shall not take for your son.
<gloss>Ezra 9 and 10.</gloss>

4. For he will turn away your son from following me, so that they serve other gods. Then the anger of the LORD will burn against you and destroy you suddenly.

5. But thus shall you do with them: their altars you shall tear down, their pillars you shall break, and their sacred groves you shall cut down, and their carved images you shall burn with fire.

6. For

---

v. 3. Yet even in outward things, no fellowship nor friendship should be sought or practiced with pagan-minded people and unbelievers by those who wish to be believing Israelites: even less, however, should such a close bond and covenant, as marriage is, be established between such unequal parts.

v. 4. Do not think that you will convert such people through your association, and that they shall become better through your presence. They will rather seduce you and make you worse. Gradually one conforms and joins in their works.

v. 5. Therefore it is better, caught in the fire of love, to surrender everything that turns us away from the pure love of GOD and wishes to place an image of seduction before our senses, in good time together with all such images to the judgment of consumption. Better that we 

**tear down all altars**, upon which the spirit of Cain, the race of Ham, and the seed of the Antichrist are accustomed to perform unclean hypocritical sacrifices in us; and through the counsel of the mouth of GOD

**break their pillars**, that is, everything that is set up for public offense under the appearance of divine service and gives cause for it: and

**Their carved images**, to which human reason has given a form, though they otherwise consisted of unshaped matter. Augustine (a) <note>original: "L. 5. de verb. Dom. c. ult." refers to Augustine's Sermons on the Words of the Lord, Book 5, final chapter.</note> notes that such things must primarily happen in the hearts of idolaters.

> "a shapeless thing, as is also honor and the other goods 
> "of life, which have nothing solid and true,

Let us then ourselves break our images, so that we may rest in the Essence.

<margin>1 Kings 8:53.</margin>
6. For you are a holy people to the LORD your God: the LORD your God has chosen you to be His own special possession <note>The German "Volck des Eigenthums" refers to a people who are God's private property or treasure.</note> out of all the peoples that are on the face of the earth.

7. The LORD did not set His affection on you nor choose you because you were more in number than any other people; for you were the fewest of all peoples.

***

v. 6. The language of pure love is only understood by those who have reached an excellent stage of naked faith <note> "Naked faith" (bloßer Glaube) is a mystical term for a faith stripped of all sensory comfort or intellectual proofs.</note>. Therefore, Holy Scripture also says that the people of love are a holy people to the Lord. It is a people who are holy for God, and not for themselves. For they could not desire the slightest holiness for themselves, nor even any virtues: and if they found that they possessed any of these as a thing attributed to themselves, they would wish that such things be quickly taken from them, and would hate them as they hate the Devil himself.

O Holiness, you are only in and before God! The knowledge of this truth will ensure that the saints, who are bare and void of all other holiness, will see nothing in heaven but the sole holiness of God Himself; which shall cause them to cry out without ceasing (a): Holy, Holy, Holy! For in this dwelling of glory, in which everything shall be found in pure and clear truth, everything shall be restored to complete unity. And this pure truth and complete unity cannot be seen outside of Him, as it is nothing but God Himself: nor likewise can this holiness be seen elsewhere, as it is composed of Him. And just as the righteous have received such holiness from God Himself through His Son Jesus Christ, so they will very faithfully return it to God alone through His Son Jesus Christ, without keeping the slightest part of it for themselves. St. Paul expressed this when he says (b) that Jesus Christ shall deliver up His kingdom to His God and Father, when He shall first have done away with all rule, all authority, and all power <note>original: "Tugend", here used in the sense of 'power' or 'virtue' as a celestial rank.</note>: then the Son Himself shall be subject to Him who put all things under His feet, so that God may be All in all.

If a soul ignited with this pure love saw itself clothed in its own proprietary holiness, it would—as soon as it was placed in the truth—betake itself into the abyss of hell to be rid of it: for it has then come so far that nothing is more unbearable to it than "selfhood" <note>German: "Eigenheit". In this context, it refers to the ego or the desire to possess spiritual gifts as one's own.</note>, and it would rather suffer anything else than allow the slightest contagion of the same, which it might recognize, to remain. Therefore, such a people is holy to the Lord. For because it is not found to be self-seeking, all holiness is for God. And this is brought about by perfect love, which gives everything to God and takes everything from the creature. However, because this is something rare, the Scripture says that this people of love is a people which God has set apart for Himself (not for His gifts, graces, and benefits) so that they might be a special people to Him in love above all the nations of the whole world.

v. 7. God has not united Himself with His dear inner people because they are greater, or because they should be more numerous than all other peoples: For, on the contrary, they are the weakest people in number, and the least in the imagination of men, because of their nakedness and annihilation <note> "Annihilation" (Vernichtung) here refers to the mystical process of the "death of the self."</note>.

<margin>
(a) Isaiah 6:3; Revelation 4:8. (b) 1 Corinthians 15:24–28.
</margin>

<column-break/>

8. But because the LORD loved you, and because He kept the oath which He had sworn to your fathers, the LORD has brought you out with a mighty hand, and redeemed you from the house of bondage, from the hand of Pharaoh king of Egypt.

9. Therefore you shall know that the LORD your God is God, the true God (a), who keeps covenant and mercy with those who love Him and keep His commandments, to a thousand generations:
<margin>ch. 5:10; Exodus 20:6; ch. 34:7; Daniel 9:4. (a) 1 John 5:20.</margin>

10. And repays those who hate Him to their face, to destroy them: He will not delay with him who hates Him, He will repay him to his face.
<margin>(a) Psalm 139:21.</margin>

11. Therefore keep the commandment and the statutes and the judgments which I command you today, to do them. 12.

***

v. 8. Rather, He has united Himself with them because He loved them. Yes, this people, so small and regarded as nearly nothing in appearance, is loved by its God; and it is also loved by Him for nothing, through a pure precedence of God, without Him taking notice of their poor worthiness. Is it then not more than right that God should be loved in return by them, let it cost what it will?

v. 9. Holy Scripture is admirable in its expressions by which it shows a soul—one that frees itself from all personal benefit of salvation, holiness, and everything else in order to be able to love God more purely—that God is pleased to find that the soul loses everything for this reason. It assures this soul that its God, to whom it surrenders itself, is strong and faithful: strong to rescue it from danger and to preserve it so that it cannot fall; and all-too-faithful to allow it to be deceived when it surrenders itself to Him without exception, and does not put itself in danger of displeasing Him by wanting to please Him for its own sake. Its love does not go outside its bounds except insofar as it loves Him above all rules: and God keeps His faithfulness to those who love Him until the end.

*He who keeps mercy with those who keep His commandments*) Thus God is both generous and very exact. He gives and shares grace and gifts richly; but He also demands in return from everyone that they repay Him with diligence in good works, insofar as each is gifted by God externally and internally. The grace of God is not given for nothing. It constantly offers us, if we take heed of it, everything we need, and demands in return from us everything we can perform. Yes, God wants to give and bestow Himself entirely, with all that He is, to His own: but He demands that we should give ourselves entirely to Him in return. His grace in us and our love for Him is the work which shall be constantly driven between God and His creature in reciprocal exercise.

v. 10. *To his face*) This is not repeated without cause, to assure that because all the godless provoke God the Lord with such manifest abominations of sin, and thereby openly show by their faces that they have no fear of God or dread of His wrath, <margin>Psalm 36:1 etc.</margin> God also wants to reveal His righteous punishment on such insolent people before their faces and the faces of others: of which may be seen the example of Korah’s company and the people still murmuring over this punishment in Numbers 16. To this also belong all unmerciful people who likewise cast away the fear of God and thus hate God; these also shall not be left without visible punishment. See Job 6:14. To which also the example of Nabal can belong because of his lack of love in 1 Samuel 25:37-38. For he who shows no love to his neighbor has no love for God.

v. 11. *Keep*) Just as I keep the covenant made with your fathers. Between covenant-partners, a keeping is required on both sides.

It warns that while God is infinitely generous with grace, He requires a total, unselfish surrender of the soul and punishes those who openly reject His love.</summary>

> 12. And it shall come to pass, because you listen to these judgments, and keep and do them, that the LORD your God will keep with you the covenant and the mercy which He swore to your fathers.
> 13. And He will love you and bless you and multiply you; He will also bless the fruit of your womb and the fruit of your land, your grain and your new wine and your oil, the increase of your cattle and the herds of your sheep, in the land which He swore to your fathers to give you.
> 14. You shall be blessed above all peoples; there shall not be a male or female barren among you or among your livestock.

<margin>Exodus 23:26. Proverbs 5:18.</margin>

God desires to graciously reward the obedience of faith, so that we might again perceive His blessing-love in all kinds of physical blessings; whereby He then also wishes to turn away all misery of sickness, plagues, and adversity from enemies. Since such a glorious blessing is now so rarely perceived throughout, this is a certain indication that obedience is also very rare among those who boast of being God’s people. But when once the glorious promise in Christ's Kingdom shall be fulfilled, that His people shall be all righteous, into whom He will put His Spirit and cause them to walk in His statutes and keep His judgments and do them; then all such physical and spiritual blessings shall manifest themselves in all perfection, and all sickness, plagues, and danger from enemies must entirely depart. Ezekiel 36:27 etc. 37:24 etc.

<margin>v. 12. Because</margin> The Hebrew word is by no means to be interpreted as a meritorious reward <note>original: "Ekev," meaning "consequence" or "heel," implies a result rather than a wage earned</note>, but here signifies a cause, just as in chapter 8:20. Yet God nevertheless wishes to make Himself our debtor. Isaiah 45:19. For

God is righteous and a rewarder: This is an established truth which requires no extensive proof, because it is written in the very conscience of men. But the right understanding of this truth is known to few, because nature commonly tends to fall back upon one's own merit and works.

It is safest that one neither seeks reward on one hand and gives place to own righteousness, nor on the other hand entirely denies or doubts the divine promises of grace, as if it were in vain for the heart to walk blamelessly and to lead a hard life before the Lord.

<margin>v. 13. Love, bless, multiply</margin> How beautifully the triune being reveals itself here in its outgoing, distinct attributes! The source, God the Father, is Love; and blesses the creature in the Son of Love, as the blessed seed in whom all families of the earth shall be blessed, through the Spirit of the Son, as the holy anointing, the outpouring and outflowing of divine love, Romans 5:5, and the multiplying power for the fruitfulness of the Church.

<margin>v. 14.</margin> Godliness has, just as in the New so also in the Old Testament, the promise of the present and the future life. 1 Timothy 4:8. For there is always a hidden meaning tucked within the promises of a temporal blessing, as Augustine (a) well recognized: however, mention is made of temporal goods for the most part because God dealt with the Israelites as with children, who prefer an apple to a precious gemstone (b). Galatians 3:23–25. And thus God entices men to His service also through temporal rewards, just as one might entice children into school with sugar and money. See Chrysostom's clever comparison thereof (c).

<margin>(a) Augustine, Against Faustus, book 15, ch. 9. (b) Theodoret, Questions on Deuteronomy, q. 6. (c) Chrysostom, Homily 4 on Colossians, p. 1111.</margin>

<column-break/>

> 15. And the LORD will take away from you all sickness, and will put none of the evil diseases of the Egyptians, which you have <unclear>experienced</unclear>, upon you, but will lay them on all those who hate you.
> 16. And you shall <term>consume</term> <note>original: "devour" or "eat up"</note> all the peoples whom the LORD your God delivers to you! Your eye shall not pity them, nor shall you serve their gods; for that would be a snare to you.

<margin>Numbers 33:55. Joshua ch. 9, ch. 23:13.</margin>

<margin>v. 15. When the LORD, upon the success of obedience</margin> and the keeping of His commandments, wishes to turn away and remove all sickness and plague, one clearly sees what the best <term>preservative</term> <note>a preventative medicine</note> against all sickness is: and why then do you need much questioning and running after physicians who cannot help themselves? Here the recipe is written out for you so plainly and clearly: why then will you gape so long after others? Receive the Word that is so near to you with meekness, even if it does not suit your corrupted <unclear>appetite</unclear>; then you will see how it will penetrate your body and soul, and you yourself will become a witness to this healing truth.

(Which you have experienced) Not so much in yourself and your own body through your own feeling; but rather in the Egyptians, when such manifold plagues were sent upon them.

<margin>v. 16. You shall consume all peoples</margin> or eat them up, as it properly means in Hebrew; there is at least a difference of degree between the two, as can be seen in Ecclesiastes 5:15.

The faint-hearted and unbelieving fear they will be eaten by their enemies. But the Church or the people of God has the gracious promise that it shall eat its enemies. The LORD Himself speaks this through the mouth of the enemies of His Church: Numbers 22:4. And Balaam agrees with this in chapter 24:8. Other passages also confirm the same. Zechariah 12:6.

And in what does this "eating up" consist? She <note>the Church</note> shall bring them under the obedience of faith; or, if they are desperately stubborn and no improvement is to be hoped for from them, then that which is threatened in Isaiah 60:12 shall follow.

The whole body of sin, the whole kingdom of the devil, of sin and of death, shall one day be destroyed and abolished, so that the Kingdom of God may come and be awakened in us.

This is prefigured by the consumption of the burnt offering and the destruction of the seven nations in the land of Canaan. This is what is meant by the prophet Amos 9:8.

Therefore, let no one believe the fearful, faint-hearted, and unbelieving spies who want to persuade you that the enemy nations are too strong and powerful for us; but rather believe the faithful and brave witnesses of God who assure us that we can well devour them. Numbers 14:9.

Thus the altar of Christ's patience consumes sin. For this reason He is called <term>Ariel</term> <note>original Hebrew: "Lion of God" or "Altar-hearth"</note>, the Lion of God, Ezekiel 43:15, because He eats the flesh of sin that is laid upon Him. And in like manner, the spiritual enemies of the LORD and His people are consumed by the fire of the Spirit, which burns upon the altar of the patience of Jesus Christ.

To this end, strengthen us, O Lord, through Your Spirit, which kills the works or operations of the flesh, Romans 8:13, and may eat up and consume all the godless peoples, all the seven nations of sins; which otherwise would eat and consume us!

<margin>Your eye shall not spare</margin> The affections or inclinations are attributed to the eyes, in which they appear or are seen: as we see in the eyes of a person whether he is well or ill-pleased or angry; which even the animals themselves can distinguish. Hence Scripture is accustomed to speak thus when it expresses the intention to be merciful or unmerciful.

20. Moreover, the Lord your God will send hornets <note>The Hebrew "tsir'ah" refers to stinging insects, often interpreted literally as hornets or metaphorically as a divine panic sent to demoralize the enemy.</note> among them, until those who are left and have hidden themselves from you have perished.

---

We should never be terrified by the power of our physical enemies, and especially not our spiritual ones, as if we could not overcome them but would eventually succumb. Instead, we must always encourage ourselves with this precious promise: that God wants to deliver us from all great trials by His strong arm, even through simple and lowly instruments, through which He can very quickly remove and destroy the adversaries. We must then only strive to be strong in the Lord and in the power of His might, and be equipped with the whole armor of God; thus we will be able to stand against the cunning attacks of the devil, both in our inner being and from the outside through his miserable instruments in which he seeks to harm us. Ephesians 6:10 etc.

Everything that should make the kingdom of Jesus Christ manifest within and outside of us is held back purely by the fear of man and despondency. For these make one weak, so that one gives up the cause as lost and allows the enemy an easy victory. From this comes the false conclusion: it cannot be otherwise, and there is no good to be hoped for in this world. But if we did not become weary, but pursued the prize and always stood diligently in the right order, God would surely show us how He is stronger than sin and does not allow Himself to be overwhelmed by it, but indeed wants to and can blot out and take it away.

# The Fifth Book of Moses, Chapter VIII. <note>Deuteronomy</note>

<margin>Psalm 78. Judges 2:22.</margin>
> **2. And you shall remember all the way that the LORD your God led you these forty years in the wilderness, so that he might humble you and test you, to know what was in your heart, whether you would keep his commandments or not.**

Divine temptations <note>The author uses "temptation" (Versuchung) here in the sense of a "trial" or "testing" rather than an enticement to sin.</note> through all kinds of adversities are merely fatherly chastenings that God imposes for our humiliation, and so that we may come to know ourselves. For if things always went well for us, the innermost depths of our heart <note>original: "innerster Herzens-Grund." In German mystical tradition, this "ground of the heart" is the deepest point of the soul where man meets God.</note> would not be truly revealed to us—showing what a stubborn, proud, vengeful, and faint-hearted heart we still possess. Thus, such events must occur where we are attacked either directly by God or by our neighbor, and through this our obedience, patience, humility, denial of earthly things, and all such virtues must be revealed; or we may have sought to obtain such through the grace of God in our hearts. See the glorious example of Abraham in Genesis 22:12, etc., and Hebrews 12:5, etc.

How many instances of the Israelites' coarse rudeness were revealed in this wilderness, as the Lord found it good and necessary to put them to the test! Not as if He needed it; for He surely knows what is in the heart. Rather, it was for the sake of the people, so that their own hearts might be revealed to them, which they otherwise would neither know nor believe. For

Most people consider themselves pious and righteous if they merely do nothing evil outwardly, and conversely, do something good every now and then. For such people, nothing is more necessary or better than to fall into temptation, and thereby learn to notice what lies within them.

When a person first sees and learns to believe that such a secret treasure of wickedness lies hidden within them, they will certainly be horrified and humbled by it. They will also learn to hasten toward a thorough cleansing and improvement, and not rest until they are truly born of God, and Christ redeems them from the works of the devil.

From this, it should be obvious to everyone why God allows so many temptations to come even upon His own people. Oh, this is a great mystery of divine wisdom and holiness that is known to few! It is a wholesome guidance for whoever learns to apply it rightly! It is actually nothing other than a discovery of the evil hidden in the heart. God has His wholesome purpose in this, why He allows such rudeness to break out. He has no pleasure or guilt in it; but because He knows that such misery sticks in the human heart as a seed of the devil, and man rarely—or not rightly—wants to recognize it, He allows for wholesome reasons that this same corruption break out now and then, betraying itself like a thief sitting and hidden in the heart. And

Therefore, believers should also learn to reconcile themselves to it when they must endure all kinds of hard attacks from sin, in which their proud flesh is greatly shamed and brought to disgrace before God. Oh, how that hurts the Pharisaic sense of self-love! One does not like to look so wretched and corrupted, or to be judged by other people.

Oh, how terrifying is this wilderness of faith, and how tedious is the length of its path! Moses reminds his people, who have reached the end of this path, of this, and says that they should not forget it, so that they may be confirmed in the certainty of their state.

**To know what was in your heart)** It is as if He said: I wanted to see if anything remained in your heart that could prevent me from dwelling within it. All the hardships and contempt through which such souls must pass are only arranged for the purging of their hearts, so that God alone may fill them.

...are so defiled by sin that they do not perceive the mystery of eternity being fulfilled within them. This is revealed only to righteous souls gradually, as they increase in detachment and annihilation <note>original: "Abgeschiedenheit und Vernichtigung," technical terms in mysticism for the process of letting go of the self to make room for God.</note>. Thus, although the Triune God is in hell as well as in heaven, He is there in a very different way: He is in hell only because of the necessity of His essence, which fills everything due to omnipresence and omnipotence; but not through the abundance of His love and His pleasure. But in these souls, He works according to His pleasure, without resistance, and in a way just as pleasant as in the blessed, bringing forth His works. And though they recognize such works only from their effects and through brief but living infusions communicated to them, yet every word from the mouth of God is a most tender and all-penetrating kiss and infusion of His Spirit to the soul.

<column-break/>

> **3. And he humbled you, and let you hunger, and fed you with manna, which you did not know, nor did your fathers know; so that he might make you understand that man does not live by bread alone, but that man lives by everything that proceeds out of the mouth of the LORD.**

One of the greatest hardships of souls in this wilderness is the lack and the hunger, where they were previously so full and are now so empty. If someone were to give such a soul something to satisfy itself, even if it were the bitterest thing in the whole world, it would still seem sweet to them. One cannot believe what kind of hunger this is in the soul, which is caused by self-love. It strikes them down and takes hold of them in such a way that the pains are a relief to them, because they still provide nourishment from something they feel, which serves as a support. In this state, Job said (a) that such a starved soul considers bitter things sweet, and feeds on food that it would otherwise have found disgusting.

But at the same time, God satisfies these souls with the manna, that is, a spiritual food in which the soul finds nothing that could give it pleasure. This manna is a certain unknown and invisible sustenance which the soul, because of its purity, may not distinguish. Nevertheless, it is a support that prevents the soul from perishing. For if it were not supported (even if it happens in an invisible way) in such a bare state <note>original: "blosen Zustand."</note>, it would abandon everything.

**Which you did not know, nor your fathers)** As long as the path of bare faith lasts, the soul does not recognize this perceptible support. Even the holiest fathers did not recognize it in a way they could describe; for God does not allow it to be revealed to the souls. For then they would allow themselves to be led further astray, nor would they withdraw from themselves. But God lets them encounter terrible states of the soul, so that they may gain knowledge,

**That man does not live by bread alone;** which are the received gifts of grace that serve as perceptible and distinct nourishment; rather, he lives much better from God alone; which has been prefigured by the word that comes out of the mouth of God.

The Word of God, taken simply, is an immediate word which is accepted as a means among the powers, through the medium of forms and images that make it recognizable and comprehensible. But the Word that proceeds from the mouth of God is an essential, immediate work proceeding from God Himself.

It does not say: "which *has* gone out." For the word which has gone out from God is outside of Him and is a created gift. Rather, the Scripture expresses it as the word that is present at all times and *proceeds* from God's mouth, to indicate the everlasting and always-active moment of the birthing of the WORD <note>The "WORD" here refers to the Logos, or Christ, whom theologians describe as being eternally begotten or "born" by God the Father.</note>, which constantly proceeds from the mouth of His Father and is never outside of Him.

Just as nothing limited is found or can be found in God, so there is no place in which He does not work this eternal generation of the WORD; otherwise, a place would have to be found that could contain God, or there would be an empty space where the God-WORD was not—either of which is as absurd as the other; for then God would not be infinite.

Thus, God necessarily brings forth His Word in all creatures. But sin greatly covers and hinders the sight in intelligent creatures, which only...

<meta>(a) Job 6:7.</meta>

### 4. Your clothing did not wear out upon you, and your foot did not swell these forty years.
### 5. So you have now learned in your heart, that the LORD your God has chastened you, just as a man chastens his son.
### 6. Therefore, keep the commandments of the LORD your God, that you may walk in His ways and fear Him.

v. 4. It is something remarkable that, although the soul walks through such extraordinary paths, its clothes nevertheless do not wear out. This clothing is yieldedness <term>Gelassenheit: A central concept in German mysticism, referring to a state of complete letting go of one's own will to be fully receptive to God.</term> and the guidance of Providence. Yieldedness serves as her outer garment: and the more wretched she finds herself, the more God annihilates her, and the more she surrenders herself to Him, being unable to do otherwise. This yieldedness now remains whole and does not wear out, even though everything else is lost. The mantle is the guidance of Providence. For the more a soul gives herself over, the more God takes care of her: but often He imposes such a manner that, while He covers her with it, she finds herself simultaneously burdened by it. Yet it does no harm. As long as she remains in the way of naked faith <note>The "way of naked faith" refers to a spiritual state where one relies on God without the help of emotions, visions, or intellectual certainties.</note> and does not step out of it, such things do not consume themselves, even if they are as old as we ourselves are; because they lead the souls in the way and accompany them until their end, without becoming old or slower in such a long way and length of time.

Your foot did not swell) For even if such a people commits many faults, their feet are nevertheless not harmed by them, unless the soul departs from its yieldedness. But as long as it remains therein and does not take itself back, every misfortune may happen to it, regardless of the weaknesses into which it might fall in this terrible wilderness because of its great nakedness. And even if the senses, left to themselves, swarmed with a thousand faults caused by weakness and haste, all this shall bring no harm to the feet. For since the desire of the soul is in no way wounded by it, she remains always standing straight and firm by her God in an unchangeable and unswerving attachment, which is represented by the shoes that did not break in the wilderness, without worrying about what goes on outside.

v. 5. God instructs the yielded soul, so dear to Him, through her own experience, just as a father instructs his son: and they let this excellent lesson, when they have progressed a little further, pass through their heart again. They recognize it not through the light of the spirit, but through the taste of the heart and through the memory of their experience, which remains so vividly impressed in them that no doubt remains for them. This may well be unknown to a person as long as he is still on the way, because of the vexation and uncertainty of this path. But when he has arrived at the appointed place, he cannot doubt that the way on which he walked was the right way: because it led him so straight, although between rocks and steep places and a thousand apparent dangers; on whose edge one walks without having the slightest certainty that one will not plunge into them—on the contrary, one must expect every moment to fall into them; because darkness always accompanies this path.

v. 6. The soul is therefore led in this way so that she may learn to walk according to the will of God without resistance, and be forced to obey Him with an inviolable faithfulness, whatever the cost.

---

she possesses them in GOD, and they are very glorious fruits in Him. To GOD, they are something excellent. Love without GOD is something very poor, limited, and withdrawn: but in GOD, it is GOD Himself. Finally, all virtues which one had lost for His sake are all found again when one finds Him again, as being reunited and enclosed in Him: which are represented there by all kinds of fruits and trees, yes, even by oil and honey.

### 7. For the LORD your God is bringing you into a good land, a land where there are streams of water, springs, and depths that spring out of the valleys and hills.
<margin>Nehemiah 9:25. Ezekiel 20:6.</margin>
### 8. A land of wheat and barley and vines and fig trees and pomegranates; a land of succulent olive trees and honey.
### 9. A land in which you shall not eat bread in scarcity, in which you shall lack nothing: a land whose stones are iron, and from whose mountains you will dig brass. 10.

v. 7. And through this yieldedness of the will to God above all self-interest, she shall be led to her end, which is GOD Himself.

It is a good land, because GOD is the essential Good: a land in which there are rivers, still waters, and springs; because all sources are found in Him, and he who is in GOD is in his source. But it is a source of rivers through the exuberance and strong impulse of His communications; a source of still and unmovable waters; a source of useful springs, which are pleasant and refreshing. Through the distinction of these three kinds of water, the Scripture explains all spring-water to show that through the emptiness and loss of all good, and through the drying up of all other water in this parched wilderness, the soul that has arrived in GOD nevertheless finds herself full of such waters, but in their source and in the fullness of GOD Himself. So that, although she has lost all gifts and all graces, all ease in being able to do God's work, and all acquired virtues, and returns again to her final purpose, she finds everything in its origin—not in small streams of communications, but in the source of all fullness. And since she leaves everything for GOD's sake alone, everything is given back to her much more gloriously with GOD Himself; because all the graces of GOD and all His glories are with Him: not for the sake of the soul, which no longer appropriates anything for herself, but for the sake of GOD, as He is rich in Himself.

But there are not only sources in GOD, but there are also in His ground abysses without bottom and very great streams, of which He also shows something to this soul. These are abysses in which she loses herself without ever coming out again. There, while being held in the abyss, she becomes one with Him: and in this essential union, there go out from her (as if from GOD; since she namely is no more, but GOD is for and in her) streams, waters, and springs, to be sent out according to each person's necessity. But for this reason, she must not only have arrived at the Land of Goods, in which she is and drinks from the source; but she must also, beyond this, be annihilated, lost, and transformed in GOD; so that through her, streams, waters, and springs can flow out from GOD: because all this wells up out of the very wide field of the Godhead, and out of the mountains of His power and His greatness.

v. 8. A land of wheat, barley, vines, fig trees, pomegranates, olive trees and honey) The new earth in which righteousness will dwell, which we certainly have to expect in Christ's glorious kingdom, will also be such an earth blessed with all kinds of physical goods, where one will lack nothing that necessary maintenance and refreshment will require, beyond which the believers will desire nothing.

But in a higher sense, it is at the same time a description of the divine perfections, which the soul 
Goodness is in man something very small, but in 

v. 9. As soon as the soul has once come to her origin, she eats her bread without any poverty. For everything that comes immediately from GOD, and all virtues that are in GOD, are precisely for that reason—because they are GOD and lack nothing—therefore also completely perfect; in such a way that one thus enjoys them without poverty or without any fault; and this not alone, but in Him everything is useful.

# The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter VIII.

10. And when you have eaten and are satisfied, you shall praise the **Lord** your **God** for the good land that He has given you.

<margin>(a) Chapter 32, verse 18.</margin>
11. Beware that you do not forget the **Lord** your **God**, so that you do not fail to keep His commandments, His judgments, and His statutes, which I command you today.

12. Lest, when you have eaten and are satisfied, and have built and inhabited beautiful houses,

<margin>(a) Psalm 144, verse 13.</margin>
13. And your herds and your sheep have multiplied, and your silver and gold have increased, and indeed all that you have has increased,

14. Your heart then be lifted up, and you forget the **Lord** your **God**, who led you out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage:

<margin>(a) Chapter 1, verse 19; Chapter 32, verse 10. Jeremiah 2, verse 6.</margin>
15. Who led you through the great and terrible wilderness, where there were fiery serpents and scorpions, and a drought where there was no water; who brought forth water for you out of the flint-hard rock:

v. 10. Experience alone can make this known. Therefore Moses says: when you have eaten—that is, when you have experienced it—then you will be filled with the fullness of **God** Himself, which fullness places the soul into a state of complete satisfaction. Then you will praise the **Lord** your **God** for the good land that He will have given you!

v. 11–14. Every danger that might be found in spiritual states, where souls find themselves full of spiritual riches, is that they can easily take some credit for it themselves and take some pleasure in it. Through this, they can easily forget their first captivity and lowliness. This is all they have to fear. This single sin <note>The author refers to pride or self-appropriation of divine grace.</note> cast the angel from heaven into hell; and this is also the only sin which can bring the soul out of **God** and cast it into hell. Therefore, Moses desires that if these people, having come so far, should be so unfaithful as to contemplate their own exaltation, they should also simultaneously remember their first captivity, from which they could never have escaped if **God** had not drawn them out through Himself and by the power of His supreme authority.

v. 15. He also wants them to remember that He alone was the one who led them through such a long and hideous wilderness full of fire-spitting serpents. For the devils are entirely fire, and they hunger for the souls found in the wilderness in order to destroy them. Throughout the entire way, they are surrounded by sins and by the rage of their enemies: how then could they have come out of there if **God** had not drawn them out? All the more so, since this wilderness was so dry that not a drop of other water was to be found there, except what **God** caused to come out of the hard rock. This unique water, which is found in such a vast wilderness, is the hardness and insensitivity of naked faith <term>Naked faith: A spiritual state where a person trusts God without any emotional comfort or intellectual proof.</term>, which does not allow the soul to think of such dangers, nor to know them as they truly are: for it is as unchangeable as the rock in defending itself against them. But this same water, which serves as support under such unavoidable dangers, is given only by **God**: because He alone does not simply rescue us from dangers and from all our enemies, but it is also **God** who gives the soul this appearing hardness, so that it might be neither terrified nor stung by the serpents.

<column-break/>

16. Who fed you with manna in the wilderness, which your fathers did not know: that He might humble you and that He might test you, so that He might do you good in your latter end.

17. An... <note>text truncated</note>

All of this actually proceeds in exactly this order. After **God** has led the soul through all the devils, and through misery and sin, as well as through all its enemies—which are represented by these poisonous animals—and while she is during such a time stripped of all help, of sensible, comprehensible, and recognized graces, as well as of all refreshment and nourishment, and has nothing else for her help but the water of His hardness and insensitivity, which finally seems to her to be rejection and impenitence: then He also gives her the manna. This is a secret and hidden food which she does not recognize, but through which **God** prevents her from being able to perish entirely.

After all such trials, **God** comes again and grieves this soul, making His hand heavy upon her. Oh, what a terrifying grief that is! It is entirely beyond everything that can be said of it. That **God** Himself <margin>(a) Job 13, verse 25.</margin> wishes to strive against a leaf that the wind blows away; oh, this cannot be expressed. Often this all-too-bold leaf thinks it wants to do well, not realizing that it is He Himself who is the strong armed one, and it wants to defend itself. Such resistance, however, serves no purpose other than to bring unspeakable pains upon its own neck. Finally, this poor leaf must bend, yield, fall to the earth, and be consumed by **God** Himself. All other trials that preceded were not to be compared to this one; because **God**, who supported the soul in an unknown and incomprehensible way, drove back the burning stings of the devils and the stings and bites of sin; and since He makes such souls very hard and insensitive, all this only touched the skin a little; or if it was much, it only frightened a little, without being able to inflict any real harm. But this other trial cannot come from nature nor from the devil: it must be **God** Himself who makes this rock bend like a leaf without mercy, throws it into a heap, and finally completely annihilates and consumes it. This is the work of **God** alone. Serpents can certainly cause death through their poisonous bites; but **God** alone has the power to annihilate the soul in His wide bosom, to consume and destroy it, and finally to transform it into Himself.

Now, because this work is the sweetest and the strongest, it is also the least to be felt; because it takes place neither in the inner senses nor in the powers, but in the very deepest center and highest part of the soul. **God** alone can work such things. And He does this precisely when He lets the center suffer, as He cleanses it from the ground up of all self-interest and pretense, losing it into Himself through annihilation: which makes it so that this work, although it is the most imperceptible of all, is nevertheless the hardest of all.

But after **God** visits the soul in this way, burdens her with her own weight, and has thereby previously annihilated and consumed her, He finally comforts her. And this signifies that He does not comfort her until she is in her "end," which is **God** Himself. And when the soul has arrived there, she recognizes that what she previously held to be a strict justice was actually a great mercy.

**To do you good in your latter end)** Job is a beautiful example of this "end" of **God**. Thus, the end of the ways of **God** is always in blessing, just as was the end of poor Lazarus. Luke 16, verse 22.

# Chapter VIII. The Fifth Book of Moses <note>Deuteronomy</note>

17. And if you should say in your heart: My power and the strength of my hand has brought me this wealth: <margin>Judges 7:2</margin>

18. But you shall remember the LORD your God; for it is he who has given you power to get wealth: that he might confirm his covenant which he swore to your fathers, as it is this day.

<note>Commentary on Chapter 8</note>

There is nothing in the Scriptures which does not express and confirm this. It happens, says the text, so that you may not attribute any power to yourselves—that God thus humbles you to nothing—and so that you cannot say: "My hand has made all of this." That is to say: "I have brought about all this great good through my labor, effort, and through my faithfulness."

Instead, you should rather remember that all power is in God, and conversely, all weakness is in you, and that he alone could have performed this great work. Such a soul is also far from attributing anything to itself: because God, for this reason, encloses such great graces in **earthen (a) vessels** <note>original: "irdene Gefässe"; a reference to 2 Corinthians 4:7, suggesting that God's power is best displayed through human fragility.</note>, so that the strength may be attributed to him and not to man. For when man becomes aware of his own earthliness and insignificance, he can claim nothing for himself.

This is very carefully impressed upon the believers, not only here but also in the following chapter: that they should by no means attribute the overcoming of their enemies, or the good things they enjoy, to their own strength and merit. Rather, they should always be mindful of their corrupt nature, and how they have so often offended God from their youth onward that he would have had good reason to reject them. When God then protects them in grace and shows them much good, they should remember that he has done so for the sake of **Christ** <note>original: "Christi"</note>, as the promised **Seed of Abraham** <note>The "Seed of Abraham" refers to the biblical promise that all nations would be blessed through Abraham's descendants, interpreted here as pointing toward Jesus.</note>, in whom all nations—and thus they as well—should be blessed. Thus, because they have accepted Christ, they become partakers of such protection and such benefits; they must therefore acknowledge this thankfully, love Christ all the more heartily, and strive to obey him.
<margin>(a) 2 Corinthians 4:7.</margin>

---

### The IX. Chapter.

->The expulsion of the mighty nations, and the idolatry with the calf.<-

1. Hear, O Israel! You shall go over the Jordan today, that you may enter in to possess nations greater and stronger than yourself, great cities fenced up to heaven;

<note>Commentary on Chapter 9, Verse 1</note>

(Note that this little word <term>today</term> <note>original: "heute"</note>, according to biblical usage, does not exactly mean the present day—whether divided by nature or art, astronomically or civilly, of 12 or 24 hours, starting from morning or evening. Rather, it simply means the present or beginning time; it is as much as to say "now" or "soon." For the people did not cross the Jordan then, nor did they intend to cross it that same day. Even if we assume that Moses spoke these words the day before his death—though it does not appear so at all—there would still have been 30 days passing afterward in which the people mourned his death in the plains of the Moabites. After that, spies were sent out from Shittim, who, after they had gone to Jericho and come back again, hid themselves for 3 days in the mountains, and only then came back to Joshua. But after 3 days, the officers told the people that they should go over the Jordan tomorrow. If we therefore count the days, we find that Moses spoke these words at least 40 days before the passage through the Jordan; which accordingly will have this meaning: "It is now at hand that you go over the Jordan." For you have no further war to wage beforehand, and no enemy to subdue, before you go over the Jordan.

<sig>Xxxx 2</sig>

<column-break/>

19. And it shall be, if you do at all forget the LORD your God, and walk after other gods, and serve them, and worship them; I testify against you today that you shall surely perish.

20. As the nations which the LORD destroys before your face, so shall you perish; because you would not be obedient unto the voice of the LORD your God.

<note>Commentary on Verse 19-20</note>

Whoever serves other gods forgets God. This is what the Savior means with the words: *No one can serve two masters.* If you serve earthly things in your mind and weigh down your heart with them, you forget God and gather perishable things, which push out the memory of God through useless thoughts and talk.

Just as the forgetting of God and disobedience toward the voice of the Lord amount to the same thing, so also the reward and the fruit that spring from it are one and the same, and "perishing" is testified here twice.

This follows naturally from one another. For that is our life, if we obey God and his voice of wisdom; and where this is lacking, conversely, life escapes us: and what can follow from this but death and destruction?

Because corrupted Christendom has also shared in this forgetfulness of the Savior’s precious commandments, and follows the god of this world in all lusts of the flesh, violent oppression of neighbors, and all kinds of injustice; therefore, because of this disobedience, it will also be struck with the curse, and thus the prophets will be fulfilled who announced this end to her, which was also the end of their prophecy.
<margin>Malachi 4:6.</margin>

But this passage through the Jordan signifies the departure of the soul out of itself, in order to be taken up into God. It must pass through its enemies: see verse 3. But God goes before like a consuming fire, to consume and destroy all its [the soul's] own powers.

# The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter IX.

4. You shall not say in your heart, once the LORD your God has cast them out from before your face: "The LORD has brought me in to possess this land because of my righteousness." For it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD drives them out from before you.
5. You do not go in to possess their land because of your righteousness or the uprightness of your heart; rather, it is because of the wickedness of these nations that the LORD your God drives them out from before you, and so that He may fulfill the word which the LORD swore to your fathers, to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
6. Know then, that the LORD your God does not give you this good land to possess because of your righteousness; for you are a stiff-necked people.
7. Remember, and do not forget, how you provoked the LORD your God to wrath in the wilderness. From the day you departed out of the land of Egypt until you came to this place, you have been rebellious against the LORD.

---

*v. 4. The thought most offensive to God within the soul is when it believes or imagines that God has performed such great miracles for the sake of its own innocence and faithfulness, and that others, by contrast, are excluded because of their sins. Alas! God does not regard our own righteousness at all as a reason to show us such great mercy! Rather, His purpose is to destroy our self-righteousness. The soul, however, must remain steadfast without contemplating itself: it must see everything in the power of God and nothing in itself, without investigating anything else. For all self-righteousness must be destroyed before one can arrive there. Thus, we certainly do not arrive through our own righteousness; indeed, God annihilates our own righteousness within us for no other reason than so that we might not think it was what allowed us to enter into God.*

*v. 5. Because of—and so that) Thus God punishes the godless because of their sin, but He does good to the pious for the sake of Christ, and He bears them with great patience in their weaknesses, though not in reigning sins. See Ephesians 1:3 and Luke 22:31–32.*

*v. 6. It seems as if Moses, through all these repetitions, cannot make it understood enough that no work, no sincerity, and no self-righteousness can bring about such a great good. For if any thing could earn such a thing, it would most likely happen through sincerity and piety. But even this must perish; God cannot be possessed by any single good or means other than through Himself, as He is in Himself.* <note>The commentator is emphasizing a mystical point: that even "goodness" can become an idol if we think it gives us a claim on God.</note>

*v. 7. Remember) your previous transgressions—and you too, who read this, for your own improvement—lest the Lord remember your sins in the fury of His wrath!*

<column-break/>

8. Also at Horeb <note>Another name for Mount Sinai.</note> you provoked the LORD so greatly that the LORD was angry enough with you to have destroyed you.
9. When I had gone up the mountain to receive the stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant which the LORD made with you, then I stayed on the mountain forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water.
10. And the LORD gave me the two stone tablets written with the finger of God; and on them were written all the words which the LORD spoke with you on the mountain out of the midst of the fire on the day of the assembly.
11. And it came to pass at the end of forty days and forty nights, that the LORD gave me the two stone tablets, the tablets of the covenant;
12. And the LORD said to me: "Arise, go down quickly from here! For your people, whom you brought out of Egypt, have corrupted themselves; they have quickly turned aside from the way which I commanded them; they have made themselves a molten image." <note>A reference to the Golden Calf.</note>
13. Furthermore, the LORD spoke to me, saying: "I have seen this people, and behold, it is a stiff-necked people."
14. "Let me alone, that I may destroy them and blot out their name from under heaven; and I will make of you a nation mightier and greater than they."

---

*Thus Moses sets before them the entire register of all the sins which they committed during this long journey in the wilderness.*

<margin>(a)</margin> *O Wisdom! O depth of the Word of God! The simple reality of our sins and our unfaithfulness should rightly convince us that He did not choose us for this inner state <note>original: "inneren Stand"; refers to a level of spiritual maturity or mystical union.</note>, and for the purity of His love, because of our worthiness. This is all the more true since we—even after He has shone upon us with His most living enlightenments and graced us with the secret ray <note>original: "geheimen Stral"; a common mystical metaphor for direct divine inspiration.</note>—have not ceased to be ungrateful and rebellious toward Him. And so God acts before He leads the soul into Himself: He shows it, piece by piece, all its unfaithfulness and misdeeds, which then bows the soul down to the earth and into the abyss.*

### Chapter IX. The Fifth Book of Moses.

15. And as I turned and came down from the mountain (and the mountain burned with fire), and had the two tablets of the covenant in my two hands:
16. Then I looked, and behold, you had sinned against the LORD your God; you had made yourselves a cast calf; you had turned aside quickly from the way which the LORD had commanded you.
17. Then I took hold of the two tablets and threw them out of my two hands, and broke them before your eyes.
18. And I threw myself down before the face of the LORD, as at first, for forty days and forty nights; I ate no bread and drank no water <note>original: "aß kein Brod und tranck kein Wasser"</note> because of all your sins which you had committed, in that you did evil in the eyes of the LORD to provoke Him to anger.
<gloss>(a) Matthew 4:2 <note>A cross-reference to the forty-day fast of Jesus in the wilderness.</note></gloss>
19. For I was afraid of the anger and the wrath with which the LORD was so very angry with you, to destroy you. But the LORD heard me at that time as well.

---

Moses reproaches them for the great sin of idolatry with the calf, with which they had so greatly angered God that He wished to destroy them entirely, had Moses not averted this through his intercession. He pleaded before God for forty days and forty nights a second time (Exodus 34), after he had previously spent the same amount of time receiving the Law concerning the Tabernacle <note>term: "Stiffts-Hütte" (Tabernacle) — the portable earthly dwelling place of God used by the Israelites.</note> (Exodus 24:18).

In the same way, the great idolatry which the Church of the New Testament has practiced with wood and stone in their temples, with men in their arrogated power, and with human ordinances, will be seen, recognized, and confessed in the light of God during the second full outpouring of the Holy Spirit. This will be done to guard against such things more carefully and to maintain the pure and simple service in spirit and in truth. See the prophecy regarding this in Zephaniah 3:9 and Zechariah 14:9. This will then bring forth true unity, whereas the former practices brought about nothing but divisions.

**v. 16. (Cast calf)** The Israelites surely knew that the calf was not God. However, it did not help them nor excuse them that they wished to worship and honor the God of Israel under such a visible image. Otherwise, the divine zeal in both Moses and God Himself would not have been so greatly incensed. What then should the excuses and "painted colors" of others be worth, with which they try to justify their service to images, as if they were not honoring the wood or the image itself, but rather what is represented by the image?

**v. 17. (threw them down and broke them)** This was to show that the people were not worthy of the covenant with God, from which they had detached themselves through this very sin.

**v. 19. (The LORD heard me at that time as well)** There are some decrees in God which He has absolutely determined to carry out and which cannot be stayed when their appointed time comes. Thus it is said, for example, that God would not hear or allow His punishment to be stayed even if Noah, Job, and Daniel stood before Him. Others, however, are of such a nature that they can still be stayed if the final deadline has not yet been fixed.

<column-break/>

20. The LORD was also very angry with Aaron, intending to destroy him; but I prayed for Aaron at that same time as well.
21. But as for your sin which you had committed with the calf, I took it and burned it with fire, and crushed it and ground it well until it became fine dust, and I threw its dust into the brook that flows down from the mountain.
22. Also at Taberah, and at Massah, and at the Graves of Craving <note>term: "Lustgräber" (Kibroth-hattaavah) — literally "Graves of Lust/Longing," where the Israelites were buried after craving meat and being struck by a plague.</note> you greatly angered the LORD.
23. And when the LORD sent you from Kadesh Barnea and said: "Go up and take possession of the land which I have given you," you were disobedient to the mouth of the LORD your God, and you did not believe Him, and did not obey His voice.
24. You have been rebellious against the LORD from the day that I first knew you.
25. Then I threw myself down before the face of the LORD for the forty days and forty nights during which I lay prostrate; for the LORD had spoken of destroying you.
26. And...

---

**v. 20. (Concerning Aaron)** Who is by no means to be excused.
**(To destroy him)** From this and various other circumstances, it can be seen that Moses includes more details here than are contained in the second book (Exodus).

**v. 21. (Burned / crushed and ground it)** By means of a special science dwelling within him. <note>The author suggests Moses possessed extraordinary or even alchemical knowledge to be able to burn and pulverize gold into dust.</note>

**v. 22. etc.** Here their remaining grumbling and constant disobedience are once again held up to them. Moses did not flatter them at all, but before his departure, he sharply rebuked the great perversity of their hearts one last time, to see if they and their descendants might truly take it to heart. He wanted them to recognize their own stubbornness, and how God—only for the sake of His covenant with their beloved fathers—had preserved them as His people and inheritance, bearing them with great patience despite their hardness and godless nature.

**v. 23. (You did not believe)** This unbelief manifests most strongly when one is exhorted to progress from Kadesh Barnea (or the weak state of spiritual childhood) into a state of true growth. From this comes the "language of Old Adam" <note>An expression referring to the fallen, sinful nature of humanity that seeks excuses for its failings.</note> which says: "We cannot be as pure as angels," or "There is nothing perfect in this world," etc.

### The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter IX.

26. And I prayed to the LORD and said: Lord, LORD, do not destroy your people and your inheritance, which you have redeemed through your majesty, and which you have led out of Egypt with a strong hand!

27. Remember your servants—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob! Do not look upon the stubbornness <note>original: "Härtigkeit" (hardness/stubbornness)</note> of this people, nor their godlessness, nor their sin!

<note>Bottom notes left column</note>
**A wooden ark — of Shittim-wood)** From this passage, some Hebrew scholars conclude, not without reason, that this was a different ark than the Ark of the Covenant. They suggest Moses made this one of plain wood and did not overlay it with gold. In it, he supposedly placed and preserved both the first broken tablets and the second tablets of the Law until the beautiful gold-plated ark, which Bezaleel made, was finished. Then, he supposedly took the whole tablets out of his wooden ark and placed them in the precious one; however, he left the broken pieces in the wooden ark he had made himself. These were later placed in the upper chamber of the Temple and kept under the Lord's protection alongside other items and most pieces of the Tabernacle <note>term: "Stiffts-Hütte" (Tabernacle) — the portable sanctuary of the Israelites.</note> (a).

**Tablets like the first)** The Law of God is twofold or double, and the mountain upon which it is received is also twofold: Therefore it must be ascended a second time, and in this second ascent Moses mirrors the person of Christ. The Ten Commandments in the letter alone belong to the child and those who are still immature, for the Law is weak and frail through the infirmity of the flesh. Romans 8:3. This weak Law comes from Mount Sinai. But the Law is also spiritual: Romans 7:14, and that comes from Mount Zion. Namely, it says...
