### Chapter X. The Fifth Book of Moses.

6. And the children of Israel journeyed from Beeroth <margin>(a) Josh. 9:17, 18:25, 2 Sam. 4:2, 8:8.</margin> of the Bene-Jaakan to Mosera: there Aaron died and was buried; and Eleazar his son served in the priest's office in his place.

7. From there they journeyed to Gudgodah; and from Gudgodah to Jotbathah <margin>(a) Num. 33:33.</margin>, a land of water brooks.

8. At that same time, the **LORD** set apart the tribe of Levi to carry the Ark of the Covenant of the **LORD**, to stand before the face of the **LORD** to minister to Him, and to bless in His name unto this day. <margin>Num. 3 & 4 and 8.</margin>

---

**v. 6. To Mosera)** This name must signify the same place as Hor in Numbers 20:28 and 33:38, and this location must have been situated near Mount Hor, upon which Moses says in the 4th Book, Chapter 33:38, that Aaron died at the command of the **LORD**.

**v. 7. Now, when a different journey is reported here and there, it must be explained thus:** that in the Wilderness of Paran they did not travel a straight path toward the land of Canaan, but rather wandered up and down, as can be seen in the travel descriptions of the children of Israel through the desert. Thus, in the 4th Book [Numbers], Chapter 33, only the general main locations are reported where they arrived one after another; however, when they returned to previous locations in between, such instances are omitted there. The Spirit of **GOD** never contradicts itself: whatever appears to be different, one must strive to reconcile as much as possible and pray for light from above. Where such understanding is not obtained, our patience and fairness are tested, so that we do not dwell on such minor circumstances but instead look upon the main work for which the Scripture was given to us.
**A land where there were water brooks)** This represents the fresh, powerful, and overflowing refreshments—and the fertility associated with them—which tend to follow in Jotbathah after Gudgodah (or Hor-Hagidgad), following the earnest circumcision of the heart and the zeal to press into the narrow way of deep self-denial. For:
**The true and living comfort of the Holy Spirit flows out from the constant mortification of our own will.** And:
**There one experiences that the water brooks in that land were but an impression of the stream** whose outlets make the City of **God** joyful. Psalm 46:4. This is none other than the **Holy Spirit**, who pours divine joy and supernatural refreshment into the whole Church. When the saints partake in this, it becomes their true Jotbathah and a concise summary of all good things, according to the meaning of the word and the words of the Savior in Matthew 7:11 and Luke 11:13.

**v. 8. At that same time)** After receiving fresh water and following the death of Aaron.
**The LORD set apart)** A separation and setting-apart is required before one can serve the **LORD**.
**The tribe of Levi)** Every word in this verse is full of mystery. Are these not those redeemed from the earth, whom the **Lord JESUS** chose for Himself out of the world, that they might be priests of **GOD** before Him and His Father? This is precisely that little flock which the **Lord JESUS** separates and sets apart for Himself out of all people: the chosen generation, the royal priesthood, the holy nation, the people for His possession. 1 Pet. 2:9, according to the pattern of Exodus 19:5–6. Blessed is he who has this testimony within himself, or even just an earnest will to be such a chosen one!
**To stand before the face of the LORD)** As those joined to **GOD**, just as the name "Levi" <note>The Hebrew name Levi implies "joined" or "attached."</note> signifies.
**To minister to Him)** Unmoved and undistracted. 1 Cor. 7:35.
**Unto this day)** In the past, present, and future time.

<column-break/>

9. Therefore Levi had no part or inheritance with his brothers: the **LORD** Himself is his inheritance, just as the **LORD** your **GOD** spoke to him. <margin>Josh. 13:14, 33; Ezek. 44:28.</margin>

10. **I** stood upon the mountain as in the first days, forty days and forty nights: and the **LORD** heard me at that time also; the **LORD** would not destroy you.

11. And the **LORD** said to me: Arise and go on the journey before the people, that they may enter and possess the land as an inheritance, which I swore to their fathers to give them.

<meta>catchword: 12. And</meta>

---

**v. 9. Levi no part with his brothers)** Namely, that they should not receive an equal share with other tribes in the distribution of the land, but rather let the others divide the land they entered among themselves, while the Levites should be content with their specific cities and suburbs, and whatever else would be given to them.
Oh, what a depth of wisdom lies hidden here! **God** indeed wishes all people to be helped; but most remain stuck to earthly things—that is their portion in this life. Ps. 17:14.
Where among thousands is there one of whom it can truly be said:
**The LORD Himself is his inheritance)** It is not enough to choose such funeral texts for oneself, wherein this is claimed without foundation. (a) If you wish to be chosen by **God**, you must also choose Him as your portion, and rightly select Him out of all things offered to you, while it is still called "Today."
**To be the inheritance of GOD** is to have surrendered oneself to Him and to be led by Him alone, just as the yielded <note>original: "gelassene" - a term for spiritual surrender/releasement</note> people do. But that **GOD** should be our inheritance cannot happen until the soul is completely annihilated <term>annihilated <note>In mystical theology, "annihilation" (vernichtiget) refers to the total emptying of the self-will so that God may act through the person.</note></term>. For this reason, those souls who are fully established and annihilated have no part in the tangible and comprehensible gifts of others; for **GOD** alone is their part and their inheritance. Just as the great <term>Mystic <note>original: "Mysticus"</note></term> experienced this pattern, when he could say in truth (a): O **God**, you are the **GOD** of my heart and my eternal inheritance! And this is exactly what the tribe of Levi—namely, the priestly generation of the annihilated ones—has specially experienced. <margin>(a) Ps. 73:26.</margin>

**v. 10. As in the first days, 40)** From which some conclude there were three periods of forty days and nights: once upon receiving the first tablets; the second time during the reconciliation of the people regarding the golden calf; the third time during the delivery of the fresh tablets with the writing. Others, however, consider this merely a repetition of the first time; and Hugo <term>reasons <note>Latin: "ratiociniret" — to reckon or calculate logically.</note></term> that from the 3rd of June, when Moses first climbed the mountain, until the 9th of September, when he descended for the last time, there are not enough days to account for three full periods of forty.

**v. 11. Go before the people)** Herewith he was appointed anew as the leader of the people, and he was assured that his intercession for them had been heard in the forgiveness of their sins.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Deuteronomy Chapter 10. Having previously discussed the physical journey of the Israelites and the appointment of the Levites, the text now pivots to the core spiritual demands God places upon His people—fearing, loving, and serving Him—and provides a deep theological reflection on the nature of divine "requests" versus "commands."</meta>

### The Fifth Book of Moses, Chapter X.

12. And now, Israel, what does the **LORD** your **GOD** require of you? but that you fear the **LORD** your **GOD**, that you walk in all His ways, and love Him, and serve the **LORD** your **GOD** with all your heart and with all your soul; <margin>Chapter 6:5.</margin>

13. That you keep the commandments of the **LORD**, and His statutes,

**v. 12. And)** Almost all the promises and benefits of **GOD** are gathered here to conclude what Israel’s obedience, duty, and obligation should be.
**what does the LORD require of you?)** Or perhaps even, according to the most literal meaning of the Hebrew word; what does the **LORD** *beg* of you? <note>original: "was bittet der HErr von dir?" – The commentator is highlighting the Hebrew root *sha'al*, which can mean to ask, enquire, or even beg/borrow.</note> See 1 Samuel 1:17, 20, 27; 12:13; Job 6:8; Psalm 20:6. Indeed, it signifies even the lowest degree of asking, which is begging; as seen in Proverbs 20:4.
O, what wonderful condescension of the Most High **GOD**, who begs of His creature that which He has the perfect right and power to command! Thus, the highest degree of Majesty and the lowest degree of humility may well stand together: and in this way, it may be neither detrimental nor unseemly for any ruler to follow the great **GOD** in this; rather, it is the surest way to obtain something from their subjects.
However, the "requests" of kings are an explanation of their commands: and what the **LORD** here asks almost as if pleading, Moses commands in the following verse.
**fear the LORD)** The fear of the **LORD** is His first requirement, because reverent fear belongs to His sovereign government and highest majesty. Malachi 1:6. It is like the door and entrance into the palace of the Great King, and is therefore called the beginning of divine wisdom. Psalm 111:10; Proverbs 1:7.
**In all His ways)** There are indeed many, but they may be condensed into three: namely, a way of the commandments of **GOD** (Psalm 119:1); a way of faith or of the Gospel, which is Christ (John 14:6); and a way of love (1 Corinthians 12:31, 13:1).
There are surely many who would gladly walk in one or another of **GOD's** ways that seems the most comfortable and easiest to them; but not in *all*. The way of the Law is most often abandoned. For it is considered neither necessary nor, moreover, possible. Therefore, people prefer to choose the path called the Gospel, without considering that this very Gospel presents such a narrow way to life: so that in the way of the Gospel, rather more than less obedience is required than in the way of the Law; (See Matthew 5:17-20, 48.) only that the **LORD** also provides more grace and strength there to run the way of His commandments.
**And love Him)** The service of love does not abolish the service of fear. But a time comes when the service of love casts out fear, which has torment. 1 John 4:18.
**Serve the LORD)** in the aforementioned fear and love. The **LORD** holds these two services so high that He has allowed Himself to be named, and has named Himself, after them. Genesis 31:29, 42, 54; Psalm 76:11; 1 John 4:8, 16. <note>The author likely refers to God being called "The Fear of Isaac" and "Love" itself.</note>
But how is **GOD** served by us? Love speaks: one does it a great service if everyone turns to it, thinks of it, and enjoys it: simply so that it may do us good, give, help, and pour itself out and communicate itself. How the **LORD** does love the people!
**v. 13. That you keep the commandments of the LORD)** Obedience to all the commandments of **GOD** flows from the two aforementioned primal sources of fear and love.

<column-break/>

which I command you today, for your good.

14. Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens, the earth and all that is therein, are the **LORD's** your **GOD's**.

15. Yet the **LORD** had a delight only in your fathers, that He loved them, and He chose their seed after them, namely you, out of all peoples, as it is this day.

**v. 13. Which I command you)** Commands are proper to the Law; requests and entreaties are proper to the Gospel. <note>original: "Befehle sind dem Gesetze eigen/ Bitten und Flehen dem Evangelio" – referencing 2 Corinthians 5:20.</note> The **LORD** leaves no means untried: He begs, and Moses commands.
But why this? Answer: Our **GOD** is in Himself pure love and goodness: therefore He begs us for our duty, so that His goodness may lead us to repentance. Romans 2:4. But because He knows our heart well, how perverse it is, and how difficult it is for it to be softened and moved by love, goodness, and mercy—indeed, it is more likely to be hardened—and thus severity, commandments, and threats are most suitable; therefore it happens that our duties are also required more imperiously, and their transgressions are simultaneously burdened with appropriately varied penal ordinances. Sin, injustice, and stubbornness cause severity and sharpness, even grimness, wrath, and displeasure; although these are not innate characteristics of our **GOD**. Just as, in such matters, the earthly authorities are often feared more than **GOD** Himself.
Thus **GOD** performs the acts of grace by Himself, but the acts of severity through His servant. He softens the commands of Moses through His own friendly begging: and so that His begging and goodness might not fail to have a good effect, they are made somewhat sharper through Moses’ commands.
But the **LORD** knows well what man should do when He seeks him, to fear Him, to walk in His ways, to love Him, to serve Him, and to keep His commandments and statutes. The **LORD** seeks no more, and requires no more, from us than we have the power and ability to do within us. He also has no personal aim in this, and certainly does not do it for His own benefit or advantage, but merely
**For your good)** Not that the **LORD** has need of you, or of what is yours.
The purpose of the entire constitution is directed toward this "good" of Israel. Thus, obedience to the commandments of **GOD** is contained within true self-love; and just as at the beginning of the Christian religion there is self-denial—which is the denial of false self-love (Luke 9:23)—so also is the end of the same found in true self-love. And from this follows a command easier than this: Love yourself.
**v. 14. Behold, the heaven and the heaven of heavens are the LORD's)** By the "heaven," he understands, according to the secret sense, the sublime power united with **GOD**, and by the "heaven of all heavens" the center in which **GOD** dwells. Thus he says that the union has happened not only in those powers, and that they belong to **GOD**, but that the center point itself, which is the heaven of all powers, belongs to Him through the essential union. For just as the spirit of man can quite fittingly be called "heaven" itself, so too can the highest part of the spirit be called "the heaven of all heavens": and to express all this with the little word "behold" indicates that this state has already arrived.
**v. 15. Only -- chose their seed)** Which is Christ **JESUS**, Hebrews 2:16, the only Election and the chosen Seed, in whom both the election and the love and grace of **GOD** are solely concluded, as well as attained and offered.
Those who now live in this divine Seed, and let it rule in them; they have seized the choice of grace. By virtue of this, those who are according to the flesh are not the seed that **GOD** chooses, but those according to the spirit are counted as the seed. Romans 9:8.
This, however, does not abolish the literal sense, according to which the seed here is interpreted as Israel according to the flesh, as it further says:
**Namely you, out of all peoples)** For what did they represent by this other than the image of the true Israel, or the assembly of the firstborn, whom **GOD** much more wished to choose for Himself out of all nations and the entire human race in the fullness of time?

# Chapter XI.

->The perception of God's power, the description of Canaan, and the promise of blessing.<-

Therefore you shall love the LORD your God, that you may keep His charge, and His statutes, and His judgments, and His commandments always.

2. And know today! For it does not concern your children, who have not experienced nor seen the chastisement of the LORD your God, His majesty, His strong hand, and His outstretched arm;

3. And His signs and His works, which He did in the midst of Egypt, against Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and against all his land;

4. And what He did to the power of the Egyptians, to their horses and their chariots, when He caused the waters of the Reed Sea <note>original: "Schilffmeers" — traditionally translated as the Red Sea, though literally 'Sea of Reeds'</note> to overflow their faces as they pursued after you, and the LORD destroyed them even to this day;

5. And what He did to you in the wilderness, until you came to this place;

6. And what He did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben; how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them with their households and their tents, and everything that had existence that followed them in the midst of all Israel.

7. For your eyes are the ones that have seen all the great work of the LORD which He has done.

---

<margin>v. 1.</margin> Love is set as the source of obedience, because God requires a voluntary and not a forced, slavish service, wherein one performs His righteous, holy, and entirely loving commands with heartfelt joy and love, like an obedient, pious child.

<margin>v. 2-7.</margin> The LORD must prove the power of His chastising justice because people do not want to recognize omnipotence in His benefits, which indeed flow just as much from His power, but are accepted by people as if by chance—as if it must be that the earth yields its capacity—and then they fail to praise God appropriately for it. Here God proves His judgments not only upon the heathens, whom He punishes because of their godlessness (like the Egyptians because of their unmercifulness toward the children of Israel), but also particularly upon His own people, whom He punishes all the more harshly for their disobedience because they received more grace than the others. Just as the swallowing up of Dathan’s company with their families was almost more terrifying than the drowning of the Egyptians in the sea. Yes, even toward His friends and favorites among His people, He does not leave their transgressions and missteps, or slips, or haste, unrequited; as is seen with Aaron and Moses in Chapter 9:20 and 4:21, 22.

<column-break/>

8. Therefore you shall keep this whole commandment that I command you today, so that you may be strengthened and enter in and take possession of the land which you are crossing over to inherit.

9. And so that you may prolong your days in the land which the LORD swore to your fathers to give to them and to their seed, a land that flows with milk and honey. (a)
<margin>(a) Eph. 6:3.</margin>

10. For the land where you go to possess it is not like the land of Egypt from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and had to water it by your foot <note>original: "durch deinen Gang" — referring to the human labor required for irrigation in Egypt, such as foot-powered water wheels</note> like a vegetable garden.

11. But the land where you cross over to possess it is a land with mountains and valleys, which receives water from the rain of heaven.
12.

---

<margin>v. 8. 9.</margin> (Shall keep the commandments — that you may prolong your days). Here we see the true means, the true Philosopher's Stone <term>Philosopher's Stone: "Stein der Weisen" — an alchemist's term for the ultimate secret, used here as a metaphor for the divine key to a long and blessed life</term> by which one may preserve oneself long in life. Man loves to live long and employs everything to achieve such a goal: only this means, prescribed elsewhere until now, is always passed by, as if it were not true or proven <note>original: "probatum"</note>, or as if it required too complex a source, which yet may be shared as easily by the poor as the rich.

<margin>v. 10.</margin> Just as one land enjoys a greater goodness and fertility from God than another, such that He exercises a special oversight and care over the good lands, while the others must be worked with great and bitter toil from which one can only barely sustain oneself; so it is also with the land of the heart. One heart is of a softer and kinder nature than another, upon which the LORD also particularly has His eye and fills it with His blessing: Ps. 33:18-19, 34:16. The other, however, is of a rough and wild nature and must then be worked with all the more labor. And when that labor is in vain, so that such a heart brings forth nothing but thorns and thistles of unfaithfulness and falsehood, then such hearts are also unfit for anything good and near to the curse, destined to go into the hellish fire. Heb. 6:4–8.
(Not like the land of Egypt) The difference between Egypt and the promised land is wonderful. The former, which represents the manifold state <note>original: "vermanchfältigten Stand" — an allegorical reference to the soul's fragmented state in worldly bondage</note>, had to be watered like a garden: and this watering is nothing but human effort, without which this land would bear nothing. The promised land, however, is not so.

<margin>v. 11.</margin> There are in that same land sublime souls like mountains; others are fruitful and pleasant like the valleys; on which, however, both the one and the other are very receptive, and they do not prepare themselves by watering it; rather they expect rain from heaven. For they are not moistened with earthly water, but with heavenly.

v. 12. God also keeps constant watch over this land and does not forsake it for a single moment: His eyes are directed toward it from beginning to end, without ceasing for a moment to look upon it. 
O how happy is the soul that stands in the cessation of all its own labor and in the expectation of the heavenly rain! Such a soul will never be deceived in its hope. For God lets no moment pass by in which He is not directed toward it with the care of His providence: He watches for the soul while it rests. Is not the work of a God then to be preferred to the work of the creature? Yieldedness <note>original: "Gelaſſenheit" — a key term in German mysticism referring to a state of letting go of self-will and surrendering to God's action</note>, yes, yieldedness, and letting God work, is what is necessary!

v. 13. All graces and all commandments that God gives us aim only at this: to let Himself be loved by our whole heart, because of the jealousy which He has for this heart, which He wants to have for Himself alone. He desires nothing else but love. O what a rare thing you are, you pure love! You cost all the effort and labor of a God: You cost all the suffering and all the terrifying stripping-away of the creature! O you pure love, where are you to be found? In God alone. You cannot even be in the soul unless God alone is within it. You are in Him, you come from Him, and you go back into Him. But outside of Him Himself—as the beginning, center point, and end of this love—nothing but impurity is to be found.

v. 15. *Grass for your cattle*) The preceding nourishment is for the inner man, but this is for the outer, animal-like man: to each according to his necessity.

**23.** Then the LORD will drive out all these nations before you, so that you shall inherit nations greater and stronger than yourselves. Psalm 2:8.

v. 18. *Lay my words in your heart and in your soul*) Through the Fall, we have a darkened heart; therefore, we have a great need for the pure and holy commandment of the Lord, which is a lamp and a light. Proverbs 6:23. Thus, the law of the Lord is also perfect for converting or restoring the soul which has gone astray and lost itself! Psalm 19:7. These words bring with them the fear of God, which is pure (v. 9, 10) and therefore also cleanses the heart. These same words are fiery words (ch. 33:2, Jeremiah 23:29) and ignite the heart, scaring it out of spiritual sloth <term>Trägheit</term> <note>refers to "acedia" or spiritual apathy</note> and dejection, making it zealous for every good work. And just as the natural heart is placed in the middle of the body, so should these words be in the middle of the heart, to rule it with divine wisdom.

v. 20. *Write them on house and gates*) i.e., Teach them at home or in private, and publicly.

v. 22. Love stands here, as in v. 13, after obedience, to show that love is the source of obedience from which all other specific duties flow.

All commandments are also considered here reflectively as a single one, which one must keep whole and complete. Therefore James also says: "For whoever keeps the whole law and yet stumbles at one point is guilty of all," Chapter 2:10. So closely are they intertwined with one another. He who therefore loves God—which is the single commandment—will also walk in all His ways and constantly cling to Him in full trust.

# Chapter 11.

->The perception of God’s power / Description of Canaan / and the promise of blessing.<-

Therefore, you shall love the Lord your God, that you may keep his charge, his statutes, his judgments, and his commandments every day.

2. And know this day! For this does not concern your children, who have not experienced or seen the discipline of the Lord your God, his majesty, his mighty hand, and his outstretched arm;

3. And his signs and his works, which he performed in the midst of Egypt, against Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and against all his land;

4. And what he did to the power of the Egyptians, to their horses and their chariots, when he made the water of the Reed Sea <note>original: "Schilffmeers." Traditionally translated as the Red Sea, though "Sea of Reeds" is the literal meaning.</note> flow over their faces as they pursued you, and the Lord destroyed them unto this day;

5. And what he did for you in the wilderness, until you came to this place;

6. And what he did to Dathan and Abiram, the sons of Eliab, the son of Reuben; how the earth opened its mouth and swallowed them with their households and their tents, and everything that had life <note>literally "the essence" or "living substance"</note> and followed them in the midst of all Israel.

7. Rather, it is your eyes that have seen all the great work of the Lord which he has performed.

<margin>
v. 1. Love is established here as the source of obedience, because God desires a voluntary service rather than a forced, slave-like service; one should fulfill his righteous, holy, and entirely loving commands with heart-felt joy and love, just like an obedient, pious child.
</margin>

<margin>
v. 2–7. The Lord must demonstrate the power of his disciplining justice because people often refuse to recognize his omnipotence in his blessings—which flow just as much from his power but are accepted by people as if by chance. They act as if it is simply natural that the earth yields its bounty, and thus they fail to praise God appropriately. Therefore, God demonstrates his judgments not only upon the heathens, whom he punishes for their godlessness (like the Egyptians for their lack of mercy toward the children of Israel), but also specifically upon his own people. He punishes them all the more harshly for their disobedience because they received more grace than others. Indeed, the swallowing up of Dathan’s faction with their families was almost more terrifying than the drowning of the Egyptians in the sea. Yes, even among his friends and favorites within his people, he does not let transgressions, missteps, errors, or hastiness go unpunished; as can be seen with Aaron and Moses in Chapters 9:20 and 4:21, 22.
</margin>

<column-break/>

8. Therefore, you shall keep this whole commandment which I command you today, so that you may be strengthened and enter in and take possession of the land where you are crossing over to inherit it.

9. And so that you may prolong your days <gloss>(a) Ephesians 6:3.</gloss> in the land that the Lord swore to your fathers to give to them and to their offspring, a land flowing with milk and honey.

10. For the land where you are going to possess it is not like the land of Egypt, from which you came out, where you sowed your seed and had to water it by your foot <note>referring to foot-operated irrigation pumps or the labor of carrying water</note> like a vegetable garden.

11. But the land where you cross over to possess it is a land with mountains and valleys, which receives water from the rain of heaven.

<sig>12.</sig>

<margin>
v. 8. 9. (You shall keep the commandments — so that you may prolong your days) Here we see the right means, the true Philosopher’s Stone <note>original: "Stein der Weisen." A metaphor for the ultimate solution or secret to success.</note> by which one may preserve oneself in goodness for a long time. Man loves to live long and employs every effort to reach that goal; yet this prescribed means is always bypassed, as if it were not true or proven, or as if one could not achieve it—though it may be granted as easily to the poor as to the rich.
</margin>

<margin>
v. 10. Just as one land enjoys a greater goodness and fertility from God than another—such that one feels a special oversight and care over the "good" lands, while the others must be cultivated with great and bitter toil just to provide a meager living—so it is with the "land of the heart." One heart is of a softer and kinder nature than another; upon such a heart the Lord has his eye especially fixed, filling it with much blessing: Psalms 33:18, 19; 34:16. The other is of a rough and wild nature and must be worked with much more effort. And when that effort is in vain, so that such a heart brings forth nothing but the thorns and briars of sin and falsehood, then such "heart-plots" are unfit for anything good, near to a curse, and destined for hellfire. Hebrews 6:4–8.
</margin>

<margin>
(Not like the land of Egypt) The difference between Egypt and the Promised Land is wonderful. The former, which represents a state of manifold worldly distraction, may be watered like a garden; but this watering is nothing but human activity, without which this land would bear nothing. The Promised Land, however, is not like that.
</margin>

<margin>
v. 11. In that land, there are "lofty souls" who are like mountains; others are fruitful and pleasant like the valleys. In this, however, both the one and the other are very patient; they do not labor to irrigate the land themselves; they await the rain from heaven. For they are not moistened with earthly water, but with heavenly water.
</margin>

v. 12. God constantly pays attention to this land and never leaves it for a moment: his eyes are directed at it from beginning to end without ceasing for a moment to look upon it.

Is not then the work of a God to be preferred over the work of the creature? Serenity <note>original: "Gelassenheit" — a central concept in German mysticism meaning a spirit of surrender or letting go of self-will to allow God to act</note>, yes, serenity is necessary, and that one lets God work!

### The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XI.

24. Every place whereon the soles of your feet shall tread shall be yours (a): From the wilderness and Lebanon / from the river, the river Euphrates, even unto the western sea / shall your boundary be.
<margin>Exodus 23:31. (a) Joshua 1:3, 14:9.</margin>

<margin>Joshua 2:24.</margin>

<margin>Sirach 15:16.</margin>
27. The blessing / if you will obey the commandments of the Lord your God, which I command you today.
28. And the curse / if you will not obey the commandments of the Lord your God / and turn aside from the way which I command you today / to follow other gods / whom you do not know.

---

<margin>V. 24. 25.</margin> First, God promises and shows us the physical blessing <note>original: "leiblichen Segen"</note>, if we would fulfill our duties toward him, and how he wishes to suppress all enemies / and grant physical peace: because man, after the fall into sin, has become far too focused on the senses / so that he notices more that which strikes the external senses. And so God also comes with physical punishments, which man, because of this focus on his senses, notices and feels more readily. Believers, however, have more reason to look to the spiritual blessing / that God visits their hearts with the rain of the Holy Spirit / and they may bring forth many fruits of righteousness / and that their spiritual enemies / Satan / their lusts and desires / may be suppressed / and they may overcome all temptations from within and without in all their actions. Just as they then must fear nothing more / than when God withdraws his gracious countenance from them / and thus lets them fall into spiritual drought and fruitlessness regarding the blessing. See concerning this the emphatic complaints of David in Psalm 30:8, and how he then was accustomed to pray for the spiritual blessing of the gracious countenance of God in Psalm 80:4, 8, 20.

<margin>V. 26-28.</margin> Through sin, the will has become entirely dead / dead to the good / and only inclined toward the evil: which, however, is a death in sins and transgressions. Through grace in Christ, a life has been gifted back to man: which consists in the light / that Christ kindles in every man, John 1:4, 5, 9. whereby he can see the good and its pleasantness / and also perceive the path upon which one arrives at the enjoyment of the good. And therefore the good / the blessing, and the way to the same / is set before man / so that he might choose this from the free choice <note>original: "freyen Wahl"</note> regained through grace and actually lay hold of it. If he does that / and is faithful in the first beginning; then God gives him more and more grace. For whoever has, to him shall be given. If he is then further faithful / God confirms him in grace / and elects him; then he cannot fall again so that he would be entirely cast away / but he is strengthened in grace through the rebirth of the Holy Spirit and powerful influence / so that nothing may separate him from the love of God.

But evil and the curse are also set before him for this reason. If he allows himself to be swept away by his corrupted nature / which even the godly possess / though they fight against it and overcome it / to fulfill his lusts / and yet sees the good / either to despise it entirely / and thus extinguish the light / or to desire it so sluggishly / that thus the

<column-break/>

29. And it shall come to pass, when the Lord your God has brought you into the land where you are going to possess it as an inheritance; that you shall put the blessing upon Mount Gerizim / and the curse upon Mount Ebal.
30. Are they not on the other side of the Jordan, behind the way toward the sunset / in the land of the Canaanites who dwell in the flat field / over against Gilgal, beside the plain of Moreh?
31. For you shall go over the Jordan / that you may enter in to possess the land as an inheritance / which the Lord your God has given you / that you may possess it as an inheritance and dwell therein.
32. Take heed now / that you do all the statutes and the judgments which I set before you today.

---

If one considers it rightly / both God, the eternal Good / and Satan, stand before the heart of every man / and indeed both with a great attractive power. And from both, one must now necessarily select and recognize: And what one then chooses and favors / that one lets inside oneself through the door of the senses and desires / and unites oneself with the same in every way.

If a soul now willingly seeks the sole eternal Good; which it is capable of through the grace that precedes it / and not by its own strength; behold, then such a choice succeeds unto infinite blessing.

But whoever remains standing in his evil natural will / he also remains lying in his natural unrest and pain / and suffers the constant condemnation of his conscience / because he has all sufficient means and guidance before and with him / yet nevertheless did not want to apply and enjoy such; thus every man experiences the outflow and inflow from these two mountains constantly within himself.

Externally, these otherwise lay in the tribe of Ephraim opposite each other / and were more like two peaks or crests of one mountain / than two separate mountains. Between these peaks was a wide valley / where the city of Shechem <note>original: "Sichem"</note> lay.

These two mountains represent Mount Sinai / from which the Law was given / which brings only the curse and announces condemnation; Galatians 3:13, 2 Corinthians 3:9. and Mount Zion / over which Christ is anointed, Psalm 2:6. whose Law brings the blessing / and who to that end also began his sermon on a mountain with nothing but wishes of blessing / and thus announced the blessing. Matthew 5:1, 3.

These mountains were also in the region where God formerly appeared to Abraham twice, Genesis 12:6, 7; 18:1. as a sign that God also appeared twice / first at the Law / where this curse had to be proclaimed; because it was said: Cursed be anyone who does not remain in all things that are written in the book of the Law to do them! Deuteronomy 27:26. of which the Law of the Ten Commandments was, so to speak, the core: Afterward when Christ appeared in the flesh. See further concerning these mountains, Deuteronomy 27:12, 13.

evil gains the upper hand; then he must not be surprised / that God finally withdraws his grace from him / which has left him unconvinced / and then gives him over to a perverse and hardened mind / which finally draws the curse after it in the righteous judgment of God. See Acts 14:17, Romans 2:5. etc.

# Chapter XII. The Fifth Book of Moses.
Pppp 3
<meta>catchword: v. 8.</meta>

### The 12th Chapter.

->The commanded destruction of all pagan abominations /<-
->and how they should adhere solely to the chosen place and the prescribed manner.<-

**T**hese are the statutes and the judgments which you shall observe to do / in the land which the LORD God of your fathers has given you to possess as an inheritance / all the days that you live upon the earth.

2. You shall utterly destroy all the places where the pagans / whom you shall dispossess / served their gods / upon high mountains and upon hills and under every kind of green tree.

3. And you shall tear down their altars / and break their pillars / and burn their sacred groves <note>original: "Götzen-Wälder" (Idol-forests), referring to the Asherim or ritual sites in groves.</note> with fire / and hew down the carved images of their gods; and you shall abolish their names from that place.

The believers of the New Testament should also have carefully observed this commandment regarding the destruction of all places of pagan idolatry. Especially in the time of Constantine the Great <note>Constantine the Great (r. 306–337 AD) was the first Roman emperor to convert to Christianity, ending state-sanctioned persecution.</note> / when they began to inherit the lands of the pagans / they should have completely uprooted, torn down, and destroyed all temples that they recognized and declared to be idol temples / according to the instruction of the Lord and His Spirit / along with all pagan and idolatrous ways, customs, and habits / by which such places were accustomed to be consecrated and the service bound to them. Instead / by retaining the temples and other outward ceremonies / they abolished only the crudest elements / as carnal prudence suggested / in order to better entice the unbelievers. Through this, however, it rather happened that the Church became an "outer court" given over to the pagans to be trampled; Revelation 11:2. Gradually, all kinds of customs and ceremonies crept back in / and were finally even ordained as law. By this, men gradually deviated from the simple service of the New Testament / which Christ ordained / where one should call upon the Father in spirit and in truth; John 4:23–24. Thus, a ceremonial service tied to temples arose among most people: even though it is expressly witnessed / that God does not dwell in temples made with hands; Acts 17:24. And Christ wishes to be in all places / wherever two or three are gathered in His name; Matthew 18:20. Therefore, men should pray in all places / and lift up holy hands without wrath or doubting <note>original: "Vernünftelung" (excessive reasoning or disputing).</note>. 1 Timothy 2:8. In this way, much strife, adversity, and superstition would have been avoided / and in the simple service within homes, the members of such small house-churches <note>original: "Haus-Gemeinen." The author advocates for the "ecclesiola in ecclesia" (little church within the church) model common in Pietism.</note> could have been more carefully observed. See 1 Corinthians 16:20. Just as Christ wishes to be present at all assemblies in His name / so also is that the right place which God has chosen; where one should also bring one's prayers and thanksgivings / to praise God there with a unanimous heart and to call upon Him in all needs. Matthew 18:19.

However, all this destruction commanded by the Lord in the external world is only an image of what should also happen in the interior according to the sense of the Spirit / and depicts how all false forms of divine service and worship / all false churches and temples / which are built up in the evil and earthly nature / together with all their sanctuaries and mixed worship services / shall be cast down and destroyed.

<column-break/>

4. You shall not do so to the LORD your God:

5. But to the place which the LORD your God shall choose out of all your tribes / to set His name (a) there / there you shall look for where He dwells / and there you shall come.

<margin>(a) Exodus 20:24. 1 Kings 8:29. 2 Chronicles 7:12.</margin>

6. And you shall bring there your burnt offerings and your sacrifices / and your tithes / and the heave offering <term>heave offering: a ritual where the gift was "heaved" or lifted up before God</term> of your hand / and your vows and your freewill offerings / and the firstborn of your cattle and of your sheep.

7. And you shall eat there before the presence of the LORD your God and be joyful / you and your households / in everything to which you stretch out your hand / wherein the LORD your God has blessed you.

8. You

v. 4. You shall—not do so) Meaning that you should not attempt to establish a worship service in every place that pleases you or seems good to you, after the manner of those pagan nations.

v. 6, 7. You shall eat the firstborn there) From this, as also from verses 17 and 18 of this chapter / one might almost conclude / as some (a) do / that those who brought the firstborn also had their portion of the meat. But that all the meat from it belonged to the priests alone / who consumed it with their families either in the temple or in the city within the walls / as was customary with the holy sacrifices; this is to be recognized from Numbers 18:17–18 and the reports of the Hebrews. Thus, the eating here must either be restricted to those pieces of which the father of the house also had his portion; or / as is most probable / the speech here refers to the priests, that they should eat it.

v. 7. You shall be joyful) The Lord wants to be called upon with a joyful spirit: therefore one should heartily ask Him for His grace of the joy of the Spirit. Psalm 51:14. Philippians 4:4. Now, humble contrition of the heart before God indeed has its time / but one must nevertheless serve God and walk before Him with a contented and satisfied heart / from which this spiritual joy must also arise.

So also should we undertake all our work / to which we daily stretch out our hand / with joy / and then enjoy with joy the nourishment provided for our sustenance before the face of God: to which the exhortation in Ecclesiastes 3:12–13 refers. But our work must also be according to the will of God / and thus a divine, rather than a sinful, calling in the works of vanity. See on this Psalm 104:23–24.

<margin>(a) Osiander on Deuteronomy 15:20. Franz, on sacrifices, disputation 13, thesis 122 following.</margin>

# The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XII.

8. You shall not do according to all that we do here this day, every man whatever is right in his own eyes.
9. <margin>(a) 1 Peter 1:4.</margin> For you have not yet come to the rest and to the inheritance (*) which the Lord your God will give you. <note>The rest mentioned here is a physical peace in the land of Canaan, but the commentary interprets it as a spiritual state of inner peace and union with God.</note>
10. But you will go over the Jordan and dwell in the land that the Lord your God will distribute to you as an inheritance, and He will give you rest from all your enemies round about, so that you will dwell securely.
11. <margin>Leviticus 26:6.</margin> And it shall be that the place which the Lord your God chooses to cause His name to dwell there, you shall bring there all that I command you: your burnt offerings and your sacrifices, your tithes and the heave offering of your hand, and all your chosen vows which you shall vow to the Lord.

---

v. 8. In the hidden sense, Moses intends to say this: that when the beloved yielded ones <note>original: "Gelassene" — a term from German mysticism referring to those who have surrendered their self-will to God.</note> have come into their promised land, they would no longer perform those works which they had done in the wilderness of faith; neither as the fruits of their own self-righteousness, nor with toil and restriction; because they have then attained a divine state, which is a state of innocence. And therefore they will perform everything that is right, not because it merely seems so to them, nor through the impulse of their own righteousness, but because they will be moved to it by the righteousness of God Himself. They will also do it in complete freedom. For although they must do many more things in the promised land than they did in the wilderness—just as Moses shows them through the account he gives of all those duties in this chapter—they will nonetheless carry out everything in complete rest, just as God also performs all things; because they will do such things in God, and through the sweet impulse of the law of His love, which, though it is multifaceted in its effects, is nevertheless very unified and quiet in its origin.

Previously, he told them that it was not because of their righteousness that they were to be led into this land. For as this was a self-righteousness, it was not yet pure enough to bring them into it. But the righteousness which was to lead them in is the righteousness of God Himself, which is free from all deception. For since the soul is then placed into the Truth, which is the eternal Law (just as the people of Israel were governed by the Law of God given through Moses), it cannot judge these things otherwise than God judges them. Thus, everything that is straight and righteous in the eyes of God is also so in the eyes of the rest. For the soul sees only through God's eyes. And this also ensures that it no longer errs and lives in a great freedom, even if men judge it differently.

v. 9. The reason why many have not yet received this freedom and righteousness is because they have not come to the rest and to the inheritance of the Lord. But when they have entered into it, they will no longer be able to restrict anything, as then everything will happen in the sweetest freedom and very great purity, because everything is done in God.

v. 10. 11. There they will possess a great peace, even in the midst of their enemies, should any dare to approach them. Then they will remain without fear, as they stand in a constant state.

<column-break/>

12. And you shall be joyful before the face of the Lord your God, you and your sons and your daughters, and your male and female servants, and the Levite who is within your gates; for he has no portion or inheritance with you.
13. Take heed that you do not offer your burnt offerings in every place that you see;
14. But in the place which the Lord shall choose in one of your tribes, there you shall offer your burnt offerings, and there you shall do all that I command you.
15. Yet you may slaughter and eat meat according to all your soul's desire, according to the blessing of the Lord your God which He has given you, in all your gates. The unclean and the clean may eat of it, as of the gazelle and the deer.
16. <margin>(a) Leviticus 3:17, 7:28, 17:10, 19:26.</margin> Only you shall not eat the blood (*); you shall pour it upon the earth like water.
17.

---

v. 12. <margin>(a) Psalm 5:12, 87:7.</margin> They will find themselves in a completely innocent joy and freedom, and rejoice together before God. The sons and daughters, and the male and female servants, will all participate in this joy of innocence. Even the Levites, who are the chief masters and shepherds of the others, will share this joy with them; because it is the only thing left to be shared among them. David had experienced this when he said (a): All those who are found in You, O Lord, are like those who are completely enraptured with joy.

v. 13. (Not in every place) The question arises: why? Answer: God wants nothing self-chosen in divine service. Through this, He also wanted to keep the people of Israel in unity of faith and worship.

v. 14. Therefore, they were to have only one place for it, which He Himself would choose.

This place, however, represented Christ Himself, to whom His people should adhere very closely, as the one whom the Lord chose, and in whom the Name of His Majesty and Glory dwells.

(There you shall do everything) For without Me you can do nothing, He says Himself in John 15:5.

v. 15. (Eating meat) Specifically from clean animals. (The unclean) also; those who otherwise were not permitted to eat of what was brought to the priests.

v. 16. But the eating of blood remains forbidden once and for all, because the animal's life is contained within it, and man, after the Fall, is already sufficiently animalistic in mind and nature. <note>The "Fall" refers to the biblical narrative of Adam and Eve's original sin, which the commentator suggests left humans with a base, "animalistic" inclination that must be restrained.</note>

# Chapter XII. The Fifth Book of Moses.

17. You may not eat within your gates the tithe of your grain, or of your new wine, or of your oil, or the firstborn of your herd or your flock, or any of your vows which you vow, or your freewill offerings, or the heave offering of your hand.

18. But before the presence of the Lord your God you shall eat them, in the place which the Lord your God chooses, you and your son and your daughter, your male servant and your female servant, and the Levite who is within your gates; and you shall rejoice before the presence of the Lord your God in everything to which you put your hand.

19. Take heed to yourself that you do not forsake the Levite all the days you live in your land.

---

v. 17. How many things are there which are forbidden in the cities—that is, in the presence of men—which may yet be performed before God in innocence? St. Paul experienced this well <margin>(a) 1 Cor. 9 and 10.</margin>. In this sense, Moses also says: *You shall not eat your tithes within your gates.* The words "your" or "thy" are understood to refer to those souls who still possess themselves <note>This refers to the "self-willed" state common in mystical theology, where a person has not yet surrendered their ego to God.</note>, and the word "city" or "gate" refers to those people who might take offense. The tithes indicate legal observances, which are all united in love. How many things in love would seem contrary to weak and unenlightened souls, and would offend them, which are in truth the purest fulfillment of the Law! But such things are known only to souls of this degree, who are more divinely enlightened. One must become weak with the weak, so as not to offend them. To Paul, all things are indeed permitted <margin>(b) 1 Cor. 10:22-23.</margin>, but not all things are helpful. To an apostle, all is allowed, but not all things edify.

v. 18. These tithes had to be eaten with joy in the place God had chosen for that purpose. For He is the one who does all things, who lays certain commands upon the soul and also frees the soul from them again. And this joy shall be universal: spreading from the Levites, or the highest part <note>In this mystical commentary, the "Levites" represent the higher, spiritual faculties of the human soul.</note>, down to the servants and maids, who represent the lowest part. Thus, one shall finally be satisfied with the goods of the Lord and take delight in all His works, in the exercise of a holy freedom which God Himself gives, and which is accompanied by no returning sorrow.

v. 19. *That you do not forsake*) i.e., that you do not misappropriate what belongs to him by divine ordinance from your sacrifices and gifts; or that you do not exclude him from your sacrificial meals.

The spiritual gifts of prophecy and the explanation of the Word of God should be preserved with all diligence, and no expense should be spared for them—though it commonly happens that people allow minds capable of serving the Lord to go to waste, who could have been used very usefully for the service of the community. See Proverbs 29:18: *Where there is no prophecy, the people become lawless; but blessed is he who keeps the law.*

<column-break/>

20. When the Lord your God expands your border, as He has promised you, and you say, "I will eat meat," because your soul longs to eat meat, you may eat as much meat as your soul desires.

21. If the place where the Lord your God chooses to put His name is far from you, then you may slaughter from your herd and from your flock which the Lord has given you, just as I have commanded you, and you may eat within your gates as much as your soul desires.

22. Just as the roebuck and the deer are eaten, so you may eat it; the unclean and the clean alike may eat it.

23. Only be sure that you do not eat the blood. For the blood is the soul <note>original: "Seele" — here used in the biblical sense of "life-force" or "life-blood."</note>; therefore you shall not eat the soul with the flesh.

24. You shall not eat it; you shall pour it on the earth like water.

<margin>Leviticus 17:13.</margin> 25. You shall not eat it, that it may go well with you and your children after you, when you do what is right in the eyes of the Lord.

---

The Lord permits us to use His creatures, provided it is done in proper order and measure; in this, one must very carefully avoid all misuse of the mingling lust of the flesh, lust of the eyes, and pride of life (1 Cor. 7:31), and ensure that the freedom of such enjoyment is not used as a stumbling block to others (1 Cor. 8:8-9).

After God has greatly expanded and broadened the soul, He places it into a new freedom, in which it may eat in safety that which previously would have sentenced it to death. In the wilderness, the people were cruelly punished because they had lusted for meat <margin>(a) Numbers 11:34.</margin>, but here they are permitted to eat as much as they themselves desire, without the slightest harm coming to them. On the contrary, they are even exhorted to do so with joy and in the presence of the Lord. This is settled by Scripture itself when it says that the first time they had desired it with [sinful] lust. Therefore, the place of their punishment was called the "Graves of Lust." But here they are far from eating it in that manner. They eat it only because it is permitted and commanded: they eat it to do the will of God, and not to satisfy their sensuality. They also eat it with joy, as all evil lust and corruption has been taken from them. These souls can no longer think of mortifying themselves <note>The text suggests that for the perfected soul, "mortification" (killing the desires) is no longer a conscious struggle because their desires have been naturally aligned with God's will.</note>, but they use everything in an innocent way and in the name of God <margin>(b) Romans 14:3.</margin>. He who eats of everything should take care not to despise him who may not eat of everything; and likewise, he who makes it a matter of conscience [to abstain] should not judge the other who eats of everything; for God has received him among His own—among those who, by belonging perfectly to Him, encounter His good will in all things.

# Chapter XII. The Fifth Book of Moses.

**Left Column:**

17. You are not permitted to eat within your gates the tithe of your grain, nor of your wine, nor of your oil, nor the firstborn of your cattle or of your sheep, nor any of your vows that you shall have vowed, nor your voluntary offerings, nor the heave offering of your hand.

18. But before the presence of the LORD your God you shall eat it, in the place which the LORD your God will choose: you, and your son, and your daughter, and your male servant, and your female servant, and the Levite who is within your gates; and you shall rejoice before the presence of the LORD your God in all that you put your hand to.

19. Take heed that you do not forsake the Levite all the days you are in your land.

---

<margin>v. 17. How many things are there which are forbidden in the cities—that is, in the presence of other men—which one can nevertheless perform before GOD in innocence? St. Paul experienced this well (a). In this sense, Moses also says: *You shall not eat your tithes within your gates.* The phrase "your [gates]" refers to those souls who still possess themselves, and the word "city" or "gate" refers to those people who are easily offended. The tithes represent legal observances, which are all united in love. How many things in that love would seem contrary to weak and unilluminated souls, and would offend them, which are in truth the purest fulfillment of the Law? But this is known only to souls at this stage of growth, who are divinely illuminated. One must become weak with the weak, so that one does not offend them. Everything is indeed permitted to Paul (b), but not everything is beneficial. To an apostle, everything is allowed, but not everything builds up.</margin>

<margin>v. 18. These tithes had to be eaten with joy in the place God had chosen for that purpose. # Chapter XIII.

->The Punishment of False Prophets.<-

IF there shall arise in your midst a prophet or one who has dreams <margin>(a) ch. 17:2.</margin> (a) and gives you a sign or a wonder;

2. And the sign or the wonder of which he spoke to you shall come to pass, and he says: "Let us follow after other gods, whom you have not known, and let us serve them!"

<sig>3. E</sig>

---

Because God commonly revealed His prophecies of future things through dreams—as seen with Abraham, Jacob, Joseph, Abimelech, Pharaoh, Nebuchadnezzar, and the like—the Enemy has also <unclear>received</unclear> power to approach the imagination of the soul at night with his lying fantasies. And just as God was accustomed to providing His prophets with divine wonders as seals of truth—as seen with Moses and Christ—so here God has permitted Satan to confirm his lies with all sorts of lying powers, signs, and wonders (2 Thessalonians 2:9) and thus to lead people astray, as seen with the Egyptian sorcerers. And all this serves as a righteous trial of man, to see whether he loves the truth he has recognized and will not allow himself to be turned away from it in the slightest by any such seductive presentations of the Enemy (2 Thessalonians 2:11). Therefore, one must look more at the matter itself being presented than at all the particular circumstances of outward prophecies, pronouncements, wonders, and the like. For now that the precious truth of the Gospel has been clearly enough presented in all its essential parts and confirmed by miracles, we have no further need for prophecies and wonders regarding such fundamental truths. However, when God, for the purpose of awakening people to impending judgments or some extraordinary guidance, permits such extraordinary prophecies and wonders alongside them, believers are to listen with holy attention and call upon God further for the revelation of His will in all patience, as well as for the strength to fulfill it, which God will add to His will if it is from Him. Regarding this, the enlightened testimony of the godly Cocceius <note>Johannes Cocceius (1603–1669) was a prominent Dutch theologian known for his "Federal Theology," which emphasized the covenants between God and humanity.</note> (a) deserves to be consulted.

v. 1. **A Prophet**) One who gives himself out as such, or who might truly have received a gift from God and otherwise brought forth good and true things.
**Such a prophet is also our Reason.** <note>The author warns that human logic can act as a "false prophet" if it leads one away from divine revelation.</note>
**A Sign**) can also be something that happens naturally, but is merely announced beforehand as a sign of what one is saying. But
**A Wonder**) is something that is above nature and does not usually happen according to its course.
**Give**) to justify his extraordinary calling.

v. 2. Theodoret <note>Theodoret of Cyrus (c. 393 – c. 458 AD) was an influential theologian of the School of Antioch and a bishop in Syria.</note> remarks on this point that we are instructed here not to pay attention to signs when the one who gives them teaches something that is contrary to true piety or to that which is according to godliness (Titus 1:1).
(a) <note>original: "Comment. in 1. Epist. ad Thessal. Cap. V. §. 116."</note> Commentary on the First Epistle to the Thessalonians, Chapter 5, Paragraph 116.

v. 3. The Lord tests you, etc.) The Lord permits such things so that you may be tested.

It is quite common today for people to cloak temptations under the pretext of Providence <note>God's divine guidance or care for the world</note> and a foreknowledge of God, not considering that the Lord often permits an occasion for us to be able to sin against him, in order to test us through it, whether we wish to seize such an opportunity or not; or rather, whether we truly love him with all our heart and all our soul, and are willing to reject and let go of everything for his sake. Many interpret such an occasion or opportunity quite wrongly and perversely.

The question arises: how then can one find the middle ground in this and be certain of the matter? Answer: God’s providential will must be explained by his commanding will. It is a piece of the eternal law of God: whatever is harmful to your soul is not from God.

When the preceding verse is taken into account, the seven duties toward God are again presented here, as was also done in Chapter 10:12 and 20, except that instead of swearing by his name, obeying his voice is placed here. And so in the New Testament, one can well take to heart the explicit institution of both sacraments, because there too one should swear by his name and dedicate oneself entirely to him as his property. See Matthew 28:19, Luke 22:19, 1 Corinthians 11:23–26. Otherwise, one reads of his external actions ordained through the voice of Christ, unless one also adds the gathering for prayer in his name. Matthew 18:19–20. All duties of Christianity toward God are internal, so as to serve God in spirit and in truth. All other commandments of a religious service are human, and can easily drive us from the way that Christ and the Apostles have prescribed for us through his Spirit.

Fear him) As a child fears his father.
Serve him) As he himself wishes to be served. Matthew 15:9.
Cling to him) As a bride clings to her bridegroom.

->So shall the punishments serve as an example, and their purpose must be improvement. Toward this end goes the judgment of God’s justice. For he has pleasure in life, and no delight in death. All governmental punishments must also have this as their aim.<-

---

It is to be wondered at that one nowhere reads that such a sharp death sentence was ever carried out on a false prophet, or an entire community, though they certainly experienced such things in the times of Joash, as well as at other times quite often; that they were led astray from the clear commandment of God to the service of the groves and idols by the leaders, who also misled the king. Instead, they imposed this death sentence of stoning upon the true prophet of God, Zechariah the son of Jehoiada, who was awakened by the Spirit of God to witness against such an abomination. 2 Chronicles 24:17–21. And Christ reproaches them for this, how they had done so to all the true prophets at all times. Matthew 23:34–37. From this we can recognize the righteous judgment of God over the external Church in the New Testament as well, where the false prophets have always been in great standing and have been the leaders among the people, who knew how to move kings with their flattering suggestions to confirm their humanly-ordered ceremonial service; and conversely, they most cruelly tortured in prisons, killed, and burned the witnesses of truth who were awakened by Christ’s Spirit to testify against it.

However, the "heresy-makers" find nothing here for their benefit <note>original: "Behuf," meaning for their purpose or use</note> when they wish to sentence to death those people they have recognized and declared to be heretics and false prophets. The law of the New Covenant, to which they claim to be devoted, prescribes a different measure in this matter. 1 Corinthians 5:13, Titus 3:10.

Now, according to the foundation of the New Covenant, it is said: *Every creature of God is good, and nothing is to be rejected if it is received with thanksgiving;* 1 Timothy 4:4. Also, *nothing is common [unclean] in itself, but only to him who considers it common.* Romans 14:14. <note>The commentator is harmonizing the strict Mosaic dietary laws with the Christian doctrine that all foods are permissible, emphasizing that the "uncleanness" was symbolic or pedagogical rather than inherent in the animal's nature.</note>

v. 3. On this basis, Ignatius writes <margin>(a) Letter 4 to the Philadelphians</margin> (a) thus: "If anyone holds any of the foods to be abominable, he has the apostate dragon dwelling within him." <note>original: "Wenn iemand einige von den Speiſen abſcheulich hält / der hat den abtrünnigen Drachen in ſich wohnend." This quote from the early Church Father Ignatius of Antioch warns against extreme asceticism that views physical matter as evil.</note>

v. 4. **Animals--eating)** Because man, after the Fall, has need of the irrational animals—both to use them for bodily nourishment and to protect his body with their skins and hides against the cold, rain, and storms—God willed to permit man the use of such things without which he could not well preserve life; yet with some distinction.

v. 5. **Deer -- Mountain Sheep)** Because these animals have no teeth in the upper jaw and swallow their food unchewed, retaining it in the esophagus, they are accustomed to bringing it back up later to chew it.

Otherwise, two species of animals appear here, <term>Dishon</term> <note>Hebrew: דישון; likely a pygarg or white-rumped antelope.</note> and <term>Zemer</term> <note>Hebrew: זמר; likely a mountain sheep or chamois.</note>, which are found nowhere else, and are therefore interpreted differently, as everyone believes they have a reason for their own interpretation. The true meaning will be revealed by the great future Light in Christ's Kingdom, when the letter of God’s Word along with its spiritual sense will be clearly revealed. In the meantime, we may and can investigate as much as each person has the ability and gift for such things.

v. 6–8. Regarding the splitting of hooves and chewing the cud, this was discussed sufficiently in Leviticus 11.

v. 9. 10. Likewise regarding the significance of fins and scales, and the lack thereof, in verses 9–12 of the same chapter.

The significance of the unclean birds was also dealt with at greater length in Leviticus 11:13–25:

v. 12. etc. And the very same species appear there in the same order as here, except that here

v. 13. one more species is added, for which one must rely somewhat on conjectures.

v. 14–19. Furthermore, these unclean birds also represent the various unclean, fleeting thoughts which rise up in the soul—sometimes toward greed, sometimes toward anger, sometimes toward impurity. Such thoughts must be quenched immediately, and one should not dwell on them; otherwise, one is, as it were, nourished by them and eats of such unclean birds. <note>This is a classic example of allegorical or "spiritual" interpretation, where the physical laws of the Old Testament are read as metaphors for the inner psychological and spiritual life of the believer.</note>

v. 20. In contrast, however, one should feed and sustain oneself with holy and pure thoughts, as if with clean birds.

v. 21. Regarding the **strangers within the gate**, who are sometimes simply called "strangers" (Leviticus 25:47), it has already been mentioned previously that these were people who had the right to live among the Jews but did not take the Mosaic yoke upon themselves. <note>These are the "Ger Toshav" or "Proselytes of the Gate," who followed the Seven Laws of Noah but not the full 613 commandments of the Torah.</note>

**You shall not boil the young goat etc.)** This commandment appears with these very same words in Exodus 23:19 and 34:26, where the notes should be consulted. And the commandment in Exodus 22:29 and Leviticus 22:27 also belongs here; thus, because of the frequent repetition, there is likely a deep meaning hidden beneath it.

The Lord does not test His young children, who are still weak in faith, with extraordinary trials of fiery temptations until they have become stronger, at which point they must present themselves to Him as a sacrifice. <note>The author links the prohibition of boiling a kid in its mother's milk to the idea of God's gentleness toward "infants in the faith," suggesting that one should not be overwhelmed by trials before they are ready.</note>

v. 22.

# The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XIV.

22. You shall faithfully tithe all the yield of your seed, which comes out of the field year by year.

23. And you shall eat before the presence of the Lord your God, in the place which he shall choose to cause his name to dwell there, the tithe of your grain, of your wine, and of your oil, and the firstborn of your herds and of your flocks: so that you may learn to fear the Lord your God all your days.

24. But if the way is too long for you, so that you are not able to carry it there, because the place is too far from you which the Lord your God shall have chosen to set his name there; for the Lord your God will bless you:

25. Then you shall give it for money, and bind the money in your hand, and go to the place which the Lord your God shall have chosen.

---

<margin>v. 22. Faithfully tithe</margin> By this, the **second tithe** is meant. For every father of a household, after he had set aside the first tithe—which belonged to the Levites, as mentioned in Chapter 12, verse 6; Leviticus 27:30; Numbers 18:21, 24, 26, etc.—had to tithe the remaining heap a second time. Although some claim to know nothing of this second tithe (a), all Hebrew authorities, including Josephus (b), affirm its existence.

<margin>v. 23.</margin> Of this tithe, the father of the household ate with his own family, but not at home. Instead, where the journey was not too far, he had to bring everything up to the place where the Tabernacle stood—or later where the Temple was, namely to Jerusalem—and consume it there. However, this was not necessarily *inside* the Temple itself, as some suggest (c); for where would they have all found the room? Rather, it was simply at that place, provided it occurred within the city walls.

<margin>v. 24. 25.</margin> If, however, the way was too far for him to conveniently bring everything there, he could sell it and turn it into money <note>The original German uses "Gelt," an archaic form of "Geld" (money).</note>. But he was not permitted to use that money for any other things; instead, he had to bring it to the chosen place. Hebrew scholars except the tithes of fruit and wine from this rule, arguing they should not be sold but brought up in person, so that the streets of Jerusalem might be "crowned" with fruit. 
If someone wished to redeem his own tithe <note>That is, pay the value in cash rather than giving the physical goods.</note>, he had to add a fifth part to its value, according to Leviticus 27:31. Where he sold it to others, however, this was not necessary.

(a) *Reitz in his notes on Goodwin’s Moses & Aaron, Book 6, Chapter 3, note 2; and Burmann in the same place; Osiander on this passage* <note>original: "ad h. l."</note>. *According to their opinion, the fathers of the households would have been guests of the Levites; yet according to the clear text, the Levites were the guests, and the fathers of the households were the hosts for this tithe. It is also distinguished from the Levitical tithe in that the latter could be eaten in all places, while this one could be eaten nowhere but in Jerusalem.*
(b) *Josephus, Book 4 of the Antiquities, Chapter 8.*
(c) *Varen, Sacred Three-fold, Chapter 11, on tithes; Goodwin, Moses & Aaron, Book 6, Chapter 3.*

<column-break/>

26. Then you may give the money for whatever your soul desires, whether for cattle, or for sheep, or for wine, or for strong drink, indeed for everything your soul shall long for; and you shall eat it there before the presence of the Lord your God, and you shall rejoice, you and your household.

27. And as for the Levite who is within your gates, you shall not forsake him: for he has no portion nor inheritance with you.

28. At the end of three years you shall bring out all the tithes of your yield in that same year, and shall lay them up within your gates.

29. Then the Levite shall come (a), because he has no portion nor inheritance with you, and the stranger, and the orphan, and the widow who are within your gates, and they shall eat so that they are satisfied; so that the Lord your God may bless you in all the work of your hand which you shall do. (a) Numbers 18:21.

---

<margin>v. 26.</margin> From this money, feasts were then prepared. This tithe was mostly consumed during the high festivals, when the whole land came together.

<margin>v. 27.</margin> To these feasts came not only the father of the household himself with his own—sons and daughters, menservants and maidservants—but also the Levites who lived among them in their district. Likewise, other good friends, as well as widows and orphans, were invited to a holy meal out of gratitude. See Chapter 12:12, where the people and the Levite are placed together. The remainder stayed for their nourishment throughout the entire year.

<margin>v. 28.</margin> This is the **third tithe**, occurring every third year, counting from the Year of Release <note>The Sabbatical year or "Erlaß-Jahr."</note>. It is considered likely by some (a)—though most do not want to be certain—that the first two tithes (the first for the Levites and the second consumed at Jerusalem) were delivered not only in the first, second, fourth, and fifth years after the Sabbath year, but also in the 3rd and 6th years. In those years, this third tithe, which was distributed at home among Levites, the poor, orphans, and strangers, had to be taken anew from the remaining stores. Thus, in the third year, there was a double tithing. This is why the third year is specifically called the "Year of Tithing" above other years in Chapter 26:12.
<margin>At the end of three years)</margin> And thus twice within seven years, since the seventh year was a year of rest <term>Sabbath year</term> when they were not allowed to sow anything (Exodus 23:10-11).
<margin>You shall bring out)</margin> Everything had to be distributed before the Feast of Tabernacles in the 4th and 7th years.

<margin>v. 29. So that the Lord may bless you)</margin> After they gave the tithes, then God blessed them.

(a) *Cited in Sixtinus Amama's commentary on tithes.*
