---

<margin>v. 34. You shall be driven mad)</margin> out of righteous judgment and because of the heavy tribulations that shall break out upon you. With whatever a person sins / with that same thing they shall be punished. But it is acting madly / when one despises the Lord’s command.

<margin>v. 40. Is it not a form of madness / when people claim to be Christians without the Spirit of Christ / and even make a mockery of that very Spirit? What are Christians without anointing <term>the name 'Christian' comes from the Greek 'Christos,' meaning 'the Anointed One'</term>, from which the name originates? They are nothing else than people without a head and without reason. If one does not wish to have this Spirit and let it act like a leaven to be strengthened for the renewal of life; then it is just in the eyes of God / that it should remain far from them / even though many witnesses of the truth stand up among them like olive trees. For their olive tree / their Christ / whom they fashion according to their own fantasy / brings no useful fruit / that might be of benefit to them.</margin>

44. He shall lend to you / but you shall not lend to him: he shall become the head / and you shall become the tail.

And into the captivity / that arises from this!

<margin>v. 42.</margin> But oh, wretched fruits / which the misfortune of hellish spirits may claim as their inheritance!

<margin>v. 43. Woe to us / when sin / as something foreign within us, gains the upper hand / and thereby the good is suppressed!</margin>

### Chapter XXVIII. The Fifth Book of Moses.

47. Because you did not serve the **LORD** your God with joy and with a willing heart, when you had an abundance of all things.

48. Therefore you shall serve your enemies, whom the **LORD** will send against you, in hunger and in thirst, and in nakedness and in lack of all things; and he will put an iron yoke upon your neck, until he has destroyed you.

<margin>Jeremiah 5:15.</margin>
49. The **LORD** will bring a nation against you from afar, from the end of the earth, just as an eagle flies; a nation whose language you will not understand:

50. A nation of fierce countenance, which will not regard the person of the old, nor show mercy to the young.

<margin>(a) Jeremiah 5:17.</margin>
51. And it shall consume the fruit of your livestock and the fruit of your land <note>Original text includes an asterisk (*) marking a cross-reference.</note>, until you are destroyed: which will leave you nothing of grain, new wine, or oil, or the increase of your cattle and the herds of your sheep, until it has brought you to ruin.

<margin>(a) Luke 19:43.</margin>
52. And it shall distress you in all your gates, until your high and fortified walls fall down, in which you trusted throughout all your land: and it shall distress you in all your gates throughout all your land, which the **LORD** your God has given you.

---

v. 47. **That you did not serve your God)** Which you should have held as a great honor and dignity, that God, who is a Lord over all and needs no service, would accept anything from you as a service and take you yourself into His service.

**With joy)** Of which service to God the great multitude, called "the world," among Christians knows nothing, and rather views everything as a <term>melancholy thing</term> <note>Meaning a source of sadness or gloom rather than spiritual life.</note>.

v. 48. **You shall serve your enemies)** So it goes: if one will not serve God, then one must serve as a slave to his lusts, to sin, to the world, and to the devil; and that with a languishing spirit, which can find no rest or satisfaction therein, but must suffer want.

**In nakedness)** Without the garment of divine light and life, in sheer shame and disgrace before God and His chosen angels.

v. 49. **A nation like an eagle)** By which is very clearly and specifically aimed at the Romans and the Roman Monarchy, who carry the eagle in their coat of arms.

v. 50. **Neither the old nor the young)** When the old remain children in divine understanding, and are found to be sinners and wicked boys of 60, 70, 80 and 100 years <note>Original: Isaiah 65:20.</note>; and when the young follow early in the footsteps of the old and grow old in wickedness: then the judgment of justice makes no distinction among them in the time of visitation.

v. 52. **In which you trusted)** The Lord cannot tolerate such false trust in anything other than Himself.

<column-break/>

<margin>(a) Leviticus 26:29. Jeremiah 19:9.</margin>
53. And you shall eat the fruit of your own body, the flesh of your sons and of your daughters <note>Original text includes an asterisk (*) marking a cross-reference.</note>, whom the **LORD** your God has given you, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy shall distress you.

54. The man who was tender and very luxury-loving among you shall look with an evil eye upon his brother, and the wife who is in his bosom, and the rest of his children whom he has left remaining.

55. So that he will not give to any of them any of the flesh of his sons whom he shall eat: because nothing at all is left to him in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy shall distress you in all your gates.

56. The woman who was tender and luxury-loving among you, who would not venture to set the sole of her foot upon the ground because she was so luxury-loving and tender, she shall look with an evil eye upon the husband in her bosom, and her son, and her daughter.

<margin>(a) Lamentations 4:10.</margin>
57. Namely, because of her afterbirth that comes out from between her legs, and because of her children whom she shall bear; for she shall eat them secretly for lack of all things <note>Original text includes an asterisk (*) marking a cross-reference.</note>: namely, in the siege and in the distress with which your enemy shall distress you in your gates. 58.

---

v. 53. **The man who)** lived every day magnificently and in pleasures.

**Shall look with an evil eye upon his wife)** even when she also wants some of the slaughtered child,

**And his remaining children)** whom he has not yet laid hands upon for the slaughter.

v. 55. Can anything more terrifying of famine be expressed than what is done here? All of which has indeed actually occurred and been fulfilled in fact.

But just as all the threatened punishments have surely come upon them, so God will also truly fulfill all His promises that He made to them, when they turn to the **LORD** their God in the latter days; as the Prophets are full of this.

v. 56. **Who would not venture to set the sole of her foot upon the ground)** This concerns those who like to travel in carriages, with a thoughtful and emphatic description of womanly softness, which is even less becoming to men.

v. 57. **The same)** As soon as they come into the world.

### The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XXVIII.

58. **If you will not be careful to do all the words of this law that are written in this book, that you may fear this glorious and fearful name, the LORD your God:**
<margin>(a) Psalm 111:9.</margin>
59. **Then the LORD will make your plagues wonderful <note>In the older sense of "wonderful"—meaning full of wonder or extraordinary in their severity.</note>, and the plagues of your offspring; even great and persistent plagues, and evil and persistent sicknesses.**
60. **And he will bring back upon you all the diseases of Egypt, which you were afraid of, and they shall cling to you.**
61. **Also every kind of sickness and every kind of plague which is not written in the book of this law, these the LORD will bring upon you, until you are destroyed.**
62. **And you shall be left with few people** (a) / **instead of being as the stars of heaven for multitude; because you did not obey the voice of the LORD your God.**
<margin>(a) Isaiah 17:4-6. Zephaniah 3:12.</margin>
63. **And it shall come to pass, that as the LORD rejoiced over you to do you good, and to multiply you; so the LORD will rejoice over you to bring you to nothing and to destroy you; and you shall be plucked from the land where you are going to possess it as an inheritance.**

---

v. 58. 59. These two verses were customarily read aloud by one of the judges during the scourging of a wrongdoer while the lashes were being administered.

v. 60. **Plagues of Egypt)** When one becomes like Egypt oneself—Revelation 11:8—one should not wonder if the plagues of Egypt also appear. Egypt is an image of the earthly nature and of this present evil world, in which the Beast and the spirit of the world (or Pharaoh) holds dominion.

v. 61. **And every kind of plague which is not written in the book of the law)** Indeed, since the time of Moses, many new diseases have been discovered and revealed in the human body.

v. 63. **As the Lord rejoiced to do good; so he will rejoice to destroy you)** Behold the goodness and the severity of God! Romans 11:22.

v. 64. **Scatter among all people)** This has especially come to pass through the final Roman devastation, which continues to this very day.

v. 66. **Your life)** or "your lives"
**shall hang in doubt before you)** as if by a thin thread, as those understand it who are satisfied with the literal letter alone: meaning that you must weigh your life every moment and have death before your eyes.
However, others—and among them very many Church Fathers—understand it to refer to Christ, who hung on the Cross opposite Jerusalem under the curse for those who were cursed; and they translate the words:
**Have no assurance of your life)** as "do not believe in your life" <note>Original: "deinem Leben nicht trauen" vs "an dein Leben nicht glauben". This is a Christological interpretation where "Life" is a title for Christ.</note>: just as, regardless, the Hebrew letter found here is the letter of the Son <note>This likely refers to the Hebrew letter 'Vav', which mystical interpreters linked to the "Son" or the "Nails" of the Crucifixion.</note>.

v. 68. This is said to have occurred through Titus Vespasianus, who sold them to the Egyptians, from where they were then brought as plunder to Alexandria, as Josephus and others report. Thus they also fell into the spiritual Egypt of heavy servitude, from which they shall not be delivered until the great and general conversion to Christ, which is discussed in Chapter 30.

Chapter 29. The Fifth Book of Moses.

# The XXIX Chapter.

->Renewal of the Covenant.<-

These are the words of the covenant which the **LORD** commanded Moses to make with the children of Israel in the land of Moab, besides the covenant which he made with them at Horeb <note>Horeb is another name for Mount Sinai, where the Ten Commandments were first given.</note>.

2. And Moses called all Israel and said to them: You have seen all that the **LORD** did before your eyes in the land of Egypt, unto Pharaoh, and unto all his servants, and unto all his land.

3. The great temptations <note>In this context, "temptations" refers to the trials or "testings" of God's power through the plagues and miracles.</note> which your eyes have seen, those great signs and wonders.

4. Yet the **LORD** has not given you a heart to perceive, nor eyes to see, nor ears to hear, unto this day.

5. And I have led you forty years in the wilderness: your clothes have not worn out upon you, and your shoe has not worn out from your foot.

6. You have eaten no bread, and you have drunk neither wine nor strong drink: so that you might know that I am the **LORD** your **GOD**.

<column-break/>

7. And when you came to this place, Sihon the king of Heshbon, and Og the king of Bashan, came out against us to battle, and we struck them down.

8. And we took their land, and gave it for an inheritance to the Reubenites, and to the Gadites, and to the half-tribe of Manasseh.

<margin>Psalm 1:3.</margin>

Whereby they are also reminded of their miserable condition: that they had not yet partaken of the rebirth to a spiritual life <note>The commentator is interpreting the Old Testament text through a later Christian lens of "rebirth" or spiritual awakening.</note>, because they had not rightly and earnestly made use of all these testimonies of **GOD'S** grace.

It is also the case that, even if one walks in a path, one cannot recognize all the things that occur in it, nor be instructed by them, nor understand them, until one has first reached the destination. Everything that could be said of it beforehand might not be grasped by a person as long as he was still on the way. But as soon as a soul has reached the goal, it is immediately struck with wonder when it sees its eyes opened, and its heart becomes capable of understanding, and it possesses the knowledge of all these things.

If this Sihon cannot prevail and overcome; if violence and power, if trampling and uprooting, cannot hinder our good thoughts and concerns: then the Devil uses contempt and mockery to see if he might make us discouraged and turn us away from our purpose. But under **GOD'S** guidance and assistance, both are successfully overcome in faith.

v. 20, 21. And these are threatened with the heavy punishments of being blotted out and all the curses; because God does not want His free grace in the Gospel to be in the least bit mixed or afflicted with an imagination derived from the Law. See Romans 3:20, etc. And

How much more will it be loathed by God—and such loathing is indicated here—when one tries to burden the service in spirit and in truth (which belongs to the New Testament, John 4) with many ceremonies that were commanded under the Law as shadows; whereby the essence is obscured and neglected by most people, who then only remain stuck to the external ceremonies and put their trust in them. ### Chap. XXIX. The Fifth Book of Moses. 779

> 24. Indeed, all nations will say: "Why has the **LORD** done this to this land? What is this great, burning anger?"
> 25. Then people will say: "Because they have forsaken the covenant of the **LORD**, the **GOD** of their fathers, which he made with them when he led them out of the land of Egypt:
> 26. And they went and served other gods, and bowed down before them; gods whom they did not know, and whom he had not assigned to them:
> 27. Therefore the **LORD's** anger burned against this land, so that he brought upon it all the curses written in this book."

**v. 24. Why has the Lord done this to this land?)** Just as one might also ask upon seeing Asia Minor, where formerly the Christian Church, planted by the Apostles, flourished so gloriously, but now everything lies under the Turkish abomination of desolation <note>A reference to the Ottoman control of former Byzantine/Christian territories, often interpreted by contemporary theologians as a divine judgment or a sign of the end times.</note>: serving us as an example and a spectacle for warning and reflection.

**v. 25–27. Because)** Since they broke the covenant of **GOD** and clung to the Romans, seeking protection from them when they cried out: "We have no king but the Emperor!" <note>Refers to John 19:15; the commentator links the biblical rejection of God to the Jewish rejection of Jesus in favor of Roman authority.</note> whom **GOD** had not set over them, and whom their fathers had not known.

And so, regarding the question of the Christian churches in the East, the answer may be given from Saint Cyprian: <note>St. Cyprian of Carthage (c. 210–258 AD), an Early Christian bishop and writer who lived through Roman persecutions.</note>
> "Because the Christians have gone astray, each seeking only to enrich himself; and therefore one craftily deceived the other, swearing in vain and falsely, scolding and wishing ill upon one another with poisonous mouths, and feuding with stubborn hatred and envy, so that even among many clerics there was no fear of God; therefore, under the tyrannical Emperor Decius in the 8th persecution, by sword, fire, wild beasts, glowing grates and tongs, living burial, and other horrific martyrdoms and pain, the martyrs became as many as the sand of the sea: but the rest fell away from the faith in countless numbers, and sacrificed to idols, or through hypocrisy bought certificates <note>term: libellatici; Christians who obtained certificates (libelli) stating they had sacrificed to Roman gods to avoid persecution, even if they had not actually done so.</note> from the authorities as if they had sacrificed."

# The XXX. Chapter.
->The Conversion of Israel: The Presentation of Life and Death.<-

> AND it shall come to pass, when all these words have come upon you, the blessing and the curse which I have set before you; then you shall return to your heart among all the nations where the **LORD** your **GOD** has driven you.

Here is contained a glorious prophecy of the future state of the Jews, how **GOD** would first allow all the words of blessing to come upon them. Just as he showed them much good in the land of Canaan, raising them up and exalting them to crown and scepter; how he also later let them dwell far and wide and endowed them with much wealth: but they finally fell away from him and denied Christ; Isaiah 1:2. Therefore, all the curses have also come upon them: so that they have be-
<meta>catchword: come</meta>

<column-break/>

> 28. And the **LORD** has uprooted them from their land in anger and in wrath and in great bitterness, and has cast them into another land, as it stands to this day.
> 29. The secret things belong to the **LORD** our **GOD**, but the revealed things belong to us and to our children forever, to do all the words of this law. Acts 1:6–8.

**v. 28. Uprooted them from their land — cast into another land)** Therefore they are now scattered over the whole earth, as can be seen in them even to this day.
According to the spirit, however, it must be understood of those who have taken themselves back <note>An interpretive reference to reclaiming one's self-will instead of submitting to God.</note> and who, by becoming their own masters again, have withdrawn from the sovereignty of **GOD** through their own wickedness to lead themselves in their deviations; for they prefer their own gain over serenity <note>term: Gelaſſenheit; a key concept in German Pietism meaning a state of letting go of self-will and worldly desire to be fully available to God's will.</note> and thus leave the place of rest to enter into the worry of themselves. Such people are instantly cast into the wrath of **GOD** and sent into a foreign land, a land in which they can find no rest.

**v. 29. God sets the seal** upon what he has said, so that the spoken wondrous events remained secret things that no one at that time could recognize until they were fulfilled; whereupon afterward one had to praise **GOD** in his holy and righteous ways, who also wished to fulfill his promised goodness to all nations, intending to become their gracious and reconciled **GOD** in the Messiah, after they allowed themselves to be brought to the obedience of this Shiloh <note>term: Shiloh; a messianic title derived from Genesis 49:10, often interpreted as "he to whom it belongs" or "the bringer of peace."</note>, who was also sent to them for redemption. See Luke 2:30, 31, 32. Until then, however, they were to hold to the revealed Word of **GOD**, that they might obey all his commandments.

Thus, this saying cannot be used to argue that one should not investigate the secret ways of **GOD**—which **GOD** nevertheless reveals in the Prophetic Word, but which are still obscure before their fulfillment—so that they might serve us for instruction in the wonderful ways of **GOD**, and thus further for comfort and expectation of the great salvation of **GOD** over the whole earth, and also for the Jews; see Romans 15:4. Yes, even of the great salvation that will continue to reveal itself in the eternities. But one should not be so prying <note>original: "fürwitzig," meaning meddlesome or excessively curious about things not yet revealed.</note> about these things that one neglects the most necessary thing, which is to do the will of **GOD**.

> 2. And you shall return to the **LORD** your **GOD**, that you may obey his voice according to all that I command you today, you and your children, with all your heart and with all your soul.
> 3. And [the Lord will turn your captivity...]

come like an oak whose leaves have fallen, and like a garden without water; Isaiah 1:30. So that they are no longer a people flourishing in their land, but a withered people, and are without the grace of the Holy Spirit. Then **GOD**, in the latter times, wishes to show them the great mercy that they would return to their hearts and rightly reflect upon what **GOD** has allowed to come upon them.

**v. 2. Therefore they then turn to their true King, the Messiah,** and become obedient to him; concerning which Hosea has so clearly and gloriously prophesied, Chap. 3:5.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the 30th chapter of Deuteronomy, transitioning from the physical exile of the Israelites to a profound mystical discourse on the soul's "captivity" in sin and its eventual restoration through divine mercy and the "nothingness" of the self.</meta>

# 3. And the **LORD** your **GOD** will turn your captivity / and have mercy on you / and will gather you again from all the peoples / where the **LORD** your **GOD** has scattered you.
## 4. When

At the same time, Moses assures us that when souls—who have stepped out from the rest of *yieldedness* <note>The German term is *Gelassenheit*, a central concept in German mysticism referring to a state of total surrender and letting go of the self-will to be filled by God.</note> and have become guilty and cast away through such deviation—return again to **GOD** and become obedient to him with all their heart, he will also draw them out of their captivity again. If, however, such people are converted only with great difficulty, this does not come from **GOD**, who is pure love and mercy and does not desire the death of the sinner, but rather that he should convert and live; who always stretches out his arms to receive those who turn back to him. For that reason, he died upon the cross with outstretched arms. This difficulty comes instead from the side of the soul, which, once it has been placed in a certain *essential state* <note>The "essential state" (*wesentlicher Stand*) refers to a high degree of mystical union where the soul is rooted in the very essence of God rather than just in feelings or thoughts.</note>, finds it difficult to move. Since it has moreover been for a long time in a state where it could not distinguish itself from **GOD** because of its close union, it could in no way turn toward **GOD** nor away from **GOD**: And as this has become a habit for it, it is impossible for it to change its nature, even though it has truly fallen.

The soul can fall into such a case in only two ways: Either through the pride of Lucifer, which moves it to attribute the strength and the power of **GOD** to itself; in that it takes pleasure in itself in this state and regards itself in a vain manner: from which it is then so far misled that it attributes to its own powers and worthiness that which **GOD** works in it or through it. And just as these unfaithful men imitate the evil angels in their fall, since they fell from such a great degree of grace and holiness; so they also imitate them in their impenitence, making their conversion so much more difficult, the more they sin with greater ingratitude and less weakness.

The other way of going out from **GOD** is when one takes oneself back so that one, with good deliberation and voluntarily, withdraws from the sovereignty of **GOD**, so that one can again enter into one's own leadings.

These are the two kinds of sins through which the beginning of a soul's corruption comes: the deviation of the spirit, through pride and through vain self-complacency; and the deviation of the will, through the withdrawal from the obedience and the sovereignty of **GOD**. This is the source of all the other sins which they afterwards commit. It is, however, also easy to see from this that it happens very with great difficulty and slowly that they should do such things voluntarily and lose themselves. Therefore, there are not easily examples—or at least very few—of souls who, having already come this far, have fallen from that state again. It is, however, enough that it is possible, in order to be on one's guard against it.

The cause, now, which makes these souls have so much trouble returning back to **GOD** after their fall, is that because they are confirmed in the state of *essentiality*, they are as satisfied in evil as they were confirmed in good. (And this is also what caused the impossibility of Lucifer's conversion.) What makes the matter perhaps most impossible, however, is that these people want to tackle repentance on the *active side* <note>That is, through outward religious works or "doing" things to earn favor, rather than through the passive internal surrender required at this spiritual level.</note>, just as they did before: and those who guide them also want it thus. Which is as impossible as it is useless. Thus you, O you guides, must only bring those who are such into the sight of their humiliation, without tormenting them with active penance, as long as they are capable of it, and meanwhile let them drink in great gulps from the cup of rejection and the wrath of **GOD**: so that they may thus learn to remain standing under the justice of **GOD**, and be content never to attain forgiveness from **GOD**, if indeed it should be his Holy Will, without worrying whether he will forgive them again and receive them back into grace, or not. Because they have fallen so high and have lost so much grace; they must be stripped of all self-interest, and thus be presented to all the hardest strokes of the justice of **GOD**. They must also not force themselves to reach a certain kind of prayer which would be lower than that in which they

<column-break/>

stood at the time when they fell. The guides must also not demand this of them. For it is as impossible a thing as if one wanted to bring a man back into his mother's womb: and since one would first not be able to finish with it, it could moreover be hindered in its progress. Keep them then in their rank, O you fathers of such souls! Abandon them to divine justice without mercy; and allow them not the very least thing for their salvation. Oh, what a terrifying penance this is, and how few are courageous enough to endure such a thing! This is precisely what has caused so much ruin in the spiritual life after a fall: in that the proper means were not applied. One offends the weak and makes the poor fallen ones despair. But if men were faithful and courageous enough to let themselves be destroyed and burned by divine justice; they would in a short time be set back into a much higher state than that from which they had fallen. Just as **GOD** also promises through the prophet for the comfort of this kind of penance (a).

The reasons why such a kind of penance is peculiar to souls who have already come far in *yieldedness* are (as has already been said elsewhere): first: because *nothingness* is the immediate order to the supernatural; since the fullness of **GOD** pours itself out upon the emptiness of the creature.

Since now the men who have thus fallen down from this high rank have stood in a very supernatural state, and are also to be set back into the same through the return to **GOD**; they have need of the most supernatural divine communications; and must inevitably stand in *nothingness*, in the acceptance and love of their rejection, and their eternal abandonment into the will of **GOD**, in order to be in the state to be able to accept such things: since otherwise, if they perhaps want to fill themselves with new exercises, new self-inventions, and powers, they would thereby place the greatest obstacles in the way of the greatest graces, which they need in order to lift them up and reintroduce them into their state. Just as every shape can be more easily introduced into a single drop of water than into another in which it finds something to be put out or cleaned.

Secondly, it is also certain that the more the soul renounces its own benefit and offers itself up to what is **GOD’s**; the more it makes itself fit for a penance that is all the swifter and more advantageous to it. For nothing can move the heart of **GOD** more to communicate his great mercy than when he looks upon his poor creature which would rather accept all the hardest strokes of his justice than desire even one own benefit for itself, or fail to sacrifice itself entirely to his honor. And even then, when the soul is entirely in this disposition; it is already perfectly converted again. For it is impossible that sin should exist alongside such a heroic love, and that grace should not be found in a heart which burns entirely with such a pure love, since such a heart moreover gladly accepts everything that can be accepted for the benefit of **GOD**, in the whole concept of his will, his justice, and his power.

Just as this is now infallibly the swiftest and most perfect penance, and also moreover drives the soul to it (because it finds itself; because these are fruits of the state from which it fell, and it still possesses a certain ease and selfhood to perform these denials and sacrifices carried so far): so one must also necessarily lead them there, and teach them not only to leave everything to **GOD**—for **GOD** alone can both give the proper medicine for their sickness and draw his honor from it—but also to desire all at once these medicinal means, for the sake of the preference which one gives to the will of **GOD** for the healing of the deadly wound. This is the very best remedy for such a great sickness. For there is nothing in any thing that is safer or more orderly than when it has been abandoned to **GOD** in the most perfect way.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Deuteronomy chapter 30, specifically focusing on the internal, mystical process of a soul’s "return" to God after a spiritual fall. It contrasts outward acts of penance with the deeper "purgatory" of the spirit.</meta>

<page-num>781</page-num>
<header>Chapter XXX. The Fifth Book of Moses.</header>
<columns>2</columns>

Those who read this might perhaps think that this repentance does not correspond to the fall; that there is no sadness or pain in it, and that it does not afflict the soul. But if they had experience in this matter, they would confess that nothing in the world equals this pain. It is Purgatory, or even Hell itself (according to the degree in which **GOD** places the soul there), which is indeed an unspeakable torment. **GOD** is much more skillful at purifying than all creatures, and the punishments of a justice-exercising **GOD** are much different from all human inventions of the exercise of justice! Such a soul would much rather endure all possible death-penalties than to remain, in the manner just described, faithful and immovable under the hand of divine justice. All exercises of penance that one might impose upon it, even the most severe, would by comparison lighten its burden and be a refreshment to it. However, one must take great care not to impose any on the soul, as this would pull it even further out of its state and prevent it from being able to be restored to it. It is natural that one stands up again in the same place where one fell, and thus continues the journey from there, without returning to the place where one began to walk in order to stand up again—since one fell before the journey was finished. Thus, it would also be no penance for such a soul if one wanted to burden it with mere physical tortures; it would rather be an invigoration for it. This is easy to understand. The pains of external abstinences and penances afflict the senses, but they comfort the spirit. Now, since the senses in these souls are very much dead—both because they have previously endured all imaginable mortifications and penances and have become, as it were, insensitive through them, and also because the senses are separated from the spirit and therefore have no more power to feel either pain or pleasure—their penance must therefore not be measured according to the senses. Rather, so that the punishment for them may be all the more painful and also equal to the crime, it must be a punishment of the spirit; for all their sin is a sin of the spirit.

But now, so that this punishment of the spirit may be intense, deep, and appropriate to the sin, it can be imposed by no one but **GOD**. For whatever one might then do to the senses would only be a stay and a support for the spirit, turning it away from its pain. But when the spirit finds itself buried under the weight of divine justice and sees itself without help and without support, abandoned by the senses which offer it no aid—oh, this is a terrifying and so great a torture that it can only be known through experience alone! It is a fire which, through its activity, penetrates even into the marrow. And perhaps among a thousand fallen people, barely three may be found who are willing to let themselves be swallowed up by the justice of **GOD**, as much as it might please Him, without taking themselves back sooner or later, and especially in sickness or at death. For then one wants to use all kinds of force to assure oneself of salvation through one's own activity.

It is certain, however, that such a soul must act just as little in death as at any other time. On the contrary, precisely at that time, one must surrender oneself to the justice of **GOD** with all the more courage, to bear its weight for all eternity. Oh, this is the purity of disinterested love! <note>Disinterested love (*uninteressirte Liebe*) is a core concept in 17th-century mysticism, referring to loving God for His own sake, without regard for reward or fear of punishment, even if He were to condemn the soul.</note> This love is unknown to self-love, but is recognized, esteemed, and accepted by pure love. A person who might be so happy as to die thus would show **GOD** an unspeakable honor and would—without going through any Purgatory (for what could be left to purify in a soul that possesses no self-interest anymore and has reached such a heroic love?)—be exalted to the highest rank in heaven. Instead, when one "takes oneself back" <note>To "take oneself back" (*sich wiedernehmen*) means to reclaim one's own will or to seek self-preservation after having supposedly surrendered to God.</note> at death, one robs **GOD** of a great honor and loses an excellent blessedness. Not that such a soul would not be saved, but it will nevertheless have to pay for its faint-heartedness in the next life.

This is more important than can be said. Therefore, those into whose hands these writings might fall are asked to pay special attention to this.

v. 4, 5. If a soul could only be so happy as to attain the aforementioned readiness—even though it might have been rejected by **GOD** because of the extraordinary greatness and long duration of its fall, and thus be as far removed as the two poles are from each other—He would nevertheless call it back and unite it with Himself. Yes, He would give it an even greater blessing and a more complete grace than that which it possessed before its fall, because of the purity of the love it would have used toward Him.

v. 6. **GOD** Himself will cut away everything from the heart that contributed to its fall, so that this person may love Him at all times with the whole heart, without taking oneself back, and live again eternally for Him in a more complete life, in consideration of the state in which the soul found itself at its fall.

(The **LORD** your **GOD** will circumcise your heart) With the circumcision of the spirit, on the eighth day, on the day of the spirit of love; and wash and purify it all around, as the 70 translators <note>The Septuagint (Greek translation of the Old Testament).</note> translated it; and take away its deadness, as the Chaldean translation <note>The Targum (Aramaic paraphrase of the Hebrew Bible).</note> expresses it.

When this happens, then man’s love is fixed upon that which is most worthy of love, and he has his delight in that which in all truth is most desirable and joyful.

(That you may love **GOD**, so that you may live) Not as if life must first be earned through the obedience of love; for true spiritual life must already be in a soul beforehand through the new birth from **GOD**. Rather, it means that this life manifests and increases itself through love and faithfulness.

In this pure evangelical sense, **GOD** may indeed promise life to His own from the love and keeping of His commandments. (Leviticus 18:5; Ezekiel 20:11, 13; Luke 10:28).

True, some would point us to faith alone for the advancement of the divine and eternal life and Kingdom of **GOD**: But this is very easily captured in a dangerous misunderstanding, as experience testifies. Therefore, these and similar evangelical insistences must rightly bring us to a healthy concept and impression of it. Love must indeed come from faith, so that one does not perhaps fall into the dangerous error that one could already love **GOD** without the spirit of faith. Oh no! That would be to demand life from the dead. For everything is hypocrisy where one does not first receive a pure heart through faith (Acts 15:9), so that the same can be fruitful through divine, holy love. But on the other hand, it is also a damnable security and a godless opinion if one holds that faith can exist without such love; it indicates infallibly that one has nothing less than true faith dwelling in one's heart.

## 3. And the LORD your GOD will turn your captivity / and have mercy on you / and will again ga-

At the same time, Moses assures us that when souls—having stepped out of the rest of <term>inner surrender [Gelassenheit]</term> <note>Gelassenheit is a central concept in German mysticism, referring to a state of perfect detachment and letting go of the self-will to be filled by God.</note> and through such deviation become guilty and rejected—return again to God and become obedient to him with all their heart, He will also draw them out of their captivity again. If, however, such people are only converted with great difficulty, this does not come from God, who is pure love and mercy and does not desire the death of the sinner, but rather that he should turn and live; He always stretches out His arms to receive those who turn back to Him. For this reason, He died on the cross with outstretched arms.

Therefore, this difficulty arises much more from the side of the soul which, once it has been placed in a certain <term>essential state [wesentlichen Stand]</term> <note>An "essential state" refers to a high level of spiritual advancement where the soul's union with God is so deep it feels like part of its very essence.</note>, finds it difficult to move. Since it has moreover been for a long time in a state where it could not distinguish itself from God because of its close union, it could in no way turn toward God nor away from Him. And since this has become a habit for it, it is impossible for it to change its nature, even though it has actually fallen.

The soul can fall into such a state in only two ways: either through the pride of Lucifer, which moves it to attribute the strength and power of God to itself, finding pleasure in itself in this state and viewing itself in a vain way; from which it is then so misled that it attributes to its own powers and worthiness that which God works in it or through it. And just as these unfaithful people imitate the fallen angels in their fall, having fallen from such a high degree of grace and holiness, so they also imitate them in their lack of repentance, making their conversion all the more difficult the more ingratitude and the less weakness they sin with.

The other way of departing from God is when one takes oneself back so that one intentionally and voluntarily withdraws from the sovereignty of God, so that one can enter back into one's own self-guidance.

These are the two kinds of sins through which the beginning of a soul's corruption comes: the deviation of the spirit, through pride and vain self-complacency; and the deviation of the will, through withdrawal from obedience and the sovereignty of God. This is the source of all the other sins which they afterwards commit. It is also easy to see from this that it happens very difficultly and slowly that they should do such things voluntarily and lose themselves. Therefore, there are not easily examples—or at least very few—of souls who, having already come this far, have fallen from that state again. It is, however, enough that it is possible, in order to be on one's guard against it.

Now the cause which makes these souls have so much trouble returning to God again after their fall is that, because they are confirmed in the state of "essentiality," they are as content in evil as they were confirmed in good. (And this is also what caused the impossibility of Lucifer’s conversion.) But what perhaps makes the matter most impossible is that these people want to tackle repentance from the "active" side, just as before; and those who lead them also want it thus. Which is as impossible as it is useless. Thus you, O you leaders, must only bring those who are in such a state into the sight of their humiliation, without tormenting them with active penance as long as they are capable of it, and meanwhile let them drink in large gulps from the cup of rejection and the wrath of God: so that they may thus learn to remain standing under the justice of God, and be content never to attain forgiveness from God, if such should be His holy will, without worrying whether He will forgive them again and receive them back into grace or not. Since they have fallen so high and have lost so much grace, they must be stripped of all self-interest and thus be presented to all the hardest strokes of God's justice. They must also not force themselves to arrive at a certain kind of prayer which might be lower than that in which they

<column-break/>

## ther you from all the nations where the LORD your GOD has scattered you.
## 4. If

stood at the time they fell. The leaders must also not demand this of them. For it is as impossible a thing as if one wanted to force a person back into his mother's womb; and since one would not be able to accomplish it in the first place, they could moreover be hindered in their progress. Keep them then in their rank, O you fathers of such souls! Abandon them to divine justice without mercy; and do not allow them the very least thing for their deliverance. Oh, what a terrible penance this is, and how few are courageous enough to endure it! This is precisely what has caused so much corruption in the spiritual life after a fall: because the proper means were not applied. One offends the weak and makes the poor fallen ones despair. But if people were faithful and courageous enough to let themselves be destroyed and burned by divine justice, they would in a short time be placed back in a much higher state than the one from which they had fallen. Just as **GOD** promises this through the prophet for the comfort of this kind of penance (a).

<margin>(a) Isaiah 54:8.</margin>

The reasons why such a kind of penance is peculiar to souls who have already come far in contemplation are (besides what has been said elsewhere of it): first, because "nothingness" is the immediate order to the supernatural, where the fullness of **GOD** pours itself out upon the emptiness of the creature.

Now, since the people who have fallen down from this high step stood in a very supernatural state, and are also to be placed back into the same through their return to **GOD**, they have need of the most supernatural divine communications. They must inevitably stand in "nothingness," in the acceptance and love of their rejection, and their eternal abandonment to the will of **GOD**, in order thus to be in the state to be able to receive such things. Otherwise, if they want to fill themselves with new exercises, new inventions of their own, and their own powers, they would thereby place the greatest obstacles in the way of the greatest graces which they need to lift them up and re-introduce them into their state. Just as any form is more easily brought into an empty <term>receptacle [Fürwurf]</term> than into another in which it finds something to remove or to clean.

Secondly, it is also certain that the more the soul renounces its own benefit to sacrifice itself to what is God's, the more it makes itself fit for a faster and more advantageous penance. For nothing can move the heart of **GOD** more to communicate His great mercy than when He looks upon His poor creature, who would rather accept all the hardest strokes of His justice than keep any self-interest for itself or not sacrifice itself entirely to His honor. And precisely then, when the soul is entirely in this disposition, it is already perfectly converted. For it is impossible that sin could persist in the face of such a heroic love, and that grace should not find a place in a heart that burns entirely with such a pure love, since such a heart moreover gladly accepts everything that can be taken for the benefit of **GOD** within the entire scope of His will, His justice, and His power.

Since this is now infallibly the fastest and most perfect penance, and the soul also finds itself driven toward it (because these are fruits of the state from which it fell, and it still possesses a certain ease and agility to perform these renunciations and sacrifices carried so far), one must necessarily also lead them there. One must not only teach them to leave everything to **GOD**, but also give only such medicine for their illness as can both heal them and draw His honor from it, and even to surrender these medicinal means for the sake of the preference given to the will of **GOD** for the healing of the deadly wound. This is the most convenient means for so great an illness. For there is nothing that flows more surely or more orderly in any thing than when it has been surrendered to **GOD** in the most perfect way.

Those who read this might perhaps think that this penance does not correspond to the fall; that there is no sadness or pain, and that it does not grieve the soul. But if they had experience of this, they would confess that nothing in the world equals this pain. It is <term>Purgatory</term> <note>original: "Feg-Feuer," literally "cleansing fire." In this mystical context, it refers to an internal state of purification rather than a physical place.</note>, or even Hell itself (according to the degree in which GOD has placed the soul therein), which is indeed an unspeakable torture. GOD is much more skillful at purifying than all creatures: and the punishments of a justice-exercising GOD are very different from all human inventions of the exercise of justice! Such a soul would much rather endure all possible death-penalties than remain, in the manner just described, faithful and immovable under the hand of divine justice. All exercises of penance that one might impose upon it, even the most severe, would by comparison be a relief and a refreshment to it. However, one must take care not to impose any: because such things would pull the soul even further out of its state and prevent it from being able to be restored to it. It is natural that one stands up again in the same place where one fell, and thus continues his way from there, without returning to the place where one began to walk in order to stand up again; since one fell before the path was finished. Thus, it would also be no penance for such a soul if one only wanted to burden it with pure martyrdoms: it would rather be a refreshment for it. This is easy to understand. The pains of external abstinences and penances grieve the senses, but they comfort the spirit. Since in these souls the senses are very much dead—both because they have previously endured all imaginable mortifications and exercises of penance and have, as it were, become insensitive through them; and also because the senses are separated from the spirit and therefore have no more power to feel either pain or pleasure—their penance must therefore not be measured according to the senses. Rather, so that the punishment for them may be all the more painful and also equal to the crime, it must be a punishment of the spirit: for all their sin is a sin of the spirit.

But now, so that this punishment of the spirit may be intense, deep, and according to the sin, it can be imposed by no one but GOD. For whatever one might then do to the senses would only be a stay and a support for the spirit, which would turn it away from its pain. But when the spirit finds itself buried under the weight of divine justice and sees itself without help and without support, abandoned by the senses which assist it in nothing—oh, this is a terrifying and so coarse a martyrdom that it can only be known through experience alone! It is a fire which, through its activity, penetrates even into the marrow: and perhaps among a thousand fallen people, barely three might be found who would want to let themselves be swallowed up by the justice of GOD as much as it might please Him, without sooner or later—and especially in illnesses or at death—taking themselves back. For then one wants to use all kinds of force to assure oneself of his salvation through his <term>own activity</term> <note>A warning against "self-effort" in salvation, a common theme in Quietist thought where the soul must remain passive to God's work.</note>.

But it is certain that such a soul must work just as little in death as at any other time. On the contrary, one must at that time surrender oneself to the justice of GOD with even greater courage, to bear its weight for all eternity. Oh, this is the purity of <term>disinterested love</term>! <note>Disinterested love (uninteressirte Liebe) is the mystical ideal of loving God for His own sake, without regard for reward or fear of punishment, even being willing to accept damnation if it were God's will.</note> which is unknown to self-love, but is recognized, highly esteemed, and accepted by pure love. A person who might be so happy as to die thus would show GOD an unspeakable honor and would—without going through any purgatory (for what can remain to be purified in a soul that possesses no selfhood anymore and has reached such a heroic love?)—be exalted to the highest rank in heaven: whereas, when one takes oneself back at death, one robs GOD of a great honor and loses an excellent blessedness. Not that such a soul would not be saved: but it will nonetheless have to pay for its despondency in that life.

This is more important than can be said. Therefore, those into whose hands these writings might fall are asked to pay special attention to this.

Indeed, for the promotion of the divine and eternal life and the Kingdom of GOD, some wish to point us to faith alone: but it is very easily caught in a dangerous misunderstanding, as experience testifies. Therefore, these and similar evangelical insistences must rightly impart to us a sound concept and impression of it. Love must indeed come from faith, so that one does not perhaps fall into the dangerous error that one could love GOD even without the spirit of faith. Oh no! this would be to demand life from the dead. For everything is hypocrisy where one does not first receive a pure heart through faith, <margin>Acts 15:9.</margin> so that the same can be fruitful through divine holy love. But it is also, on the other side, a damnable security and a godless opinion if one holds that faith can indeed be without such love, and it indicates unfailingly that one has nothing less than true faith dwelling in his heart.

<margin>v. 7.</margin> **The LORD will lay all curses upon your enemies)** So look up, O Zion! You who have sat so long in dust and ashes, fed with tribulation and bitter heartache, clothed and covered with reproach, mockery, and shame. All those who were hostile to Zion shall bear the guilt—those who trampled your glory underfoot and practiced all manner of wantonness upon you; who killed your sons and daughters, where they lay slain in the streets of the great city called Babylon, Sodom, and Egypt <note>These cities are used figuratively here to represent states of spiritual captivity and wickedness.</note>. Behold, the days of your imprisonment are coming to an end, of which those who shake their heads over you say in their hearts: "Who shall deliver these?" Arise, arise! For your King comes and desires to adorn you before the eyes of all your enemies: and in the sight of all those who have hated and despised you: your seed shall possess the gates of his enemies: those who robbed you shall be robbed in turn; and those who broke you shall be broken in turn! Lift up your head and see your King and Redeemer, how he has raised his banner against all who have troubled you! They shall all be cast out like thistles and come to nothing like the thorns consumed by fire. For the zeal of the LORD of Hosts <note>original: "Zebaoth," a Hebrew title for God as a divine warrior leading heavenly armies.</note> shall burn against them like a fire, and the wrath of the God of Jacob will be kindled over all who have offended you.

<margin>v. 8--10.</margin> Along with the promise of the Holy Spirit, by which the hearts of the Jews shall be circumcised so that they may love God in Christ in holiness and righteousness—from which all spiritual goods spring of their own accord—He will also bring all bodily blessings upon them. Because they will then walk in the ways of God, God will be able to rejoice over them, once they have turned to his dear Son with all their heart. See Romans 9:27, 11:25, etc.

For He takes pleasure in such a soul that has turned back to Him and remains within it with delight: because it is now more than ever freed from old self-love, and because its fall gave it all the more reason to be estranged from itself and to hate its own [selfish] nature, and on the contrary to take up all the more love and trust toward God.

Namely, the Gospel of Christ and his appearance in the flesh, his suffering and resurrection from the dead, would then no longer seem so wonderful <note>In this 18th-century context, "wunderlich" means "mysterious," "strange," or "incomprehensible" rather than "marvelous."</note> and inconceivable to the Jews. <margin>v. 11.</margin> **This commandment is not too wonderful for you, nor far off)** It is not dark, or hard and difficult to understand, nor a burden beyond your power, strength, or ability.

The way of faith is not, as almost everyone thinks, such a very difficult and remote or strange thing that it should extend to only a few people. All people are capable of it; for this requires only a heart completely subjected to God. The most important part of this work depends on His grace, which is equally powerful to perform this in all who surrender themselves entirely to it and are faithful—allowing God to pursue, destroy, and annihilate the "self" within them. The reason, however, why so few are found who want to enter this path is **self-love**. It moves people to look at themselves, to hold onto themselves, and to pay attention to their own interests. They fear surrendering themselves to God because they believe they would do better if they led themselves than if they surrendered themselves entirely to Him.

<margin>v. 12. It is not in heaven)</margin> namely, locked away.

Unbelief imagines for itself a strange, absent Savior who is supposed to make one blessed merely through imagination. It wants to climb up into heaven and fetch Christ from there, because it thinks Christ is locked up there.

But see to it that you do not lose your way and grasp an imaginary Christ—indeed, a false word—instead of the true one. Also, see that you do not, instead of seeking a thorough visitation from Christ, only gape at high mysteries and images of the truth, and say:

**Who will go up to heaven for us and fetch it?)** Almost all excuse themselves in the same way to avoid embarking on the path of faith. "This is too high for me," they say; "it is only for heavenly souls." Since Moses well knew that this would be the most dangerous temptation—and because it is covered with a **veil of humility**—he anticipates them with a clear conviction. For all those who distance themselves from such a good, although they would have the greatest right in the world to it, say: "We are not worthy of it; we may not strive for it: it would be pride in us." But this is not at all true humility, but rather a **faint-heartedness** <note>original: "Kleinmüthigkeit," implying a lack of spiritual courage or smallness of spirit.</note>. This is so true that if such souls could have all the advantages of others without having to risk anything for it, they would gladly accept it. They do not seek the graces, nor the rewards and the crowns that depend on them, but only avoid the suffering and uncertainty required to arrive there through the laying down of all "sensible" and "enlightening" gifts <note>These are spiritual experiences that the soul feels or understands intellectually; the author suggests true faith requires letting go of these comforts.</note>, which they do not like to lose.

### Chapter XXX. The Fifth Book of Moses. 783

13. It is also not beyond the sea, that you might say: Who will go over the sea for us and bring it to us, that he may let us hear it, and we may do it?

Furthermore, it must be admitted that all those who practice the virtue of humility are still very far from the humility that causes annihilation <note>The term "annihilation" (*Vernichtigung*) in this mystical context refers to the total emptying of the self so that only God remains.</note>. Through the virtue of humility, the more you humble yourself, you still make yourself into "something": because you believe that you exist and persist, and that you act with strength and virtue. For it is certain that whoever wishes to lower himself must be "something," and must also be elevated. A person who bows down, or even throws himself upon the earth, must have been standing and elevated before. But he who lies at full length upon the ground cannot lower himself any further, because he is in his greatest lowliness. The more these people think they have lowered themselves through their virtuous humility (which in and of itself is very good for a time, as long as one is still unsuited for anything else), the more they remain secure in their own elevation. This is because the depth of a fall indicates the height from which one was elevated; and in their foundation, they seek a spiritual elevation in a subtle way within this very act of humbling. True humility, as a virtue, will not even enter heaven; rather, it must first pass into annihilation before it is worthy of God and can be filled by Him—yes, by Him alone. But it is not so with the souls of whom we shall now speak. Such souls can neither humble themselves nor let themselves down, because the depth of their lowliness prevents it, as they have fallen into their "Nothingness." And if they wished to do so, they would have to climb back up and thus depart from their state.

Therefore, it is not actually a perfect humility of the creature when one humbles oneself; rather, it is when one loves one's own nothingness, remains standing in that nothingness, lets God act according to His pleasure, and believes that He can do all that He wills. Would it have been humility in Mary if she had refused to become the Mother of God, and thereby placed difficulties in the way of promoting the divine Incarnation? No, certainly not: it would rather have been a subtle and secret pride that would have moved her to do something of herself, or to set herself against the will of God over her.

Clinging to humility cannot be true humility; for such a thing is contrary to pure love, which commands that the creature should not keep the slightest thing for itself, and that everything must be sacrificed to the supreme will of God through a total resignation. Many are mistaken here, supporting their humility through their own will. And by failing in the denial and total death of themselves, they offend divine love while speaking in favor of a humility that is not humility at all where it does not agree with love. If one only had the light to distinguish, one would clearly see that one elevates oneself by the very means through which one seeks to humble oneself; that in intending to annihilate oneself, one seeks one's own preservation; and finally, that one tastes and possesses the "honor" of being humble as a choice virtue, right in the midst of the exercises of humility one performs.

The true "Nothing" does nothing and resists nothing. It lets itself be driven and led wherever one wishes. It believes that God can make everything out of it (without looking at itself), just as He can make everything out of a blade of straw. And there is more humility in believing these things and surrendering to them without desiring anything for oneself than if one tried to resist them. Let us only surrender ourselves courageously! If God makes nothing of us, He will be doing right by us, for we are useful for nothing: and that shall be His glory. But if He undertakes great things with us, then one must say with Mary (a), that He has done great things for us because He has regarded our lowliness.

v. 13. Not beyond the sea) The essential Word is not far from you, so that you would have to travel across the sea for it, as one does for temporal goods.
(a) Luke 1:48, 49.

Is in your heart) This is a truly evangelical speech; which Paul therefore uses in Romans 10:8, where more will be said on the matter.

The Word of God needs to be sought and fetched neither here nor there, neither in the heights nor in the depths, but it is closer to everyone than they can be to themselves; namely, in the secret place of the heart and in the innermost part of the conscience: but, alas, it is recognized, esteemed, or accepted least of all and by the fewest people. James 1:21.

v. 15. Moses now concludes what he had presented so far regarding the renewal of the covenant: namely, that he has shown them the way to eternal life, the essential Good, and also to death and damnation, as the only Evil. This is and has been

Set before you) and the basis of it is in the human being themselves. Whatever a person grasps and nurtures within themselves, that is what they get to eat and enjoy. If someone likes to awaken and keep anger, then they must burn in it. But if one chooses love, then it becomes eternal life in JESUS, the love of the Father. And

These are the two main arteries of the common government in heaven, through which the great Lawgiver binds His people to obedience, from which earthly lawgivers have also taken an example: namely, rewards and punishments. Between these two, however, we should—according to the will of the Lord—rather allow ourselves to be won by the first. Therefore, He also places life and good before death and evil.

Just as He instructs Israel how they should first announce peace to others in their wars, and only if that is not accepted should they strike and kill (ch. 20:10–13), so He also deals with Israel. First, He lets the white banner of His love, goodness, and mercy fly. If one follows that, He graciously promises life and immortality. But if it is despised, He puts out the black flag of enmity, death, and destruction. Romans 2:4–10. He would, of course, much rather that His goodness gently lead us to repentance than that we should have need of compulsion like a dumb, irrational animal. Psalm 32:8, 9. But if such a great goodness of God cannot win us so as to keep us in the way of His commandments, and we instead deviate from Him, then He hedges our way with thorns. Hosea 2:6. If His mercies can accomplish nothing with us, He sends His judgments. If the offered rewards of grace will not move us, He distresses us with His punishments: and if lighter tribulations will not do it, He sends heavier ones.

v. 16. Nothing but obedience to the commandments of God can bring us His true blessing.

->Here he now shows / how this conversion shall take place.<- Namely, the **Gospel of Christ** and His appearance in the flesh / His suffering and resurrection from the dead / would then no longer seem so wonderful <note>In 18th-century German, "wunderlich" means "mysterious," "extraordinary," or "incomprehensible" rather than "marvelous."</note> and incomprehensible to the Jews; so that they would no longer need to expect a Messiah to come down from heaven / or if He were to rise again, to wait for Him to be sent from far-off lands with the Apostles to instruct them in faith in Christ: but all of this would be unlocked in their hearts through the enlightenment of the Holy Spirit / and they would thereby be powerfully converted to Christ; so that to Him alone all honor for this may be given in time and eternity. v. 11. **This commandment is not too wonderful for you / nor far off)** It is not dark / or hard and difficult to understand / nor a burden beyond your power or strength and ability.

## 13. Neither is it beyond the sea, that you might say: Who will go over the sea for us, and bring it to us, that he may cause us to hear it, and we may do it?

One will further admit that all those who practice the virtue of humility are still very far removed from the humility caused by annihilation. Through the virtue of humility, you make yourself into something the more you humble yourself: because you believe that you exist and endure, and that you act with strength and virtue. For it is certain that whoever wishes to humble himself must be something, and even something exalted. A person who stoops down, or even throws himself upon the earth, must have previously been standing and exalted. But he who lies upon the earth at his full length cannot humble himself further, because he is in his greatest lowliness. Now, the more these people imagine themselves to have been humbled through their virtuous humility (which virtuous humility is, in and of itself, very good for a time, so long as one is still unfit for anything else), the more they remain entangled in their own exaltation: because the depth of a fall indicates the height from which one was exalted; and in truth, they seek a spiritual exaltation in a subtle way within this very act of humbling. Actual humility, as a virtue, will not enter heaven; rather, it must first pass into annihilation before it becomes worthy of God and is filled by Him—yes, by Him alone. But with those souls of whom I am now to speak, it is not so. Such souls can neither humble themselves nor let themselves down: for the depth of their lowliness prevents them, as they have already fallen into their "Nothing." <note>The author is describing a state of "mystical death" or "quietism," where the self is so completely surrendered to God that even the active effort to "be humble" is seen as a lingering expression of the ego.</note> And if they wished to do so, they would have to climb back up to a height, and thus depart from their proper station.

Therefore, there is actually no perfect humility of the creature when one actively humbles oneself: rather, it is when one loves one's own nothingness, remains standing in one's Nothing, lets God act according to His good pleasure, and then believes He can do everything He wishes. Would it have been humility in Mary if she had refused to become a Mother of God and thereby placed difficulties in the way of furthering the divine Incarnation? No, certainly not: It would rather have been a subtle and secret pride that would have moved her to do something of herself, or to set herself against the will of God over her.

Attachment to humility cannot be true humility; because such attachment is contrary to pure love, which commands that the creature should not keep the slightest thing for itself, and that everything must be sacrificed to the most holy will of God through a total renunciation. Many err in this, supporting their humility through their own will: and while they fail in the denial and complete dying-off of themselves, they offend divine love while speaking in favor of humility—which is no humility at all where it does not agree with love. If only one had the light to distinguish, one would clearly see that by the very thing through which one strives to humble oneself, one exalts oneself; that in imagining one is annihilating oneself, one seeks one's own preservation; and finally, that one adorns oneself with and possesses the "honor of being humble" as a choice virtue, right in the midst of the practices of humility one performs.

The true "Nothing" does nothing and resists nothing. It lets itself be driven and led wherever one wishes. It believes that God can make everything out of it (without looking at itself), just as He can make everything out of a stalk of straw: and there is more humility in believing these things and surrendering to them without desiring anything for oneself than if one tried to resist them. Let us only surrender ourselves courageously! If God makes nothing out of us, He will do rightly by us; for we are useful for nothing: and that shall be His glory. But if He undertakes great things with us, then one must say with Mary <margin>(a) Luke 1:48, 49.</margin> (a) that He has done great things for us because He has regarded our lowliness.

**v. 3. 4.** Thus he now confirmed Joshua as the commander <term>Heerführer (military leader)</term> who would hold such honor before him and would gloriously carry out everything under the LORD's power.
**v. 5. 6.** They should strengthen themselves only in this power of GOD (Ephesians 6:10) and henceforth prove themselves courageous in the struggle against the enemies, executing GOD's judgments upon them with their total destruction: God would not leave them in the slightest, but would always lead and protect them with his hand.
**v. 7. 8.** He instills this same courage in Joshua with the very same promise that he had also made to the people.
And so it is well when both subjects and rulers strive for the blessing of GOD, in order to share in the precious promises of Christ, and to destroy all enemies who rebel against GOD: then they both may be certain of divine protection and victory.
The exhortation of Scripture otherwise mainly aims at this: that one should never make excuses for refusing a path that seems difficult to the creature who relies on its own strength, but which is very easy in GOD. Take heart, it says, and have good confidence! It is indeed nothing that you can undertake by yourself: but God himself will be your leader. Only surrender yourself to him, and he will not forsake you: he will not leave you alone for even a single moment! Oh, the advantage of serenity <term>Gelassenheit (a state of surrendered trust in God)</term>! The soul does not need to preserve itself, nor to worry about itself. When it leaves itself to GOD, he leads it himself. Oh, what a secure guidance that is!

<column-break/>

9. And Moses wrote this law and gave it to the priests, the sons of Levi, who carried the ark of the covenant of the LORD, and to all the elders of Israel.
10. And Moses commanded them, saying: At the end of seven years, at the appointed time of the year of release <term>Erlaß Jahr (the Sabbatical year of debt cancellation)</term>, at the Feast of Tabernacles,
11. When all Israel comes to appear before the face of the LORD your GOD in the place which he will choose, you shall have this law proclaimed before all Israel in their hearing.
12. Assemble the people, the men and the women and the children and the stranger who is within your gates; so that they may hear, and that they may learn and fear the LORD your GOD, and be careful to do all the words of this law:
13. And that their children, who do not know it, may hear and learn it; so that they may fear the LORD your GOD all the days that you live in the land where you are going over the Jordan to possess it.
14. And

---

**v. 9.** it is most appropriately understood that Moses, at the end of his administration, wrote the entire history of the people of GOD, from the beginning of Creation, and composed it in the five books; which was called "the Law" after the most prominent part contained therein: which he delivered to the priests to read diligently and to instruct the people from; to whom also the ark of the covenant was specially entrusted, which was otherwise carried by the Levites in the wilderness (v. 25 and Numbers 3:31) but on special occasions by the priests (Joshua 3:13, 1 Kings 8:3); and then also to the elders of Israel to uphold such law.
**v. 10. At the Feast of Tabernacles)** This happened at the end of the first day of Tabernacles, when the 7th year came to an end and the new one began, when the trumpet was blown throughout all Jerusalem and the people were called together.
**v. 11.** Then a large part of the 5th Book of Moses was read publicly in the hearing of all the people. This was done by the High Priest, or, where there was a king, by the king himself, on a high wooden pulpit <term>Cangel (platform or pulpit)</term> that was prepared for it.
**v. 12.** Not in the inner Court of Israel, but in the outer Court of the Women, where all the people—including women, children, and servants—could see and hear him. For the women were also meant to hear it, but they were not permitted to enter the inner court.
The sections that were read were these: First, the entire first chapter until the words in Chapter 6:4, "our GOD is one LORD." Thereafter Chapter 11:13 etc. Further Chapter 14:22 etc. And then Chapter 26:12 etc. After this, he went back to Chapter 17:14 etc. Finally, he read the blessings and curses in Chapters 27 and 28.
**v. 13.** The purpose of everything was: so that the descendants might constantly be instructed in the knowledge of the true GOD and his ways and his will; so that one might fear GOD and learn true wisdom.
