# The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XXXI. <note>original: "Das V. Buch Mose"; this is the book of Deuteronomy.</note>

14. And the **LORD** spoke to Moses: Behold, your days have approached that you must die; call Joshua, and present yourselves in the Tent of Meeting, so that I may give him a charge. And Moses went with Joshua, and they presented themselves in the Tent of Meeting.
15. But the **LORD** appeared in the Tent in a pillar of cloud, and the pillar of cloud stood over the door of the Tent.
16. And the **LORD** spoke to Moses: Behold, you shall lie down with your fathers, and this people will rise up and go whoring after the foreign gods of the land where they are going to be among them; and they will forsake me and break my covenant which I have made with them.
17. Then my anger will be kindled against them on that day, and I will forsake them and hide my face from them, so that they shall be devoured, and many misfortunes and anxieties shall befall them. On that day they will say: Have not these misfortunes befallen me because my **GOD** is not in the midst of me?
18. But I will utterly hide my face on that day because of all the evil they have done, in that they have turned to other gods.

<column-break/>

19. Now therefore, write this song for yourselves, and teach it to the children of Israel; put it in their mouths, so that this song may be a witness for me among the children of Israel.
20. For I will bring them into the land which I swore to their fathers, which flows with milk and honey. And when they have eaten and are full and have become fat, then they will turn to other gods and serve them and blaspheme me, and they will break my covenant.
21. And it shall come to pass, when many misfortunes and anxieties befall them, then this song shall answer to their face as a witness: For it shall not be forgotten out of the mouth of their seed. For I know their thoughts which they are already entertaining today, before I bring them into the land that I have sworn.
22. So Moses wrote this song on that same day and taught it to the children of Israel.
23. And <meta>catchword: They</meta>

---

Here He now delivers to Moses a special song, wherein He presents to the Jewish people their future condition until the end of this world through His omniscient Spirit: which they were to learn by heart, and for their future instruction and warning, strive for it in faith with a contrite, repentant spirit; but also for the encouragement of all repentant hearts among them, showing how **GOD** would finally turn back to them in grace and allow Himself to be reconciled through His dear Son.

This song was to be a witness in their mouths: how **GOD** had fulfilled all His promises to them, and especially the last and most prominent one—the sending of the promised Seed of the Woman, the Seed of Abraham, that is, Shiloh <note>A title for the Messiah from Genesis 49:10.</note>, the Peacemaker, the Messiah—which He would fulfill in His own time.

v. 14. **GOD** here specifically commanded Joshua to be called.
v. 15. And appeared to him in the pillar of cloud, just as He had always appeared to Moses therein: by which He wished to show the people how He would henceforth also reveal Himself to Joshua, to lead and govern them through him in all their doings.
v. 16. He also announces to them beforehand how they would further sin in the future with disobedience and idolatry: which occurred especially in the times of Solomon and also thereafter (see 1 Kings 11:2 etc.).
v. 17. 18. Therefore **GOD** would allow them to fall into great tribulations: as happened initially under the Judges at various times, and afterwards especially in the Babylonian captivity, and then following that under the Syrian and Egyptian kings; of which the Books of the Maccabees <note>Historical books covering the Jewish revolt against the Seleucid Empire in the 2nd century BCE.</note> and their historian Josephus <note>Titus Flavius Josephus, a 1st-century Romano-Jewish historian.</note> treat at greater length: where **GOD** often left them in distress for a long time, yet always took pity on them again until Christ appeared among them, at which time they lived in considerable outward prosperity.

<column-break/>

v. 20. Whom, however, they would blaspheme, despise, and reject, and so at the same time reject the New Covenant which He wished to establish with them through Him, of which the prophet Jeremiah prophesied at greater length (Jer. 31:31).
That Christ is thus dealt with here in a hidden way—He who would appear among them in the flesh—the prophets afterwards prophesied so manifoldly, sometimes of His birth (Isa. 7:14; 9:6-7) and how He would speak with them face to face (Isa. 40:5; 52:6-8; 35:4; 9:9; Mal. 3:1) and in other places besides: but since they would sin so grossly against this, their **GOD** and Savior, by rejecting Him and His new covenant of grace, it is spoken of more clearly in the song itself in verse 15.
v. 21. Then the great misfortune would befall them for the last time, which is also treated at greater length in the song, which would almost finish them off in the Roman destruction, had not **GOD** resolved to have mercy for Christ’s sake and to be reconciled in Him (Chap. 32:43).

---

All the evil that happens to people occurs only because **GOD** is not with them, both because they are utterly forsaken through mortal sin, and because they withdraw themselves from Him through a lack of courage to remain in yieldedness <term>Gelassenheit (a state of surrendered, quiet submission to God's will)</term>, namely, by taking themselves back after their surrender. But as long as one remains constant in yieldedness to **GOD**, there is nothing to fear, and no evil can touch us.

# Chapter XXXI. The Fifth Book of Moses <note>Deuteronomy</note>

23. And he commanded Joshua, the son of Nun, and said: Be strong and of good courage! For you shall bring the children of Israel into the land that I have sworn to them, and I will be with you.

<margin>Be strong) We should not wait in a lazy state of surrender <note>The author warns against a passive "quietism" where one does nothing while waiting for divine aid.</note> until God strengthens us, but rather—especially a leader—must stir up the gift of God that is within us. 2 Timothy 1:6.</margin>

When souls who are to be led require strength to allow themselves to be guided without fear along a path that appears to most to be full of steep precipices, and which the human spirit cannot grasp, then those who are meant to lead others have even greater need of it. These leaders must not only endure their own specific attacks and experience their own personal fear of being led astray, but they must also take upon themselves all the terrors and anxieties of all those whom God sends to them to lead. They must bring them into this terrifying wilderness which, according to reason and understanding—even when spiritually enlightened—is a true and unavoidable darkening and downfall. And not only this, but these leaders of souls must also withstand all the blows that should have fallen upon those who are subordinate to them. And such is a very heavy burden.

It commonly happens that when a leader loves inward reflection <note>original: "Einckehr," referring to a state of meditative or mystical interiority.</note>, not only all fleshly-minded people but even the devils themselves are against him. And if they can find nothing to fault in his behavior, they still complain about his associations and want to burden the leader with all the weaknesses and faults of those he leads. And this is an exceeding great injustice; for all faults belong to the person who commits them. If God—in order not to violate their free will—does not prevent such souls from falling, and indeed sometimes draws even more glory from their fall because they are humbled by it (or for other secret but very just reasons), on what grounds can one demand that the leader be responsible for all the failings of those he leads? Was Judas poorly led under the immediate and visible guidance of Jesus Christ? Was St. Peter not one of the most prominent among the Apostles, and yet he fell most heavily? Why then should one interpret it poorly for the leaders when souls encounter some weaknesses, without blaspheming their path? One sees that many thousands are lost outside of this path, and yet people remain silent about that. But if a single soul on this path commits a fault—which often might only be a fault in appearance—the whole world murmurs about it and attributes a personal deficiency to the path and the leadership itself.

Thus, a leader must possess great fortitude and great faithfulness if he is not to give up, despite the tribulations inflicted upon him, and bring the souls to the end. Such a person can be assured that God is with him. Often, when leaders see themselves so oppressed and persecuted, they leave everything behind and lose their courage; indeed, because they believe everything is crumbling in their hands, they may even go so far as to become unfaithful and flee from their solitude. Let them be exhorted in the name of God never to do such a thing! This is exactly what the devil wants through all the persecutions he stirs up against them; he tries to make it seem as though everything is being sustained in the others they lead, while they themselves suffer the greatest damage and become a cause for the loss of many souls who, because they have no leader, never reach the place prepared for them. One cannot believe how much Satan gains by this! And for this very reason, he raises up so many ramparts. He even makes use of good souls to reach his goal: by misleading them under all sorts of false appearances of spiritual intentions to rebel against this pure leadership; then they imagine they are doing God a service when they persecute His dearest friends. <note>original footnote (a): John 15:21, 16:2.</note> God, however, uses these very same means to strengthen His faithful servants in His love. Yet this does not prevent Him from occasionally punishing their persecutors and finally opening their eyes to recognize His truth, so that they may return to themselves.

27. For I know your disobedience and your stiff neck. <note>original footnote (a): Isaiah 48:4.</note> Behold, while I am still alive with you today, you have been disobedient against the Lord! How much more then after my death? <note>Acts 20:29.</note>

So misfortune will befall you in the latter days; because you have done evil in the eyes of the Lord, to provoke him to anger through the work of your hands.

# The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XXXII.

<header>The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XXXII.</header>

## Chapter XXXII.

->The Song of Moses.<-

<margin>Isaiah 1:2.</margin>
**1. Give ear, O heavens, and I will speak; and let the earth hear the words of my mouth!**

**2. My doctrine shall drop as the rain, my speech shall flow as the dew, as the drizzle upon the grass, and as the showers upon the herb.**

This mystery-filled song—which God Himself, and indeed Christ, the Angel of the Covenant, delivered through Moses to the entire Israelite Church as a witness—contains within it a justification of His ways toward them during their destruction due to their ingratitude and disobedience. It specifically addresses the great sin of rejecting and terribly mistreating Him as the Rock of Salvation during His appearance. Yet, in the end, He raises them up again with the hope of their redemption, so that they might laud and praise Him together with the Gentiles.

In verse 1, he first calls upon heaven and earth as witnesses, who must acknowledge His justice in His dealings with His people. By this, we must actually understand the holy angels and all inhabitants of the earth who will come to the knowledge of the great salvation in Christ. They are to judge that Christ, according to His justice, could not have dealt with this people of the Old Testament in any other way.

**I will speak)** and that not secretly, but publicly, before the firmament of heaven, so that everyone may hear it.

**The earth hear)** in all ages <note>original: "Seculis," referring to long spans of time or world-eras.</note>, across its entire length and breadth, with all who dwell upon it.

According to the spirit and the inner meaning, this song is perhaps known to few. For one must have advanced very far in God if one wishes to understand it. It is the "new song" which is sung in heaven before the Lamb, and which was given to Moses at the end of his days in the flesh as a pattern of that which he should sing eternally in glory.

Blessed is he who receives this song and understands it in some measure through the Center Point <note>A mystical term referring to the deepest part of the soul where the human meets the Divine.</note>; which comes from God Himself and is sung in the "soul without soul." For the soul does nothing else but receive and give back the voice and words that are placed within it.

In verse 2, although the soul returns all honor and praise to its God, it nevertheless confesses that everything coming out of its mouth is great and fruitful, because it proceeds from God Himself, just as the rain and dew that make the earth fruitful come from heaven. For all the words of those souls who are truly annihilated <note>The term "annihilated" (German: *vernichtiget*) in this mystical context refers to the state where a person's ego and self-will have been completely surrendered to God.</note> strike home and cause much fruit to come forth because of their fertility.

**My doctrine shall drop — flow as)** That it might not only penetrate deeply, but also have the effect that dew and rain have upon the

**Grass and herb)** Which are thereby refreshed and brought to life and growth.

He thereby indicates the blessing that this presentation of His would have among angels and men in the proclamation of the Gospel. For even the angels "longed to look" into that which was proclaimed by the Apostles, sent from heaven through the Holy Spirit (1 Peter 1:12). This then had a great blessing among Jews and Gentiles, so that the Word fell upon their hearts like a fruitful rain and dew and did not return empty, but accomplished that for which it was sent. See Isaiah 55:10, 11; Psalm 72:6. And because the drizzle and showers tend to fall during very warm times and sunshine, these may well signify the refreshments in tribulations with which the proclamation of the Gospel is occasionally intertwined.

Truthful in His promises: and because He is without injustice, He cannot deceive us. Thus He returns what is given to Him with abundance. As one who is upright, one need only follow Him to walk in righteousness; for no deceit is to be found in Him.

<column-break/>

**3. For I will proclaim the name of the LORD: Give majesty to our God!**

**4. He is the Rock, whose work is perfect! For all his ways are right. He is a faithful God, and there is no injustice: Just and upright is he!**

In verse 3, the sum of the Gospel is reported: that Christ proclaimed the name of the Lord, as that Name was in Him (Exodus 23:21). He later proclaimed this in the days of His flesh when He preached the Kingdom of God and explicitly said: "I have manifested Your name to the men whom You gave Me out of the world" (John 17:6). And there He taught us how we must give the proper honor, majesty, and glory to God the heavenly Father, and also to Him the Son, as the true God.

**I will proclaim)** The annihilated soul is in a state to call upon the Lord in a new way: because it no longer calls upon Him for its own sake, but for the sake of His own honor; so that its worship is nothing other than a declaration of the glory of God.

In verse 4, Christ now also describes Himself—who He is, and how He proved and commended Himself at the revelation of His presence in the flesh to the hearts of all the good-hearted and faithful (who became His children precisely by accepting Him). Namely, that He is the Rock to which one must take refuge, just as in former times one turned to castles built upon rocks to be safe from enemies. See Proverbs 18:10. Therefore His work or undertaking is perfect: namely the great work of redemption, which He carried out so perfectly that with one sacrifice He has perfected forever those who are being sanctified (Hebrews 10:14). And so all His ways—which He undertook in His teachings, miracles, deeds, rebukes, and all His endeavors—were right. All the promises of God became "Yes and Amen" in Him (2 Corinthians 1:20); for God first proved Himself in Him, and He proved Himself, as the faithful and true God who committed no sin and in whose mouth no deceit was found (1 Peter 1:19, 2:22). Therefore He is emphatically called "the Just One" in many places (Isaiah 53:11, 1 John 2:1, etc.), and He showed Himself upright and sincere in all His doing. He sought the salvation of men with all faithfulness and earnestness, and never let it lack for faithful exhortations, warnings, or works of love.

**Whose work is perfect)** Moses means to say: Why does one not let oneself be led by God, since everything He does is so perfect that anything found to be deficient is only because the creature has laid its own hands upon the work?

**All his ways)** or leadings, in which man should have walked,

**Are right)** and blameless, even if they might seem like foolish leadings to the fleshly-wise, because they are founded only upon blind abandonment <note>original: "Gelassenheit," a central Pietist concept meaning total yieldness or surrender to God's will.</note>, which excludes all human deliberation and all human strength. For by relying on God and losing all one's own caution, one uses the very greatest caution through this means. Is it not a great caution to hand over one's own weakness to such a strong Protector, and to entrust one's treasure to such a faithful Friend? Especially since one finds oneself so powerless to preserve it oneself; indeed, one is rather certain that one would lose it, or at least put it in great danger, if one tried to preserve it by oneself.

As a faithful one, He will never abandon us; for

5. As- <note>Catchword for the next page, beginning the word "As faithful..." or similar.</note>

<summary>This page contains the opening of the Song of Moses, interpreted through a mystical and Christocentric lens, emphasizing God's perfect justice and the soul's need for total surrender to His leading.</summary>
<keywords>Song of Moses, Rock of Salvation, Christ as Angel of the Covenant, mystical annihilation of the soul, Gelassenheit, justification of God, perfection of redemption</keywords>

<meta>This page continues the commentary on the "Song of Moses" from Deuteronomy 32, moving from the opening invocation of heaven and earth to the specific indictment of Israel’s unfaithfulness and the definition of true spiritual surrender.</meta>

### 5. Has he corrupted them? Not at all! His children are their blemish: of the perverse and crooked generation.

Here, the crime of His people, with which they have so grossly sinned, is announced in advance. And indeed, through Moses, God first earnestly clears Himself of the guilt: that He has by no means corrupted His people; namely, that He did not become enraged against them so quickly because of one or two crimes, nor did He visit them with the great judgment of rejection for such a long time without cause.

He presents this as a question, in order to submit it to the investigation of all justice-loving souls: whether this great destruction can in any way be attributed to a violent wrath of God that once flared up over their manifold sins which they committed against Him? To this He says, No! Not at all: it was a particularly heavy sin with which this perverse and crooked generation sinned—just as this sinful people was also specifically branded as such in the time of Christ, Philippians 2:15 (see also Isaiah 1:4). Specifically, His children—those who recognized and accepted Him, the Rock of Salvation (as can be seen in Peter in the name of all the other disciples)—because these were lowly fishermen, tax collectors, and the like, whom the elites counted among the great sinners, they despised them in their eyes and held them to be a blemish among them and a curse. Just as they expressly said: *Does any of the rulers or the Pharisees believe in him? But this crowd that does not know the law is accursed!* John 7:48-49. See also Matthew 21:14, 20, 31; Luke 7:34-35. And so it also happened after Christ's ascension, when those who were despised and foolish in the eyes of the wise and prudent of this world were called by God and chosen as His children, 1 Corinthians 1:26. They held these to be vagabonds or useless babblers <note>original: "unnütze Wäscher," a derogatory term for someone who talks nonsense, echoing the "babbler" in Acts 17:18</note>, Acts 17:18, mockers and deceivers, even though God had chosen them as His witnesses of the truth, Acts 9:15. And

So it happens at all times when God awakens a special testimony against the corruption among His people. Indeed, when Christ allows the testimony of His coming to His glorious Kingdom to go forth with power, then His witnesses will also be held as dreamers and deceivers, who will not be allowed to step forward anywhere even with the boldness to testify: which will then be the heavy sin that brings the final judgments of total destruction—presented in the sixth seal—over the external Church of the New Testament, just as it happened then over the Church in the Old Testament.

**Has he corrupted them)** This means that this work no longer resembles the image according to which it was created. Righteousness, or conformity with the upright God, has transformed into the crookedness and perversity of a

**Crooked generation)** or conformity with the devil, the crooked serpent, Isaiah 27:1.

Moses, in the ecstasy of the spirit, had no sooner made known to the people of Israel the advantage which they felt and would feel in surrendering themselves to God, than he immediately testifies against them through a prophetic spirit: how they, when they removed themselves from God, would not worthily bear the name of the children of God. And these are the ones who do not want to enter into *Gelassenheit* <term>Gelassenheit: A key term in German mysticism meaning "yieldedness," "resignation," or "surrender to God's will."</term>; or those who, although they have come far through the help of surrender, nevertheless take themselves back <note>meaning they reclaim their own will</note> in the time of the greatest and hardest trials.

The interrupted speech that he uses shows the loftiness of his spirit in God: and what seems to the mind to have little order is brought into order in a holy way by the Holy Spirit, who speaks through the mouth of this great prophet.

...the delight of the creature in Him. Do not think you are the only ones who walk in such terrifying ways. Many people have walked through them before you, and many others accompany you in them, even if you do not know them. God demands from His most beloved surrendered ones tests of naked faith and generous love, which correspond to the greatness of the surrender He has placed in them. Do not wonder, even if all others seem to you to walk quite differently. For the paths of those who want to go of their own accord, and desire to know where they are going—even if they rely on their Beloved—are different from the paths of those who let themselves be moved by their love and surrender themselves blindly to it. But stay just a little longer on the testimony of the ancients, until you can go to God alone through God Himself, without any other support.

<column-break/>

### 6. Should you repay the LORD this way, you foolish and unwise people? Is he not your Father, who has acquired you? It is he who has made you and established you.

### 7. Remember the days of old: consider the years from generation to generation: ask your father, and he will show it to you; your elders, and they will tell it to you. 8.

He wants to say by this that they should remember their first fathers—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—and upon what they had placed their salvation. Furthermore, why He had distributed such a particularly good land to them as an inheritance; namely, that they should expect therein the Shiloh <note>A messianic title from Genesis 49:10</note> and Savior of the world, whom the nations would obey: since the Lord had indeed accepted them generally as His inheritance, but would yet declare how they would not all be His children of the promise, but only the believers among them, whom He would accept along with the Gentiles as the Israel of God and His inheritance. See Romans 9:6, etc.; Galatians 6:16.

In verse 6, the people are confronted with their base ingratitude toward the manifold physical blessings, which should have brought them to the knowledge of salvation for their souls (of which verse 15 speaks). But because they were not faithful in small things, they could not become capable of the greater, spiritual salvation. Therefore, they are called a people who willfully rob themselves of their understanding and of the wisdom they could have had if they had kept God's law constantly before their eyes. See Chapter 4:6. Since they could have learned to recognize through Christ that He was the one who had purchased and acquired them as His own property through His precious ransom: Exodus 15:16; 1 Peter 1:18-19. Yes, who is also their Creator who made them—which is otherwise properly attributed to the Father (see Job 35:10; Isaiah 54:5)—and who finally also established them, and thus prepared, empowered, strengthened, and grounded them; which is properly the work of the Holy Spirit. And thus Christ wanted to bring them to the knowledge of the true Triune God, if they had been willing to pay attention to all preceding blessings.

The word **repay** <note>original: "vergelten"</note> is used to indicate the giving back of everything that we possess from Him as a gift. Just as it is certain that God has given us everything we are, so we must also give back to Him everything we are. And this happens through the abandonment of all goods, honors, life, and soul, salvation, eternity, righteousness, holiness, and finally everything that makes up both our exterior and interior. Is it not to have lost one's understanding when one does not do such a thing?

**Is God not your Father?** Has He not love and affection enough for you? Must He not possess you, and do you not belong to Him by right? Must He not possess you as His own property? And since He knew how to form you, should He not also be capable of preserving you, yes, if it were His will, of bringing you forth anew?

**v. 7. Remember** what you have known from of old, so that the experience of God's goodnesses may increase your trust. Ask your fathers and grandfathers who walked in these ways, how it went for them. For even if they appear to you as a terrifying wilderness, and it might seem to you that they aimed only at an eternal loss; yet those who have completed such a long, arduous, and dark course will assure you that these ways end in nothing less than God Himself, who is finally found quite alone through the happy loss of all things in walking such terrifying ways.

<meta>This page continues the line-by-line commentary on the "Song of Moses" in Deuteronomy 32. Having established God's faithfulness and Israel's corruption on the previous page, the text now focuses on God's sovereign choice of Israel and His tender, parental care for His people during their wilderness wanderings.</meta>

<header>The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter 32.</header>

### 8. When the Most High divided to the nations their inheritance, when he separated the children of men from one another; he set the boundaries of the peoples according to the number of the children of Israel.
<margin>(a) Acts 17:26.</margin>

### 9. For the Lord’s portion is his people; Jacob is the cord of his inheritance. <note>The "cord" or "line" refers to a measuring line used to divide land into portions.</note>

### 10. He found him in a desert land, in a waste, howling wilderness <margin>(a)</margin>. He surrounded him and instructed him: He kept him as the apple of his eye.
<margin>Ps. 17:8. (a) ch. 8:15.</margin>

---

<margin>v. 8. He set the boundaries of the nations according to the number of the children of Israel)</margin> This does not only mean that for the then-unborn Israel—which was yet to come—a sufficient space was designated (which the Canaanites were to occupy in the meantime), as the common interpretation suggests. It also means that, as the Hebrews note, God looked simultaneously at the number of Israel and counted and divided the nations accordingly. Thus, some (a) count 72 nations or languages of the world, with which Luke also agrees in the genealogy of Christ in Gospel chapter 3, showing 72 generations from Christ back to Adam. So also writes the apostolic disciple Clement (b): "Every nation has its angel to whom the administration of that nation is entrusted. — For the Most High God divided the nations of the entire earth into 72 parts and appointed angels as princes over them." The translation of the 70 Interpreters <note>original: "70 Dolmetschen," referring to the Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Old Testament.</note> actually has this in the text itself, saying "according to the number of the angels of God" instead of "according to the number of the children of Israel."

<margin>v. 9. The cord)</margin> With which the Israelites formerly used to measure their lands in the Promised Land; the line of His inheritance, which He chose and selected for Himself, in order to gather and establish His Church among them.

God has, from the very beginning, separated the children of Adam (who lead themselves) from His own children, whom He has set apart to be His people and His appointed portion. Surrendered people <note>The German "gelassenen" implies a state of spiritual yielding or "Gelassenheit," where the soul lets go of its own will to rely entirely on God.</note> are very happy to be God's appointed portion. As soon as God becomes our only portion, we also become His: while others, meanwhile, remain heirs of Adam. And since Adam makes up a good part of their inheritance, all is labor for both Adam and them; everything is bounded for them. But in the Lord, there is nothing but rest for His children; everything is full of freedom, full of expansion, and full of immensity.

<margin>v. 10. He also brings to their minds how He held them together in the terrible wilderness—where nothing but murmuring and howling was heard from them—instructed them in His Holy Spirit, and carefully protected them.</margin>

But where did God find this people? And how did He recognize that they were His? Truly in the desert, in the total separation from all creatures, in the emptying of all good things, in the loss of all supports—in that place of solitude, terrifying to both nature and spirit, where the soul finds itself quite naked and alone, unaccompanied by any thing. It is there that God can most conveniently deal with the soul. Oh, then He takes care of her and instructs her in His purest truths: He preserves her

<margin>as the apple of his eye)</margin> This word expresses God's care very well; these words fit these matters so well and so precisely that it is impossible to add anything without robbing them of some of their beauty.

<margin>(a) Irenaeus, book 3, Against Heresies, ch. 33. Epiphanius, book on Measures and Weights. Augustine, book 16, City of God, ch. 3, 7. Zeno of Verona, sermon on Ps. 128. Genebrard, Chronology for the years 1850 & 2649. (b) Recognitions, book 2, folio 32.</margin>

<column-break/>

### 11. As an eagle stirs up her nest, flutters over her young, he spread abroad his wings, took him, and bore him on his pinions.
<margin>Isa. 31:5.</margin>

### 12. The Lord alone did lead him, and there was no foreign god with him.

---

<margin>v. 11. The tender love of God toward His creatures, and especially toward His faithful people, is compared with the fervor of birds toward their young; there is not a single word in this verse that does not provide edification.</margin>

As an eagle stirs up her nest) and encourages her young to fly; so also Christ teaches His disciples self-denial—to leave the "nest" of selfhood, to gradually soar and rise to God, to trust themselves to the guidance of His Spirit as the free air, and to venture forth in faith. God encourages surrendered souls, as His children, to follow Him, to abandon themselves to Him, to surrender, and to let themselves be led. Therefore, He hovers over them like an eagle.

Flutters over her young) wanting to encourage and make them courageous, and also wanting to entrench and protect them; through this hovering, He gives them His Spirit. He

Spreads abroad his wings) over them, to hide them from the storm of the times, of the cross, of persecutions, and from the arrows of Satan and the flesh. He preserves them from all danger and covers them with His protection (a). Under the shadow of His wings: and not only this, but for even better security, He takes them to Himself and carries them on His shoulders.

O you all-too-happy souls! While you are raised up on this royal eagle, you look from above and high down upon all the other little birds, who tire themselves out fluttering around laboriously, and must also constantly hover in danger of being devoured by hawks, falcons, and other birds of prey; and who, moreover, barely rise a little from the earth. But you, you happy young eagles, you approach heaven without any effort! You rest and yet fly; according to our rest-filled flight, you nevertheless surpass all things. And although you move forward in a very swift manner, you are not in the least bit weary; because your progress itself is a perfect rest, and you progress all the more, the more you rest in stillness upon the shoulders of this heavenly eagle. What a happiness which cannot be grasped, but yet can be experienced! Namely, when one gives oneself over and entirely surrenders to God.

v. 12. But where does the happiness of these souls come from? Is it indeed such an undeserved happiness? It is because God alone has been their leader, without having had any foreign help with Him.

O you poor souls, who trouble yourselves greatly in the multiplicity of your ways! If you could recognize the happiness of the souls who rest in the arms of Providence without the effort of caring for all things themselves, you would be astonished at it; and you would regret all the paths you have lost by walking with all your might without moving further ahead.

The Lord alone) So that they stood in need of no other help. And though He did employ the Angel of the Covenant here (Exodus 23:20-21), yet that was no foreign help from creatures, like a created angel, but it was Christ, the true God Himself, who thus alone and everywhere led, governed, protected, and sustained them; and who still leads and governs so many millions of people—each of whom needs His special guidance—each according to his measure. Rightly should we therefore cling to the Lord alone with thankful love and renounce all selfhood until the end, so that God may be great and glorified above all.

<margin>(a) Ps. 17:8.</margin>

<meta>catchword: great</meta>

<summary>This page interprets the Song of Moses (Deuteronomy 32:8-12), emphasizing God's sovereign choice of Israel among the nations and His tender, eagle-like care for surrendered souls in the wilderness. It contrasts the rest found in God's guidance with the weary labor of those who rely on their own strength or "selfhood."</summary>

<meta>This page continues the line-by-line commentary on the "Song of Moses" in Deuteronomy 32. Having previously described God’s guidance through the wilderness, the text now focuses on the abundance of the Promised Land and the subsequent spiritual "fattening" and rebellion of the people of Israel.</meta>

<header>Chapter XXXII. The Fifth Book of Moses.</header>

### 13. He made him ride on the high places of the earth, that he might eat the increase of the fields; and he made him to suck honey out of the rock, and oil out of the flinty rock.

### 14. Butter of kine, and milk of sheep, with fat of lambs, and rams of the breed of Bashan, and goats, with the fat of kidneys of wheat; and thou didst drink the pure blood of the grape.

**v. 13.** Who also thereafter, after the arduous pilgrimage through the wilderness was endured, brought them into the Promised Land, and there made the mighty ones along with their fortresses—as the "heights of the earth"—subject to them; a manner of speaking which is also used regarding the final overcoming of all enemies of the Church in chapter 33:29 and Isaiah 58:14.

A soul that is thus carried on the wings of God ascends to a high land, both because of its high mountains and because of its excellent fertility; that is: above everything that is created, both the heavenly and the earthly, above all pure concepts, and above all powers and virtues. She penetrates everything and finds rest only in God alone, to whom He Himself leads her on the wings of His providence and His love.

Then this soul eats of the fruits of the field: in that she nourishes herself with nothing more than the most exquisite thing, which is God Himself and His holy will. The will of God is the fruit of all lands. For all the labor that must be spent in other ways is directed solely toward this: that one might thereby attain the knowledge and fulfillment of God's will. But this soul eats the fruits thereof without having to cultivate them; because she herself is transformed into Him in a constant state, without ever departing from it again, unless she were to commit a Luciferian infidelity. She also enjoys there

<margin>Honey from the rock</margin> which in this soul indicates the good qualities of the rock, which are: its firmness, its hardness, its insensitivity, and its immovability. Thus is this soul fastened in the will of God like a rock. She also has its hardness: for no arrows nor any blows can cause her harm, and everything is broken at her feet without being able to penetrate her. In other respects, she is also insensitive toward all bodily, human, and spiritual things, like a stone: and finally, she is as immovable as a rock; for she can neither move from her state nor turn back, even if all of hell rose up against her. This is what is called sucking honey from the rock. Thereafter she also draws

<margin>Oil from the hardest rock</margin> Namely: although she is so firm, hard, immovable, and insensitive to everything, and fastened in the will of God, in which she remains unchangeable; yet a heavenly oil and balm flows out of this rock which—though the rock feels nothing of it—nevertheless penetrates everything that approaches it, and pours itself powerfully into the hearts that God sends to her.

**v. 14. Fat)** according to the biblical manner of speaking, signifies the best in every thing. Genesis 4:4, Psalm 81:17, 147:14.

**Bashan)** was the fertile land which they had taken from Og, the Amorite king: there, as well as in Canaan, there was blessed livestock breeding, especially of sheep, and also a blessing of precious wine; by which, in the case of the

**Wine-berry blood)** <note>original: "Weinbeeren-Blut," a poetic term for red wine</note> the particular goodness of a land can be perceived, as the red wines also have a special strength and grace, and thus bear witness to the goodness of the land, as was also promised in Genesis 49:11-12.

It is to be noted, however, that not everything is to be understood as past events, though expressed here in the past tense: rather, it happens *anticipatively* <note>original: "anticipative," meaning in anticipation of the future</note>, in a prophetic manner, where the future is presented as past or present.

<column-break/>

### 15. But Jeshurun waxed fat, and kicked: thou art waxen fat, thou art grown thick, thou art covered with fatness; then he forsook God which made him, and lightly esteemed the Rock of his salvation (a). <margin>(a) Ps. 95:1.</margin>

### 16. They [provoked him to jealousy with strange gods...]

Now he comes to the description of the principal sin with which they provoked God to their rejection: where the name is very significant:

**Jeshurun)** which is as much as to say: "they shall see": namely the Messiah, whom God will send to them as the Rock of their salvation, in whom alone they were to seek their eternal salvation, as the foundation and cornerstone toward which all prophecies aim; such as Genesis 49:24, 18; Psalm 118:22-23; Isaiah 28:16; Zechariah 3:9. Above all this, Christ expressly calls Himself the Rock upon which He would build His congregation. Matthew 16:18. And Paul also calls Him the Rock in 1 Corinthians 10:4.

Furthermore, three stages of benefits are recounted of this people: that it became **fat**; which can fit the time of the Judges: it became **thick**; in the times of the Kings: and finally **strong** (or, as it can be called according to the emphasis, **entirely covered with fat**); which happened after the Babylonian captivity, when they spread far and wide and possessed great wealth in all places.

In the face of such countless proven benefits and all the abundance that God let come to them, they should have honored, loved, and feared Him. But see, instead of this, oh base ingratitude! Three sins are also reported, which likewise steadily increased: in that they, with their manifold disobedience, already kicked out like a wanton calf in the times of the Judges, and would not be told; see Acts 9:5. Then, that they "let God go" <note>original: "Gott haben fahren lassen," meaning to abandon or forsake God</note>; which occurred with their manifold idolatry, indeed already in the times of the Judges, but even more so later in the times of the Kings, when Solomon went astray with a bad example, whom thereafter Jeroboam and all the kings in Israel—especially Ahab—and also some in Judah, such as Manasseh, followed. Yes, their choice of a king also belongs here, of which God Himself testifies that they had thereby rejected Him, so that He should not be king over them. 1 Samuel 8:7.

Finally follows the greatest sin, which they committed in the rejection of Christ as the Rock of their salvation, whom they not only did not receive when He came to them as His own people, John 1:11, but moreover

**Shamefully mistreated)** <note>original: "Schändlich mißhandelt"</note> This is an emphatic word, which can first mean to regard one as a fool. This includes all the blasphemies, and then also the shameful mistreatment which they practiced upon Him during His life, and especially in His suffering, yes, even when they still scolded Him as a deceiver after His death. Matthew 27:63-64. Thereafter, it signifies to make someone wither; namely to kill him through a violent death: which happened in the crucifixion, where they let Him gradually give up the spirit through the very painful draining of His blood.

After Moses has depicted the blessed souls who have entered into the nakedness of the wilderness, as well as those who have allowed themselves to be brought to God; he now also describes those who have been led through illuminations and through "taste," and calls them the **fat ones**. The first were only carried by God; because they were entirely annihilated: and these, who seem to be God’s most beloved and pleasant, have forsaken or forgotten God only because they were too fat. They were fattened, and thereafter they exalted themselves. This is common to the state of illumination, that God makes the soul fat through a certain fullness which is communicated to her. And then she begins to exalt herself, because she finds herself, in her imagination, in a much better condition than others: so that, while she is full, she rests in her fullness, which is like a fatness and the fulfillment of the three qualities and powers of the soul—namely the understanding, the will, and the memory. And because she recognizes nothing better, she believes she has already come to the end of her course.

<meta>This page continues the line-by-line commentary on the "Song of Moses" in Deuteronomy 32. The previous page discussed the spiritual "fattening" of the people of Israel and their subsequent rebellion against God after receiving His abundance. This page moves into the specific nature of their idolatry and the divine response.</meta>

<header>The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XXXII.</header>

> 16. They provoked Him to jealousy with strangers; with abominations they provoked Him to anger.
> 17. They sacrificed to the demons of the field, not to God; to gods <gloss>(a)</gloss> whom they knew not; to new ones who came from nearby, whom your fathers did not fear. <gloss>(a)</gloss> Psalm 106:37.

Those who have reached this point <note>referring to a high state of spiritual "enlightenment" mentioned on the previous page</note> already possess a great assurance of their salvation; and the goodness of their state does not allow them to doubt it. From this, however, two types of evil befall them. First, they attribute everything to their own faithfulness, which then moves them to despise others. These others seem much more imperfect to them, even if, in truth, they have progressed further—provided they have been truly annihilated <note>The term "annihilated" refers to the mystical practice of *Vernichtung*, where the human ego is emptied to make room for God.</note> in spirit. Thus, they lose the memory that God has done all this out of pure goodness, without them having earned the slightest bit of it. Secondly, they find rest in the gifts of God with which they find themselves filled; they forget to run to God Himself and to travel *through* all gifts to find Him. Thus, their very abundance of God’s gifts becomes an occasion for them to leave God, because of their poor application of those gifts and because they cling to them in a self-centered way. These people, who stand in such "enlightenment," are still the Lord's much-beloved until the end (though in a much different way than others), as God shares many endearments with them. For gifts and graces can coexist with self-will, as long as it does not become a mortal sin. But God alone cannot be found there: He does not give Himself to the soul until she has lost all self-will in the cruel wilderness.

v. 16. Yet another sin is added to this one, which also greatly provoked God to anger: they clung to "strangers." By this, the Romans are understood, with whom they made a covenant after the Babylonian captivity. Judas Maccabeus was the initiator of this, as seen in the history of 1 Maccabees 8, where verse 18 specifically mentions the reason: they sought help so that the Kingdom of Israel would not be oppressed by the Greeks. In this, they wavered in their trust in God. Jonathan did the same later, renewing this covenant and even making a treaty with the Spartans. 1 Maccabees 12.

**To jealousy)** just as a husband is moved to jealousy over an adulterous wife.

**Through strangers)** <note>meaning foreign gods</note> which He can tolerate as little as an honorable man can tolerate his wife involving herself with another.

v. 17. Therefore, God counts all this heavily against them: that they sacrificed to "demons of the field"—or more accurately, to "the destroyers and devastators." Just as the idols of the heathens instilled nothing but cruelty into their servants, causing one nation to rage against another with slaughter and devastation in war and robbery.

And so, they finally received their "destroyers and devastators" in the Romans, of whom their fathers knew nothing, and who eventually brought about their total destruction.

**Gods whom they knew not)** Serving an unknown God is an irrational worship and an effect of extreme blindness. Acts 17:23.

**To the new ones)** Also to the god Maozim <note>original: "Mausim," a reference to the "god of fortresses" in Daniel 11:38, often linked to the Antichrist</note> in the final times, when many will fall away to the Antichrist. For the prophetic spirit looks through all ages; and when the song is one day sung at the sea of glass <note>A reference to Revelation 15:2</note>, then everything that was spoken here in the past—though it was then still in the future—will have truly reached its fulfillment.

<column-break/>

> 18. The Rock that begot thee <gloss>(a)</gloss> thou hast forgotten, and hast put out of mind <gloss>(b)</gloss> the God who bore thee. <gloss>(a)</gloss> James 1:18. <gloss>(b)</gloss> chapter 8:11.

> 19. And when the Lord saw it, He spurned them because of the provocation of His sons and His daughters.

> 20. And He said: I will hide My face from them; I will see what their end <gloss>(a)</gloss> shall be! For they are a very perverse generation, children in whom is no faithfulness. <gloss>(a)</gloss> Daniel 9:27.

v. 18. Here their great sin is once again held up to them: that through the aforementioned things, they have forgotten Christ—their Rock, Redeemer, and spiritual Father—and God their Creator. They have even completely let go and put Him out of mind, as they explicitly cried out against Christ: "We have no king but Caesar!" John 19:15.

<margin>John 19:15.</margin>

God, who is entirely full of love and grace toward "shorn" <note>likely a metaphor for souls stripped of worldly attachments</note> or enlightened souls, cannot refrain from giving them such a loving rebuke: You have abandoned the Goal for the sake of the Means. You have lingered among the gifts and forgotten the Giver. You rested when you were running your best, when you should have instead ascended to your Origin. One must note that although God shows these weak souls so much grace, He does so to some extent with reluctance and only because of their weakness. In this, He is deprived of a great honor and an infinite pleasure He would have if these souls, with a magnanimous contempt for all His riches, passed through them to reach the created Good itself—and, just as rivers fall back into the sea from which they flowed, reached Him again as their Origin.

v. 19. Now follows God’s judgment upon Jeshurun <note>A poetic name for Israel, meaning "the upright one"</note>—the people who saw the Lord with their eyes but let Him go and thus spurned Him. After a time of patience—which He showed them for about thirty years—the Lord wanted to see and, as it were, examine their ends (see Genesis 18:21), in order to proceed to the righteous judgment of their rejection. Hosea explicitly mentions this in Chapter 9:17: "My God will cast them away, because they did not listen to Him; and they shall be wanderers among the nations." Here, however, the cause of their rejection is shown to be that they caused much "provocation" to His sons and daughters—those who had accepted Jesus in true faith (John 1:12)—by persecuting them everywhere, mistreating them, and even killing them. This can be seen in the example of the "breathing" Saul against the Christians, and elsewhere throughout the Acts of the Apostles. Acts 9:1, etc.

Because the Lord does not want to lose these enlightened, self-willed, and self-interested souls, and yet knows well that they would lose themselves without this, He allows them to experience "provocations" <note>or afflictions</note>. He sees it, however, and is vexed by it, with the explicit protestation that because they deceive themselves so, they should never reach their goal in this life—which is to possess God Himself and not just His gifts. Therefore He adds:

v. 20. **I will hide My face from them.** Which is to say: they shall be deprived of the possession of the Highest Good, because they preferred such lowly goods.

So too was the rejection of the Jews set in motion, in that God hid His face from them and gave them over to a hardened mind (Romans 11:25). Indeed, God decreed that this rejection and hardening will last until the end of the war in the Church Militant (Daniel 9:26, 27), because they persist in their perversion and twisting of all the prophecies of Holy Scripture. Thus, they would forget all faithfulness and faith in God, even though they pass themselves off as His witnesses.

It describes the divine judgment of "hiding His face" as a response to the people's preference for earthly alliances and their persecution of early Christians.</summary>

<meta>This page continues the line-by-line commentary on the "Song of Moses" in Deuteronomy 32. Having previously described Israel's rebellion and idolatry, the text now focuses on God's response: His righteous jealousy and the specific judgments He will bring upon the people through foreign nations, interpreted here as both historical (the Romans) and prophetic (the New Testament era).</meta>

# Chapter XXXII. The Fifth Book of Moses. 793

21. They have provoked me to jealousy with that which is not God; they have provoked me to anger with their vanities. So I will also provoke them to jealousy with those who are not a people; with a foolish nation I will provoke them to anger.
22. For a fire is kindled in my anger, and shall burn unto the lowest hell <margin>(a) Ps. 86:13.</margin> (a), and shall consume the land with its increase, and set on fire the foundations of the mountains!
23. I will heap mischiefs upon them; I will spend mine arrows upon them all!
24. They shall be consumed with hunger, and devoured with burning heat and bitter poisonous pestilence;

---

v. 21. By desiring to possess that which is less than God, one becomes incapable of the enjoyment of God Himself. Oh, what an irreparable loss!
**They me — I them also)** Like for like.
**With that which is not God)** such as the Romans were. <note>The commentator identifies the "not God" with the pagan Roman Empire that would later conquer Judea.</note>
**Provoked me to anger)** caused me only vexation.
**With their vanities)** with their vain human ordinances.
**To provoke to jealousy with those who are not a people)** namely, God's people, who according to the emphasis of the word are bound to God, and thus also to one another, in the fellowship of His gifts of grace, so that one has a share in the other. These were the heathens, from whom they learned idolatry; see Ephesians 2:11–12, Romans 9:4. These He would accept as His people, over which the Jews would then become jealous.
Thus the Spirit of prophecy in Moses points here to the times of the New Testament. As Paul himself in Romans 10:19 applied this passage to that end.
We see the fulfillment in the Acts of the Apostles, how greatly the Jews were embittered by it and fell into a spirit of jealousy because the Apostles went to the Gentiles and proclaimed to them the salvation of God in the Gospel. See Acts 13:45, 17:5, etc. Some, however, according to the Lord's gracious intention in Romans 11:14, were also provoked to a good jealousy and to emulation, to also accept Christ, since the Gentiles thus converted to the God of their fathers, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.
**With a foolish nation)** These are the Romans, who lay in the greatest idolatry and abominations, whom they <note>the Jews</note> chose for their protection; these, says the Lord,
**I will)** make highly hateful to them through the greedy and cruel, unjust conduct of their governors <note>The term "Landpfleger" refers to Roman procurators or governors like Pontius Pilate or Gessius Florus.</note>, whom the Romans will set over them after the subjugation of the Jews.
v. 22. etc. Therefore, afterward, the heavy judgments broke out in the bloodthirsty war of the Romans against them.
v. 23. **My arrows)** All my plagues, which are named in the following, and are precisely the plagues that will also come upon the corrupted Church in the last time.
v. 24. To completely exterminate them, as the lineage of Cain was totally rooted out, God never took into His mind for the sake of the promise made to the fathers: since, even in His anger against them, He wanted to preserve Moses and make him into a great nation. **Strangely)** so that they should attribute such things to their gods and their great power rather than to the true God, and it would be
**Not the LORD)** the Christ, as the Christians claimed, who had done all these things; they would have destroyed the people so that nothing of them could be seen or known.

# The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XXXII.

28. **For they are a nation whose counsels are lost, and there is no understanding in them.**

29. **Oh, that they were wise, and considered this; that they would mark their latter end!** <margin>Hosea 14:10; Luke 19:42.</margin>

Verse 28. Here the judgment of these heathens—the Romans—is presented, as well as that of all enemies of the Church. It shows how all their schemes would come to nothing, for there was no true understanding in them, even though they boasted of great fleshly prudence. <note>The author interprets the "nation" in Deuteronomy not just as ancient enemies of Israel, but as the Roman Empire and later opponents of the Christian Church.</note>

For they) the heathen Christians and antichristian heathens, among whom the Jewish people lived in much distress toward the end.

Are) no better than the Jews were.

A nation whose counsels are lost) Because they only pursue earthly things.

There is no understanding in them) to recognize and consider what serves their temporal and eternal salvation.

All those who, in their evil nature, do not give their hearts to wisdom—and do not allow themselves to be guided by it toward the future and be prepared for it—are fools and simpletons.

Verse 29. Just as the Romans (who were described above in verse 21 as a foolish nation) remained mostly in their heathen unbelief, even though Christ had the Gospel proclaimed to them among the first. <note>referring to the Apostle Paul's mission to Rome.</note> Although Paul specifically went among the heathens and came to them, they mostly did not want to recognize true wisdom, nor their end and destruction, as had been threatened to them in <margin>Daniel 2:44, 7:22.</margin>

Oh, that) Whatever God has ever commanded us, His miserable creatures, to do or to suffer, certainly all flows from His pure grace and mercy. How many thousands of times more must such love and faithfulness of God be the foundation when He comes to us with such yearning wishes and desires! Indeed,

This patience and condescension of God is all the more wonderful and incomprehensible, the more He has to deal here with us fools, at whom He could rightly be angry.

They) the corrupted state of Christendom.

were wise) Who among us must not admit that, in the most important and necessary things concerning the soul, we do not yet use such proper wisdom and foresight as God requires of us?

Therefore, this wish applies to all of us in general: that we might be wise toward what is good, and, if we already think ourselves wise, that we might learn how we must become even wiser.

And indeed, this prudence of the truly righteous should look toward the future.

That they would mark their latter end) Who can say that he has applied enough earnestness, diligence, and care to preparing for the "last things"—what will happen to him in and after death? Where is the unceasing "dying before one dies"; the impartial judging of oneself before one is judged; the living knowledge of the state of the soul after its departure? Has not the present vain nature of this world so occupied and blinded most people that the future seems like a fable to them? Yes, that is precisely the foolishness of the flesh: that it fattens and contents itself with present, perishable goods, while forgetting the best and rightful ones.

O, let us be put to shame by the people of the world themselves! They place the essence and foundation of true prudence primarily in having a far-reaching view of the future, so that plans and actions can be shaped accordingly. How many thousands of times more must a Christian turn away from the present and into the future, since the entire essence of his faith looks and aims at the future and the invisible things he hopes for!

It is certain and beyond all doubt that the most important changes and events still lie before us. Our necessary purification and humiliation, our complete dying to all things, our outward bodily death, the impending specific judgment over every soul, and the passage from this time into eternity—these are all such great matters that they should truly make us attentive.

Therefore, let no one think this requirement of God does not concern him. It strikes most heavily upon the one who thinks he needs it the least.

<column-break/>

30. **How should one chase a thousand, and two put ten thousand to flight? Is it not because their Rock sold them, and the Lord delivered them up?** <margin>(a) Isaiah 30:17</margin>

31. **For their rock is not as our Rock: even our enemies themselves being the judges.** <margin>(a) Isaiah 26:4.</margin>

32. **For their vine is of the vine of Sodom and of the fields of Gomorrah: their grapes are grapes of gall; they have bitter clusters.** <margin>Revelation 14:18.</margin>

Verse 30. This was fulfilled when the Emperors who confessed the Gospel achieved great victories against the heathen idolaters and their protectors. Their "rock"—the Dragon <note>symbolizing Satan or pagan deities</note>—had to abandon them because he could not help them, as the Lord gave them over to the power of the sword and allowed their crude idols to be destroyed.

Verse 31. Now the believers step forward—those whom God converted far and wide from among the heathens—and they boast that their Rock, the Lamb <note>referring to Jesus Christ</note>, is not like the rock of their adversaries, the Romans. Many of the Romans remained stuck in blind idolatry, and their rock abandoned them. In contrast, Christ powerfully protected and preserved His own. And even though their enemies imagined they could completely exterminate the Christians, it was their own crude idolatry that was powerfully destroyed and wiped out in this fourth kingdom of the world <note>The Roman Empire was traditionally viewed as the fourth kingdom mentioned in the book of Daniel.</note>.

Even our enemies themselves being the judges) Namely, the enemies of the believers themselves had to be the judges who carried out the judgments upon the idolaters. By this, we can understand not only the hostile armies led by the Christian Emperors (which mostly consisted of blind heathens), but also the Emperors themselves and their followers. These later outwardly confessed the Christian faith in great numbers, where protection and benefits were enjoyed and external idolatry was destroyed everywhere; yet they eventually became enemies to the true believers. For the heretical teachers who deviated from the pure truth in the fundamental articles of faith—such as the Arians, who denied the deity of Christ—attached themselves to the Emperors and caused the believers to suffer many persecutions from them as enemies.

Verse 32. And thus, such a "vine" established itself, setting itself against the true vine, Christ <margin>John 15:1.</margin>. To this false vine, all fleshly teachers and sinful men attached themselves, seeking from it the juice of temporal goods and honors. These thus became the Anti-Christ and the true anti-Christians; a "mystery of iniquity" that was already moving in the time of the Apostles. <margin>1 John 2:18, 4:3.</margin> From these fleshly teachers and their protectors—the great and powerful of this world—there later sprang nothing but the harmful poison of fleshly lusts, outward pomp and pride, great riches, and earthly treasures. Then came great violence, the forcing of consciences, and bitter persecutions—namely from the Beast and the false prophet, as the Revelation of John calls them <margin>Revelation 13; 16:10; 17:3; 19:19.</margin>. This also became the root in Hebrew thought that bore gall and wormwood. <margin>Deuteronomy 29:18; Hebrews 12:15.</margin>

Their) the antichristian church's

Vine is of Sodom and Gomorrah) It is not the true Church, as she claims and blesses herself in her heart. Rather, the so-called Christian Church is fundamentally corrupted, just as Jerusalem formerly became like Sodom and Gomorrah.

Verse 33. Their wine) from the golden cup of the Babylonian Whore. <margin>Revelation 14:8, 17:2, 18:3.</margin>

# Chapter XXXII. The Fifth Book of Moses.

34. Is this not stored up with me, and sealed in my treasures?

35. Vengeance is mine and recompense, in the time when their foot shall stumble! For the day of their calamity is near, and what is prepared for them hastens toward them!

<margin>2 Kings 14:26.</margin>
36. For the **LORD** will judge his people, and have compassion on his servants. For he will see that their power is gone, and the captive and the forsaken count for nothing.

37. Then he will say: Where are their gods, the rock in whom they took refuge?

38. Who ate the fat of their sacrifices, and drank the wine of their drink offerings: Let them rise up and help you, so that there may be a shelter over you!

---

Verse 34. Stored up with me and sealed) The secret of wickedness hidden under the name of "Christian" is well known to **GOD** the **LORD**; as is what he intends for both his Church and its enemies. Even if we do not know everything precisely, he knows what he has decreed, and he keeps it closed under his seals until it pleases him to open them and provide a revelation of it.

Now that the great misery from the bitter fruits of the wild vine of Sodom <note>The "vine of Sodom" is a biblical metaphor for a corrupt and sinful society or church.</note> has been presented—which believers in the final times will feel quite strongly—their redemption is promised here. It is, so to speak, stored away in the archive of Holy Scripture and sealed there until the full revelation, when the great treasures of **GOD'S** grace, which he has reserved for his people here on earth in the glorious kingdom of his dear Son, shall be shown and shared with all.

Verse 35. Then the righteous vengeance of **GOD** shall be revealed against the false vine, which is Babylon <note>original: "Babel." In this context, Babylon usually represents a corrupt or worldly church system.</note>, when it is at its highest and most flourishing state, but first begins to stumble. That is, when it first begins to be truly exposed in many hearts and starts to fall within them. This initially happened during the Reformation; after which the revelation of the entire Babylon in the whole external Church, and then its final fall and complete overthrow, will follow. Therefore it is repeated twice: *She is fallen, she is fallen, Babylon the great, etc.* Then afterward it is written concerning the recompense: Revelation 18:2, 6, 7. These are the bitter fruits she made others taste, which are now prepared for her to consume in return.

Verse 36. Then the **LORD** will indeed first judge his people and his servants through a "judgment of love" under the fifth seal, and therein refine and purify them: see Daniel 11:33, 35; 1 Peter 4:17. But, when their misery seems to be at its greatest, so that all their power and ability is gone; (see Daniel 7:12; Revelation 3:8) then the testimony of those who are either still shut up within the congregations or are forsaken of all human help outside of them, will no longer count for anything and will have no more strength:

Verse 37. At that time, the adversaries will mock God and the Rock, whose inner testimony of the Spirit the believers had relied upon;

Verse 38. When these believers are killed like sacrificial offerings and their blood is shed, while those others enrich themselves with their goods, and thus mock the help that was supposed to come to this lowly little people:

<column-break/>

39. See now, that I, yes I, am the same, and there is no **GOD** beside me! I kill and I make alive; I strike down and I heal: and there is no one who can rescue from my hand.
<margin>Hosea 2:10.</margin>

40. Then

---

Then Christ will suddenly appear with his gracious help as the only true living **GOD**, who can very quickly give life back out of death, and can heal the struck and the wounded. On the other hand, he will plunge the adversaries into such a judgment from which no one will be able to rescue them.

<margin>Zechariah 12:10.</margin>
See now, you Jews, and recognize with uncovered eyes,

<margin>John 18:5, 6, 8.</margin>
That I am the same) Whom you previously did not wish to recognize. I am he.

This verse also teaches us how much **GOD** longs for us to surrender ourselves to him, and that we should certainly not rely on anything outside of him. For he means to say: Since you recognize that I alone am he, and that nothing can be found that is equal to me, I also want to be and work in you alone. Who indeed has the power to do what I do? Is there any other **GOD** but me? I alone can make souls die to themselves, and no human labor can accomplish such a thing. But I alone also give them life again, awakening them and making them live again after I have killed them.

Tell us then, O Divine Love! what are your inventions <note>original: "Erfindungen." Here meaning the methods or "devices" God uses to test the soul.</note> which you use to wound your most faithful lovers? Oh, how poorly would these be recognized by mortal men if you were to tell them to us directly! It is you who strikes; and at the same time you hide yourself, leaving nothing behind but the pain of the wounds you have struck. A soul thus wounded thinks she can never recover again: she resists your blows as long as she can: she even doubts whether they could truly come from you; and while you are striking her, she cries out bitterly and complains to you against those very blows you give her, as if they came from someone else, because she does not know it is you who strikes her. She thinks that because she is so full of wounds, and thus so disfigured, you will no longer love her; and the horror of her wounds leads her to want to do herself harm; believing she has deserved it, and that if she had defended herself more bravely, she would not have been so marred by this invincible hand. But take comfort, take comfort, you poor beloved one: you do not know who your innocent murderer is. If you knew, you would count yourself much luckier to be killed by his hand than to be made alive again by anyone else, whoever it might be.

What does this lovely, "cruel" one do? <note>This refers to the mystical concept of God "cruelly" breaking the ego to save the soul.</note> He also heals again all the wounds he himself has struck: and indeed in such a pleasant way that the soul wishes for nothing else than to be constantly wounded in this way, just to have the pleasure of being healed by him.

Know, however, dear souls, that this healing, which seems so pleasant to you, must cost you your life. Oh, that will indeed be a different kind of pain for you! The pain of death is much different from the pain of wounding; and when the death-stroke is given to you, you will just as well recognize the one who has killed you.

The poor soul is so blind that she believes she has plunged the dagger into her own breast. No, no! The Unknown One kills you. But he kills you only so that you may become alive again: but with a different life than the one you had before; which was more of a constant death, because you only lived in order to die: whereas here, on the contrary, you will only die in order to live in a constant, abiding life. Resist only as long as you can; your struggles will do nothing more than prolong your pains: because no one can escape his hand. No, no! All your efforts will be in vain. You may take it however you wish, this much remains certain: that you cannot escape death.

<margin>v. 34.</margin> **Stored up and sealed with me**) To the LORD God, the "mystery of wickedness" <note>This refers to the "mystery of iniquity" (2 Thessalonians 2:7), a common term in this period for spiritual corruption hidden within the visible church.</note> among those who bear the Christian name is well known; and likewise, what He intends for both His Church and her enemies. Though we do not yet know everything precisely, He knows what He has decreed, and He keeps it locked under His seals until it pleases Him to open them and provide a revelation.

Now that the great misery caused by the bitter fruits of the wild vine of Sodom has been presented—which believers in the end times will feel deeply enough—their redemption is promised here. It is described as being stored in the "archives" of Holy Scripture and sealed there until the full revelation, when the great treasures of God's grace, which He has reserved for His people here on earth in the glorious Kingdom of His dear Son, shall be revealed and distributed to all.

<margin>v. 35.</margin> Then the righteous vengeance of God shall be revealed against the false vine, **Babel** <note>In this context, "Babel" or Babylon refers to a corrupted, worldly church system.</note>, when it is at its highest and most flourishing state, but begins to "slip"—that is, when it first begins to be truly exposed in many hearts and starts to fall within them. This initially occurred during the Reformation, after which the revelation of the entire "Babel" in the whole outward Church, and then its final fall and complete overthrow, will follow. Therefore it is repeated twice: *She is fallen, she is fallen, Babylon the great* <note>original: "Offenb. 18/" refers to Revelation 18:2.</note>. These are the bitter fruits she made others taste, and which are now prepared for her to consume in return.

<margin>v. 36.</margin> Then the LORD will indeed judge His people and His servants, first through a "judgment of love" under the fifth seal, to refine and purify them (see Daniel 11:33, 35; 1 Peter 4:17). But when their misery seems greatest, and all their power and ability is gone (see Daniel 7:12; Revelation 3:8), the testimony of those who are still "shut up" in the congregations, or those who are "forsaken" outside of them—as if abandoned by all human help—will no longer count for anything and will have no more strength.

<margin>v. 37.</margin> At that time, the adversaries will mock the Spirit and the **Rock** on whose inner testimony of the Spirit the believers have relied.

<margin>v. 38.</margin> While some are being killed like sacrifices and their blood is being shed, others will enrich themselves with their goods, mocking the help that was supposed to come to this lowly little people.

<column-break/>

### 39. See now, that I, even I, am He, and there is no God beside me! I kill and I make alive; I strike down and I heal: and there is no one who can rescue from my hand.
<margin>Hosea 2:10.</margin>

### 40. Then

Then Christ will suddenly appear with His gracious help as the only true living God, who can quickly give life back from death and heal what has been struck and wounded. Conversely, He will plunge the adversaries into such a judgment from which no one can rescue them.

**See now**) you Jews, and recognize with opened eyes <margin>Zechariah 12:10.</margin>

**That I am He**) Whom you previously did not wish to recognize. I am He. <margin>John 18:5, 6, 8.</margin>

This verse also teaches us how much God desires that one should surrender to Him, and that one should not rely on anything outside of Him. For He means to say: Since you recognize that I alone am He, and that nothing can be found equal to me, I alone will be and work within you. Who has the power to do what I do? Is there any other god but me? I alone can cause souls to die to themselves, and no human labor can accomplish this. But I alone also give them life again; I awaken and make them alive after I have killed.

> Tell us, O Love of God! what are your inventions that you use to wound your most faithful lovers? Oh, how poorly would mortal men recognize them even if you told us! It is you who strikes, and at the same time you hide yourself, leaving nothing but the pain of the wounds you have dealt. A soul thus wounded thinks she can never recover: she resists your strokes as long as she can; she even doubts whether they come from you. And while you strike her, she cries out bitterly and complains about the blows you give her. She thinks they come from someone else because she does not know it is you who strikes her. She thinks that because she is so full of wounds, and thus so disfigured, you will no longer love her. The horror of her wounds drives her to want to do herself harm, believing she has deserved it, and that if she had been more faithful, this invincible hand would not have so deformed her. But comfort yourself, comfort yourself, you poor beloved! You do not know who your innocent murderer is. If you knew, you would count yourself much more fortunate to be killed by His hand than to be made alive again by anyone else, whoever it might be.

What does this **Lovingly-Worthy Cruel One** do? He also heals all the wounds He Himself has struck, and does so in such a charming way that the soul wishes for nothing else but to be constantly wounded in order to have the pleasure of being healed by Him.

Know, however, dear souls, that this healing, which seems so pleasant to you, must cost you your life. Oh, that will indeed be a different pain of wounding; death is much different than the pain of a mere wound. And when the death-blow is given to you, you will then truly recognize the one who has killed you.

The poor soul is so blind that she believes she has stabbed the dagger into her own breast. No, no! The Unknown One kills you. But He only kills you so that you may become alive again—but with a different life than the one you had before. That previous life was more like a constant death, because you only lived to die; whereas here, you will only die in order to live in a constant, remaining life. Resist as long as you can; your resistance will do nothing but prolong your pain, because no one can escape His hand. No, no! All your efforts will be in vain. You may try whatever you will, it remains certain: you cannot escape this death.
