# The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XXXII. 796

40. **For I lift up my hand to heaven, and say: I live forever!**

41. **When I whet the lightning of my sword, and my hand takes hold of judgment; then I will bring vengeance upon my adversaries, and repay those who hate me!**
->Isaiah 34:8<-

42. **I will make my arrows drunk with blood, and my sword shall devour flesh! From the blood of the**

v. 40. When these words are added to what has been said, they indicate that God kills such a soul only because it possesses a life which is contrary to His life. For the lifting of His hand is like an oath; as if He were saying: I swear death to this soul, because it still lives in itself, and yet I alone must live in it. But so that I alone may live, I must annihilate everything that is still found living in it which opposes my own life. And when this is accomplished, I will live in it eternally.

Furthermore, it is very clear from this verse that this prophecy belongs to the end times: because not only in the prophet Daniel (12:7) regarding the end times of the 3½ years <note>The text says 4½, but usually refers to the 3.5 years/1260 days of biblical prophecy</note>, but also in Revelation 10:6 and following, at the beginning of the final judgments, an angel must repeat and speak the same words in the name of the living God. Thus, the text here speaks of and begins with the actual vengeance that Christ will exercise on His enemies in the end times, under the sixth seal: where He first adds His oath to all these prophecies, showing how everything will be put into effect—what He, the faithful witness and Amen, has testified through His Spirit in this song—concerning how things will go until the end for His militant church here on earth.

v. 41. He, the living and almighty King of His people, will then in the final time put His flashing sword into the hands of His enemies, as it were, so that they exercise vengeance upon one another and consume each other; as is prophesied in Isaiah 19:2, 17, 18.

v. 42. And as they have shed the blood of the saints, so God will shed their blood in return, and let their flesh—that is, all their power—be devoured and consumed. See Revelation 16:6, 17:6, 19:2, 17, 18.

From the blood) Others translate this as "because of," and thus understand it as the blood of those slain and captured by the followers of the Antichrist, and the vengeance for that sake.

God is not content simply to kill a soul chosen for Him; He also pursues it after its death to annihilate it, so that nothing of it remains. He wills that no blood remain in this creature—that is, no origin of life at all: just as it is written, <margin>(a) Leviticus 17:14.</margin> (a) that the soul of a living animal is in its blood. Since the source of one's own life is contained in the blood, it is not only necessary that none remain; but the sword of the Lord shall afterward even cut and devour the flesh that came from the blood. He does not say His sword will merely cut off this flesh: in order to indicate annihilation all the more. By this "flesh of the blood," however, all things belonging to one's own life are understood. The first life of one's own is the life of the flesh or of sin, which one puts off when one is converted. But the other life, which must be lost here, is the spiritual life and the life of the soul, represented by the blood. And although it is a life of the spirit, it is still somewhat carnal and mixed with the flesh through self-will.

<column-break/>

**slain and the captives, from the head and the locks of hair of the enemy.**

43. **Rejoice** (a) **you Gentiles with His people!** (b) **For He will avenge the blood of His servants, and bring vengeance upon His adversaries, and atone for His land and His people.** (a) Psalm 47:1. (b) Romans 15:10.

Just as it is not enough to have died, but one must also be annihilated: so too must the captivity be lifted. This captivity is a certain narrowness of the soul which prevents its expansion, and which can be opened in no other way than through annihilation. But the head of our enemies, from which it stems, is self-will <note>Original: "Eigenheit," referring to the ego or the self-centered nature</note>. This self-will is indeed stripped bare by death; yet a certain kind of reservation remains which keeps the soul captive and prevents it from expanding: and this is what is finally swallowed up by annihilation.

In the same way, God will also judge the "head" which has raised itself up in His Church and usurped power over consciences, which belongs to Him alone; because He alone is the head and needs no visible heads beside Him to rule the believers, who are all meant to be members. This judgment will also strike the "locks of hair"—those who hang upon and depend on this head, deriving their power and prestige from it; as is also discussed in Psalm 68:21, 23 and Psalm 110:6.

v. 43. Now follows the triumph of the Church in the glorious Kingdom of Christ, which is then redeemed by the Lord from the hand of all her enemies who oppressed her, just as one hears such songs of triumph in Revelation 19 and 15:2-4: where all the Gentiles rejoice with His people Israel, who will be converted to Christ in this final time, according to Chapter 30:3, 5, Jeremiah 30:18, 31:38, and Ezekiel 40, etc. Thus there are two kinds of Gentiles here: those who survive the slaughter and enter as the "fullness of the Gentiles," being converted to the Lord. For because a rejoicing is to arise among them in fellowship with His people, the Gentiles of the Old Testament cannot be meant, as the "partition wall" <note>Referencing the "middle wall of partition" in Ephesians 2:14</note> was still present, which is only taken away in Christ so that they can reach the fellowship of the Church.

Thus, all the events of the Jewish people and the Church of Christ—gathered from Jews and Gentiles from the beginning to her end, or rather her perfection here on earth in the glorious Kingdom—are contained in this song in seven parts:

(1) How the Gospel would be proclaimed among the Jews, but they would greatly despise the believers. v. 1.

(2) How the Jews would greatly abuse all God’s benefits and not let themselves be led to the knowledge of their salvation, but rather would reject the Rock of their salvation in a terrible way. v. 6–18.

(3) How God would therefore let the heavy judgment of destruction fall upon them. v. 19–25.

(4) How God would also judge their enemies, the Romans; and how He would also have His people among them: to whom the enemies themselves would outwardly profess and become their judges and protectors; but they would also allow a foreign vine to grow up among them, from which the bitter fruits of worldly lusts would grow. Then the Jews should not be offended that the New Testament Church, in its outward state, would become as corrupted as theirs, because of human prestige and traditions which they both had to experience to their ruin. v. 26–33.

(5) How God will judge the destroyers of His Church and graciously take up His people again, who will fall into great tribulations. v. 34–39.

(6) How God truly intends to finish off His enemies. v. 40–42.

(7) And finally, how He will take His people back into grace, so that they, with the Gentiles in true union of the spirit, will praise and glorify Christ in His glorious Kingdom. v. 43.

### Chapter XXXII. The Fifth Book of Moses. 797

44. **And Moses came and spoke all the words of this song in the ears of the people, he and Hoshea <note>original: "Hosea"; refers to Joshua, the son of Nun</note>, the son of Nun.**

<margin>(a) Matthew 7:28.</margin>
45. **And when Moses had finished speaking (a) all these words to all Israel;**

46. **He said to them: Set your heart upon all the words which I testify to you today, that you may command them to your children, that they may observe and do all the words of this law.**

47. **For it is not an empty word for you, but it is your life: and through this word you shall prolong your days in the land where you are going over the Jordan to possess it as an inheritance.**

v. 44. **He and Hoshea** The two faithful witnesses of God, Moses and his successor Joshua, had to publicly read the contents of this song and deliver it to the entire Jewish people, so that it would be a testimony to them until the end of this world.

v. 46. **Command your children, that they do all the words of the law** How can one do this if one is stuck in unbelief oneself, holding the belief that keeping the law is neither possible nor necessary?

Commanding is also without impact when the examples <note>original: "Exempel"; refers to the parents' lived behavior</note> are worth nothing.

One cannot believe how much children pay attention to their parents, and how gladly they imitate everything they do. Whatever they see is impressed upon them as if into wax, so that they retain the images and the power of that influence for the rest of their lives.

In children, one has the most precious pledges from God, than which nothing is more costly. They are immortal souls that cannot perish in eternity. As one treats them, so they become. If one places good examples before them, they will be good. Through evil ones, they become evil. Of this, one can be certain.

Only let it be understood correctly, and not of hypocritical examples. For hypocrisy creates hypocrites in turn. The false powers and pretenses of a "respectable" life propagate themselves just as much as—and even more than—that which is good.

But just as the "law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus" <note>A reference to Romans 8:2</note> is meant here, as can be seen from the following verse; so also must it be the life of Christ and such godliness where one is truly earnest, walking in God's eyes both secretly and publicly, taming one's flesh and lusts, and letting oneself be governed by the Spirit of God. Then children soon notice that it is a matter of earnestness, and that they too are bound to it. Just as an earnest walk binds others alongside us to the same: it is indescribable what divine authority is hidden within a godly life and walk.

With such a repentant life, one will accomplish a thousand times more with one's own family and gain more respect from them than with all the hitting, shouting, and talking. A single look <note>original: "Mine"; facial expression or countenance</note> can often put others in awe and reverence, if it is a glimpse and ray of God's image in the soul. Everything divine leaves an impression on the mind, so that one feels shame and is gladly willing to be guided, and that with love and goodwill.

v. 47. (**Not an empty word**) of human invention.

**But**) the word that showed them the origin of their life and of eternal happiness, both in the land as long as they would dwell therein, and afterward when they would be cast out of it.

(**It is your life**) It is a great advantage for a soul when it can, as it were, look into God's heart through the light of the Spirit during all His commandments, and recognize what is intended by them; seeing how in all His demands He seeks not our harm or vexation, but pure salvation and blessing. Whereas otherwise, false reason is quick to blame the eternally good God, as if He merely took pleasure in commanding us humans so much, or as if He were only asserting His rights with His commandments without caring whether it benefits us or not.

<column-break/>

48. **And the Lord spoke to Moses on that very same day, saying:**

49. **Go up this mountain of Abarim, Mount Nebo, which lies in the land of Moab, which is opposite Jericho, and behold the land of Canaan, which I will give to the children of Israel for a possession:**

50. **And die on the mountain where you go up, and be gathered to your people; just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people:**

51. **Because you committed unfaithfulness against me in the midst of the children of Israel, at the waters of strife <note>original: "Hader-Wasser"; refers to Meribah</note> at Kadesh in the wilderness of Zin, because you did not sanctify me in the midst of the children of Israel.**

52. **For you shall see the land opposite you, but you shall not enter into the land that I give to the children of Israel.**

Thus the Lord finally prepared Moses for his death, so that he should await it just like Aaron, according to His command.

v. 49. 50. And indeed on Mount Nebo, which was a part or a specific height and peak of the mountains of Abarim.

<margin>See Numbers 20:11 etc. and 27:12.</margin>
v. 51. There, the crime of both was again presented to him, in order to conclude his end with a repentant and yet faithful contemplation of the ways of God.

There it may well be said: "If this happens to the green wood, what will become of the dry?" <note>Luke 23:31. The author compares Moses, the "green wood" or faithful servant, to the common sinner or "dry wood."</note> Does God seek everything so precisely even in the best and most faithful souls, that He does not overlook the slightest unfaithfulness in them? And must Moses, who has the testimony of the greatest faithfulness from God Himself (Numbers 12:7; Hebrews 3:2), be reminded of his oversight so often, and be excluded from entering the promise because of it? O sinner, O sinner, what will then become of you? Rely on your church-going, baptism and communion, prayer and alms, as you will! The Lord your God will be sanctified by you: and if you do not sanctify Him, He will sanctify Himself through you, and let you experience that He is truly righteous!

v. 52. **You shall—see**) The secret here is that even such souls who still stand under the Law, and have not yet fully stepped out of the first dispensation of the Father, may through a special grace sometimes have a vision or a glimpse of that other world. They may have a spiritual sight of the "many mansions" that are in the Father's house (John 14:2) and other even more important visions and revelations.

**But**) to enter into rest, to remain therein, they are not yet fit. The disciples must go down the mountain again (Matthew 17) and first into death.

(**Not enter in**) In the same way, David was not allowed to build the temple for the Lord, even though he was permitted to see its model.

<header>The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XXXIII.</header>

# Chapter XXXIII.
->The Blessing of Moses.<-

And this is the blessing wherewith Moses, the man of God, blessed the children of Israel before his death;
2. And he said: The LORD came from Sinai, and rose up from Seir to them; He shined forth from Mount Paran (a), and He came with ten thou-
<margin>(a) Habakkuk 3:3, etc. (b) Hebrews 12:22. Jude v. 14.</margin>
---
Just as Jacob, as the younger patriarch of the twelve tribes, endowed them before his death with a mystery-filled blessing by divine impulse: so Moses, the great prophet of God—who had begun to put into effect the promise made to the fathers to give them the land of Canaan—had to wish a similar blessing upon them before his death as they entered that same land. This blessing was to reach its full fulfillment among the physical and spiritual Israel, which was to become his spiritual seed from the Gentiles through faith in the "Seed" promised to Abraham. However, due to the passage of time and because it was not recorded in writing, it is very obscure how the literal understanding was fulfilled among "Israel according to the flesh" <note>This term refers to the biological descendants of Jacob as opposed to the "spiritual Israel" of believers.</note>. Therefore, believers in the New Testament, in the light of the Lord, should rather observe how such a blessing has been fulfilled little by little in a mysterious way among the Israel of the New Testament; which the contemplation of the events in the blessing and in the church histories of the New Testament can show more fully.

<margin>v. 1.</margin> **The Blessing of Moses** This has one particular advantage over the blessing of Jacob: it contains nothing but blessing. In contrast, Jacob did not prophesy the best for Reuben, Simeon, Levi, and Dan. Yet Moses does not contradict him in this, but rather passes over the bad and indicates only the good that each tribe, especially in the end, should obtain.

<margin>v. 2.</margin> Furthermore, there is first a preface here that makes known the appearance of the Lord—who was specifically Christ—showing how He gave His law on Sinai amidst a terrifying fire (Exodus 19:16; Hebrews 12:18, etc.) and thereafter shined forth among them with the pillar of cloud in the mountains of the Edomites and in the wilderness of Paran, which were three mountains lying near one another in one region. Thus He deemed them worthy of His miraculous guidance and protection. See Numbers 10:12, 20:14, 33:37, etc.

**The LORD came from the mountain** Which is His throne; and this throne is nothing other than He Himself. He came from the higher places <note>original: "super-Orten"</note>.

**From Sinai** a mountain of grace, a mountain of illumination and of love. But He also

**Rose up from Seir** from a desolate place; and

**From Mount Paran** through a new communication of His graces: but not through Muhammad, as his followers wish to prove the threefold revelation of God through Moses, Christ, and Muhammad from this passage.

**With the ten thousands of the sanctuary** Which are the blessed spirits and the annihilated souls <note>original: "vernichtigten Seelen"; a mystical term for souls that have completely surrendered their own will to God</note>. These blessed spirits are very holy because nothing is found in them except what is of God. They are also always with Him, for they are holy only because of Him.

This also further indicates the glory of God, which never enters a soul alone, but is always accompanied by many gifts and graces and by an abundance of heavenly caresses. These are all the more sublime the lowlier they appear; and thus also much purer the more they are found within Himself and do not consist in the creature's own perception: Just as the thousands of angels who accompanied Him on Mount Sinai are very closely and eternally united with Him.

<column-break/>

sands (b) of the sanctuary! At His right hand was a fiery law for them. Jeremiah 23:29.
3. Yet He carried the peoples in His bosom. All His saints are in Your hand: and as they were placed in the midst at Your feet, they received of Your words.
4. Namely the law that Moses commanded us for an eternal possession of the congregation of Jacob. Psalm 147:19-20.
---
**A fiery law for them** is love, which is meant to consume and annihilate everything that is found in man that is of man. For as long as anything of that remains, he cannot be holy. This fiery law is precisely what makes the saints; and no saint can be holy without passing through this fiery law.

Therefore, although in view of unrepentant sinners it is nothing but a killing "letter" of curse and damnation that proclaims and impresses God's wrath and fiery zeal, it is nevertheless, in view of believers, nothing but light and love, blessing and life. For them, it also brings the most glorious promises, even though it brings judgment for both; yet for believers, this judgment must be more a joy than a sorrow. For it is nothing other than the precise will of the Father, which Christ reveals through the Holy Spirit, by which sin is to be separated from man—just as through the heat of fire the hardness of metals is dissolved, and the good ore (gold, silver, or copper) is freed and purified from the dross. To that end, it kindles the heart and consumes everything of self-love found within it, so that pure love alone may remain therein.

<margin>v. 3.</margin> Therefore, even though the Lord made known the law—and thus His omnipotence—with great terror, He nevertheless cherished His people like a child in the bosom with much love and mercy. He spared them at all times and preserved them fatherly, as He always had His saints and covenant-partners among them, whom He allowed to be ruled by His hand. Yes, as the whole people presented themselves at His feet, like students before their teacher (Acts 22:3), they were instructed in the way of life from His pure, holy mouth.

<margin>v. 4.</margin> And they thereafter received the remaining law through Moses, because they could not endure the immediate speech of God (Exodus 20:19). This was the true treasure of the congregation of Jacob, through which they were assured of and made partakers of the gracious goods of God and the eternal heavenly inheritance. See Isaiah 58:14.

But it was not intended as the Jews, in their begrudging way, interpret it—as if the law were entrusted to them alone so that others (whom they view as heathens) were guilty of death if they read it or possessed it; and that consequently, anyone not descended from Jacob "according to the flesh" who concerned himself with the law was a thief and a robber (a). <note>original: "Libr. Sanhedr. c. 7"; refers to a passage in the Babylonian Talmud, Tractate Sanhedrin.</note>

God loves all peoples—that is, all believers; He carries them in His bosom. But the "saints" are strictly speaking only in His hands. These are the resigned souls <note>original: "gelassenen Seelen"; those practicing 'Gelassenheit' or total yielding to God</note> who allow themselves to be moved according to His will. They are in His hands for Him to do with them whatever He pleases. And those who seat themselves at His feet—namely those who are even softer and whom He has made the footstool for His feet (for this refers to the lowly)—such as these will receive of His doctrine and His words, and be instructed in His secrets that are hidden from others. These understand the stewardship of His guidance, and also comprehend the highest will which is above all things, and they marvel that it is revealed to such "little souls."

(a) Book of Sanhedrin, ch. 7.

<meta>This page continues the commentary on Deuteronomy 33, moving from the general introduction of Moses’s blessing to the specific interpretation of Verse 5 regarding the kingship in Jeshurun, followed by the individual blessings for the tribes of Reuben, Judah, and Simeon. <header>Chapter 33. The Fifth Book of Moses.</header>

# 5. And he was King in Jeshurun, when the heads of the people and the tribes of Israel were gathered together.

In these few verses, Moses beautifully encompasses the beginning, progress, and infinite fruits of contemplation and the "passive way" <note>The "passive way" (leidender Weg) refers to a mystical state where the soul ceases its own activity to let God work within it.</note>.

When the love between God and the creature grows in this way, it makes the soul holy. And as soon as such souls begin to become holy, they also begin to become patient and long-suffering. Then, as they surrender themselves with even greater magnanimity and leave themselves in God’s hands, both grow simultaneously according to their proportion. The holier a heart is, the more "yielded" it is; and the more yielded it is, the holier it is: because holiness is not to be found outside of God <note>The term used is "Gelaſſenheit," a central concept in German mysticism meaning a state of perfect detachment, serenity, and submission to God's will.</note>.

From this, it clearly appears that the more one pushes away this sanctified yieldedness, the more one distances oneself from holiness; because one does not wish to cast oneself into the hands of God, but rather to rely on one's own hands, and so to speak, to walk upon them. On the contrary, the most useful means to quickly attain holiness is to throw oneself as swiftly as possible into the arms of God; which is nothing else than blindly trusting God and submitting to His will without exception. For this is the foundation and the rule of holiness.

<margin>(a) Luke 10:39.</margin>
Should one not think that he wishes here to depict Mary (a) sitting at the feet of Jesus Christ, as she listens to His word; and with her, all those standing in contemplation, of whom she was an image? Just as all those who sit in peace at the feet of the Lord unfailingly learn His teaching—because, by listening to Him, they allow Him space to instruct them—so, on the contrary, those who do not desire to enter into this rest will never learn the Lord’s teaching. Because they always want to speak to Him themselves and never listen, they leave Him no room to instruct them; and as they clutter themselves with the unceasing and strong movements of their senses and powers, they leave Him no power to unite them with Himself. For God is nothing but pure rest: and therefore, it is necessary to remain in rest to be united with Him. And because His WORD is nothing but Word, one must be pure silence to hear it, and pure ear to receive it entirely. Thus Moses wishes to teach us that one must be silent, rest, and listen, so that the "birth of the Word" <note>A mystical concept where the Divine Word is spiritually born within the soul of the believer.</note> can occur in the soul: which is actually receiving the teaching of the Lord. For the WORD is the teaching of the Father: and when it is received, it comes to reign.

Therefore, Christ is also declared here as the King of His "People of Vision" <note>Original: "Schau-Volck," referring to those who experience the beatific vision or deep contemplation.</note>, who have been deemed worthy to see the signs of His majesty and to hear Him speak Himself, with whom He has entered into a covenant, and whom He has undertaken to rule as a King and as His own peculiar people: (see 1 Samuel 8:7) where all the heads and the tribes entered into such a covenant and publicly made it with the Lord. Exodus 24:1, etc.

When Christ appeared in the flesh, He also presented the lovely Law of the Gospel, which is love itself, upon a mountain: He also testified to His fatherly love toward all the wretched. He went about among them, instructing them as their Teacher while they sat, as it were, at His feet on the mountains, in the deserts, and elsewhere. As Cocceius <note>Johannes Cocceius (1603–1669), a prominent Dutch-German theologian known for his covenant theology.</note> and others after him explain, this refers to His second appearance in the flesh—that they were "traversed by Christ’s foot," if one must take it literally (with which he compares Leviticus 26:11-12) and thus received His heavenly teachings from Him, when He was also declared anew as the King of His people, who received the inheritance promised to Abraham—namely the Gentiles and the ends of the world—for His dominion. Psalm 2:8, Romans 4:13. And there He also ordained His twelve Apostles as heads of His twelve spiritual tribes from Jews and Gentiles: to which the promise of Christ points, that the twelve Apostles who followed Him should sit on twelve thrones in the new birth of the New Testament and judge the twelve tribes of Israel. Matthew 19:28.

<column-break/>

# 6. Let Reuben live, and not die; and let his men be a number!

# 7. And this is of Judah: and he said, Hear, LORD, the voice of Judah, and bring him unto his people: let his hands be sufficient for him; and be thou an help to him from his enemies.

v. 6. The tribe of Reuben shall not perish, although he greatly sinned against his father's marriage bed, but shall be preserved as a remnant.

**A number)** which is found concentrated in the 12,000 sealed of the last times. Revelation 7:5.

Because the people of Israel deserved death and rejection for their repudiation of the Rock of Salvation, he wishes life for the firstborn son, Reuben; by which he points to the Jews, who were to be the first to receive the grace of the Gospel, and who, according to the weight of the work, have seen the Son: see Isaiah 9:6. He wishes that there might be a good number of them and not few; these became the "remnant according to the election," while the rest remained hardened and thus fell into spiritual death: Romans 11:5, 7. These, as the holy first-fruits, were to leaven the whole lump, and as a holy root, were to bring forth the holy branches. Romans 11:16.

In the Septuagint <note>The "70 Dolmetschen" (70 Interpreters) refers to the Septuagint, the ancient Greek translation of the Hebrew Bible.</note>, Simeon is also mentioned in this verse, thus: *And Simeon shall be great and many in number.* Indeed, they were—excepting Judah and Dan—the strongest tribe, numbering 59,300. But others attribute him more to the following:

v. 7. Because the tribe of Simeon always held to Judah and was, as it were, incorporated or tucked away within them, so that his hard anger and wrath might be a little softened, and Jacob's prophecy of scattering (Genesis 49:7) would also be fulfilled in this tribal prince. As is explicitly reported in Joshua 19:9, the inheritance of the children of Simeon was within the portion of the children of Judah.

According to the WORD, Judah himself makes known the first confessors who became believers in Christ, and who therefore had to experience great hatred from their kinsmen among the Jews: (John 20:19, Acts 5:17). These then turned all the more earnestly to the Lord in prayer and called upon Him for His help and protection against their hostile blood-relatives. See Hosea 1:7.

But the request is very significant: that God would bring these, His faithful witnesses, the "spiritual Judah," to His people. This cannot be explained regarding the physical Judah—how he should have been brought to his people, the other children of Israel. Instead, one can understand it in a spiritual sense regarding the faithful confessors of Jesus Christ. When they saw that their kinsmen according to the flesh rejected the Gospel, they could well notice that God would also reject them, so as to be His people no more (Hosea 1:6, 9). Conversely, Christ would accept the Gentiles as His people, since He had become a light to enlighten the Gentiles who receive Him and thus would become His people. Therefore, these spiritual confessors of Jesus Christ, whom He still recognized as His people, pray that the Lord would bring them to their people—namely, the believing Gentiles, who had come into the fellowship of Christ and all His treasures of grace, and thus had become His people—and unite them together with them in true love. See the entire Acts of the Apostles concerning this, and especially Chapters 10 and 11:1, 17, 18.

Judah is always taken to represent Jesus Christ. Therefore, the blessing assigned to this tribe is not so much the blessing of the other tribes. It is spoken as a prayer of the tribe of Judah made to God—that is, in the name of Jesus Christ, who asks His Father to bring Him with His people into the land of eternal salvation, which He will give to His elect through Him, and to set Him as their Redeemer and Defender.

Under the tribe of Levi, he now presents here the spiritual priesthood under the New Testament / which Christ chose—not from the physical tribe of Levi, the priests and Levites of his time / but from the Jews who were then in the land / and who are thought to have been from all sorts of tribes / chosen without distinction: namely, first and foremost, the twelve Apostles; of whom none is mentioned as to which tribe he was from. See Luke 6:12, etc.

v. 8. These were now to receive first the <term>Urim and Thummim</term> <note>These were sacred lots used by the High Priest to determine God's will; the terms are often translated from Hebrew as "Lights and Perfections."</note> / which otherwise only the High Priest wore in his office or breastplate / about which more notes can be found in the commentary on Exodus 28:30 / receiving them anew from Christ himself / in whom they essentially reside / as perfect holiness and truth; he also particularly shared this essence in the gift of his Holy Spirit with his twelve Apostles on the day of Pentecost / (see Acts 2:1, etc. and v. 14 where Peter makes mention only of his other eleven fellow Apostles /) from whom thereafter all believers should be exhorted / that they might likewise receive this light and holiness as the spiritual priesthood in the gift of the Holy Spirit. See Acts 19:2, etc. 1 Peter 2:9.

He calls Christ the Holy One and Favored One / whom the Father sanctified for this purpose, Psalm 16:10, and who was his favored companion and beloved Son / by whom also all believers must be sanctified / so that they might again obtain favor and grace with GOD. And this man, the Holy One, was then also the true GOD / whom they had tested and provoked at Massa and Meribah / as discussed in Exodus 17:7.

v. 9. Here he describes / what the spiritual priests of the New Testament must be like / through that which Christ also demands of them in Luke 14:26; see also Matthew 10:21–22. <note>This refers to the radical call of discipleship where loyalty to God supersedes even the closest family ties.</note>

The lineage of Levi is always the lineage of those souls who have already progressed far / who are set apart to lead others. Therefore, they no longer know anyone according to the flesh / neither father nor mother / neither brothers nor children: in that they are stripped of all fleshly, natural relationships and of all the births of self-will.

Toward this, the first Christians not only applied these words / but also reminded one another / that the service of God is to be preferred above all friendship / and godliness above all kinship. (a)
> They did not acknowledge, nor even listen to, any of their relatives / who wanted to turn them away from the hope of heavenly reward through earthly flatteries. (b)

Such faithful souls and leaders now have no more private intentions / which might prevent them from doing the will of GOD. Therefore, it is also said / that they observe his word / and keep his covenant: This covenant is nothing other than <term>Gelassenheit</term> <note>A technical term in German mysticism meaning "yieldedness," "devout detachment," or "resignation to God's will."</note> / through which the soul gives itself entirely to GOD / to fulfill his will: where GOD also acts with the soul / and assures it / that he himself will lead it / and work within it / provided it remains yielded to his guidance / so that it can do his will. Is this then not a covenant / through which the soul voluntarily surrenders itself to its GOD / and GOD in return promises his protection / and thus wishes to be the guarantor in all things? Thus, one can keep his covenant / when one remains in this state of yieldedness.

v. 10. For these they also pray to GOD, Ephesians 1:16, etc. 3:14, etc. indeed, they sacrifice themselves entirely for their service / as Paul emphatically testifies of himself in Philippians 2:17 and 2 Timothy 4:6. This is indeed the true incense, 2 Corinthians 2:15, and the true whole offerings in the New Testament / which are brought to GOD by these spiritual priests / and are well-pleasing to him in Christ.

v. 11. See 2 Timothy 4:14, 3, 2. Psalm 9, 10, etc.

v. 12. "The beloved of the LORD" is none other than Christ / Matthew 3:17, 17:5. The High Priest was a type or figure of him / who had his dwelling in Jerusalem / which was situated in the tribe of Benjamin, Judges 1:21.

By Benjamin, however, one can especially understand the believers in the first three centuries / who confessed Christ very steadfastly through so many persecutions and heavy martyrdoms / and thus laid the foundation for Christianity; who then, according to the word, were true "Sons of the Right Hand" <note>The name Benjamin literally means "Son of the Right Hand" in Hebrew.</note> and beloved of the LORD / whom the true help of the LORD protected / and whom he embraced with special love / so that through the constant indwelling of his Spirit they were equipped with such power / that they were able to endure all such hardships. This may well be what the expression emphatically means:

"That he has settled between his shoulders"; that is / that by following Christ's command; *he who does not bear his cross and follow me cannot be my disciple* (Luke 14:27) / they, in such taking up of the cross upon their shoulders, also received Christ's assistance / who settled upon them / and made them so faithful unto death / that they carried away the crown of glory / as was promised to this church of Smyrna and also to the Ephesian church / to which the spiritual Levi belongs, Revelation 2:10.

<meta>This page continues the mystical commentary on Deuteronomy 33. <header>Chapter 33. The Fifth Book of Moses.</header>

## 13. And of Joseph he said: May his land be blessed by the Lord with the choicest gifts of heaven, with the dew, and with the deep that lies beneath!
## 14. And with the choicest fruits of the sun, and with the choicest yield of the months.
## 15. And with the finest things of the mountains of old, and with the choicest gifts of the everlasting hills.
<margin>Genesis 49:26.</margin>
## 16. And with the choicest gifts of the earth and its fullness. And may the favor of Him who dwelt in the bush come upon the head of Joseph, and upon the crown of the head of the Nazirite <note>The German "Naziräer" refers to someone "consecrated" or "set apart," echoing Joseph's separation from his brothers.</note> among his brothers!

---

This blessing takes precedence over all others, and nothing can be added to it, because the best of heaven and earth is incorporated within it. Therefore, Christ must necessarily be sought here in all things, in whom all fullness was meant to dwell.
**v. 13.** Joseph signifies the Church as it was delivered from persecutions in the times of the Emperor Constantine, when pagan idolatry was destroyed far and wide. Then Joseph, as it were, came to power within the believers in the spiritual Egypt of the nations—believers who previously often had to spend most of their time in prisons.
However, she is promised the most blessed part of the earth in its three divisions: such as Asia Minor, Syria, Egypt, Greece, Italy, Spain, France, and England, etc. These lands have a very temperate heavenly air and many sweet and healthy springs, and brooks and rivers rich in fish.
**v. 14.** Where also the fruitful influences of the sun and the moon produce many noble and tasty fruits.
**v. 15.** Where also the most prominent of the world empires, the Roman, was located, which at that time was mostly made subject to Christ according to outward confession; and within it, Rome, which people used to call the Head of the World <note>original: "Caput Orbis"</note>; and likewise many other significant dominions, both of which are presented under the symbols of mountains and kingdoms. Though one can also understand the physical ones at the same time: such as Lebanon, Taurus, the Alps, and the Pyrenees mountains, and others of that kind.
**v. 16.** Thus the best part of the inhabited earth, and its populous cities and villages, became subject to the kingdom of Christ. And that was not only according to the outward confession, which in the early times was likely all most people possessed; but the earth was also fulfilled and blessed with the favor of Christ—who had previously revealed himself to Moses in the bush (Exodus 3:2)—in many precious souls in whom Christ’s fiery love and a great light of knowledge revealed itself. This blessing came upon these believers as true Nazirites and ones set apart from their brothers. For in this church age, there were not only many precious, godly, and learned teachers, but also many godly hermits who went into the deserts and there led a strict and holy life as true Nazirites.
*The favor of him—must come upon Joseph.* Just as the favor of God rests upon Christ (Matthew 3:17; 17:5), so also the favor of Christ rests upon his believers, especially those who most strictly preserve their "Naziriteship" in separation. *I in them, and you in me* (John 17:22, 23), and the Spirit of the Father and the Son, as their best favor, rests upon us (1 Peter 4:14). But if the Father is to have such favor in us as he has in his Son, then Joseph, the son of love, must take shape in us through the power of his divine love according to all his holy attributes. This is something only his transfiguring Spirit can work in us, through whom God’s love is poured out into the hearts of those who desire and seek it.

<column-break/>

## 17. He has a majesty like the firstborn of his ox, and his horns are like the horns of a unicorn. With them he shall push the nations together to the ends of the earth. And these are the ten thousands of Ephraim, and these are the thousands of Manasseh.
## 18. And of Zebulun he said: Rejoice, Zebulun, in your going out; and you, Issachar, in your tents!
## 19. They shall call the nations to the mountain; there they shall offer sacrifices of righteousness. For they shall suck the abundance of the seas and the hidden treasures of the sand.
## 20.

---

**v. 17.** Finally, it is also reported of this Church how the highest power of the worldly rulers—such as the Emperor was, and many others besides—would confess her; they would keep the enemies away far and wide and thus protect the Church. See Chapter 32:30, 31 in the explanation. And these have become the many
*Ten thousands of Ephraim:* the Church toward the West <note>The author associates Ephraim with the Western/European church.</note>; and
*The thousands of Manasseh:* the Church toward the East <note>Literally "the Morning."</note>, which was surpassed by the former in quantity and fruitfulness; the former has also lasted longer, while the latter is now diminished under the Turkish yoke <note>A reference to the Ottoman Empire's control over Eastern Christian lands.</note> and is, as it were, forgotten according to the word.
**v. 18.** Zebulun is placed here by Moses first, as he was by Jacob, although Issachar was older: just as he then spoke the same thing over both tribes.
However, the prophetic spirit here passes over to the witnesses of truth who emerged from among the great multitude of the external churches (which had become very corrupted by human ordinances). These witnesses are presented under the symbol of Zebulun because the Spirit of Christ, according to the meaning of the word, wanted to take up his dwelling in them, so that such people should rejoice in their "going out" from such corrupted churches, and become the spiritual Issachar, who according to the meaning of the word were to receive the true reward in the righteousness of Jesus Christ and eternal life.
This then can point to the Waldensians <note>A pre-Reformation Christian movement that began in the 12th century, emphasizing poverty and lay preaching.</note> as precious witnesses of truth, who arose in the twelfth century and testified gloriously against all the errors and superstitions of the Antichrist.
**v. 19.** Now that the nations have been invited to the mountain—which is also presented as seven mountains upon which the woman sits (Revelation 17:9), who made a worldly kingdom out of the spiritual kingdom of Christ—these witnesses of truth, namely the Waldensians, and afterwards the great following of the precious witness of truth Wycliffe <note>John Wycliffe (c. 1320s–1384), an English reformer and "Morning Star of the Reformation."</note>, who appeared in the fourteenth century, have offered the sacrifices of righteousness in their tents, having confessed the Lord's name with their lips (Hosea 14:3; Hebrews 13:15).
These then also sucked the wealth of the seas, since they arose by the seas in France and England and gained a great following; and they sucked the hidden treasures in the sand, namely the souls who lay in the dust of contempt and did not preserve or value their own lives, as the believers are described in Psalm 22:30, 31, 32.

# The Fifth Book of Moses, Chapter XXXIII.

**20.** And of Gad he said: Blessed be he who makes room for Gad! He has laid himself down like a lion, and will tear the arm, and also the crown of the head.
**21.** And he saw the firstfruits for himself; for there was the portion of the veiled lawgiver: and he came to the heads of the people; he carried out the justice of the Lord and his rights toward Israel.
**22.** And of Dan he said: Dan is a young lion; he shall leap forth from Bashan.
**23.** And of Naphtali he said: Naphtali shall be satisfied with favor and full of the blessing of the Lord. You shall possess it as an inheritance toward the evening and toward the south.
**24.** And of Asher he said: Let Asher be blessed with sons; let him be pleasing to his brothers, and dip his foot in oil.

---

**v. 20. 21.** Gad signifies a "troop of warriors" <note>original: "Kriegshaufen"; refers to Genesis 30:11</note>, and according to the insight of the Mosaic Bible concerning this chapter—as with the following tribes—these represent the combatants against the Anti-Christ. To these, room and air were made in France, England, and Bohemia. In the midst of the kingdom of the Adversary, they gathered the firstfruits and stepped forth against their enemies; specifically **Jan Hus** and **Jerome of Prague** <note>Jan Hus and Jerome of Prague were early Bohemian reformers executed at the Council of Constance in 1415, here seen as "firstfruits" of the Reformation</note>, when the fathers of the people were assembled at Constance <note>original: "Costnitz"</note>. They did what was right before the Lord with a great confession of truth even unto death. Like courageous lions, they attacked the "arm" of worldly power and the "rational crown" of the beginning and portion of the **veiled lawgiver** <note>The "veiled lawgiver" is interpreted here as the Pope or Church hierarchy who claims to give law while hiding the true Gospel</note>, who set himself up in the Church as a lawgiver and covered himself with the twisted testimonies of the Church Fathers, as if the government of the entire Church of Christ had been entrusted to him in the name of Peter.

**v. 22.** In the tribe of Dan, bravery is noted, which was physically proven especially in Samson. Just as Dan signifies a "judge," it follows in the prophetic context that this refers to one who must reveal God's judgment over spiritual Babylon. Regarding this, the aforementioned Bible states: "A hundred years later, Dan sprang forth like a young lion from Bashan—namely **Luther** together with his companions—so that the Anti-Christian beast (in fat Bashan) trembled and quaked; though this bravery soon vanished, so that the Angel to Sardis <note>A reference to the Seven Churches in Revelation; Sardis is often interpreted as the post-Reformation era that became spiritually dead</note> has only a few names who have not soiled their clothes, while the rest merely keep the name of the first heroes."

**v. 23.** "Naphtali thereafter (as the same Bible further states) is satisfied with grace and full of the blessing of the Lord in the dear **Philadelphia** <note>The Church of Philadelphia in Revelation represents a period of brotherly love and spiritual awakening</note>, which now breaks forth like the dawn. And it is she who receives an open door to take her inheritance toward the evening and south." And here the precious testimony of the Lord is to be found in our days: that he already has his blessing in souls eager for salvation, though in its own time the fullness of grace and blessing will show itself even more among those who wish to wake from the sleep of security and rise from the death of sin and worldly love, so that Christ may enlighten them. (Ephesians 5:14).

**v. 24.** Asher had a very fat <note>meaning fertile</note> land, which was especially rich in olive trees and stretched from Sidon to Mount Carmel. But he shall finally be "blessed with sons," which is to say, with the whole of Israel and the fullness of the Gentiles in the glorious kingdom of Christ. Regarding this, see: "Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection!" (Revelation 20:6), which the name Asher <note>meaning "happy" or "blessed"</note> alludes to. Here is such an abundance of the gifts of the Spirit that Asher "dips his foot in oil."

<column-break/>

**25.** Iron and brass shall be on your shoes, and as long as your days last, so must the report of you be!
**26.** There is none like the God of Jeshurun! who rides upon the heavens to your help, and with his majesty on the highest clouds.
**27.** A dwelling place is God from the beginning, and underneath are the everlasting arms. And he shall thrust out the enemy from before your face, and shall say: Destroy!
<margin>(a) Psalm 46:4.</margin>
**28.** And Israel shall dwell safely alone by the fountain of Jacob (a), in the land where corn and wine are: there his heaven shall drip with dew.
<margin>(a) ? (b) / Isaiah 58:16. (a) chapter 4:7. (b) Revelation 3:9.</margin>
**29.** Blessed are you, Israel! Who is like you (a)? You people who are saved through the Lord, who is the shield of your help and the sword of your majesty: and your enemies shall flatter you (b), and you shall tread upon their high places.

---

**v. 25.** "Here is such power and strength that they trample their enemies as if with iron and brass shoes, so that Christ alone may reign in his chosen ones."
*As long as your days last, so must the report be:* "As of an always very blissful tribe, as the name implies." This great bliss will last the entire appointed time of the **1000 years**, after which Satan will be released again from his prison for a short time. (Revelation 20:3, 7).

**v. 26.** Hereby Christ will now gloriously prove himself as the strong God to his **Jeshurun** <note>A poetic name for Israel meaning "upright one"</note> or his host of people, who will see his glory with their own eyes. Just as the prophetess from the tribe of Asher <note>Referring to Anna in Luke 2:36</note> formerly helped him in his childhood and spoke of the glorious redemption through him (Luke 2:36, 38), he who ascended into heaven (Psalm 68:19) will reveal himself with his mighty help toward his chosen ones.

**v. 27.** For he has always been the dwelling of his believers above, where they have been taken in (Psalm 90:1), and down on earth he has carried and protected them at all times with his arms of love. (See above v. 3 and Isaiah 40:11).
Thus he will then also finally destroy the enemy, Satan, and bind him in prison, and with him all his instruments—the **Beast** and the **False Prophet**—who will be thrown into the lake of fire. (Revelation 19:19, 20).

**v. 28.** Following this, nothing else can follow but a very peaceful state in the glorious thousand-year kingdom of Christ, where everything lives in great peace, and every family especially lives in great pleasure. They will be refreshed by the rich gifts of the Spirit and also enjoy the physical blessing of holiness, of which the prophets are entirely filled. (See Micah 4:3-4, Isaiah 12, Hosea 14:6-8, Joel 3:18).

**v. 29.** Then this victory will be praised continually in the tents of the righteous: that Christ has brought everything in the world under their feet. (See Psalm 118:15, Isaiah 58:14, Amos 4:13).

# The XXXIV. Chapter.
->The Death of Moses and the Succession of Joshua.<-

AND Moses climbed from the flat plains of the Moabites up to Mount Nebo (*) / to the heights of Pisgah / which is opposite Jericho: and the LORD let him see the entire land / Gilead as far as Dan; (*) <gloss>chapter 32, verse 49.</gloss>

2. And all of Naphtali / and the land of Ephraim and Manasseh / and the whole land of Judah / as far as the western sea / <note>original: "das hinterste Meer," literally "the hindmost sea," referring to the Mediterranean.</note>

3. And toward the south / and the region of the valley of Jericho / the City of Palms / as far as Zoar.

---

v. 1. **To Mount Nebo)** which signifies / prophecy or contemplation / all those must climb who wish to rightly prepare themselves for such a high grace / so that they, like Moses, may be led into the contemplation of great things. They must rise above the external life / the sensory inclinations and agitations / into the life of faith. They must live in the Spirit; which is the true mountain of prophecies within us. Revelation 4:1-2. The more we live according to and in the Spirit / and elevate ourselves above the flesh and its earthly sensations; the more easily we may be gathered / drawn or led up / to contemplate that which the goodness of the Lord is willing to reveal to us. John 14:21.

# The Fifth Book of Moses, Chapter XXXIII.

**20. And of Gad he said: Blessed be he who makes room for Gad! He has lain down like a lion, and will tear the arm, and also the crown of the head.**

**21. And he saw the firstfruits for himself; for there was the portion of the hidden law-giver: and he came to the leaders of the people; he executed the justice of the LORD and his judgments toward Israel.**

**22. And of Dan he said: Dan is a young lion; he shall leap forth from Bashan.**

**23. And of Naphtali he said: Naphtali shall be satisfied with favor and full of the blessing of the LORD. You shall possess it toward the west and toward the south.** <note>The original German uses "Abend" (Evening/West) and "Mittag" (Midday/South) for the points of the compass.</note>

**24. And of Asher he said: Asher be blessed with sons; let him be acceptable to his brothers, and dip his foot in oil.**

---

v. 20. 21. <gloss>Gad signifies a "troop" (Genesis 30:11). According to the insights of the prophetic Bible regarding this chapter, and as with the following tribes, this represents the liberators from the Anti-Christ <note>The term "Anti-Christ" here refers to the perceived corruption in the institutional Church that the Reformers sought to fix.</note> for whom room and air were made in France, England, and Bohemia. They gathered the firstfruits in the midst of the realm of the Adversary and stood as a bridge for their enemies—especially Jan Hus and Jerome of Prague <note>Hus and Jerome were Czech reformers burned at the stake for heresy in the early 15th century.</note> when the fathers of the people were assembled at Constance, doing what was right before the Lord with a great confession of truth even unto death. Like courageous lions, they attacked the arm of worldly power and the "crown of reason" of the hidden law-giver <note>The "hidden law-giver" is interpreted here as the Papacy.</note> who set himself up in the Church as a legislator, covering himself with the twisted testimonies of the Church Fathers as if the governance of the entire Church of Christ had been entrusted to him in Peter's name.</gloss>

v. 22. <gloss>In the tribe of Dan, bravery is noted, which was physically demonstrated by Samson. Just as Dan signifies a "judge," in the context of the prophetic sense it signifies one who must reveal God's judgment upon spiritual Babylon. Regarding this, the aforementioned Bible says: "A hundred years later, Dan sprang forth like a young lion from Bashan—namely, Luther and his companions—so that the Anti-Christian beast (in the fatness of Bashan) trembled and shook." Though this bravery soon vanished, such that the Angel at Sardis <note>A reference to the Seven Churches in Revelation 3.</note> has only a few names who have not defiled their garments, the others merely retain the name of those first heroes.</gloss>

v. 23. <gloss>"Naphtali afterwards (as the same Bible further states) is satisfied with grace and full of the Lord’s blessing in the precious Philadelphia <note>Philadelphia is viewed by Pietists as the true, loving church of the end times.</note> which now breaks forth like the dawn. It is she who receives an open door to take her inheritance toward the west and south. And here the precious testimony of the Lord is to be found in our days: that He already has His blessing in those souls who hunger for salvation, though in His time the fullness of grace and blessing will show itself even more among those who wish to wake from the sleep of security and rise from the death of sin and worldly love, so that Christ may enlighten them (Ephesians 5:14)."</gloss>

v. 24. <gloss>Asher had a very fertile land, particularly rich in olive trees, stretching from Sidon to Mount Carmel. But he shall finally be "blessed with sons," that is, with the whole of Israel and the fullness of the Gentiles in the (glorious) Kingdom of Christ. Of this it is written: "Blessed and holy is he who has part in the first resurrection" (Revelation 20:6), which the name Asher <note>Asher means "Happy" or "Blessed" in Hebrew.</note> alludes to. "Here is such an abundance of the gifts of the Spirit that Asher dips his foot in oil."</gloss>

v. 25. <gloss>"Here is such power and strength that they trample their enemies as if with iron and bronze shoes," so that Christ alone may reign in His chosen ones. As long as your days last, your fame must endure "as a tribe that is always most blessed, which the name itself implies. This great happiness will last the entire appointed time of the 1,000 years, after which Satan will again be released from his prison for a little while (Revelation 20:3, 7)."</gloss>

v. 26. <gloss>With this, Christ will gloriously prove Himself as the mighty God to His Jeshurun, or His gathered people, who will see His glory with their own eyes—just as the prophetess Anna from the tribe of Asher once did in His childhood (Luke 2:36, 38). v. 27. <gloss>Since He has always been the dwelling place of His believers above, where they have been received (Psalm 90:1), and here on earth He has always carried and protected them with His arms of love. See above at verse 3 and Isaiah 40:11. Thus He will also finally destroy the enemy, Satan, and bind him in prison, and with him all his instruments—the Beast and the false prophet—whom He will cast into the lake of fire (Revelation 19:19, 20).</gloss>

v. 28. <gloss>Nothing else can follow this but a most peaceful state in the glorious thousand-year kingdom of Christ, where everything exists in great peace, and every family lives in great contentment. They will be refreshed by the rich gifts of the Spirit and also enjoy the physical blessings of holiness, which the prophets are entirely full of. See Micah 4:3-4, Isaiah 12, Hosea 14:6-8, Joel 3:18.</gloss>

v. 29. <gloss>Then this victory shall be praised continually in the tents of the righteous—that Christ has brought everything in the world under their feet. See Psalm 118:15, Isaiah 58:14, Amos 4:13.</gloss>

<meta>This page concludes the Fifth Book of Moses (Deuteronomy). The previous page ended with Moses viewing the Promised Land from Mount Nebo. This page describes his burial by God, his physical state at death, the mourning of the Israelites, and the transition of leadership to Joshua. It concludes with a high praise of Moses’s unique relationship with God and his role as a forerunner of Christ.</meta>

### The Fifth Book of Moses. Chapter XXXIV.

6. And he buried him in the valley in the land of the Moabites, opposite Beth-peor <note>original: "Hause Peor"</note>: and no one has known of his grave, even unto this day.

<margin>Joshua 14:10, 11.</margin>
7. And Moses was one hundred and twenty years old when he died. His eyes had not become dim, and his strength had not departed.

8. And the children of Israel wept for Moses in the flat plains of the Moabites for thirty days: then the days of weeping and mourning for Moses were ended.

---

v. 6. It is certainly not denied that it happened largely to prevent outward superstition among the people, that the Lord Himself buried the body of Moses and did not want anyone to know of his grave; thereby cutting off the opportunity for Satan to drive the children of Israel toward idolatry with this grave and body, which would have greatly defiled the true religion. This is why the Holy Spirit also reports the dispute between the Archangel Michael (or Christ) and the devil over this matter in Jude verse 9. Therefore, this serves as a sign of a false prophet when his followers preserve and misuse such things for adoration. This should have served as a warning to the Church of Christ not to venerate the departed bodies or relics of the saints and their graves in such a way, but rather to keep their memory in blessing and to follow them in their godly way of life. See Hebrews 13:7.

But it may yet be permitted to believe that something more is signified by this, as was noted just before.

**No one has known of his grave**) From this, some conclude through conjecture—and it becomes quite probable when one considers that he appeared with Elijah before Christ in his true body during the Transfiguration (Matthew 17:3)—(a) that although he died and was buried, he was also soon resurrected by God and translated before he underwent decay. This is without even considering what might be concluded from the Epistle of Jude verse 9 to confirm this, which will be discussed in its proper place.

v. 7. **Moses was 120 years old**) This is the exact time or period of grace in which God waited and had patience with the first world (Genesis 6:3). Some calculate this in a prophetic sense as a number of Jubilee years, making the conclusion that when 5880 years have passed since the beginning of the world—a number arising from 120 Jubilee years, each reckoned at 49 years—or, according to another reckoning (b), when 1739 years have fully passed from the time of Christ, the Lord will no longer contend with men through Moses, nor keep His Church in the wilderness, but will bring them into Canaan and make it manifest. <note>The author is referencing Matthias Wasmuth’s chronological calculations, a common practice in 18th-century Pietist and mystical circles to predict the beginning of a new spiritual age.</note>

**His eyes — strength — not departed**) The Law and its "fire" or quality of righteousness, from which it flowed, has its strength and living impact. It has power over a man as long as he lives: and all men are under condemnation as long as they live in sin. But when we are dead to sin, the Law is also dead to us; and then the "body of Moses" is buried by the Lord, and we die to the Law through the body of Christ, so that we may be married to another, namely, to Him who was raised from the dead.

v. 8. **The children of Israel wept for Moses**) It is difficult to part with divine persons and leadership, especially when one has seen and recognized much of the glory and power of God through their service, even if something higher and more perfect is meant to take their place.

**30 days**) The same as for Aaron (Numbers 20:29). Otherwise, mourning lasted 7 days (Genesis 50:10; Sirach 22:13).

<margin>(a) Abraham Calov, Prolegomena to the Pentateuch, p. 209.</margin>
<margin>(b) According to the Wasmuthian Computation</margin>

<column-break/>

9. And Joshua the son of Nun was filled with the spirit of wisdom, for Moses had laid his hands upon him: and the children of Israel obeyed him, and did just as the Lord had commanded Moses.

<margin>Numbers 12:7, 8.</margin>
10. And since that time, there arose no prophet in Israel like unto Moses, whom the Lord knew face to face;

11. According to all the signs and wonders for which the Lord sent him to perform in the land of Egypt, upon Pharaoh and all his servants, and upon all his land.

12. And according to all that mighty hand, and according to all the great terror which Moses performed before the eyes of all Israel.

---

<margin>Numbers 27:18 etc.</margin>
v. 9. Thus Joshua now actually enters the office into which he had been installed by Moses at the Lord's command through the laying on of hands. This power exists because God has reserved the free authority to immediately choose whom He wishes to set over His people, as happened later with the Judges (Hebrews 2:16) and the first two kings, Saul and David, whose family was then confirmed in the government.

**For**) Thus, the laying on of hands by a holy man of God according to the will of God is of great power; whereas the imitation of an assumed office of God, as experience testifies, proves to be a ridiculous, self-made power.

v. 10. **No prophet like Moses**) Who, according to calculations (a), made 53 journeys, performed 50 of the greatest miraculous works, and had 173 conversations with God. One would have liked to share his glorious prefiguration of Christ here at the end; but because space is running out, it must be saved for elsewhere.

A man who reached so far and remained until he could be brought to the final step of perfection, like Moses, is such a rare thing, as the Scripture thoughtfully wishes to make known here. Almost no men are found who enter into God in a perfect way; which is to be known by the Lord "face to face"—namely, without a veil and without a mediator. This is because of the great difficulty which people have—especially those who possess some knowledge and virtue—in allowing themselves to be "annihilated" <note>The term "annihilation" (Vernichtung) here refers to the mystical concept of "poverty of spirit," where the ego is set aside to allow God to work entirely through the person.</note>, as is necessary in the secret death and for the annihilation through which a man can only enter into God.

In the preference of Moses above all other men who were raised up as mere mortals, God intended to turn us away from all men and point us toward the one Prophet whom Moses himself promised, and to whom he commanded obedience (Chapter 18:15 etc.; Hebrews 3:3).

v. 11. **Therefore his wonders were in the place to which the Lord sent him**) And as some conclude from certain reasons, he will soon be sent again as one sent by God, to perform similar signs and wonders in the "spiritual Egypt" <note>A reference to the "Two Witnesses" in Revelation 11 who perform miracles like Moses and Elijah.</note>, and to bear his witness before and against the spiritual Pharaoh and his kingdom (Revelation 11).

v. 12. There, great terror will also manifest among all who have not wanted to attend to their salvation.

-> T H E   E N D. <-

<margin>(a) Micraelius, Church History, book 1, chapter 2, question 7. (b) Revelation 11.</margin>
